#1
Spoiler: AN: Content Warning


I, Greg Veder – first of my name, stir myself awake.

F-ILUR-​

What was that?

-lower difficulty challenges first. Altern-​

I shake my head to clear my vision, blue lines of holographic text filling my vision before apparently dismissing itself.

I push my hand out to the side to push myself up from my bed, I frown as I feel paper crumbling under the pressure instead of smooth fabric. I rub at my eyes and grab the paper, squinting to read the note aloud. "Three favours. We will contact you." My eyes move down. "C."

And not just any 'C'. I jerk upright, staring at the page. THE 'C'. The secret government conspiracy that controlled superpower distribution on the dark side of the internet.

I remembered finding them. Taking almost the entirety of what my parents had left behind for me and offering it on a quiet, text-only chat room hidden so well that it had taken months to even guess at its location.

They had agreed, and then I woke up back in my bed. I glance at the window. Morning. Phone calendar? Sunday. It was Tuesday afternoon when I had sent that message. Had I been abducted, mind-wiped and returned in the span of a week?

It wouldn't surprise me. It was extremely obvious that the government had the technology to do that, even before parahumans came along.

More importantly, did I even have powers now? That was the deal, I was sure. Powers for a few favours and an IOU for the trust fund money from my parents. I didn't feel like I could fly, or breathe fire, turn invisible. Had I fallen for the equivalent of the online ads telling me about the hot singles in my area?

Surely not.

All I had were these flickering lines at the edge of my vision. I shake my head trying to clear them. Still there.

"Greg! Get down here! If I have to cook for your worthless ass, then the least you can do is show up and eat it!" Alice. My 'mother', as she insists on being called despite the lack of blood relation or any warm feelings at all, calls up into my room. She kind of hates me, or possibly just men in general - the feelings been mutual ever since my dad cheated on her to have me with some random lady off the street. That lady had handed me off to my father nine months later and promptly ran off to do whatever she did with her life. Nobody in my family ever saw her again. I lived with my father and the rest of the 'family' for a few years without issue.

Then my old man drops dead out of nowhere and I get to put up with life under the hellish purview of my 'mother' and my half-sister – who were already openly antagonistic when Dad was around, and have only gotten worse since then.

"Yeah, Greg!" The other member of the household jeers. "Leave your Chinese cartoons alone, they aren't going to fuck you! Not that anyone else would either, but you could at least pretend to be less of a slug - it's painful to have to share the house with you sometimes." Rude. My sister Clara doesn't like me either. I'm not quite sure what set her off, but she's always sided with my mother for almost everything. I don't know what she's been told about me or Dad, but she's never shown any inclination of wanting to get to the truth herself.

"Coming." I let out a put-upon tone into the voice. But if they weren't going to comment on my apparent disappearance for a week... then it seemed I could rely on whatever mind-control chips the Cape illuminati had installed to cover their tracks.

My mother's irate voice floats back up the stairs. "Gregory Michael Veder, don't take that attitude with me-" I roll my eyes, flicking on a new shirt. "-took you in and asked for nothing-" I check my phone again. Nothing notable happening in the gaming newsphere. "-your worthless, wreck of a father-" Some new episodes to catch up on, but nothing that can't wait now that I may or may not have superpowers. "-a little bit of respect!"

Sensing the end of the rant, I exit the room and start descending the stairs. I shake my head again. Still the blue lines and symbols. Can't seem to lose them.

I catch a glimpse of my mother's back as she disappears into the kitchen, a transparent, almost holographic, padlock seeming to hover next to her - seemingly invisible to her eyes judging by the lack of hysterics from her.

TUTORIAL

VEDER HOUSEHOLD 1/8

CHALLENGE?​

I snap my eyes away. The text and symbols melt sideways into the nearly invisible lines on the edge of my vision that had been bothering me ever since I woke up. My eyes roam back towards her again. The text reforms effortlessly.

"It's like a HUD!" I breathe. I already knew my next step. I cast a hand out in front of me like casting a magic spell. "Status." Nothing happened. "Properties. Skills. Save. Quest. Journal. Inventory. Observe." I pout and lower my hand. Did the power-people at the government not understand how gamer powers were supposed to work?

She half turns to give me a disgusted look. "Stupid boy. Do you think real life is a game now too? I never should have let you keep those ridiculous toys of yours. Start behaving your age, or I'll throw out every last one of-"

I take some more steps forward to keep her in my line of sight. Having my power explicitly label something as Tutorial made my next move extremely logical. "Challenge." I whisper.

And the world disappears in a blur of fractals. I reappear in my room - having somehow climbed the stairs once more already.

Mover power. Check. Teleportation is neat, but let's see what the rest does before we get excited.

I tilt my head like any proper hero would as I listened out for any unusual sounds around the house. Nothing. I could hear the vague sound of a running tap downstairs, but other than that there didn't seem to be anything of note happening.

With a shrug, I retraced my steps from just a minute prior - wandering down the steps towards the lower floor.

Alice Veder has her back to me when I enter the room, and the roar of the taps seems to stifle any noise I made entering the room. The lack of movement is somewhat creepy, and I can't help but wonder if my quick power experimentation had done something unpleasant to her. I sidle closer. She doesn't move a muscle until I poke her lightly from behind. "Alice?" She doesn't respond. I clear my throat and repeat myself louder. "Mother?"

She silences the tap and spins around in a movement almost too fast to follow.

I laugh. "You had me worried there, I think you were miles away. Did you say Dinner was ready? I don't see it-"

She turns away towards the kitchen counter. Well. That's nicer treatment than I usually get. I'll take that as a win.

I turn my thoughts away from the oddly good mood of my mother and turn my thoughts back to my power. What did challenge even mean in this context? I would have expected more from a tutorial level - as much as I hate hand-holding in games, I could really use a simple set of instructions to get me started here. Was it something related to Alice specifically? Was this scene the equivalent of a cutscene before the event happened? It seems exactly like real-life, so I'm not entirely sure that my power has done anything but a minor light show and move me back to my bed.

Instant transportation to my bed was actually a moderately useful superpower, but it wasn't particularly cool.

A searing sensation of pain blossoms from my back, a near-identical one slamming into my right arm. I gasp and choke, shoving myself away from the source as a white-hot line curves its way down my arm. I spin around, backpedalling under the table and emerging the other side as I come face-to-face with my mother clutching at two bloodied kitchen knives like a woman possessed.

I let out an articulate scream as she takes another wild, inexpert lunge at me across the table - one knife leaving a small slash into my shirt before I twist away and dive past her.

"What the fuck is wrong with you?" I hiss, stumbling backwards as I clutch at the bleeding wounds. They weren't deep - probably not the ideal knives for stabbing that she could have used - but my shirt was already soaked in blood. There's a cold, sinking feeling in my stomach as I realise the likely answer to her sudden attack: this was something to do with my power.

She rushes at me again. She's kind of fat, so it's simple to dash around the counter and sprint away, the stab wound didn't feel deep – probably more due to the low quality of the knife and the lack of technique behind the stab. I was more concerned about my arm and chest, both bleeding profusely as I run. I'm overthinking this. Keep running.

"Clara! Alice has gone fucking crazy!" I yell up the stairs as I frantically unlock the front door. "Call the police and get out of here!" There was no reply forthcoming. I bodily shove past the door and out into the drive, the street spins briefly in my vision before I force myself to focus - staggering down the street in an adrenaline-fuelled burst.

Phone. Police. PRT? Why didn't I grab my mobile? It was right on the counter, there was no chance of going back to get it now. The streets are entirely devoid of people, nobody in the stores or houses either - or at least as far as I can tell. Was this part of my power as well? How far did the effect extend? If I could escape this alternate-reality bubble, would everything return to normal? Could I contact someone outside of the effect?

Was there even a payphone anywhere around here? Did they still have those these days? The street spins again in warning as I accidentally walk into a wall, the road seeming to split into two as I lean against it. Blood loss. Bad. I should... stop the bleeding. Somehow. Was the wound on my back even that deep? It had felt like the least painful wound compared to the one on my arm, but that meant nothing considering what other problems that kind of injury could cause.

Now I wished that I had paid any attention to that first aid class they did last year. A wet cough surges from my chest and sprays blood onto the ground in front of me to join the bloody trail that I had been leaving behind me. That was bad. All the TV shows with dying characters had them do that at some point.

A trail that I was leaving behind me... I numbly realise the problem at the same time my mother rounds the corner, peering at the ground like a dog as she literally follows my footsteps all the way here.

"She's following me." I groan as her head snaps towards me and she begins her slow charge - already out-of-breath before she started to run, and barely gaining speed when she started. "Of course she is."

I push myself off the wall, my head pulsing at the mere thought of trying to run away again. Instead, I turn to the nearest building - a standard office block towering above me. I'm sure there is usually a guard here, but this time nothing stops me from shoving the door open, racing across the lobby and stumbling into the elevator. I slam the button for the top floor, before allowing myself to sit on the floor - legs feeling heavier than lead all of a sudden.

Alice bulldozes through the entrance door just in time to watch the only elevator close. In what seems like moments, I'm whisked up thirteen or so floors away from my homicidal step-mother.

"Floor, Fourteen. Doors opening." The automated voice chimes out.

I don't move, other than to stick my leg out to keep the elevator open. She was doubtlessly waiting at the bottom, trying to call the elevator back down. If I just sat here, then she would be forced to take the stairs- at which point I could take the elevator all the way back down again with a massive time lead.

Even more so considering she was already huffing and puffing after a short jog across the streets. If I was lucky, climbing a full thirteen flights of stairs might hospitalise her without me having to do anything. I let my hand fall to the floor from where I had been clutching at my grazed neck. Not as deep as the one on my shoulder or chest, or I would probably already be dead. I think. A cut throat is an insta-kill in most movies and games anyway.

...I'm dripping blood onto the floor again. Could blood get into the electronics of the lift? Was blood conductive to electricity? I giggle slightly, well aware of the steady decline in rational, logical thought that I was experiencing. Blood loss is bad! Greg Veder making revolutionary strides in medicine!

Steady, calm breaths. I have to focus on the sounds around me, like a proper ninja. I could hear the heavy footsteps on the stairs. Trying to estimate how close she is seems impossible in my current state.

I hold off for another minute, then I stop blocking the door and make an attempt to hit the ground floor button. My right arm, slick with blood, refuses to move without crippling amounts of pain. I twist on my ass and slam it with my left arm instead. Even if she turned around immediately, I should have a large enough lead to get away safely. There was a police station not too much farther down the street if I could make it there...

"Floor, One. Doors opening." I attempt to push myself up, only to find my legs and arms buckling under the pressure immediately. I stare at my hands as I idly kick my leg out to block the doors from closing. I attempt to pull myself up on the railing but find that I can't remain standing without it. I feel like I've just run a marathon - I've never done one of those, but I imagine that this bone-deep exhaustion would be what it feels like at the end of it.

I can't move. Or at least, I can't walk. Trying to escape at a mere crawl would guarantee my death. Even with minutes to spare I doubted I would be able to drag myself much past the door of the office and across the road – leaving a huge trail all the way.

I need to gather my energy and...

And what? I ask myself, already hearing heavy footsteps on the stairs coming back down. So much faster than they were on the way up. A choked sob escapes my mouth as reality slowly dawns. I can't escape. All I'm doing now is delaying things in the hope that it fixes itself.

Sooner or later, Terminator-lite is going to catch up with me and finish me off - if the blood loss and shock doesn't get me first.

I blink once, eyes feeling heavy.

I jerk awake at the sound of a door slamming - adrenaline the only thing allowing me to expend the energy to lunge at the top floor button again as the overweight, older woman pushes the door to the stairs open once more.

The roar of fury as the door closes in front of her is music to my ears, but the smile on my face doesn't last for more than a second before I remember that I'm still in a horrible position.

"Floor, Fourteen. Doors opening." I block the door with my foot again as the alarms start to blare around me.

Alarms? I glance up at the flashing red lights and the synchronised noise of every office door in the corridor slamming open.

"The fire alarm." I whisper to myself, before paling as I realise that the lift isn't trying to push against my leg anymore. I hit the button for the first floor.

"Out of service. Please evacuate using the emergency stairs." The automated voice drones at me.

Can't use the elevator while the fire alarms are active. What shitty lift was this? That's just my luck. I crawl out of the lift, hacking up more blood along the way. Emergency stairs. The only way out. Reach out to the carpet, knees up and drag yourself forward. Solid Snake. But with more bleeding.

Follow the trail of emergency lights. Come on Greg. You can do this.

It gets faster once I have a rhythm to it, though I don't think I would be winning any awards for speed anytime soon. Soon enough I come to the exit leading to the outside emergency stairs. I stare at the release mechanism, a normal push-and-shove - inconsequential for anyone standing up, but when I was unable to even bring myself to a proper seating position without something to pull me up it seemed nearly impossible.

I improvise a bit. It takes a few tries for me to spin my legs upright against the door, then to slam my heel correctly into the mechanism to shove it open. Blissfully cool air washes over me as my legs flop over the doorway.

I roll myself down the first set of metal stairs, knowing that at this point I lacked the cohesion to even drag myself down the stairs in a timely manner. My head bounces on the last few steps, sending stars flying across my vision as I struggle to separate up from down.

At the very same instant that I recover, I hear a heavy boot on the metal stairs above me accompanied by heavy panting.

My vision is blurry, but I know she's caught up with me. I took too long, left too obvious a trail. "Pleash." I spit out blood. "Alice. Please. Talk to me. My power did this, this isn't you. You don't want to do this. I know you didn't want anything to do with me, and I haven't been the best-"

She descends the steps silently.

"I'm sorry." I blubber incoherently. Tears blur my vision even further. "Don't kill me. I don't want to die."

She stops next to me. I still can't see properly. One arm wraps around underneath my bloodied legs, the other around my neck.

No stabbings. No boots to the face. I feel a tiny flutter of hope that my powers effect is gone as she pulls me upwards almost gently.

That hope vanishes as I feel the wind intensify as she moves me away from her own body. "No." I struggle weakly as she suspends me in the air off of the stairs. I can't see anything anymore, and I wouldn't want to see the 14-story drop anyway. "No, no - don't. Please. Alice."

Then, with a final heave. She flings my body clear of the stairs, tumbling over a dozen stories towards the cold, hard ground.

I wish I could say that I couldn't feel the pain of landing.

On the second bounce, the world melts away in a storm of spiralling colours, the sensation of pain abruptly vanishing and the blue text of my power returning once more.

FAILURE

Hint: Enemies that are UNAWARE will not deviate from their usual routine unless they become aware of the player. Take all the time you need to prepare yourself and plan your approach, before ambushing enemies at your leisure!

In ALERTED (ALRT) missions, the enemy will instantly detect your presence - but not your location. In these missions, remember that the enemy can prepare surprises or hunt you down too!​

I stare blankly at the text as it hovers in the air, the world starting to fill itself in piece-by-piece.

I'm alive.

Just a... simulation. From my power. Like a dream. I flex my arm. It responds easily, as if nothing had ever happened. No phantom pain. Even the sickening memory of my bones shattering in the fall already seems like it happened some time ago. As if I was remembering the pain of the trip to the dentist last week, painful in the moment – but a distant, bearable memory now.

I settle backwards onto the step with shaky legs as Alice finishes her movement back into the kitchen. Her padlock is locked again, a two hour timer floating above it as she disappears out of my vision. A countdown until I can do it again. Undoubtedly.

"What the fuck are you doing just sitting there? Move, dickhead!" Clara storms past me on her way to the kitchen, a foot finding its way into the side of my chest as she passes. She turns around, doubtless to give another scathing remark before catching sight of my face. "Wait, are you crying?"

"It's dust-" I lie, my voice coming out in a weak warble.

"You're actually crying! God, you're so pathetic." She sneers. "Did you break one of your little toys? Can't you go and jerk off in a corner somewhere else? Some of us actually have futures and real life problems to focus on, I would rather get on with my life without having to look at you again."

I stare at her with a blank look.

"Nothing to say? That's what I thought." She spins on one heel, the open padlock above her head spinning in the air. "Later, loser."

My eyes follow her.

TUTORIAL

VEDER HOUSEHOLD 3/8

(TIME)​

"Its not real." I breathe out quietly. "It's fine if I die." Nothing matters. Alice didn't notice anything. It had nothing to do with real-life, and apparently memories didn't carry across either.

"Hm? You say something?" She queries.

I breathe out, oddly calm despite the events of just a few moments prior. "Yeah, I did." I lock eyes with her firmly. "Challenge." The walls fall away as the world goes white.

It was probably stupid to rush into a possible repeat of the traumatic first usage of my power. But I didn't want to think about that right now. I didn't want to deal with my sister's words. I didn't want to go and sit opposite someone who had just stabbed me in the back and actually killed me via throwing me off a building. I wanted to get to the bottom of my power and what it did.

My power presented an alternative course of action, and I took it without a second thought.

Not that there was a way back now. Was there? I lean back into my bed, still not fully formed. "I give up. Forfeit. I surrender. Suicide. Menu. Alt-F4. Escape. Concede. ID-Escape. Cancel Simulation." Nope. I cut my musings as the world finishes reforming.

I reappear in my room again. If that hint from earlier meant anything, then these challenges might have modifiers attached to them. TIME was listed under this one.

Presumably short for timer. A limited amount of time to win? A countdown to reinforcements? Or was it a grading system? Did it count from the start, or from when I got spotted? Is it a countdown to an event happening? Only experimentation could answer that question.

If it was a simple timeout before failing, then that was easy and painless to check. I set my watch to a timer and leave it running.

In the meantime, I should sneak around the house, gather a few supplies just in case my sister did try and murder me in a few minutes.

Sneaking out the corridor and down the stairs is easy, I can hear the keyboard tapping and music blaring from her room. A cursory inspection of the kitchen and the street outside reveals that once again, nobody else seems to be present in this strange mirror-world.

Just me and Clara. 1v1. Deathmatch.

Not that I particularly wanted to use the term Deathmatch. I was hoping that there were different ways to win, that didn't involve murdering someone that I interact with on a regular basis – however unpleasant the interaction was.

She might not even try to kill me. She could turn around and reveal that TIME is a reference to the fact that this challenge is a race around the block and back.

I glance at my watch as two minutes pass without incident. Nothing yet. Good start.

That optimistic thought didn't stop me from tucking a kitchen knife into my back pocket and picking up the second largest to tuck under the carpet just outside her room. I locked the shed, hid the keys and quietly blockaded the entrances to the house with the downstairs furniture.

I rush back upstairs as my watch buzzes five minutes, watching for any movement from my sisters room. Not a single blip.

It's the distant sound of police sirens that causes me to swear instead. I shove open the door to my sisters room, immediately attracting her attention.

She glances at me, a glimmer of surprise in her eyes that swiftly turns blank and stormy. She jumps upwards and dashes towards her desk without a word.

I don't want to kill her in cold blood. I have to be sure that she's just the same as Alice was.

In less than a second, she's already halfway across the room with scissors in a two-handed overhead swinging motion. "Thought so." I grimace, pulling out the brutal-looking kitchen knife. "Mine's bigger."

She seems to reconsider the odds at that, turning towards the back of the room and the window. I lunge after her as she struggles with the lock - the window half jamming forward as the knife arcs around to connect with a stab at her vulnerable neck. It skitters wide, leaving a bloody trail as I recenter myself and land a decisive stab deep inside her flesh.

"He's inside! Gun him down!" That was the police, already hammering at the door. The decision to blockade the door seems to be a good one, even if it was just a temporary measure.

Clara staggers, a bloody stream flowing from her chest as she paws at the wound in abject disbelief. There's a weak, prick from the scissors in retaliation - but I just ignore it as she sinks to her knees.

Nothing matters. It's not real. No going back now. I kick her to the floor fully and stab wildly at her again. I know how long I lasted after a weak and relatively ineffectual stab. I couldn't leave things to chance here.

Stab.

"Please die." I whisper, incredibly aware of the splintering noises coming from the front door. I didn't want to find what a real bullet feels like.

Stab.

Slash.

She stopped resisting a long time ago. "Hurry, hurry, hurry. Die already! FUCKING DIE!"

As if on cue, the world starts to splinter. I vaguely register a stinging pain in my side as the police finally reach me - but slightly too late to matter.

The blue text lights up in the white void ahead of me.

SUCCESS

Reward: Clara Veder +
​
I breathe out quietly. Just my power. Just a dream. It wasn't real. I'm not actually like that. I hate my sister's guts, but I don't actually want her dead.

I take a deep breath and read the text. I scowl.

"What do you mean, plus?" I grouch, trying to calm my nerves a bit. "What about XP? Money? New powers?"

It was one thing to know that it is all just my power, but it felt real - I just stabbed someone to death and felt... satisfied at the end of it.

No answers were forthcoming from the blue text, and soon enough I found myself seated back on the stairs once more.

"'Scuse me." Clara brushes past again. She frowns at me as she passes. "Hey, bro. You seem a bit down, is everything okay?" I blink at the sudden turnaround from her usual attitude. She glances at the kitchen nervously. "Was it mom again? She'll warm up to you one day, I promise. She's just... prickly at the moment. You know? I'd rather not get involved in the fight, but if you need to talk – my door's open."

I stare at her. Was she actually being nice? I belatedly realise that she's waiting for a response. "Ah, oh. Yeah. Sure." I finish lamely.

"Well. Don't let her get you down. I have no homework. You have none, right?" I nod dumbly. She wiggles an eyebrow at me. "We can play one of your games after dinner? That Cape Fighters Unlimited one."

"Ultimate." I correct automatically. Was this really my sister? This was undoubtedly the effect of my power. If this was my new sister, then I had functionally killed my old one with my own two hands.

And yet, I couldn't help but feel happy with the change. Happy with the outcome. It wasn't as if there was any love lost between us before. Perhaps this way, I could experience a normal sibling relationship?

I smile at her. Pointedly ignoring the locked symbol next to her. "I'd like that."

TUTORIAL

VEDER HOUSEHOLD 4/8

(GANG)

LOCKED​

Dinner was a tense affair. Alice continued to barely tolerate me, although Clara was clearly uncomfortable with the hostility for once. Alice seemed to take the sudden change in attitude completely in stride - as if this was the way the family dynamics had always been. Retroactively fixed? A stranger power? Or had events actually been adjusted to allow for the new Clara? Knowledge of other capes told me it was just the first. A picture on the wall of me and Clara smiling next to each other told me it was the second – or perhaps some strange mix between the two.

I kept to myself, avoiding the conversation as much as I could. Instead, I settled down and eyed the next challenges that would soon become available to me.

Alice was simple, it looked like I was locked out of 'Veder Household 1/8' until the countdown was finished. So I could probably get another try in this evening. I could see vague hints of malformed text below the challenge - possibly hinting at more to come after I beat this one.

Clara's didn't have a timer at all. Just a locked padlock, like almost everyone that I had scanned outside of the house since discovering my power. I focus my attention at it, causing the lock to shake negatively.

CONDITIONS NOT MET​

Unhelpful. Would it kill the developers to add a more useful error message?

Still. I could make a guess. Completing the "tutorial" missions in the listed order might unlock it - Clara was listed as the third. Alice was the first - and possibly the second as well, I would find out soon enough.

There was likely some other, hidden conditions as well - unless the tutorial explicitly locked out every other challenge then I should have other targets on people out in the street, but the neighbour's challenges remain locked out even though I can see them through the window.

Well. There was nothing to be done about it now. It was clear that if I wanted to get anywhere with my power, then I had to work through the system as it was given to me.

It was a game. Essentially. Take out the fact that it's someone I know and it becomes a simple and easy matter to win, now that I know the rules.

I fix a nod and smile as Alice snips at me to clean up. I could grin and bear it for another hour or so until I could attempt her challenge again. If Clara's challenge turned her from absolute hatred to a somewhat sympathetic sister, then it was likely that my 'mother' would face a similar fate.

"Greg?" I snap out of my musings as Clara approaches me from behind and leans against the table with arms crossed. "You're spacing out again. Are you sure you're alright?"

"Yeah, I'm, uh. Fine." This was still weird.

She makes a low droning sound. "You're so out of it. Come on, ditch the plates – I'll do them when I wake up in the morning. Mom was a little bit harsh with you earlier, I feel a little bad so I'll allow you the treat of getting destroyed by me in your video game thingies. Cape Fighters. Best of Five."

My resistance crumbles. With any luck, Alice would be a lot more pliable by the morning anyway. "No items?"

"Of course not." She snorts. "I'll go set it up, I'm pretty sure I remember how to do that." She practically skips away.

Fifty minutes later, my ego is hurting. "There's no way." I swallow and lean forward.

"Bro, you suck!" On the screen, Narwhal does a mid-air pirouette on her shield before sending Eidolon off stage with a devastating down-kick.

"Narwhal is just overpowered-" I attempt to defend myself, ears burning as her character poses in a taunt.

"I just picked the first girl character I saw – shouldn't you be able to beat me as anyone?" Peels of laughter emerge from her mouth, so familiar and yet so very different from what I am used to. Friendly in a way I didn't think she was even capable of. "Face it. You're getting beaten by a girl."

And now she had taken a round off me at my own game. I was still winning overall, but I didn't think my ego was capable of sustaining another loss to a casual.

I grit my teeth. "Best of seven. No Narwhal. No Eidolon."

She makes a thinking pose. "Hmm. Alright. How about we go with that, but if you lose you have to concede once and for all that you got beaten by a girl. You've got to tell me to my face that I am superior to you in every way, especially in video games - and that you just suck at everything and want to be more like me in the future." Hint: Event (EVNT) modes can often be solved in ways that aren't always immediately obvious. Consider all of the knowledge and powers at your disposal as well as the victory conditions before committing to a plan of action!

"Useless." I grouse at the hint. I turn around, taking the step up to my bus before I can even make out the slowly reforming face of the driver.

The second challenge in, and I had already found myself a major stumbling block. I had nothing to hand that could actually protect me from a cloud of bugs, no powers that could do the same.

Sprinting away in a random direction was probably my best bet, I didn't know how fast bugs were compared to my fastest sprint but Taylor's range had to have a limit on it - and she clearly wasn't visible to me on the street at the time, so she already has to be in a building or car. That gives me an idea of which direction she might be coming from.

But that left the very open possibility of other pursuers, which I felt was implied by the wording of the task itself, and more to the point – I was not at all convinced that distance alone would save me thanks to the presence of the ZONE modifier to box me into a limited area.

I sigh. Offense might be better than defence in this case. Taylor was a lot of things, and one of them was squishy. If I could get a power that could give me a weapon and a way to reach her then I could dispose of her in seconds once I knew where she was.

Well, finding her at all would probably take a few failed attempts a day for a few days. I had... about twenty seconds between regaining control of my body and getting drowned in bugs? I didn't need to survive for long, just verify whether she was or wasn't in a specific area before dying painfully.

One attempt to check for her hiding among the cars, another attempt each per building. Maybe it would be easier to try and map out the limits of her range? I assumed it was a perfect circle, seeing how far the swarm chased me and mapping it out could give me a more precise area.

Hookwolf. Shadow Stalker. Rune. Circus. Maybe Battery if I could charge it during my scripted speech? Can Othala effect herself?

Even if not, that was plenty of options to get started on alone. All I actually needed was to get line-of-sight on them a few times a week until I managed to get past their first levels. I could cross the villains off of the list for now, apart from getting lucky with anyone going to school I was unlikely to run into any of them safely and consistently enough to be able to progress.

Rogues and mercenaries were probably off too. The only easily accessible one was Parian, and I don't think she would be particularly useful in this particular case. Not to say I wouldn't swing by at some point.

So. New Wave. The Wards. The Protectorate.

New Wave patrolled pretty regularly, I'm pretty sure I could find them if I kept an eye on the few cape forums that tracked their movements. Glory Girl played taxi for Panacea sometimes right? Might be able to catch her at a hospital if the news broke out fast enough, and that was excluding the possibility of just… walking to their house and peeking through the window.

The Protectorate didn't have any big events coming up as far as I knew. Maybe I could have a look at the next meet and greet session that they did, other than that I was stuck hoping to spot them on patrol somewhere.

The Wards were easier, but patrol schedules weren't public information. A few forums had reasonably accurate predictions, but I would have to have free time to go and find them. Might attract attention, especially if the government is keeping tabs on people trying to unmask the wards. Which I was, kind of.

New Wave then. Known residence. Known places of work. No worries about accidental unmasking. Very public. No thinkers watching over their shoulder. A plethora of viable targets that were likely to hand me some useful mover powers and a few offensive options.

And pretty much all of them were smoking hot. Sure, it would probably be a long time before I could get anywhere with any of them but a guy could dream right?

God yes, I could dream.

Ahem. Distractions.

I rounded out the bus trip home with a random but spirited murder attempt on the guy sitting directly in front of me. It turns out he's actually a boxer or something in his free time because I barely lasted for three seconds once I finally found him wandering the streets.

Unless I didn't learn them over the course of a year. I drum my fingers as I get a good idea for once. Uber. Victor. Skill trainer and skill stealer. Very, very viable... once I could find them.

I announce my entrance distractedly, already racing up to my room. I lost track of time after that, a half-dozen printouts of locations, times and potential patrols being stuffed into my bag before rushing out of the door again. Winslow high school finished quite a while before most businesses, which gave me an opportunity to make my way over to the Dallon household and… lurk in the area. Just to catch a glimpse of the capes returning from work and school.

I probably wouldn't catch Glory Girl easily, she might already be home if she flew. But my target this time around wasn't her, though I would definitely try if I could spot her. My target was the one member of the household that I could time my watch by. Someone I could easily catch sight of every day without fail thanks to her consistent schedule. Strong offensive options and a breaker-state for me to try and grab a knock-off copy of.

I whistle a jaunty tune to myself as I eye my watch. Ten minutes until she left the office. A short ten-minute drive after that. I didn't think it would be much more than a five-minute walk for me from where I am now, so I should have loads of time.

Brandish, here I come!

AN: No lewds? In a chapter almost 11k words long? Impossible, perhaps the archives are incomplete.

Anyway, this chapter goes a bit more into the system I have in mind. Some challenges will draw themselves from the past, most will be in the present, some from what would have been the canon!future, a few from the new!future and others will just be made up scenarios that never existed at any point. I do have an in-universe explanation for it to vaguely justify that, but the real reason is that I wanted Greg to be able to face off against characters at their peak while actually developing said characters in a different way. Khepri will never happen here, but I thought it would be fun to write Greg going "WTF" at the thought of having to beat her.

In addition, there's no real way to justify startofcanon!Taylor to be any trouble to him for long without making the challenge more about the modifier than it is about Taylor. Him rolling Taylor over before she gets any real experience would be a direction I could take the story, but I don't want this to be "easy" for Greg. He's got to earn his lewds - and that means eventually taking on Skitter and the gang in her prime. It means discovering that Glory Girl is actually a stand user. That a bloodlusted Panacea is the most dangerous cape in the bay.

Greg's powers will be pretty weak at first until he gets deeper into the challenges - and I opted for a bit of a limiter in terms of using multiple powers at once as well. He needs to concentrate on what power he's holding on to - as opposed to wielding every single power in the bay simultaneously.

Next chapter will be a chapter of stalking New Wave. Then the one after will be... taking on the Terrible Trio? Sounds good.

Finding a place to lurk isn't as easy as it seems. After arriving at the street and finding the Dallon's house, I scanned around for some kind of bench, seating area, cafe or even an alleyway that I could sit in and look unobtrusive. It had to be somewhere where I could reliably wait for a decent length of time every day, where it wouldn't be suspicious for me to be seen if I was noticed.

Unfortunately for me, the street is too clean and orderly for me to do that. Nowhere to stop and rest. No shops in sight of the house. No park, fountain or bench. Not even a convenient wall to rest against while pretending to wait for someone.

Nowhere to hide except inside a neighbouring house. Sneaking in wasn't a reliable thing to do regularly, the odds of getting caught eventually were too high.

But who said I had to sneak in like a thief? Why not just get invited inside?

The house next door has a busty red-head visible through the window.

KATARINA WURSTEN

SINGLE MOTHER 1/4

(REAL)

Come on power. Give me some easy ones. This would enable me to do some harder ones later, so it would balance out, right? "Challenge."

She takes a step back and looks towards a cupboard behind her. Probably for a weapon, I lunge straight for her - dragging her down to the floor before she can reach whatever she was going for.

She's no fighter. Not as scrappy as I am after my last few days of scrappy fist-fighting. My head rocks back from a well-aimed fist, but I don't allow myself to flinch or let up on the attack. I rain blow after blow on the woman, who is forced to give up on the offensive and attempt to shield her face from the increasingly debilitating hits.

She slumps backwards, no longer even responding to my attacks as she is blindly keeping her hands up in the air.

Single Mother 3/4

Maybe I'll leave this for later.

There's no conceivable reason why I would know anyone well in this area, and a shared history would almost be more suspicious than having absolutely none. Not that anyone would care to scrutinise it in this particular instance – but this scenario would surely happen again.

"Sure." I oblige her.

"Come in, come in." She calls over her shoulder as she walks through the house. "No point in standing out in the cold."

"Thanks." I step inside. "What did you need?"

"Oh, it isn't that much. I'm just doing some fundraising right now, and I've been making things to sell. Mostly cakes and cookies-" She babbles happily, eyes roaming up and down my body. That was convenient. "We've never met before, right?"

"Hm? Uh, well. No. I guess you think it looks a little bit weird just to invite someone in like that-" She looks a little crestfallen despite a strange glint of another emotion in her eye.

That was pretty weird. "That's not weird at all. I'd love to help."

She beams. "That's great!" Way too convenient to be a coincidence. Did I control the rewards?

No – I'd already gotten rewards that I wasn't happy about. It couldn't be just down to me. But now I was sure that there was something else that went into it depending on the situation – not just a blanket effect that happens to everyone. Which made sense, I suppose. It's not like my power could realistically fix my life's schedule in such a way that I had a previously existing relationship with everyone I challenged. I hadn't thought about it – a recurring theme that I had noticed. Still, I hadn't even had my powers for a week. I'll cut myself some slack there.

Let's work this out. I didn't need anything other than an attitude change going forward from this woman – same with the various gang members I had seen around Winslow. She still has a friendly, if not outright flirty attitude, but we're still meeting for the first time now. Was this a subconscious thought on behalf of my power, or was it simply that I had the unconscious ability to decline parts of rewards?

No. I was speculating. I couldn't make assumptions, not when making a mistake might get the truth of my power revealed and getting me sent off to the birdcage. In this instance, my power had given me exactly what I wanted. My gut feel was that my power had recognised what I had needed, realised that there weren't any major changes needed and had simply given me the space to interact with her in the way I had wanted – expending the least amount of effort needed to do so safely.

Wait, was that it? My family had all been maxed out in the space of about two days, with not much in the way of interaction between challenges. That's no time for a relationship to truly form, so once I had reached the upper levels, increasingly drastic changes had to be made to justify it. If I had spaced it out over several weeks, taking advantage of the attitude adjustments to sprinkle in some real memories – pushed some boundaries on my own – would there have been any need to invent a new past?

The vague idea felt correct. And perhaps this gave me a bit of hope that I could somewhat evade the Thinkers that I would eventually come up against. At least, while I was still getting myself set-up. I guess that most cape-challenges would naturally pace themselves – even if I wanted to max Taylor out this very second, I couldn't do it – I wasn't strong enough to manage it. That meant I would have days or weeks to interact with her, or anyone else, between levels in most cases. In high-school, relationships could begin, flourish and end in a week alone – a bit of interaction from me and things would seem perfectly natural from an outsiders view.

Assuming the most common student has four levels – which seemed to be the norm, a few had less – but not many had more. The first level of a normal student would only result in them talking to politely or being a bit flirty – that wasn't entirely unreasonable, on the face of it. The second would result in a more obvious show of interest, but no more than you saw on display around every corner of the high school – at least, not without me reciprocating. That level might not even require my power to have told them that we've interacted before – simply adjusting their feelings about me going forward would do the trick.

But if I did something unreasonable and went ahead to instantly convert someone all the way into, essentially, a loving sex-slave – then my power tries to smooth things out by telling the world that we've been on-and-off for months and that she has a submission fetish. Because that's the only way to explain Greg Veder, shut-in extraordinaire, having a hot, slutty girlfriend crawling over him in school.

But what about in a few weeks or a few months? When Greg Veder was a regular popular guy in school or a genuine hero in his cape-guise? An entire life-story didn't need to be rewritten to justify someone wanting to sleep with a rich person, a cape or the most popular guy in school. That happens naturally in real life, so with any luck, those drastic changes would be less readily apparent and have fewer holes in them once I become better known – simply because only the change in attitude would be necessary.

Again. Speculation. I undoubtedly had details wrong here.

But it was speculation I could at least partially check. I glance at the redhead's retreating back. No better time to test this out than the present. At the moment, she thinks we've never met before. I'm fairly certain she was checking me out at the door – but I don't think she's ready to go that much further than some flirting.

"Challenge." Let's see what I can do about that.

I wasn't going to rush. That was the worst thing I could do. Rushing was fine if I never intended to win in one go, but I had no intention of losing here. I was getting used to how this worked. No mistakes.

Time to take advantage of the fact that the backup was busy, and that there was no REAL or TIME modifier to screw with the idea of taking things at my own pace. Slowly, ever so slowly, I inch open the window and clamber out the back.

There were a few people around, unlike my previous forays into town when I was working through my family challenges. None of them seemed inclined to interact with me, however, and there were certainly fewer people than there should be.

What it doesn't stop me from doing is walking all the way home, grabbing my trusty axe from the shed and then walking back with it tucked away in a bag. Why it wouldn't let me keep my school bag for the challenge, I'll never know.

Getting back in through the window I left from is a considerably harder task than it was to leave, but ultimately I'm able to make it work by boosting myself up using a particularly sturdy bush to give me the height needed to grab the ledge. If I had thought about it, I should have hung a bedsheet out or something like that – like in all the prison-break movies.

A few seconds of scrambling up the wall later, I collapse into the room wheezing. Need more upper body strength. And lower body strength. And everything else too, if I'm at all honest.

I give myself a few more minutes to catch my breath. It's already been at least half an hour. What's one or two more?

Then I creep down the stairs. The TV is on, and it's loud. I'm not entirely sure where the TV is, but I can follow the sound easily enough.

The living room is already open when I arrive, Katarina is sprawled over an armrest clutching at half-a-dozen small cushions as the show plays out. She can't see me from this angle, so it's all too easy for me to plant my axe firmly into the side of her skull.

To my surprise, the world doesn't immediately start collapsing once Katarina takes the deadly hit. Instead, she twists in place to try and wrench the weapon from my hand, no hesitation to use the fact that it's lodged inside her as extra leverage in our brief tug-of-war. When she reaches up to the handle and starts to pull, I start sprinting back to the room I had started in, dashing inside the room as I spot the kid stumbling out of his room – entangled by cables and already screaming in rage. An agonised roar behind me indicates her success at retrieving the weapon – but I've already locked the door behind me and holed up inside the room.

The kid is already trying to ram the door, and the berserk woman will be here shortly as well – to try and batter down the door with the axe if nothing else. I shove some furniture in front of the door. This must be a spare bedroom of some kind, with the amount of crap left in here.

I had leapt down from the low-hanging roof above them, thrust my knife in a perfect line into the back of her neck – and then she had faded into a black pile of smoke that I passed through without resistance, until she reformed a second later in a position to effortlessly murder me via repeated applications of boot-to-face – shifting into smoke at every failed, desperate swipe with the knife that I make.

Cape.

Not just any cape. Shadow Stalker. The Ward.

…Taylor is going to be pissed when she finds out. Not yet though. The last thing I want is Winslow being drowned in a biblical plague of bugs and her being shunted off to the birdcage. I'll just… sit on that information for a while.

More importantly, I now knew a few things. Firstly, her power automatically kicks in when I stab her. Presumably not after every nick and scratch that she gets, but there was a threshold of damage that her power can detect and transform for her.

Secondly, she had no issues with abusing her power once it was revealed – and yet didn't use it at all in our first meeting. Why? Simple. The REAL modifier. When confronted with physical violence in school, the real Sophia wouldn't out herself if given the choice. Even if their sole purpose in life was to kill me, my enemies still stuck to their usual methods and tactics in a fight. Glory Girl didn't hang back throwing boulders at me, she rushed in and punched skulls like she did in real life. Panacea didn't lurk in dark corners to try and prod me unconscious from around the corner.

So with Sophia, actually rushing her head-on with all of her friends around limited her options until I showed myself as a cape or I was actually about to kill her – only because that is exactly how she would respond to real, physical violence at school.

Anyway, new information aside, that was a miserable failure. A little embarrassing, actually.

Which takes me to today. I sidle into the class a little later than usual. Heading over to sit next to Taylor at the back. "Challenge." I hiss it under my breath before reaching my seat.

This time, I take advantage of my fellow ABB gangsters. "Follow me!" I sprint forward, towards the group with the dogs. The ABB follows in my wake, slightly hesitant at first and then with far greater urgency as they notice the swarm rushing after us.

I round a corner. The only people on the street are either my enemies or my allies. No civilians. So naturally, anyone Taylor finds with her bugs is an enemy to chase.

She could clearly somewhat sense and direct her bugs at range, but could she see through them? By taking the rest of the gang with me and getting out of line-of-sight, she was now entirely reliant on whatever senses her bugs gave her. I lead the group down the street. "Split up! Go your separate ways! If you see anyone on a dog, shoot them!" I roar at the terrified men trailing behind me.

I subtly redirect a few bugs onto my other men, then focus on my bug sensing power some more. I just needed to find a spot… there! I sprint into an alleyway, past a few bugs that were clearly too small to warrant Taylor's interest. I smash my way through a window, getting through with only a few small traces of blood on the ledge.

There weren't any bugs in this room. Not even one. This was someone's house, or at least it would have been if other people were around. A few stray, uncollected bugs were at the edge of my range in the next rooms over – but there was nothing to find me in here. I whip off the curtains to cover the window I had broken into, then pull off my shirt to block the underside of the door connecting this room to the rest of the house.

Finally, I rush myself into what appears to be an empty, abandoned closet. I shut myself inside, curl up and prepare to wait out the rest of the challenge.

Heavy thuds outside the window draw my attention, and I still my breath for a moment. "…lling you, he's hiding in there." A girls voice. "Waiting for us."

A gruffer, heavier voice answers her. "This is Lung. Hiding is the last thing I expect of him."

"I don't like this either." Another male voice offers. "Ten bucks says he bursts out of the roof as a fifty-foot dragon and eats bug girl, and then us. Or us, and then bug girl. Or maybe both-"

"You don't understand! Something's wrong, this isn't what Lung does – something's different about him, about his power!" An element of frustration underpins her voice. "He'll just come after us lat-" She breaks off her sentence as a distant note reaches my ears. "Armsmaster."

"If he's going to lay low rather than chase us then that suits us fine. Leave it, Tattletale." The boy orders. "Let's get out of here before Oni Lee catches up. We're leaving. Bitch." Two sharp whistles precedes the sound of something heavy rushing against the walls, before heavy footfalls race away from my hideaway.

I hold my breath. No bugs to find me. They seem to be leaving. Armsmaster has no reason to find me here.

I fall through the floor, and let out a roar of satisfaction as I finally get the result I've been wanting for days.

SUCCESS

Reward: Taylor Hebert+​

I quieten down before I start to return to the real world. Don't want to draw that much attention to myself in the middle of class. Taylor glances up as I approach, not saying anything – but she does take the step of moving her bag and books out of the way of the seat next to her. That was as clear an invitation as I had ever gotten.

"Hey Taylor." I plonk myself down next to her. "How's life?"

"The same as it was yesterday." She sighs, sparing a glance towards the front of the class where a group of girls were glancing at us and giggling. A week ago, those giggles might have been more mean-spirited. I had beaten at least one challenge for a full half of those girls, and some of them I had cleared two. Even if I hadn't actually done anything to them, their opinion of me was a lot better than it was before my power.

But it was still fairly negative. Hanging around with Taylor was still a major social faux-pas in school. My reputation got dragged down by association, no matter how much it had improved.

Not that it mattered. Street cred could be acquired any time I got bored and had a target in sight. A top-tier waifu is forever.

"I am going to get them off your back one of these days." I inform her. "Just you wait."

She rolls her eyes. "I won't hold my breath." She doodles in her textbook for a moment. "You would be better off not sitting somewhere else, you know? All you're doing is making yourself a target as well."

I shrug, an easy grin coming to my face. "Sure, but if they're wasting time trying to get to me – then that's time that they can't use to get at you." I spread my hands. "Sharing is caring, Taylor."

"You're an idiot." She makes a point of not looking at me, struggling to maintain a scowl. "But thanks, I guess."

I wave her off. "What are friends for?"

She pauses for a moment. "…Right."

I mentally fist pump. We're totally friends. Proper friends. Not Tsun-friends.

The conversation lapses into a comfortable silence after that. The interest from the girls in front doesn't stop, but over the course of the lesson, I make it a point to clear off the first few challenges of some of the gossiping gang. Not much of a change in their behaviour for now, but that's how peer pressure works – I suppose.

The class clears off immediately once the lunch bell goes off, I'm one of the last to leave – only to find myself being pushed back through the door by Sophia Hess, flanked by Emma and Madison with similar scowls on their faces.

I cough. "Challenge." Before they can get out a word, I enter Sophia's challenge.

This time, I had another tool available to me and a better plan on how to use it. A straight-up fight suited me fine. Two minutes later, I walk through the cafeteria door without a fear in the world.

My most important asset was the REAL modifier. Even with the knowledge that her entire life's purpose was now to kill me, Sophia wouldn't out herself without cause. She wouldn't bust out her power just for a friendly neighbourhood scrap.

She spots me instantly, jumping up from her chair and sprinting towards me.

I don't try any fancy punches this time – just a massive grapple attempt. She makes me regret the idea instantly, of course, a devastating knee to the stomach – and if this was a pure fistfight that would have been the end of it. But she doesn't know that I have a variant on Panacea's power. For a moment, my arm comes into contact with her face and stays there. Not a punch, just a gentle grasp against her face that she ignores in favour of punching me again – a repeated, devastating impact that saps my breath with every hit.

I deliver my instructions to my power, feeling the change at work. It's a tiny change, on the face of it. Not too different from sealing a basic cut, or turning someone's skin blue. A tiny change with a vast effect. It's only a few seconds later when she turns away from punishing my exposed body to shoving me away as fast as she can. She disappears into smoke and backsteps across the table, reforming with a silent scream.

I glance up with a bloody grin, spitting out blood onto the floor as students fled the room. I was bruised all over from my brief time in that scrap, but somehow I had come out of it better off.

Sophia's face is a mess. Sealing her lips and nostrils together had taken mere seconds, and my last, spiteful claw at her face had put my fingers right over her left eye for a fraction of a second. Eyes are delicate things. It doesn't look like I was able to blind her entirely, but she's definitely got problems of some sort based on how she is struggling to focus on me. A fly dive-bombs into her good eye, causing her to flinch back as I grab the bug-power again for the split-second it takes to switch control to another minion and give it identical orders.

I throw a discarded tray at her, it misses entirely – but she fades into smoke anyway. I lunge across, going for another grapple – she catches my wrists easily, then drops me a moment later with a pained hiss as I try my best to cross as many muscles and veins into each other as possible in her hands and wrist. I don't seem to be able to just open up cuts wherever I go. It's like I'm only allowed to ease things into a slightly different shape or form. Whatever the case, the brief amount of time I had clearly isn't enough for me to really effect things under her skin.

She backs away as I approach. She bumps into a table, then comes up clutching a knife in her hands. That doesn't matter. She doesn't need a knife to be a threat to me. Nothing has really changed.

I blink as blood sprays from the black girl, immediately followed by a pained gasp for air and a spurt of blood. "Did-" I shake my head as the black girl screams, wrenching her knife further through the thin film that was all I had been able to do to bind her lips together. "Did you just stab yourself a new mouth?" I grimace at the bleeding hole in the otherwise blank area where her lips should be. "That's gross. Metal, but gross."

"Fuck off, dickwad." Her breathing is making a funny noise through that hole, and despite the fact that it's disgusting I can't help but grin at the nasal pitch of her voice. "We'll see how well you laugh off a crossbow bolt."

She disappears into smoke, streaking towards the exit over the tables as I pursue. It's a hopeless effort to try and catch-up, so after a moment I double-back instead. She was going to get a weapon, I was going to get to a safer position.

I decide to make my stand in the half-open janitors closet underneath the stairs. A disused storage area. Some open corridors in between discarded walls of packages, boxes and a variety of well-used cleaning machines of some description. Small, cramped conditions suited me far better than her. All I had to do now was wait for her to find me.

She does find me first. Unfortunately, she doesn't subscribe to the idea of joining me in the room straight away. No. The first sign I have that she's found where I am is when a crossbow bolt materialises inside my left shoulder – if I had been facing a different direction, I would be dead now.

I don't scream, or give any acknowledgement that I've been hit. The most immediate concern is that she shouldn't be able to see me. There are no windows and she shouldn't be able to see through walls. I rest one hand against the door, wrestling with the bolt in my shoulder before giving up. Not a tranquiliser, which would have worked far better at taking me out in one shot. I had a chance against real bolts.

Another bolt sails over my right hand and I jump away, mind racing. That was a clear miss. Why? She clearly can't see me if that was a real attempt, was the first time just a fluke.

I need to test this. Even if I die. I drop down and lie flat on the ground, shaping myself like a pencil perpendicular to Sophia's angle. A second later, my hands are grazed by a passing bolt.

My hands again. I push myself to my feet, putting my right hand on the doorknob and stretching my body as far away from it as I could manage. Not a moment too soon, as another bolt sails through where any normal person would have been standing if they were trying to open the door.

My hands. She can see my hands. Proximity to the walls? No, she saw me the first time – right in the middle of the room. Not my hands. I stare at my hands for a moment, then I swear. Not my hands – but my watch. Some tinkertech bullshit. She can see the metal. Or the electricity. Something like that. I drop the watch to the floor and scramble upwards onto a pile of discarded boxes next to a shelf of blinking lights.

One bolt speeds across the floor. Two bolts. Three bolts. All sail through the spot where I would be if I was lying down. I grin. That's it.

After a few more shots, the bolts stop coming. Limited ammo, I would guess. If she was smart, she would back off and get more. Or call the PRT if that was an option. But that didn't seem like Sophia. I had hurt her. Pissed her off. It was personal for her now.

So when her shadowy form starts to eke through the door, I'm already flying through the air from above to land on top of her. She's shoved her usual hockey mask on, but not her full costume. I land a heavy punch against the mask, attempting to find exposed skin with my other before she erupts back into smoke – almost instantly appearing in a standing position behind me and connecting with a downwards kick. I grab the foot, only to feel it slip through my grasp once again.

I roll away as another kick goes wide, her gaze follows my general movement for a second as she lunges again – missing me by miles. She scowls as she rips off the hockey mask, one good eye briefly inspecting the cracked goggles above them. "Useless thing." Her voice still has the nasal tint to it as her deformed face twists in anger. "Don't need it to deal with you." With her next kick, she doesn't miss – leg phasing through my attempted block and reappearing an inch from my face. I roll head over heels backwards, moving with the motion to gain some distance.

Got to touch her. No bugs in here that can fly. Stupid. Should have grabbed one and taken it with me. I'm bleeding a bit from my shoulder, but I still feel fine. Touch her. Touch her. How do I lock her down? It seems impossible, now that she knows what I can do. If there is even a slight threat from me then she can fade away and reposition.

So she needs to make a mistake. I push myself to my feet as she saunters forward. It's a small room. Little more than a storage cabinet for the various cleaning machines and chemicals around. I make my way to the door.

And hit the lights.

The room plunges into pitch darkness. I rush forward,

I collide with her messily, before she effortlessly shifts again and plants her foot in my stomach as I fall. I scramble back up and grab her again, attempting to toss her sideways. She shifts again – this time landing a punch into my side with a mocking laugh at my attempts to reach her.

Impossible. I leap at her again, hands flailing for anything to hit her with from the shelves. I swing without thinking, dragging a shelf down onto her and me together. I feel her shift again as I shove the falling debris away from me, but I can't miss the flash and crack of electricity behind me – nor the sizzling of burning flesh that fills my room as an agonised, keening cry fills the roam.

I turn to stare as the crackle of electricity fades to briefly illuminate a burnt, very-much-solid Shadow Stalker still under a small pile of cables and appliances. Some switches and computers that had been left on and hidden on the shelf instead of tucked away in a network cabinet somewhere. I didn't know what they were used for or why they were here – perhaps some old signage machines? Something to manage the network upstairs? Manage the WiFi?

The light quickly fades again, but I take the opportunity to jam my hand into the spot where her face was. I can feel her try to shift again, only to be ejected with another hiss of burning flesh.

No going through electricity? I can work with that. My hands grapple against her face, she doesn't – or perhaps can't – shift away, so she tries to bite me instead. Fortunately, that's nearly impossible given the current state of her face in general – leaving me for a brief moment unopposed with a full hand covering her face. I fuck up her other eye first. A mirror of what I did to the first one, a swift and easy change to permanently blind her. She kicks away once, twice at the boxes before fading away backwards through the opposite wall successfully before the active devices and cables could fall back onto her.

I back away. I know that she has some kind of sense of things in her cloud, even if she was blind now. I didn't want to fuck this up now.

I creep around the room, no longer able to see her. Somehow I manage to make it back to the doorway unscathed, flicking the light back on to see what I had to work with.

With the room well lit, it's easy to spot the dark cloud in the dead centre of the room. I watch her for a moment, watching as she briefly switches back to breathe in again before shifting back and staying in that state.

She can't leave. She doesn't know where the door is, or whether there are wires in the walls. She only knows that where she is now is safe. She knows I'm here, and that I'll easily take her out if she tries to blindly feel her way out. I take a step forward as she shifts back, and her face snaps towards me as she makes a leaping kick in my general direction. No danger of hitting me, she lands painfully into a stack of chairs, briefly shifting into smoke and back to manage her landing.

I back up to the pile of fallen debris, prompting her to make another lunge towards me as she follows the sound of my movement. I throw a computer at her, only for her to phase through without noticing. I cut off my muttered swear as I notice the absent power cable, lost beneath my feet.

But still – she has to shift into her shadow state to beat me in close quarters. She's blind. She can shift freely as a wraith to beat me, but only when she knows that her power will cover me to give her some awareness of where I am.

She halts her advance as I stumble back onto the pile of debris. Back in her human form, she slowly probes the pile, throwing pieces to the side as she works through it towards me.

Not much time. I race to the nearest powered device, uncoiling the cable that had been tucked down the back of the shelf to hide it from view. It was easily long enough to give me enough to form a solid loop or three around my arm with some more slack, without uncowering the computer itself.

So when Sophia finally reaches me – I swing the computer overhead at her, which she predictably dissipates into smoke to avoid. The slight blip of static the only sign that the device actually grazed her shadow state before she dodged. When she then attempts to rush forward to engulf me in her shadow, she runs straight into the live power cable coiled around my arm – collapsing into a screaming, burning mess once more. I coil the slack of the cable around her neck while she is stunned, then retrieve the original computer and bring it smashing down onto the bridge of her nose.

She screams, attempts to shift and then screams some more as burns continue to spread across her body – now plainly visible on her face as blood spurts from her nose. Must not have been a very good hit, I was sure that would kill her. I swing again. And again. And then I swing through empty air – my heart stopping for a moment before I realise that it's just my victory and not her power at work.

SUCCESS

Reward: Shadow State (1)
​
I roll back on the blank, empty floor of the void. I'm exhausted. More so than most of my challenges to date. I can see why she's one of the more respected wards in terms of combat ability now. Her weakness to electricity aside, she's all but invincible to most threats save for her own attitude.

"Fuck you Sophia." I shake my head, waiting for the screen to fade and reality to resume its course.

"-king to you. Are you even listening?" Emma's face fills my vision.

Sophia closes the door firmly behind them. "We need to talk."

I fail to disguise my groan. I've had enough Sophia for today. Is this how Taylor feels all the time? A heeled foot stomps down onto mine as Madison grabs my bag and starts flicking through it, apparently on a whim. All the while, Sophia presses me further back against the desk. Right. This must be how Taylor feels all the time.

I spread my hands nervously, idly hoping to distract Madison from finding the hidden compartment with the more… cultured literature in my collection. "Alright then ladies. You have my attention." I let out a grin, eyeing up all three of their open, available challenges. "So. Let's talk."



AN: I was hoping to get this out last week, but I got distracted. Repeatedly. Story of my life, really.
