#364
I might not be the sharpest knife in the drawer sometimes, but it doesn't take a genius to work out that the only reason for the Trio to approach me alone has something to do with me hanging around Taylor. The specifics of exactly why they were bothered about me now was still a mystery though. I've been hanging around her for months – was it just that Taylor was responding more positively now, which ticked them off enough to do something about it?

Or, from their perspective, perhaps we've been this friendly for weeks or months – making an intervention from them well overdue. It doesn't particularly matter either way – the end result is the same. A month ago I would probably have been almost wetting myself at the possibility of a beating from Sophia, but in reality, they were just trying to scare me, and I wasn't that concerned about my well-being.

I mean, really. This was an incredibly one-sided confrontation when you thought about it. At worst they would hurl some particularly vicious words and perhaps a stray punch or three at me – while I, on the other hand, had been given a perfect chance to drag them one step closer to servitude. Perhaps I would be successful today, perhaps not. Either way, the simple act of being in my presence gave my power some background to work with when it came to smoothing out the history between us.

Sophia crosses her arms, looking as confident and cocky as ever. "We're here to talk about your choice of friends."

"Oh?" I spread my hands wide, flicking my eyes over their open challenges to remind myself of what I was facing. "Which ones?"

Madison Clements

Schoolgirl 2/4

(GANG) (TIME)​

Probably the easiest of the lot with my new powers. A bunch of civilians guarding Madison. No real trouble.

Emma Barnes

Schoolgirl 2/4

(EVNT) (HUNT)​

This one was a lot more possible now than it was before. The scenario was just a mugging gone wrong that I have to survive. Except that I have the equivalent of a tracking beacon on me and they will pursue me to the ends of the Earth if they have to. Now that I have some powers that indirectly help with combat – I should be able to manage this within a few tries as well. The exact logistics of stealing a knife and then coming out of a 1v4 as the victor was something that I still needed to work on, but I would manage it eventually.

Sophia Hess

Vigilante 2/6

(EVNT) (CONT)​

I conceal my frown, the description for the Ward had changed this time around. I'm positive it was "Schoolgirl 1/6" last time. Did it change relative to my perception of her? Or is it a more specific name for her next challenge. I would expect a name like "Heroine" or "Ward" if it was tied purely to my perception, so perhaps the latter was more likely.

Ignoring that change, I haven't attempted this level yet. EVNT modifiers tend to give me scenarios that are very different from the usual deathmatches that I get. I would have to wait and see what I could do with this one. CONT… I don't remember ever seeing a modifier like that before. I guess I was going to learn something new today at least.

Madison smirks, drawing my attention back to the conversation. "Don't act like you have enough friends for that to be a real question. You know we're talking about Hebert."

My faint smile drops slightly. Rude. Evidently, rushing through challenges with a few of my other classmates hadn't done much to change my reputation around the school. Not yet, at least. "What about her?" I bring my hand up to cover my mouth as my eyes meet Madison's. "Challenge." I whisper it into my hand, I doubted anyone would read too much into the word – but there was no sense giving Shadow Stalker questions if she was ever to investigate my cape side in the future.

The world fades away, replaced once again with Madison's challenge. Like Emma with her alleyway, Madison seemed to have a theme. People. Social networks. Parties. Fighting large numbers of grunts to get to the queen bee. This challenge had already foiled me before, but I was a lot stronger now than I was back then.

I don't rush through the door quite yet though. Before I got started, now would be a good time for me to test out my newly-acquired power.

I grasp hold of the mental cube in my mind's eye that represented the power I got from Sophia, and to my surprise, it doesn't wait for me to try and control it – it simply activates itself the moment I select it. A black cloud erupts around me as I wave around my phantom limbs, appearing only as indistinct movements within the black fog. A second or so later, the power wriggles out of my mental grasp as I collapse back into reality. I try to grab it again, yet fail to get a proper grip and select it again.

It must have some kind of cooldown. That would make sense, both of the other powers that I had earned so far had been significantly reduced or changed from their original owners. It made sense that this one was the same. A relatively short, fixed duration on the shadow state before it kicks me out, and then it also has some internal cooldown before I can use it again. The weakness to electricity is probably still there, and I don't seem to be able to selectively apply the effect as freely as Shadow Stalker does. It's still extremely useful. I'll just have to clear more of Sophia's challenges to upgrade it over time.

The power solidifies again in my mind, I tap it and find myself encased in shadow once more. The cooldown wasn't too long, short enough to justify using it early and often rather than saving it for the 'boss'. Stalling for a few seconds over the course of a fight wasn't a huge problem against normal opponents. Serious capes might just kill me in that downtime, but I wasn't facing them yet.

Which meant that I could use it against the civilians standing between Madison and I without any issue. I wait for it to become available again and then barrel through the doorway, attracting the attention of the entire room in the process. I don't dare to stop moving, fully aware of how painful being torn to shreds by an angry mob is by now. I duck past a right hook and make straight for the stairway. Two boys step into my path, but I slip straight through them in my shadow state – sprinting up the stairs without any more obstacles left to get past. On the second flight of stairs, I glance back down behind me, sure enough, the guests were practically clawing at my heels in their haste to reach me. Madison wasn't among them as far as I could tell.

Which was all according to plan. I had noticed on my last two attempts that this version of Madison was more than happy to stand back or even outright retreat to safety while her friends mobbed me. This crowd didn't seem terribly realistic compared to others that I had seen. They moved as a single unit, all mindless fury and no independent thought.

So, when I reach the top floor, I simply wait for them to catch up and surround me. I don't make any attempt to escape, merely pacing around the furniture to grant myself a few more seconds for more people to reach this floor.

And then I activate my shadow state and slip through the floor.

I barely make it past the ceiling of the bottom floor before my physical body forcibly reasserts itself. Sophia's ability allows me to reset my momentum pretty quickly, even if outright gliding with it like she does is still beyond me – allowing me to land on my feet with little more than a light ache from the impact. I should count myself fortunate. I was half expecting to fall straight into a bunch of electrical cables going through the floors, but it looks like today is my lucky day.

I turn and grin at the only other occupant of the room. Madison Clements, in the flesh. I didn't have long. The mob upstairs would be coming back down once they fight their way through the crowd still going up. She waves a knife at me as I sprint towards her, but it's clear she has no idea how to use it. I slam my hand against hers, ignoring the bite of steel and the rush of blood as I grasp the blade firmly.

My shoulder slams into her frame at full force, pinning her against a cupboard as she reels from the impact, her momentum slamming her head back against the hardened wood. She's still clutching on to the knife, but can't employ it while my bleeding, ruined hand is holding it in place despite her efforts to twist it away. My forehead smashes into her nose. My knee flies into her stomach. My other hand encircles her neck and slams her head back and forth once, twice and then hurls her to the floor – only now releasing my grip on the blade. Not that it helps her in the slightest, she's not in any coherent state to fight any more.

My foot smashes down onto her weapon hand, her fingers making painful cracks as the blade skitters away. I can hear shouting from behind me, but it's already too late. I retrieve the knife and make a simple, clean motion towards her neck before diving out of the window in my shadow state to escape the first attempted tackle from the angry guests.

I stand in the garden for a moment, watching curiously as the mob spills out of the house towards me. The knife probably wasn't one that I would use – but I had a pretty good idea of how effective they were these days. Just a few moments longer, and that would be the end of it.

As if in response to my musing, the world disappears into nothing.

SUCCESS

Reward: Madison Clements+
​
Nice. That should turn things a little in my favour. I frown as the world starts to reform. It is tempting to continue onto the next challenge immediately, but perhaps it was better to take things slow? Nobody had noticed any changes yet, but then I hadn't interacted with such a tight-knit group yet. A few minutes later, I hear the teacher's voice rise above the chaotic sound of tapping keys and mouse clicks. "Taylor Hebert! Stay behind at the end of the lesson and we'll talk about what we should and shouldn't be browsing the internet for during class."

I very, very deliberately don't turn around to acknowledge the burning glare at the back of my head from the other side of the room as the class titters at the scolding. That was not my fault. I am not responsible for her tech-illiteracy.

That wasn't the only reason I didn't turn around. Something on my own screen had caught my eye: A notification on one of my watched PHO topics.

Tickets now on sale for Wards Meet and Greet!

We are pleased to confirm that the final batch of tickets for the upcoming "Meet Your Heroes!" fundraising event has now been released. Up to four of Brockton Bay's young Wards will be in attendance at the event – alongside veteran heroes Armsmaster and Triumph. Exclusive Cape memorabilia will be available at… [read more]​

A wide grin splits my face. Perfect timing.


I pass my ticket to the doorman on the way in, struggling to contain my grin as they scan my belongings. These PR events were usually incredibly dull outside of the initial surprise of seeing a certain hero in real life – they only ever got interesting when a new hero or Ward was announced and one of these was their first event, but even then most people would just watch the highlights on PHO if anything funny happened.

All of that meant that the entire event just turned into a regular old party, with a set of speeches on one end of the show and a constant stream of refreshments, music and dancing on the other. The heroes were the guests of honour, of course – spending most of the night surrounded by admirers until they withdrew to the relative safety of the VIP section, where all the top donors were invited in case they wanted a conversation longer than ten words.

My sister was technically escorting me – but she had already run off ahead to the bar to take advantage of the free drinks with a fake ID, which left me to move around at my own pace and find all of my targets hidden in the crowds. Drawing any of them into a conversation was nearly impossible out here, and even getting within touching distance was a tough ask between the semi-rabid fans and the tight security around them.

But I didn't need that. Even just a moment of line-of-sight would be enough, and then I could just go and find some dark corner of the room to whip out my phone to kill time – then hopefully come back for round two once the cooldown timers wore off.

"Greetings!" My eyes light up as my first target appears. Clearly, there is some sort of schedule for one of the Wards to be assigned to greet new arrivals at all times – because based on his stance, this usually-jovial Ward looks like he would rather be anywhere else right now. "The main event is just down the hall, as you can probably tell by all the signs pointing that way. I'm sorry I can't do autographs right now, as I have been assigned the extremely critical task of being a signpost. Rest assured that I shall soon be free and available to grace you all with my magnificent presence in the main hall in just a few short minutes."

CLOCKBLOCKER

Hero 1/6

(LUST)​

"I'll look forward to it." I murmur. Of all the powers I wanted from the Wards, it was his and Vista's that I wanted the most. Both tinkers were all but useless to me in my simulations, flight was fairly common and the various brute powers were nothing too special in the grand scheme of things.

That wasn't the case with these two. High-tier powers that often terrorised the Versus threads on PHO – but more than that, would greatly complement my own challenges. Clockblocker's power alone would turn a single touch on an opponent into a death sentence – I could hang a frozen opponent, get in position to cut their throat, handcuff them to a wall, surround them with even more frozen items…

Too many ideas. Too much synergy. But I need to actually acquire the power first.

I start to walk past him as he attempts a pick-up line on the girl behind me.

Time to die, Clockblocker.

"Challenge."

#431
"Challenge"

I patiently wait for the new level to load. I didn't know what the LUST modifier did, but I felt that it was probably a safe bet that it wasn't anywhere near as fun as it sounded. I had a vague recollection of a previous hint threatening to apply it for failing some condition or other. Still, I didn't have any experience of it directly as of yet.

I frown and look around at my surroundings as they form. What I had initially confused for a tiny room was actually an elevator, the last trickle of colour fills in the finishing touches of detail to my surroundings to reveal the lit-up buttons on my right as I realise that I was already in motion.

As if in response to my discovery, the elevator slows to a crawl and opens its doors – giving me a completely unobstructed view across the room to where Clockblocker, wearing his trademark white costume, sat alone in front of the TV. I stare at him. He stares at me.

He rushes to his feet as I swear, ducking out of the elevator as he begins his sprint towards me. "There goes my prep-time." I mumble to myself, already working overtime to think of a solution to dealing with a fully-costumed Clockblocker chasing after me. I had been hoping to catch him unawares, but with that option gone, I would have to experiment with what I could do.

The odds were good that touching him meant death – even if I was only held up for a short time, he could easily chain-freeze me while he set up a lethal trap or found a deadly weapon. That rendered Panacea's touch-based power useless. Taylor's had some minor use as a distraction to enemies with exposed faces – but it wouldn't do anything to Clockblocker's costume unless he took it off for some reason. Sophia's power was honestly the most useful – letting me briefly slip out of any of those dangerous situations before he could touch me, and potentially even after. The only downside was that I strongly suspected this was home territory for the Ward – an isolated base out in the Bay with two tinkers was bound to be brimming with electricity. Attempting to go through the walls would be risking death on each occasion, but if I was forced to it, then it remained an option.

All of that left me with very few options for actually killing the Ward. Aside from the protection from his costume, he wasn't a Brute – he would die if I hit him with something that would kill a baseline human. The only issue was that I had nothing that could hit him at range, and trying to hit him in melee would just let him freeze the weapon and probably break my hand in the process.

I barrel down the stairs as fast as I can, I'm not quite as athletic as he is, but I do have one notable advantage. His costume, while not particularly clunky, doesn't provide quite the same flexibility as my plain-clothes outfit that was so helpfully provided by my power. Not that I wouldn't swap that flexibility for some light armour like his in a heartbeat – but there's nothing I can do about that.

I spare a glance upwards as I notice the conspicuous absence of his footsteps on the flight above me, only to be treated to the decidedly unwelcome sight of Clockblocker vaulting the railing and plummeting down to my level in seconds. Instead of continuing to plummet through the gap between each flight of stairs, he pulls on the suddenly-rigid and unmoving sheet of paper in his hand – which had been gently curled inwards to cup his palm, forming an easy handhold for him to use without cutting himself. His downwards momentum turns into a powerful sideways swing after the limited number of flights that I had managed to gain with my lead.

If I had been watching it at home from PHO, I would have applauded the move as something straight out of an action-movie. I wasn't at home. And as his momentum starts to transfer into his opening attack, I realise that I don't have a chance of dodging both his initial kick rising towards me and then his landing immediately afterwards. I let out a snarl of frustration as his boot lashes out at my chest a split-second from brushing against my shirt-

Death.

-and then passing harmlessly through the wispy cloud of smoke I explode into. He lands awkwardly on the stair, nursing his arm but already rising to chase my fleeing shadow. If going down the stairs isn't going to buy me some distance, then perhaps going up them will. The thought does occur that perhaps entering the stairway wasn't the optimal choice – but I wasn't exactly overflowing with options at the time. Perhaps on the next attempt, I would have better luck diving past him and rushing through some closed door – I could at least hold it closed against him while I planned out something better.

I dash up the stairs two at a time, with Clockblocker dangerously hot on my heels. A barely visible shimmer in the air causes me to lurch to the side, narrowly avoiding a razor-thin string that had clearly been left behind on his way down. When did he even find the time? I charge forwards again, seeking to gain a few more inches of distance before the Ward caught up with me. Somehow, I manage to last the two flights of stairs that it takes before my shadow-state returns without being tagged. I immediately use it to pass through the closest exit out of the stairwell without opening the heavy door – then sprinting across to the far side of the room towards the window overlooking the Bay.

I hear the door being shoved open behind me, but it's a heavy door that kills his momentum entirely. I had plenty of time. It would take Clockblocker more than a few seconds to cross the room into melee range-

As if to punish the thought, I feel something wrapping around my leg. I turn my head to see Clockblocker with one arm extended – a lengthy line of cord projected from his glove to my leg. I swear crassly as my leg locks up as if I had just run into a wall made of barbed wire – except that even barbed wire would have some give in it before it slowed you to nothing. I let out a choked scream as the wire slices into my leg as my velocity is cut to zero instantly. Even ignoring my now-lacerated thigh, I'm positive that I just broke my leg. I can't even fall properly with my leg locked at such an awkward angle. Even after I manage to get my other leg to support my weight, I'm still forced to hold my broken and bleeding one in position to prevent it from opening up even more wounds for me to bleed from.

I mentally paw at Shadow Stalker's cooldown-gated power in increasing desperation as Clockblocker sprints across the room. Any moment now. Any moment- Now! I barely dodge Clockblocker's touch – but now that I know that he can catch me over open ground with his cord, I need to gain distance in another way. A risky way. I phase through the floor.

Or at least, I try to. A split-second later I rebound out of it, lightning coursing through my body as what feels like a hundred tasers apply themselves to every part of my body simultaneously. I deliriously try to push myself up and lurch into a backwards dodge, keenly aware of the white costume in the corner of my vision reaching out to touch m-

-e. I feel gravity take a grip on me as the room seems to teleport, my feet light up in pain a split second before the rest of my body sends the same signal. Suddenly more aware, I take a moment to take in my surroundings through the pain to try and work out what happened.

He touched me. Froze me in time, and then… what? I glance downwards to try and analyse the screaming signals of pain from the rest of my body, almost immediately halted by a dangerously thin wire by my chin that threatens to draw blood. It isn't the only one, around every limb multiple wires have been strapped around me – and the buzzing coming from the large one around my waist tells me that he's recognised Shadow Stalker's power and its weakness. I'm still at the awkward angle of my failed dodge, only held upwards in the air by a multitude of crisscrossing wires digging harshly into my back and my other suspended limbs. Instead of overtly moving, I slide my eyes down instead.

Glints in the air draw my attention, different to the near-invisible strings – small, indistinct objects floating like grains of sand in between the spiders-web of lethal lines. I can't move my arm – but I brush one of my fingers up against them, which promptly comes away slick with blood. Shredded paper. Tiny bits of it that would cut me to ribbons if I tried to pass through it – at least, whatever bits of me that weren't already cut to ribbons by the wire. With how minuscule some of these pieces were – I wouldn't be surprised if running into one would cause it to pierce through me like a tiny spear or a bullet.

I feel a tug from behind, yanking me backwards against the razor-thin wires and eliciting a fresh scream from my throat. I ignore the new wounds that the movement causes me. What pulled me? Another cord? No. Something thicker and sturdier.

I can't use my shadow-state here without running into the electrical wires wrapped firmly around my chest. If I could look down or move properly, I might be able to cut those wires using the frozen ones – but even the slightest movement threatened to slice me up even more. The only reason I had stopped falling was that the objects below my feet and back had penetrated to my bones with the help of gravity, and then mercifully stopped there – supporting my entire body weight while lodged inside me.

Another light tug draws my attention. Seeing as I don't see any way to get out of this on my own, I might as well see what Clockblocker's plan is from here. I jerk my head to the side in a fast, decisive movement. My mouth floods with the taste of copper as my cheek is sliced open. Unfortunately, I can't even consider moving any further for fear of yet another wire directly in front of my eye. I try to ignore the unmoving, miniature blade of paper pressing against my tongue as I take in as much info as I can.

My movement is just in time to see Clockblocker emerge from the elevator as it attempts to close behind him, the shadow of something large being left behind as the door closes. I don't realise the plan until the strings of cord leading into the elevator snap taught as the elevator starts to move and the pulling sensation on my limbs resumes, this time at a strength a full order of magnitude greater.

I'm not sure when I start to scream. When Shadow Stalker's power activates and instantly fails, sending an ungodly amount of electricity into my twitching body? When the full weight of the elevator and its contents forces my body through a literal blender, puncturing dozens of tiny holes through my torso and slicing my skin to ribbons? When I hit the ground, still being dragged backwards – and look up to see that I've left well over a full half of my body behind on the spider's web of wire, flesh and blood?

The elevator only stops when my head meets the closed doors and refuses to go further. If I still had lungs, or a functional neck, or any coherent thought other than pain – I would have said some lame pun or joke at my current situation. But as it is, it's all I can do to pray for my all-too-slow death to come a bit faster.

Clockblocker doesn't make a move towards me. He doesn't need to – I'm already dying. As far as he is concerned, the only chance he has to lose is if I nail him with a surprise attack at the last second – I don't have anything like that, but he's prepared for the possibility. It's a very un-Clockblocker thing to do. The method of attack. The lack of banter. The practically torturous process of execution.

And I'm absolutely positive that it's because of the new modifier. This Clockblocker will stop at nothing to kill me, using his powers in a way he would usually never even consider. In every other event so far people have fought much like I would expect them to. Taylor didn't kill everyone within her range indiscriminately, only attacking me when she detected it was specifically me. Shadow Stalker still acted like a student that was concerned about her secret identity when she was at school. Glory Girl went straight to her usual punching instead of waiting outside to throw a car at me or something. A normal Clockblocker would have frozen me and let me wake up inside containment foam, after which I may or may not have been killed immediately – but the point was that his fighting style would have been normal, if perhaps more lethal for me than most people.

I was reminded of a speculation post that I once made on PHO. Clockblocker on an aeroplane. He freezes the guy next to him, and suddenly everyone behind him gets struck by an effective missile travelling at 500 miles an hour which destroys the plane and kills everyone on it. Everyone had ridiculed the idea because Clockblocker is a nice Ward and wouldn't do that. But the idea behind it was sound – and that was the type of Clockblocker I was looking at here. One who would do literally anything in his power to win.

A true Deathbattle modifier.

Bloodlust.

FAILURE​

I draw in a deep breath the moment I finally die, filling my lungs with more air than I actually need thanks to the instant reset of my body. I've never quite gotten used to that sensation, especially in my more grisly deaths. The one's where I'm knocked unconscious somehow, or take a knife wound that kills in seconds, or where I just instantly die – those are my favourite deaths.

The fact that I could spend my last moments counting the body parts that were pulled in different directions across the wires was something that I hadn't particularly enjoyed. Although, I was admittedly thankful that after my head and upper torso detached from the rest of my body, I just lost all sense of pain from below my neck. An itchy feeling of loss was infinitely preferable to feeling everything from the parts of my body fortunate enough to still be attached. That wasn't to say that the chunk of my skull missing or the two separate holes through my throat weren't painful, but it could have been worse – I could have been feeling the absence of the organs I was trying to name on the debris I left behind me.

I say it could have been worse, but not much worse. That was vicious. Easily top three in my Most Painful Deaths list. Maybe even higher. Only a few short days later, being devoured inside out by a biblical plague of bugs already has stiff competition!

Hint: Rock. Paper. Scissors. Some powersets make it far easier to trump others, consider your enemies weaknesses – and consider going after their counter first!​

"Just get a blaster power." I sneer at the hint. Apparently, that last useful one was a fluke. "It's so easy. It's so obvious. Just get one!" And of course, a less supernatural option was forbidden to me thanks to my powers insistence on outfitting me without any equipment of my own. Not to mention the unnatural string of events that tended to plague me every time that I put an earnest effort into acquiring a gun in these challenges. "Just win the lottery!" I clamp down on my complaints as reality starts to reassert itself.

"Sorry, just going to squeeze past young man…" I absently sidestep as someone brushes past me. I shudder as colour settles back into my vision. I focus on Clockblocker and the timer next to him. Three hours between each attempt. Longer than most for the first round, but the event should last for just over four hours – assuming everyone stayed to the end, I could get two attempts for everyone without any trouble.

Hopefully, not everyone would be as brutal as Clockblocker. I didn't even mind the violence as much now that it was behind me, but the worst part is that I still didn't have a plan to beat him. He's faster than me, can catch me from range if he has line-of-sight, is deadly at melee, can lay traps, has a near-perfect physical defence, has the home-turf advantage which also helps nullify one of my own powers and also has a completely sealed costume that neutralises two of my others.

I can't beat him right now. In an ideal world, I would beat someone else present at this event and then come back for him – but I had no guarantee that those people would be any easier, or even that they would give me a power good enough to win with.

I continue down the corridor towards the main event. My targets are easily visible on arrival, which makes sense considering this entire event is about them being visible and trying to show everyone how heroic and accessible to the public they were.

Best to tick everybody on my list off at once. My gaze settles on the distant, unapproachable-looking form of Armsmaster first – standing apart from the crowd, just far enough inside a restricted area to dissuade his fans while still being involved with the ongoing proceedings. I highly doubted that I would beat Armsmaster straight off the bat, and I didn't really need his power right now anyway. I couldn't take tinkertech into a challenge with me, and the soft-enrage that every challenge seemed to have put an artificial timer on any potential tinkering inside the simulation.

ARMSMASTER

Hero 1/6

(PREP) (CONT)​

PREP was new, but I assumed it was self-explanatory. CONT was unfortunate, but the only power I had that would possibly help was Shadow Stalker's – as long as I didn't use that, then there wasn't much downside to gathering information. "Challenge."

I shift my weight from one leg to the other as the world loads. A distant droning fills my ears as the street materialises around me. The ArmsCycle. No real point in running. He drifts to a stop and dismounts in the same move – I sidestep before I even see the attack coming, just in time to watch the dart go skittering past me. He tried that same move when I met him on Taylor's ABB challenge – clearly a well-practised part of his kit.

This wasn't a great challenge for me. Armsmaster starts in his standard blue power armour, usual armaments and only gives a little time to prepare before he engages. Far from the ideal challenge for me, but pretty much all within expectations. The best I could really do was die here without showing any of my powers.

I absently duck under the first swing of his halberd, only to stagger as it folds itself in half to impale me from above. I hear something in the weapon make a brief 'click', and I feel a brief but agonising moment of pain as electricity floods through my body – lasting only for the quickest of movements before my vision goes black.

FAILURE

Hint: The Preparation (PREP) modifier gives the enemy a significant amount of time to prepare to fight you prior to your arrival in the challenge. Some enemies might choose to prepare countermeasures for your powers, adjust their costume, lay some traps, fortify their defences or even just get a headstart running away! This modifier also provides enemies with a basic summary of your current powerset.
​
I swear under my breath. So he already knows about my powers. Lovely. I wasn't going to beat this any time soon. Not that I expected to before. This was probably my fastest failure yet, but Armsmaster wasn't really a priority compared to my main targets: The Wards.

I glance around. I would tick Triumph off as well, but I couldn't actually see him around at the moment.

I pace around the hall, making a good show of being a typical awestruck fanboy for the benefit of the cameras. Not that it was hard. I was a hardcore cape fanboy. Which meant that I knew it was very likely that someone was watching people in the convention looking for signs of suspicious things going on. Some lackey in an office with nothing better to do. It wouldn't take much to fool anyone who wasn't a thinker – attempting a challenge had almost no tells aside from a single, muffled word from me. Even if I succeeded, the effects of winning once were almost always minimal to the wider world – and my power tended to cover its tracks fairly well in the cases where it wasn't so minimal.

I join the primarily female crowd gathered around Gallant, signing off on autographs while trying to maintain a safe distance from the fans. I narrow my eyes at him. I didn't have much use for a tinker, let alone one who had so little to show off after such a long time in the wards. Anyone could make a powersuit. I was pretty sure that Squealer was a better tinker than him.

Still. A power is a power. It might synchronise well with something else later on.

GALLANT

Hero 1/4

(ZONE)
​
"Challenge." Just a ZONE modifier. Narrowing down the area that I could fight in. Nothing too serious.

I close my eyes for a moment, and reopen them to find myself in very familiar surroundings. Right back at the entrance to this very building. A glance through the glass in the door shows me that it is, in fact, this specific event that's been chosen for the venue this time. The same fanboys and fangirls are wandering around. A few PRT troopers are lazing around by the doors. One or two other heroes being drowned by the mob and heading backstage for some rest.

And then Gallant himself, centre-stage. Still signing autographs.

First things first. The ZONE modifier. How far did it extend this time? A quick glance behind me told me that the entrance to the building was the limit on this side. Looking through the doors – I couldn't see anything past the windows on the far side of the room, which I felt made it a good assumption that there would also be another wall there. Just this building then. Workable.

I didn't really have a good weapon to hand, and I don't expect to find one either. If I enter the hall, I'm likely to kick off the fight immediately – so I opt to back out instead and investigate the other doors in the corridor. I ignore the two toilets, but do try what I hope is a supply closet. It's locked, but slipping into my shadow state is more than enough to bypass it. I flick the light on and inspect the rows of cleaning equipment and stacked chairs. I didn't see anything that usable as a weapon here. A baseball bat, or a pipe, or something like that would be really nice.

In the end, I just grab the meatiest, heaviest, metal chair that I can hold above my head. I highly doubt it will be that effective against power armour, but it will probably be better than trying to punch him.

I pause as I drag the chair by Clockblocker. This was primarily information gathering, so it wouldn't do any harm to find out what level of realism and interference I could expect from Gallant's allies. "Hey!" I attract his attention. "I'm going to go and kill your friend!"

He shoots finger guns at me. "Good luck with that!"

I pause. He might be joking. He might not. That wasn't the best test. "I have superpowers, and I'm going to kill Gallant with them!" I shift into the shadow state and back directly in front of him.

"Nice!" He doesn't even blink. "Have you considered joining the Wards?"

Not very realistic then – and not that likely to be his allies in a fight. That makes it easier for me, but it still isn't looking great for my chances. Once again, the costume was working against me here. I wasn't getting any skin contact against that heavy armour, or getting any serious attack through the plating.

Whatever. Even if it's a failure, there's nowhere else for me to look for something better. Hoping for a concussion by hitting him with a heavy chair is a better bet than trying to needle him with a kitchen knife through power-armour. The only thing that might work is stealing Armsmaster's halberd, but that alone would probably be tougher than beating Gallant in a fistfight – no matter how unrealistic their personalities were, I didn't doubt that taking overt action against the NPC's would set them to violence.

I heft the chair up to my chest in a loose, two-handed carry. It is heavy – one of the large ones with the solid metal frames, not some cheap and flimsy plastic crap that they put out at school assemblies. Shifting through the wall of the supply cabinet straight towards the hall lets me enter through his blind spot, preventing him from immediately starting a fight.

I hold my position and wait for Shadow Stalker's power to come back. This way, I could move freely for a second without a single footstep sounding. Overly precautious? Perhaps. But everything depended on my first attack here. I advance another few steps once the power returns, then halt again. When I'm watching and waiting for the target like this, it's clear the difference that the lack of WLRD or REAL modifiers makes to his behaviour. He's acting exactly like a background NPC – being handed the same picture to sign by the same few girls, over and over. The crowd doesn't move, and therefore he has no reason to turn as he repeats his exact motions until I do something to change that. Nor does the crowd react to my blatant show of aggression and supernatural ability. I shift again, and creep a bit closer before stopping once more to wait for the cooldown to return.

It takes another three shifts, but finally, I emerge out of the shadow state only two paces behind him – the heavy, folded chair already in full swing as I bring it down onto the Ward's armoured helmet. He reels away and staggers to the floor, I follow up again – hoping to continue landing hits to prevent him from planning out a response to the sudden assault in the middle of his autographing session.

I make another solid impact as he looks up, but at the same time a solid orb of light blasts from one upraised hand to blast me dead-centre – sending me stumbling back into the crowd I just came through.

I don't stand up. What's the point? It would be faster for everyone involved if I had just killed myself right at the start of this challenge. I can hear Gallant staggering to his feet, but there's just no point pressing the advantage. I never stood a chance anyway. Might as well just wait for someone to get over here and kill me.

After what seems like a full minute, I shake my head. Wait. What? That's not what I'm here for at all. That isn't the mind of Greg Veder, superhero-extraordinaire! "Emotion blasts." I spit, struggling to my feet. I've never experienced them before, so I had underestimated the emotional component of his blasts over the purely physical impacts that they had. Just like Glory Girl's aura – something that sounds weak on paper, but is on a whole different level when you face it head-on.

The target has escaped the area. All enemies enraged.​

Escaped? I vaguely remember a hint saying that enemies could sometimes escape ZONE modifiers, but I wasn't expecting it to come up unless I was assaulting someone's base and they had a secret teleporter or something. I wasn't expecting him to just… run out. I glance around at a suddenly hostile arena. A dozen angry fangirls surround me, I lash out at them to get them to fall back for a moment – only to find myself put into an expert armlock in seconds by the unassuming girl closest to me. My arm makes a painful crack as the rest of the girls draw closer to finish me off, shouts of rage only drowned out by my own pained scream – only to melt away as I catch a glimpse of Armsmasters Halberd disintegrating half of someone's torso as it completes its journey from his hand to my skull regardless of anything or anyone in between.

FAILURE​

Instant kill. Excellent throw, Halbeard. I had to respect that.

Hint: In certain ZONE missions, enemies can escape the boundaries of the local area to enrage all remaining NPC's and give them powerful modifiers. The target can still be defeated after escaping, however you will never be able to pass the boundary for any amount of time. Enemies of increasing difficulty will spawn until the encounter ends.​

So, he can just walk out. If I had a blaster power, or poison, or something else that could kill him while I was stuck inside – then I could still be in with a chance at that stage. As I am now, escaping is just the functional end of the challenge as I have no way of finishing him off.

That makes me zero for three so far. In fairness, I had expected that to be the case. Beating a cape's challenge on the very first try was hard – even with the benefit of perfect information and repeated attempts, I had struggled to claim the relatively minor powers I had gained so far. Only one effect at a time, which slowly unravels as time goes on – which naturally means that a larger use of the power will take longer to become available again than a smaller one. Got it. I can remember that.

"Young man? I'm going to have to call security if you insist on ignoring me-" Vista was probably on the stairs right now, with the elevator out of action. It would be unusual for my target to take their time or take an extended detour when the option of a direct confrontation was available to them – at least, not without the REAL modifier.

But I could win that fight. Especially in a cramped environment like this. How was Vista going to kill me in a fight? I wasn't exactly a 'roided-up monster, but I kind of manhandled her in the last challenge – the difference in size and gender more than enough to make up for my lack of formal CQC training. It was a surprise attack that time, but even still – she wasn't able to get out under her own power when I had her in a good hold. She wasn't likely to come down here with a gun in hand, so as long as I manage to close the gap, then I should win again.

I must have dropped two or three flights of stairs from my original location, so she can't be far off now. I step over to the doors to the stairwell, listening intently for footsteps. I hear them. Loud. Fast. Interspersed with heavier impacts that might well be her jumping down several stairs at once. I step over to the opposite wall, and slam my fist through the fire alarm glass.

As I hoped, the alarm immediately starts blaring, and every one of the office workers lets out a simultaneous groan and pushes themselves up from their chairs. The NPC grabs me by the collar. "What do you think you're doing? Do you have any idea how much that little prank-" I bring my leg up hard and fast, leaving the man to let out a breathless gasp and fold down to the floor with a whimper – curling up around his groin while trying to fight back the eye-watering pain that always accompanies such a hit to the family jewels.

A glance around behind him shows that few people are paying the fallen man much in the way of attention, instead crowding down stairwells, fire escapes and corridors in the polite rush to evacuate the building. Many of them brushing right past Vista, who reaches my floor only to get stuck struggling to fight the flow of traffic heading in the opposite direction.

I can't sit and wait for them to pass completely – even if it means interference, Vista will destroy me once the crowd is gone and her full powers can be brought to bear. I close the distance without any struggle, pushing a few paper pushers aside as I grasp Vista's arm and roughly tug her back into the room towards me. She doesn't exactly resist, but she does take the opportunity to use my arm as leverage to perform a jumping, two-legged kick into my thigh. I swear roughly as I stumble, attempting to swing her into the ground unsuccessfully before she flips me instead – sending us both tumbling to the floor as I pull her with me.

"Hey, what are you doing to Vista?" A hand grabs my arm and tries to separate us. Damn it. Apparently, pulling her out of the crowd so roughly attracted a white knight, here to save the day. There wasn't anyone else left on this floor – and the door was already swinging shut. Deal with this guy, and I won't have any more interference. He pulls my arm harder, threatening to break my only hold on the Ward.

I latch my legs around Vista in response as she jabs me in the stomach, grabbing the bystander with my now-free limbs – I hold his hand tightly, bringing Panacea's power to the fore. I push it away after only a few seconds, and he lets out a yelp of shock at the green-blue mess that I've turned his hand into in only a short amount of time. "I've poisoned you. If you don't get to a hospital then you'll die-" Vista punches me in the stomach, then attempts to wrestle out of my grip and knee me in the balls. My words seem to have done the trick though, he gives a terrified scream and runs back to the stairwell – taking the steps three at a time until I can't see him anymore.

I didn't think I was that believable, but I guess non-capes don't know any better right now. It was nothing more than a simple change in colour, I couldn't do anything complicated like poison even if I wanted to. It wasn't even a colour change all the way through, if he rubbed his hands together he would probably notice it start to fade away. I pull back and take a massive swing down at Vista's helmet, only to slightly miss and receive another bruising punch to my torso in return. I scowl. Even if she can't use her full powers in melee, apparently stretching a few inches here and there is more than enough to give her the edge in trading blows.

But I've still got my legs wrapped around her. The 'mind' behind her, what I would call the AI in a video game – it clearly hadn't gone into this with a serious plan. At a guess, it's just copying Vista's abilities and fighting style and pasting it into a new scenario. Without the REAL or LUST modifier, it simply isn't smart enough to realise that closing to melee is the only way it can lose – even when the real Vista would have known that. All it seems to know is that Vista has happily gone into melee scraps before and came out the other end as the victor.

Hell, the real Vista would probably have just called security and stayed upstairs or played support when dealing with an unknown cape – but this version wanted to start a fight just as much as I did, and only realised that melee was disadvantageous after the fact. Much like the civilians I had fought over the last week, happy to close to melee without considering that I might have a knife in my back pocket – which I didn't this time around, but the point was the same.

Of course, that didn't matter much for most civilians. I was probably going to win anyway. But it did matter for capes. I'm sure that someone like Aegis, Dauntless or Armsmaster weren't too disadvantaged by being piloted straight at me without a grand plan – but Vista was best used in a support and ranged role. She could box me into a room from the floor above me, stretch the walls to cover the doors and roll containment foam grenades into the room until my Shadow State didn't have anywhere to run to. I didn't know exactly what my shadow state would do if I tried to reappear inside containment foam, but I didn't want to test it either.

Although, it might be worth checking. Finding another weakness in Sophia's power could be very useful for later. It's way too versatile for me to dismiss casually. It's the crutch on which almost all of my challenges seem to fall back on so far, next time I head to the Power Rankings thread on PHO I won't be so harsh on Shadow Stalker. Probably.

Back to the topic. All of that wasn't to say she was a pushover like this, by any means. She was still dangerous in melee, despite her size – it's clear that she's used to fighting like this against capes and thugs. Still, it isn't optimal – you could compare it to Othala coming over to try and beat me up in person with her gang rather than hiding at the back and sending an endless stream of invincible thugs my way. Just because she might know kung-fu didn't mean that it was the best choice.

It would be interesting to see if that would change at later challenges – even without specific changes in modifiers, I had noticed that they tended to be more difficult as a rule. Would that extend to capes being smarter about their abilities and limitations, and therefore closer to their real life counterparts? Closer to their true potential? My gut said yes, but I had nothing to back that on so far.

I roll across the floor, dragging Vista with me. I'm still stuck with the same problem I had last time. That costume is tougher than it looks. And my grapple isn't as solid as the last one I had on her, this time it's a much more even fight – and the amount of abuse my body is taking is starting to rack up. Drowning her is probably out of the question this time around, I can't just take a few steps to the side and drag her into the water. But perhaps I could do something similar? We were quite high up, after all – if I could just get us both outside, then I could survive a fall much better than she could as long as my shadow state was available before I hit the ground.

Vista arches upwards, fist lashing out into a right hook that I narrowly dodge. I move to seize her arm, and promptly find that same arm pressed into a dangerous looking hold before I can blink. She twists harder, clearly intending to break the offending limb – but she's not quite fast enough to stop me from shifting into my shadow state to escape the hold. I take the opportunity to wind up a heavy kick at her face, while she immediately reaches behind her back the moment my limb turns to smoke.

I recognise the chirping noise a split second too late to do anything about the taser as she lunges upwards towards me, but I still make a heavy connection with my downwards kick that knocks her down for a moment. We both fall to the floor, separated again despite my best efforts. I bite back the scream as I attempt to control my fall – merely falling to my knees and stumbling forwards instead of being sent flying back to the floor Vista was. I was only hit for a brief moment thanks to the timer on my shadow state being so strict and short – but I could still feel the burnt skin on the left side of my body where the electricity has inflicted a far greater toll on my body than should have been possible if not for Sophia's power.

Taser. Of course. If she has a constant awareness of my position with the HUNT modifier, then she could clearly see that I managed to move through solid walls using her teammate's power. Idiot. I push myself upwards, cursing my arms for shaking as my body protests the sudden damage.

Still. Vista isn't doing so hot herself – she hadn't at all been prepared for the full-power kick straight out of my shadow state. I may have taken a painful hit, but I hadn't slowed down my attack at all – she can't afford to take hits like that, something that she had been careful to do this far into the fight. I may not be an adult yet, but the sheer amount of force I can output on a heavy kick is so much more than her childlike frame can easily handle – especially when she didn't see it coming at all. Now she's on the floor, winded and looking in just as bad a shape as I am – although my injuries are likely to last a bit longer if we were to both back off and wait for a second round.

Which is why I can't give her that chance. I managed to abuse the people in the office to limit her power and allow me to close the gap the first time – but she will never let me get close again if she gets away. My leg gives way as I try to put pressure onto it, but I at least manage a half-baked hop – which I combine with as rapid a pinching of space as I can manage between Vista and I.

The mental sense I get with the power is strange, and I can see that she's already twisted the space between us into an unholy mess of vectors and twists – if I were to try and walk towards her I'm sure that I would at best be turned around 180 degrees in seconds, and at worst twist an ankle or something as the twists in space do strange things with my balance and footwork. I almost feel bad that my simple task of connecting point A and B skips past all of her effort, like I've just tunnelled a highway over the top of some intricate cave network. That feeling doesn't last long though, as a moment later I find myself grinning with my weight pinning Vista to the floor again.

She's dropped the taser, but I don't trust her not to have a backup – I need to be more careful next time. I elbow her in the ribs as she attempts to shake me off, narrowly avoiding a vicious knee to the balls in reply. Note to self: Find one of those crotch-protector things. Wait, no – I can't take stuff like that into challenges. Correction: Find where the PRT stores their crotch-protector things so I know where to steal them from. They must have them right? All cops should. My experience on that was entirely based on a throwaway line on the last buddy cop movie I watched – but it made sense so it was probably true.

I test my leg again. Flex it once, then twice before nodding to myself – bracing for another kick into my side from the diminutive Ward. Not quite as strong as she was before, I might have given her a bit of a concussion – even if that helmet still looks as strong as ever. My leg feels fine too – it looks like I can stand properly again, even if I can't do anything about the pain or the unwanted twitching now and then. Everything hurts – but I can't afford to draw this out any longer. Fact of the matter is that I overestimated my chances here, I can't win this brawl. I caught her off guard once, but the simple fact is that she's just better than me at CQC. I have a few tricks, but I can't do anything lethal to her in these circumstances unless she's out of costume or I manage to knock her out.

Which is why I have to accept the loss. You can lose the battle, but still win the war in the end. I grab her with both hands by the front of the costume, dragging her up and across the room – gritting my teeth and pushing through the double-kicks targeting my stomach as she uses my own grip as her leverage. Need to suck it up. Pain doesn't matter. Injuries don't matter. Only death matters.

I'm almost to the far side of the room when she curls her body upwards around my left arm, wrenching it at an angle that sends screaming signals of pain to my brain – but this time I can see the minute pause she makes before it seems she would complete the motion. She was waiting for me to shift again, probably to blast me with another cheap shot with a second taser. I could easily grapple a weapon from her hand if she tried to use it, but there wasn't a chance of her missing the super-effective attack once I turned into a cloud of shadow. She seems surprised when I simply keep running, but doesn't hesitate for long before simply continuing the motion. Bending my arm at an impossible, agonising angle until the sensation comes to a sudden halt as a loud, crystal-clear snapping noise reaches my ears.

I hope my scream damaged her ears, but I didn't let go of her with my other hand – her move had only made it easier for me to carry her instead of needing to almost drag her across the room. I pull her body tight to mine as I charge through the external fire exit, a simple push-to-open contraption that offers no resistance to our combined weight.

Out on the metallic fire escape trailing down the outside of the building, Vista had suddenly realised my game plan. She wasn't trying to inflict damage on me anymore, no attempts to break my other arm or to inflict additional punishment onto my body – she was trying to escape. An earnest, desperate struggle born of something more than the simple tactical advantage she was seeking before.

Too late. Far, far too late. I push her up against the railings with my one hand, my now-useless left arm flopping uselessly behind me. Two blows to the stomach send me reeling – but it's just too easy to throw her weight around even with only a single arm. I practically roll her over the side, only looking slightly annoyed when I realise that she used her power and extended the step outwards to that side as well. I can't exactly clamber over without probably throwing me off or at least claiming the advantage – and if I left her alone she could extend the staircase below her feet all the way to safety. I couldn't afford to let go and take any action and she knows it, based on her immediate reaction to twist my arm into another professional armlock.

She probably thinks she's in a good position here. The real Vista might be more worried, and try to adapt to her situation with more caution once she realises how abnormal my strategy is – but this challenge has thrown me against a glorified combat dummy. It fights like Vista, reacts like Vista does and has all the experience that Vista does. But it doesn't quite think like Vista. Has Vista ever fought a villain that didn't care about themselves? One that didn't care about their own death, as long as they won? No. Of course not. Against any of her previous opponents breaking an arm or two was a near-guarantee of winning the fight, not that Wards usually got into a fight that serious – but rules like that went out the window in this challenge. Any normal opponent would have already started running away, all of the combat experience that she had would support that.

So this doll with Vista's face could never consider the threat from a double suicide.

I treasure the look of shock on the visible part of her face as I step through the railing in my shadow state, wrapping my arms around her and using my momentum to hurl us out into the open air. The step extends just a few inches behind her, but she isn't fast enough with her power to save herself – and once we are truly falling there is nothing left that she can do other than hopelessly spin with me and beat her fists fruitlessly against my face.

Of course, this will kill me. I won't get my shadow state back before I hit the ground. It's a massive drop, but I know from experience just how fast that gap can disappear with a bit of help from gravity.

But that didn't matter. As long as Vista died first, I would win. And thankfully, the basic power that I had gotten from Vista in the first round? Even if it wasn't as flexible or strong, it also didn't weaken as much when a furious, screaming girl is wrapped around me and causing issues with the Manton Limit. It's a question of timing, but it's easy enough after the first few rotations to work it out. Just as Vista passes above me, I trigger my power to shrink the distance between us and the ground. The power isn't all that fast, at shrinking space – but it does just enough to accelerate us downwards to hit the ground at the exact point that Vista is directly below me. The last thing that I see is the tiniest hint of Vista ragdolling off the ground just below me and a flash of pain as I collide with her a split second later.

I gasp awake, trying to calm my adrenaline as I flex my left arm again. Working. Functional. Not painful. I might be getting used to debilitating injuries, but I certainly wouldn't volunteer for that again. The myriad bruises littering my body were healed as well, as expected.

That did the job. I didn't really get to see much of what happened, but Vista was definitely below me when we hit the ground. I glance up at the almost-empty void, reading the ghostly-blue words etched across what should have been the sky.

SUCCESS

Reward: Vista+​

Hell yeah.

The hall of people returns to my sight around me, the Ward shows no obvious sign of change – and she wasn't even looking in my direction anyway. The fanboys and girls surrounding her continue their chatter, it's as if nothing has changed at all. Which was a good thing, obviously. I could probably assume that Vista liked me better now, but as we had literally never spoken that didn't mean a lot.

Still. I won, which means that I could go again. I cast my eyes over her new challenge.

Vista

Heroine 3/6

(LUST) (CAGE)​

Now that sounded interesting. I wouldn't have expected a CAGE modifier to be in Vista's favour, but clearly, there was a plan of some description in here. "Challenge."

My vision shifts again, even before it had fully finished filling in the details of the real world around me. My feet settle onto solid ground, and I already start moving forward before I even spot my opponent. Close the distance. My plan immediately goes awry, the instant I spot Vista, standing a bit further away than most of my previous cage match opponents. Taking more care about where I place my feet slows me down notably, but it becomes a moot point when the ground beneath Vista rises up into a large pillar propelling her to safety.

She's not done there though – even as she moves away, the mysterious material making up the floor and walls rises up around me to box me in. I lunge at the nearest wall, using Vista's power to pinch the distance between its highest corner and myself – the aim was getting on top of the thing to stop her from just boxing me in again, but before I can even try to act on the shortcut, my control over the space gets unceremoniously torn from my grasp. My mental image staying intact to inform me of exactly how many useless ribbons of twisted space my shortcut had turned into. Judging by the sluggish stillness of the power, almost refusing to move back like usual or perhaps simply forced to stay in place – it wouldn't be reappearing in my repertoire for quite some time.

With my initial plan foiled, the walls curve around to box me in, even sealing up my escape to the ceiling. The beige material of the floor and ceiling actually seemed to be my source of light itself, so I could at least see – but the only thing that meant was that I could see the newly raised walls closing in closer and closer. I throw myself at the closest wall, shifting into my shadow state and barrelling through it – hoping that I could make it out without her noticing, enabling a sneak attack while she thought I was being slowly crushed. My shadow state runs out its brief timer, and I find myself forcefully ejected out of the same side that I tried to escape from.

Fuck. That likely meant that I hadn't even crossed the halfway mark of the wall within that one-second sprint. The walls were still closing in, under normal circumstances I would say that she couldn't crush me directly thanks to the Manton Limit. Unfortunately, the sheer amount of material that she's moving means that she doesn't have to. She just has to manipulate the space on her side of the wall and let the other side continue to press towards me as it takes the path of least resistance to resolve the pressure it faces from her end. Like squeezing out toothpaste, even if she wasn't allowed to touch the paste itself – as long as she squeezed the far end correctly then natural physics would take care of the rest. Toothpaste on the brush. My bones smeared into coal or whatever bones turned into. Same thing.

I take a few more attempts at escaping with Sophia's power before the walls finally finishing closing in on me, but ultimately there's nothing I can do to save myself before I find myself without even any room to breathe – unable to even expand my chest out before something in my ribs gives way under the pressure. Blood spurts into my mouth as I lose consciousness, thankfully unaware of the rest of my body being literally ground into dust by the makeshift-compresser.

FAILURE

Hint: LUST maximises the combat effectiveness and bloodlust of the target to its theoretical highest levels in a given scenario. A powerset might be used in ways that the original user had never considered, and powers that are limited by the users experience, morals or mental capacity will no longer be as restrained as they were – greatly enhancing their combat potential.​

Interesting. Not entirely unexpected, but it did nearly eliminate one of Vista's weaknesses by boosting the speed and complexity of her power – even to the point where she can do all of that with me at the centre of it all. As far as what little I saw of her, she hadn't pulled out anything truly new – I had seen her accomplish similar feats before on PHO, albeit usually on unoccupied space.

And despite the large movements of the 'rock' or whatever I was supposed to call the mysterious substance that made up the walls, it wasn't moving unbeatably fast under Vista's direction. Or at least, not unbeatably fast for someone with a mover rating. I couldn't do anything about it now because I couldn't stop her from boxing me in – but if I could run or fly fast enough, then I might be able to do something. Or even just teleporting, now that I think about it. Oni Lee's power would probably trivialise this fight, depending on cooldown and distance limitations.

Well. That's enough thinking. It's a moot point now. I double-check Vista's timer as she comes into view on the off-chance that the timer had gone down from it's previous one – but this time it has just over four hours remaining. No third-chances today, this event will have long since packed up by then.

Time to move on. Of all the remaining targets, the only one I felt like I had a good chance of beating was Clockblocker. Even if he was making excellent use of his power, it was still quite limited in what it could do. Very strong within those limitations of course, but limited all the same. With just a bit of planning on my part, I was sure that I could handle him in a fight. "Challenge." I give the world a few seconds to half-form, but this time don't wait for the elevator doors to open before shifting through the floor. Getting out so early meant that I didn't even have to jump that far because the actual elevator hadn't made it to the floor above at the time. He didn't have a modifier like ALRT to start out so aggressive, it was just the situation that I had started in that accomplished the same thing. If I wasn't in the elevator to lock eyes with him when the doors opened, he would just stay in that room until something else alerted him to my presence.

Not that I saw anything here likely to do that. I would have to be quiet on the stairs, but I seemed to have the run of the building for now. Especially because I didn't see anyone else in the area, perhaps this challenge was devoid of people entirely? That wasn't uncommon at all, but I hadn't had that scenario and been inside such an important building before.

I spend most of the next hour exploring, not finding that much of interest apart from some user credentials stashed under a keyboard. Walking around the corridors and trying out some of my new passcodes on different doors got me foamed for my trouble, but Sophia's power got me out easily enough. Given the lack of blaring alarms, I assume there's a manual step in the security process where a human would assess the situation before escalating – but seeing as no security team appears at any point and no death-dealing laser-turrets burst out of the walls to kill me, I guess that I'm pretty safe here aside from the inconvenience of getting foamed.

Most of the doors aren't electrified, so it's easy enough to flit in and out of different buildings and rooms. Eventually, I find the jackpot. Containment foam grenades. I found the launchers and tanks too, but I remember someone saying something about some security control that didn't let unverified people fire them. Special gloves? Fingerprint scanner? Something like that. It was a long time ago.

Still, the grenades had no such issues. I toss one down the hallway, and beam to myself as the liquid erupts into the air – each individual droplet swelling into foam globules the size of my head as they soar through the air then succumb to gravity or cling to the walls as they continue to expand even further, connecting smaller globs together until the entire hallway was covered in a single, impassable mass of foam.

Perfect. Tag Clockblocker with a single one of these, and I've won. Best to take a whole bundle of them just in case, but my exploration has finally paid off. I could drag this part out longer before confronting him, but I didn't want to count on him staying in one place forever. He was still human. What would happen if he went to take a shit and saw me out of the window? Or if he was scheduled for patrol in a few hours and suddenly started moving away? I was probably worrying too much, but caution was a good thing as far as my power was concerned.

I inch my way up the stairs with Shadow Stalker's power. No footsteps, even if it made for a slow ascent. Soon, I'm back where I started – and no longer concerned about being heard. I rush up the last of the stairs and burst through the door as I see a sliver of his costume come into view. That was all I needed, no chance of being ambushed now.

Of course, he charges towards me with a shred of hesitation, and I do a fantastic act of pretending to back away while keeping my arms hidden behind my body. I don't even spot the first string wrapping around my leg, but it isn't important anyway. Fifteen metres. Ten. Five. With one swift yank, I activate three grenades and toss them to each side and above him. I repeat the motion on the other hand, dropping another grenade at my feet and rolling the second towards him. To his credit, he dives excellently to freeze two of the grenades before they explode – and another is wrapped in string with ludicrous precision, but he can't stop them all. Especially when the sixth and final grenade is still being held in my own hand as I stroll towards him in my shadow state.

I lean forward as he desperately reaches out towards me, ignoring the razor-sharp cords bisecting the air between us. "I win this time." The grenade slips from my hand to the floor as victorious spite widens my grin to psychotic levels. "Bitch."

In an instant, we are both foamed from head-to-toe – his struggles only sealing him in harder. I simply wait for a few seconds for my shadow state, then easily escape without any struggle at all.

"The only problem with this, is that I have no idea how to kill you in there." I peer at his helmet, barely visible through the foam. "I could try to poison you, but I'm not a real expert at chemicals – and destroying the building might give you a way out or turn on some random security system. If I poke you with a knife, you might be able to tag me and you could definitely freeze the knife." And with the LUST modifier, would he be capable of permanently freezing an object by perfectly timing his ability to apply again instantly on expiry? If I got tagged, I could wake up to find that the foam was already long-gone and the tables turned.

He doesn't reply, of course. Not the most talkative guy in this challenge.

"So the safest thing to do, is to simply leave you there to starve. Or die of thirst, I suppose. You're still human in there after all." I drum my fingers against the foam, which promptly gets them stuck and forces out my shadow state again. "I'm very confident that you can't get out of this without the foam dissolving. You can't freeze your own body. I have enough grenades to keep you there until Christmas if I have to." I clap my hands together. "Excellent! I'm going to find a McDonalds, and we'll have another chat later!" I turn around and head for the door.

I didn't actually find a McDonald's, mostly because the forcefield-road wasn't extended and I was stuck on the manmade island unless I wanted to swim. I did find a cafeteria though, so after a few false starts with the kitchen, I made myself some basic fast food and went back to exploring.

I had time to kill, after all.


"Hey there Clockblocker! Long time no see!" The boy says nothing as I toss another grenade at him, the previous foam not even half of its original size before I liberally re-apply it. "Now I know what you're thinking! How did you sleep Greg? I'll tell you. I slept really well. I didn't consider that you guys might have your own rooms over here, but I am glad that you do! I guess you don't need to use them often – but I'll concede that they are fancy as hell."

He still doesn't reply. Rude.

"Now. I know what you're thinking. You're thinking, Greg. You sound like a crazy person! I'm not even talking back to you, you're just talking to yourself! And you would be right. That is exactly what I am doing. But you didn't ask why!" I give him a pause in the conversation to let him ask, but he disappoints me again. I peer at the window, slightly sunken eyes staring back at me. "It's because the internet isn't working. I got onto the computer as some flunky without any problems, managed to get into some low-level database as well before getting locked out – but the internet doesn't work."

I raise my smoothie upwards, bringing the straw to my lips. Lack of good flavours aside, my experimentation with the cafeteria's stock was opening up the possibility of a career as a burger-flipper if this cape business didn't work out. I was killing it, even without any instructions to go with.

"My father, may he rest in peace-" I start solemnly. "-once took me out into the countryside. Gave me some deep speeches about the American spirit, becoming a man and the thrill of the hunt. I broke down crying and screaming after a few days. That was probably the lowest point in my life. Six entire days without electricity. No internet. No games. No porn.
