#581
Somehow, it felt like it had been weeks since the last time I was at Winslow. Which… probably wasn't as crazy as it sounded, considering how long many challenges I had been through since Friday, some taking hours if not entire days to complete. Even if it had only been two days in reality, with my mixed success at the charity event I was a different man as I crossed the school gates.

That's right. A new man. Confident. Powerful. Charismatic-

"Out of the way, dweeb." I find myself shouldered aside as a pair of skinheads pass by. A spark of irritation almost sends me on a crusade to get back at them via a challenge, but I just can't muster up the energy to have a difficult scrap with some mook that I will forget about by tomorrow. If I had an offensive power that would end the fight quickly I wouldn't be opposed to it - but if I was going to have knife fight or deadly street brawl I wanted to get some actual benefit out of it other than saving my ego.

And I suppose I was standing right in the middle of the path. I could see someone finding that annoying.

Regardless, I was going to be late if I stuck around. Cape Studies time! I practically sprint across the courtyard, through the corridor and into my usual classroom. "I'm not late!" I shoot some finger guns at Mr Gladly. "Mr G!"

"Mr Gladly"

Winslow Teacher

(DOOM)​

"You are late." He disagrees. "I think-"

Detention is lame. "Challenge." I race out the whisper.

A nice, easy DOOM modifier to start out the day. Beat the countdown, or whatever the doom flag was this time around. Then cave his skull in. Or perhaps cave his skull in first. I wasn't quite sure what the order was supposed to be, seeing as I hadn't beaten one of these yet.

Maybe it seems a bit strange for me to so happy to jump to the part where I inflict horrible amounts of violence onto my favourite teacher, but he was only my favourite because all the others were shit. And besides, it wasn't like it was actually him I would be beating up. Just a simulation. If people in this city could tolerate racists doing it every day in real life, they should be able to put up with me doing it in the privacy of my own head.

Not that anyone was asking them.

The challenge-world fills in around me, and I materialise at my desk. Staring across at Mr Gladly.

I shift into shadow state as he leaps at me, sending him tumbling ungracefully into my seat. I opt not to take the easy follow-up attack, instead, glancing around to find out what exactly this DOOM modifier was for. No timer or objective in the corner of my vision, no obvious pillar of light- well. Maybe I spoke too soon on that one. A glance out of the window spots the gibbering skull in the sky hanging directly over the school - as large and distant as any other visible cloud. It was impossible to truly state exactly what building it was hanging over, but there certainly was something happening.

And it wasn't something that Mr G was doing. He was just lunging at me constantly, trying to tackle me to the floor – ignoring any of the viable sharp objects nearby that would help him in a fight. My gaze sharpens as I hop up onto a table and leap across another row of chairs, leaving him behind as he tries to scramble upwards himself without ripping his clothes with the movement. He's trying to slow me down. Not even kill me, though I am sure he wouldn't pass it up if he was able. He's trying to stop me from… what?

What was the modifier doing? It wasn't outright telling me to go elsewhere, like the last one had. Was there an event I needed to stop? Not that I could tell. The few other students in the class speak amongst themselves, clearly disinterested as they wait for their name to be called in the register. Another student walks into the room, not even blinking at the carnage we were causing as she takes her usual seat.

Wait. I glance at the clock on the wall. 8:30 AM flat. I check the calendar. Tuesday.

Tuesday, 8:30 AM. I would normally be in a different building, about to have my first lesson of the day in mathematics.

Was my power constructing the scenario out of the circumstances leading up to me making the challenge?

Only one way to test it. Get to my usual class before my name is called in the register. I've already wasted a bit of time, but I have plenty of ways to make up for it. Mr G is just a civilian, if it was possible for me to do unpowered – then I am vastly overqualified as I am now.

I dash out into the corridor, shoving people to the side as I go. I had to run through most of the length of the school here, as opposed to an easy shot between buildings. Vistas power was slow to restore itself, so I would probably only get one shot at using it.

Cutting out the detour to the stairs would be the best use, so I opt to save it on the straight down the corridor past the rapidly thinning swarm of students working their own way into their classrooms. I burst out of the central building through the fire exit, heading straight towards the window of Ms Rothman's class in the next building over. Timing is key here. If I want to skip the stairs to make up for the time I wasted at the start, I only have one shot at it before being forced to take the long route.

Three. Two. One. Vistas power to shrink the gap between the second-floor window and myself, not quite strong enough to make it into a single step but enough that I can reach the ledge and pull myself up - shifting into my shadow state as I do so to let my momentum keep moving me up and then past the window.

I tumble into a room of disinterested students. "Nailed it."

Ms Rothman doesn't respond. "Grace Vallory."

"Present." A brunette responds absently.

"Gregory Veder." She drones.

"Yo." I raise my hand.

The lighting of the room changes, I glance back through the window to find the floating skull withering to dust - the standard blue sky replacing the ominous red it was previously emitting.

No victory screen though.

But there was Mr G. Panting hard as he races through the courtyard towards this building.

I steal my neighbour's pencil case thoughtfully. Theory: DOOM simply adds an impending failure event other than my death. If Clockblocker reaches the Protectorate HQ before me or perhaps even at all in his challenge, I lose. In this case, if I miss my name being called at register - I lose. That event can be stopped or beaten, dispelling the modifier - or simply delayed until I complete the actual win condition, which in this case is unchanged from normal:

Kill Mr G.

Which would imply, then – that a sufficiently powerful offensive power or weapon would nullify the need to worry about the DOOM modifier. If I completed the win condition before I lost, it was no different than any other challenge. A simple and irrelevant modifier like TIME, as long as I ended it fast enough.

I feel like applauding myself. Good scientific research, Greg! Sure, it wasn't particularly arduous this time - but it would have been trivial to beat the challenge without learning any more information.

I lounge around for a minute, waiting for the door to open. The moment it gets shunted open, I punch Mr G in the face. He isn't a trained fighter, or even someone with much of a build-advantage over me. That isn't to say that I am a trained fighter either, but I have experience and no sense of self-preservation or risk management – I know for a fact that if I just rush at him and beat him down, I'm going to come out on top in the end, even before my powers come into play.

He reels back and swiped out blindly with a rough swear, I step out of range of the wild counterattack - then tackle him with a flying leap. He has weight and reach on his side, but he isn't particularly fit and I have all the advantages I could ever need. He stumbles and tries to shake me, but my only aim is to drag him to the floor - and he doesn't have the leverage to resist me. He falls, and I quietly apply Clockblockers power to the pen lid clenched in my fist right in front of his face as gravity takes over. My hand stings as my momentum practically rips the object from my hands, but Mr Gladly isn't prewarned of the threat. He doesn't react in time to dodge, not even understanding the attack until it has pierced his eye.

His body comes to a stop around the time frozen object, I grip his skull hard and press down - feeling oddly little resistance as the action elicits an ugly scream from my victim which abruptly cuts off as I shake his skull like a ragdoll with the pen-lid frozen inside.

Gross.

"-well. Just hurry up and sit down." He shakes his head, then gestures back to the board. "Getting back to the lesson. Leviathan's continued attacks on major ports soon created a shipping crisis where many ships were unable to be assigned an appropriate port that could handle them. Standard trade routes became unprofitable overnight, and ships unable to offload their cargo were sometimes even abandoned by their owners entirely."

Score. Looks like it doesn't take him liking me that much better to let him play favourites.

I shuffle down the centre of the class, glancing at Taylor in the back and sending her a grin. A chair is thrust out slightly towards me, and I turn to find Emma deliberately not looking at me with a severe frown.

Right. Don't talk to Taylor at school and I can hang around with them as they ignore her, that was the deal. I mean, I didn't do much of that anyway and she didn't seem too broken up about it either - so it was a pretty lopsided deal in my favour anyway. Besides, Emma was crazy hot and how was I supposed to say no to a girl like that?

I send Taylor an apologetic look, but she just rolls her eyes and keeps taking notes. I take the offered chair with a grin, keeping my voice well below the quiet mumbling of the rest of the class and the droning of the teacher at the front. "Miss me that much?"

"Don't get too full of yourself." Emma snorts. "I need someone to copy off of when I fall asleep."

I glance to the other person opposite her. "What's wrong with copying your friend over there? Do you think so little of her? Should I feel compelled to defend poor Julia's honour?"

Julia glances my way, an ugly sneer on her face as she recognises me. "If you really have to sit here-" She gives a meaningful look at Emma. "-then do us all a favour and shut up."

Bitch.

Julia Robinson

Winslow Student 1/4

(ALRT) (HUNT)​

"Challenge." There was a time where two modifiers on a target was scary and new. But without any powers to speak of I wasn't scared of that increasingly common combination.

I spawn in Winslow, and wait halfway up the stairs. She should come to me with these modifiers.

She comes rushing at me from the lower floor, I take the time to run up to the higher one - then phase through to the bottom as she reaches me. She turns around, taking the steps as fast as she can - until Vista's power shrinks the air between me and her next step as much as I can. She skips over four steps within the space she would usually find one - then screams as she falls thanks to her suddenly unbalanced weight, heel bouncing off the fifth and sixth steps as her head bounces off the step behind her.

Bounce. Bounce. Scream. Bounce.

I wait for the drama to stop, then I nudge her broken body with my foot. "You dead?"

No reply.

"For what it's worth-" I sigh. "I feel a bit bad that you aren't. Because that angle looks really painful. And also because I don't have anything sharp on me. Choking you out takes ages to actually count as a kill, eye-gouging is super gross and I would feel bad going for a super-tryhard neck snap on someone who is already..." You wave a hand at the unresponsive girl.

Monologuing like this is getting to be a bad habit of mine, but it actually makes me feel a lot better. These challenges are somewhat lonely, action aside. I can spend days in a row not talking to anyone if I find a group of people that I'm interested in or encounter a particularly long challenge.

I mean, I pretty regularly went days without actually talking to someone – but that was usually because I was playing games or uncovering secret power-granting conspiracies than anything else.

My foot connects with her face, sending her sliding a short distance down the corridor. This is better. It feels a bit less personal than actually getting my hands dirty. It feels a bit easier to switch back to sweet-talking people in real life when I haven't just been violently choking them out moments before.

I miss her head but hear her ribs crack on the second strike. Crack more, was probably a better way to phrase it. Her entire body was a mess at this point, I could probably go off and eat some technically-zero-calory food at the cafeteria and wait for her to die to whatever terrible internal injuries she had – but I wasn't all that hungry anymore. I boot her again, her eyes rolling around in her skull as her head spins around as far as it will go before risking breaking her neck.

I almost make it the corner before my foot passes through her body entirely on the next swing.

SUCCESS

"-because some of us are trying to sleep here." I hear Julia's voice continue, a quiet snigger emerging from a nearby girl who I can't pinpoint until my eyes are back to normal.

"Sorry to break the news, but at least one of us in this row needs to do the work." Emma's voice rings out, just as detail and colour return to my vision.

Not for the first time, it strikes me just how normal Emma is when it comes to anything not involving Taylor.

"Anyone would think you only want me for my brains." I mourn.

"Sounds about right." The pair nod in sync with each other. "Nailed it on the head."

I make a noise. At least they're cute. For the rest of the lesson, I resign myself to making notes.


The end of the lesson signals the start of lunchtime. Faced with the unpleasant prospect of the Monday cafeteria menu, I find myself filled with determination to make some more progress. Taylor, most notably - I should honestly have tried her third challenge already, but losing to her the first few times was just… unpleasant. Checking out the trio's challenges was also on my to-do list. I didn't want to rush and risk exposing myself to some weird master/stranger protocol that Sophia applies to her everyday life or something – but I could always throw the fight after doing some information-gathering, just to help myself succeed whenever I was ready to take it.

Let's get started.

One lone bug harasses the gunman, the shadow state lets me slip free of the grunt restraining me and I slap aside the approaching knife thrust as I move to rush the gunman - freezing the blade in time at the cost of a painful cut to my hand, which is in itself preferable to whatever the failed thrust did to the now-screaming gangster as he massages his hand, thumb bent at a funny angle as he pays the price for not holding the blade properly when it froze in time - all of that momentum continuing to crash into the now-rock-solid hilt.

The gunman sneers at my approach. My old bug has perished already courtesy of a lucky slap to his own face, so I target another one on him as I start to weave from side to side. A few more seconds until I had my shadow state again, the man holds his nerve and trigger finger - but promptly loses that discipline when my fly suicides into his eye. The shot goes wide and I lunge at him, not even needing the shadow state as I shrink the space between us to wrestle the gun from his grip and kick his leg sideways - not breaking it like I had hoped but still sending him clattering to the floor in pain.

My foot slams into his unprotected nose, dropping him all the rest of the way to the ground like a puppet with cut strings. His hands try to raise themselves to defend against nothing as he unconsciously groans and shudders – eyes looking around and seeing nothing before he slumps down entirely.

For a moment, I consider using Panacea's power to blind them – but after a moment I realise that the HUNT modifier meant that he didn't need eyes anyway. I had bigger problems anyway, I had been keeping half an eye on my original end of the alleyway to be ready for the grappler to give chase and knife-chick to come at me again – but I hadn't seen any movement yet. The reason for that soon becomes abundantly clear as I peer into the gloomy area I originally appeared in. Two ABB thugs on the floor. A pair of crossbow bolts sprouting out of both of them.

Sophia was nice sometimes. I didn't know why she sometimes helped on these challenges, but anything that caused me less work was something I should be happy about.

I wasn't happy though. Not when I glance a little further down the alleyway. Towards the pair of figures walking menacingly towards me.

The pair of capes.

"This definitely did not go down like this." I complain to myself out loud.

The taller man, already standing almost a full arm's length above the man behind him - waves a hand wreathed in fire.

"Die." Lung tells me.

'Fuck you.' I try to tell him. "Gkh gk." I say. Something in my throat. I bring my hand up, trying to cough to clear it properly. My hand comes away soaked with crimson.

Too slow. Too sudden. I had zeroed in on the strongest Cape in the bay about to set the entire alleyway alight, and failed to realise that the most immediate threat was already behind me. Slowly, too slowly, the man at Lungs side crumbles to ash. Oni Lee – having long since teleported behind me to slit my throat.

My body drops to the ground, blurry vision coming to focus on the man standing over me. He staggers as a crossbow bolt lands inside his torso, but otherwise doesn't react. I attempt to say something derogatory about ninjas, but I can't even properly breathe at this point. As if to add insult to injury, the man standing over me erupts into ash just like the original - which comes to settle on me like the world's most unpleasant confetti.

FAILURE ​

The hint describes the EVNT modifier again for me. Useless.

Fucking ninjas. Didn't even feel it. He didn't stick around to gloat either. Even if I tried again and lashed out with a knife at the right time, I don't think I would even land the blow on him. Even if I did, I didn't have an answer to Lung. Shadow Stalker was helping with her covering fire, but that didn't help much in this case. She would just be a momentary distraction as I ran.

Ran where? The conditions for this event were the same as the previous, if I could escape then I would win. Unfortunately, with the HUNT modifier, the only real escape was either their deaths or some place where neither Lung nor Oni Lee were able to reach. I didn't have a place like that.

I wasn't too devastated, I had planned to throw this fight anyway if I had started winning, just so that my power didn't do anything crazy to try and cover the change - which I wouldn't mind letting happen if there wasn't a Ward hanging around as her best friend. But even my plans to leave it for another few days had been schooled now. I didn't have anything that could beat Lung in a fight. Running from Oni Lee was difficult, but not impossible if I managed to cripple him at the start.

The only place I was sure that would count as a successful escape would be the Protectorate HQ in the middle of the bay, with the forcefield bridge taken down after me. Lung shouldn't grow to a point where he could make it across the bay in that time if I didn't fight him, and Oni Lee shouldn't be able to cross that gap under his own power either.

Well. I've seen videos of Oni Lee teleporting into and from mid-air before, but he doesn't do it consecutively. He building hops for a reason, so clearly there is a limit to it.

That would count, surely. In the original challenge, merely escaping a certain distance granted the victory – even though in theory those men could have searched the city block-by-block to find me. The event must allow a 'good enough' escape even if it was conceivably possibly for the pursuit to continue in another form, like Lung charging across the waters of the Bay in a speedboat.

But to get that kind of distance away from the pair I need... flight? Superspeed? The full version of Clockblocker's powerset? And something to disable the bridge. I hadn't found any easy 'on-off' button when I had spent a few challenge-days on the artificial island, but surely, I could just rip up a cable somewhere or unplug a battery to turn it off. Superstrength might be needed for that, or at least some kind of offensive power.

Not something I had now.

Damn it. How come Emma was so much harder than almost any other civilian I had ever met? Was it just the association with capes? My power realising how much I wanted this one and taunting me with it? Bad luck? I didn't know, and that annoyed me.

Moving on. Madison wasn't within speaking distance in this class – but my power didn't care.

Leviathan.

Well. A scenario of a post-Leviathan attack. I can't say that I'm all that happy to be reminded that my city is a viable target for the lamest Endbringer, but at least I can take solace in the fact that there is a much nicer city with a better port just down the coast, and that we had already done such a good job wrecking ours that he no longer had any great reason to attack us in real life.

There seemed to be more people around this area, huddled under shelter and looking around warily at the people around them as they go about their business. This must have been recent, from their perspective.

A pair of workers up ahead pull a mangled body from the rubble of a destroyed store. One shakes his head, and they both drop him and move onwards - shoving aside rubble as they work to uncover more of the fallen building.

Well. I already knew my power invented scenarios on the fly sometimes. There was no particular reason to take this as a sign of gospel truth from the future. FAILURE

Hint: Some environments are inherently dangerous without any input from your target. Whether its finding yourself in the middle of an active battle, landing in the wrong place at the wrong time or simply becoming the victim of the fallout from a previous fight - make sure to watch your step when in unfamiliar territory!​

I snort. It wasn't like I was going to make a habit of getting jumped by normies. I didn't really get much scouting done this time, but I could probably assume, given the setting of an Endbringer attack aftermath, that I could find her in some shelter or temporary community, surrounded by a bunch of people who would die to protect her.

And the sight of a relatively well-off guy walking along the street was sure to incite greed in every other greedy or desperate soul on the way there.

Annoying. But not hard. Not in the way Emma's was. It would just need a few attempts to narrow down the search area and a good path to not get shot in the back while getting there. I wasn't likely to lose to a gunman I could see and react to, but if I was already hit then I didn't have a way to fix that.

It wasn't a slow struggle to catch her out, but instead a binary checklist about if I had a power that countered her or not.

That's lame."

She could be reasoned with. She had an ego. She wasn't 'tryharding' or even trying to win, she was just being herself. The scenario was built around her, she was just existing in it.

"I didn't even realise that it was you." The boy confesses. Kalin nods. That was good, he had always felt that there was a… respect of some kind between the two of them. "I just saw three huge guys chasing a girl and my body just moved on its own."

Kalin grins, that does sound like Greg. Zero thought behind anything he does. No consideration for the consequences.

Jake speaks up, not stopping his routine for a second. "Sounds bad when you say it like that, but we were just trying to scare her a bit. A hot chick asked Adam to do it in exchange for nudes. Girls are crazy, man."

Adam laughs. "I'm not usually the kind of guy to spread it around, but I know you're pretty cool about stuff like this. Here, have a flick through." He tosses the phone through the air.

Kalin stretches his arms up into the air. "I guess we should probably apologise as well. I was kind of pissed off, wasn't really thinking straight. Hope we didn't mess you up too bad?" Greg was still glancing between them, muttering to himself every now and then in between glances at the pictures.

Greg glances at Kalin, before an angry, somehow almost disappointed, expression crosses his face. "Fuck." He gets a curious head tilt in response. "Nothing. Yeah, it's fine. Already forgotten about it." He turns to Eve and Jacqueline. "What about you two? Not feeling bad at all?"

Jacqueline stops her press-ups for the first time in the conversation. "You big baby, want me to kiss it better?" She strolls forward with a smirk, showing off the vast difference in height. "I would have done exactly the same to anyone else if they had pulled a stunt like that. It looks like the lesson didn't ruin your pretty face, so I think you came out of it alright in the end." She blandly pulls his face directly into her chest with a smirk, suffocating him with her mounds on either side. "That makes it a bit better, right? You little perv."

The other girl in the trio waits for Greg to be released before speaking. "I don't apologise to anyone, but at least I ain't as much of a prude as her." With that, she pulls her sports bra up to expose her tits to the world without a shred of shame.

"Stop flashing the guy. You're only embarrassing yourself." Kalin laughs. "Now he knows for sure that you use pads."

"It's true." Jacqueline adds with faux-sadness. "Filling out even that tiny little bra of hers is just a bit too much right now."

The subject of their teasing covers herself again, red-faced. "Quality over quantity! Greg appreciates them." She whirls on Kalin. "And don't you laugh! Or should I start making jokes about how your needle dick barely makes a bulg-"

"I have to go." Greg interrupts, looking a little harried. He tosses the phone back to Eve.

Kalin blinks as Greg practically sprints out of the door. "What was that about?" It wasn't that he was concerned for a friend, because they weren't really friends. In fact, they've barely ever talked to each other apart from today – but they saw each other around the school and indirectly interacted. There was a mutual understanding there, or something like that. A kind of respect that didn't need to be acknowledged or justified.

Eve regards her phone for a moment. "At a guess, he might know a friend in a bad part of the world right now." She shows him the screen. "Looks like the smurf is about to descend on Canberra."

"Shit." Kalin pauses. "Where-"

She rolls her eyes. "Australia, dumbass."

"I'm the dumbass?" He retorts. "This is coming from you? Who had to leave all of your shit in the men's changing rooms because you can't line up enough brain cells to remember a 4-digit code for the women's? I can't believe this."

"Whatever. I guess that means school is cancelled for today." She cheers lightly. "Greg should have stuck around, I'm buying a pizza to celebrate the day off and I'm not sharing with you losers."

"Celebrating because an Endbringer is attacking? Kind of morbid." Jacqueline remarks.

"I'm not celebrating, I'm pre-emptively mourning. With pizza." The other girl justifies.

"Is that any better?"

"It totally is!"


Greg POV

Shit. Shit. Was I going to be too late? Probably not, but I should still hurry.

I doubted the teleporters would have come straight to Brockton Bay, given the relative lack of heavy hitters who went to Simurgh fights – so I could probably count on reaching the usual staging area in decent time.

I would be the first person to tell a new cape that going to an Endbringer fight was dumb. I didn't need telling.

But all of those capes. All in one place. I was almost drooling just thinking about it.

My costume was effectively non-existent. I had flipped my coat around and wrapped someone else's scarf around my head for now, but I would have to find something more permanent later.

The streets are fairly deserted for now, nothing stopping me from barrelling along to the high street. Don't need to run all the way to the PRT HQ, just need to get to the police station. Another few minutes-

Or not. I shout and wave at a passing police car, which pulls over by the side of the road. One officer gets halfway out of the car before I start talking. "I'm a cape! I need to get to the Endbringer meeting area. Can you take me there?" I warp space enough to make my hand appear to stretch across a particularly large cube from his perspective as I reach through it.

The officer clearly has mixed feelings about the request, but begrudgingly nods. "Get in."

It's a short ride, but it saves me a lot of time running.

The officer kicks me out of the car and after a quick verification with another PRT officer, I find myself pushed into a large room to sit among a sea of unfriendly masks and faces. Not aimed at me, but the atmosphere is grim.

"Who are you?" I spin, backpedalling for a moment as a PRT agent peers at me inquisitively.

"I'm a new cape. No name yet. I'm a Trump." That was information that was bound to get out eventually. No sense hiding it now and making them wonder why.

"You'll have to be inspected by one of our Thinkers upon reaching the staging area. Just stay put, they'll come to you." He taps something into his tablet. "They'll give you a temporary alias and confirm how long you can stay within a certain range of the Simurgh." Wasn't actually planning on getting in range at all, but it probably wouldn't be right to say that now.

"Alright." I give him a thumbs up. He makes a pointed gesture to a pile of domino masks, I make a point to steal one and slip it on subtly while nobody is looking. My scarf was good, but not that good.

I glance around. No ABB. No Merchants. Othala and Victor were the only offerings from the Empire. New Wave didn't usually show up for the Simurgh, but Panacea was apparently being escorted by Manpower – they likely wouldn't be anywhere near the fighting. Nobody from Faultline's crew. Armsmaster, Dauntless and Velocity had all opted in by the looks of it.

I didn't blame the others for sitting out. The mere fact that she was a flier made most people useless for anything other than search and rescue, the likelihood of being sniped out of nowhere from random bullshit and AOE was higher than against Behemoth and you had to put on a literal suicide collar to even be allowed in. If I didn't see this as a literal cape buffet that could accelerate me months ahead of schedule, I wouldn't show up either.

Not until I was strong enough to matter, anyway.

"Star Shifter will be teleporting in thirty! Gather up, please hold hands!" A guy with a megaphone calls out to us. I join the small huddle of capes, I get some interested looks – but not a single one gives me more than a nod. No real greetings. No attempts at recruitment.

Either they all expect me to die, or there is just an agreement to not try anything with anyone showing up for a fight. An extension of the Endbringer truce beyond the obvious. No poaching. I slot myself between Manpower and Velocity. Lots of capes for me to make attempts against here alone, but I wasn't trying anything with the threat of a Thinker inspection hanging over me.

…was this a bad idea? No. Probably not. They would be looking for people looking to break the peace or cause issues in the fight, and I technically wasn't doing that – and I fully intended to be hiding at the back with Panacea and Othala, because I was kind of a healer even if it sucked more than either of theirs.

"Porting!" A man in a skin-tight, shockingly yellow outfit appears – slaps his hand on Velocity's shoulder and I feel myself stretch and spin, head spinning wildly as my surroundings blur into a kaleidoscopic mess.

And then I was in Australia. Or at least, I assumed it was Australia. We might have gotten lost. I turn around, spotting a sea of capes and uniformed staff milling around with purpose. Right place then.

The group immediately splits up, off to collect armbands and collars being distributed outside of the areas that were clearly designated for incoming teleportation.

A smiling black-haired woman stands in front of me with a clipboard. "You must be the new Trump from Brockton Bay? Please, come with me. We have rooms dedicated to this process." She turns her back on me and walks towards a dull building, the uniform colour scheme and odd, square-like shape possibly implying it was built in a hurry by a cape.

I smile awkwardly and chase after her. I feel a little bit lost here, stemming from the complete lack of planning that went into this decision. Usually, I have things planned out in my head before I ever do them, and then the plan goes to shit from there – but completely winging it like this on something so important is a bit unusual for me.

"I have to make a report which will involve a few questions about your power and what you intend to do in the fight. I should note that a somewhat redacted version of the report will be stored in our databases for future reference, but you shouldn't worry about weaknesses we find being used against you later – we take security very seriously here." She moves into the first unoccupied room and claims one of the seats separated by a desk. I don't follow her in.

I stare.

"Do you now?" I ask quietly.

"Yes." She confirms, the smile never leaving her face. "It's something we go to great pains to enforce." She flips a fedora of all things onto her head, leaning back into her seat as she talks. "I can talk about your power with you, or I can talk about your power with someone else. It's up to you."

That was a threat. One that was working. I had gone into this assuming that I would be checked by a Watchdog Thinker, asking me a few pointed questions and kicking me out the door to do something vaguely helpful to the fight. What I was reading now, as I stared into her challenge box, said otherwise.

CONTESSA

AGENT OF CAULDRON 1/4

(DNGR) (HIGH)​

If she was with Cauldron, she probably knew about me. Was that good? Bad? What did they want from me at this stage? I had assumed my favours would be called in once I was Eidolon-tier, not earlier.

I could, at least, try to stack the deck in my favour – two new modifiers or not. "Cha-"

…

FAILURE

Certain challenges and individuals are considered high-difficulty (HIGH), being nearly impossible to defeat without clearing a large number of lower difficulty challenges first. Alternatively, a specific, rare power may be required in order to complete a condition where no amount of trickery or cunning can bypass the requirement.​

I stare at the failure screen as it fades away.

What just happened? What happened to the challenge? Did I cancel it somehow?

The timer ticking down from an hour in her vision implies otherwise.

"So." She smiles. All the more menacing for the apparent lack of malice. "Shall we talk?"

Can I just 'undo' the last hour of my life?

"Alright." If I get out of this without heading to the Birdcage, I'll be happy. "Let's talk."

Despite the length, I'm a little unsatisfied with this chapter. No lewds or real progress on the powers front and I think the overall chapter quality is down thanks to most of it being made on my phone while the laptop was out – but that will change next time around. Hopefully.

#680
I settle into the seat opposite the Cauldron employee. "So, I assume you aren't really here for a nice interview."

"No." She agrees easily. "And you aren't here to do your part to help fight the Endbringer. We're not concerned about that."

"You aren't?" Not going to the Birdcage? That was what I was hearing.

"In fact, we fully encourage you to stretch yourself as far as you can. We'll be very interested in seeing exactly how far your power can stretch." She hums to herself. "Which is why I'm here today, to call in one of our favours to satisfy our curiosity and to give you a warning."

"A special favour from me, right as an Endbringer attacks?" I cross my arms. "You want me to challenge her?" That made sense. If we got lucky, the fight would be a perfect mirror of what would happen during the attack – effectively pre-cogging whatever shifty plans she had.

"Not quite. We simply want you to see if it is possible." She sips at her water. "In fact, if you try to use your power against her, I will kill you."

The deadpan delivery of that last sentence catches me off guard, my brain taking a moment to process the threat for what it was. "Hey, hey!" I put my hands in the air for a moment. "No need for that. I probably wouldn't beat her anyway, but even if I did – I'm responsible enough to keep a mastered Simurgh out of trouble."

"Do you know why Alabaster isn't here?" She ignores my outburst. Rude.

"The Nazi?" I bite my lip for a moment. "Well. He's a Nazi, for one. Not usually much of the helping type." Othala excepted, but even she was only here for the Empire's PR engine.

"It's true that he doesn't usually show up anyway, but consider his power for a moment." Contessa meets my eyes. "A total body reset every few seconds. Active cape powers wash off him like water, body parts will be restored, mental damage and pain will be muted. His body can even reform elsewhere if the area where it would appear is blocked by something else. It's a power you can relate to yourself, correct?"

When I exited a challenge. Sure. "Did you have a point?"

"Alabaster exists in a city with no real threats to him. The only people with the capacity to kill him instantly are heroes who are aiming to capture and have an image to maintain. What would happen if he came to this fight, and stayed within range of the Simurgh's song past the time-limit?" She throws the question at me.

"He would become a Simurgh bomb." I reply confidently.

"Most likely." She flicks a pen against the desk idly. "Even if the rest of his body resets, even if almost his entire head can be destroyed and reconstituted without harm, the simple fact that he is thinking, making memories and decisions - that indicates that he is vulnerable. Grey Boy victims. The loop is supposed to be perfect, and yet they gain new memories of their torment on every loop. Even unpowered individuals, implying that the brain is exempt from the rules that define everything else in the loop. Making new memories and thoughts that would in theory allow them to become Simurgh bombs as well."

I could see where this was going. "And you think that might apply to me?" I point to myself. "I challenge the Simurgh, come back from the experience planning to bomb the president? Alabaster's powers are mainly for his body, I haven't seen any real feats against mental effects. Grey Boy is a special case even by cape standards. Some of the challenges I've been in, I've been a gibbering wreck on the floor – two seconds later I feel absolutely nothing except slightly annoyed at losing."

"I know that it applies to you." She holds one finger up in the air. Perfectly pointed at her own challenge modifier list. DNGR. "Danger. What do you think happened to you, when you tried to use your power on me?"

"I died instantly?" I hazard a guess.

She says nothing, clearly expecting more from me.

Wrong. Think about this. I close my eyes. Five seconds of silence. Ten seconds. She's patient, I'll give her that. I hiss in through my teeth as I realise what she's getting at. Looking at the conversation up to now, it seems a bit obvious. "You mind-wiped me inside the challenge." I open my eyes. "The same cape you used to erase my memories of the exact process behind how I got my powers." I knew the theory of it, but my memories of that day were falling asleep at my desk and waking up the next day in my bed with my powers up and running. I had been a bit too distracted to really think much more of it, but it was hardly something that needed much thought to realise.

She nods. "It's likely that the 'me' within the challenge has access to some of the resources of Cauldron as a whole. A perfect victory, from her perspective, might be that you have gained no knowledge and made no progress after being defeated. We have several capes that could theoretically manage to remove your memories of Cauldron like that, but we've never used them against you." She pulls out a mobile phone and starts to type away. "And, with no particular need to limit herself to only your new memories, she targeted all knowledge of our base of operations, including that which you learned before your attempt."

"And I got lucky, because she could have lobotomized me instead?" I could see that.

"Just so. It's a good sign, actually. Not permanently crippling you implies that the 'me' you faced shares at least some of our original goals, albeit with an overriding need to defeat you when you face her." She really has this conspiracy thing down doesn't she? Talking about the organisation's shady goals and sinister secrets without spilling the beans, I'm all curious now. "Needless to say, you should try to avoid challenging me again any time soon – or this conversation might become a repetitive one."

I mock-salute. "Yes, Ma'am. No using my power on you. Promise."

"Not until you are certain that you can win or kill yourself instantly. Months. At least." She holds my gaze steady, still typing into her phone without looking. "We have high hopes for your powers potential as you develop, but you don't need to be concerned about avoiding us in an attempt to avoid making enemies of us. If anything, I look forward to the day you succeed in defeating me – should you get that far."

"I… have no idea what to say to that." Someone telling me they were looking forward to the day I was good enough to Master them? Weird.

"You don't need to say anything." She cracks her neck. "In truth, most mental effects shouldn't be of concern to you. Active-types will expire with their owner once the simulation ends, as if they had been killed in real-life. Emotional, hormonal or direct body control will be reset with your body and mind. It needs to be subtler manipulation. Embedded either in your thoughts directly or within your power itself, however rare that is. The other reason we speculated that the modifier might show up is when it could be possible to stall the round out near-permanently."

I pause. I'm a dumbass, but I'm not completely stupid. That sentence may sound weird but it makes loads of sense if you think about it. "Like the Grey Boy bubbles you mentioned earlier, if he was still alive. If he hits me with one - I can't kill him, but I'm permanently kept alive without a way to forcibly leave the simulation or even kill myself properly. Probably not good for my mental health."

The Cauldron Cape nods. "It's speculation, but we believe that is correct."

I snicker to myself for a moment. "You know, you seem to know my power better than I do. I don't suppose you kept a manual lying around somewhere…?"

"We researched it with you quite extensively." Contessa confirms. "And then it seems you challenged me, among others, as you were about to be sent back home. With mixed results." And got my head cleared out for the trouble. Nice one, Past-Greg. Way to ruin it for everyone. I tilt my head. Mixed results? Did I succeed against someone else? Was that why she was here now instead of someone else? "We opted to simply monitor your natural growth rather than attempt to artificially accelerate you again." Again? I didn't have any powers at the start, so they tried and failed?

Ten bucks says my power screwed them with shitty scenario's for whatever Capes they tried to feed to me first. It was an asshole like that.

"No chance of you telling me any of the Capes out there that I'm likely to beat in one go?" I wiggle my eyebrows.

"No chance at all." She agrees. I pout. "And not purely because the scenarios your power creates require significant effort to model. We think the struggle quite literally makes you a stronger person in the end, and we suspect that your power is unusually active when it comes to directing your growth and the means with which you achieve it. In the limited time we had, we found that lining up Capes that you should have easily been able to defeat led to improbably difficult scenarios compared to targets you sought out yourself."

"Sure, but there's a difference between throwing me into a cell with crippled Capes and hoping I win and telling me the names of a few Capes that would really help me out later on." I tilt my head out towards the likely direction of the fight in the city, even if I couldn't see it that was there the fliers were coming from earlier. "The stronger I get, the more likely I can help with that. The faster that happens, the better it is – right? If you aren't scared of me getting too strong, then why not try a few things to make me as fast as possible. You only had me for a few days, we could experiment a bit more."

"There is such a thing as growth that is too fast, in this case." That didn't make any sense. Especially not when the Endbringers are right here, slowly destroying humanity in its entirety. I'd seen the doomposting that happened on PHO every now and then by new Thinkers. "Not to mention that most of those Capes you are talking about are all either locked in combat with the Simurgh, trying to destroy a large Tinkertech device she is assembling in the centre of the city or simply trying to protect the evacuating civilians from a bio-engineered horde of local fauna." Those who had left the city when the Simurgh's slow descent began, was what she meant by that. The ones stuck inside at this point wouldn't be so lucky unless Scion showed up any moment now, they were probably marking out the perimeter to be walled off already.

Wait. I blink. "They've already started?"

She stares at me owlishly. "You weren't intending to fight anyway. This is just the initial staging area, quite a distance from Canberra. The medical station for high-priority Capes and injured civilians that managed to be evacuated is just next to this building, which is the safest place for anyone in the area to be until the Simurgh leaves and a closer, more convenient base is established." Right. Don't want the Simurgh dropping a rock on Panacea, the actual fight must be miles away – otherwise the Simurgh changing course and drifting this way over the course of the fight might catch incoming reinforcements and the support team within building-tossing range if not her actual scream. "You'll be heading there after we're done."

There's no room for an argument in that statement. I nod. Of course, she knew that I intended to use Panacea's and hopefully Othala's powers in the med-tent to at least somewhat contribute while sticking around possible targets, but it did pinch at my ego to be so obviously excluded from the fighting. I could see why, obviously. If I got mind-whammied by the Simurgh, I would escalate into an unstoppable S-Class threat seeking to dominate every powerful Cape on Earth-Bet, turning them into my adoring slaves as I demand the submission of the entire world as its new God-Emperor.

I mean, I might end up doing that anyway, but I wasn't going to be evil about it. When I first saw this chick, I assumed that she was going to Birdcage or kill me for a good reason – and whatever reason they have for not doing that, and actively encouraging that, is good enough for me not to prod at it. For now. I mean, they are the Illuminati and power Mafia rolled into one – their plans for me probably weren't anything good long term. Some crazy mind-control stuff to rule the world from the shadows, something like that.

"Are you ready to take a look?" She stands up, circling the desk.

"At the Simurgh?" I swallow drily. "Now?" Now that I think about it, they never specified what would happen if I didn't follow through on a favour. I wasn't sure I wanted to find out. "You're sure it's safe?"

"You won't be entering her range at all. Your power works through windows, mirrors and see-through materials – as long as you can see the target in real time in sufficient clarity." Not videos, live-streams or CCTV – I tried that very early on. She pulls up a small bronze telescope with whirring, moving parts from behind the desk. Obvious Tinkertech. She holds it up to face me at a strange angle. "Look through this. Door."

A tiny window of space opens up in front of the device, allowing her to ease half of it through to the other side. I check the other side and note the disappeared half. A portal? I could really use that.

I peer through the lens. Even with the portal my sight a bit closer, all I could make out were tiny dots floating on the horizon. Before I can say anything, she adjusts a dial to zoom in closer. Still tiny, but there was less blank sky now. She continues to twist the dial as I speak up. She wasn't joking when she said I would be a long way away, at this distance I was surprised that my sight wasn't being blocked by debris, clouds or dust in the atmosphere. Clearly, they intended to take no risks here.

Then, another click and I'm watching the fight live. I recognise a few names and costumes. Eidolon and Legend at the front, carving away chunks out of the protective barrier encircling the Endbringer – concealing just enough of her that I can't fully focus on her enough. As I watch, a building uproots itself and adds itself to the shield as more debris frees itself from the shield – fired like a cannon at a trio of fliers, sending two of the pair plummeting to the ground as they connect. One is caught by their companion and flown away – the other left to hit the ground. Still no obvious line of sight on the main target. But there was Legend, one of the few Capes that a lucky victory would let me steamroll-

"Not a word. Not against anyone." I open my other eye to find a gun pointed at me.

I swallow drily, extremely aware of my mortality out in the real world. Right. No challenges. Apparently, that extended to other people around the Simurgh in her book.

"I know." I raise my hands. My shadow state could probably deal with it, but I didn't want to even guess what other tricks the Thinker had in store. "I'm just waiting for some debris to get out of the way."

She doesn't reply, or lower the gun. I close my left eye, hoping that if I ignored her it would go away. Back to the fight. A stream of blue energy erupts from Eidolon's hands, annihilating vast swathes of the debris while Legend lays into the Endbringer herself – who I could finally catch the barest glimpse of as she shields herself with her wings.

But even just seeing her wings was enough for me.

SIMURGH

Hope-Killer 1/4

(HIGH) (DNGR) (EVNT) (DOOM)​

I pull away, closing my eyes as I hear the portal snap shut. "Yep. I can see her. Four rounds. High-difficulty, danger, event and doom." I hum to myself in thought. "My gut tells me that it's going to be a standard Endbringer fight, with all of the usual allies – drive her off before the city needs to get quarantined. The doom modifier is for me spending too much time within a specific range, like the bomb collars except those wouldn't work on me after a few brute powers."

"Quite specific for a gut feeling." She comments, sweeping a few items into her suitcase. Including the gun, thankfully. "But thank you, that will be all."

I shrug awkwardly. "I mean, it's just a guess. It would make sense though." Awkward silence. "Is that really everything? It seems a bit anti-climatic for the super conspiracy to pop in on."

"We're always interested in powers that could conceivably work on the Endbringers. We would have done it while you were in our custody, but she has demonstrated a notably weaker ability to perform her usual manipulations to her full capabilities while in combat and under time-pressure. Pointing a telescope into orbit might have caught her attention or given her an opportunity and we couldn't take that risk." She taps her phone some more. "You should consider the Simurgh, Sleeper, Scion, Eidolon and myself to all be too dangerous for you to attempt for the time being – to the extent that attempting any of the first four without permission will force us to kill you."

The Sleeper, keeping me away from that made sense without any real need for elaboration. A bloodlusted Eidolon probably had a bunch of Master abilities at his disposal that might stick on me. Scion was kind of an odd one out, seeing as he actually appeared in my TIME modifier to kill me if I stalled long enough. They were probably scared of the kind-of-dumb guy not helping against Endbringers if I messed with his personality. Reasonable, and it's not like I could beat him until after Eidolon anyway. She was putting herself on a high pedestal there, but thinking about how much past-Greg had left me at a disadvantage when it came to learning about my power – I couldn't really disagree.

Now that I think of it, my power had immediately given me the tutorial rounds against my family once I got back home. Sure, it was a bit traumatic – but maybe there was something to her earlier words about my power deliberately making things difficult if someone else was trying to set me up without my input. If it was automatic then I should have gotten those tutorial rounds when I was wandering around their base.

The woman leans across the table to pin a badge against my shirt. "That will let you into the medical centre. A report has been made detailing your powers as a Trump that gains related powers as you build relationships with the Capes around you, with a secondary Thinker ability to subtly change your own actions to appear more likeable to other people and speculation about a weak, unreliable pre-cognitive ability. We'll leak it to the PRT when you make your debut."

I would have protested, but that actually made sense. There were certain aspects of my power that I couldn't hide. If the PRT went to another Thinker or just made a few assumptions based on incomplete data then that could go really badly, really fast. "Thanks, I guess." They were kind of nice for a shadowy organisation taking over the world.

"Door." With a single step into the portal opening behind her, she is gone – leaving me alone in the room.

Huh. I'm still alive, not in prison and I have approval from our secret lizard overlords to keep on going the way I have been.

"What do your powers actually do?" She sits down heavily as the last civilian patient starts to cough and attempts to stand. "I know I'm not really supposed to ask, but I've never met a power copier that my power blanks on like that."

"Weak copies of powers as I interact with people better. Seems pretty random about when it happens, but I guess I go to school or live somewhere close to Shadow Stalker, Clockblocker and Vista. Picked up yours and Othala's recently as well, hoping I can get stronger versions at some point or I'm going to be a C-Lister hack for the rest of my life." A little bit of truth to go with the lies.

"Probably not as bad as it sounds." She sighs. "But I get it."

"Wait." I slam my fist into my palm, brain catching up with the conversation. "Your power doesn't work on me when I'm using my copy? At all?"

The Dallon girl gives me a strange look. "I didn't try, but I guess not the bit that tells me what I'm doing, at the very least – which is pretty important if I want to not mess anything up on the inside."

"Can you try?" I hold my hand out. "Just, like – try and heal a freckle or something."

"Why not?" She grasps my hand and frowns at my face. After a few seconds she lets go. "Yeah, still works – but that's a lot harder and slower than usual. Best to keep it off if you ever land in hospital, or I'm not going to be able to do anything about the bullet in your chest."

I nod distractedly. "Good to know, good to know." Should have thought about it earlier, really. When I was up against Vista, our space-warping overwrote each other's powers. Against Taylor, my single-target bug control overruled hers entirely. I should be trying to be more aware of how powers stack up against their original owner, it wouldn't exactly have been hard to try hitting Panacea with her own power with a single experiment – and while it wouldn't have done much offensively if it gave me some defensive ability to not get one-shot at a touch then I was confident that I could beat the shit out of her before she worked past it. "Challenge."

Fighting Panacea with a simple CAGE modifier was pretty difficult for me before thanks to my power dropping me in without clothes that fully covered my skin, but now I knew that holding Panacea's power would likely slow her down enough to not one-shot me with a touch – it was worth having another shot. I was going to hold off until I found a Blaster, but I had subtly tried two of the patients already in-between healing sessions and both times I had been fried at range after exhausting my shadow state.

I idly select Echo, miming a punch in the air as I had seen the now-deceased original user do before. The power dims in my mind, but doesn't deselect itself. Only one action, and I couldn't store it while switching to another power – use it or lose it.

Well, that was fine. I backstep for a moment. Perhaps some other combat-veteran Capes would be wary of my actions, but Panacea wasn't a real fighter – she was just running straight at me again with her hands outstretched.

I trigger the echo, the punch rocketing into her right cheek and stopping her charge cold. No instant knockout, but enough for me to capitalise on. Moment of truth. I grab Panacea's power and punch her in the face.

Not unconscious, nice. I kick at her wildly, shifting into my shadow state as she throws herself into a full-body tackle around my waist. She lands heavily on the floor, I kick at her head as she tries to shield herself – one leg being grasped in both hands as she slides her hand under my socks to touch bare skin. My vision spins for a moment, but I'm still aware enough to stomp down at her with my other foot. Her grip slackens, only to disappear entirely as a second clean connection ends the fight entirely.

Easy. I'm such a better fighter than her that even if it only takes her, say, five seconds to knock me out, that's still a few seconds too many for her to beat me 1-on-1.

SUCCESS

Reward: Amy Dallon+​

Nice. Seeing as there was a likely power attached to the third round, I might as well try the next one as well.

Amy Dallon

Heroine 3/7

(GANG) (ALRT)​

"Challenge." No sense in dragging it out.

I come to inside an unfamiliar building. Looks like a hospital of some kind, but not Brockton General.

Nobody immediately comes out to rush me, which with the ALRT modifier is a bit of a surprise. I walk forward, glancing through each room in the corridor as I go. Nothing there. Standard patient there. Nothing that would indicate Panacea and her crew raring for a fight.

At least, until the far side of the corridor erupts as Glory Girl soars through the open double doors – giving me a brief glance at Panacea leaning over another patient while glancing warily at me before the doors close again.

I see. The GANG in this case are all injured at the start. They join the fight as Panacea heals them, so I need to rush to the far side of the building and interrupt her before the numbers get too far in her favour.

As it is, I'm not getting past Glory Girl. I grimace slightly as she pulls down a light fitting and hurls it at me like a javelin – following up with a kick that probably would have separated my head from my body if it hadn't immediately killed me on connection. I'm not even going to try on that front, if I could manage that fight I would have beaten Glory Girl's first challenge already.

FAILURE

Hint: Some challenges can be approached in different ways depending on your abilities. Play to your strengths! Use brute force where you are stronger, blitz past your enemies when you are faster and outwit your enemies when you are smarter! Few opponents will have the perfect answer to every approach available to you.​

I tilt my head. The hint probably had a point this time. The only objective was to assassinate Panacea. With the ALRT modifier, everyone knew I started in that corridor. Even if I had a speedster power or teleportation, it was unlikely that I would be completely fast enough to prevent Glory Girl from joining the fray entirely – but if I just hid somewhere, or tried to sneak around the outside of the building. Perhaps even time-locking the door to try and shut them out if they all left the room.

Hell, for all I knew Panacea would wander off alone into the girl's toilets after healing everyone and sending them off to search for me. Even if I couldn't beat Glory Girl I had a few options available to me.

"Challenge?" Amy Dallon peers at me. "Are you alright?"

Did I say that last one too loud? Probably shouldn't start it in the middle of a conversation when people are paying close attention to me. "Yeah. This whole thing is a, uh, real challenge for me. My power feels kinda weak compared to what you can do."

"I can't be everywhere." She gives me a faint smile. "For what its worth, I'm glad you're here. It's always nice to see another healer around, especially one from the Bay. The Nazi doesn't count."

I grin. "Thanks, I'll try to swing by and say hello sometime – hopefully when my powers are no longer so weak that I might lose in a fight against Velocity or Chubster."

I'd have liked to see another healer around too, I was really hoping that Scapegoat would be here – but no dice. That offensive part of his powerset would have been a crazy addition to my arsenal.

Not that today had been a bad haul at all, and it wasn't even done yet.

I glance around at the near-empty room. Volunteers were emptying out beds and starting to pack things away, the number of injured reduced to almost nothing apart from minor scrapes and bruises not dangerous enough to need parahuman support. "So, what happens now? Do we all just pack up and go home, or do we stick around until everyone else comes with?"

Amy makes a face. "Not a clue, actually. At a guess, they'll start teleporting people back in groups once everyone from the area is gathered together. I guess we just stick around for a while until they call for us."

"Sounds fun." I tilt my head from one side to the next. "Well, I guess I should go and introduce myself to a few other people while I'm here. Not exactly the debut I was hoping for, but it would be rude to deny them the honour of being in my presence."

"I'm sure they can't wait." Sarcasm is rude, Amy. She stands up as well. "I'll see you on the port back, I guess. Try not to get lost."

I snort. I wouldn't be going far. I direct my gaze to the few Capes that were supervising the proceedings and playing at protection for the medical team. Victor, one of my main hopes for becoming a martial wizard. Manpower, my main hope for rolling over future Shadow Stalker challenges. Armsmaster and Dauntless were out in the field somewhere, I could at least try to handle the latter. Narwhal. Dragon. Legend. Alexandria. Whatever other fliers and Blasters I could spot as they returned to their hometowns.

I needed to at least make an effort – even if it was kind of difficult to achieve a win on the first try, that argument didn't hold weight for the Brockton-ites. I would undoubtedly be seeing them again at some point, so even just seeing what their challenges were would help guide me for the future.

I bounce on my heels for a moment. Right then. Let's go and break the Endbringer Truce even more than I already have.

Even if Cauldron wasn't going to step in and help make me a god overnight, there was nothing stopping me from doing that myself. I didn't just want to be a hero in theory, winning only in the safety of my head. I wanted to be a badass in the real world too. I wanted people to rely on me – to do things that nobody else could, much like that dead Cape earlier. A new Eidolon. What people were hoping Dauntless would be before he started to get diminishing returns on his items.

I had a long way to go. Time to get to it.
