#778
I couldn't sit around and stall for too long. The Simurgh fight had been quick and brutal, from what little I could tell without ever being involved in the actual fight. As a defeat ending in the city being sealed off, there weren't any notable search and rescue efforts to be performed after the perimeter had been established and the countdown to leave the area had ticked down to zero. Not that I was anywhere near that, but as a bit of a Cape fanatic, I knew a bit more about how Endbringer fights went than most rookies.

Most of the people here would be leaving almost immediately – at least, whenever the teleporters lined them up in their schedule. A few volunteers, primarily long-range Blasters and Movers, would be responsible for enforcing the quarantine alongside the local army, while the normal humans worked on erecting a basic wall, monitoring system and fortifications around the city. A lot of people triggered during and after Endbringer attacks, so the danger of approaching even what looked like innocent citizens trying to flee was high enough that most would-be escapees would be bombarded from a kilometre away without even knowing how they died.

A few months ago, I would probably have described that as 'kind of metal' or 'hardcore as fuck' from the safety of my room. Somehow, a little closer to the action, it just left an oily feeling in my stomach.

But that's why I'm here. Doing my thing. If I had my way, the next time that the Simurgh came calling, I would be a living god – ready to send her packing on arrival. Or, better yet – convert her into a cute angel waifu like the one currently set as my desktop background.

Sure, there were some moral quandaries about the steps I would be taking to get to that point – but in reality, the wider world already agreed with my 'greater good' argument. Just look at Heartbreaker – yes, he tends to lie low most of the time, but he has clashed with law enforcement before. If the world really wanted him gone at the expense of the damage the people around him would cause after his death – he would have been vaporised a long time ago. Same argument with me, if I managed to stop an Endbringer – or even all of the Endbringers – anyone would consider that a worthwhile tradeoff for a guy they would probably never meet having a superheroine-filled harem.

But that's way too far off in the future. Talking about that like it is going to happen anytime soon is almost as cringy as the people acting like Dauntless was going to be Triumvirate within the next decade - when it was painfully obvious that his gains were starting to get diminishing returns already. I was pretty sure I didn't have limits like that, but I wasn't going to get cocky and assume that I didn't. What if I won a few more challenges and got a pop-up saying that I could only store ten powers and that I had to pick one to drop in order to free up the slot? That would suck, and I couldn't entirely rule it out either.

No. Smaller goals. Armsmaster first. That was the level I needed to be at. I loved the guy – no homo – but if I could beat Armsmaster, I could consider myself at the top of all the capes in Brockton Bay. Lung might be the exception to that, but he tended to excel against teams and completely job in smaller engagements so I was probably going to be a good counter to him if I caught him at the right time with a hard-hitting powerset. After Armsmaster, I could just pick any A-Class threat and surpass them. Then the Triumvirate – and only then could I dare to consider approaching S-Class threats, when I could confidently say that I was the strongest Cape in the world.

But even Armsmaster was too lofty a goal for me right now. I could see him from here, standing stiffly among a group of other heroes as he waits for the Brockton Bay group to be called up – but there wasn't any point in challenging him. With the PREP and CONT modifiers to worry about, I didn't have a chance of winning, nor did I have anything to gain from fighting him over and over apart from giving him more data to work with. I needed more powers in general before I could dream of taking him down, even just for the very first challenge.

Fortunately, if there was one thing that this Endbringer fight had provided – it was a significant number of Capes that I rarely met and the opportunity to challenge them. I might not be able to just throw down with every Cape I saw thanks to my power kindly throwing a warning headache and increasing levels of aches and lethargy my way whenever I started doing too many challenges too fast – but I could certainly give a few of the Capes currently waiting for a teleport home a round or two in the metaphorical ring.

Which, really, was the hardest part of attempting to direct my growth in skills. It was one thing for me to point out certain Capes that would be ideal to challenge and grow from – Purity, Hookwolf, Miss Militia, Leet to name just a few – but actually laying eyes on those people in such a large city was far more difficult than you would think. Well, it made sense. If it was that easy for a random civilian to find a villainous Cape or get easy access to the local heroes then that was just begging one of their enemies to take a hit out on them. New Wave learned that the hard way.

In terms of maximising the pure, economical efficiency of my challenges while I was here – it would generally be better to focus on people who live in the Bay, safe in the knowledge that even if I lost, it would still be a valuable learning experience that would help me beat them later. It was true that there were fliers and Blasters around that I would dearly love to beat – but that was a club that was somewhat hard to enter without having a similar power of my own. And it wasn't like there was a huge lack of Capes like that in the Bay – I could just stick with those I already knew when I had less pressure on my schedule.

It wasn't that I wasn't interested in the likely top-tier powersets that the Triumvirate offered, or the exploits I could use with someone like Narwhal – but I just didn't have a power that let me hit at their level. I could punch people, sneak up on them, stab them with a knife or drop something on their head – which worked very nicely for people who I could physically match or didn't have a power suited for close combat. With Narwhal as an example, even if I got a perfect sneak attack and stabbed her in the neck – she would take a literal blink of the eye to separate my head from my shoulders on pure reaction. There wasn't anything to learn from that.

I mentally run through the list in my mind. Dauntless. Armsmaster. Velocity. Othala. Victor. Panacea. Manpower.

Out of those, Othala's challenge was still cooling down after my previous failure. Panacea's cooldown was a stage higher, and I wouldn't be able to repeat it today without stopping by the Dallon household trying to catch a glimpse of her – not happening. Dauntless had little to no value in completing other challenges thanks to my inability to take in equipment so far, but there was a lot of potential to get the ball rolling on powering up in real life. I narrow my eyes at him in thought.

DAUNTLESS

Hero 1/6

(ZONE)​

Just a limited area to engage in, not a particularly harsh modifier unless it was one of the ones where he would try to escape – which would be impossible to stop against the teleporter. That seemed unlikely though, there was already plenty of difficulty to the challenge thanks to his armoured costume – without me having a likely way to get through it. With all of his defensive and mobility capabilities, I didn't stand much of a chance here however much I really wanted to get started on his power.

Armsmaster was a dead-end as well, for reasons already mentioned. Victor and Manpower on the other hand, were much more viable targets. Manpower might be a Brute, but he wasn't the brutiest of Brutes – if that made sense. It was possible to catch him unawares or without his power augmenting him. Victor was a baseline human with a bunch of extra skills to work with, which should be even easier.

Not only did I feel like they were within reach, but their powers were also useful. Manpower doesn't get to flex his powerset much, but its value to me was almost entirely focused on the fact that beating him would likely give me some form of electric powerset to beat Sophia with – on top of being my first Brute-like power in general that would finally give me a meaningful advantage in a melee that didn't require an unarmoured target. A two-for-one, even if I didn't see him reliably enough to properly pursue beating the rest of his challenges. Victor's benefits didn't need much explanation. A little time hanging around a douchebag boxer or two, a few gun-toting gang members and maybe some star athletes and students around Winslow and I would be an all-star student and combat expert before I knew it.

Not that it would pay to get cocky and assume this was a guaranteed win, even if the cooldowns on the first round were sometimes fairly short – there was a chance that people wouldn't stick around long enough for me to get a second shot.

Best hurry then.

VICTOR

Empire 88 1/5

(REAL)​

And then Mr Hair-Gel himself.

MANPOWER

Hero 1/5

(TIME)​

I let out a cheerful hum to myself. In both cases, I had to deal with only a single modifier that didn't seem likely to cause me much lasting trouble. Manpower's fight would be won with a surprise attack in the opening minutes or not won at all, making the reinforcements trickling in through the TIME modifier mostly irrelevant. The real part of the challenge came from the man himself and his powerset.

Victor's fight would depend on the scenario I was dropped into – REAL modifiers could be both a good and bad thing for me. They make the target a bit more unpredictable and better at reacting to my adaptations as I repeated the challenge, but also gave me a slight layer of security in that they didn't go absolutely 0-100 on the murder scale the moment they saw me. For Victor, that probably didn't mean as much as it did for Sophia – I was pretty sure he wouldn't care about pulling a gun on me and letting loose if I started a fight out of nowhere, not to mention the fact that his power wasn't so visible that it would stop him from being able to use it without outing himself in public.

I glance around for Velocity, intending to scan him as well. I saw him not too long ago so there wasn't any real chance of him being dead, but I can't spot him right now. I glance across at other groups to try and find him. Toilet break? Running an errand? Whatever the case, I'd get him before I was done for the day. Velocity was pretty low on the Brockton Bay tier-list, but his power would actually be quite valuable for me even in whatever diminished form I ended up with – I could use the mobility a lot better than he ever could.

Of the two I could see now? Victor seemed the most likely choice to start with. Manpower was clearly the more difficult of the two and I wanted every advantage I could get for that fight. Victor also lacked the armour that I was finding so difficult in a few of my recent fights. Armsmaster, Gallant – even Vista to an extent. Parts of their costume that just didn't give me a cheap way to win the fight with a lucky stab.

Victor it is then. "Challenge."

I grimace in discomfort as the word leaves my mouth, my body aching just a bit more noticeably than before. Panacea's earlier comment about how tired I seemed suddenly feeling a lot more accurate, but a bit of lethargy wasn't going to cripple me – I would just have to be careful not to overstretch myself. I could enjoy a bit of downtime tomorrow to recover, but opportunities like this didn't show up every day and I had to make the most of it.

I glance around as the challenge constructs itself. Light. Sound. Colour. Well-dressed patrons weave through obstacles that have yet to form around me. Some kind of nightclub? A high-end restaurant? Patrons and service staff mill around the tables. I was sat alone at the edge of the room, but I couldn't spot Victor from my current position – and surely it would be a bad idea to run around drawing attention to myself without knowing what I was looking for.

There was no way that Victor would have any reason to be in costume around here, unless he was due to attack the place with the Empire? No, white people were clearly the majority here – it was unlikely to be a target like that. Enough non-whites to discount the possibility of it being Empire owned, so it was likely that Victor was here as a civilian. A bit unfortunate, but more unsurprising than it would have been for most Capes – he was known to disguise himself as a normal guy during Cape activities anyway, given his powerset. I'd have to do a bit of searching around for people who fit the bill before I skipped to the stabbing.

But before that, I needed to get out of sight. Into a position where I had a clear view of the venue, without being easily spotted myself. Even with the REAL modifier, I couldn't be fully confident that Victor wouldn't start gunning for me the moment he spotted me – while some REAL targets ignored me until I did something suspicious, that wasn't consistent enough for me to rely on it when I may only get the one serious attempt to win before they disappear back off to their own territory once we teleport home. Even then, he had probably stolen some super-secret spy training at some point and might spot me if I made it obvious I was stalking him. The longer I stayed out in the open, the more chance I had of a disguised Victor glancing over his shoulder and spotting me in the crowd without me even realising that he had aggro'd on me.

I push myself up and out of the chair, the sound easily masked by the thrum of music and the bustle of the patrons. Fortunately, not far from my starting position I can see a sign with directions to the nearby toilets – providing me an easy getaway from any stray glances from my target that was likely among the patrons somewhere. I give a nervous glance at the hand-dryers arrayed along several edges of the wall. Ideally, leaving the building entirely would be for the best – but even if the outside was beyond that wall, there were great odds that I would run into a cable or three and cripple myself, or worse, knock myself out and end the challenge.

Fortunately, going sideways wasn't my only option. This room had provided me with exactly the kind of escape I had in mind. Past the glamour of the nightclub outside, the toilets were notably more bland and spartan – the grid-like appearance of the ceiling and the rugged appearance of the panels between the lines was my ticket upwards to the rest of the building. Getting into the ceiling and going upwards again would take me up to the floor above, or perhaps even just outside if this was just an extension tacked on to the end of the building. Either way, I would be in a great position to just keep climbing upwards, then hanging out far above the stage, the diners and partygoers to observe what was going on.

After all, who even looks up at the ceiling in the middle of whatever spectacle performance was being put on as entertainment next? I would find out, I suppose.

I enter one of the stalls, grimace, flush and then drop the seat down to give me something to stand on for more height. Vista's power shrinks the empty space between the ceiling and the lowered toilet seat, allowing me to reach out and simply brush a ceiling panel out of its socket and nudge it to the side. I test the weight briefly. I'm too heavy – but the object is small enough to let Clockblockers power turn it into something sturdier than the rest of the building put together. I follow that with a light swing upwards and let Shadow Stalker's power carry my momentum up through the rest of the ceiling to drop me into a dark, cramped area. Another floor above me, I would guess.

The moment that Vista's power returns, I continue upwards – this time able to spot the layout of the cables on the ceiling and deliberately avoid them before once again phasing through to the next floor. It's an easy process, and not actually all that time-consuming despite the waiting-around for certain powers to recharge or finish their duration. I hadn't really considered it before, but I really did have a great selection of powers for ascending a building like this.

With some minor acrobatics to help bridge the gaps that Vista's power doesn't quite stretch across, it doesn't take me long to find myself next to a convenient window to phase through to perch on a ledge outside. From there I start climbing from handhold to handhold along the gentle curve of the roof and signage instead, inwardly grateful that the scenario hadn't involved rain otherwise I would certainly have slipped off by now.

The night sky, only broken by flashes of headlights and neon signs on the street below, gives me enough confidence to risk glancing through a skylight to properly take in the layout of the room that I had so hastily left before. Time to work out where I needed to drop back in. I already knew from my brief glance around the room at the start, the area immediately below this domed roof should be dominated by the stage – which was then surrounded in a half-circle by the diners seated at their tables, alternating between watching the show and conversing with their companions. Now, with more time to spare, I focus my attention on more specific features. The half-balcony off on one side of the room with a smattering of guests distracted by themselves, the musical band hidden in an alcove just off the side of the stage. The bundled-up curtains that would conceal the stage when out of action – all things that I didn't have time to appreciate when I was getting myself somewhere less conspicuous.

My first plan had been to literally slip through the roof directly onto the light fixtures – freezing them in place as I land to prevent any unexpected noise or disruption from announcing my presence. Upon closer inspection, I wasn't nearly so confident in that idea – the fact that the lights were obviously getting power from somewhere had slipped my mind until it was right in front of me, which would require me to come it at a bit of an angle anyway, but I also wasn't convinced that using it as my perch would go unnoticed forever. Clockblockers power probably wouldn't allow me to tag the entire frame thanks to its size, so I would have to hit a smaller part of the fixture – which left the rest of the light free to start swaying, clattering and generally attracting attention either on the initial landing or in the brief moment I would have to reapply it whenever it wore off. Considering I expected to be observing for a while, that was too much of a risk to allow.

My gaze slides around to other elevated platforms that I could conceivably use. A number of overhangs and ledges were available thanks to the general architecture of the building, but they offered little cover in return. The curtains of the stage, however, might be a viable target. The bundled-up edges were out of the spotlight and relatively shrouded in darkness, with a great elevated view for me to watch the guests from. I could reach it quite reliably by jumping through the wall right next to the stage, and the lack of obvious electronics gave me hope that I wouldn't be punished for the attempt.

I move away from the skylight and skip along the rest of the roof, trying to guess the correct amount of distance I would need to travel to slip through the wall at the correct point. About… here. I slip through the wall, exactly a second later finding myself ejected into a pillow-like mess of bundled fabric after a short fall. I remain there for a moment, listening for any sounds of concern from the crowd or any curious staff coming to investigate my entrance – but nobody seems to have noted the slight shuffling in the shadows, or perhaps just brushed off the activity in the corner of their vision as the off-stage crew doing a task of some kind.

The lack of attention enables me to squirm around in the fabric until I could see out between the folds in the fabric and netting around me, body hidden and face concealed in the darkness – inspecting the stage and patrons without fear or urgency for the first real time.

If, after all of this trouble, it turns out that he's sitting out the back in costume and all my effort here was for nothing? I'm going to be so annoyed. My only argument against that was that my power usually didn't mislead me – if I started facing towards a building or street, that was usually the way to go. There were a few cases where finding the target was part of the challenge, like with Madison's current challenge – but even then, I'm fairly sure that I wasn't being pointed towards the opposite end of the city as my target.

I'll just assume he's in the crowd somewhere. Time to start narrowing it down. I filter out the more diverse tables first, I didn't know if he was outright as racist as the typical E88 thug – but it was probably a safe bet he wouldn't have any regular friends among the minorities of the city. From there, eliminate anyone who looked… well, like me. Even if I had gained a bit of muscle recently, Victor was built like a tank – a muscle-guy, even if he was wearing a suit or something he would stand out like a sore thumb among the classy types likely to visit this establishment.

One lone man on a table in the corner. A couple talking amongst themselves front-and-centre. A family group enjoying a meal on the outer ring. I mentally cross out the last one, the kids looked too old – and assuming the rumours that Victor and Othala were together were true, my research into Othala's skintight bodysuit over the years could attest to the fact that she was certainly not a MILF.

The couple could be Victor and Othala, or he could be the man on his own in the corner. They both had similar features from what I could see. I resolve myself to wait. The REAL modifier meant that my targets would actually do something other than sit there forever as the night went on, hopefully letting me eliminate one of the remaining two options to find the real Victor.

I wait. And I wait, and I wait some more. Meals are delivered and taken away, customers come and go – and the stage is filled with act after act to entertain the crowd. It's actually quite enjoyable, like I've just gone to a theatre for the evening instead of plotting a murder. The nice thing about my fist-fights with Sophia at school was that they really let me get a grip on what her power was good at – helped me speculate on how it worked, and how an expert could use it in ways that really messed with a normal persons instincts. He lucked into avoiding my own attempt to take advantage of his predictability, but I had also managed to guard against a blow that might have ended the fight there and then. I'd take that.

He seems warier about leaving his speed state now, seemingly content to just keep me on edge as much as he can for every inch I take towards the relative safety of the wall. I take advantage of the low cooldown of the echo power to keep down his angles of attack, switching into the shadow state whenever he succeeds in knocking me down or tripping me up. Then, finally, I hit the wall.

Now things are looking up. In our limited exchanges without his speed power, he hasn't done all that well. He's well-trained, sure – but it clearly wasn't his comfort zone even before I had my single use of Vista's power used in small bursts to shrink or expand the air in a wide, random tunnel before me – only lasting about twenty seconds before I replace it in a different formation again. The echo, enabling me to constantly threaten a large area around me with a casual leg sweep and win any normal exchange of blows when he doesn't escape with his power.

I didn't have anything to be too afraid of here. His breaker state was annoying, but it wouldn't put me down – it was more like being stuck in a room full of noisy, angry children. Sure, I could feel the impact of each hit and they all inevitably snuck past my guard to exposed parts of my body, but as long as I protected the right areas I could just put on a tough face and grimace through it. Even strikes to my groin and face didn't really hurt, I just had to fight my instincts to not flinch at every blur in that direction. He wasn't capable of dropping the breaker state at the exact moment of impact, so any of the real attacks had a notable and obvious wind-up to them for me to respond to. I could manage this.

The thought of pulling a string of fabric loose from my clothes and stretching it into a lethal weapon for him to run into does occur to me, but even if he was a terribly weak hero – he wasn't stupid. He would probably see me setting it up, and I was fairly sure PHO said that his particularly brand of speedster was more about him going at normal speeds with everything else slowed down, rather than actually zipping around too fast to stop when he feels his leg brushing up against a time-locked thread. Without the help of gravity or actual speed, I was fairly sure that someone running into a thread at normal speeds would be more along the lines of 'bad papercut' and a bruise rather than the instant, confused bisection that I was dreaming of.

I feel a pressure at my back and then my heels, finding myself being inched forward as the wall presses against me. The room was shrinking? I had guessed that might happen previously in the previous times that I had seen the CAGE modifier but it was hard to really tell at the time with the bland shape and colouration of the walls. This was the first time that it had come up as something that might be of use in a fight, I just had to figure out how to use it.

My next thought is that I could try diving back into a pile of containment foam with the shadow state, then wait long enough for Velocity to get squished up against it as he would have no similar method of getting deep inside of it. Unfortunately, the piles weren't uniform in size, and it was probably a safe guess that he would find a safer spot to stand while I found out exactly what happened to any squishy people inside when containment foam was compressed. My guess was that it would get messy.

But the idea itself was workable. Trapping him between a rock and a hard place. It took the burden away from me trying to get a finishing blow on a target that was near-impossible to hit when he wasn't being cocky – and instead just required me to hold him in place for some time. That was much more achievable, even if still difficult.

The wall nudges me forward another half-step again, slightly faster than before but still very slow – a decrepit old man hobbling across a street with their walking stick would easily outpace its advance for now, and with the original arena stretching out like a football field I wasn't feeling any major time pressure. What to do? Clockblocker's power was the only thing that could act as an anvil for the wall, but my weak variant wouldn't work on anything that he was wearing or items that were over a certain size. I could take my shirt or belt off, sure – but to then position it in a way that would kill him once I held him into place was the hard part.

Perhaps setting something up for him to see coming in advance was an impossible idea, made worse by the fact that the timer might well expire at an inopportune moment if it didn't immediately start crushing something. I couldn't use my own clothes either, the power doesn't work on things that are encompassing me or others like that. Although, saying that, I already knew that my freezing power would forbid me from tagging a watch around my wrist but allow it when I was just holding it – if I did the same to my shirt, that was probably the largest object I would be able to use in this arena. As soon as I got a solid hold on Velocity, I could freeze it and wait for the wall to catch up.

Too complicated. Dumb it down. Stick to the basics. There was no way I could get the shirt into a decent position, freeze it and then trap him against it as the wall approached. Even then, I would have to remain there holding him in position – unable to shift out without freeing him as well, leaving it entirely up to luck as to who got killed first. I didn't need to kill him outright like that – I just needed to win the fight off of the attack, a massive injury or crippling blow would suffice too. He would never let me attempt it again if it failed, unlikely to even enter my half of the room until I either starve or the challenge decides I've taken too long and awards him with enough buffs to wipe the floor with me.

If I could just get any grip on him at all, I could go back to my string idea. Don't worry about trying to get him to run into it, just keep him near a wall – grab onto an important appendage and freeze the string into a blade that would slice off the offending limb once the wall reaches the thread despite any resistance from the flesh between the two objects. All I would have to do is survive his attacks for the few moments it would take for the wall to trap him in place, then he would abruptly find himself crippled and bleeding out with no way for him to do anything about it.

Easy. All I had to do was catch him. I'd get battered for it, undoubtedly, but he wasn't so much stronger than me that I couldn't take a solid hit or three if it would assure victory. I absently pull a loose thread away from my shirt, snapping it cleanly off and pinching it between two fingers – just waiting for an opportunity to use it.

I start to slide my way towards the corner of the room, ignoring the obnoxious harassment from the speedster trying to keep me off-balance and threatening blows at my face and crotch. He never fully commits though, likely realising the same thing that I had – shifting back to normal speed gave me a chance to counterattack as well. Even something as simple as latching onto his fist would all but eliminate his power, his speed wouldn't help him break free from my grip – so he was as stuck as I was, waiting for me to make a mistake so that he could capitalise risk-free. Neither of us had the capability to truly hurt the other while the stalemate went on.

At least, until he makes a mistake. He had doubtless assumed that my plan was to abuse the corner to limit his options even further, forcing him to face me from a single direction without the possibility of flanking or dodging out to one side. This time, he commits to preventing me from reaching that – the continuous deluge of weak hits driving me backwards despite my attempts to push forward. One step, two steps – I begin to let myself get pushed backwards even more, leaving one arm hanging out to the side and holding the echo there, not as a fully formed strike like he had come to expect, but merely as the solid shape of my arm that would serve to bar his path should he try to walk through it once activated.

He steps into the invisible trap, and then past it. I don't hesitate in my immediate assault – triggering the echo to block any quick backsteps out of my reach and immediately using Vista's power to shorten space between us. My low tackle aims down at his legs, and his immediate retreat is blocked by my ghostly hand for just a moment too long – my arms bundle around his leg even as he ducks under the outstretched limb, realising too late what had occurred.

"Gotcha." I grin at him as we tumble to the floor, with myself wrapped around the single leg I was able to reach first – his speedster power abandoned and my echo powerset useless without the ability to take a proper swing at him. Panacea wouldn't work through the bodysuit, Vista's power slowly undoing itself for another thirty seconds or so – I didn't have anything special to help hit him or reduce the damage I was taking. I do my best to drag us both towards the wall, not concerned about the hits he was landing on me. Without his speedster power, he was already doing more damage to me than he had done over most of the fight so far – but the moment we roll into the wall, such minor injuries don't matter anymore, even if he is unaware of that fact.

Admittedly, he isn't at all hesitant or unsure now about how to deal with me now that I've managed to catch him – he immediately starts assaulting my exposed head with a barrage of powerful stomps from his remaining leg, not realising the danger that I was already setting up with the string dangling from one hand. I freeze it vertically in the air next to his upper thighs, then grab the other leg as his foot slams into my cheek. Holding both limbs in place, there's nothing at all to defend me from him as he sits up and starts swinging wildly at my unprotected back and head with massive, bruising punches. I just bitterly endure it, face locked in a grimace as my vision spins from each successive strike. It only takes a few seconds of Velocity's attempt to wriggle free of my grip for him to accidentally bump the upper part of his leg into the frozen thread. To his credit, he immediately recognises the power in question and immediately changes his tactics from assault to escape – trying to backpaddle with his arms and pushing away by leveraging his arms against the wall and my own body, to no avail thanks to my vice-like grip.

For my part, nothing changes. Hold the legs in place. Don't move. Just survive. We were already extremely close to the wall, to the point where I could feel my shoulder being pressured by the movements of the wall. Despite his obvious panic and frantic escape attempts, he does make a momentary effort to grasp my upper body and force it into the shrinking gap between thread and wall – but the idea occurs to him too late and he can't find a strong enough grip in time before the gap becomes too narrow to push me through.

His leg locks up and straightens as the space he has to move shrinks down to nothing, and then the compression begins. The squish goes even better than expected, an agonised roar emerging from Velocity is almost drowned out by the cracks and pops that emerge from the upper half of his leg being ground to a pulp by the movement of the wall – bone splinters and bloody viscera emerging in every direction as I pull back myself. I had expected a brutally clean cut after seeing Clockblocker's example, but the loose thread that I had so hastily set-up is nowhere near so thin or precise – it just acts as a dividing line between two sides of the body that crumple and snap around the line, only finally starting to work through bone when there is nothing left to give on either side.

It only takes a few seconds for the grim task to be complete, the agonised howl of the hero acting as music to my ears as I push myself up away from the wall – tossing the bloodied, broken pair of legs to the side as Velocity backs away with two bloody stumps attached to his torso, using his arms to backpedal away instead. Using his power to keep up the speed, clearly – but the river of blood he had left in his wake told the real story. This fight was already over. I might not catch him, but his power is working against him here. If I understand his powers right, activating his speed state lets him experience time normally while everything else slows down, but all that does now is ensure that from my perspective he'll just bleed out multiple times faster than he would have previously. I knew very, very well at this point what shock and rapid blood loss could do to someone – so as long as he didn't get a chance to somehow stymie the bleeding, it was only a matter of time before he lost consciousness and I could finish the job.

I don't have to wait that long to work it out. Whatever surge of adrenaline served to keep him up and running seems to run out, the now-distant form of the crippled man slumping over as the last of the fight leaves him.

He wasn't any good at fights like this. There wasn't a combat-based Cape in the Bay who couldn't trash Velocity in a fair fight. He was the support guy. The scout. The wait-for-the-real-heroes-to-get-here guy. Not a fighter. No special way of attacking, and using his power rendered him pretty much useless at anything other than pure repositioning. In truth, he would probably have more of a chance trying to fight me without using his power at all – his slightly superior physique and training against my echo, shadow state and as much fuckery as I could do with Vista's power. If I hadn't been able to abuse the slow shrinking of the room, it was hard to imagine what I could have done to him that would have actually put him down.

On top of that, it wasn't really Velocity I was up against. He fought like him, clearly, but the real one would almost certainly have never closed the distance against an unknown combatant with unknown powers or even confronted me alone at all. With this version, he only started to respect the powers as I revealed them – trying to account for the possibility of echo attacks and changing his angle of attack when I screw with space on one side – but without the PREP modifier or any other information to work with there just wasn't any way for him to know about any powers I hadn't shown. Ironically, if I was a bit stronger and had revealed a more dangerous power in melee I might have just scared him off from approaching me at all – leaving me with no way to catch him in a reasonable time frame and ensuring my eventual defeat.

I couldn't count on being this lucky next time.

SUCCESS

Reward: Relativity Adjustment (1)​

I savour the reward text for a moment. Finally. Finally. My first Mover powerset. Flexibility. Something that put me firmly in the superhuman-category. Something that put me in a position where I could always outpace a regular guy, or escape from a bad situation when cornered. That would, in theory, stop the increasingly-rare-but-still-too-common losses to regular people with knives or guns.

I suppress my grin as the sights and sounds of real life make themselves known to my senses once more, along with a slight feeling of shakiness as the continuous string of tough challenges continued to make take its toll on my body as a warning. One more. One more and I would call it quits for the day.

I glance at Velocity again, who is none-the-wiser about my recent victory.

Velocity

Hero 2/5

(REAL) (WRLD)​

I frown at that. I wasn't intending to challenge anyway, but it did bring most of Velocity's strengths back to the table – reinforcements, the ability to stall for time and the incredible ease with which he could escape a losing fight. On top of that, he now had the capability to restock any gear he ended up using, could ambush me with impunity and might even just have friendly people out in the field or patrolling with him that I would have to fight.

A problem for future-me to deal with. This first version of his power was more than enough for me to work with. It was another tool, just like Sophia's power – something that would let me solve a different challenge, which might reward me with another power that I could put to work on this one.

No, the target for my last fight of the day was already decided in my head. Manpower. A Brute, thanks to his power augmenting him with electromagnetic strength and shielding. I wanted a Brute powerset for obvious reasons, but I was also optimistic that his abilities would be effective against Sophia's power in future challenges.

I draw in a deep breath to steady myself, let my eyes roam over to Manpower and the lone TIME modifier floating next to him. No trouble. "Challenge."

The familiar site of the Pelham household appears in front of me. I had scouted it out before, but had pretty swiftly given up once it became apparent that people weren't coming in and out as regularly as the Dallon household – and there weren't any windows that were positioned in the right way for someone in the street to peer through without looking suspicious. With my interests aimed primarily at staying under the radar at the time, I had simply moved on to other things for the moment – but I could still recognise the house when I saw it.

A TIME modifier was nice and easy to work around, even if did prevent me from really scouting around for the perfect ambush or weapon to work with. It was probably a safe assumption that he was inside the house, waiting to aggro the moment I alerted him. My tactics were going to pretty limited here, find a blade, sneak behind him and stab him. In a head-on fight, I didn't stand much of a chance – the moment he activated his powers I would no longer have any means to hurt him, but until that time he essentially didn't have a Brute rating. Apart from the bit where he was a 7-foot-plus behemoth of a man that was probably the poster child for gym-goers and male models everywhere. Nothing major.

But enough idle speculation. I reach out to my new power, keen to give it a try. The speed-state was almost certain to be weaker than Velocity's in at least a few ways, meaning I had little hope of it helping me in direct combat at all – but now was a good time to see its limits, in a challenge where my odds of winning naturally were admittedly fairly low. I flip the mental switch to engage the power, feeling my body slow to a crawl for a second, two seconds, three seco- and I can move again. I take an experimental step to the side, feeling the physical drag of my clothes against the wind slowing me down far more than I was expecting. Despite that, the leaves kicked up at my feet seem sluggish and slow as they drift through the air – the only real sign I have that my movements are faster than usual relative to my usual self.

It's a little bit harder to slow myself down as well, finding purchase against the ground with my other leg to just stop moving seems to take longer than usual. I was certainly thinking comparatively faster to how fast I was moving. Gravity still works in terms of keeping me oriented correctly, but seems generally weakened in terms of keeping my grip on the ground firm. Jumping? I leap into the air experimentally, not gaining a huge amount more than usual in height – but certainly falling down slower, with the unpleasant feeling of my clothes momentum dragging me upwards for a moment as I start to fall. That could be a bit of a problem. A bit more testing reveals that sharp turns are almost entirely beyond me without using an object to parkour off of – the combination of my lack of grip and momentum from my clothes dragging me off my intended course on every attempt.

Straight lines only – or gentle, wide curves at worst. Crashing into a wall or object is an easy, painless way to stop, but I don't think I could repeat Velocity's trick of circling an opponent and hitting them from behind in a timely manner.

Speaking of which… I flick the speed state off. My body locks up again, refusing to move a muscle even mid-stride for a few moments – sending me tumbling to the ground thanks to my off-balance position. After a moment, I can pick myself back up again. I check the mental switch. Available. No cooldown on it at all, just a mandatory start-up and cool-down period when swapping between states. Unusable in most fights, standing still for three seconds or so would be certain to get me beaten to a pulp. It was a safe assumption that the original's restriction on not lifting or hitting things with any real force was still an issue. It might be worthwhile to ditch the loose shirts and jackets if speed was massively critical in a future challenge to handle the air-resistance issue, but I wouldn't be caught dead in a bodysuit as lame as Velocity's one – I'd rather cruise through town half-naked than that.

Still. Even with all the caveats, restrictions and weaknesses – I couldn't help but have a little grin on my face at the simple, floaty feeling of sprinting around like I was. An actual speedster, vastly faster than the average guy. I knew, intellectually, that the power wasn't the strongest in my arsenal – but out of all the powers I had gathered it felt the most satisfying to use. The most fun, for lack of a better word.

After failing to run vertically up a wall for more than a few steps without pushing myself away into thin-air, I decide to save any further experiments for another day and actually make an attempt at beating the challenge before the TIME modifier came into play. I suppose I could at least confirm that the timer went by real-time and ignored the additional time I personally experienced while in the speed-state – otherwise, I would already have the first wave of reinforcements coming for my head.

I peer through a window, and seeing nobody around, phase through it in a single smooth movement. The house was fairly quiet, save for the gentle hum and clatter of whatever household appliances were running in the background. Television, some furniture – but no angry Cape. I quietly step through one doorway into a corridor, peering into a tiled room to find the dining room. Nothing there-

I freeze in place as I hear a footstep, half-turning to find my target in the doorway to a room I hadn't checked yet – staring directly at me. I was positive that I hadn't made any sounds that could be heard over the washing machine and dishwasher nearby, and his expression and demeanour didn't seem like he had detected me and decided to search. No. He fucking moves around. I curse my luck as I dive through the doorway into the kitchen. The vast majority of targets that were on their own like this didn't move at all, unless a REAL or WRLD modifier was involved.

I hit the speed-state immediately upon breaking line of sight, freezing in place for an agonising number of seconds. Halfway through the count, Manpower bursts through the wall like a battering ram – sparks glistening across his body and arcs of electricity outlining him and coalescing into small shields to deflect debris. It's a small mercy that he can't see me immediately as he bursts through, the brief delay in catching sight of me giving my speed-state just a little bit more time to activate.

And then I was free again. Quickly backstepping away from his full body charge, then stepping back again as I note the blue-white wall of lightning manifesting just ahead of his charge. He was slow, but I couldn't hit him like this. I kick off the counter to change direction quickly, noting in the process that he was already adjusting his course in my new direction. Not fast enough to catch me, but it was clear that he could still track me easily enough. The shattered pieces of the wall scattering around the room are more of an obstacle than the charging Cape – attempting to nudge them aside takes too long, each fragment needing a hefty shove to redirect, all while my foe closed in from behind at a pace too fast to ignore, even slowed-down as it was. I duck under the obstacles instead, clambering across the floor just fast enough to maintain the distance I had from the Brute – then scrambling upwards to gain more space.

And then an explosion of force sends me flying into the wall faster than I can react, unable to adjust my course – and even if I could, I wouldn't be able to get past the rubble that follows after me. I try to push clear for a moment as I see Manpower gaining on me, electricity layer reforming around him already. I knew he could detonate his shields like that, but I was more familiar with it knocking people off their feet when they were right next to him – clearly my speed-state was magnifying the force I was receiving instead of the reverse, changing something that should have sent me stumbling for a moment into a force capable of slamming me into the opposite wall. I reach out for another power on instinct, only to realise that I had to disable the speed-state first. With that mode unlikely to get me past the rubble and debris coating my body in time, I bite the bullet and start the change back to normal.

Manpower immediately speeds up, his previously sluggish movements now turning into a blisteringly fast bull charge. I'm frozen. One second. Two- and he's got me in his grip, slamming me back into the wall before pulling me back. He practically hurls me into the floor with his one-handed grip, my muscles loosening up the instant before my head is about to crack open like an egg. I pick Sophia's power on pure instinct to save my skin, but a fraction of a second later, I morbidly realise what's about to happen as the air around me turns blue in every direction.

FAILURE

Hint: Some challenges are difficult to confront head-on. Consider avoiding a fair fight and change up your tactics when needed!​

I scowl at the hint. As if that wasn't what I was trying to do, before the challenge decided that this fight wasn't hard enough and that he should be patrolling his house instead of just waiting for me.

Then I frown down at my hands. That was a fast death though. I had expected it to be extremely painful and to kick me back into my physical form, but skipping straight to here after impact implied that the attack had killed me outright. Or at least instantly knocked me out, at which point he killed me. It wasn't clear which of those was the truth, but it did at least prove that his power was as effective on Sophia as I had expected it to be. This was the way forward for her. Get Manpower's first power and use it to clear through Sophia's challenges with ease. The first level of her power was easily my most-used option and getting its full functionality would be hugely valuable going forward.

Alas, it wasn't to be today. Based on the scenario, my initial guess that I needed another power to match him was probably correct – I hadn't appreciated the speed with which he could flood the air immediately around him with electricity, so even my optimistic plan of knifing him and running away would probably fail now that I knew Shadow Stalker and Velocity's powersets weren't viable escape tools from him.

Contrary to my expectations, the Endbringer truce doesn't dissolve the instant we return back. I mean, I wasn't expecting outright fighting or attempted arrests, but the cordiality between heroes and villains as they gathered themselves together and waited for people to give them a lift was something to behold. I opt to slip away before anyone else tries to talk to me, having had more than my fill of challenges for the day. Everything felt sore, even without any real injuries to speak of – but I was very happy to mark the day as a whole as a big success for me. I couldn't say the same for Canberra, but with the Simurgh you rarely could – so I'd take what I could get.

I duck into a side alley to lose my mask and change my outfit as much as I could, but I'm not being followed as best as I can tell – so I just take the extended walk home. It was long, but I didn't have anything better I wanted to do today – and when I finally get home, neither Alice nor Clara comment on my late appearance. Content with the days work, I flop inelegantly onto my bed and close my eyes.



The next school day, my morning lessons are spent paying only a fraction of attention to my lessons – most of my focus is dedicated to working out what was wrong with the skill thief power I got from Victor. I had, naturally, activated it almost immediately upon entering the school, but nothing seemed to happen. I leave it on during History class, and I get the vague sensation of the power briefly siphoning something out of a few of the keener students at the front for a few minutes. From almost everyone else in the room, it was as if they weren't even there. I struggled for a while to isolate the cause, shifting seats to see if proximity or line of sight had an effect, trying to focus a particular person and holding a specific mental image of what I wanted to drain. No luck. Even those siphons tapered off about halfway through the lesson, and I wouldn't get anything on my trip through the corridors to Computer class either.

But that's where I worked out the trick to it. My Computer class is, to put it bluntly, divided into the nerds and the mouth breathers. One side of the room is full of people who probably attend a tech-related club and are only really here for attendance and to work on projects for their grade, the other is full of students who need a lot of help to get anything done and would be lucky to get a passing grade if they had an extra year to study. This time, my leeching-field practically lights up with the half of the room waiting for the lecture at the start to be over and being given permission to work on their own tasks – which then peters out once they actually start working on those activities.

It's practice. Or to be more precise, wasted practice, if there was such a thing. The people who are learning new skills, absorbing facts or improving their abilities get completely ignored. Only those who are repeating things they already know or are executing familiar tasks get targeted. In a game-sense, it feels like people who have maxed out their experience points in a certain skill become eligible for me to skim the wasted points off of the top. When they move onto an unfamiliar subject, they go back to earning XP for that non-maxed skill.

I could only assume that meant that I would, eventually, become as good a student as whoever the best, most knowledgeable person in each of my classes happened to be – but I probably wouldn't be able to advance beyond that level unless I found a library or something with some university students or rocket scientists revising things to themselves. For more practical skills, I would need to find a martial arts club in session to leech from, ideally with plenty of people who have already plateaued or reached the top of the sport in question.

I'd have to admit to being a bit disappointed that it wasn't something I could really use against an opponent directly, but my larger fear for the power was that any gains would be merely temporary and that doesn't seem to be the case so far. Passively becoming a better student in general was always a good thing. But by far the best usage I had found so far was when I had quietly left it running when I showed up for my regular beat-down with Sophia's current challenge. I had been delighted to find that I could leech off of her as she beat me up, evidently meaning that I wasn't enough of a challenge to force her to improve – but if it worked out in my favour I would shut my mouth for the moment and count my blessings.

Lunchtime comes and goes. I don't spot either Taylor or Emma's group for most of the day, only running into them during our last scheduled class in World Issues. Mr G was, as always, being drowned out by the rowdy squabbling of the likely-delinquents on the left side of the room – and instead of trying to silence them, assigns us our project for the next two weeks. Research on an issue and a presentation, organised in groups of three.

I resign myself to waiting for the majority of the groups in the room to resolve themselves and for the stragglers to collate together – but Emma sashays over to me with a wide grin on her face, claiming me for her group without needing to say a word. A few of her friends seem surprised at her departure, but quickly resume deciding groups among themselves in fear of being left out.

I consider Emma for a moment. Her challenge dropped me into a fight with the Azn Bad Boys in an alleyway and told me to escape, if I remembered correctly. I check again to remind myself.

Emma Barnes

Winslow Student 3/4

(HUNT) (EVNT)

But couldn't I outrun them now? Oni Lee was fast at teleporting around an area, especially at sharp angles that would confuse anyone in a fight – but in terms of feats, PHO threads cited his lack of ability to keep up rapid jumps in a straight line against speedsters, fliers and vehicles. For someone with instant teleportation, it was proof that there were internal limits on his abilities somewhere – if I hopped into my speed state and sprinted away, I would wager money that I could start making some serious distance between us and eventually win the challenge.
