Still. An actually useful hint that wasn't full of motivational garbage was appreciated. As for Taylor… her new skill put a bit of a damper on my progression again. It was probably a safe assumption that she was hidden somewhere safe and not out where I could see her, so to make any progress… I would have to map out her range with consecutive challenges to see how far out I could get in each direction before she stopped following me. She would probably move and chase after I managed that, so it was probably impossible to get all the reliable points of data in one session – but after enough attempts I should be able to draw a circle on a map and work out what building she is in, then start to raid that building top to bottom as the scenario begins.

I look at her challenge box. Three hour cooldown. Another lengthy time-waster, but at least each challenge would give me another bit of data to work with. I could have the location worked out within the week, even if actually killing her before she killed me proved a bit more difficult to achieve.

The girl next to the window mouths at me to fuck off again. I snap off an irritated "Challenge." – not only because she was annoying, but also because I wanted to work out this Administrator power in a safe environment. I don't even look at the challenge box properly past the ALRT notice.

Half a minute later, the girl has a broken leg and finds herself pinned underneath a large wooden desk that I had tipped on top of her – leaving me free to try and work out exactly what the problem was with my new power.

It wasn't lighting up. It didn't feel like I had met some condition that it needed to be selected. 'Assign Administrator'. What did that imply? Admin rights? Or a more literal translation of delegating responsibility? That second meaning gives me pause for a moment. Taking into consideration the one other power it had stemmed from - delegating to a bug, perhaps?

Bug Control drags a housefly towards me, settling onto my hand. The instant it touches me, I feel my new power became ready to trigger. I select it- no. It wants to be pushed instead of selected. I feel the power slide onto the fly, suddenly becoming vaguely aware of its position around me as it does so. That was nice, I could usually only find it again when I had Bug Control as my active power.

But this felt incomplete – something was missing in what I had done. The slot that I had pushed towards the fly felt empty, almost like I could push something into it. On a whim, I try to select Sophia's power – somehow entirely unsurprised when that power vanishes from my list of options. I select bug control again to give it a new command - sending it flying away, dashing through the solid oak door in a puff of black smoke.

I can't use the shadow state while the bug has it, but no sooner does the thought of wanting it back cross my mind than I feel the power return – my connection to the bug withering to nothing as the bug abruptly falls to the ground, dead before it hit the floor.

After some experimentation, some of the powers seem slightly reduced in effectiveness when delegated, and the requirement to re-select Bug Control to give it new instructions is a bit unfortunate – but I could appreciate the strategic possibilities this opened up for me. Clockblocker's power applied at range for one, and the surprising synergy that Bug Control itself had with the powerset – I was initially surprised to see the administrator bug was capable of attacking with multiple bugs at a time, then realised that it was actually rapidly swapping between them to issue new commands faster than I could think. Each bug would be driven to fly in a certain direction or dive downwards in a sudden movement, then be unable to course-correct as it regained control before the administrator returned and repeated the command. I couldn't redirect the administrator bug without killing it when it was doing that, having passed away my Bug Control power – but that was a small price to pay for making that power slot actually somewhat useful.

Well. The only thing I came into this challenge to do was check out what this power could and couldn't do. No sense in sticking around. I saunter over to the corner to pick up a wooden footstool, returning to the crippled, dazed test dummy and swinging it at her exposed head with all my strength. The footstool breaks after the first few hits, the shoddy workmanship becoming apparent when put to the test – but the challenge area fades away in the end nevertheless.

SUC-

I ignore the rewards screen, brushing it away as soon as it arrives. I didn't care about whoever that was. We didn't even share a class, I was pretty sure. She wasn't important.

Now I step away from the window, returning to my classroom again. It was a good thing that I was done with this – I was probably starting to get a reputation for either my 'bladder problems' or people spotting me snooping on Taylor at her classes.

But that was enough worrying about new challenges and shiny toys. I quickly return to my class, waiting out the time until the end of the day – then immediately make my move over towards the Dallon household.

After all, I had a lead on Glory Girl! A real way to get around her shield – give it a solid hit, then follow up in the brief moments before it re-established itself. There must be a certain threshold of force to hit, otherwise any single friendly touch would break it – people would have noticed by now. That meant my speed-state was out, even if I had a way to apply a deadly blow from within the breaker state.

Knowing was only half the battle. I had to go close-range with a Brute and land at least two consecutive hits, when she is both vastly faster than me and any real hit from her might accidentally part my head from my shoulders. I had seen the feats thread. I had filled out part of her feats thread. Top recorded speed clocked at eighty-six miles an hour, plummeting down on one of Squealer's monster trucks and writing it off for the scrapyard in a single blow. It was one thing for me to hit her once when she wasn't expecting it, then check if the shield was down – quite another to land a decisive neck stab immediately after and then survive her retaliation.

If she flew through the wall as she did when first I challenged her, surely her shield would be down for the brief moment afterwards? I started with a knife in hand, could I just stand next to it – try and lash out as she comes through? Perhaps that put me at risk of getting hit by rubble, if not by Glory Girl herself, should her reaction be faster than mine.

Was there an alternative? The idea of stepping outside and trying to fling a rock at her as she arrives, taking out her shield before she hits the wall paints an amusing picture, but she's certain to see me and the odds of me hitting such a throw against someone that fast are low enough that I would be coming back here for days.

I note the flier appear over a nearby building, no Panacea in her grip today – had she already headed off to the hospital again? Whatever the case, Glory Girl was right on time. I glance over at her singular ALRT modifier and nod to myself. "Challenge."

I cast my gaze around at the surrounding windows this time – catching Glory Girl flying overhead in a wide loop, doubtless moving from wherever she had spawned towards whatever angle she wanted to bust through this wall with.

Seeing the wall again, I wasn't sure I wanted to get anywhere close. I was far away last time and hadn't been paying attention, but the explosion of brick, wood and glass seemed like it was going to be hazardous to my health. I clutch the knife I had been gifted at the start of the challenge, then call a bug to my side. I apply the new administrator power – then give it Clockblocker's powerset, allowing it to hover next to the wall. I remain in place, not wanting to move and cause her to approach differently from last time.

When she busts through the wall again, I lose my grip over the bug almost immediately – some flying shrapnel more than enough to take out the unflinching insect. But, like the hero he was, he froze the shattered fragment that killed him in its place – and when Glory Girl's momentum carries her forward like a vengeful goddess, she instead finds herself folded around a large wooden splinter that just refuses to move. I had seen some rather terrible videos on the internet before, drivers going at relatively low speeds – just hitting deer or trees at a bad angle. Horns and branches just piercing through them or their seats even when they weren't even going insanely fast.

Glory Girl had been going fast. A full frontal-charge after spotting me through the window. Not her full speed, but more than enough for a sharp, sliver in the air to act exactly like a spear would in the hands of some low-tech warrior from ancient times. Her momentum is killed near-instantly, a shocked gasp as the air is knocked out of her – blood racing through her costume as she comes to realise that she's been impaled on something. She clearly doesn't understand what happened entirely, the object is embedded inside her now – not quite penetrating through to the other side, clearly slightly too blunt. That only works in my favour though, even if it is in her body – the power is still keeping its effect, if only for a few more seconds. She tries to fly upwards and away, only to let loose an agonised scream as she tears up her insides even more with the action.

I lunge forward with the knife, in truth – this was a bad angle for me, she was too high for me to take a swing at the more critical spots on her body. That wasn't important though, either I would land some additional damage to help bleed her out when she got free – or she would fend me off, only dealing more damage to herself internally as she moved. The knife scrapes against the forcefield, then the next stab scrapes her leg as she kicks towards me – I attempt to hamstring her for the attempt, yet only skitter across the barrier again for my trouble. That's fast indeed, Three attacks from point-blank range with speed as my primary focus and two of them were still easily no-sold without her needing to do anything.

She lets out a furious roar, and I find my knees folding underneath me as the full force of her aura hits me like a truck. I blink up glassily at her as she tears herself free by force, the bloodied object yanked free of her body through a new exit wound – messy, probably just killed herself, but that didn't matter if she managed to kill me first.

Blind fear gives way to fear-fuelled instinct as I mentally start to pull myself together from the aura-based attack, her desperate attempt to splatter my brains across the room with her leg is foiled by my abrupt explosion into a shadowy fog – which regrettably drops my sole weapon to the ground. The state doesn't last long enough for me to make it through a wall, but I do escape through the hole that she made and manage to hide around the corner before she fully reverses course to pursue in my footsteps.

Or not, as the case may be. Instead, she opts to cut me off by charging through the window – leading with a flying punch aimed to decapacitate me. Again? I could only assume the shock and blood loss had given her tunnel vision and rendered rational thought into an impossibility – otherwise I don't know why she expected the second blind bull-rush to fare any better than the first. The glass breaks around her forcefield, and then her arm breaks as it impacts a hastily-frozen fragment of a brick no larger than my finger – but immovable all the same. The wind of the impact buffets my face, the sickening crack that her arm makes a testament to exactly how damaging that kind of impact was for the Brute when her forcefield wasn't available. I dash around the corner again as she stops in the street, nursing the gaping wound in her chest and her useless arm – then I activate my speed-state and run.

Somehow, Glory Girl finds it in herself to give chase after a moment. Surging to life almost as soon as my mandatory-timeout ends, the speed of her flight not lowered at all by her injuries. Which gave me an interesting fact to work with, me sprinting away from her full-speed gained a fair bit of distance – but as she accelerated, that lead slowly begins to reverse inch-by-inch. It wasn't much, but I was just slightly slower than her once she hits her stride. Faster reactions still, obviously, but running in a straight line wasn't going to end well. I do a jumping kick into the wall of a nearby street, if it weren't for this breaker state giving me the force-projection of one of the sponge-balls we used to throw at each for dodgeball in gym class – I would have been painted across the wall like abstract art. Instead, I bounce off it – the most damage I take is from my legs landing awkwardly as the rest of my body slams into the wall. Then, I reverse course – sliding under the angry Brute as she realises that I've gone from at least seventy miles-per-hour to nothing faster than she can blink. Building up speed takes a while, but she has to completely change her direction – something she isn't amazing at compared to the rest of New Wave.

Not that I need to worry about that in the end. She was already running on fumes, as indicated by the trail of blood she had left behind her that I was now running through. Glancing behind me, I can see her falling into a truck on the road – no longer to concentrate on her flight or maintain consciousness.

Score.

SUCCESS

Reward: Personal Shield (1)​

I bite my lip as I consider the reward screen. I had mixed feelings about that as a reward. On one hand, an explicit defensive power was really nice. On the other, I would probably have preferred super-strength or flight for powers that expanded my options further.

I shake my head, focusing my attention on Glory Girl as she lets herself into the house.

Victoria Dallon

Heroine 2/7

(ALRT) (LUST)​

A LUST modifier to work with. Nothing that invalidated my previous strategy, but it would make her use her powers a little more optimally and ignore injuries to a greater extent. "Challenge."

Same room. Same set-up. I twirl the knife in my hand for a moment. Trying the same trick was worth a try, surely? She didn't have a PREP or CONT modifier to have advance warning of the powers I have, so as long as she came through at the same angle I might just score an instantaneous win again.

It only takes a moment to set-up the admin bug with Clockblocker's power, then it was just a matter of waiting. Six seconds later, I have my answer. The wall does explode inwards as expected, the freezing trap working as expected to stop the attack in its tracks – but as the dust settles, it isn't the agonised figure of Glory Girl that's been pinned in place, but a silver pick-up truck that's been hurled at me instead. A moment later, a small red car comes flying through the window to its left – and I realise that this Glory Girl is more than content to bombard me from range until the entire building comes down on top of me.

Hoping to avoid her notice, I phase through the side wall to try and escape – running directly into an electric wire and being ejected for my trouble. Thankfully, she's too busy picking up ammunition to take advantage of my momentarily charred and crippled state – but by the time I can finally pick myself back off the ground, there's barely anything left holding the store up. Without any other options, I activate my speed-state and make my escape out of the holes she made in the front.

She's on top of me near-instantly, snatching up an entire street light in passing as some mockery of a weapon to hold – extending her effective range to a silly extent. I repeat my trick of killing my momentum against the wall at a street corner, but this time her makeshift weapon near-beheads me for my trouble – metal bending and screeching as she forces it to gouge a path through the street and walls of nearby buildings alike, kicking up a storm of dust and debris in the process. I still get the juke in the end, she overshoots me as I reverse course the way I came – looking to repeat the trick and get out of her line of sight. Once I succeeded in that, I could drop the speed-state and phase into a nearby building – planning my attack while she had no idea where I was.

Unfortunately, that plan goes awry at the first hurdle. Unintentionally on her part, the storm of dust and debris she had kicked up gave me genuine resistance in my speed-state. I already felt the effects of air-resistance every time I moved, but now I was fighting through tiny flecks that I wouldn't even have noticed without the breaker state. I get through the cloud in the end, but I've barely gotten back into a proper sprint when a wall of icy-cold, mind-numbing fear slams into me. Against my will, my footing stumbles – even when I was expecting the aura, I just can't seem to fully mitigate it.

A hand wraps around my arm, giving me just enough time to turn and see Glory Girl's expressionless face before I get hurled into the ground face first. The sharp, jarring impact knocks me out of the breaker state – leaving me frozen again in the worst of all positions. Lying stunned on my back I watch Glory Girl toss the one arm she was holding me by to the side, I realise the implications of the action faster than I realise what my screaming nerves were telling me. She'd pulled my arm off in the same motion as the throw. I gurgle incoherently as the speed-state wears off – Glory Girl seeming content to not follow-up on her attack immediately.

I attempt to move, shift into my shadow state – but I feel sluggish and lethargic, somehow too tired to even move an inch or activate any skills. I look down, trying to decipher the pain signals all over the rest of my body. My vision is blocked by Glory Girl's leg.

Oh. That would do it. That made sense. A heel-stomp from a Brute wouldn't have any real reason to stop at my ribcage. I hadn't even felt it, at least until she started pulling her bloodied foot free. I try to scream, I could certainly feel the pain as she did that – but my lungs are already half-gone, and the next heel-stomp towards my head is utterly unavoidable.

FAILURE​

I didn't even get to use the new shield. I had been expecting flying punches and telegraphed attacks, but once I had been grabbed there wasn't any way to get out of that before my speed-state dropped. After that, I had already lost.

Was there another way I could have tried that? Without tricking her with Clockblocker, my only hope to break the shield myself was to use my echo – but I was certain that would be too slow to follow-up as a second hit and incapable of dealing the kind of damage that would save me from an immediate death once she returned the hit. I would need to lure her into an echo I had already made, then attack her once it dropped the shield for me. That had to be a lethal attack, ideally with the knife – but how could I bait her into melee, towards a location of my choosing, without being able to use any powers until I released the echo?

The first step, clearly, was to remove the ranged options. Getting to an underground shelter perhaps. Some trains went through underground tunnels as well, although I didn't know anything about their routes. Anything that took away her ability to just toss a car at me when it looked like I was set up in a comfortable defensive position.

And once I had that… what? The last challenge had shown that even if the wound inflicted would kill her eventually, it didn't necessarily stop her from killing me first – something that would be exacerbated by the LUST modifier. Having put myself in such a position where flight and ranged options didn't counter me, how would I then escape and prevent her from following me while I waited for her to bleed out? Clockblocker's power could work, but I had limits on the size of objects that I could freeze.

I wrack my brain for alternatives, hare-brained ideas that might find some value in a second round. Containment foam grenades from the PRT, if I could find them in the challenge. With a solid connection in a small space, she shouldn't be able to get free. Again, that requires me to escape her initial sight cleanly and prepare an ambush. Drowning? She might follow me down into the waves if she thinks she has an advantage, maybe I could… net her and freeze her down there? No, too much difficulty with the execution and too many assumptions on what actions she would take.

Nothing smart was springing to mind. Getting into some kind of tunnel and trying to catch her with a strong enough hit from the echo was all I could think of, and that plan seemed difficult enough that it would require multiple attempts out of me to land a decisive hit without her dodging and escape afterwards.

I would need to prep beforehand to find a spot to lure her towards, which began with working out whatever street name I started at. I should have checked that first while I was still inside. More trial and error attempts to escape her sight and bombardment. There wasn't much I could do to stop her from seeing my go through the first wall with the window the way it was and the holes she knocks into the side of the building, but if I could slip through a few walls in a row I should lose her pretty easily. It just required me to find a spot in the wall without a cable going through it – which couldn't be that hard.

…but that was a lot of things to work out. Especially when Glory Girl wasn't Taylor, who I could see at any point of the school day if I wanted – I could reliably see the flying brick about three times a week thanks to her usually flying home after school.

Which meant that I wouldn't be getting flight or Brute powers off of her anytime soon. I didn't have a reliable way to see Manpower at all. Aegis was a Ward, who I likely wouldn't see much until I signed with the heroes. The Brute I saw in the bank robbery challenge… I didn't recognise him at all. Maybe that was a pre-cog situation and he would show up on my doorstep sometime? Otherwise, my remaining Brute options lay solely with the Empire – Hookwolf, the giantess twins and Krieg in a non-traditional sense. I pinch my nose. "Fuck."

I don't particularly want to go to the Empire. I don't trust them not to screw me, and if my collaboration gets exposed or becomes well-known then bad relations with the PRT and general public are a near guarantee. First impressions are important.

I start to head home, still mulling over my options to myself. There was a real worry about going to the heroes early on that I would get uncovered too quickly. It gave me greater access to the local heroes, but between power testing and whatever Thinker tests I got put through, the worry that the truth of my power would get out was a real concern. Coupled with that, the constant close proximity of people I was beating challenges for regularly might attract attention as well.

You could see it in the people I had challenged at Winslow, a fair number of people had near-maxed out challenges in my class – yet they still rarely interacted with me or did anything unusual, seeming to act normally. Which made sense, it likely simulated a crush – not imagining up an entire relationship from nothing or tweaking memories of what was already there. We had never interacted, so nothing came of it. Yet Emma, now interacting with me on a regular basis, had escalated fairly rapidly between her own problems and my… encouragement of them. If someone noticed that I seemed to have the entire Wards team thirsty for me to start dicking them just a few weeks in, a witch hunt for a master wouldn't seem unreasonable at all. It would only require one or two people with the right mindset to have harder challenges and not fall in line with the others, could I take that risk? Probably not. A slower burn was required, slowly converting the local heroes and villains into people who would at least be sympathetic to me in the event of any outrage. A gradual change, over months and not weeks.

I would still need to find them, of course, and that meant interacting with patrols and cape fights in real life – that kind of interaction was the only way I was ever going to reliably run into them with the news the way it was, unless I could get into some more events like the Wards meet and greet. If I had to show up on the streets in some capacity, likely using Velocity's power, then perhaps a stint as an independent hero wouldn't be entirely misplaced. Start out with some low-level patrols to attract attention and introduce myself as a hero-

I pause at that thought, then grin. Of course. If I was going to go out on patrol, went out to the right areas, made enough noise… perhaps I could catch the attention of a certain bug-controller that hadn't been snapped up by any teams just yet.

Now that sounded like a plan.


"Drop your money on the ground!" The voice echoes down the alleyway, the unbalanced tone and slurred voice indicating some combination of drug use, alcoholism and a mental disorder or two on top.

Melanie stares wide-eyed at the gun pointed at her head, mentally cursing herself for not taking a safer route back home at this time of night.

"Bitch." Spittle flies from his mouth. "I said put your money on the ground! Are you deaf?" The gun wavers slightly. "Think I won't shoot? I can take if off your corpse just as easy, but I'm a nice guy – so help me out."

"Woah!" A voice draws her attention, and that of the mugger, down towards the side of the alleyway. "Are you being mugged?" A teenager, looking at his build – a bizarre combination of a hoodie, baseball cap and a domino mask serving to mask his identity. No obvious weapons, but also no fear when the gun turns to point at him. A cape? Her heart swells in hope at the thought.

"Yes! Help me!" She calls out, getting a boot in the chest from the drug-addled man for her trouble, winding her and driving her down onto her knees.

"Fuck off, dickweed! You don't want anything to do with this." He waves the gun in the boy's direction.

"Gotcha, just checking." The boy leaves without another word, casually sauntering off to the side as if nothing was wrong.

"Little shit pretending to be a cape to scare people." The man snorts, turning the gun back to her with a gap-toothed grin. "Listen girlie. The police take half-an-hour to respond to calls here this time of night. Scared of the gangs, you see. Gives us plenty of time to get acquainted – nice and proper. I was going to just let you go without your money, but if you're trying to get me attacked by passers-by… now that just isn't nice, is it? I'm thinking you should show me how sorry you are, then I might not splatter your brains all over the floor for not listening the first time."

This can't be happening. She stares blankly as the man fumbles with his belt, gun weaving as his stinking, repulsive cock emerges to point at her menacingly.

And then a shadowy fog descends noiselessly behind him from the rooftops overlooking the alley, materialising into the same boy that she had just seen at the entrance from the street.

"Poke." He reaches around and taps the gun with a cheery sound – then leg-sweeps the distracted man, who somehow bounces off the gun as he falls when the gun fails to move an inch from where it was tapped. The boy swings his foot into the side of the man's jaw – then stomps his groin the instant it's exposed. Screams penetrate the atmosphere of the night, only interrupted by the boy repeatedly kicking the man in his stomach and chest until he rolls over defensively – already sobbing and bawling for mercy.

Melanie takes in the beaten, bruised man and her apparent saviour. "Thank you-" She breaks off as the boy deliberately stamps down hard on the fingers of the fallen figure, the crack loud and clear in the relative silence of the night city. She swallows drily as the boy turns his gaze to her.

"That'll probably do it." He nods to himself. "And yeah, sure, wasn't a problem. Happy to help. Sorry, it took a while to get here, had to find some stairs to get closer to the roof – nothing to climb up around here and he might have just shot you if I ran at him, if you see what I mean? That would be a shitty start to my night."

Friendly, it would seem – just a bit brutal on the takedown. And talking a mile a minute. "Well. I'm grateful, if you hadn't come along when you did-"

"Yeah, that guy would have all of your money and you'd be sucking his dick. Lucky break for you that I was here this time, eh?" He lets out a jovial laugh and gives a thumbs up. For understandable reasons, she doesn't find it so funny.

"Piece of shit." The man on the ground murmurs, having stopped his whimpering and pushing himself to his feet - stumbling a moment as he tries to put pressure on the hand with clearly-broken fingers. "I'll show-"

"Man, how am I even supposed to do this?" The boy complains out loud, turning back to face the mugger – waiting for him to get all the way up before his fist lashes out, stretching impossibly across the distance to collide with the man's face – then grabbing him and holding him in place as a ghost of some sort seems to repeat the hit. Teeth and blood go flying from both hits, then he knocks the man to the ground again with another kick to the crotch. "You would think that they would just stay down once it becomes obvious that I'm a cape, but they keep on trying anyway!"

Even sprawled on the ground, the man moves his good arm to his waist, then wildly swings across the ground with a knife – seeming to scrape harmlessly off of thin air mere millimetres from the boys' ankles. Another hard stomp down on the hand elicits another crack, and more screaming to accompany it.

The boy seems unbothered about the wails, continuing to talk to himself. Or her? It was hard to tell if he expected genuine input, but she was very keen to stay on his good side. "I mean, it would be fine if I just knocked people out and called it a day – but I read this vigilante guide and it said that head injuries are a big no-no and somebody will probably die. But how do I keep a guy down without that? I don't want to break their bones, but it's not like they sit still long enough for me to zip-tie them or whatever."

She wets her lips, finding her voice. "That sounds, uh, difficult."

"It really is tough." He agrees, lamenting over his woes as he kicks the mugger onto his back and sitting down on top of him – clearly not anticipating any more threat from the man with multiple broken fingers on each hand. "I mean, I knew this whole hero thing wasn't going to be a cakewalk – but things are just so much more complicated in real life when there aren't any obvious objectives to go and do." He waves a finger in the air. "Listen to this, you know why I stopped to ask if you were being mugged? It was because just yesterday I jumped in to save this woman from a guy who looked like he was about to rape her, choking, screaming – the whole works. Took the guy down, but they were apparently married." He spreads his arms. "Who decides to fuck in a disease-ridden, filthy back-alley like that?"

She nods carefully. "What happened then? If you don't mind me asking."

"Oh well, they were a bit mad at the start but I managed to salvage it with my charms." He scratches his neck awkwardly. "I suppose you could say that she used the experience to move on from the relationship. Got a taste of a better man, I suppose." He grins to himself as if he had just told an inside joke that nobody else was going to get. "Anyway, you called the cops, right? Unless you just want to leave him, I don't really care myself."

She glances down at the twitching, broken man and the beatifically smiling boy lounging on his back. The boy was well-meaning, clearly. But… he was a little bit 'off'. "I think I would like to leave."

"Sure, sure. Will you be safe from here or should I escort you?" He fishes up the gun from the ground nearby, flinging it into a nearby dumpster as he stands.

"I'll be fine." She takes a half-step away from the rookie vigilante – curiosity preventing a hastier escape. "If I may, what's your name? As a hero, that is?"

He facepalms. "Knew I forgot something. Talking all this time and I never introduced myself once. Can't get brand recognition like this! Let me try this again." He steps across the body of the mugger again, still groaning in pain. "It's a pleasure to meet you. I'm a hero, here to help." A cocky smile spreads across his face.

"Void Cowboy, at your service."

#1,199
I kick my feet off the side of the roof, looking down at the dimly-lit street below. Glory Girl's shield was toggled on as my current power, not requiring any real focus to maintain but still occupying my active power slot. The recharge was notably slower than hers, but the biggest drawback by far was the fact that it didn't recover at all unless I had it selected – meaning that in a typical fight, I'd only get to block one thing if I was using my other powers constantly. Still useful, just a bit of a dampener on my dreams of invincibility.

On the plus side, I was now mostly immune to rain. Taylor, or should I say, Bug – obviously couldn't say the same. There was something mildly amusing about seeing the masked cape wearing an oversized plastic coat with a large hood just to keep herself dry in the downpour. She hovers under the streetlight, looking around in all directions before settling in to wait.

"Challenge." I whisper. I go backwards this time, spinning around 180 degrees and bursting forward in my speed-state before the bugs properly reach me. Keep running in a straight line. Don't respond to anything else. When the clouds of bugs streaming to intercept me stop, I stop as well. I look around for familiar landmarks, not finding any I knew already – but plenty that I could look up later when I had a map or some spare time. "Chang's Jewellery. Bus stop 7, route 18. Apartment blocks. Parking block two-hundred metres. Methodist Church." I repeat them to myself in my head, then nod firmly.

The bugs were still creeping towards me at a much slower pace, and Taylor wasn't stupid – she would realise I was trying to map her out if I zipped across her range like this a few times in a row within a single challenge. The biggest mistake here would be getting bad data by her moving or faking me out, which would only screw me later on.

I do a double backflip off a roof to exit the simulation to the sound of rushing wind and snapping bones.

FAILURE​

I brush aside the notification, impatiently waiting for the real world to come back into my vision. I quickly note the shops, addresses and signs I had seen onto my phone – doing my best to shield it from the rain as I did so. I'd have to check on my computer at home, but once I found and marked that spot I could consider that to be another marker along the northern-edge of her range from wherever she started. The data I already had didn't make a perfect circle yet however I twisted it, but the more points I had the more specific the model would get. Repeatedly marking the edge of her range like this should eventually make a circle around a particular building, then I would have my target.

But enough of that. I didn't put on this get-up in the pouring rain to do geometry in my free time. I drop to the ground in my shadow state, just a few steps behind Taylor. "You know, I would have been happy to delay on account of the weather if you had asked."

She spins around at the sound of my voice, marginally relaxing as she takes in the sight of me. "Are you-"

"You must be Bug." I give her a friendly wave. "I'm Void Cowboy, though I'm sure the name needs no introduction. You must have heard of me before this cape business, right?"

Her mask creases slightly as she seems to frown through it. "No, I only recently started looking through the site at all to start preparing for what I should do as a cape – I've never really spent much time there before that. Your thread kind of... jumped out at me when I was flicking through on a whim, I suppose. I saw a few people mentioning you being a long-time poster, but I didn't really understand the context of that much of it." She shrugs helplessly. "I guess you're a bit of an internet celebrity?"

My palm impacts my face full force. "If we're limiting celebrity status to the local boards, then I suppose you could say that." Not many people had recognisable names that weren't actual capes, moderators, leakers or PRT spokesmen. "I was just curious if you recognised the name, nothing to worry that much about." I gesture for her to follow me out of the rain towards an overhanging roof that could act as shelter. "Let's get out of the rain before we talk."

I guess that answers one question that had been plaguing me for the entire weekend. My decision to announce that Void Cowboy was a cape had been reasoned out thoroughly, with plenty of beneficial arguments to it that weren't purely limited to the ability to troll PHO and also get a kickass name out of the deal. Those beneficial arguments were too long and complex to list out here and now, so people will just have to give me the benefit of the doubt on that. That said, I will admit that there was one potential downside that I realised about twenty-four hours after the reveal. I had told Taylor my username once.

A silly gesture on my part, of course. Who is silly enough to give someone the details to connect online activity to their real identity? Usually not me, but in this instance, I had been riding high off a string of successes and more interactions with Taylor in a week than I usually got in a year. I had gotten the Trio off her back for a bit, made sure she knew it was because of me… and offered to keep in touch via PHO while the Trio did their best to keep us separated.

Even though I hadn't remembered that I had done that at the time, I wasn't that worried upon realising my mistake. After all, in the nicest possible way – Taylor has no friends. Apart from me, I guess. She isn't going to gossip to anyone about it. She's also kind-of mastered into liking me a bit more than before, she has no reason to particularly dislike me or be angry once she knows my identity. It's not ideal, of course – spreading information like that is never good – but it would just become another facet of our relationship. School buddies by day, cape partners by night.

So I had, naturally, expected her to be a little more… aware when she messaged me. Not to the extent of revealing herself, of course. But… a hint of recognition. An ounce of casual greeting. A bit of confidence that she knew who she was dealing with. I didn't get any of that in the shy, stumbling messages that asked me for a bit of help and guidance, but I had brushed it off as potentially not wanting any trace of digital logs to be kept of our interactions – which was perhaps too optimistic of me, Taylor didn't know enough about technology to be worried to that extent. She wasn't stupid or ignorant, but she wasn't exactly at the top of computer class or likely to be concerned about hacking concerns or the latest surge in online privacy violations.

With her reactions now – still shy, anxious and seemingly a little starstruck just by meeting another rookie cape – there was no doubt in my mind as to what happened when I slipped her my information. Message from Greg about some internet thing? Straight to the junk folder. So used to brushing off my offers to link up that she glossed over the message on sight, mentally declining it before even taking in the details.

That… stung a bit, actually. Not just because of the action which I was very used to, but because this was after I had already done a little tweaking to make her friendlier. I wasn't mad or anything. I know that she's a bit of a technophobe, obviously – and that actually creating a social media account and using it to interact with people who knew her would be a big step for someone who doesn't even bring their mobile phone to school. I couldn't be too annoyed, especially when it was probably for the best that less people knew my real identity – and therefore this result worked out better for me.

It was fine. It just didn't do much to preserve my ego. What I'm trying to say, is that I'm not bitter or twisted about this turn of events at all. Really.

Well. The upside is that as long as I don't bring it up, she can't blame me for not spelling it out to her – because I shouldn't have any reason to know who she is and would hardly have a reason to bring it up again. She probably wouldn't take the news gracefully if I hinted that I knew her identity, so pleading ignorance is the best play here.

Which is fine. I'm great at being ignorant – girls tell me that all the time. "So, you said that you could control bugs?" I quiz innocently, ducking under the shelter and gesturing for her to do the same.

"That's right." She nods stiffly. "I can use a much larger swarm, but most of my bugs hate it when it rains as much as this." She forms a quick circle of flies in front of her before dismissing them.

"Relax. No need to be so tense." Having the advantage on her like this for once was fun – knowing that it was a rather nervous Taylor under the mask while she tried badly to look cool and professional for the first impression. "We're all on the same side here, just getting to know each other before we head out on patrol. Gotta make sure we know what the other can do and that we don't get in each other's way in the middle of a fight. I'm a Trump, with a bunch of grab-bag powers that I can use one of at a time – the most notable being a neat personal forcefield, intangibility, a speedster powerset and a limited version of Clockblocker's powerset. Most of my powers are knock-off versions of other capes around the Bay, although I don't know the exact mechanic behind the new ones I get over time. I'm trying to keep the fact that I get new ones a secret, so don't go spreading that one around just yet." She nods seriously at that. I believe her. Again, no friends to gossip with.

I can't help but notice as Taylor shrinks with every word, opting to cut my list of powers short and let her get a response in. "I, uh, I just have bugs. I don't know how much use I'll be on a patrol, but I did bring some equipment!" She jiggles the backpack behind her, the sound highlighting that the container was clearly packed to the brim with bits and pieces that she thought might be useful.

I make a face. I'd have to convince her to drop the bag eventually, or maybe let reality do the work for me as she realises how tiring lugging that around was going to be. Although, she probably wasn't going to be fighting in melee like I did and a heavy backpack wouldn't be nerfing a speedster power that much either. Maybe it would be fine? "I wouldn't be that down on yourself. There's a lot that you can do with bugs. Remember that we're only really likely to run into muggers most of the time. Trust me, if you cover someone head-to-toe in bugs they aren't going to be able to aim at anything because they'll be panicking so much. Then, if they still cause trouble – get the whole swarm to start crawling into their mouths, ears, nostrils. You can win the entire fight without them even setting eyes on you."

She doesn't say anything for a moment, as if processing my words a few times over in her head. "But don't you think that's going a bit too far?" She looks somewhat perturbed at my words, as if I was the sick mind who came up with the idea of using bugs like that.

Still, her question only had one answer. "Not really?" I wave at her. "These people have knives, guns and the intent to use them if it means getting away. It's fine for me, because a lot of my powers are solid in an actual fair-fight-" As much as I complained about how gimped my powers were, I didn't lose to unpowered people anymore – and guns had little value if they didn't catch me by surprise way out in the open. "-but you could get shot once and that would be the end of it. You can't be much of a hero if you lose in a fight to a mugger day one. You can't expect them to play fair if you do beat them either, people might be cautious of getting on the PRT's bad side – but any of the gangs would happily force you into their service or kill you if they got the opportunity, to say nothing of the more minor criminal elements who have no use for recruiting capes."

I didn't feel the need to spell it out, but as a girl and an independent both, the price of her being defeated and captured by either a random criminal or two out of the three larger gangs in the city would be somewhat more traumatising than it would likely be for me.

"I know that, but skipping straight to that level of violence doesn't seem very heroic. We're supposed to hold ourselves to a higher standard." Taylor insists. "I want to be a hero, not some thug that gets a reputation for pouring bees down someone's throat at the slightest provocation."

"Do you think I want to run around breaking bones?" I pull a face that she can't see. "I don't have many great capture options, and none of my powers are flashy or intimidating enough to make someone surrender at the sight of me. I look like I got caught in an explosion at a thrift store somewhere, and that won't change until I have a reputation behind me. I'm not going to say that you need to make an example out of everyone to cross your path, but you need to use the cards that are available to you."

"Except those cards are bugs." There's a tinge of uncharacteristic bitterness to her voice. That wasn't to say that Taylor wasn't often bitter about something, but that this time the bitterness was directed at herself.

I suppose it makes sense. It seems silly for me to imagine, having felt first-hand how devastatingly effective even a 'small' swarm of bugs can be in a life-or-death fight – but to her, the idea of being anything other than a tourist attraction or a scary story to tell children about is the height of wishful thinking. I highly doubt she's used her bugs in an actual fight in any capacity, so she probably thinks that people could just ignore her bugs as a minor annoyance.

I cross my arms, musing to myself. Let it never be said that I never looked out for other people, the best way to fix this was to set her onto some unsuspecting mugger. "Well. I think you are underselling yourself, but I can tell that you aren't going to take my word for it. We both came out here to patrol, so I think the best thing I can do to convince you that you are wrong is to find some violent looking thug for you to handle."

She looks like she wants to argue for a moment, but then relaxes and nods her head in acceptance. "I'll do what I can." After a moment, she pipes up again. "Although, how do we actually patrol? I mean, I know we do a planned route and look for trouble and all of that – but what should I actually do specifically?"

Back into conversational territory that I am an expert in. "Well, I've found that the worst part about patrolling is actually finding some trouble to get involved in. I have a pretty decent speedster power when it comes to just travelling around, so I was thinking that I could scout around and look for trouble – if I find anything, I just zip straight back to the main street to meet up with you and we can approach it together."

"That just sounds like I'm holding you back." Taylor grimaces. "You could have handled it yourself twice over by the time I get there."

"In some cases, sure." I give a vague shrug. "If it's something time-sensitive, then I might have to do it myself – but there are plenty of things I run into that I have to pass up on intervening. Usually, when there's a few guys involved and I suspect guns might be involved – a gang stirring up trouble or moving something illegal-looking around."

She seems doubtful, like I'm only saying that to keep her spirits up.

I hold a finger in the air to attract her attention. "It might not seem like it sometimes, but I'm very aware of my own limits and mortality. I'm pretty cautious about things that might get me killed, and I have no intention of going out because I tried to punch a guy right as his buddy with a gun comes back around the corner after buying smokes. But with you, suddenly we have the numbers advantage. Those people with a gun are sitting ducks for you and your swarm, and you can easily scout out any reinforcements or enemies lurking in the shadows with your bugs. If we need to scare them off? A giant, teeming mass of chittering insects twice their size is going to make anyone turn and run for the hills. Give it a chance and I think you will find that your power can do a lot of good in the right situation."

"I guess we'll see." She peers out under the hood of her coat at the rain beyond our temporary shelter. "I'm willing to try at least. So, should I just… keep walking in a straight line and wait for you to come find me?"

I nod enthusiastically. "I'll run ahead with my speed-state, but it's pretty easy for me to miss things – especially if they just happen in an alleyway I don't happen to run down. You can see through your bugs, right? Maybe-"

"No." She shakes her head. "I mean, I suppose I have a… sense about what they are doing and where they are, but I can't actually see through their eyes or use their senses."

I frown internally at that. Then what did that mean for her current challenge? There was no way for her to have actual line of sight on me throughout so many streets, and even somehow collating all the local CCTV together wouldn't give her the full coverage of my movements inside the buildings. Nor was there a delay in her swarm adjusting its path to pursue me, even when I was sprinting at twice along at twice the local speed limit. Was it another possible future challenge, except with a Taylor that had second-triggered? Or had I somehow already been compromised, a small bug hidden on my person from the start just like at the bank challenge? Surely not, I had dipped into my shadow state at points to go through walls and the swarm had unerringly pursued me despite the fact that any bugs should have been dislodged by the move. I would probably find out more once I actually pinned down her location, being able to rule out the use of cameras or a friendly cape power would tell me the specifics better than pure guesswork could.

"B-but I can still keep track of people around me." She hastens to add, doubtless taking my momentary silence in the wrong way. "I mean, my bugs land on people all the time – and I can sense their position well enough to know that they've landed on something that's moving and alive. Keeping track of people moving from there is trivial, even if it's hard to work out who those people are or what they are doing just from my bugs alone. I'd have to have my bugs work out an outline of what they look like, which would probably attract more attention than we want."

"I don't think the average citizen out for a late-night stroll would appreciate it." I agree. "It would be rather bothersome if the PRT showed up to investigate the new bug-themed villain terrorising the streets – but even having a vague idea of where people are is good enough for what we need. Gang members are quite distinctive in their movements, not many people are willing to be outside for long at a time like this without half-sprinting wherever they want to go. Anyone patrolling back and forth or standing guard somewhere is pretty suspicious."

The bug-themed cape expresses her understanding with a hum. "Alright. I- Is there anything else we need to talk about, or should we just… go?"

I stretch my arms out, letting my personal shield fade out as I duck out of our temporary shelter – immediately getting plastered by the heavy rain outside. It was supposed to stop soon, but that was small consolation for us here and now. "I'll investigate ahead, checking out a few of the alleyways ahead of your range. If you keep walking in a straight direction, I'll double back and find you every few minutes and we can see if either of us spotted anything strange we can investigate." I give her a mock salute. "See you in a bit!" I freeze mid-wave, switching my powers mid-motion in an attempt to make it look as seamless as I can.

I barely catch her hasty farewell as I zip away in my speed-state. As much as there was some merit in being organised and talking things over with each other in advance, I think the best thing I could do to help her out was to push her in at the deep end. Well, not the deep end. The middle of the pool, maybe. A solid, practical example of her power being useful and powerful, that also reminded her that she could do a lot of good with it and she wasn't wasting her time in the attempt. I could tell her that as much as I like, but I don't think the message will ever sink in until she actually ends up in a fight with the local street thugs.

Dashing through the streets is oddly relaxing, my wet clothes and the increased resistance of the raindrops in front of me serving to slow me down more than usual – but there is something viscerally satisfying about actually being able to see the individual droplets falling around me and dashing past them before they even get close to the ground.

The satisfaction can't keep me entertained forever though. I needed to find a suitable target, which was the only reason I had suggested this area to meet-up in the first place. There were always shady characters around these downtown areas just outside of the docks. The ABB likely held more of a claim to the area than anyone else just because of the local demographics, but it wasn't exactly a stronghold of theirs that they ever needed to actively defend from other gangs. Passive ownership. Not white enough for the Empire to care, not important enough for either of the major gangs to really bother fighting over it. Mostly minor players, unaffiliated drug dealers and thugs – clearly distinct from the deliberately visible gang members passing through. An unpleasant place still, yes - but not in the somewhat war-torn way that you saw in the worst districts of the city.

In truth, I hadn't been entirely honest with Taylor about my searching methods. Some of it was true, of course, I was checking out the streets and alleyways and generally looking for criminal activity – that just wasn't very likely to be effective. Online testimonies from ex-vigilantes attested to that fact being normal, that even in notoriously scummy areas the odds of you just walking around and stumbling on a crime in progress was minimal. So, I cheated. Instead of hoping to just catch someone in the act, I just followed likely criminals around – knowing that they weren't likely to be up to any good this late at night.

That train of thought would likely send alarm bells ringing for the more alarmist sections of social media, in a city with as much blatant racial tension as this one – racial profiling and discrimination was obviously a hot topic. Fortunately, I was free of such bias.

CARLA WATFORD

"However nice you try to be, your first impression is almost always going to involve someone spotting a swarm of bugs the size of a building and running away." I make a defeated gesture. "I don't know, I saw the yellow and black and thought – 'Aha! She's going for a wasp theme, or maybe a bumblebee. Dangerous, but cute in its own way. She just hasn't added the stripes in yet.' "Cu- Ahem. I think you're overblowing it. And it wasn't a fly costume, it was just insect themed." She's sulking now, I can feel it. "It's practical. "Are you going hiking?" I protest. A school trip to the countryside? "And I wouldn't be so proud to list all of that preparation when you didn't pick up the number one most obvious inclusion on the list – a mobile phone?"

"I don't really use phones." She wags a finger in my direction to deflect the accusation. "But you're one to talk. You didn't have one either!"

"You didn't bring a phone because you live in the 1990s." I inform her solemnly. "I didn't bring one out of concern for the ceaseless erosion of privacy in the digital age, where mega-corporations, governments and rogue tinker groups can control these devices to spy on our activities in ever-greater detail. We are not the same."

There is a heavy pause. "That just sounds like an excuse to me."

"Electronics mess with one of my defensive powers." I admit begrudgingly. "Can't even have it in a backpack. My watch is weak enough that it's fine, but anything significant makes me pretty vulnerable when I need it the most."

"Oh." That deflates her attack a little. "Well, if we're going to team up - I suppose I'll carry a phone for both of us then. Who knows when we'll need it ourselves, or if we run into something like today where nobody on the scene has one either. That's what teammates are for, right?" That last part accompanies a look to me for assurance. Cute.

Taylor trying to be friendly and earnest is fun to see. I almost want to record it and replay it to her the next time she gives me a dour expression at school. "Right." I stretch my arms out above my head. "Maybe the synergy won't be that bad after all. Taylor had stopped dead in the middle of the street, causing me to walk straight into her. "Say that again?"

I flick one of her bugs off of my shoulder, selecting it with bug-control, assigning it as my administrator and gifting it with Vista's power in the same motion. "Like th-" I pause. Usually, I maintained my understanding of the positioning of the administrator even when I didn't actively select the bug-control powerset. This time, as I had switched back to the usual forcefield that I use for travelling – I had lost that feeling. I had a slight mental tug indicating the vague direction that my missing power was in – but I had quite clearly had authority taken away from me.

And now Taylor was poking her finger through a tiny cylinder of shortened space – the digit visibly lengthening as it passes through. "Oh, wow."

"Didn't expect that to happen." I reach out with bug-control experimentally, yoinking back control of the administrator. Back to normal, despite Taylor's plaintive cry of protest. "Although, maybe there's more potential in that than I had thought."

Had I ever swapped away from bug-control when using the administrator, while within Taylor's range? I suppose not. Usually, I used it for a purpose that required specific and refined control. My assumption that the priority the first power had over Taylor's would extend to the second power I had got from her was quite clearly flawed, but was that such a bad thing? If we ever fought – an incredibly likely occurrence for one very obvious reason – that sucked for me. I hear a quiet whisper from the girl. "That's amazing." I can't see her eyes behind the goggles, but I'm certain they are sparkling right now. "We need to experiment. And make some new strategies around it. And you need to tell me what other powers you can use-"

"Bug." I raise a hand to calm her down. On one hand, it was nice to see Taylor excited and talkative about something. On the other, I felt that I wasn't too far away from being chained to a post and used as a lab experiment for the next week. She looks disappointed for a moment, but nods regardless. "You're right. There'll be other times. No need to rush things now." Not just as a practical thing, not even as you helping me out as a rookie – just, um-"

"I get it." I shoot her a thumbs up. "Like I said before, I'm looking forward to working with you. "-or, did I misunderstand what you were going for there?" Maybe I interrupted too fast?

"No! I was- It was stupid. Don't even know what I was going to say, really." She pointedly fixes her gaze to the sidestreet, as if looking out for a crime that would break up the conversation. "I'm just feeling a bit giddy, the adrenaline – I guess. Need to calm down a bit." I could relate. I knew I could get pretty babbly when mouthing off to a defeated enemy after a particularly difficult challenge. Don't sound so emotional over that. You already have a friend! Me! Greg-me! I genuinely don't understand girls sometimes. "Void Cowboy and Bug. The dream-team." I nod in approval.

Taylor makes a pained noise. "The name is a bit- I mean- Maybe we should think about rebranding before it gets too well-known." There is a shifty tone in her voice. Like she wants to try and raise a subject without being the one to actually point out the issue. "Bug isn't great." I admit. "But it also isn't the worst thing you could be called either. "You aren't wrong. My name could be worse too-" She hesitantly starts.

"You could try something completely unrelated to bugs, if it's that much of a struggle." I offer. "As a team, we could make an awesome combo name together." I punch the air dramatically and strike a pose. "Void Cowboy! Void Cowgirl! The ultimate tag-team strike once again!" I raise my hands defensively as Taylor turns to look at me like I was one of her insects. "What?"

"Did you seriously, unironically just suggest that I should rename myself Void Cowgirl?" What was with the disbelieving tone? Don't make it sound like a crazy idea – it's for the sake of the theme!

"Sure, why not?" I watch her shake her head in disbelief. "No, really – what's with that look?"

"It's a lost cause." Her flat, almost mournful tone is somehow more offensive than anything else she could have tried. "I don't know why I even listened to your comments on my costume. I'm sure I can get better advice somewhere else."

Rude. "If this is about my costume, I'll concede that it doesn't look like I know what I'm talking about. This isn't my ideal hero costume. It's super basic, thrift store stuff – I can't make my own gear like you can. But one day, I'll be dressed like a badass and still have the awesome name I started with. You're doing things in reverse! You can fix the costume later, but people are going to remember the name you started out with – people on the internet remember these things!"

She looks away. "I'll think about it." Then she brightens up. "But- we are teammates, right? It would be awkward to have long names in the middle of a fight, wouldn't it?" I make a cautious noise of agreement. "So, maybe it would be best if I just called you Void for short."

People call me that online already. "I don't see a problem with that."

"Great." Why does she look so relieved?

I move the conversation on to the next logical topic. "How about team names then? Void Rangers?"

"…it's getting late." Taylor increases her pace without giving an answer, bursting into a brisk jog instead of giving an answer.

... that was too pointed even for me to ignore. "Don't dodge the question so obviously!"



-I hurtle towards the ground, waving a cheery farewell to the swarm racing up to devour me.

Splat.

FAILURE​

"Middle of the crossroad next to the cemetery." I murmur, tapping it down into my phone. That was consistent, at least. The range to the south was shorter than that to the north. It was hard to get an exact value out over the water to the east, but with enough data points to mark out the beginnings of a curve – I think I could put together a suitable guess for where Taylor was hiding. I needed my computer again. Or a physical map that I could draw the circle on – I needed absolute specifics, guessing the wrong building because I was lazy would set me back too many attempts. It was too easy for her to flood the entire building in bugs, I had trouble even checking a few rooms before the sheer volume of insect life started to affect my ability to phase and use my speed-state effectively.

Searching a large building, especially with the knowledge that she could be hiding in a cupboard rather than being out in the open – it was going to be time-consuming regardless. I just had to be efficient about it. Get the right area. Find Taylor. Kill her. Each step used a lot of attempts, but there was a certain inevitability to it as well. It wasn't a brick wall like Armsmaster – each attempt brought me closer, got me more data. It's only a matter of time.

"What was that?" Taylor asks, peering at me through her half-mask.

"Nothing." I look back up again as my vision fully returns. "How many people, do you think?" This was our third patrol in as many days. Our first one had been a short affair, but this time and the last had consumed basically our entire evenings. Productive, but a bit tiring in its own way.

She makes a thinking gesture. "Seven, I think. Unless any more have miraculously dodged all of the bugs inside so far, but that's pretty unlikely."

How on earth was it possible to lose someone when the building was filled with a swarm that size? The Empire would recruit me, the Protectorate would drop me in the cells for a night and come to play hardball recruitment in the morning. The skittering noises around us were audible as Taylor gathered her swarm back towards her, but I tuned them out for the moment. He would expect his opening move to be lethal against rookie capes. I haven't challenged him directly, but he's shown up enough in other peoples challenges that I know how he tends to start a fight off.

And I'm ready. I didn't expect a civil response, but when the feathery light touch of his blade appears on my neck – Clockblocker's power is already primed to meet it. I idly note that she had taken the opportunity to conceal all angles of the alleyway in a small wall of bugs. Smart. He probably couldn't teleport through that without clear vision.

Taylor zooms away with unnatural speed to easily escape the explosion, a wall of bugs in front and behind her preventing Oni Lee from directly intercepting her in a single move. "Hey!" I shout at the real Oni Lee, safely out of range of the explosion that I had tanked with Glory Girl's kindly donated power. "Fuck you, dickweed!" I take the opportunity to take the penalty required to enter my speed-state, a brief moment of paralysis passes without interruption – Oni Lee clearly showing a bit of caution before investigating my potential escape. Another grenade is tossed into the cracks of the wall left by the previous explosion. Here he comes.

Think. How do I run away? This building was old and broken down enough that he was unlikely to feel any compunctions about bringing it down around me if I tried to hide in a dark corner. Any extended escape attempt across the open road would be a disaster, he would just carpet-bomb the entire street to get to me – I wouldn't be able to shield myself with the paralysis required to drop the speedster powerset. I knew I should technically be faster than him on the long-distance movement thanks to my experience with Emma's challenges, but I didn't have a headstart this time and now I actually had to be concerned with the consequences of getting civilians killed in my escape.

Sneaking out one of the walls at the back was risky, expending a defensive option on the pure hope that he wouldn't be checking the outside perimeter for an escape attempt.

I pause. But then again, so did he. While Oni Lee was a known killer, this wasn't the rabid, bloodthirsting dog present in my simulations. He had his own morals to stick to – maybe a random innocent life wouldn't convince him to drop the bomberman act, but how about his own team?

Two more explosions brings the remains of the wall down along with a small section of the roof still relying on it as support. Before the smoke clears, I'm sprinting through. Not out into the city or to hide myself, but straight into the warehouse we had just attacked. Taylor clearly hadn't been quick to call her bugs off after our initial panic about Oni Lee – not a single member is left standing. Alive, by the looks of it – but either wishing that they weren't or just entirely unconscious.

Perfect. ABB gang members as collateral for his grenades, more than likely at least some of the things stored here were going to react poorly to explosions. I just had to dodge and dip around in my speed-state until he got tired of knifing me. Lung wouldn't allow the real Oni Lee to just kill his subordinates and screw up his operations just to get back at some rookies. He would rather we escaped for him to handle personally than have his subordinate be a loose cannon.

"That's right." I grin at him as he appears in the entranceway. "Behave." I don't bother to look behind me to see if he has already appeared at my back, I just start running. Faster than a car, way faster reactions – I wasn't going to get tagged that easily, even if he could teleport. I just had to move unpredictably, so that I didn't end up running into his blade before I could adjust.

Zig left. Zag right. Over the crate, around the pillar, trample on a fallen gang member – footsteps lighter than a feather in this state. Periodically, an ever-silent Oni Lee would appear in my path – already swinging his blade in an attempt to cut me off, or thrust at an unexpected angle around a corner to catch me off guard. We both turn to glance at the entrance when it loudly swings shut, I get a brief glimpse of Taylor's costume before the door closes.

Why- ah. I could see it now. I'd been so focused on stalling him out and waiting for him to give up or tire, that I hadn't considered the possibility of winning outright. He hadn't noticed yet, it would seem – but the windows have turned into a seething mass of bugs. Not just to let new additions to the swarm in, but serving to prevent him from easily escaping through an exit. Even a grenade might not clear a large enough hole in the swarm, considering how easily any gap could be filled with bugs by the time the smoke had cleared.

Still. That left me with the simple issue of putting him on the back foot in the first place. I duck under a slow-motion lunge, idly tugging at the grenades at his waist. Nothing. I couldn't pull them free with Velocity's power active. Too weak.

Other than that… what options did I even have? I was stuck in this state until I could hide from him for a few seconds, and Taylor shutting the door closed down the most likely escape avenue I could have tried – even if she did likely have her reasons. Find some form of super-cocaine powder and throw it in his face? I could probably pick up something like that, but the odds of finding something so convenient just lying around for me to pick up was astronomically low. I change direction again, dashing left to go behind his back after his latest teleportation – did he just try to trip me? Maybe that would work on other types of speedsters, but I'm a 'everything is slower' guy rather than 'I'm super fast'. I can react to that.

Taylor's voice calls out – recognisable despite the deeper tone caused by the state I was in. "Lights!"

Lights?

Lights. "I could kiss you right now." That was her plan. Block the windows not just to prevent escape, but also to blot out the ambient moonlight and streetlamps. Close the door for the same reason, block out every light source but one – and if I could just turn that off, mister line-of-sight teleporter will be as blind as everyone else!

Of course, the first time I loop around to the light panel – I realise I can't just press the switch normally. Not when I'm crippled by Velocity's power. I take a light graze across my arm for the trouble, opting to sprint another lap around the warehouse instead. Taylor is helping as best she can, even when she can't see. Rotating walls of bugs that block line of sight, yet thin enough to only slightly slow me down as I burst through them. The ceiling coated in a chittering, skittering horde that practically pulses with malevolence – no easy purchase for him to move to a convenient vantage point up there. He's forced to use his teleports in sharp bursts now, once up to the film of bugs – swipe through it to lay eyes beyond it, then again to enter the next section of the room.

This time, with enough force behind them – the lights shut off. In moments, the entire room is utterly black. I can't even see a few inches in front of my face.

The ceaseless chittering noise that's been following me ever since the alleyway changes pitch, it's focused now. Every bug, save for – presumably – those blocking the windows, changes direction. Converging on a single point that I can't see, but the result is obvious. An explosion shakes the room, a brief moment of illumination as I realise that he is trying to clear the cloud of bugs with grenades – and perhaps illuminate the room enough to teleport as well.

I take the opportunity to slide myself into a hidden corner between a few empty cardboard boxes and unused crates, stumbling a little in the dark as I go – the warehouse making for treacherous ground even when I know I just need to follow the wall. This should be pretty safe, given the size of the warehouse. I drop the speed-state. Absently handing off the Othala power to a bug sitting on my hand – basic durability this time – then raising my personal shield once again. With my back to a wall, I could phase out of things got really hectic – but I didn't fancy my odds at actually escaping a lucky grenade throw by running around in the dark like I was. I wouldn't even know which way to dodge.

And clearly, he wasn't as worried about the collateral as he was before – but he no longer had infinite grenades to work with. Without his ability to teleport and leave his clone to use its entire arsenal, it didn't take long for him to run out of stock. I could relate to the helpless feeling that he was probably experiencing. Bugs were oppressive. Even if his mask prevented the worst of it, even if they could never really deliver a conclusive blow while Taylor was being nice – there was a sense of powerlessness when you were caught in the swarm. You can never do enough to clear them away from your eyes and ears, you constantly feel surrounded – you can't shake the knowledge that if you could just get your hands on Taylor, you would win but you just can't get there. You don't know where to go, or even where to run to – your sense of direction is long gone, and the entire time all of your senses are screaming at you about how gross, disgusting and repulsive this entire experience is.

I did feel bad for him. Even if he tried to kill me. I should probably be angrier about that, but somehow I find it hard to muster up any complaints about it. Even if it's the real-life version for once, I can't go around hating everyone who makes an attempt on my life – I'd never make any friends. I know it should be different, but I just can't get that personal spark of anger there to start holding a grudge.

I hear the door open, and shut. A brief outline in the doorway, only highlighting the absolute mountain of bugs spiralling at the centre of the room. "Are you okay, Void?" She sounds a little unsure. On reflection, that's probably because her bugs are telling me that I'm curled up in a ball in the corner – with no idea if I'm injured or not.

"Thank god." Taylor lets out a ragged sigh. I can hear her pacing towards me, steps far surer than mine in the dark – the only sense of distance I have is the slight tug indicating that the Othala-bug had applied itself to her and died in the process. Unnecessary in the end, but even a weakened buff is something she can get value out of. It's a good habit to get into. "I, uh, choked his airway a little. Thought it was the best I could do. I shrug helplessly. "Stick a paper bag on his head? I don't think he would fall for the same trick again if he got free." Otherwise, there wasn't anything to do until the police-

I bite my lip as Taylor finds the lights and flicks them back on. Could I- Dare I? A supervillain, no witnesses, except for Taylor who should be at least partial to my ideas… especially if I just claimed he vanished into the night when I wasn't looking. Could I just… kidnap him? Drop him in a basement somewhere, and just keep challenging him day-in, day-out?

It would be selfish. Dangerous. But, potentially, very rewarding. I doubted that there was such a gap between us that I couldn't bridge it with enough attempts. How many wins before he, or she, was loyal enough to ignore the forced captivity? How powerful would the full version of his powers be – and how much would that accelerate my growth?

Stop. Greg. I'm getting carried away. List the downsides. Everyone will know that Oni Lee disappeared after a fight with the two of us. We'll be a threat from that point on – especially once I show up with a powerful version of his skills. My power might not be able to fully cover for the switch between actually taking them captive and then suddenly having them join my team. I might look like a Master to the other groups in the city.
