I doubted my ability to win against Lung fast enough to turn him to my side – so the risk of a fight between him and I, or an even more one-sided one between him and Taylor, was a real possibility.

Fuck. If Taylor wasn't here, or there were fewer gang members as witnesses, fewer sightings of massive bug clouds…

Whatever. Maybe it was something to think about in the future. Take a road-trip to another city, throw a quiet villain in the back of the van and take them home. The risks, in this case, were just too much, even if I was willing to try and work my way around Taylor's morals to do it.

"-Yeah. Stop him from seeing anything, call the police for pickup." I pause. "Or, PRT actually."

"Already called them." She tosses some zip-ties at me to apply to the other fallen gang members. "I don't suppose you have regeneration up?"

"No." I check. "Reflexes." I hand it off to the closest bug, watching it out of the corner of my eye as it flies into Taylors chin and falls away – dead. "Is it bad?"

"Not terrible." She denies, clearly being far rougher with her own ties than needed to secure the ABB cape. "Just a few grazes from debris, rather than the explosions themselves. He didn't chase me for long. Some bruises where I hit the wall a bit hard coming to a stop."

It was hard to be sure about the exact route he took. It would have been trivial to traverse a few rooftops, offload some grenades and be back to my chosen hiding spot in the house in seconds for him. If I had chosen a more standard escape route, it could have seemed like he was near-omnipresent with his teleportation capabilities.

We wouldn't get so lucky a second time. He would have avoided me if he was aware of my defensive options, while Taylor would have been a priority target with her area denial – if he had continued the chase, her buffed speed would have expired and she would have been a sitting duck.

More arguments for the idea of not letting there be a next time... I shake my head. I don't even know how to keep someone captive, or even where I would do it. Nor do I need an easy reason to be arrested whenever Tattletale finally lays eyes on me and realises that I have an easily-provable crime under my belt.

I check Othala's power again. Strength. "I'll heal you myself in a moment, once this guy is all tied up." I glance around as I snap a quick picture on my phone as proof of our victory. Keep the caption short and sweet... done. "Just five?"

"The others ran off at the start, I just let them go." Understandable. Hardly something to complain about, given the results. Before long, there's nothing left to do but wait – my attempts to cycle through Othala's power taking an embarrassingly long time, leaving me with little choice but to close the most obvious cuts and bruises that I could see manually with Panacea's striker ability.

I'm not even close to complete by the time Taylor announces that the heroes have arrived – but at least she isn't bleeding over the floor now.

I take a steady breath in. Oni Lee, defeated. But not to any great benefit for me – not yet. I needed to challenge him before the heroes took him away, and then make any progress I could against the heroes themselves as well.

And then… what? I hadn't expected a real cape fight so suddenly, so soon. Not in these unwanted backwaters, deliberately chosen for how non-critical they were to the gangs. I did well, given the circumstances – and Taylor was impressive too given her lack of experience. But it only highlighted the disparity that remained between most capes and I. Tricks and gimmicks were fine, but all of them combined weren't enough to convincingly defeat Oni Lee alone. Face him on even-footing? Certainly. I was a real cape now. But I only had one life, out in the real world. Taking risks like this… it wasn't good enough. I should only be taking fights that I know I can win, that I know I have won before. I didn't have a choice this time around, but that wouldn't always be the case.

"Well then." I fix a wry grin on my face as Taylor steps up next to me. "Ready to hear another recruitment pitch?"

Her face falls as she realises the truth of my words. "They are going to do that, aren't they?" She groans. "And here I was looking forward to a bit of honest praise."

"You can get it from me instead." I console her. She crosses her arms as if to challenge the statement. "No! I'm serious. That was a great plan. You used your bugs well, came to my rescue like the gallant knight in silver armour that you are. How can you expect me to say anything other than nice things?"

"It's embarrassing coming from you." That actually looks like the truth, she practically shrinks under every word I say.

I pace towards the entrance. "Well, I mean it. I fully expected you to do the sensible thing and run away to get help, but you really- Ow! What was that for?" I nurse my shin for a moment after she sends an annoyed kick my way.

She struts past me, shoulders stiff. "What do you even mean, you expected me to run away? I can't believe you sometimes. You say one nice thing, and it's like you have to say something twice as dumb to make up for it." Is she angry? I think she's angry. "You said that we were a team."

"We are!" I raise my hands in the air. "But that doesn't mean that course of action wasn't the smart, logical thing to do- hey!" I dodge the kick this time, only causing her to pout harder.

"You don't get it." Taylor looks like she has something she wants to say. "You- Hmph. Jerk." She exits the building first, as if that final statement summed up everything somehow.

"I'm not apologising!" I call after her. "You know that I'm right!"

"Girl trouble?" Triumph peers through the entrance at me, calling out in a stage whisper.

I adopt a mournful expression. "Always." I toss my thumb behind me, to the bound ABB members held in a line – now wide awake and likely regretting their life choices, if only because of the insects I could see roaming out of their pants even now. "Care to take these guys off of our hands?"

A group of PRT officers rush through the doorway at his gesture, sweeping through the warehouse and gathering up the captives. A glance behind Triumph shows Taylor talking with Miss Militia. One of my highest priority targets, if I got a solid version of her power – that is. It was easy to imagine getting screwed by my power again, but I only needed to get lucky once.

Three challenges. Oni Lee. Miss Militia. Another attempt at Triumph. Make up with Taylor, for whatever reason that was needed. Troll PHO and gloat to all the people with ABB tags. No big deal for the one and only Gregster. The evening isn't over yet!

#1,263
One of the advantages of my power is the exact same as one of the disadvantages. There is no preparation beforehand. No set-up required or even possible before attempting a challenge. While that came with the disadvantage of not being able to bring in tools or change the scenarios in advance, it did mean that only a single glance on my target was required to give it an honest attempt. Sure, a few challenges here and there did change location in response to where I was in real life – but usually, I would be dropped into the same situation in the same position against the same enemy.

This was my first time seeing Miss Militia in person. My first time laying eyes on Oni Lee. Yet, in theory, I could collect their powers for myself in what would seem like mere seconds in the real world. Optimistically, of course. It wasn't that common for me to win challenges in a single attempt, even though eventually that would become the norm for me as I grew in power. A fact supported by the fact that my little dance in real life with Oni Lee hadn't ended with my untimely death, even if he had the advantage – I was a real Cape opposing him, not some kid with a few party tricks.

I was being optimistic, of course. But even if I failed, I would be happy to expand my knowledge of the challenges facing me. These two powers were close to the top of my most-wanted list. A ranged attack and teleportation. If I could get Miss Militia's powerset at even a fraction of its strength I would be able to one-shot every non-brute in the bay from an ambush.

With my power's track record, I was already aware that I was probably overestimating the likely reward - but I had, sometimes, been pleasantly surprised by the utility of my rewards before. I could at least be confident that I would be no weaker after a victory, so I had nothing to lose making the attempt.

The only question was what order I should start in. Oni Lee's power would obviously help Miss Militia's challenge a lot, but could I hope to defeat Oni Lee in a fair fight, without Taylor coming to help? I wasn't sure about that. I could stall forever, but actually landing a killing blow would require an ambush and a suitable weapon, both of which would be difficult given his ability to instantly teleport away as I attack him. Any hope of just tiring him out would likely struggle thanks to the anti-stalling measures of the simulation improving his stats as the hours ticked on without any signs of combat or movement.

Miss Militia, on the other hand, should be significantly squishier – with the simple disadvantage that she had a massive range advantage on me and would likely have no qualms about being exceptionally lethal. Where Oni Lee and Triumph would likely enter melee range at least momentarily as part of their fighting styles, Miss Militia would snipe me from some distant rooftop before I even knew that she was there.

Triumph was here as well, but I was even less sure about how I would be able to defeat him - despite the growth I had made, I wasn't really any better suited to defeating a brute than before. Even if I claimed the first tier of Oni Lee and Miss Militia today, I doubted I would even come close to beating him. It was just a bad match up - even if he wasn't the strongest Cape around, I just didn't have anything that hit hard enough to win.

Well. Without any idea what I was in for, the order probably didn't matter that much. I mentally flip a coin, then settle my sights on Miss Militia.

Miss Militia

Heroine 1/6

(ZONE)​

Not the modifier I had expected, but not getting a GANG modifier was undeniably a good thing. But I'll have to actually get inside before getting my hopes too high. Sometimes challenges are way harder than they seem on paper. "Challenge."

My real-life view of the heroes erupts into white light, my body experiencing a brief moment of weightlessness before settling on solid tarmac once more.

To my left, ruined streets and half-demolished buildings. To my right, the main road lined with cracks and fissures – gaping holes and broken-down vehicles littering the street.

What was with my power and imagining some apocalyptic scenario as a backdrop for some of these challenges? I can't see my opponent from here, but that likely didn't mean much- I throw myself to the ground as my forcefield goes down, the sound of the bullet that hit it reaching me a moment later. That proves to be a mistake, a second bullet slamming into my leg as I fall and then a third narrowly whizzing over my shoulder. I shift into my shadow-state, taking advantage of the free-movement as a shadowy mass despite my actual leg being shredded. I dive behind a nearby car as temporary safety from the rain of bullets.

Not safe enough, apparently. The next bullet cleaves through the remnants of the chassis to hit me in the torso, eliciting a roar of pain and surprise from me. A split-second later, another bullet pierces my cover – this time far off to the side. She might not be able to see me, but I remember Miss Militia's power. If it isn't using some special ammunition, she doesn't need to waste time reloading – she just uses her power to switch to a gun with full ammo.

Which meant that she could just bring the biggest, nastiest sniper rifle she could find and fire it as fast as she could aim. The only thing stopping it from being something like a machine gun was probably the recoil and the ability to aim at this kind of range. I tear my hoodie off and over my head, eating another shot in the process – then I drape it between the car and myself, nailing it with Clockblocker's power before it can fall.

A full, perfect shield – for as long as I could refresh the time-lock on it. If she realised what I had done, she would probably be able to swap to some kind of missile or explosive weapon – but concealed by the car, she wouldn't be able to see exactly how I was surviving these shots.

Surviving… I look down at myself. Red, bloody puddles pooling at my feet. My vision swaying and doubling wherever I look. My clothes already ruined. The familiar, icy-cold feeling of shock settling in from the bloodloss of a half-dozen bullet wounds already. Perhaps surviving wasn't the right word, this time around. The clockblocked shield was a great idea, I just didn't think of it fast enough – didn't have the time to react when the challenge started with me already within her sights. My first instinct had been to make myself a smaller target to the shooter to buy a second or two to find cover between rounds, but the area I started in had no real cover close by and Miss Militia didn't need to reload anyway. Couldn't clockblock the car directly, it was too large to be affected by the weak version of his power that I have. My own clothing couldn't be used until it wasn't being worn by me anymore, the Manton effect in full force at this level – and taking the time to take it off gave her time to riddle me with bullets.

Belatedly, I realise that I've fallen onto one knee. I shift into my shadow-state and back. The healing factor of the power was weak, too weak to save me – but it does help to bring me back towards some semblance of lucidity.

"Greg." I murmur to myself. "Don't die for nothing." Don't die cowering behind a car, waiting for an unlucky bounce of a bullet to kill you – or for the hoodie to lose its temporal lock at just the wrong moment. That won't help me next time. I need to find out more about this challenge. Where do I need to go, what am I actually fighting – and what options could I try next time?

Don't wait for death just because it won't stick and I can try again. Go. I swap back to Glory Girl's forcefield. I need it as the active power for the cooldown on the shield to recharge, the hoodie briefly comes unpaused once – requiring me to re-freeze it before my head gets parted from my body by another lucky shot. Once the forcefield is back up, I swap to my shadow-state and rush to the side of the street as far as I can. The shadow state ends, and I'm forced to inelegantly hop on my uninjured leg for the last few steps – praying that the forcefield manages to block enough for me to make it into cover once more.

It does, and it doesn't. I stand facing the alleyway at the side of the road, not quite out of sight from where I assumed Miss Militia was shooting from. If I was another metre ahead, I would be safe – hidden in the alleyway, in another try I could have dashed straight over here and potentially slowly healed my injuries as I advanced through the buildings towards her. Unfortunately for me, that isn't possible. The heavy, dense feeling as my hand presses into what should be thin-air tells the story – about the importance of the modifier of this zone, the nature of the challenge and what I need to do to advance.

A ZONE wall. Ensuring that I couldn't leave the confines of the chosen battlefield. Miss Militia doesn't miss my now-prone body, I don't even feel the pain of impact before my field of vision briefly jerks to the side before normalising.

FAILURE​

I brush away the hint informing me about the ZONE mechanic. I didn't need to know, nor waste more attempts to even try to scout out the other walls of the ZONE. I could understand the scenario based only on the positioning of that one. A long, thin battlefield along the road. Miss Militia on one end, with all the firepower at her disposal – and me on the other, needing to close the distance and avoid the bullet-hell she sends my way. There was cover in the street, abandoned cars, fallen rubble and disused roadworks – but not enough to keep me truly safe. The direction of my approach would always be predictable, the challenge didn't allow me to flank or hide in a permanently safe spot – it was just a question of reaching her position before she kills me. No option to leave the road into an alleyway or neighbouring house, just a straight shot along to her position.

And there was a long way for me to go to reach that point. I hadn't spotted her, but I fully expected her to be at the end of the vast stretch of road I had seen in the challenge – the elevated city hall that was visible from so very, very far away on this particular road. She would always have sight of my movements so long as moving into the safety of the alleyways was out of reach, and at this distance I had only experienced a fraction of her arsenal. Perhaps a sniper rifle was all she could hit me with for now, but when I drew closer on my next attempt I would have to start contending with actual machine-gun fire, grenade launchers and who knows what else she would try to hit me with.

Not stacked in my favour at all. My action plan for the second round was clear to me already, dive to safety again – set up my clockblocked shield and then use the few seconds of safety to overcome the paralysis inflicted by my speedster power. I would be stuck in that power from then on, never having any time to survive the momentary freeze needed to exit the power – but hopefully the combination of being a small target and moving around faster than a car would let me close the distance despite the bullet storm. From there… well, I would have to try and work something out at that point. Perhaps I would be able to enter the building and take cover from there, or at least find somewhere to hide and shift back to normal.

It wasn't going to be easy, as fast as I was in that state, bullets were faster. I would be relying on her aim being unable to keep up with me, and that any attempts at wildly spraying fire down the road didn't hit me by pure chance. I didn't have Velocity's full power set – I wouldn't be able to roll with the bullets or try and mitigate their impact. Just as my attacks in that form were pitifully weak, attacks against me had a much greater impact if they actually made a solid connection despite my speed and improved ability to dodge. She would surely not have any real qualms about just bombarding the street with grenades and rockets if she felt it would be easier to hit me – I would need both strategy and a fair bit of luck to win.

But oddly, I felt somewhat optimistic about it. It didn't feel like an insurmountable challenge. No. The worst part about it was just going to be getting those second, third and fourth attempts. Even with a clear and logical path forward, my power didn't allow me to repeat failed challenges immediately. Where previously there was a challenge icon, now there was thirty minute countdown until I could attempt it again.

I didn't really want to try and get them to stick around for thirty minutes. I expected them to be gone in ten, and I was already thinking of how I was going to be dodging all of their questions or deflecting to something easier to talk about. Extending a conversation would naturally lead into my powers, which would obviously raise eyebrows back at the PRT. Nobody would fail to draw the connection between the different powersets I displayed and their original owners around the bay, all it would take was someone getting nervous about whether the Wards identities were exposed or someone to guess that I was an exponentially growing threat. It was a minor miracle that there were no real Masters or Strangers in the Bay – their mere existence would bump my threat rating dramatically once the supposed 'truth' of my powers came out.

Nor would they turn their body cameras off. They would have a file on me already. Analysts and perhaps a Thinker or two would look at the footage, trying to build a profile of my actions, personality and capabilities. With this costume on, limited exposure and my rather wild post history on PHO I had no doubt that most Thinkers would be thrown wildly off in their first assumptions about me – that I was a loudmouth and a braggart, a thrill-seeker with an ego to stroke rather than a legitimately dangerous threat.

Mostly because… that information was also true. Or was true, at least. I was self-aware enough to admit that. I've changed in a lot of ways over the last few weeks, but I'm still Greg at the end of the day. But I couldn't rely on the consistency behind my past actions to maintain my safety, the façade wouldn't last if I gave them reason to doubt that their assessments are wrong – even if that reason was something as innocuous as an extended interview or power testing the abilities they already knew I had. That wasn't to say that running away at every opportunity and acting like I had something to hide wouldn't cause much the same scrutiny, but that was the kind of awkward situation I was in. My best bet was to be non-suspicious for as long as possible, then, if it came to it, prevent any suspicions that did arise from being turned into facts or action. There was a time-limit for any consequences to happen to me – once I was Triumvirate, no, even Lung tier… I would be safe enough to avoid outright conflict without warning.

I shake my head to clear the lingering stars from my vision, taking in the sight of the real Miss Militia in front of me. She struck a less-imposing figure than I had expected from promotional posters and fanart, the presence of the slim pistol in her hand pointed at the ground notwithstanding. A combat specialist, yes. Dangerous from a distance and up-close, true. But I wasn't the Greg of old that only drooled over the possibilities behind manifesting firearms at will. Looking past the obvious weapon, I saw someone that I had beaten dozens of times in melee already.

Not literally, of course. But looking at her build, the complete lack of real protection on her head and neck along with my own knowledge that there was no Brute rating at all to speak of? If I somehow got into a grapple or a knife fight, I would win more often than not.

Boys are stronger than girls. I had gotten my ass kicked by girls enough to not underestimate them, so that statement couldn't be called arrogance or sexism. Even if she trained every day, I would likely win in a simple contest of strength or speed even now. I would have made a good fight out of it even a few months ago, before I ever got my powers. I might get manhandled the first few times, if only to learn what her usual grapples and manoeuvres are - but I'm confident that I would win in the end with the aid of more useful powers at melee range, knowing that her own power would be near useless with her arms locked up.

The only recourse for her would be... what, an explosive of some kind? That would hurt her more than me. A melee weapon only favoured my suite of powers and skillset more, a pistol or any other small weapon still needs to be aimed - difficult when I would know exactly what to expect and where it would appear.

"-oy?" I drift back to attention as she waves at me.

Right. Greg. Focus. Stop thinking about how badly you would crush her if she didn't start literal miles away from you. You're here to look awesome and leave without explaining anything. Get on that. "Sorry, a few of those grenades got a bit close. My ears will probably be ringing for a bit. What did you say?"

She doesn't look happy to hear that. I suspect she didn't approve of us jumping into a fight with a known mass murderer – the reminder of how close things were likely reinforcing her opinion. "I wanted to ask for a proper statement on what happened here? While we are, naturally, only to happy to receive Oni Lee into our custody – your testimony is extremely valuable when it comes to bringing him and his allies to account for his actions." She nods behind her, to scorch-marked roads and light embers smouldering from buildings that were thankfully already too ruined to catch fire in the explosive spree. "It also helps to avoid any wild accusations about your own actions, choosing to leave without a statement might open up members of the public to demand reparations for damage caused in the fight. You might not be worried about having to respond to that, but reputational damage can follow you for a long time as a Cape."

I glance over to Taylor, also being approached by Triumph. It was hard to say if it was a deliberate choice to separate us, but I was willing to assume that it was just well-practiced procedure and nothing personal at all. Two statements that weren't checked with each other are better than one rehearsed one, all the better to spot inconsistencies and gather the real truth for the PRT. "Sure, we don't mind filling you in. We'd better include Bug in the conversation though, I spent most of the time running from Oni Lee – she definitely has more knowledge of what other people were actually doing than me."

She nods amicably. Good. No special demands for a separate statement or concerns about us specifically, it made sense – no point being antagonistic to two likely candidates for the Wards.

"Hm- Oh, Void!" Taylor turns as we approach, an element of concern in her voice. "Triumph was just making a good point about Lung and how this might make us a target if it becomes common knowledge. Without any other witnesses, Lung is likely to just blame the PRT if nobody says anything. I know we didn't really plan on fighting any of the ABB capes, so maybe it would be a good thing if we just kept quiet for a bit? I'm not sure, what do you think?" Taylor is oddly babbly - clearly excited about the presence of the heroes.

I breathe in through my teeth sharply. "That's not possible. Sorry."

Miss Militia shifts uncomfortably. "I know this must seem like the PRT trying to steal your thunder and the bragging rights for taking down Oni Lee, but our concern about Lung is genuine. You were extremely fortunate that Lung was seen outside of Brockton Bay not long ago, if he was in the area you could both have died. He's an incredibly durable, powerful Cape that even the entirety of the local PRT would struggle to stop at his peak – certainly not in time to save you if he decided to seek you out." She reaches a hand up to tweak the position of her scarf. "It's inevitable that he will find out the truth eventually, but if it comes after a clash with the PRT or long after Oni Lee is moved to a secure position – you will at least have a chance to be a lot safer by then."

Triumph speaks up. "Joining a team for deterrence, for example. However annoyed Lung is, he won't try and kill a Ward – but he knows that he can probably get away with murdering a few independents without too many consequences coming his way. We won't just stand by and allow that to happen, of course, but there is only so much protection we can provide to unaffiliated strangers who we know nothing about. If he attacks you on a patrol halfway across the city, we might not reach you in time to help."

This time, Taylor shakes her head before I can say anything. "I'm still not sure on joining the Wards yet. I have a lot of respect for you, but I'm happy with how my partner and I are getting along so far. If we're worried about trouble, we'll keep the offer to join in mind – but for now, I think we'll face whatever comes out of this together." Aw. She didn't even need to ask for my opinion to know what it was. Confidence from Taylor, it was great to see. "We both knew what we were signing up for when we came out here, after all. It might have happened a little sooner than we would like, but we would never have ventured outside together if we were afraid of fighting other Capes."

Triumph shakes his head. "That's admirable. And I do, genuinely, respect that attitude. I think that's a fine feeling for budding heroes to have. But Lung isn't an ordinary Cape. The guy is a real monster, a thug by every definition of the word. Believe me when I say that I am not underestimating you when I say he would beat both of you with ease. He would beat me as well. Miss Militia too. He doesn't fight fair, he won't walk up to you and introduce himself before ramping up – the first you'll hear about him is when he crashes through a house wall, already three times your size before the first blow is traded." The concern is genuine, I think. His points aren't entirely wrong, either. "If you want to take credit later on, or when the subterfuge has passed its usefulness – we won't stop you. I just don't want to see an angry dragon man dropping the corpses of two promising heroes on the street as a warning to everyone else before you have time to reconsider your choice."

Taylor looks at me as I cough apologetically. "You do make some great points, but like I said. It isn't possible." I make a shushing gesture as they move to object. "Not because it was a bad idea, I can see the appeal of the rest of the ABB not hunting us down until Oni Lee and these other guys getting out and telling everyone – but I actually already posted on PHO about this while we were waiting for you guys."

There's a pregnant pause for a moment as all three faces turn towards me in disbelief. I pull my phone back out and turn the screen towards them in silent response.

I scroll through a few comments for them as they peer at the small screen, not even reaching halfway through the page before pulling away. I think they can get the gist of the situation from that.

"I see." Triumph sighs. "Well. There goes that idea. I'll only ask that you be careful, perhaps stay away from ABB territory for a while. We don't really know why Lung left town, but our best guess is that he's taken the recent territory losses to the Empire hard and ran off to recruit some more manpower. We won't know until he comes back, but I'm sure you would rather not get ambushed by both Lung and an unexpected Cape or two as backup because you got too predictable."

"I appreciate the advice – but we do tend to be pretty sensible about these things, despite what this looks like." I glance at Oni Lee, cuffed but not yet taken away – they seem to be happy with my makeshift blindfold, evidently not having a super-special PRT-branded one in their vehicle to put on instead. "We usually scout out our attacks pretty extensively and avoid direct fights, Bug over here has great situational awareness, and most fights are over before they ever begin anyway. I don't think there's any real danger of someone finding and catching us without a Mover or Thinker rating to work with."

I was drip-feeding them some of Taylor's abilities here, but it isn't anything that she wouldn't have happily shared herself if I left her to it. She doesn't have an aversion to the heroes like I do, she just doesn't want the Wards to be like Winslow all over again. The heroes were all too happy to let me talk, and I get to keep my own details to a minimum – even if they were curious, I didn't think it was likely that they would push that much outside of power testing offers or a conflict scenario. Too likely to cause a discussion that might push someone away or hit a sore spot, I'm certain that their policy was to maintain constant, positive relations above all else – at least, until something happened to cause the gloves to come off.

Team leader's prerogative.

"Bug." I catch up with her. "Let's delay going back for a moment. Can you find us a nice, private spot where nobody can see or stumble across us?"

Her steady pace halts for a moment. "W-what for?"

"Do you really need to ask?" It wasn't like we had talked about anything else. Besides, even if the bullying had tapered off dramatically since my interactions with the Trio – I wouldn't ignore the possibility of an untimely shove or shoulder landing on an unattended bruise. To say nothing of what people would say in an actual changing room before whatever sports the female students were doing right now at Winslow. "Just trust me on this. You'll feel way better afterwards."

"R-right." I can't see her full expression behind the half-mask, but she obliges nonetheless. She breezes through the street for a few more minutes in silence, before pausing at the third alleyway we come across. "This should do." She decides. "Nobody moving around the street, no windows to see us, nobody inside the buildings on either side and I don't see any cameras either."

I duck in after her. "Works for me." I wiggle my fingers at her. "Now then. Let me get under that costume, we'd best get it done as soon as possible."

"W-we probably shouldn't-" Taylor shifts half-heartedly. "-b-but maybe just a little bit is fine if it's in the dark…"

I give her a strange look as she looks flustered. "Sure." I circle around behind her, considering her costume. "I don't know if you have any other plans as a heroine-" I step up behind her, one hand rising up to cover the side of her neck. A slowly-colouring bruise that I hadn't managed to handle completely before the heroes arrived. "-but if you intend to stay partnered with me for a while, it might be useful to change your costume plans up a little bit. Something with a bit more skin showing, or if that doesn't work for you – something that at least comes off a little bit easier than what you have now."

"I'm not- I'm a superhero!" Her voice sounds a little agitated and the feel of her pulse against my hand is far too fast – although the somewhat-frozen stance the rest of her body has taken runs counter to the idea that she's angry. I tilt my head to the side, my hand moving away from her now-unmarred neck as I peer at her in the dim light – trying to find another visible spot to heal. "I'm not going to- to dress up like a stripper in public!"

When did I ever say that? Although there was a certain appeal to the idea. "I never said that you had to do that. Although it would help in some ways, admittedly." I begin. "But there is a certain appeal to me being able to apply a full-power blessing to you at any time, without being diminished by going through your bugs. I need skin contact for that. To say nothing about how difficult doing this kind of thing would be if you were badly injured or unconscious." I didn't even fully understand how she got the suit on, let alone how to take it off. "I don't see anything else up here… you said you hit a wall, right? Open up the suit, take it from me – being stab-proof doesn't help protect you from crashing into things very fast."

There's a lengthy pause. "Oh." Taylor says eventually. "You were talking about injuries."

I frown. "Yeah? What did you think I was talking about?"

The newbie heroine stays suspiciously quiet. The silence stretches on for a moment as I recount the last few exchanges.

If I was to be fair, I did kind of let the conversation drop before randomly continuing again a few minutes later once my internal debate about independence and ethics concluded. It isn't entirely crazy to think that the two conversations were entirely unrelated. Unfortunately, I wasn't going to be fair.

"Pervert." I accuse simply.

She splutters. "What? No! I was- You were the one who-" She waves her hands and starts to deflect. "Let's just move on. You wanted to see my back, right? There's a flap here that covers the seal, then you undo this strap-"

I let her narrate the half-dozen steps it takes to turn the bodysuit into something that might be possible to get out of. I would certainly be sticking with hoodies and solid-looking jackets for now, at least until I picked up a tinker specialisation somewhere.

"-And then this just peels off easily, at least until I get around to finding some way to armour it." My attention snaps back to Taylor as a part of her costume comes away to reveal bare skin. She turns around to glare at me sullenly. "And this is all you get, by the way." Doubtless referring to her now uncovered back – the front of her suit still covering her front as she holds it tightly to her. "Even if you are oblivious to the fact, I am a girl and certainly won't be turning around for you."

I raise my hands in surrender. "Easy, easy! Here I am trying to be nice and fix you up before school, and you're practically hissing at me the entire way. Are you still mad about what I said earlier, about how you should have just ran off?"

"Of course I'm still mad about that." I was pretty sure that was a lie, and I had only just reminded her of it, but now she was doubly angry. "Even if you say it would be the right choice, I can't accept that. I want to be a hero. Not just someone looking out for themselves or trying to survive. If it was just about me, I wouldn't even have gone out on patrol once yet. What kind of hero would leave their teammate to die against a serial killer like that?"

I keep my words to myself, pressing a hand against her upper hip – I was pretty sure now that she had undersold how hard she got tossed into a wall, far too many budding bruises and red marks to account for a simple stumble. Oni Lee clearly hadn't stayed around to finish the job, likely just doing a carpet bomb of the alleyway Taylor was in before teleporting towards me as his primary target – not even seeing if the grenades hit or not. He wasn't omniscient, and I was pretty sure he didn't share vision with his clones either. Was it simple luck, or had she managed to us her bugs to adjust the paths of the clones and their grenades enough to save herself from the full blast? It didn't matter now, I guess.

The bruises probably extended further down her side and thighs, but I think that pushing Taylor to remove the bottom half of her suit would possibly be a step too far for her right now. Small steps.

She seems to take my silence as understanding. "I made my choice to come out here, with you. I think you would do the same as well, even if you don't want to admit it." Her voice takes on some imperceptible quality, a lighter tone that I can't quite place. "Even if you would sit there and say that you were the logical choice, or the only one who could outrun it – it would just be an excuse. You're a good person." She casts a glance over her shoulder at me. "So… don't call it a mistake. You've been looking out for me when you didn't have to. I want to help you too. We work well together – we aren't just two strangers that happen to be on patrol together, ready to sell the other out at a moments notice. We're more than that. Fr- Teammates. Partners."

I'm not really sure how to take that. If it was anyone other than Taylor, I would call them cringe for unironically saying something that sappy with a straight face – but coming from her it actually feels genuine, the awkwardness somehow part of the appeal. "I'll try and live up to that." I slide one hand upwards, smooth and undamaged skin left behind my touch. I couldn't discount the possibility that there were marks and bruises that would only show up later that I had missed, but even if Panacea's power was limited in range, it was highly effective.

"That does feel better." She concedes, one hand lightly pinching at the skin I left behind. "Though I can't say it doesn't feel weird to be- you know- in this situation."

"Situation?" I echo.

"Well, hiding in a side-alley with my costume open." She clutches the costume in question closer to her chest as she talks. "And letting a boy see me like this at all, let alone touch me. Even if it is for a perfectly logical reason, it just doesn't seem very… glamorous or heroic. If that makes sense. You hear all about the big Cape battles on the news and the celebrations afterwards, but you don't hear anything about things like this. It seems anticlimactic. Like Armsmaster having a flashy battle on the news, then sticking around for an hour after the fight to pick up screws that fell off his bike during the clash."

"Well, that wouldn't make for good TV – so it's no surprise they don't bother. Nobody wants to hear that the heroes all sat in an empty room for half a day running tests after meeting a new Cape with unknown powers – even if that is the most practical thing to do. And as for us doing this in particular, it isn't that weird. I'm not just any boy, after all. I'm Void Cowboy – hero extraordinaire and professional doctor." I tap my chest. "And never mind the perfectly good reason – you seemed all too happy to play along earlier, Miss 'It's fine if its in the dar-' Urk!" I spit out a fly that dives into my mouth mid-sentence. "Rude."

"It was an accident." The barefaced lie wouldn't fool a toddler, and she knows it. "And you have the wrong idea, I wasn't thinking of anything lewd. I was thinking of something else entirely."

"Strange. I never said that what I was thinking was lewd in the first pl-" I dodge another fly. "-ace, but I definitely believe you!" I rush out the sentence as an ominous swarm circles around me. Taylor definitely couldn't take teasing that well. It wasn't really her fault, of course – this was all very new to her. With two relationship boosts, I knew all too well that she was at least somewhat attracted to me. Perhaps not enough to make a real move on her own, but enough that if I wanted to push the issue – I probably could.

But I didn't really want to. I liked our interactions. I didn't feel any issues about blasting through the challenges of someone like Emma at whatever time was convenient to me, because even if she had some redeeming features – in the grand scheme of things, she was just a pretty face. Her value to me wasn't personal, it was almost entirely around the fact that she was attractive and that the eventual makeup-slash-hatefuck threesome with her and Taylor was going to be amazing. She was fun enough to be around at school, but utterly irrelevant to my ideal life once my powers have taken me to the logical endgame.

But, Sophia? Taylor? The eventual addition of the Dallon sisters? Tattletale? I wanted more than that. A deeper bond, something that was more than just sex and obedience. More than just a cumdump, individuals that would interact with me as their own selves – however twisted from the original they might be. And while that was all a way off, that path started early. If I pushed things here, turned teasing words into action just by moving my hands a little bit forward and up – I wouldn't be able to take it back. I was pretty sure I would get away with it even if she pulled away before things got too far, but we wouldn't be bantering cape-partners anymore – we would be fuckbuddies, every meeting escalating from the last. And that… would be a shame. I didn't want that, even if I wanted the prize at the end – it would take away from the satisfaction to break what we had built up to this point by grasping onto it too hard.

"I guess it's just my dirty mind then." I show mercy. "Last call to let me poke anything I missed, otherwise you're just going to stay sore until the next time we meet up." I zap her with Othala's power again. The slot rolls into pyrokinesis. "Especially because I don't have a reliable dummy to cycle these powers out on."

"I'll be fine." She assures me. "I feel way better now than I did before. I mean it."

"Nice. I hope you'll indulge me with a quick question then." I push myself to my feet as she closes the back of her suit again in an all-too-complex motion, straps, utility belt, rucksack… I won't deny that she's more prepared than I am. The skintight suit is impressively strong despite appearances – but it all looks like such a hassle to work with. It isn't something I could do. Way too organised. "So does all of that mean that mean that the next time my dear partner gets injured, they won't have any problems with telling me and letting me heal them? Instead of disrespecting me by thinking that I would rather them suffer alone for days than take three minutes out of my time to fix them up?"

"I-" Taylor wilts, clearly not happy about me wording that in such an unflattering way. "I think your mysterious partner will be sure to ask you for help next time, yes."

"Good to hear." I give her a genial smile, not that she can see much of my face from her angle. More importantly, Taylor's challenge cooldown was about to run out. I should probably tag that before we split up.

She shifts, one hand scratching her cheek awkwardly. "I really thought you were going to ask a different question." Taylor confesses.

"Oh?" I probe.

"I mean, you're a boy – I thought you would have been surprised about, you know." She waves at her back vaguely. I don't know. "The bra!" She says with exasperation as my blank look conveys its message. "Or lack of it, at least. Usually girls-" She breaks off with a pained look. "-forget it. If you weren't curious, it doesn't matter."

"Oh, no." I shake my head. "That one's obvious to me. There's just no need for it." That support and breathability was already built into the front of the costume directly. The undersuit was an all-in-one in that respect, not terribly different to going naked underneath a wetsuit. The padding in that area had been obvious to me from the start, if only because I was something of an expert when it came to knowing how big Taylor's chest should be.

The whole costume was genuinely impressive already. Even if her power generates the materials via bug-control, the sheer quality and functionality of the design was absurd for someone without any experience in that area of design. If the heroine thing didn't work out, she could probably give Parian a run for her money in terms of quality.

I blink, focusing on Taylor's stiff, sulking shoulders as she stomped away from me. "What's the matter?" I turn my head at the sound of buzzing, finding a host of buzzing insects hovering menacingly on either side of me. "Did I say something wrong?"

"Void. I take back everything nice I just said about you." Her voice calls out over her shoulder. "There's some things you just can't say to girls!"

I cup my hands around my mouth to call after her. "I didn't say anything!" I give a helpless shrug at the air. I didn't think I said anything odd anyway, although admittedly a solid half of my attention had been directed at the final few seconds of Taylor's remaining challenge cooldown.

This time… things would be a bit different. I had all the data I needed. A perfect circle around the city, and not only that – but I had proven that her range was a sphere- no, an oval, when it came to vertical reach. If I went to the far, far edge of her range, then climbed a ladder – she couldn't reach me. I could actually walk slightly inside her outwards range and remain safe – owing to the fact that the diagonal angle from the centre of Taylor's power was technically further than the straight line on the ground. For it to shrink inwards instead of expanding after climbing a single floor, I had confirmed something critical: Taylor was either on the ground floor or, more likely, below it.

I pull out my phone briefly, only to double check the marks I had left on the map. All of the data circled around one particular office block, no more than a minute of solid running from my starting position. Straight ahead, left through the alleyway and then look to the opposite side of the street on the right. I lock my gaze onto Taylor's retreating back as she resumes her strangely-offended, sulky silence. "Challenge."

This was a proof of concept run. I didn't need to win, just prove that Taylor was exactly where my experiments said that she was. I'd have time to work out a strategy another time, once I saw what her set-up and defensive situation was. And given that I had no need to keep the benefit of surprise, I opt to not use my speed-state. The moment of paralysis would be problematic when it came to actually entering the building, giving the bugs enough time to both cover me and fill the area I would usually try to escape into.

So I pull out my anti-Taylor trump card right away. A horde of bugs chitter and skitter around me, uselessly bouncing off Glory Girl's personal forcefield. It was incredibly effective, but Taylor would have a countermeasure soon enough – bugs carrying tools and knives from silken threads to drop and swing into me. They were slow and cumbersome, a messy method of attack – but even a glancing blow would be enough to drop the shield.

But she didn't have that ready at the start – or at least, I had only seen it when I had tried to abuse this forcefield to search the entire area in one go. It took a bit of time to recognise the power and set-up the counter, clearly. That left me plenty of time to head to the target building at a dead sprint, knowing that for all of her gathered armies – she couldn't actually stop me right now.

I leave the swarm behind me at the office door, using my shadow-state to go through instead – cutting the massed swarm into a steady trickle of reinforcements through cracks and gaps in the walls. This room, an overly-large reception area – clearly wasn't her base of operations. That meant I needed to head down, into a basement area of some kind.

I head into the elevator, hammering the only floor lower than the ground floor – B1. The button briefly flashes red before switching off. Not allowed, clearly – perhaps it needed some kind of key to allow that to be input. I remove my shoe, very deliberately – then phase the floor the moment Shadow Stalker's power returns. My momentum is killed swiftly and sharply as I freeze the shoe and use it to break my momentum – taking the breath out of my body with the harshness of the stop.

But it did work. I'm hanging over the void of the elevator, looking down at what should be the door I need. Vista's power to shrink the gap, a delicate swinging motion – and just a few seconds of waiting until my shadow-state returns… I drop from my improvised stepping stone, gliding through the door with ease and-

-and collapse to the ground screaming as every nerve in my body seems to catch fire. I barely hear the muted roar of a pistol breaking down my hastily-raised forcefield, and my only understanding of what actually happened comes from the brief moment of lucidity as the world fades away and the usual failure sign appears. Taylor, in her all-black suit. A gun in one hand, a bottle of some kind of pepper spray in the other. A mass of silken threads in the background and dangerous-looking spiders descending down on me as I fall.

FAILURE​

Which meant… what? What would even cause that interaction? I'd never felt anything quite like it, it seemed too radically different for a second-trigger. Or… no. Perhaps it was less about Taylor, and more about me. The spray. Regardless of how effective it might normally have been, perhaps it had a boosted effect against my shadow-state? The power usually shoved aside other matter, like the bugs – or just shoved me aside into an empty area if I tried phasing into a wall or another person. Did that rule not apply to aerosols? If it just treated it like any other gas, then I would regain my physical form with all sorts of nastiness inside my blood and skin.

Logically, there was no way that I was literally appearing with particles like that spread inside me – otherwise any usage of the power would end with vast amounts of oxygen bubbles in my blood and brain and who knows where else. It must be some interaction with how my body is reformed, like there is something left over that gets messily expelled by my power or messes with the sensitive electrical receptors in my body and nervous system.

Which meant that it probably worked on Sophia as well, which was good to know for the future.

Next time… I'd just have to keep away from that initial blast as I came through the door. I could fight through it if it wasn't for the power interaction. Maybe it would just be better to come through the ceiling instead, less predictable and there wasn't as much lighting up there as I had imagined.

Whatever. I had found her. Finally. The hard part was over. All I needed to do now was find a strategy to get here, close the gap before the gun gets any real value and then beat to death before the spiders get me. That wasn't too much harder than any other challenge I had done.

I let out a ragged sigh, ignoring the phantom taste of my own blood in my mouth. At least the spiders didn't really get anywhere this time. "Bug!" I call out. "I'll see you in a few days, right? We'll stick with the heroes advice, hit a different gang this time?"

She turns. "Obviously." I knew she couldn't stay mad at me for whatever her issue was. I'm too awesome for that. "I'll send you a message on PHO to let you know when I don't have anything else that I need to do for the night."

That was every night, Taylor. Don't try and pretend you have a busy social life to maintain. "I'll keep an eye out." I promise. "See you soon, try and think of a proper name while you wait!"

Her body language gives off a pained expression. Clearly, she's been struggling with that issue for a while now. "I'll try. See you around."

I let out a merry whistle as we split up. Our next patrol would probably take a while to get organised, which gave me some time to play with. The Protectorate had been terribly quiet recently, and their patrols were secret and unannounced enough that it was too hard for me to get across the city in time to spot them once the news spotted them in the Boardwalk or elsewhere. The Empire's capes were firmly holed up in the middle of their territory, not making aggressive moves into ABB territory quite yet – although that was certain to change.

So perhaps it was time to investigate a target that wasn't going anywhere at all. Faultline's crew had been spotted in Boston recently, so they might be returning soon enough – but there was one Cape in particular that was both easy to find and not at all suspicious to interact with.

PHO Mobile

New message from: ParianDesigns

That time works for me as well. I'll reserve the slot and we can discuss your requirements in more detail face-to-face. I can't start the work until you bring the deposit, so please make sure to bring it via the approved payment methods on my site.

… I was going to have to loot some more criminal dens and drug dealers over the next few days. I needed the cash to actually pay for this job – my savings were nowhere near enough, even for the deposit alone. But that was fine. What else was I even spending my money on? A proper costume would pay for itself, even if I couldn't take it into the challenges.

But that was a task for tomorrow. I stop in the middle of the street. For now… I select my newest power and watch flakes of ash rush away from my body to form an ashen clone in front of me – slightly eroding over time as ash streams away into the wind. I consider the thrum of the power still awaiting my input. It was staying active, perfectly still as it waited for a command. It hangs there for ten seconds, then twenty – until it became apparent that it wasn't going anywhere until the wind wore away enough of the ash to break its form.

I push a thought at it. It raises a hand into the air, fingers spread wide and palm straight – meeting my own in a high-five. A solid connection, despite the material he was clearly made from. Then he erupts into a black cloud that rapidly fades into nothing.

Not a true clone of Oni Lee's ability. No teleportation, nor was it a flesh-and-blood clone like his. Mine was a mass of ash in a mockery of my form, given one single, basic task to do before destroying itself. No clear time-limit, but a lengthy cooldown given its apparent simplicity.

I wait out thirty seconds before summoning it again, immediately attacking it as it forms - dissipating it immediately. Weak defensively, as I had imagined. It seemed solid enough for a single hit on the offense, but that was all. The power lights up in my head immediately as the thought crosses my mind, the cooldown already expiring.

"The cooldown is the same as the amount of time I had it up." I conclude. If it's active for a second, it comes back almost right away. If I had it up for thirty minutes before it completed its task, I'd best hope I wouldn't need it again in the fight. Interesting. And it opened up the possibility of using it in my close-combat battles in combination with Echo, rather than as a one-off strategic tool.

I'd need to test it in battle properly… but progress was progress. It was a shame that the power wasn't actual teleportation, which had been my most desired aspect of his power – but this would do for now. I couldn't be upset with the days work, even without the knowledge and experience gained both in real life and in the other challenges I had faced – an extra power was nothing to be scoffed at.

To say nothing about the conniptions PHO was now going through at my success against Oni Lee. That was my real next task – to brag and gloat all across PHO until I got temp-banned again.

Trolling the internet is the real endgame here. Best get started.
