-bugs surround me, biting into skin and striking at every exposed orifice they could find. I had miscalculated here, just dodging Taylor's hits wasn't enough, simply attacking her would cause my forcefield to drop – and dropping it for tiny fractions of a second between punches left me exactly like Glory Girl in the bank challenge, with hundreds of bugs slipping through to the wrong side of the shield as it comes back up. My expectations from my initial adjustment - namely, concealing Shadow Stalker's power until the very last second - had gone perfectly. I had phased through the door with no pepper spray awaiting me this time. It worked well, caught her completely off-guard. Getting to the position I was in now, a physical grapple against a weaker opponent - was nearly a guaranteed win in my experience.

Nearly. Unfortunately, I had overlooked one crucial aspect. Armour. Now, I was used to being fucked over by costumes in these challenges - so this was nothing particularly new, but what was new was getting a real look at exactly how effective Taylor's suit was. Usually, a few solid blows to the head and a few slams into the ground were enough to take someone out - but even if her physical struggling slowed and notably weakened, she didn't die. She didn't go unconscious - merely briefly dazed from the impacts.

I, on the other hand, was starting to suffer. For all that I was dominant in pure physicality between us, her bugs closed that gap and then some. Even if she was struggling to match me blow for blow, her bugs didn't share that desperation. They methodically cover me from head to toe, blinding and pouring into every orifice they can find - forcing me to repeatedly cycle through powers to stop them from just killing me right away. Shadow Stalker into Glory Girl, but I can't afford to keep Glory Girl's shield up when we next trade blows or I'll never have it again for the fight. Back into the Ash Clone and spamming Echo to copy my blows to her head and chest - but it's never enough for a finishing blow. The armour is too solid, the helmet attached by some mechanism I can't fiddle with mid-fight nor dislodge by pure force.

This wasn't the nervous, amateur Taylor I was used to patrolling with, that had evidently adjusted her costume plans to appear at least somewhat more appealing and less villainous - there was no exposed skin to strike at, no soft underbelly or even a strap to manipulate. Even so, it wasn't really enough to pose a significant barrier to me - it's only natural that in a contest of strength, the one at the mercy of the other would eventually lose even if they did have better armour. I was just faced with the realisation that I didn't have the time.

I loosen my grip on Taylor, allowing her to get her arm back and retrieve her fallen gun - already being taken towards her by dozens of bugs tugging it by string. I wasn't going to kill her in time before her bugs killed me, unfortunately. Better to save myself the feeling of a rather terrible death than waste time trying to make the impossible happen. The pistol angles back at me, locking dead-centre with my forehead before firing.

FAILURE​

I grimace, but can't quite hide the pleased hum of excitement that courses through me at the feeling of making progress. That was a good plan. A really good plan. Taylor's information was entirely limited to what I showed on the approach to the building and the elevator, so not using my shadow-state at all until the final entry into the room meant that she didn't have the pepper spray out and ready. Unfortunately, even closing the gap as effectively as I did wasn't quite enough – not when there were so many of her bugs in the room, using enough tricks that it was almost a physical presence holding me back with strings and sheer mass, even while the rest did their best to kill me.

But the approach was sound, at least. And the reason I had lost this time was due to the bugs – a solution I had already 'fixed' in the very first challenge. There was no ZONE modifier, I could leave – dress myself in the most fashionable armour that I could whip together from the nearest store and repeat exactly what I just did. I would only be showing off the speed-state as I left the area, and so long as I made it to Taylor without revealing my shadow state in advance – she wouldn't have the spray ready.

Doubtless, the lack of free movement would be more of an issue with that kind of haphazard armour - but if I sacrificed Glory Girl's shield or just took a few glancing blows from bullets, I would probably be just fine in the end. With enough layers of protection, I would never need to phase away except perhaps to scatter the increasing amounts of string tugging me around - and if I didn't need to do that, then I was free to beat her helmet again and again until the curves went inwards instead of out. Trying to break limbs wasn't the solution, I had definitely done something permanent to her leg this time around - but neither she nor her bugs had been fazed by the loss.

I just needed to try again later, grab some protective gear and go straight for the kill. And while punches weren't my favourite weapon - it seemed at least more likely to succeed than some flimsy knife against solid armour plates and a spider silk bodysuit, even ignoring how effective I expected the bugs to be at restricting any item I tried to get into the room with me.

I clear my vision as I refocus on the class. World History was always a dull one, never going into the actually interesting parts and always going on about useless things, like the Agricultural revolution and its effect on transforming society. Thankfully, I had plenty of good targets here to break up the monotony. Waste a minute or two listening to the teacher droning on, then let my eyes roam over the class to find a suitable target – the habit was probably a bad one to keep up, and I had deliberately started failing my challenges after realising that clearing the first and second rounds of most of my classmates was making me... not quite popular, but certainly close enough to it that my paranoia was getting the best of me. Becoming the most popular kid in school was cool, of course - but with all the other risks I was taking and all of the things that could go wrong for me, I'd be damned if the thing that sunk me was my ego getting to me at school and risking myself for no real reward.

Patience. That was the name of the game here. My power was... rational, in the changes it made. Somewhat. If I provided a ready, easy explanation for them to be close to me - it wouldn't do anything drastic or obvious. The path of least resistance, or perhaps the least effort expended. The mechanics of it were beyond me for now, it would take some serious experimentation by a Thinker or Tinker power to work out how my power was doing what it did. It was a powerful tool, one that was honestly the only way I could ever keep allies by my side in the long term, but it was dangerous as well.

Dangerous, because I was still weak. Oh, sure - I towered over most normal humans by now. And given a dozen attempts, I could clear the first challenge or two of most Cape's that I ran across - so long as I had the time and ability to find them to get those challenges done.

But I wouldn't have a dozen chances in real life. Armsmaster wouldn't let me apologise and come back later, only to challenge him again when I was sure I could win. I wouldn't be able to pick myself up with a sour expression after a furious Glory Girl kicks my skull open in one blow, or Taylor devours me alive, or Oni Lee ambushes me with a suicide attack.

One chance. One life.

Which was why I had to make the most of it. And take all the chances to get stronger safely that I could get. I let my eyes settle on Sophia, two rows up from me and one across - glaring daggers into the teacher's back as she leans her chin heavily on one arm, looking just as bored as I am.

Sorry, Sophia. One-person trip. You'll have to stay miserable. Thank you for your sacrifice. "Challenge."

I idly stretch as I saunter into our agreed meeting point. "Ready to get beaten up?" I throw the question out into the darkness.

"Isn't that my line?" Sophia - or perhaps I should refer to this figure as Shadow Stalker - doesn't take long to appear.

"I wouldn't say so." I reply, a hint of seriousness hidden in the playful tone. "When you think of how unfair this fight should be, don't you think they should be a little more one-sided in your favour?" I duck under the first punch to come at me, Sophia liked to switch her attacks up – but her fighting style never changed. Taunts led to an immediate punch or kick. She always sought to catch me in a headlock or armbar – evidently aware that a match of strength and endurance worked in my favour. And, critically, she only used her powers to reposition – to fully defend or fully commit to an attack.

Like I had seen with Taylor, there seemed to be some progression in the challenges – the modern Shadow Stalker, the one that had been a Ward for some time now, was well used to letting attacks pass through herself harmlessly while simultaneously lashing out herself. Partial transformations were a part of her repertoire, like phasing out only a part of her arm behind the punch or letting a kick float harmlessly through her chest without fully phasing – on one occasion, I had seen a video of her punching through someone's tight guard by precisely bringing her arm back to the physical world only after each part of it had gone past her opponent's limbs. It looked impressive in slow motion, and I was intensely curious about how difficult it was to master.

Presumably, the answer was 'very'.

Because this Shadow Stalker couldn't do it.

The vigilante version that got caught by Armsmaster before her induction to the Wards program. Oh, she had the capability – but the few times that I had seen her pull it off were when she was caught by surprise and panicked, rather than a deliberate plan executed mid-fight. She didn't even seem to realise she did it, I wasn't sure if that lack of insight into her own capabilities and growth potential was a deliberate restriction of her capabilities in this challenge or it truly was something that slipped her mind. She only learned it in real life after joining the PRT and going through power-testing, after all.

That isn't to say that she's an easy fight. Quite the opposite, in fact. With my first battle against Sophia, I at least had plenty of electronics around to mitigate her ability once I found her weakness. This time, I had no such luck – and she was far, far more cautious about getting near walls, gadgets or anything that looked potentially electronic. And without that? I couldn't win. Knocking her out in a single blow was, in theory, the best I could do – but even when I did land hits on her, none were decisive enough to knock her out without her shifting into her shadow state and creating distance. I meet her punch with my own - meeting nothing but air as she phases directly through me, only for her to reappear directly in the path of a spinning backhand that slams against her helmet.

She matched the attack with a solid kick to my chest, but as I shake my pained, ringing hand protesting about my choice of targets - I'll call it worth it. I roll away from a spinning kick that attempts to decapitate me, catching the follow-up leg as she attempts to stomp down on me – prompting another explosion into shadow as she reforms a metre away, looking supremely confident. "Bold words for someone who can't seem to stop losing." She taunts me back.

"It's true, after limiting myself this much I can't seem to get a decisive win." I sigh loudly. "Not that I think you should be happy about barely scrapping out victories against a guy with the Cape equivalent of a blindfold and handcuffs on. Doesn't this hurt your ego?"

Her expression goes flat. "This is pity, nothing more. In a real fight you would be dead at the entrance." Another attack incoming. I don't fully dodge the punch, but she doesn't notice my leg lashing out at her ankle until I've already made contact. We scatter again, I wasn't so fortunate as to break her ankle – but she didn't look happy about the landed blow. It was happening more often than ever, and she knew it better than anyone.

"Another hit. One side using powers, one side using none." I adopt a sing-song tone as she blurs into a wall of shadow. I crouch and bring my guard up, sidling backwards slowly - knowing that there was nothing to do against this but grit my teeth and block. Her attack could come from any angle while in that state, the ability to reform her body in any position with the cloud enabling her to punish any move that wasn't explicitly defensive in nature. "But don't get me wrong, I'm grate-" My arm screams at me as I swing them down to block the spinning kick aimed at the side of my torso. "-ful!"

"As you should be." Sophia ambles backwards, letting me recover - very obviously not concerned about any followup charge coming from me. "You aren't strong enough to match what Armsmaster did, after all. The illusion that you are even close to winning is a gift on my part. Happy birthday, or something." So she does know how this scenario went? Or should have gone? Interesting.

"A few months out." I drawl. She shrugs carelessly. "But no, I'm grateful. Without these little sessions, I don't think I'd have become even half as good in an unarmed fight as I am now. I was just some nerdy guy, getting by with brute-strength and surprise attacks, sometimes a lucky weapon that I found. I didn't really tend to win fights because I was just better - but that changed when I met you." The hockey mask hides her expression, but I like to imagine that behind it - a rare, bashful expression appeared on her face. Wishful thinking, probably. Especially when I was just about to ruin it. "Just look at me now, genuinely better than Sophia Hess. What a change, am I right?"

A beat.

Two beats.

"What." The voice is almost dangerously flat.

I grin. "Well. It's a bit of a given, isn't it? No different from what I've been saying for the last few minutes at all, though I'll forgive you for not picking up on it earlier - I know you aren't the wordy-sort." I gesture at her helmet, as if to draw her attention to the fact that I did manage to tag her face not even a full minute ago. "If we're evenly matched with you using your power and me using none, then you don't need any fancy algebra to realise that I'm better than you when you don't have your power."

"We are - not - equals." Sophia stresses, already prowling towards me with murderous intent. I match her approach, a mocking smile on my lips. It wouldn't last, of course. I wasn't quite that delusional - but there was a hint of truth to my words. I was getting better, and she... wasn't. Oh, she had picked up some tricks - gotten used to predicting me in some ways, worked out how I liked to dodge in response to certain attacks but she wasn't becoming a better fighter. She wasn't improving her power, her skills or her reactions - she was just... remembering what I did. Even if she was still better, the gap was shrinking. Had shrunk - to the point where if she stopped using her power completely, I would probably win at least three in every ten bouts. Not that she would ever willingly do that.

This insight into the CONT modifier was useful. It might reveal my past strategies to them, but that didn't mean that they were guaranteed to be able to adjust for it. While I didn't know exactly how my power worked, if I imagined it in terms of fighting a bot in a video game - the bot might be aware that I like to do the equivalent of spamming jump attacks and guard accordingly, but it's still programmed at the same difficulty that it started with. It responded to my moves better than the original over time, but it wasn't actually improving underneath.

Some small semblance of hope for the Armsmaster challenge, at least. But no time to think about that now. True to her usual form - Sophia responds to my taunts with immediate violence.

I backstep to handle the first haymaker that comes my way, lashing out with a light jab only for her to erupt into smoke and throw out an exact copy of her first attack a moment later. I duck towards her, gripping her leg and twisting to knock her off balance- then rolling away as she slips through me like air again, narrowly failing to catch me in a headlock but still managing to wrap her fingers around my shirt before I can fully slip away. I'm bodily slammed back into the ground, the base of her other palm rushing towards my nose as she makes an attempt to pin me down completely. I can't dodge the hit entirely, simply making an attempt at moving my head to turn it into a jarring, glancing blow is the best I can do - but even that slight movement is all she needs to wrap her legs around me in the beginnings of a submission hold.

I don't even try to contest it. She's pretty good at these, and she gets sulky if I give into my instincts to phase out of her grip - shooting me with arrows from the darkness on my next attempts until she decides to forgive me. Instead, I shift my entire body to try and grip the arm she had just attacked me with - not quite able to get a firm grip from this angle, but enough to get the unguarded side of her arm just in front of my face. Amateur hour for costume design - I could relate. The armour and padding were good on her costume, but only present on her torso and outer side of the limbs. The inner arm? Thighs? Hips? All viable targets that would only be safeguarded properly when she joined the PRT and had a redesign.

I chomp down. A pained, slightly bewildered scream cuts off almost instantly as the vice-grip she has on me disappears in a flash - the cloud of smoke retreating momentarily before doubling back towards me at a sprint. I actually manage to catch the boot seeking to make contact with my face, yanking her other leg away a half-second later to send her toppling towards the ground. It's a fast movement, and I'm certain she wasn't ready for me to react from this vulnerable position - her face is mere inches from a nasty impact with the street, when she collapses once more into a pile of smoke that almost immediately resolves back into a standing position - this time with her boot on my neck as the sound of angry panting fills the street once more.

"I win." She breathes out heavily. "Again."

I tentatively test the pressure against my throat. She presses down in warning. Yep. No chance to get out of this one. I raise my hands in surrender. "I yield, truly - I am no match for you."

"Shut it." She snaps, as usual, not in the mood for pleasantries, sarcasm or anything inbetween. "Not in the mood to hear more of the crap that drivels out of your mouth. Especially after that cheap move." She inspects her arm with a scowl. "What the fuck, Greg?"

I don't think I'll ever get used to the fact that all of my simulations have my apparent canonical superhero name as 'Greg'. Not being called 'Veder' or 'You!' almost feels strange out of her mouth. "You can hardly complain about me using every tool that I'm left with. Haven't I handicapped myself enough for your benefit without restricting my body as well?"

That would rankle her. She was trying to act unbothered, but I knew our arrangement was living in her head rent-free. Her power was drastically ill-suited to her personality. A defensive power suited to ambush tactics, repositioning and stealth - stuck on someone preaching about the survival of the fittest and the rule of the jungle. She'd be thrilled to have a more directly combat-oriented power, I'm certain - even if her current one was clearly excellently suited to actually winning in these pure melee 1v1 matchups.

I wiggle my eyebrows. "Although, if you are still annoyed - we could always even the score. You're welcome to bite me too, people pay for that sort-urk!" She pressures down on my neck needlessly hard.

"Not listening." She shakes her head. "It doesn't matter. You'll never beat me with a move like that anyway-" As expected, she was going to stubbornly ignore the fact that the strategy resulted in her completely abandoning an easy victory via her chokehold. The fact that she won anyway was irrelevant. These fights were closer now. Longer. She probably realised that too. "-so just do what you like. You aren't entirely wrong with your words, you have improved... marginally. It's slightly more entertaining beating you into a pulp than killing Nazis, so I'll let this go on despite your attitude problems."

She pushes me away with her foot, I shove myself back to my feet as she takes her usual stance. "My attitude problems? It seems to me like you're just salty that every word I'm saying is the truth! There's no shame in it, you know! Boys are generally stronger than girls-" This time, I don't manage to block the opening kick well. My limbs scream in protest as one arm droops uselessly to my side - protesting even the slightest attempt at movement. "-isn't it rude to attack while someone is talking?" I protest half-heartedly, throwing out a kick of my own to gain space. "And what about attacking a crippled opponent? Where's your sense of honour?"

Sophia actually pauses at that. "I might be more inclined to help if you stopped talking once in a while." She sighs. "Come here." She holds her hand out, gesturing at my dislocated arm. I don't move. "Come here!" She snaps.

Begrudgingly, I inch towards her. One step, two steps. When no aggressive action comes - I allow her close enough to touch me. Sportsmanship? From Sophia in a fight?

Not a chance. "Idiot." She places both hands on my bad arm, then immediately converts it into an attempt to twist me into an armbar once more. I twist the other way, a mad grin in my eyes as my arm makes an obscene, noise in response to the motion - the flash of pain turning into blank nothingness despite still being attached. Briefly painful at the time, but nothing compared to many of my deaths to date.

Her momentary hesitation and disbelief at my self-mutilation is all I need. I lash out with my foot before my brain can properly comprehend the signals its receiving. A full swing, with a perfect connection to my target. Shadow Stalker's power had a near-automatic response to certain levels of damage - but not pain.

I sink to the floor, not even glancing at whatever the hell I just did to my arm. "Suffer with me." I roll over, taking in the sight of Sophia, backtracked almost a dozen-steps away - half-curled over in agony as she covers her crotch with a silent, pained gasp. "Heard-" My head spins briefly. "Heard a girl once say to their boyfriend-" Despite her pain, she never takes her eyes off of me. If looks could kill... "-that girls felt that kind of pain too if they get hit right. Still don't really believe that it can compare to a shot at the balls-" I roll myself onto my back. Can't push myself up anymore. Don't even want to. My arm was not supposed to be facing this way. Looked painful, but the ominous lack of any feeling meant nothing to me right now. "-but I guess there was a smidgen of truth in there somewhere."

"I'm-" Sophia stomps to her feet. Or, tries to stomp. The slight bow-legged shudder at her knees and somewhat squeaky voice ruin the effect. "-going to fucking murder you. I hope you know that."

"That's the spirit." I gasp. "Only-" Lots of stars in the sky tonight. Fairly sure that I'm about to lose consciousness anyway, but it's worth struggling on for a few seconds just to get one last jab in to ruin her day. Or, whatever passed as a day in here. "Only one issue with that."

She's wary approaching me this time, inching closer as if I might bite. Which is a fair description, given recent events. "What is it?"

"Times up." I grin as the EVNT timer hits zero. A furious scream of rage tears out of her throat - before everything dissolves into white and grey.

FAILURE​

I idly flex my fixed arm a few times as the failure notice fades away. Maybe it was a little petty of me, but it was always worth a bit of temporary pain to knock Sophia down a peg or two. Perhaps not the most practical move in a real fight, or even in a challenge - but at the end of the day... I scored some really nice hits on her in that session. The old Greg couldn't have done that. Sure, I lost again - but that was expected. I was handicapped to not using any of my gathered powers going in, that was the deal for her to ignore the scenario and just brawl with me - because I certainly didn't possess any means of actually locking her down and capturing her. May as well get at least some value out of the challenge, right?

Especially because nobody said I had to be entirely honest with her. My version of Victor's power wasn't amazing, not a true leech on someone's skills yet - but it did leech the results of practice and repetition from people around me when it was active. Not so much when learning new things, but it was ideal for both idling in a boring classroom as well as my supposedly unpowered brawls against Sophia. A minor boost to the rate I improved was always welcome.

I wonder if I could use Armsmaster in the same way as I was Sophia? It was hard to imagine a more capable sparring partner anywhere in the Bay, something to think about when I have more consistent access to him. I wasn't naive enough to think that I could get by with only Victor's power - but the idea of repeatedly going all-out against the best in the Bay outfitted perfectly to fight me wasn't a bad one if I wanted to be the strongest guy around.

Sophia half-turns her gaze from the teacher towards the window, then snaps her head towards me as she notices me looking at her from the corner of her vision. The faint look of confusion, minor disgust and derision is textbook Sophia, and her unamused expression fails to improve as I give her a cheeky nod before sliding my gaze back to the front of the class. Sadly, not noticeable further ahead in the lesson than when I had started the challenge. A few seconds skipped, at most - but I was feeling refreshed now. More than capable of sitting through the rest of the rather dull lesson before finding something else to kill me.

That conviction lasts approximately ten seconds. World History was really, really dull right now. In some ways, my abuse of Victor's power during these classes was a mistake. I knew I would already ace the test, thanks to the kind donations of the uber-nerds at the front of the room that were getting exactly no value out of the class and thus allowed my skill siphon to take the results of their avid attention. I push myself to my feet. Nope. Can't do it. Way too bored, way too hyped - two damn good fights in a row where I could taste the progress. I make a vague hand gesture at the teacher on the way out of the door, not attracting too much attention along the way - barely getting a nod of approval from the slightly confused man. He was on his third challenge, we were basically best friends right now - it's only natural that he wouldn't care about me leaving for any reason at all. People left his class all the time for clubs, trips and other appointments - one more was nothing special to anyone here.

I wander the hallways. Taylor on cooldown, Sophia on cooldown... and nothing for me to do or strive for until they came back up. I wouldn't have this trouble at Arcadia, everyone knew the Wards were around there - to say nothing of New Wave. I'd be in way better shape if I spent every day there instead, assuming I was subtle about it and didn't get caught. But no, Winslow it is. No skipping the transfer queue either, I'd checked. If I aced every test, I might get in sometime next year - way too late to matter. Not that I was particularly keen to leave Taylor and Sophia, but... I mean, they'd still be here - just waiting for me to come back and snap them up properly. They were mine, after all - even if they didn't realise it yet.

A younger, hornier Greg might have eagerly added a few normies to the list. Emma, Madison, Julia... a few of the regular bullies that could really use a proper dicking to fix their attitudes. It was probably rude to think of them so dismissively, but what could I do about it? They had no powers, no particular rewards for going after them over than them being attractive in general - a fact thrust into my face whenever I interacted with them, every time that Emma made a blushing, jealous play for my attention at Taylor's expense... my power was reminding me that with a little more work, I could have a genuine heroine making the same face. Sure, that sounded like an asshole-ish thing to think, but I would put money on other people agreeing with me when pressed. Ask any guy if he wants to fuck around with some random chick in college or bang Alexandria. Not even a question, assuming they were being honest.

Don't get me wrong, if Emma suddenly gained powers I'd be more than happy to add her to my collection - but until that time, I wasn't going to expect much from our relationship in the long term. Some things weren't meant to last forever.

I didn't let that stop me from indulging Emma whenever she had one of her jealousy-induced moments, I was still a self-sacrificing gentleman at heart - but the fact remained that the thought was always in the back of my mind for... non-Capes, for lack of a better descriptor. Can't help it, really - I'd need a blindfold or something to stop myself from seeing someone's challenges and the rewards history so far, and telling Emma that I needed to wear a blindfold to properly appreciate her sucking me off under a teacher's desk would probably go poorly. Teeth might get involved.

But she would be hot while she was mad, I might have higher aspirations - but I can still appreciate the passion there. Can still look forward to what's in front of me, even if I recognise it as something that is probably temporary.

But enough musing about my poor choice in school. It wasn't quite lunchtime yet, but I had my own plans today. Parian's shop was rarely open in the evenings, so it was up to me to find the timeslot during the day to go and meet her. If I left now, a little before lunchtime - I could be done and back here without even going into the empty slot in my timetable. Plenty of time to have lunch after getting back.

The only problem was actually getting to her place. She was a fair distance away, but I had a speedster power to handle that - the more serious issue was finding a 'safe' spot to change. I wasn't dumb enough to bring my costume with me in my bag, as that would expose my identity if I was ever searched for any random reason - so all that was left was finding a suitable hidey-hole nearby that I could easily retrieve it from. Somewhere outside of the school, because even if I could enter and leave in disguise - I didn't want some lucky guy catching me on camera and realising that the legendary Void Cowboy went to Winslow.

That would be dangerous for me. I didn't have decoys like the Wards were supposed to have in Arcadia. If you listed out the school's population, eliminated all the girls, eliminated everyone who was clearly too tall/short, eliminated everyone with the wrong skin colour and then picked out the ones who were internet savvy enough to be a dedicated shitposter for years you would end up with... well, most of my Computer Science class, admittedly. But the point remained that even with just a few easily obtained hints, my identity could be narrowed down to probably less than two-dozen people at the absolute most. At that point, you can just compare fitness and muscles, see who has a club or some other alibi on social media around the time of Void Cowboy sightings and the case was practically solved.

I could have done it. Would have done it. I knew better than anyone how easy it was for the wrong person to put in the right kind of effort - and you could never take something back once it was on the internet. Typing 'Brad Meadows' into a PHO comment might get your post filtered for review by a moderator, but people hadn't forgotten the PRT's botched announcement thread for Hookwolf's arrest and attempted trip to the Birdcage - and he knew that people remembered too. There was a reason Hookwolf was always found deep in Empire territory, the loyal guard dog of the dog-fighting rings. It's because he wasn't safe anywhere else, for all that the PRT tried to do damage-control after his escape - his identity was out forever among those with the internet-savviness to look. I didn't want that for me, hence - stashing the thrift-store clothes I used as a costume under dumpsters in dark alleyways or in the forgotten recesses underneath a bridge. Anywhere that I could walk, be alone - and then sprint out of in costume with nobody the wiser.

I breathe a sigh of relief as I find my bag safe and sound. No wandering beggar or thug stumbling across it and taking it for themselves, nor any in the area to see me get changed - or at least, throw my costume over my normal clothes. The jacket was deliberately a size too large precisely so that it could reliably cover my shirt when done up, and my jeans weren't distinctive enough for me to worry if someone got a glimpse under the extra layer applied to my lower half. I hadn't shelled out for a different pair of shoes, but it wasn't like I had a special brand to worry about revealing - these were as generic as they could get.

Once I'm set, I activate my speed-state. Racing through Brockton Bay's streets was bound to cause way more of a panic than it ever did in my challenges - but I was more than capable of going via the rooftops. I was both light and fast in this state, floaty enough to travel between moderate gaps comfortably and safe enough that the impact was barely noticeable if I misjudged it and hit a wall or tumbled down to the street level.

It takes me only a few minutes to reach Parian's designated meeting point. A simple one-story building with a small sign and a window - nothing too fancy, but it didn't need to be. Parian didn't need a massive store to work her magic, the sales volume simply wasn't high enough for that - and even when she was running a major promotion, she was well-known for collaborations with other stores in the area to allow them to handle the business front. Her puppet shows weren't done on site either, so ultimately all she needed was a suitably large place to store all of her materials - and considering how well most fabric can fold, that wasn't much space at all.

Time to head inside. I glance around the area as I approach the door. Nobody's watching, nobody's looking, nobody cares. It's a quiet time of day, before the lunch rush out into the streets and cafes - but not so early that there's no foot traffic at all. It's just that the few people around are the smart ones that keep their head down and don't raise a fuss about every Cape that they see - particularly when it isn't an official Protectorate or Wards member. Almost a shame. I would really appreciate some real fangirls, but there was a time and a place to work towards that goal.

I enter the building, casting my gaze around to take it in as the bell at the door dings to indicate my arrival. There's a counter on the far side of the room, but nobody's manning it yet. The interior is relatively clean and neat, as befits a professional tailor's shop. There are a few tables and chairs along the walls, but there aren't any customers present yet. I kind of expected a Rogue's workplace to be closer to a flashy, modern style that highlighted their economic dominance over the marketplace that politicians would have us believe in, but it seems that she prefers to keep things old-school. In hindsight, her Victorian-era costume could have told me that - but nobody had ever accused me of being interested in fashion.

A doll's costumed head - that could only be Parian - pokes out of a nearby door. I wave. "Hey, I'm Void Cowboy. I had a meeting booked around now? I appreciate that I'm a little bit early - I can wait if needed." I eye her critically as I spool out my polite greetings.

PARIAN

Rogue 1/6

(HUNT) (ZONE)​

Now there was a combo that I don't think I had ever seen before. Probably because on the face of it, they should work against each other - one to restrict the playing field and another to allow pursuit over long distances and prevent hiding. There was overlap there, which seemed off even for a first-level challenge - to me, that implied that there was a gimmick to this.

Parian shakes her head. "Oh, now is fine too. There's nothing else I need to wait on first, and I don't think this will take long." She gestures at me. "Please come through and take a seat, I invited another guest over as well - I hope that won't be an issue for you? He won't be at all interested in listening in to your fashion plans, don't you worry about that. I'm sure he can wait in the shop while we chat."

She deliberately withheld that information, but I couldn't blame her for it. Doubtless, it wasn't a lucky coincidence on her part - perhaps she had some form of arrangement with a local Cape to act as backup for these meetings, in the event that someone saw an unaffiliated Rogue and decided to take a shot at recruitment. I didn't have enough of a good reputation to have earned the level of trust yet - I had actually expected her to just shoot me down over PHO, but evidently she saw more value in being friendly with another Cape than risk. My relatively public crime-fighting spree and recent co-operation with the PRT helped with that, I'm sure.

"Of course, no issues with that." An understatement if there was ever one. I was ecstatic at the implied threat in the event of trouble. One person acting as a bouncer or a bodyguard of sorts? The odds of that being another Cape were excellent for me. Jackpot. I smile, useless as it is through the biker's helmet. Get it out of the way now, if I lose - maybe I could get another in before the session ends if the cooldown timer isn't too long. "Challenge."

The room fades away as I find myself in an enclosed corridor, separate paths twisting and looping around me - a dozen doors on either side just waiting to be opened. A ZONE modifier that is still going to make me find my target? Or, no - that wasn't entirely the point. It was about allowing Parian to run. The twists and turns, the multiple rooms - if I gave her a moment to breathe, she would be able to dodge me forever with perfect knowledge of my position granted by HUNT. Meanwhile, I would be constantly harassed with her dolls from the very instant I drew her attention - the only reason I was safe for now was the lack of the ALRT modifier that usually came with HUNT. She didn't know I was here yet, but once she become aware - she'd have a perfect radar on me until one of us was dead.

But knowing that and being able to do something about it were two different things. Presumably, even making a bit too much noise opening and closing these doors would be enough to alert her - any slight glimpse of me through a keyhole or even a door that was left ajar would be enough as well. And yet, my options for finding her in turn were all too sparse. I lacked a true sensory power to flush her out with, nor any real way to deny or block off paths that she might use to escape through. My offensive capability wasn't much better, even if my defences and mobility would suffice to survive for a considerable length of time against her dolls.

Although, I'd seen the one, singular clip on PHO about Parian's dolls clashing with Fenja and Menja simultaneously. The ground had shaken, the road buckled, the earth had heaved and at the end of it all, the twin giantesses had been the ones cradling bloody knuckles as they fled the scene. Brute strength and durability shouldn't be underestimated, even if Parian probably wouldn't have the same level of preparation that she had then.

All of which, put together - didn't leave me with many ways to approach this, as far as I could think. If Parian went to Winslow, this would be a good deal less of an issue - I would just sacrifice a run or two to narrow down the area she was in, then rush her down from the outset of the challenge. But I didn't have that kind of assured, regular interaction with Parian - even if I did manage to secure some kind of recurring meeting under the guise of costume development, an undertaking that her website had assured me would be cripplingly expensive and easily eliminate all of the funds that had been donated and 'donated' to me by grateful citizens and unconscious criminals alike.

Not 'just' eliminate those funds either. Even more would be needed afterwards - and it made sense, dealings with other Parahumans had none of the major restrictions the government placed on Rogues, so she'd naturally ramp up the costs to those most likely to be able to afford it on account of the added risk of interactions with that crowd. I'd need more patrols to find a drug dealer or twenty to beat up, or a major gang bust, to bring up those kinds of funds again. If things got truly, truly desperate then there was the angle of blitzing a rich lady and having her become my sugar mommy, but then those funds amassed from one source would have a legal background to them, and that kind of traceability was something I wanted to avoid. Criminal cash and one-off minor donations were fine, even if that payment option came at a premium according to her website - but I didn't want to do anything that would draw attention to me or the civilians I surrounded myself with.

Getting distracted. The point was that these meetings, even if I did manage to set them up in the way I had hoped, wouldn't be cheap, long or frequent. Parian wasn't often seen in public outside of certain scheduled events. I had to make the most of the few attempts that I had, and that meant not wasting any attempts on simple information-gathering missions. I liked quick, frequent bursts of action broken up by long stretches of planning rather than every round being a bitter fight to the death against the odds that left me mentally and emotionally exhausted. I liked it, but I couldn't do that here.

Or, I think I couldn't. I'd need to maximise what I learned, obviously - I just couldn't put myself in a losing position for the sake of learning information faster.

Take stock. What do I know?

Firstly, I've been sat here for a solid minute - and I hear nothing. No movements, no sounds. No alarms, no heavy impacts. There isn't a patrol here, nor does there seem to be any special scenario happening around me aside from the odd building I found myself in.

Secondly, some of the exits I could see from here visibly sloped sharply - turning into rapid, smooth climbs or slides that turned in on themselves, presumably leading to another similar floor both above and below me. Perhaps even more than that. I didn't see the ZONE wall, so I could assume that those floors would be available to me if I slid down, or managed to scramble my way up the steep slope going upwards. The ZONE likely just blocked me into this building, preventing my escape. Not that I would want to escape - I had no abilities that would benefit from range, especially not against a Master with a HUNT modifier.

Thirdly, this was the first challenge. So far, I think almost all of the challenges had been... fair approximations of the Cape's default strength to the best of my knowledge. Armsmaster's was probably the most bullshit for me to handle, but... also fairly realistic if I was a known villain and he loaded up to fight me. They hadn't come out of the gate with a modifier that made them disgustingly overpowered, that came later. So when I look around at this challenge and see a layout that appeared to buff Parian to levels I would expect from a much later challenge - I think that means that I'm missing something.

Whatever that was, I couldn't see it from here. My only options were to either move to another floor and see if anything was present in those corridors, or head into these closed-off rooms and see what was inside. Changing floors might make a little too much noise on its own, trying to phase through the floor would definitely result in a thump when I landed - so my best option was to check out the rooms.

I approach the closest door and inspect it. No obvious traps. No electronics - little more than a standard door much like those found in Winslow. All the more reason not to open it. The ones in Winslow creaked like hell when pushed open, and I didn't want to test how far sound carried in the otherwise ominously quiet building. I phase through the door silently.

No Parian here. A desk. Some stationary. Some soft, cushy chairs in the corner and a fireplace on the other side of the room.

...nope. I wasn't seeing it. There was a trick here, and it had gone completely over my head. I was definitely going to kick myself later on, but I was just going to move on for now - the other rooms might have more insight. I leave the same way I came, phasing through the door and pacing to the next room - checking down the hallway for any movement as I go past a fork in the corridor. Nothing. The next room is slightly different, yet somehow just the same. A new layout, new furniture and decorations - a jewellery box on a counter, a scented candle flickering in the wind, curtains drawn just enough to show the slightest hint of the ZONE wall beyond the window.

Was it just a hide-and-seek challenge? Now there was a thought. What if Parian just decided to hide under a bed while I raced around, dodging her puppets from the moment she heard me move?

No, that would be silly. These challenges usually kept some semblance of the original's moves, personality and fighting style. Parian disliked fighting and shied away from confrontations, but had never hesitated to engage in combat when gangs had showed up to try and recruit Brockton's only real Rogue.

I leave the room.

And promptly get punched in the torso by a floating doll, not even a third of my size.

Not a lethal hit, but it completely blindsided me - sending my skidding and gasping across the smooth hallway before I roll to my feet - already looking to dodge the followup attack. I'm pleasantly surprised to find that the doll didn't move straight for an execution blow like most of my enemies did, and even more pleased to see that the reason for that was because it had knocked me so far away that it hadn't closed the gap in time to stop me from getting up. I back away, a light jog enough to keep the distance between us the same. Slow. At least, compared to what I had seen Parian do before. Small, too. Not that I was complaining.

Copper on my tongue. Bleeding. Maybe something internal, maybe not. Wasn't important now - if I was going to die, it was going to be because I got flattened by an angry stuffed teddy bear not because I didn't go to the hospital and something got infected and killed me two weeks from now. That wasn't how challenges worked. I need to focus on important things. Important questions. Like, why?

Why was it here? Was it patrolling the corridors this entire time? No. It was waiting for me outside that room. The scenario had activated somehow, Parian had noticed me moving about - had my footsteps been too loud? Had a floorboard creaked and I hadn't heard it, muffled by the carpet as it was? Was she flicking through CCTV feeds, and had just spotted me walking around?

And the timing of it was strange too. I couldn't have been in there that long. As long as Sophia's power had been on cooldown, no more. That varied but wasn't that long - somewhere between six and ten seconds maybe. That wasn't long enough for that doll to race across the floor from out of sight and get ready to clobber me upon exit. That meant that she had either noticed me as I entered the first room, and she just needed time to discretely deploy this doll - or she detected me as I moved towards the second room and immediately deployed this thing to attack.

Of the two, the first was unlikely. I knew that Parian could make dangerously large dolls. If her strategy was to wait and ambush me, then I would have come out the third or fourth room and been instantly killed in a single strike by a bear taller than me. I wasn't. I was knocked around by a baby - to me, that implied that she had created the first doll that she had to hand and immediately deployed it to attack me from wherever she was. This was all that could reach me in the time between her spotting me and me leaving that second room. She was either very close and noticed me going into the room, or quite far away and noticed me in the corridor. Based on the lack of sounds or reinforcements, I was betting on the latter.

As if to punish the thought, another doll floats into sight from around the corner. This one heavier, actually brushing against the floor in some vague facsimile of walking as Parian's telekinesis propels it forward. Closer to a canine doll, although lacking the distinctive flair and detail of her usual work. The sight of it confirmed my theory. Dolls were coming as fast as she could make them, although from what little I understood of her power - her limit was three. Whether that was a hard-coded limit of her power, or simply a lack of ability to concentrate on more than that - I didn't know.

But I did know that three dolls would eventually corner me if they started getting much faster than they were - and this canine doll was indeed faster than the creepy, fat baby. It looked like it had more mass to it as well, the effort from Parian to genuinely propel it forward off of walls and the ground showcased that well - rather than simply being dragged around in the air by telekinesis.

I needed to move. I could probably run past them without a problem in my speed-state, but I didn't want to risk it. Not only was there no guarantee that the next floor would be safe, the brief moments of paralysis at either side of the speed-state might get me killed. And I couldn't open doors like that, because Velocity sucked and his power sucked too. On him, at least. I could at least use it sometimes, but the suckiness still brushed off on my version. No, I wasn't bitter and no, I wasn't irrationally biased against the guy. My dedicated hateclub was perfectly rational. I couldn't reliably dodge the dog-doll at my base speed though, let alone fight it.

Instead, I run backwards - diving down the slide leading to the floor below. Escape wasn't feasible. Not with the HUNT modifier, but I needed to at least isolate the possibilities of what had happened. What Parian was doing, how quickly she escalated with her dolls, where her materials came from, how she had detected me and exactly how viable it was to evade her various dolls with my usual combination of mobility skills. Every one of those questions left unanswered could be something I die next time to find out if I don't work it out here.

This time, I don't hesitate to open the doors normally. No need for stealth when she already knows exactly where I am. I flit around the rooms. Nothing out of the ordinary. And, just as importantly as not seeing any sign of Parian, this was a dead-end floor. No further paths sloping downwards - only a few exits pointing back up the way I came. That didn't eliminate the possibility that Parian was hiding on my original floor, but the odds were good that she was on the third floor or a hypothetical higher floor if one existed.

I pause as a bloated, vaguely man-shaped doll floats around my original entry to the floor. Not approaching, just staying there. The dog-doll from before has evidently circled around via a different route, blocking off what I assume leads to another exit. No sign of the third doll yet, but I wouldn't be surprised if it was sitting at a third and final exit - seeking to slowly pen me in from all sides that I could escape down.

That was fine. I came down here for a good reason, slowly and methodically penning me in was better for me than being chased. I dive back into one of the rooms, jumping up onto the bed. Vista's power to shrink the gap above me, then one good jump into shadow-state takes me to the floor above.

The lumbering footsteps from below me are immediately obvious - a frantic pace to both relocate floors and block off access to Parian herself. Vista's power hadn't recovered yet and I can't get the height to simply jump up to the next floor without it, even from the desk. I grab a small sewing kit from the side of this room - freeze it in the air with Clockblocker's power and use it as a stepping stool to get the extra height I need to make the jump to the next floor.

Thankfully, I once again make it through without my attempt being mercilessly cut short by an unlucky electricity cable running through the ceiling.

Third floor. I head to the exit of the room, racing out only long enough to verify that there was a floor even higher than this. Back into the room. Shadow Stalker's power was already nearly back, but Vista's power was still unravelling itself down on the bottom floor and Clockblocker's was locked until my last object unfroze. Not an issue. I clamber up to the highest point I can again, then bring out my Ashen Clone to simply stand in place by the wall - hands clasped together in a foothold.

Not the most solid or reliable of methods, given how fragile it is most of the time - but if it can throw out a punch and connect solidly, it can be stepped on for long enough not to let me slip through like an idiot. I lodge my foot into its hand and press my weight onto it as it propels me upwards - the extra momentum giving me just the amount of momentum I need for my shadow-state to glide upwards without most of the effect of gravity. My shadow-state times out as I pass through the floor, forcibly ejecting my body onto the upper floor gracelessly.

I roll away as a fist larger than my head puts a clean hole through the space I was just standing in. The large doll I was now sharing a room with not even pausing before converting it into a body slam. No hesitation, but still foiled by the simple fact that its downward momentum was slowed and disrupted by various pieces of furniture blocking its downwards descent first - knocking it to the side long enough for me to get my feet under me and start running. Door was already open. Parian was here - no way that thing got through the door on its own.

As if to highlight my point, the doorframe explodes outwards as it gives chase. Fast. Really fast. This was the level I had expected from this thing, but it wasn't perfect. It's poor choice of attacks had left it's form peppered with holes - running through furniture and walls with such reckless abandon had it looking more deflated than it should, and when I run into the next room - the door seems to explode with a little less violence as it enters after me.

I vault the bed in the room as I phase through the wall, idly noting the state of the room as I pass. Bedsheets stripped down to nothing. Curtains yanked away from the windows. This was the missing piece to what I had missed earlier - Parian didn't have any dolls ready at the start. She needed to make them, and the materials to do that weren't sitting in a pile waiting for her, they were scattered around the various rooms of the hotel-esque building. This was, at least in part, a stealth mission. Sure, she would be fairly dangerous with even just her small scale textile manipulation in her starting room - but if she was stopped from racing from room to room, if I only aggroed her when I was already inside the room with her, she would never get the chance or materials to make a bigger, more dangerous doll.

Hell, if I won fast enough - she might not get to make a doll at all. I didn't know how long it should take her to convert the layered, interwined fabric from a hotel's professionally laid-out bed, but I imagined it wouldn't be particularly easy without neatly separated fabrics and no easy access to sewing needles.

Not that the realisation would help me now. It was a bit too late to put the cat back in the bag, she was very aware that I was here and had doubtless plundered every room on this floor - she had probably already relocated to a safer floor already, letting her minions do the chasing for her. I had assumed I would be safe while her three dolls moved floors, but that assumption had a fatal flaw: She didn't need to keep those dolls. Doubtless, one, two or even all three of those on the floors below had collapsed into nothing as Parian focused her efforts on her stronger creations up here.

A fist punches through the floor of the room I had slipped into. Not a small fist poking a hole in the floor, a gigantic fist larger than most of the container units on each side of the room put together knocked a hole large enough to fit a car through into the centre of the room. The heavy stomping from behind me indicates that the wall is going to burst open from the rampaging fat one that I had passed through the wall to avoid.

End of the line. My Ash Clone has already dissipated and recovered, so I buy myself a brief second as it blocks the path of the doll - notably slowing it as the puppet seemingly fails to notice it at all, but nothing can stop the sheer bulk of the sweeping hand smashing towards me like a hammer blow. Even if Sophia's power would come off of cooldown a moment earlier, I didn't have a path towards victory here any longer. Nowhere I could escape to, nor any secrets I could uncover before my death.

My body practically dissolves on impact with the ridiculously-oversized arm - knocked back and through the wall just in time to receive the shoulder-charge from the damaged doll that had been chasing me. I'm treated to the delightful sight of the blood-soaked doll deflating as bits of my body drip from its form. The third-party view I got after an instantaneous death was always a treat. I was more used to seeing my body bounce around a bit, because usually I only got the opportunity to see it on large falls - most other deaths had me lose consciousness for a little while first before my body gave up.

FAILURE​

No shit.

But... promising. Save for one, crucial point.

I had no idea how she had spotted me. I had made a half-guess at the start that perhaps she had some tiny dolls floating around that she could see through, but the evidence lined up against that theory. Not only had her dolls lost an opportunity for a killing blow due to what could only be a lack of awareness about its surroundings, but she clearly didn't have any other dolls in the area aside from that initial one sent to attack me. I hadn't seen any sign of a CCTV system, nor did the rooms on her for have any form of special vantage point or any unusual features compared to the others. I felt safe ruling out footsteps, knowing that she was actually two floors above me - I wouldn't have been shocked if she heard me from the floor below, but I wasn't loud enough to even entertain the idea that simple walking was what gave me away.

And that was frustrating. Because that could kill me. I had a clear, obvious path to victory now - find Parian on the 4th floor without being detected. If I did that, I'm 100% sure that I would win on either the first or second try - depending on how capable she is with melee and multitasking. But that path was slammed shut in my face if I couldn't stop her from aggroing from two entire floors away. She'd have at least two large dolls ready by the time I got up there, either by clambering the steep, smooth slope that had replaced the stairs or waiting on Shadow Stalker's power to give me a simple, predictable route up.

Or... no. That was it. It didn't solve the question, but that might not matter. I think I was undetected going into that first room. If my theory was sound that I had only been detected sometime after I had left and continued exploring, then entering and only moving upwards from that point was a viable strategy. I could climb directly upwards from there, take my time - keep quiet. Let my powers recharge fully instead of blitzing through under pressure like before. I'd be two floors up without a whisper of noise if I did it right, and at that point - the only thing that I would be missing from a perfect run would be finding the right room. And if I aggroed her on that floor, she couldn't send a doll out the door to fight me without revealing herself - and if I didn't, I would keep phasing into rooms until I ran into her and killed her then and there. Probably not the intended method, but having all of these powers at my disposal gave me options to work with.

But that was irrelevant for now. I shake my head and follow Parian through to our apparent meeting room. Fifteen minutes to stall for this challenge. Reasonable. Very reasonable.

I take a seat where directed. Just outside of the door, I note a flash of orange passing by as the apparent chaperone settles down just outside to wait.

Newter

Mercenary 1/4

(DNGR)​

I pause at that. I knew Newter, of course. Faultline's gang of jailbreakers and misfits that made their home in the nightclubs of the shady part of town whenever they weren't taking on contracts of dubious legality around the world. I didn't actually know they were back in Brockton yet, last I heard they were lying low after getting involved in a prison break of some kind and pissing off the Protectorate in the process. The details escape me, but no one guy can be expected to remember all this stuff when it happens in a place not called Brockton Bay.

Case 53. Hallucinogenic touch - or rather, all of his fluids were drugs. All of them. I had asked the world to be sure about that fact before, and one brave poster had responded that she and a pair of friends had experimented with what she referred to as 'the trippiest handjob of my life' with the aid of a thick pair of clothes. Worth the ban, and I got a rather useless tip that giving him a blowjob would go exactly as poorly as you would expect and require a hospital visit - and also that a facial 'wasn't that bad' compared to his usual fluids but could still send you tripping for a week. Not a combat tip I expected to need here, but it was of at least a little interest - if only because it gave some sign of the quantities involved before it got dangerous. A melee fight to the death would doubtless get me to that level, the PHO feats thread showed him basically knocking people out in a single strike and it was debatable how much of that was the drugs and how much was his Brute strength.

But once that drug was in me, I would be feeling it even outside of the challenge. Was there any other way to take that modifier? All of the previous people I had seen it on, it was obvious. Masters, people who could modify memories or that had powers capable of lasting effects even once the challenge was over. Newter was a known quantity, if he had the DNGR modifer the only way for that to be true was if his drugs weren't purely biological and would interface with my mind or power directly to cause an effect in real life if I was too affected.

On the flip side, it was a biological substance that would be entirely cleansed post-challenge. You could dilute his hallucinogens, treat them in a hospital. I could acknowledge that the mental effect might linger for a short time - but it shouldn't last that long once the substance was gone. A bit of time for the brain to steady itself out from any trippy patterns it had gotten into, that should be all - logically speaking.

... I couldn't risk it. I had a meeting with Parian right now, and if I started obviously tripping balls even for just a minute without ever touching the guy it would not only damage our working relationship, but also raise a lot of questions about how the hell it happened. And the DNGR modifier was one that I didn't really want to get that close to. The idea of lasting consequences was a large departure from most of what I had done so far, with the exception of the life-or-death battle against Oni Lee.

I reluctantly drag my eyes away. It was the smart thing to do. I knew that.

...I shift my chair just enough to remove the glimpse of orange skin from my peripheral vision. I know what I'm like. I'll have a moment of boredom and decide that there's no harm in giving it a try.

"So." Parian is a softly-spoken woman, with the kind of voice that spoke of an intense focus on keeping her accent as neutral as possible. Probably for her own safety, judging by her life choices. If she was white, she would have accidentally flashed a bit of skin to the Empire by now and enjoyed their sudden protectiveness of her as they hail her as one of the most stand-up moral capes in the city. It was hard to rule out any other races, I would expect even nervous asians looking for protection to think twice before signing up with Lung. And being a black person in Brockton Bay... well. Sub-optimal to say the least. The community was supposedly tight-knit in its shared misery, and frequent PRT patrols did a lot to provide some element of safety from the two powerful, racially-charged groups that either mildly disliked or outright hated them. "I received your up-front payment for the consultation, I'd be happy to assist with your needs in costume design and creation - but the actual cost of that is quite significant, both in terms of the cost in materials and in the actual stages of design and creation. I don't want to lead you on, but I must repeat what I said online - this will get expensive. Most of my clients prefer to wait until they have support from a larger organisation or are well-established, I'll need to ask for upfront payment at all stages because of that."

Straight out of the gate with the money speech. Expected. For all that actually being heroic had gotten me this far, from her estimation of me I would be a penniless vigilante that had expended all of his funds on a motoring helmet and some extra jeans - only capable of getting this far off of my looted-gains from petty crooks. Not a reliable source of income, not when a gang could come and squash me - or when the PRT could snatch me up along with my business. Not committing to any work that she hadn't been paid for was understandable. Sensible. Mildly annoying for me personally, but I got it. "That isn't an issue for me. I'll ensure that you are appropriately paid before we proceed past each step." I opt for a polite tone.

She makes an indeterminate sound, something between a sigh and a grunt of acknowledgement. "Then let's get started. First of all - let's talk about limitations. You mentioned on PHO that you were something of a Trump, any powers that would need to be kept in mind before we start designing? Holes for Blaster powers, open mask, toolbelts, things like that?"

"I need to be able to touch things directly with my hands." I start out, thinking of my current - and possible future - powerset. Othala, Panacea, Clockblocker. "So full gloves are a no-go. I've already got a stash of useful items, so I wouldn't exactly say no to a better holder. As for the rest-" Were any of the Blasters in the Bay the sort that actually fired out of their body? It was hard to tell without a closeup shot, and their costumes usually didn't reveal much. I'd guess not - but I could change it later. "-I might need my mouth free as well, though I also see the value in a full-face helmet..." The absolute deadpan of her masked expressions somehow leaks through. "Right, appreciate that isn't the most helpful description. Half-mask, but also full-mask... maybe we can experiment a bit to see what works? I'll pay you every time, of course."

That was the important part, snuck in at the end. Recurring visits. Approving this change or that, tweaking a minor detail here and there - scheduling another meeting for when its done. Expensive, yes - but reliable visits to a Cape was worth the investment. It wasn't like I needed the money for anything else right now, and looting criminals never got old.

I sally back and forth over costume designs with all the passion in the world at my disposal. Flitting about from half-formed point to half-formed point in a deliberate exaggeration of my usual conversations at school. I didn't want to make progress, I didn't want a quick meeting - and I certainly didn't want her to show up at our next one with a costume that we could both agree was perfect. Being an annoyance like this, with contradicting requirements - armoured gloves, exposed skin, half-mask, full-coverage, easy-removal, heavily armoured... it was obvious that so many of these requirements couldn't coexist outside of a Tinkertech piece. But, if pleading ignorance led to a more iterative process... that was the real aim here.

Eventually, Parian loses the will to live first. "Let's stop here." A hint of exasperation, combined with a slightly thicker accent that isn't masked properly. "How about this, I'll pull some designs together-"

"With the colour schemes I sent?" I ask innocently.

"-I'll attempt to incorporate your... suggestions." Very delicate, Parian. Smooth. I'd have told me to fuck off by now if I was in your shoes. Guess that's why I don't work retail. Or work at all, but hey - I'm still a student. No big deal. "I'll draft some designs for the accessories and smaller pieces that don't require as much material. You can work out what does and doesn't work, make your decision around them - and we can move on to constructing the rest of your costume once you have those essential requirements pinned down. Does that sound good?"

I nod enthusiastically, trying to look like I am still paying attention. Minor slots now. Chest and leg slots filled later. It was obvious which ones would be more expensive, and it also meant that any coherent theme could be switched around at a later date. "Sounds great! I'll be sure to let you know if I think of anything else." She makes a noise of agreement that almost manages to avoid sounding slightly pained at the thought. Poor Parian, I must have sounded so put-together and reasonable over PHO. Alas, it's your own fault for being a recluse.

"I'll send you an estimate for the bill." Trying to scare me off from coming back? Not going to happen my dear. I'll pay that twice over.

I smile through my helmet. "It's been lovely to meet you." I stand and bow lightly. "I've heard so many great things about you and your work, and I'm really quite new to this so I am sorry if I'm bumbling around a bit." Dial up the innocent fanboy. Don't want to leave her with too much of a negative impression. "But that's why I came to you! I know that you're the expert in all things costume around here, so I'm really looking forward to what we can make in the future and what advice you'll have for me. I'll try not to waste your time, so thank you for looking after me!"

"Think nothing of it." She loses some of her aloofness like a slowly deflating balloon. Minor success.

We exchange pleasantries for a short while longer, while I watch her challenge sheet like a hawk. Fifteen. Twelve. Ten. Seven. "I should probably get going then. I'll look forward to seeing what you come up with." Three. Two. One. "Challenge."

I don't delay before retracing my steps to the first room I explored last time. No minute of introspection first, just a rapid entry and subsequent ascent with the only delay being the few seconds mandated by Sophia's power being on cooldown. Space warping to get up one floor, Ash clone for the next. I deliberately avoided the Clockblocker method in case the object falling once it unfroze made a noise if it fell the wrong way.

I pause once I reach the 4th floor, straining my ears. No rustling of cloth. No loud footsteps. No banging doors. Not that I heard much of those last time, but I wasn't this close when the fight had started either. Nothing. I phase through the door. Open corridor- no. Was this really the best move? I had moved around the first room and all the rooms above it safely so far, didn't that imply that whatever method she had used to detect me couldn't be used inside the rooms? That her surveillance only covered the hallways? It was far from guaranteed based on such a small sample size of tests, but if she was able to detect me going through the halls two floors away - it was pretty likely that she would notice me on the same floor.

I wait out the timer, then slide back into the room I had just left. The general layout of these floors seemed to be much the same as those below, and my frantic race around the building last challenge had given me a solid idea about which ways the various corridors went. Which, in theory, meant that going into a wall that didn't lead out into a corridor should drop me directly into a neighbouring room. Obvious in principle, but the idea meant that I could effectively explore every connected room as one large batch without ever entering the corridor. There were some that would require checking on the 'inside' ring of rooms, and the gaps left by the modified stairs would also stop me from going past all at once - but I wasn't under any time pressure yet. This was the objectively correct, safest way to do this - so however annoying it was, I needed to just sit tight and phase into every single room whether it takes an additional three minutes or three hours.

I drift between rooms. My initial fears that I was going to sprint directly into an electrical outlet seem unfounded so far. It just isn't a very... electrified building, if that was the right word. Just as well, because running directly into an electrical current in my shadow state was really fucking painful and the screaming that results afterwards isn't exactly voluntary - even in a circumstance like this, where making such a noise might just spell the end of my attempt.

Icy-clarity returns to me. Drugs long-gone from my system. A reset. A perfect reset. Was that all that was needed in this case? Simply challenging something else to reset me properly? Perhaps I couldn't assume it would always be the case or even be a safe option for mental effects, but it was good to know.

I smirk to myself. I wonder if Sophia even realised that, in a very roundabout way, she said that she respected me? Certainly not. I'd throw that back at her next time and watch her seethe.

"-stening to me?" Sophia's voice cuts across the rooftop. "I said, what the fuck are you doing here? Who are you?"

"Ah, Shadow Stalker." I tilt my head at her. "I'm Void Cowboy. A hero. I'd say it's a pleasure to meet you, but I don't really see any need to get along with the PRT's lapdogs. I find being a vigilante suits me best for now."

She'll be fuming at that. The full-face mask saves her from knowing that I know, but her clipped response comes out steadily despite the fact that her face is probably scrunched up like a lemon at the moment. "Whatever. I'm asking what a loser like you is doing fucking around outside a school. A whole bunch of losers are lining up to try and take pictures of you as you go past, it's too much attention. You think that the PRT won't snatch you up just for trying to showboat?"

I know what you're like Sophia. You rant way too much for me not to know your true feelings. "I'll be sure to avoid that. It would be a shame to be handicapped like you were. Should I take it that you haven't called them down on me yet then?"

"Not personally." She crosses her arms. "But that doesn't mean anything. Anyone could assume you were doing something illegal with you running around like that. They'll probably send someone to investigate soon, even if you are supposed to be a hero." The air quotes? Really?

"Don't pretend you don't know who I am. Void Cowboy? I had an announcement thread and an AMA just last week." I sag at the ensuing silence. "Whatever. I assume you go to Winslow too then? That would explain a lot."

She bristles. "Wrong kind of question to be asking, even implying that you're trying to track down a Ward can get you fucked over." She pauses. "And don't imply you go here too, I don't want to know about it - and trust me when I say that the PRT working out your identity is fucking shit."

"Well, I'm afraid it gets kind of obvious thanks to my powers. I'm a Trump, so I sometimes get weaker versions of the powers from people in a wide area around me. It doesn't tell me who does and doesn't have powers-" Technically true, I had to find that out the hard way the first time around. "-but it's kind of obvious when I get a shadow-related power in the middle of class." I shift into my shadow-state and back.

That got her attention. And if she's anything like the other Sophia, she'll be annoyed as hell about it.

"I'll admit though, I'm kind of curious as to how it compares to the real thing. I'm just here to burn off a bit of energy, so if you aren't here to slap me with the law or give me a speech - then why not join me in something a bit more entertaining?" I grin behind my helmet. "Wanna fight? It would be cool to see how I measure up to a Ward, and I'm not the type to go crying to the media if I get a bruise or two. I've got a reputation to maintain."

She considers me for a moment. "You know what?" She snaps her crossbow back into the holder. "First smart thing you've said so far. Let's go."

Bitch. I said a whole heap of smart things just now, you're just so dumb they went over your head. "Let's get out of the public eye first. Try not to make it too easy for me."

"Oh, believe me." Sophia threatens. "That won't be a problem. You can go through ceilings?" I nod. "Second building on the right, the floor under the roof level. I'll meet you there, and I'll beat some much-needed humility into you - out of the goodness of my heart."

I smile. Ah. Violence. The true language of love.

Let it never be said that I wasn't a romantic.
