#2,235
"What does Mush look like? What's his name?" I ask politely.

After my somewhat-embarrassing oversight with Skidmark in plain clothes, I'd taken a more proactive approach to identifying potential Capes in the crowd. Every blonde woman was a potential Squealer, and after a dozen attempts on random partygoers - I was left only with a minor headache and my original assumption that she was in the warehouse in the next building over. As for Mush... I didn't have a clue what he looked like. The only mentions of him on the news or PHO were of the trash-giant squaring up against Squealer's tank and losing - and then the Merchant's crowing about their new recruit. He could be a Case-53, or he could be a Changer - or even a Master. I didn't know what I was looking for, and save for challenging every single person at this party - I was never going to find him off of blind luck.

Still. Ideally, I didn't have to wait for Skidmark to get off his ass and grouch at the two other Merchant Capes. I had my own ways of 'asking around' without drawing attention in real life.

"What's Squealer's real name? Does she leave her workshop during the Merchant parties?" Admittedly, my questioning hasn't yielded many answers so far. Most of my opponents are largely mindless save for their combat skills and tactical prowess, but even those with a proper personality or the REAL modifier weren't guaranteed to be willing to talk to me or answer my questions. Regardless of their state of mind, one thing took precedence - the fact that I was the enemy.

Or, maybe they didn't actually know? I was making a few assumptions about how influential and 'in-the-know' the average person in this room was. It was possible that their claimed inability to answer my questions was genuine, rather than a testament to the unbending desire of the simulation to spite me at every turn. It would make a certain amount of sense. The lady below me right now didn't exactly seem to be the picture of defiance. The broken, terrified sobbing was certainly making me look like the bad guy here, and while there was a certain validity to that - it also didn't change the fact that mistaking this for real life would get me killed. I'd made that mistake before. A few too many times, honestly. Took a while for the lesson to sink in - but getting stabbed by people you thought you were showing mercy to has a way of sharpening a guy's focus.

"Please let me go." She whimpers.

"Am I not being reasonable?" I scowl down at her broken body. "You're lucky, you get that - right? Because it might look weird if I beat all of your challenges and you start fawning over me in front of Skidmark. That would be weird no matter what my power does to smooth things over. And if I beat this challenge, I don't have any guarantee that I'll find another REAL modifier in the next one. You're privileged to be someone that is more useful alive than dead, because if - if - you can get me valuable information when asked, it's worth it for me to kill myself rather than you. Skidmark. Squealer. Mush. Weaknesses. Location. Appearances. Aspects of their power I might not know about. Give me a reason here. I'm doing my best to help you win, why can't you help me in return?" I shake my head. "Because if you can't..." My boot presses down on her neck. "...then I'll just have to take my chances with the next one."

"I really, really don't know-" I lash out with my foot again at the weak response.

"Not sure whether to blame you or my power. Whatever." I grouch, kneeling down to peer at her. "I mean, you could at least have lied. Sent me running around looking for, Katie or something who can usually be found shooting up drugs in the ladies room. I would have been fucking annoyed, but I would have respected you more for it." Like Tattletale at the bank challenge. Infuriating at the time... but I respected the level of petty spite that came from opposing me in any small way like that. And now I knew to watch out for her, as an added bonus. "You're not doing much to help the stereotype of how much of a waste of space the Merchant's are. Like, I literally just told you I was going to kill you if you didn't tell me something good - and you just, shrugged your shoulders like there was nothing you could do? I'm actually kind of pissed off. If you're a big shot in the gang, no wonder you've never achieved anything in the city."

I don't wait to hear her next words.

SUCCESS​

I swipe away the reward screen without reading. Irrelevant.

No information. Or, not what I wanted, anyway. A lot of talk about the Merchants in general. A surprising number of complaints about Skidmark and new hotshots in general. And no small amount of division over what exactly the Merchants were or should be in the future. I'd mentally classified them as just a 'gang' forever because that's what PHO said - but it was probably more accurate to call them a group of allied drug dealers that were slowly being dragged into a coherent gang by the twin pressures of Skidmark pulling and the rest of the city's established ethnicity-based gangs pushing them into a corner. Not everyone was happy about it, but they fell in line by simple virtue of the fact that Skidmark was essentially running a Cape-based protection racket to seize every unaffiliated dealer in the city under his banner. The Merchants would probably explode in about five seconds if the ABB and Empire suddenly left town, that was the slapdash nature of their 'organisation'.

Which was interesting and something I would probably post about on PHO in the future to sound knowledgeable and cool - but it also wasn't a name or a location to go and find the Capes I wanted.

Not that I was really expecting much. Most challenges were set at a certain time and place, usually months or more in the past - finding something modern, combined with someone talkative and also in-the-know was a tough ask. If this party was in more of a fixed location I might have been able to abuse a WRLD modifier and try getting CCTV logs without being stonewalled by my power, but the pop-up nature of this party denied that possibility.

No need to beat myself up over it. It wasn't like I needed to get that information at all costs. I just needed to lurk around Skidmark and play the part of a Cape groupie living the dream as he unwittingly hands his life, power and organisation over to me on a silver platter. His barely-disguised contempt towards me and my attitude was a dream come true. He didn't suspect me of being anything but a delusional Cape groupie hoping to suck up to the boss, and as the public winner of his little fight club - being seen ordering me around like his personal bitch was good for his street cred. This was everything he wanted, looking like the undisputed leader of the Merchants to everyone who he needed to prove it to.

And, this was everything I wanted too. Skidmark's challenges available on cooldown, and simply following him around was likely to lead me to both Squealer and Mush at some point in the evening. And the fact that a significant chunk of the non-Cape leadership of the gang had a somewhat positive opinion of me already thanks to a smattering of early challenges being completed was a good thing too. I didn't have a use for that kind of foothold now, but maybe I could turn the gang into a force for good - or, perhaps, just as another way for me to consolidate the reins of power over the city.

Skidmark snatches the shot glass out of my hand, swigging it down in a single motion after brushing flecks of powder from his nose. "Fucking garbage." He announces to anyone that would listen.

The drugs or the drink? "I see." I nod airily. I was getting a good feel for Skidmark's personality by now. Crude. Abrasive. Permanently complaining about something. And almost certainly about to make his bad day somebody else's problem.

"You see? You see what exactly?" He gets up in my face. "You think that's what the Merchants are about up here? Think that's what's normal?"

I shrug. "I... wouldn't know." Diplomacy, Greg. It probably would have been better to say nothing, but Skidmark was on more of a hair-trigger than I thought. Lack of impulse control, probably a symptom of whatever the hell he was on right now.

"Of course you wouldn't. What would a stupid-looking twink like you know about anything? Stick to punching things. Leave the-" He makes a vague motion with his hands. "-leave the smart shit to me. I'll tell you what's what. And what I'm telling you now, is that the goods today-" He tosses the glass behind him. "-are fucking trash."

I nod silently this time.

"Which means?" He prompts insistently. "Use that fucking brain of yours."

I have to answer now? "I should get something else?"

He leans in aggressively, seeming all-too-sober in the blink of an eye. "Which means that the supplier thinks I'm a fucking joke, too drunk or high to tell that he's watering down the shit that I paid for. Nobody skimps out on my service. It's about respect. Somebody cheats you and gets away with it, they think you're a joke. They tell their friends. They all start getting ideas. So you have to nip it in the bud. Every. Single. Time. Come with me. Make yourself useful for once."

"Sure." I fall in line behind him. Five seconds. Four. Three. Two. One. "Challenge." The whisper is easily drowned out by the noise of the party.

Situation check. Big bunker. Lots of super-strong fields around it, with one gap in the middle as an entrance. He's got a... well. The end result is basically a rapid-fire tank cannon - but it's probably just a normal gun of some description boosted to ridiculous levels of power by the booster fields that the PREP modifier gave him. In a way, the sheer power on display makes it simple. Attract his attention from the bunker, he looks in that direction and makes that entire direction disappear. Fine, treat it like a strange DOOM modifier and find another approach.

I settle down on the ground, well out of Skidmark's potential line of sight. What was the trick here? I wasn't a stranger to unreasonable-looking challenges early on, but often there was a certain trick to it. There were only two issues - recognising the trick, and having the tools to execute it.

...it was definitely the roof. It was so, obviously, a weak point in the defences that even a child could spot it. Now that I know the basics of how Skidmark is defending his bunker, it's easy to see how both his offence and defence are near-perfect in a 360-degree circle. But the fields are giant, flat walls. They don't curve up and over to cover his roof - nor would they need to. There's no access from that direction, there are no nearby buildings that someone could easily jump from. It didn't seem necessary.

And, critically, his power wouldn't let him do it.

The current set-up was easy to understand. He circled his bunker, layered his walls over and over in the PREP phase, investing hours, or even days, into the process. But when he isn't looking, those layers start to fade. I'd seen videos of his fields functioning even hours after he was in a fight, so the process must be slower in areas where he had invested heavily - but in the first challenge, I was able to abuse that aspect of his power as he turned around for just a little bit too long. Even now, his layers were probably slightly eroding wherever he wasn't looking - but they were already so comically dense that my power's anti-stalling measures would kick in before I could take advantage.

But the restrictions still applied when he was setting them up in the first place. He couldn't make a field above the bunker - he would have to leave the bunker to have that kind of visibility on and over the roof, and that would mean allowing another wall to weaken as it goes unattended.

I take a minute to reposition myself at the top of the nearest building.

Options? Flight was the obvious one. I didn't have it now, but in the worst-case scenario - the moment I managed to catch New Wave on a full-team outing, it was pretty much guaranteed. There were plenty of fliers in the Bay, the fact that I didn't already have it was as much bad luck as anything else - and that streak couldn't last much longer. Still. I wanted to win here. Today. Coming back in a few days or weeks, if I even had another opportunity like this - that was far from ideal.

Using all three of my shadow state charges to glide, shrinking space with Vista, Clockblocking some kind of platform to stand on to recover both Vista and Shadow Stalker's powersets and then gliding again - that was more than sufficient for the horizontal jump, but it didn't cover the vertical challenge. The nearby buildings just weren't tall enough relative to Skidmark's fields.

That left my Tinker powers, and my new kinetic fields from the last challenge. Alas, my version of Skidmark's power was predictably nerfed for the first reward. I couldn't build myself an elevator or some kind of trampoline, because I couldn't really layer the power in the same way. I activate the power, toying with it for a moment by flexing my fingers.

The best way to describe it was ten seconds of fingerpainting. Find a surface, and start applying either of two effects until time runs out. The first, which I was temporarily labelling 'Direct' would paint little arrows in a direction of my choosing and attempt to drag the surface and anything touching it in that direction - and 'Repel' would apply crosses and just... well. Repel things. It didn't apply to the object it was attached to, or allow for a set direction on its own - it was closer to a trampoline-like effect on the covered surface, Repel had notably more force behind it than Direct - but, equally, Direct could continually apply to the target while Repel would swiftly expel and therefore stop affecting whatever happened to touch it. Whichever one I chose, a second activation of the ability would kickstart the effect, at which point it would steadily wind down as it stayed out of my line of sight until the power was gone and therefore ready to be used again. The more shapes I applied at once, the stronger the effect - as many as I could apply in ten seconds was the limit I had found.

Which would be great, if I could apply enough of either of those effects to move a human body forcefully through the air. As it is, it's closer to the kind of stiff wind that sends tables and chairs bouncing down the street - something that you can plant your feet, grit your teeth and hold in place if you put in the effort. Skidmark was several times stronger than that with less set-up if he focused his power correctly. I've got nothing. Nothing save for some hare-brained solution of steadily stripping off more of my clothes to use as a Clockblocked platform, float upwards by repelling my shadow-state from the platform after guessing the exact three seconds that the Clockblocked object would fail - and then reapply yet another platform to stand on and use as a secondary repel, assuming I even got it back in time. A clunky solution, even ignoring the insane luck I would need. And the entire time, I would be in plain sight of Skidmark the instant he even glanced in my direction - and he pretty much had to be circling his bunker by default, so it was only a matter of time.

And then there were my Tinker powers.

I haven't really had the chance to experiment with my newfound Tinker powers much. Mostly because they don't seem well-suited to me just... building something myself. Great for collaboration, great for outright stealing designs and recreating them in a flash once I had the materials - but then the design was gone and I needed to find another. Or recreate the plans again - which, in the case of the relatively simple mecha-blade I pinched from Leet, wouldn't be hard - but without the mech to attach it to, it didn't really have the same value.

The idea of me just sitting down with some scrap and scraping together a working piece of artillery to blow that bunker to smithereens just wasn't going to happen for the time being. Not until I got more specialisations under my belt. Leet's power could add an 'interesting' effect to whatever I built, but trying to Tinker solely with that power meant creating every single component piece with that power, rather than just putting the final product together. That was a dozen extra 'quirks' to account for in the design, a spiralling loop that demanded more and more time if I wanted something that wouldn't kill me when I hit the real-life equivalent of a natural one. Nothing that couldn't be fixed with a few hours or days of research and designing... but then, what should I make? What was the one design that would make the effort worthwhile, taking my combat prowess - or my progress elsewhere - to the next level? That was the struggle.

...I should take Leet up on her offer sooner rather than later. It wasn't just about the possibility of challenging Uber and potentially appeasing whatever power was restricting progress on Leet - but I needed to work out ways of getting value out of my Tinker powers. In theory, they were the most flexible powers that I had - but it was just hard to find a way to put them to use. Too many annoying restrictions, too much time needed to invest - if I could offload the design work to Leet, request the designs to be limited to a certain kind of easy-to-acquire base materials and load my Tinker power with a ready-to-print design that could help on a patrol... or, even a challenge? Did designs carry over into the simulations? Maybe. I should test it, if I managed to get my way into Squealer's workshop.

I pause at that. Right. Squealer was here. Well, not in this simulation specifically - but somewhere around where I am in real life. Maybe that was the trick that I was missing here. I needed to propel myself up and over the walls? What better way than by making use of a transport Tinker? Even if I couldn't exactly just steal a design outright without being noticed, if I gained a specialisation from it like I did with Leet... surely a simple contraption - some wheels, a ramp, a glider of some sort - wouldn't be too difficult? It didn't need to be amazing, even a non-Tinkertech tool to help my glide would 'almost' be enough if not for the extra height I needed to gain. A tool specialised for the task? Getting myself up and over would be a complete walk in the park.

Viable. Although, not helpful in clearing this challenge immediately.

Then, for this challenge - even if the odds of success were low - I needed to get a better understanding of what was inside the bunker. How Skidmark would want to fight. The kind of weapons he had access to. And that meant walking through the front door. Even if it was obviously a trap, simply knowing what the trap was could help. Was it something I could weaponise against him? Was it something he might use against me once I actually got inside? Did he secretly have reinforcements in there watching the door, that might come to help him once I drop in?

None of those questions would get answered if he just shot me before I got halfway down the path to the front door. So, time to make my distraction. I hop into my speed-state and race to the opposite side of the bunker, circling out wide to ensure he didn't accidentally spot me moving. Three minutes of searching later, I have my distraction. A discarded wheel from a truck of some kind. The plan is simple. I load up Skidmark's powerset, I slap a bunch of arrows on it that would point it towards the barrier then activate it once I'm back on the opposite side of the map - and either Skidmark sees the movement and attacks, or he hears the thunderous noise that the wheel makes as it hits the barrier and bounces off to slam into the glass windows of the buildings behind it. Either way, he'd definitely be looking if my first attempt meant anything. Meanwhile, I race through the front door and hopefully punch him in the face and win.

Hopefully.

Test run. I activate Skidmark's power, jabbing my finger all over the side and outer rim of the tire. Honestly, this should pick up speed pretty quickly - that was one of the upsides of my power compared to Skidmark's because my fields essentially were stuck to the object, they wouldn't lose their pushing force once they left the starting line. They would keep going faster until either the power started to fade, or until air resistance and friction matched the accelerating force of the object in question.

Activate. I issue the mental command. The tire springs to life, moving under its own power - and then, just as quickly, grinds to a halt.

In a second, it's obvious what the problem was. "It's a circle. It rotates, and all the arrows are pointing down now." I clasp my head with my hands. "Sounds really obvious when I say it out loud." In fairness, my testing had primarily involved pushing boxes along a street and throwing people off of buildings.

I look away, letting the power dwindle to nothing after a minute of increasingly weak wobbles. If anyone else had seen me do that, I would be mortified. That was the kind of flop that got memed about on PHO for years on end. That could have been the end for me and my reputation online. But now I knew. And, the more I thought about it - the more I could see the value in it. I could still get the shoving effect on a flatter surface that wouldn't spin around - but this would let me power gears and wheels in the future. My in-the-works glider could have a bunch of forward-facing arrows attached to it, and it wouldn't screw with the steering or controls in any way.

Hell, if I could find a ranged weapon with a large enough bolt - I could extend the range massively without ever sacrificing stability, so long as the arrows were straight. Or a melee weapon that could swing or thrust with unexpected force at the flick of a switch - the delayed-activation nature of the power meant that I could set it up far in advance on something of my choosing, then activate it mid-fight after cycling through my other powers as needed.

I reapply the arrows again, this time pointing each of them into the next, following the curve of the wheel to ensure that it would rotate, rather than complete a quarter-revolution and then fruitlessly hammer into the ground. This time, it shoots off like a rocket - slamming into a nearby wall and then spinning flat on the ground ceaselessly until I let it fade away once more. I might have a bit of trouble keeping it in a straight line for the real deal, but it didn't really matter if it was slightly off-target - any slight touch of the massive kinetic fields that acted as walls would be sufficient to send it flying and attract Skidmark's attention.

Distraction set-up and operational, I race back to the entrance. No sign that Skidmark had noticed anything abnormal yet. I mentally send the signal to activate Skidmark's power. I had a choice here. Speed-state, and be faster and more likely to dodge - at the expense of being frozen in place once I left, with potentially lethal consequences? Or, don't use the speed-state, be slower - but be able to use Glory Girl's forcefield, my shadow-state charges, my Clockblocking effect, Vista's space warping and spawning my ash clone right on top of my opposition inside the bunker.

Considering the weight of powers on one side, and my general dislike of Velocity, it feels like it should be a clear choice. But, that singular speed power meant a lot. Even if it made me fragile, it would turn the likely perilous series of traps into a simple blitz that might not even have time to trigger given my comparative lack of mass and sheer speed.

But then I'd be inside, locking eyes with Skidmark - and faced with the reality that I couldn't damage him, but the tiniest application of his power would absolutely hurtle me in any way he liked. And if I dropped the powerset, I'd be frozen long enough for him to just throw me aside with ease anyway. With his power, giving him those brief moments to work with was the worst thing that I could do. In the previous challenge, I'd seen how fast he could fling me around if he concentrated his power in a small area - I'd be hurled outside and turned into a relativistic missile before I could so much as twitch a finger.

No speed-state then. If it wasn't for the added vulnerability of the form, I would try just wrapping myself around his body to try and outlast the forced paralysis - but I needed to focus on my core objectives. I wasn't aiming for the single-percent chance of winning, I was fact-finding. And that meant triggering these traps, and yes, probably dying horribly - all for the sake of making sure that my next attempt would go off without a hitch. Assuming I beat Squealer, that is. If not... well. I guess I'd have to try and see how far my own somewhat lacking engineering talents and Leet's Tinker abilities could take me in an area as beaten-down as this. Not far, I suspected - maybe if it was something I had some amount of innate talent at, but my crafting abilities were sadly restricted to the computer screen so leaning on Tinker powers was all I really had.

A thundering, crashing sound erupts in the distance - a mere second later, Skidmark acts exactly as expected by firing in the general direction that the noise came from. He couldn't see me, but that wasn't a problem with the firepower he was packing. I could already hear the distant rumble of buildings collapsing in on themselves between bursts of fire, and if I had actually been anywhere around there - I would be dead. But I'm not. I was in completely the opposite direction, sprinting for my life down the suspiciously empty corridor that his fields had left as an entrance.

Glory Girl's forcefield tanks the first hit from a hidden landmine, and I invest a charge from my shadow state into gliding past suspiciously disturbed patches of earth before I land on the paved surface of the actual entrance. The firing had stopped already, even before I had triggered the mine - which meant that he'd spotted me, or maybe had some kind of motion sensor? No, if that was the case - why hadn't he spotted me immediately in the first attempt when I was testing his fields? He would have no reason to set up one but not the other.

I bound over the tripwire at the doorway, memories of Parian's tricks making me paranoid at the glimmer found at ankle level. This was dangerous, and it had taxed some of my defensive measures - but perhaps this wasn't as terrible an approach as I had expected.

Then Skidmark arrives. Even if the entrance doesn't have any of his zones covering it, he still has a firing position at the centre of the room. He levels a pistol at me, three shots ringing out as I turn to shadow - and then take a moment to cower behind my Clockblocked-shirt, held loosely in front of me as a shield. My ash clone surges into life a few metres ahead of me, instantly dispelled in a single shot - and just as instantly reforming again. Good. Let him waste ammo and effort on that. I needed my shadow state charges back to close the gap, and the more he focused on my clone - the less likely he would be to just wall me out with a more focused use of his power.

And then I'm on fire.

Or, everything around me is on fire. I'm mostly okay myself, save for the torrent of fire pouring around every crease and crumple of the time-locked fabric in front of me - spilling onto the ground at my feet and racing off into the distance behind me. The momentary shift into my shadow state to simply process what the hell just happened costs me a precious charge, but I do get enough of an intangible glance during a brief pause in the assault to see that - yes. Skidmark just has a flamethrower sitting there. And not just a little one, but a true belcher of a contraption that was pouring out burning liquid at a riotous pace. The range on that must be absurd, given how light the 'cargo' was - the effect of his power could probably extend the range all the way down the street with ease. A true road of fire for anyone wanting to take the front door while Skidmark was in position to spot them. It showed my distraction had value, at least.

A series of explosions rips out behind me, the sea of flames setting off every explosive I'd dodged on the way in and then more traps that I'd escaped by simple blind luck. I ignore the lances of pain across my body. Shrapnel. Fragmentation grenades. Not lethal. Or, not yet - at least. Not enough to stop one foot from moving in front of the other, not enough to knock me unconscious - and therefore, not something that would stop me. It didn't matter if I was only going to bleed out in sixty seconds, so long as the adrenaline kept me going for now. More traps trigger ahead of me, their effects not even visible thanks to the torrent of fire blocking any view past my impromptu shield. Irrelevant. I was too close for that to be a problem now, I had freedom of movement once my shadow state charges returned - straight up, left, right, even down into the ground to spring up at him from below. I had options... so long as he wasn't looking at me to apply his power and send me flying to my death. That was what my clone was for. To be a distraction.

A task that it was failing at.

As for why? It wasn't because it was gone or dispelled. It wasn't even being suppressed by his power in the corner somewhere, which would have been perfectly understandable. It was jumping at him... and simple bouncing off. The sullen green glow of his Cape told the story. I didn't know he could do that, that was... horrible news, actually. If he could just deflect me at will, I'd need to land on him from above and snap his neck as the very first move of the fight in order to win. Now that was always my intention but... I'd been hoping that I would be heavily favoured in the melee if I could get that far.

I shift to Vista, shrinking space at an angle - shrinking the air at the entrance of the bunker to allow the solid walls to act as a shield instead. Not quite as effective as the original power would have been, Vista could have expanded the walls rather than shrinking the gap, an important distinction that would have blocked it off completely - but this version wasn't quite perfect. I couldn't shrink it so perfectly as to close the entrance entirely, or just raise the floor or widen the walls directly like the real Vista could - but it was at least enough that the splash of his weapon couldn't nearly splatter harmlessly around my shield - instead, it was settling on the ground of his own fortress. The smoke and rising flames would force him to stop, even if this place didn't seem flammable enough for him to actually need to escape.

"What a fucking pain." I grouse, a heavy tension in my voice that I know comes from raw, unadulterated agony. My feet are burning. No, worse than burning. Burnt. I'd already gone past the stage of being able to identify actual feedback from them anymore, which was a good thing - acknowledging the phantom screaming from that part of my body and actually looking at the damage was the worst thing that I could do. I could still stand, that was enough. Everything would be reset once I won or lost here. I just needed to do my best.

Fine then. Even if grappling was out, he'd made a kill-zone himself. Simply knocking him into his own fields would be utterly lethal, regardless of any defensive measures he took. The moment I judge that I have enough cover from the smoke, I dive sideways into the wall with my shadow state, then upwards - erupting from halfway up the wall with a flying punch from what I was hoping was his blind spot. I didn't need much. He was manton-limited, as long as I made contact with his skin, I could convert any hit or daze into a full-bodied throw.

Unfortunately, he must have predicted the move or had already utterly neutralised my ash clone. He's locked onto me from the second I emerge. Surprisingly, Skidmark doesn't backpedal. Or dodge. Or try to retarget either of his guns. Or even to just use his power to send me flying with ease. Instead, he seems to welcome the blow - one hand rising up to meet me in exchange.

Perhaps it's the rustling of air beating against my face in a room that should have been perfectly still, perhaps it's a honed battle instinct - but I realise that I'm dead a full second before it happens. I should have been more patient, recharged Glory Girl's power while Vista brought me time - because as I'm falling, I have just enough time to realise that the back of Skidmark's gloved hand should be black instead of green - and that if he could apply his power to his Cape in a pinch, then why couldn't he apply it to his lone glove for hours on end?

FAILURE​

I don't even register the sensation of his glove touching my face. Instead, I skip straight to an out-of-body experience to watch my headless body slump to the ground - a bloody trail in the air indicating the direction that my head had been blasted in by a field the exact strength of the impenetrable walls that surrounded this place. If I squinted, I could just about make out the dot in the distance slowly falling out of its arc - and then the simulation starts to shut down.

"...he could do that the entire time?" I eventually mutter, still in half-disbelief at the fact. On one hand, it still felt a little embarrassing to lose to Skidmark again - but I was also feeling pretty vindicated right now. My years of battleboarding hadn't gone to waste. Once I beat up Skidmark and reformed him into a cute girl, I would have so much ammunition to go into old powerscaling threads with proof that I was right the entire time.

"-the fuck are you gawking at?" I barely refrain from wrinkling my nose. Still. 'Cute girl' was one thing that the current Skidmark was certainly not. Odious, repulsive and undeniably dangerous - not because of any threat that he might use his power like the bloodlusted simulation had, but because he was violent and unhinged even before the drugs in his system had anything to say about it. "Get moving, shit for brains."

"Yes, boss." I mime a salute and catch up with him where I'd fallen behind.

That application of his power... could I do that? Was I a Brute now? I'd already considered the possibility of enhanced weaponry, but I'd just assumed that the Manton limit would cover clothing in the same way that Clockblocker's did - and I hadn't really had the opportunity to test it to find out anything to the contrary. Assuming I could do that... well. I'd have to commit to either offence or defence. The nature of the power encouraged stacking effects as much as possible over the same area, there was no point slowing down a punch by 5% all over my body - but if a small bit of preparation could turn a gloved fist into a point-blank kinetic blast at will - or if I could turn a bracer into something capable of warding off retaliatory blows to defend one side of my body...

Lots of potential. I'd overlooked the potential in the first level of his power, assuming that I would need further challenges to get anything seriously useful. I wouldn't quite be able to match Skidmark's feat. My current power wouldn't let me stack effects to that extent, but if I concentrated everything into a small surface area - I already knew how lethal a normal punch could be in the right place. The ability to send someone flying into a wall, or off a roof, that could win fights all on its own.

"You." Skidmark finally makes his way to the 'bar', if that's what you could call the hastily set-up area. "You. What the fuck is this?" A glass is swept off the counter and hurled into the man's face. He reels back, his face a mask of confusion as the glass shatters on the ground.

"Who-, uh, Skidmark." The man's instinctual surge of anger dies out as recognition dawns in his eyes. "Can I, uh, help you?"

"Don't act any more stupid than you already are." He gestures at the shattered glass and the droplets of liquid pooling on the floor next to crates of plastic-wrapped boxes. "Who put you up to this?"

"I- I don't know what you mean." The bartender is quick to shake his head. "Is there a problem? I can pass on feedback to our suppliers-"

"Problem?" Skidmark laughs, and the sound grates at my ears. "The problem is that this shit's not even close to what we paid for. You think I'm stupid, huh? Think I can't tell if somebody's trying to screw me over? Someone starts serving basic shit as soon as Skidmark throws a party for all the big names in the Merchants, it obviously reflects badly on me. So. Who put you up to it? Give me names."

The man shakes his head. "I don't- I haven't a clue what you-"

Skidmark makes a gesture to me. A simple, to-the-point motion that leaves no room for argument about what he wants. Violence. Fortunately, it's something I have no problem with providing. After all, regardless of this guy's position - he was a gang member too. Profiteering off of drugs and crime... and I fully intended on breaking the gang as a whole today if I could. What did it matter if I took one of them out a little early for the boss?

The man doesn't seem to register my presence until I've already slid over the counter and my fist is already buried into his gut before he realises the danger. Four seconds from start to end. And I made it look good in the process. Smooth.

I shift in place as Skidmark presses the man's face into the table harshly. "We're the fucking Merchants. Nobody stops me from leaving, but the stern gaze of the door guards as I pass them is enough to prove the words of my 'colleagues' true. Just... had to find them. An incorrect assumption. This entire part of town was basically a dumping ground. No wonder the Merchants had felt safe setting-up shop here. I glance around at my surroundings as I pace past a half-dozen likely candidate locations.

Mush

Merchant Affiliate 1/5

(HUNT)​

I stop dead, keeping my gaze firmly locked in place - as if the challenge box might fade away to nothing if I glanced to the side. Which, for all I knew, it might.

Because I didn't see anyone right now.

I was pretty sure I was just looking at a mound of rubbish.

Slowly, I look to the left. Some knocked-over bins. But more importantly...

Mush

Merchant Affiliate 1/5

(HUNT)​

...also registering as 'Mush'.

As far as my interrogations had been able to gather, Mush was a Changer - but more in the, shaker kind of variety. Changer in terms of threat, but shaker in terms of mechanics. They form tendrils of power to pull trash and loose debris to themselves to bulk themselves up with the worst kind of power armour I've ever seen. Was my power identifying anything that Mush currently had control over, as his actual body? That was interesting. And, I suppose, not entirely unusual. It wasn't like I needed to lay eyes on skin specifically - full-body costumes and partial-glimpses of a person were enough to work with. Really, if all of this trash was something that would move with Mush the moment he flexed a muscle, what made it so different to seeing Armsmaster in power armour? A larger gap than normal between the 'main' body and what I was looking at? My power didn't seem to care.

And I wasn't going to complain. Not only did it tell me that I was actually in the right place, it meant that I didn't have to go searching for the kind of dangerous hobo that was the type to actually want to hang around here. In the heart of his power, no less. He was probably on drugs, and regardless of my escape options - I didn't want to test out how fast and hard he could weaponise the trash-laden streets around me.

"Challenge." I whisper.

HUNT was a simple modifier. Once he saw me, he got a free 'radar' on me for the rest of the round. I'd never be able to lose him or sneak up on him, no matter the distance.

But fortunately, it wasn't paired with ALRT. He didn't get the 'free' alert at the start to aggro him on me, which meant that - until I was spotted naturally - his modifier wouldn't do a thing. And even when it did, so long as I didn't intend on running away - it wouldn't help him there either.

Our new arena seems to be much like the street we were on in real life. Run-down buildings, trash sprawled across the street and the general lack of care that just summed up the 'bad' side of Brockton Bay. My first priority is to slither my way directly up onto a rooftop. My optimal start here would be to get the jump on him, and that meant staying out of his line of sight and certainly not touching any trash that he might have under his control - incorporated into his personal armour yet or not. I knew from personal experience that the rooftops of the Bay tended to be pretty clean in that respect, and it was rare to start a challenge on a street and have the target hiding out inside a random house unless they had obvious guards. Most likely, Mush was lurking in his natural habitat. Just needed to find him again, this time - without the benefit of my power lighting him up for me.

Easier said than done. But, if all else failed - simply making enough of a ruckus would have him shambling towards me with murder in his eyes. I'd lose the chance to ambush him, but that wasn't a guaranteed loss. I was actually kind of confident - but, not so confident that I'd throw away a potential edge. If Mush became hostile to my continued presence in real life, this might be one of the only easy chances I had to make him 'friendly' - to say nothing of the fact that I might never get back into the party to link up with Skidmark and Squealer.

Just needed to find the guy, preferably without leaving the rooftops and exposing myself. I was confident enough by now that people never really looked up unless you made too much noise, and this challenge had been fortunate enough to include the thrum of distant traffic and chirping of birds. I wasn't worried about a single footstep being detected from across the street, as some challenges loved to do to me.

Of course, I had a plan. An idea. I could probably assume that he was sitting in a trash mound somewhere. Maybe a dumpster. Whatever.

See, part of the fun of spending too much time on PHO was theorycrafting about the absolute limits of powers. The points where they manifested, the ways in which they arbitrarily hit their limits and stopped working. Usually, such discussions didn't go anywhere - but when I actually had the powers in hand to test, I had all sorts of ideas to actually test my powers on. Vista was a great example. The limts of this first level were clear on paper. I could only condense or stretch 'empty' space and air, one 'use' at a time, manton-limited, sight-based and the effect would slowly unravel on its own from the first second. Pretty simple.

But then you dig deeper. You look at examples of how it fails, why it fails - what it does when it fails for one reason versus another. And when answering the age-old question of 'Is it really Manton-limited or does it work if I don't actually know I'm affecting a human?' I had found an interesting discrepancy.

Attempt to pinch space with an object blocking the middle? The power takes effect only up until it hits the object. It pinches the half on this side, and then stops as if I had targeted the end point at the blocking object.

Try to pinch space with a human in the middle? Nothing. An instant failure. Something that I'd discovered pretty quickly when trying to weaponise Vista's power to help me sneak in punches with a bit of extra reach. Nothing stopped me from trying again, with a more specific target - but that split-second was crucial in a fight.

I digress. The point was that my power treated the 'errors' differently. Which meant that, so long as I could see and target a point beyond the trash cans and dumpsters my target was likely hiding in - I had a radar of sorts. If Vista's power attempted to pinch the air up to the target, my enemy wasn't inside. And if it failed completely? I had my man.

Finding the best angle to work with, I line my finger up to the first oversized pile of refuse waiting on the street, and give Vista's power a nudge. Just the slightest application. It would be terrible if I found the guy but blew my advantage by being too overt. I didn't need to shrink the distance in half, I just needed it to fail or not fail. The actual effect was as minimal as I could make it at this distance - and if I had to describe it, I would say that I was just applying italics to the air. Not too dissimilar to a simple summer haze, a slight distortion if you happened to look at the right angle - but you would sooner ascribe the fleeting, out-of-focus image to bleary eyes than an actual parahuman ability.

Of course, with the effect being so minimal - the effect was swiftly undone before I even lined the next target up. And for once, the simple fact that I couldn't affect a real substance directly was working to my benefit. He might notice if I started moving his trash around, but unless he started moving - he was never going to notice the tiny lines of slightly-off space hanging in the air, even if they were right next to him.

I rotate in a spiral, checking each waste pile, dumpster and discarded trash bin around me before moving on to ones further afield. "I've got a habit of piling things up in my sleep, or when I'm just lazing around. Landlords don't like it, and I guess those guys managed to work it out when their nice, pretty car park turned into something like this overnight." She makes an annoyed sound. "You'd think that I'd get some premium 5-star accommodation as a signing bonus with the Merchants, but all I get are warnings from Squealer that she'll fire me out of her tank if I ever try to sleep in her workshop. That's crazy, right? They should be treating me better, don't you think?"

I attempt a sympathetic smile. "Maybe they don't trust you that much yet? You've only been a Merchant for, what, two days? I'm sure once you prove yourself-"

"Five weeks!" She complains.

I blink. What. "Weren't you fighting Skidmark and Squealer just this weekend?"

"That was just-" She waves a hand in the air. "Disagreements over my working conditions. Skidmark had been calling me a freeloader and a waste of space ever since they pulled me out of that one bind with the ABB I mentioned, and once every other gang in the city started fighting each other - he figured now was a good time to tell Squealer to point a tank at me and make a big show of recruiting me to the cause in front of everyone."

I tilt my head. That was... a very different story to what PHO had guessed at. "And were you? A freeloader, I mean?"

"No!" She protests. "I just hadn't done anything yet, and he seemed to resent that I was eating and living around them without needing to lift a finger."

This time, I don't even need to say anything.

"Okay, okay. Maybe that sounds a little like freeloading." She allows. "But that's the nature of the job! I agreed to show up for Cape fights, but nobody is interested in fighting the Merchants - it's a sweet deal for me! I'm living up to my end of the bargain, he's the one in the wrong here!"

I scratch my chin. "Would Skidmark say the same thing if I asked him for his version of events?"

"Ehhh." She pulls a face. "He's not the type to admit when he's in the wrong- wait, that was a hypothetical, right? You're not actually going to snitch on me?" She affixes me with a pleading gaze. "Please? I'll admit it. I was wrong. I'll change my ways. I'll put my life back together. Starting from tomorrow. Thank you for your insight, kind sir-" She tries to tug the lid of the trash can out of my hand - a weak, but insisting motion as if the conversation was now over and she was trying to ineffectually slam the door on me.

"I think tomorrow might be a bit too late." For me. Even if Skidmark didn't think much of my decision to find Mush - even if he threw me out over some perceived slight - any momentary contact with Squealer, on top of the second-chance at a challenge once Skidmark inevitably showed the pair off to the wider crowd - that would be more than worth it as a parting gift.

"No~" She groans softly. "I don't wanna. He's just going to shout at me and complain, and I'll actually have to talk to people and it will just be a complete disaster all around. Let's just leave it here, you pretend that you never saw me - we both leave happy."

"I think you'll be the only happy one in that scenario." I cross my arms. "Look at it this way, show up once now and look good as a card-carrying member of the Merchants - and he'll never be able to have a good reason to come and beat you up for slacking again without looking like he's lost control."

Mush considers that for a moment. "That's a good point. That's really smart actually. I could do that. There can't be that many people at the party anyway, right? A few dozen people at most, I can just walk past and nobody will pay any attention to me."

"A few hundred, maybe." I cough quietly. "But it's not like they'll make it their mission to get in your way or anything. Nothing to worry about."

"...nope. It's over." She tries to close the lid on herself again. "Tell Skidmark I'm dead. I leave all that I own to the first person to claim my stuff. Throw my body into the sea, at least the fish might appreciate me-"

This girl might be hopeless. "I'm going to roll you to Skidmark in that thing at this rate."

"That could work." Somehow, she's seriously considering that idea. "I just stay in here, and you just sneak me inside and you can tell Skidmark that I was always around and that there's no need to go looking for me. And I won't need to show my face to anyone. Everyone wins." She nods at me. "You're really smart." She tries to close the lid again. I keep my hand firm.

"Are you scared of people seeing you in there? I'd have thought you would be something of a celebrity to them." I cough. "Us, I mean." Supposed to be a Merchant right now.

"Maybe, but I'm just- I'm not much of a party animal. I'd probably just bring the mood down, and I was kind of happier on my own anyway." It's not like I can't sympathise, being an introvert was second-nature to me until my power gave me the chance to win at a real life harem eroge. "I'm... a bit of a mess, I can admit that much. People can kind of tell at a glance, and I just... don't really like that kind of attention? People expect a lot from Capes, and I don't really... have that kind of presence." She makes a pitiful expression. Or, a more pitiful expression than her default one, at least.

"Kind of sounds like you're scared to me." She winces at that. "But, I don't really get it. You're a Cape. You don't need to wander around trying to look intimidating while looking like a regular girl."

And a thoroughly unintimidating one at that. When you looked at Sophia, or even Taylor - you could see the relative fitness and combat capabilities that they had. Not quite a much for me in pure physical matchups, but I wouldn't bet against them in a random encounter on the street. Mush was... me. The old me. Except also female. The sedentary, lazy lifestyle obviously didn't involve any trips to the gym or combat training. Thin and reedy - borderline anorexic, to the point where it looked like she might lose to a stiff breeze if it wasn't for the protection of her personal trashcan on all sides. I doubted her appearance was down to any attempt at a diet or personal discipline, I was rather suspicious that she was just skipping meals to avoid having to interact with people or leave her post.

I continue. "Why don't you just show up as, well, Mush? Nobody's going to argue or look down on you if you're a giant suit of metal and plastic twice their height."

"Skidmark will yell at me for making a scene." She leans her head back against the edge of her trashcan, eyes closing as if she was about to fall asleep. I let my gaze slide downwards at the opportunity, noting with some approval that her shirt was certainly a few sizes too big for her - despite her evident curves, the material just hangs too loosely for me not to notice. Nice.

"I think you making a scene is exactly what Skidmark is hoping for. He wants to show off the power of the Merchant's Capes right now, so showing up and showing off to the regulars is exactly the kind of thing he wants to see." Probably. Maybe.

"You think so?" She considers that for a moment. "Then... I wouldn't even have to show my face. I could just-" The bin rises up into the air as tendrils race out from the sides of the trashcan, two rudimentary legs being used to push upwards before the materials have even finished gathering. "-go like this-" A makeshift claw firmly takes the trashcan lid from my hand, returning it to its usual place - only for the girl inside to pop it slightly ajar, leaving only her eyes visible as her construct grows, selectively gathering and splitting off sturdier materials to weld into the larger body with casual ease. A metal sheet is shorn in two with contemptuous ease, both halves then rising up to conceal the 'torso' where her trashcan and real body resided. "-and nobody will be able to see me."

I angle my head upwards to peer at her. "I think people will still be interested in where the voice is coming from, but, yeah - that looks good to me."

"I'm not going to be talking to them." Her voice booms. No wonder I didn't twig she was female when she was still inside. The way that echoed throughout the structure really hid the nervous, higher pitch if you weren't looking for it. "Because you're going to be doing all the talking for me."

"I don't remember saying that." Not that I was opposed to it, I was a genuine social butterfly these days - and it wouldn't even be strange for the Merchants to see me trailing around yet another Cape at this stage.

"It was when you said you didn't want to go back to Skidmark empty-handed." She tells me, an unmistakable smug hint in her voice that tells me that this is her best attempt at being spiteful. Subjecting someone else to what was apparently her idea of hell.

I raise my hands in mock-surrender. "Fine, fine. If that's what you really want - I can do the talking in your name. You'll have to make appropriately threatening gestures though, the guards were pretty happy to see me leave and they seemed to be looking forward to not letting me back in." I shake my head as she doesn't respond to that, doubtless considering leaving me out to dry out of spite for dragging her out of here. "-which would leave you to face Skidmark all alone-"

"I won't let that happen." She assures me hastily. "We're in this together, you know?"

"Never doubted it." I drawl. "Now, time to go."

Somehow managing to convey body language even through her constructed body, she makes a forlorn shrug of her 'shoulders' and begrudgingly pilots the legs of her new body around the broken piles of materials that she'd been staying in - not seeming fazed when one pile collapses under the weight. However strange it looked, it was the same principle as my version of the power - it wasn't a knight. Or a mech. It was a tendril dressed up to look and act like a mecha - but it didn't entirely act like something that weighed that much did. It wasn't a Tinker's toy, this was a Changer - and future challenges would probably highlight that distinction if I got too comfortable exploiting the weakpoints of her chosen armoured body.

She half-turns, just to make sure I'm following - then sets down the path. I trail behind, eyes locked on the challenge box floating next to the hulking giant.

Mush

Merchant Affiliate 3/5

(CAGE) (PREP)​

The third challenge tended to have pretty sizable cooldown timers between each failure, and not knowing how long Skidmark would continue to allow my presence - there was a good chance that I might not get a second attempt while undercover. Better to make it count, but the strategy I used last time won't be nearly as effective in a CAGE environment. My ash clone won't be able to hide itself or its actions as effectively, it wasn't great at defending or dodging most of the time - it's longevity in fights usually came from the counter-intuitive cooldown, where the quicker it gets taken out, the shorter the downtime is for me to resummon it. But any resummoning, complete with handing off the administrator status again on top of Mush's powerset - would start from scratch every time as Mush reincorporates any scrap that gets stolen.

I could do it myself, but it wasn't the most human-friendly power in the first place - and my need to swap away my active power to survive would eventually cause the same issue.

I'd still try. Of course I would. But I'd do so when I'd tried everything else first. Anything that would give me an edge in a fight I expected to be heavily weighted against me. Skidmark. If I could level up his power, just to some modicum of the power that he used against me - that could send a grown man flying with a look - it was a power practically built for CAGE modifiers. Nowhere to run, no tricks to pull - just constant, unrelenting force. Invincible, once the set-up was complete. And, of course, I was hoping that Squealer was the key to solving Skidmark's current challenge. It all tied together.

And Mush was leading me straight to them.

Or, would be leading me - if she hadn't frozen up at a challenge from a patrolling guard at the outer barrier of the compound.

"Get out of the way, idiot!" I swagger up to the guards as they look undecided as to whether they should challenge the approaching giant or not. "You think Mush wants anything to do with you?"

"Is that really Mush?" One guard peers upwards. "I know there was a new Cape around, but I haven't been told much about them-"

"What does that matter? Are you going to get in the way, or is she going to have to step on you?" Behind me, metal shifts and creaks ominously.

"Easy, man. I'm just- just doing my job." He backs down, seeming aggrieved by my attitude. Good. It wasn't the same guards from earlier, but I could hardly resist the opportunity to ham things up and watch them squirm. "Supposed to check on everyone coming in, and why. It's not all that serious."

"And your job is waylaying one of the only Capes the Merchants have? Does it look like Mush wants to talk to someone like you? Why do you think that they're so quiet, even now?" I lean in. This is fun. "It's because they're struggling. Struggling to contain the bloodlust they feel towards this upstart with a peashooter, that thinks he's capable of stopping even this small fraction of their true strength! I'm trying to save your life here man. Mush, I know them well. And they're not the conversational type. They're the kind to kill you on a whim, they're crazy - you don't want to spend any more time than you have to around them. Why else do you think Skidmark usually keeps them away from everyone else? Even he's nervous about it."

The man looks nervous, perhaps weighing up the mood swings and violent tendencies of Skidmark, and considering the possibility that this one might just be just as bad or worse. "You can go through." He steps aside quickly.

I march onwards. I make it around the next corner, then about five metres before a clawed hand picks me up gently - dangling me in the air, turning me to face Mush eye-to-eye. A very teary, pouty set of eyes.

"You-" She looks like she wants to strangle me. "What are you even saying-" She chokes out. "What does that guy even think of me now, what's he going to tell all of his friends!?"

"That he and all of his buddies should avoid dragging you into small talk for no reason." I respond innocently. "You're welcome. I'm full of good ideas, I know."

"That last bit was fine, the rest of it-" She shakes me in the air from side-to-side. "What was that?"

"Well, you could explain the misunderstanding to them if you want." I grin. "Or, you could just take it as a win that the next time Skidmark sends someone to get you - everyone's going to be real invested in getting lost along the way."

"I'll get you back for this." She promises me ominously. The effect is slightly lost thanks to the embarrassed flush in her expression and the hint of furious tears in her eyes.

I shrug. Maybe I got a bit carried away. I saw an opportunity to fuck with her, I had to take it. "Whatever. Skidmark should be- well. He was in that building, but he went to talk to Squealer, so I suppose he's in there now?" I point out the connected buildings. "But, I don't think you'll fit through the entrance without getting out of that thing."

Her entire body stiffens at that. "I don't know if we need to do all of that. I'll just squeeze in to the garage like one of Squealer's vehicles."

"I think those doors are pretty firmly closed-" I start. And... she's already gone. I hurry after her to catchup, issuing threats and warnings to every curious partygoer that scatters at the approaching Cape's approach.

She arrives at the garage doors blocking the way to Squealer's temporary workshop, and with a flex of her arms - forces them open, the screeching protest of metal causing the onlookers to wince and cover their ears, even as she ducks into the entrance she's forced into the garage - with me lurking just outside, trying to get a peek inside without being spotted in turn. Just a single glance at Squealer, and I wouldn't even have to deal with an irate Skidmark annoyed at me making decisions for myself - I could go back to the club and plead ignorance. It wasn't like Mush knew my name or anything.

I draw close just in time to hear the occupants of the room greet Mush.

"You fucking moron! I told you that if you ever set foot into my workshop again, I'd fire you out of the cannon to get you to leave - and what do you do, you charge in and start breaking things! Look at what you're standing on. I spent ages on that! How are you going to fix it?" A mumbled response isn't quite audible to me. "No, you know what? You'll just make it worse by trying. Just get out. You have five seconds, then I get the tank ready."

"Don't you dare move a fucking muscle Mush!" Skidmark roars. "Where the fuck have you been? I explicitly ordered you to show up today, and what do I discover but you sneaking back out the moment I turn my back. I barely expected anything out of you anyway, but surely even a shitstain like you can appreciate showing up when you're supposed to - and not turning one of my parties into a freakshow by showing up and acting like this? What's the point of the stupid fucking suit? Get out of that shit and explain yourself-"

"I- I- I-" Mush half-turns, and suddenly I'm grabbed from my hidden position next to the entrance - abruptly put on display right in front of Squealer and Skidmark. "It's all his fault! He told me to do it!"

I give her a wounded look over my shoulder. She's ducked completely into her trashcan to avoid meeting my gaze. I turn back to the angry-looking Skidmark, and the somehow-even-angrier woman at his side - who now seems content to transfer all of her irritation at Mush towards me instead. I glance down at Mush's foot, the flattened remains of a motorbike of some description has already been sheepishly pushed away by Mush - but it's easy to see that the damage won't be easily fixed.

I let out a quick laugh. There went the plan of being discrete, but this wasn't so bad either. Skidmark. Squealer. Mush. All in one place. An opportunity for me, this exact situation was what I'd been hoping for this entire time.

And so long as my real-life body could survive the three accusing stares full of blame, I'd be making it out of here like a bandit.

"H-hey boss." I give Skidmark a nervous-looking grin. "Thought I'd show some initiative, go find the missing member. Not a bad job, right? The gang is all together again." I spread my arms wide as much as I can, which wasn't far with Mush still firmly holding me in place. "No need to thank me."

Skidmark takes a long look at me with an expression of growing fury. Then at the shattered remains of Squealer's work. Then at the gaping hole in the workshop that a few dozen Merchants were curiously peering through. Then at the towering figure behind me that was trying to use me as a meatshield. Then back to me again.

"You're fired."

Alas. The job market sure is tough these days. No appreciation for the real go-getters.
