"You're fired."

I almost chuckle at Skidmark's declaration. Good comedic timing, really highlighting the absurdity of the situation and breaking the tension with a quick one-liner. Then, I remember that this was Skidmark and he probably wasn't cracking a joke. He was probably serious. Or as close to it as he could get without actually shooting someone. I drop the smile before he can notice my reaction.

Focus up, Greg. It's easy to get arrogant and complacent. Easy to think that everyone in this room was a future ally, that even if the rest of the evening didn't result in much success - that all three of the Merchant's Capes would soon be a trio of buxom women falling over themselves to serve me. But even if that might be true, these people were all criminals first. Uber and Leet barely qualified for the label - despite my disguise as one of their goons, all three of the people here were closer to Oni Lee than they were to Leet. Still a good deal clear from him, to be sure - but criminals nonetheless. People who had not only survived, but ultimately thrived in the cutthroat, treacherous underworld that they had made into their home.

So. Don't get too cocky. In all likelihood, Skidmark could shoot me right now and nobody would blink an eye at my 'death' - at least, until my forcefield took them by surprise. I'd completed challenges on Mush to 'upgrade' her - and the fact that it was 'her' was a bit of a surprise. One that I wasn't sure about what it could mean. Was it just that my powers had prioritised making them into someone I might have some interest in, and gone straight for the drastic changes that usually would come later? It had been the earliest that I'd seen such a conversion, but then again... the original Mush was probably the ugliest fucker I'd seen yet. So maybe that tracked.

But I would be stupid to just assume that it was a gift from my power. Not when my power was so willing to throw me under the bus at other times. However much her personality was quietly amusing, no matter how much I appreciated that she was very much a woman under all of that scrap and steel - and however much more enjoyable she was to be around compared to her original counterpart likely would have been - this wasn't free. My power didn't do handouts like that for something that I would have done anyway. As a working assumption for now, I'd have to guess that the radical changes to her personality and body were balanced out by a general lack of loyalty or any extra friendliness towards me. Other 'strangers' that I had challenged tended to go from neutral acquaintances to clear 'friends' after a challenge - and only later on in the challenge lists did the more extreme changes occur. I could consider this as a simple re-ordering by my power, which would probably indicate that Mush wouldn't be stepping in to shield me anytime soon.

Evidence in point: Her decision to throw me to the wolves and use me as a shield for herself instead. In some ways, this was the worst outcome from my power in a purely pragmatic sense. Yes, one extra girl in the scene - and I was happy for that - but at the same time, I was surrounded by three enemies. Saved only by the fact that they didn't know that I was an enemy yet. If it came down to a fight... Mush would almost certainly side against me.

Something about that grated. The idea that I could pick a fight with Skidmark or go and beat on some random drug-dealers, and one of my girls would side with them? That was the trick in thinking. It would be hard to get annoyed at the idea of opposition from the gangly, warped man that I had glimpsed during the challenges - in the same way that I didn't really feel anything about the idea of Skidmark fighting me. But Squealer? The new Mush? I was already considering them as mine. I could already half-picture the two kneeling in front of me, each taking their turn to worship my cock as the other provides updates on the status of the Merchant's to their new leader-in-the-shadows.

And instead, they'd follow Skidmark? Skidmark?!

Maybe my power knew me too well. Because that thought burned hotter and harder than anything else so far today. Not the ignoble defeat against an aspect of the man's power I wasn't ready for, not the casual insults he heaped on me as I played the part of assistant - but the idea that one of my girls might side with him over me? That stung. Too effective. To the point that it felt deliberate. Like a toxic game mechanic, just goading you into getting mad about something that you could fix if you played a little bit more. I could almost feel the challenge from my power, I could visualise it - as if it was right next to me, wearing my face with a mocking smile. 'Don't like the idea? Mad about it?' That's what I would say. 'Then why don't you go and do something about it?'. Just win another two challenges to try and sway them to my side instead. Just handle Skidmark, and then breed the needy slut that remained behind as one last act of spite towards the pride and legacy of the man who dared to lay claim to something that was mine.

I shift slightly, trying to keep any expression off of my face. Not the flash of murderous hatred. Not the ghost of a smile at the humour I found in Skidmark's not-joke. And certainly not any hint at the strain in my pants at the thought of what the three other Capes in this room might look like and do once I was done with them.

Lock in. Stop getting distracted. Stop feeling nervous about the possibility of failing a challenge and just try it.

First of all. Not getting kicked out. Or, at least, delaying getting kicked out. Now, it wasn't like I was actually interested in a career in the Merchants or even staying here for long at all - but making a bad impression and getting thrown out early could only be a bad thing. My power liked to build on existing relationships where it could, twisting and morphing what was already there as a preference. It wasn't like my power set a relationship to a certain level of friendship, it just... morphed something about them into something more palatable to me. Just as it was theoretically possible for someone to fall in love with me without a single challenge, it must be equally possible for someone to despise me so much that they still dislike me several challenges later. Sophia was still dishonest about her feelings, even to this day - and I had zero doubts that if I were to falter or humiliate myself somewhere, she would be too busy laughing and gloating to help me up.

I hadn't tested how possible it was to make a true enemy out of the people that I had fully 'cleared'. If I just treated Emma or Madison like trash continuously for no reason, would they come to resent me? Or were there high opinions of me being continually nudged by my power even now? I didn't truly know. Which was why I wasn't entirely sure if I was 'safe' to fuck this up or not. Even ending up with a case like Sophia would be a mess, I just didn't have the same level of reliable access to these people to ensure that their thoughts went in the direction I wanted - and without a talkative and all-too-honest challenge-self to talk to, I didn't have a great insight into their personalities either.

And that was saying nothing about the fact that this disguise wasn't real. Taylor, at least, was evidence that the general 'tug' in my direction would persist regardless of which identity I progressed the challenge under - but unlike Taylor, I wouldn't be starting from a neutral position when my power started to influence them. I would be a hero, their explicit enemy. Or, as Greg Veder, I would be an irrelevant non-Merchant with no reason to ever interact with their lives as Capes. Even if, through a stroke of luck, I was able to become 'friends' in this disguise - it would fall apart under any real scrutiny and that temporary bond would disappear the moment 'James' vanished for good. Or, worse - that bond wouldn't vanish and they might resist any advances by Greg and Void Cowboy because their old flame 'James' was still out there somewhere.

"Easy, boss." I smile winningly. "You'd already mentioned how you were looking for Mush. Figured I'd go ahead and grab her while you were talking. I didn't quite expect her to just bust down the side of the building like this, I was just planning to let her walk in and go back to waiting outside until she started dragging me along." I attempt to flex my shoulders to make a point. "Literally."

"Stop fucking talking." He snips at me. "I gave you one fucking job. To shut the fuck up, bark when I tell you to bark, do what I say and nothing more. You think I look at you now and see a real go-getter? No. I see someone that thinks they know better than me. Did I tell you to go find Mush? No. If I wanted you to get her, I would have said so. Don't you think so?" He sneers at my sheepish look of response. "Mush, tighten up that grip. I need to hear some sincerity from him." Mush shifts her grip slightly, but it doesn't feel any different. "I said TIGHTEN IT!" He practically screams the sentence out at her, flecks of spittle glinting in the air at the exclamation - immediately followed by all the wind leaving my lungs as Mush hastens to obey.

"G-got i-it. B-boss!" I wheeze out. Yep. Mush was definitely still on Team Skidmark once the chips were down. The camaraderie and jokes from earlier were real, but I could call it something similar to the friendships among the patrolling guards outside. Friends, yes. But if Skidmark told them to punch each other out for his personal entertainment, both sides knew that there wasn't really much of a choice.

So I'd try not to hold it against Mush. Not when I could practically feel the panicky shaking of her frame even through the layers of interconnected beams that kept us separate. Not when she'd loosened up almost immediately after getting the initial exclamation of discomfort out of me, the inner layer of her 'fist' remaining fixed in place even as the outer layer creaks ominously. A dramatic display for Skidmark's benefit... and a needless risk for her to take. Skidmark would be livid with her if he realised that I was actually breathing easier now than I was before he started screaming. All for someone that was still trying to do her best to not obviously glower impotently at me after the realisation that Skidmark never actually asked me to bring her here.

Not... a terrible person.

And that brought its own difficulties with it. If I could just write them off as evil, or know that they would be so utterly unrecognisable in a few challenges time that nothing I said or did really mattered - I could just act as I pleased in the most selfish way possible. And while I couldn't profess to be a saint or even to have selfless aspirations at all, I still liked to feel like I was kind of the good guy in all of this. Mush, even with her allegiance largely unchanged, already felt like 'my' girl in my head. If this all came to blows, did I really want to fight her just to keep up appearances? Not really. But I wasn't willing to just let Skidmark shoot me if he gets mad either, and I wasn't willing to sabotage 'Void Cowboy' and his heroic reputation by being overly soft against the Merchants.

It would be best if I could just solve it all here. We never attack the Merchants, because they all fall under my sway - right here and now. I wasn't arrogant enough to call it likely... but there was a chance.

A small one. I level a look at Squealer. The only one here that I hadn't challenged yet. And, generally speaking? I was getting pretty good at beating the first challenge for Capes these days without too many retries.

Squealer

Merchant Villain 1/6

(EVNT)​

...but that was probably the worst modifier I could see. It wasn't much of a surprise. She didn't strike me as the straight-up combat type. Even if she got the 'tank' I kept hearing about, I was very comfortable that I could outmanoeuvre its fire long enough to slip inside and kill her in close range. Assuming it wasn't some, Tinkertech monstrousity with homing missiles, fully-automated turrets and anti-gravity thrusters or something silly like that. A standard tank, with some extra juice somewhere - I could definitely handle that.

But an EVNT modifier - that was a different story. Killing her wasn't necessarily the condition. Given her speciality... a race? That definitely felt like her 'thing', and my power would have all-too-many real life examples to pull data from when spinning together the simulation. She did races constantly, whether to just test her rides, show off how she could leave the cops behind or just to keep the gangs busy angrily chasing after her while the rest of the Merchants ran away - PHO was full of footage showing Squealer in her element.

Naturally, I'd seen it all. Would that help here?

Maybe. Or maybe the EVNT modifier wouldn't even do a fraction of what I was suspecting it would. Only one way to find out. "Challenge."

Silver flashes through my vision before establishing itself into semi-familiar grey walls splattered with grime and graffiti. My vision is briefly wrested away from my body, the disconcerting feeling of a 'cutscene' playing as I zoom through...

...some very-clearly marked streets. A racecourse. I fucking knew it. I regain control of my body as it shows the 'start line' - a rusty-looking garage littered with half-dismantled vehicles and power tools.

THE GATES WILL UNLOCK IN SIXTY MINUTES.

PASS THROUGH ALL CHECKPOINTS BEFORE YOUR OPPONENT TO COMPLETE THE CHALLENGE

ENEMY PARTICIPANTS WILL GAIN ENHANCED PHYSICAL ABILITIES WITHIN THEIR DOMAIN BEFORE THE GATES OPEN

THE ENEMY PARTICIPANT WILL RESPAWN IF KILLED OR DISABLED​

A timer settles into the corner of my vision. Sixty minutes. Fifty-nine-fifty-nine. Fifty-eight.

Clearly, the intent was to give me - and presumably Squealer - time to cobble together a working machine out of the scrap around us, then use that to race. A test designed to favour Tinker abilities, rather than pure physical might. I didn't see Squealer here, but the distant sounds of clanging through the wall probably meant that she was just next door - already hard at work on her design.

Technically, with Leet - I had a Tinker ability. Technically. But I already knew that particular flavour of Tinker had some flaws to work around when working on big projects. And even if there weren't, Tinker's were like Thinkers - the powers were great, but they were a lot better when they could synergise with something that was already there. Leet's power wasn't shoving ideas into my brain and taking over, and I didn't have the natural talent to just dream up a design that would blow the specialist Tinker away in her own field. Not in a mere hour, anyway. What would I even make? Just because I knew that the teleportation pads or that one speedforce-like suit were theoretically possible, didn't mean that I could take the early levels of my variant of his power and match the efforts of what Leet could do with an entire workshop, a trained assistant, years of tools built up in their lab and weeks of work between each stream.

Even just visualising what I would need for a simple powered bike was a pain - a half-hearted sketch into the dusty floor at my feet sending alarm bells ringing as I run through it with Leet's power. Half a percent-chance for the power source to overload every time the steering was engaged. Two-percent chance for the brakes to lock up every ten seconds. More, minor things that wouldn't cause a major failure that I could ignore for now. I could see the workarounds, the ways to use those faults and take advantage of them - the surge in energy could top up a battery or energy supply somewhere if it could be harnessed. The brakes would fail because the cables were too close together in my hasty drawing - and the power would go into the accelerator instead for a massive boost. Useful, Leet would be thrilled at the opportunity to take advantage of that... but I didn't have the time, or the knowledge, to implement those extra features safely.

And then, even once those features were added - that was a new design. With new elements and 'quirks' that would suddenly appear. Finding a stable version to settle on probably took Leet multiple attempts and days of work at the best of times. I'd never seen them do a live Tinker-marathon or race like this, and it was pretty clear why.

But I couldn't just sit back and cry about it either. A powered vehicle that could beat Squealer was a step too far, too fast - fine. What did I have?

I consider my drawing, shaking my head before moving my hand over to wipe it out. My Tinker power lights up briefly, only to fade as I pull my hand away. I hover my hand back over the dirt drawing. It's ready to copy that design? I suppose I never had the chance to test if it worked on anything other than paper designs, thanks to that hefty cooldown on it. Did that mean I could pinch digital ones too? Not that Tinkers posted their work online that much, but if I could get into Armsmaster's lab... I could do something there. Hell, if I could find a way past the doors - I wouldn't even need to do it in person. The WRLD modifier had the kind of detail and fidelity I needed to get working passcodes and logins to half the PRT, why wouldn't Armsmaster's lab be the same? I'd never managed to get past the security before, but it couldn't be too hard with some dedicated effort - right?

Useless without Armsmaster's power to actually learn and use the designs. I remind myself of that one important fact. Getting ahead of myself.

I continue wiping away the design. Good to know, but this one wasn't going to work. Maybe if I had a few more hours - and I hadn't even considered if I actually had the materials my design wanted to hand. I wasn't going to out-Tinker the Tinker. So I needed a strategy.

First and foremost. I wasn't locked in here. Looking outside the only exit, the 'gates' were pretty obvious. It was basically a ZONE wall with a timer on it. But there was some space for me to move around outside this specific area and out into the city. Enough to roam around for more parts, or even try and set something up outside the garage if I needed. I wasn't allowed inside the 'start zone' yet, but exploration wasn't exactly forbidden.

Including Squealer's garage? Sabotage seemed a viable strategy. And not just by putting obstacles in her way. The challenge wouldn't need to give her 'enhanced' abilities in her area if it didn't need to protect her from me just... attacking her and stopping her from doing anything at all.

So, how enhanced was 'enhanced'? A minor Brute rating? Or something that would make Alexandria jealous? Because if I could stop her from making anything at all, then I could cruise to victory in my speed-state. Which I hadn't forgotten about. But fragility in that state aside, my speed-state was about as fast as a normal car cruising on a highway. Comparable to Glory Girl's top speed, and certainly more than fast enough to breeze past regular city traffic like it was standing still. Squealer wasn't going to be normal, and she certainly wasn't going to be obeying any speed limits.

From what I could approximate from the starting 'cutscene', I could probably clear the full track in under ten minutes with my speed-state. I'd be surprised if she couldn't whip something up that could do it in five if I left her alone. But the difference wasn't absurd enough to dismiss entirely. If I could just force her back to the start by killing her once, or destroy her original vehicle, that would be enough. I had a basic plan for that. Block her in with Clockblocked material to get a headstart, then I'd get one chance only to annihilate her car with a second round of time-locked string in an ambush later down the track before she overtook me for good.

That wasn't Plan A. That was Plan... D, or something. Because that was a gamble. If she dodged, or saw it coming, or had a powerful enough backup vehicle that she could scrounge together, or just took a route that I wasn't expecting - the challenge would be over. I'd never get another chance to get ahead of her and set up the trap at a high enough speed where it could stop her and shred her vehicle apart.

No. Plan A was simple. A betrayal of everything this challenge seemed designed to encourage. Something that probably wouldn't work in later challenges if this theme held true. My objective: To turn this into a foot race.

I phase through the wall rather look to navigate around the main entrance. Primarily to prove that I had escape options if the wall wasn't electrified, and also because it would be a lot harder for her to see me coming like this.

It's immediately obvious that whatever she's building, it's going to be a monster. Four engines have already been cannibalised and strung together at the back of her working area, and the shell of the design alone towers over both of us. If she wasn't a Tinker, I'd have labelled it as an over-designed monster truck and walked away confident that it would break down at the first corner. I knew better than to doubt Squealer in her own field.

This garage had more resources. More tools. More half-built vehicles to work with. I could deny her options, perhaps start ferrying things through the wall via my shadow state to stop her from completing her full design. But did I even know what I needed to take away? What, out of this entire workshop, was so critical to her design that it could not work without it? I didn't know. So that eliminated that option.

I could attack her vehicle directly, but my effectiveness wasn't guaranteed - Squealer was well-known for barely-working, lumped-together monstrosities. Far from the sleek, technical designs of Armsmaster - I doubted that doing my best to tear things off or phase screws into the engine would have the effect that it might have on a Tinker with... tighter specifications.

No. All of those things might help. And if I genuinely intended to match her in a Tinkering battle, or to construct something of my own - I might well have tried it. But I wasn't that good. Not done-in-sixty-minutes good. So the core part of my sabotage would be in the most vulnerable part of this vehicles construction: The builder.

"Get away from my ride, bitch!"

The tinker had just noticed my intrusion - and dashed towards me with a first-step that left an indent in the solid floor at her feet. Right. Physical boosts. I sway to the side, dipping and diving away from the untrained-yet-overpowered blows. A Brute rating, but not an absurd one. Yes, she just left a fist-sized imprint in concrete - but as was always the case, speed was the most important aspect. And even if she was faster, she wasn't fast enough to catch me through my host of defensive abilities.

Dip. Duck. Tilt head. If the timer was shorter, I could probably win like this. But constant dodging for sixty-minutes seemed like a tall order when every flailing strike threatened to decapitate me. Even if not for her Brute rating, I couldn't seriously fight her back either. The rules had warned that she would simply respawn if killed or disabled.

Hm.

Parian's power edges a loose thread from my shirt. I freeze it in place directly in the path of a haymaker. A wild, agonised scream emerges from her throat as she practically cleaves her arm in two - the offensive power of her new Brute rating apparently superior to the defensive aspect. To her credit, she keeps attacking. A crazed flurry of attacks that only worsens the blood loss, until even Brute-enhanced attacks slow to a relative crawl - as she limply collapses to the ground-

-only for a second Squealer to stomp over her disintegrating corpse with a bloodthirsty grin on her face and the same vigour that she started out with. No injuries on this one.

Good to know. Good to know. That would be the respawn the rules mentioned. It wasn't a surprise that it had happened, but the interesting part was the timing of when it happened - or rather, when it hadn't happened.

In the end, what did 'disabled' mean, exactly? My power hadn't used the term before in relation to me, but if I had to make an educated guess - I would say that it was some arbitrary line that prevented her from completing any of her objectives for the challenge. Death and unconsciousness obviously counted, and some scenarios were also a given - if I cut off all her limbs and threw her into a garbage bin, for example. She'd never be able to escape, so she'd just respawn in her workshop hale and hearty. But, the effect hadn't triggered after basically losing her right arm just now. Only when she succumbed to blood loss. So what if I just broke a few limbs and left her down the street instead? If there was nothing stopping her from crawling back to her workshop and resuming her task as ineffectually as she could - would that count?

That sounded like an idea to me. However impossible it might seem against the furious juggernaut facing me now, the rules had made it clear that this wasn't just a straight-up buff for her.

Within her domain.

That was the condition for the Brute rating. If I had to guess, that meant this specific workshop. So the second she took a step outside, did that make her a typical human being? That was my interpretation of the rules, and if my power was going to screw me over just because I actually bothered to read them for once - I was going to be pissed.

My ash clone surges to life and sweeps at her leg, I yank on her overextended arm as she stumbles - but I abort the throw and shift into my shadow-state before her other hand blurs through the air where my face just was. A bit too slow on that. I'd been a bit too surprised that it had worked. Her fist dismisses my clone an instant later.

I just needed to bait her over the line. Simply retreating does nothing, she stops a few metres clear of the exit and turns back to her vehicle - apparently debating whether to throw a wrench at me as I inch closer again. Got to trick her. Vista could do it if I could get to charge at full speed before shrinking the space in front of her, leaving her unable to stop or redirect herself before crossing the line. If the opportunity arose, I could try it - but that kind of wild charge just wasn't something she needed to do when I could barely get more than a few inches of breathing room between each strike.

But that same forced-closeness did offer another way to get her over the line. I'd just proven that I could throw her. It sounded stupid to try against a Brute, but she didn't weigh any more than she usually did. She wasn't rooted to the ground more than a regular person. In fact, she was lighter than most people I was used to throwing around at this point.

Dodge left. Backstep. Duck. I stall for the few seconds I need to get my ash clone back, Parian's power teases another thread out from my shirt in case I need it - but the original Clockblocked thread still hasn't faded yet. It could come back in two seconds or two minutes, I couldn't rely on it right now. I dance closer to the open exit of the garage, doing my best to make it not seem deliberate. Squealer hesitates to follow for a moment, only for me to slug her in the face for the indecision. Ineffective, but transitioning into a jab at the eyes does the job. She grabs my arm, attempting to snap it in two before it fades to smoke in her grip. She ineffectually chases for a moment longer, lunging at the still-physical parts of the limb-

-and my ash clone surges to life again next to me, as I grab her arm, pull her up and over me as I fall under her - plant two feet onto her torso and kick her up and over past me as I complete the roll. Ironically, the unyielding nature of her Brute rating actually helps the motion - and with my ash clone suicidally adding its strength to the move coupled with a quick shrinking from Vista, Squealer tumbles through the air with the grace of a sack of potatoes.

Not without consequence. She'd gotten a hand on my left foot - and I'd opted to keep the strength of the motion and delay the shift into my shadow-state rather than risk the strategy as a whole. So my foot... yes. Broken. Pulped, perhaps, would be the best way to describe it. This wasn't a simple case of a snap, but rather that her fingers had closed around it completely and not found any resistance until they reached her palm. My foot was more of a... soup, held in place by the remnants of my shoes.

But all for a worthy cause. Because suddenly, the pace of the fight had slowed. Drastically. My ash clone had remained on the offensive as I launch into a stumbling crawl after them. And this time, my ash clone wasn't being dismissed. The Brute rating was gone, just as I had hoped.

I give the furious, swearing figure a nasty grin. "No tinkering for either of us, I'm afraid." Squealer had some muscle, but little-to-no actual fighting experience. It takes mere moments to twist and snap an arm around and away - which only serves to make it easier to do the same to a leg.

Stop. The mental command to my ash clone is obeyed instantly. I couldn't go too far here. Not without risking crossing whatever arbitrary line my power had set to allow her to respawn. I have the clone drag her by one leg across the street, to the furthest corner on my side of the starting checkpoint - a shame that I didn't seem to be able to roam further, but I could deal with it.

Now, let her start to crawl back. I settle against the wall, idly watching my ash clone pace after the desperate attempts of the crippled Tinker to drag herself across the street back to her workshop - getting around halfway before being roughly dragged back to where she started.

Again. Again. My clone is fast enough to dodge the slow, sweeping kicks that Squealer attempts as it approaches - and even if the simulation is realistic enough to mirror a certain degree of vulgarity, there's no sense of giving up or even shifting her approach to begging like a real person would have by now. Idly, I wonder if its even possible for my foot to completely heal via my usual repeated use of the shadow state. It tended to put things back together slightly better than they were, but was there a limit to that? I could deal with it, obviously - I'd functionally earned myself infinite time here. But putting serious weight on it was a bit of a pain, the speed-state helps with that - letting me practically throw my near-weightless body around with a fraction of the effort.

Ten minutes pass. Twenty. Thirty. I take the time to peer at Squealer's half-started design, trying to probe the idea behind it with Leet's power for insights. Sadly, there wasn't a complete design document for me to look at - so I was limited to guesswork for the specifications of her planned vehicle.

Fourty minutes. I find myself sketching out the mecha-blade that Leet I had worked on with Leet. The recreated drawing was good. Too good. Swift, clean strokes and measurements springing to mind and onto the hasty sketch without even struggling to cast my mind back. Evidently, recreating past design documents was a free bonus with the Tinker powers. I idly burn the schematic into my held Tinker slot. I didn't intend to use it now, but I needed to know how this power interacted with my challenges. I'd have tested it before if I'd had some Tinker schematics to work with, I just hadn't expected that I could recreate the schematics myself to a level of detail that would satisfy my power.

Fifty minutes. I categorise the general types of metal and materials in her workshop, then pile it all up and set fire to it. Just for good measure.

At the sixty minute mark, the walls blocking us from entering the wider street fade away without ceremony. I leave my ash clone to its mission of bullying Squealer and slip it into my speed state. I mentally map out the track as I go, trying to think of good potential ambush spots and tricks I could pull out next time. Because there would most likely be a next time. My power liked to iterate on themes like this sometimes, and when I missed the point of the theme or sidestepped it somehow - I usually just got a slightly harder version that couldn't be exploited so easily.

A narrow spot in the marked road that could be a threat for time-locked objects. A pair of back-to-back blind corners that would make ambushes easy. A small U-turn at checkpoint four where I might have a chance to catch up if I fell behind. A corner through the docks that would send someone hurtling into the sea with a quick application of Vista's powerset to make them misjudge their approach.

Lots of options. But, none of them as good as just not racing in the first place. I couldn't afford to be arrogant and assume that Squealer couldn't surprise me. I'd already slowed myself down against Skidmark by doing that, if I had time for a half-dozen more attempts against him - maybe I could just brute-force the front-door entrance with a more fine-tuned approach. If I had been more deliberate in the earlier failed challenges, if I'd invested more effort into finding him in the crowd earlier - and then, after meeting him, been able to navigate the minefield of a conversation to keep him easily accessible... I could do it differently, if I could just redo the whole thing.

But these were the cards I had. And my best play was to assume that trying to beat Squealer at her own game was doomed to failure. I needed to make her play mine. Combat and treachery. It wasn't about matching her efforts, it was about making her as useless as my baseline self is - and then racing to the finish while she is busy sulking over the smoking wreckage of her masterpiece.

Not this challenge though. It wasn't needed this time around. But I was glad that I was thinking ahead. It was easy to get in the habit of just winging it sometimes, knowing that my power threw enough modifiers and curveballs that I would inevitably need to die a few times to get the trick of it. But nihilism didn't help anything.

I cross the final checkpoint at what would have been merely a gentle jog to the naked eye, thanks to my persistent limp - but there isn't any competition to hurry me along. My speed-state fades on its own as the world collapses around me.

Easy. Nicely done.

SUCCESS

Reward: Tinker: Vehicles (Rugged Designs) (1)​

No second slot. Fine. I wasn't that surprised, the extras from Leet's first few rewards were likely just a one-time thing for getting my first Tinker power. I activate the power and let my mind wander on potential things I could build.

The speciality itself wasn't quite what I'd hoped for. A general vehicle tinker would have been fine. Movement in general would be even better. This sub-speciality seemed focused on the bulky, unstoppable aspects of her usual vehicles. Something that would be amazing if I wanted to build something that could withstand a tank round, or drive through a sandstorm or surge across a muddy trench somewhere. But my ambitions right now were a glider of some kind to help with Skidmark, and all of the ideas I was defaulting towards with this powerset were either too complex for me to do easily, or too large to fit into the instant-build 'box' that my power provided.

It was fine. Squealer was always going to be the hardest power to use out of my haul today. I'm not going to let myself get upset over one of objectively the best days I've ever had with this power - and I wasn't even halfway done yet.

Squealer

Merchant Villain 2/6

(EVNT) (CONT) (REAL)​

The exact same modifier as last time, with a bit of an incentive to not fail - and most likely an additional bit of abuse from my competitor. I could almost hear my power daring me to try the same strategy again, see what happens.

I eye my Tinker slot, noting Leet's blade was still in there. So the held design could be smuggled in and out of challenges. That was good to know. Maybe it could help me prepare in challenges I was completely stuck on, taking in a prepared-design that I could easily find the right resources for - although I wouldn't exactly have many chances to iterate on my failures, the long cooldown on the ability ensured that.

"Challenge."

A minor disadvantage to me, given that Squealer would definitely be able to max out her speed if she ever got that far - but my intentions were still to never allow her to have an honest race.

Same room. Same sounds next door.

THE GATES WILL UNLOCK IN SIXTY MINUTES.

PASS THROUGH ALL CHECKPOINTS BEFORE YOUR OPPONENT TO COMPLETE THE CHALLENGE

ENEMY PARTICIPANTS WILL GAIN ENHANCED PHYSICAL ABILITIES WITHIN THEIR DOMAIN BEFORE THE GATES OPEN

THE ENEMY PARTICIPANT WILL RESPAWN IF KILLED OR DISABLED​

...same rules. No extra exceptions telling me that I can't go and bother Squealer.

Well. I couldn't entirely dismiss the idea that my power hadn't weighted things against me like that. So I had to try. Even if I was doubtful that my power would let me get away with sidestepping the main thrust of the challenge twice.

I phase through the wall.

Pain blossoms in my mouth, my upper torso and my left arm - I'm already reeling back and hurtling back through the wall with my second charge before I even have time to register the honest-to-god autoturret attached to the ceiling of Squealer's workshop.

Cheek wound, straight through both sides of the mouth. Not that I trusted Shadow Stalker's healing abilities much at all when it came to serious injuries. I dump the last charge into a full-body phase. It phases my fleshy body out, and when I phase back in - it puts things back together in a way that is slightly more 'correct'. It helped with avoiding scars or lasting cuts, but the effect was slight enough that it was only really that effective when done repeatedly over time. That had gotten easier now that I had the extra charges of the shadow state refuelling constantly - but still, nothing compared to what a real healing factor could do.

I shift into the shadow state again the instant my shortest charge recovers. One second at a time. I'd only tested this on minor injuries. Five charges could stop a simple knife cut across my palm from bleeding. Fifteen would remove every last trace that something had happened. How long would it take to close the bullet wounds in my chest? Would it be more efficient to only phase out certain parts of my body? I sink onto my back, a lethargic sense of weakness leaving me laying down in a steadily-expanding pool of my own blood.

"Woo! You deserve that. What, did you really think I would leave my babies unprotected? Think again, fucker! You're lucky Skids isn't here, a bullet in the skull would have been a mercy for even trying to fuck with me!" The triumphant call from next door seeps into my ears. These walls are pretty thin, I can hear every word and she clearly knows it. "Maybe think about your mistakes for a bit, or save us both the trouble and just off yourself the next time around!"

I grit my teeth. Ignore it. Or, don't ignore it. Get mad. Think of all the violent things I wanted to do to shut her up, get focused on that - and use that to keep awake enough to blow through my shadow state charges.

I phase again. Don't fall unconscious. That was the most important thing. Every phase I got off, took me one massive step closer to survival. Assuming I healed at the same rate all across my body, I would be stopping any internal bleeding just as quickly as the external wounds - and I already knew how fast those could be slowed and stopped. I didn't need to worry about anything else. Squealer wasn't going to chase after me and try to finish me off. She was focused on building her car. I could sit here and heal as much as I could unimpeded, aside from the occasional bit of mocking abuse she sent my way through the wall. That was as ideal as it could get, given the circumstances - most other opponents would have killed me while I was down. It almost felt a little strange having the challenge work in my favour for once.

Phase. Phase again. I spit blood off to the side. Apart from the faint whistling through my cheeks as I try and breathe, I'd say the lesser wounds were done. I shake off the sensation of dizzyness, belatedly realising that all of my charges were back. Phase. Phase. Phase. Had I lost unconsciousness for a moment there? Or, just a lapse of focus due to blood loss?

Doesn't matter. I was past the worst of it now. Phase out. This time, I start to push myself back out of the pool of sticky, goopy blood that had yet to decide if it wanted to congeal properly or not yet. Still a bit woozy. I brush my hand against my cheek. A definite hole, but already slightly patched over. A few more uses of the shadow state would fix that too.

Most importantly, the wounds had healed enough to stop bleeding - which probably meant that the internal wounds I'd suffered had stopped bleeding as well. It didn't really matter if a perfect recovery would need another ten shadow states or a hundred - I could just use it on cooldown until the time ran out while I was doing other things. Now that I wasn't at risk of outright dying, things could only get better.

27:52

Aside from the timer. That only got worse. A little over half my allotted time spent drooling on the floor as a barely-coherent mess. It was avoidable, honestly. I could see in my shadow state, so if I had devoted an extra charge to just taking stock of the situation before materialising I'd have still had the third charge to escape once the bullets started passing through me ineffectually. No, this would be all about putting those tricks and traps I had scouted out in the previous challenge to use. The downside of that, was the strong possibility that the CONT modifier would still be in place next challenge as well - at which point...

I glance down at the dirt at my feet. At which point she would be too cautious to lose in the same way. She'd take the long way around, or make it run along walls to avoid being caught by me on the ground. Running into time-locked string was something she'd only fall for once.

So. Time to plan ahead again. Assuming I win this round, assuming I can slice her vehicle to ribbons or pile it into the sea before she can overtake me - how was I going to win the third challenge?

Tinkering, I suppose. I didn't have another set of trump cards, other than turning the course into a deathtrap. I still had the Tinker slot. Having seen the first level of Squealer's power, there was no point trying to save it for Skidmark - it wanted too much for even a conservative design to fit within the 'box' that the slot could paste the design into. I might not be able to conjure up the absurd wizardry of some of Leet's better inventions at my current level, but I understood what the power actually wanted me to do - and that had to count for something.

And I didn't need to entirely make my own design. The Tinker power I was drawing from was 'Prototype', after all. Take a base design, and start adding to it. More features. New ideas. Every invention a step above the last, forced onwards by the ever-increasing probabilities of the quirks in the original design making themselves known. And even if I only had one design made by someone that knew what they were doing - the mecha-blade designed for a robot several times my weight and size - that was a pretty useful design to start with when I really, really wanted to just destroy Squealer's tank in the kind of straight-up fight that she would never expect after my intended plans for this race.

I lean down to scrawl on the floor. I wasn't a mech, so the power systems that fed the slicing motion of the blade would be the first issue. Fortunately, I had plenty of space and weight to sacrifice if I wanted it to be human-portable. If I could settle it over my arms and shoulders as if I was fulfilling the control systems and aiming, I wouldn't need to keep any of the more complex joints - I wasn't sword-fighting here, one angle was more than enough if it had enough power to cleave Squealer's ride in half. No hydraulics, I don't have the materials. I'd need to liberate one of the engines in my garage as a starting source of power, but the sheer amount of power that the blade would want to generate would burn through too much to allow it to be portable over the course of the race.

Not a problem if I just attacked her right out of the starting gates. I didn't need longevity, I'd either destroy her or lose immediately - no in-between. There was a question of if I actually had the right materials to stand up to the pressures the blade would output on the frame holding it, and I was pretty sure that the answer to that was no. Three seconds. Squealer revs menacingly, belching out smoke from all sides of her creation. I shift into my shadow state, the brief moment of paralysis taking over. Two. One. God I love this power combination.

What a pain for thinking of future ways to beat her. But it didn't matter how fast it was this time.

Because you couldn't break Clockblocked objects with pure speed. Those objects would break you.

Her new ride doesn't split down the middle as it crashes into the tripwire-like obstruction, but it does crumple around it - coming to a halt in a scrunched-up ball of screeching metal before I can even blink. Not that they would have helped at all, but still.

I'm confident in that much. Knocking him out was probably the safest play, but treating him a bit like our capture of Oni Lee would be somewhat fine too.

She waves me off. "Of course we can handle him, I'm saying - IF - we can't, what happens. Some miracle happens, we fuck it up - whatever. What's the plan? I'm not committing to anything if you're just hoping all goes well."

"Then we pull the stops on our powers and leave." I shrug. "It's not a big deal. I go on PHO to get the first word out, bragging about how I infiltrated the Merchants and got in spitting distance of Skidmark - talk all the shit in the world about how trash the party was and how lax I found the security. You can keep yourself hidden for the action, I'll just say that my 'companion' was just my ash clone keeping appearances up. It can use the shadow state as well, so its a great alibi. There's no good resource online about what my powers can or can't do, and it's well known that I've got something similar to your powers at this point."

She stays silent for a moment. "If we do this- if we do this-" She stresses. "-I'm hanging back. This is your thing. I'm not getting caught, not for anything. If you fuck it up, I'll call the PRT for you and nothing more - I'm not going to juvie because you lost the plot."

"That's fine. This is an invitation for you to enjoy the spoils with me, I don't need you for the execution." I smile nastily. "Because you're right. I do need to get back on him, in more ways than you realise - and maybe there's a few things that Void Cowboy can't get away with, that a scorned Merchant can. We can make a lesson stick here. In my career, in your career - have you ever done anything that the villains will seriously remember? This is a chance for that, and if we do it right, it never even traces back to you or I. I mean, if we humiliate him badly enough... he won't even want to tell anyone what happened if he can help it."

"Why am I even listening to you..." She groans. "It's so stupid. I know that. It's just- it's also kind of appealing. If we pull it off- it's got to be something serious, all right? Like, if you try and give him a noogie and call it a day - I'm breaking both his arms before we leave." She holds her head in her hands for a moment, looking up at the sky. "I'm not committing to anything, but- but we should go and beat up those two guys first. We can decide the rest later, talk about the finer details - take things slow. But if those guys get away, the whole plan is a bust."

I grin. Got her. "Right. We can refine a few details after we've settled into our new disguises. Can't let our two little hunters get away, we've already spent too much time talking - they'll probably be thinking of giving up soon, if they haven't already."

Sophia lopes after me as I lead the way across the rooftops. My gaze sharpens as my two pursuers from earlier come into view further down the street. They don't have a reason to look up here on the rooftops, even if they could make me out - but I could see them just fine. They were clearly stalling, not even pretending to search at this point - just loitering at the side of the street, killing time.

I descend on one of them from above like an angry god. Sophia has the other in a chokehold before he can even turn around to investigate the noise.

Six minutes later, I give a considering look to Sophia. And it was Sophia now. The Shadow Stalker costume was tucked away in a hidey-hole, and the scowling visage of a Merchant gangbanger stood in its place.

"What's with all of-" I gesture at the extra accessories and mess of hair trailing down her face. "-that?"

"I need them to not see my face, obviously." She snarks.

"Wasn't planning on letting that happen anyway. You look ridiculous." I inform her.

"Stuff it. Your plan is ridiculous, I don't want to hear shit about how adding one sensible bit of precaution to it is suddenly a problem." She snips at me.

I check on my ash clone, seems like its done dragging and securing the two naked Merchants over to a distant street. They'd probably get noticed and called in pretty quickly, but nothing they eventually said to the cops would have any real meaning - if they said anything at all.

"Glad you've made up your mind, at least." I grin at her.

She shifts uncomfortably. "Just focus on your plan. I'm not bailing you out if you fuck it up. You talked a big game up to this point - don't think I'll forget that if you botch this up. I know you've done some good work before, but this is- this is a bit different."

I shift my leg in and out of shadow state. A bit sore. But, for the most part, usable. I hold the guard's knife up to eye-level. Intended to slit my throat at the end of it all. The sensation of wetness trickling down my neck, still there no matter how much I wiped it clean. The constant contempt in every request that I handled for him throughout the evening. The phantom pain in my balls, even after this many shadow-states.

The memory of Squealer, giggling as he pulls her close - a coupling that was offensive merely for the fact that it existed.

The sickly feeling of uncertainty, a flash of fear that I'd overstepped into a situation that I couldn't get out of.

"This is different." I acknowledge with a serene smile, tucking the knife into its holster.

"This is personal."

#2,473
"This is so stupid." Sophia repeats for the third time straight. "Like, top ten-"

"Yes, yes. You've said." I agree testily. "And yet, it's working, isn't it?" I glare in the direction of one errant partygoer straying too close to our route around the edge of the compound, swinging my gun around aggressively with the motion. The man quickly finds another corner to piss in after sending me a foul look.

"It shouldn't." She grumbles. "Just one person saying something-"

I snort, keeping my voice down. "And who would do that? There's a hierarchy here. Capes. Guards. Everyone else. We don't see any guards, because they're all either sitting in their one position or following the same patrol route as us. Squealer is tinkering in her workshop. Mush is... not the kind of person to willingly talk to anyone. And Skidmark, if he even knows who his guards are and what they look like, isn't exactly outside right now to spot us."

"I get all that." Sophia kicks away a discarded bottle in our path. "It's just-"

"Just what? We haven't even done anything difficult or risky yet. This is the equivalent of walking into an employees-only room with a high-vis jacket and a clipboard, except we also have an escape route that they can't stop." I look at her doubtful expression with a confused look. "Your power is perfect for this sort of thing. Even my discount version is amazing for it. Going through walls or just peaking, blending into shadows, general weightlessness, the lengthy glide - I do this sort of thing all the time, even with the cooldown problems that my version has. As long as you don't mess up and land on something as you come out of the shadow state, you've got all the time in the world to slip around like you own the place. Feels like everywhere has space in the ceiling to hide in and peer through, and literally nobody ever looks up - or would even recognise the slight wisp of a sliver of your smoky-face peeking through the bathroom wall."

"Maybe, but that doesn't change the fact that it's a risk." She argues. "You're risking your life doing this, waiting for one thing to go wrong."

"Isn't it the same every time you try and punch a Nazi in the face? They could have a gun, or a taser - or a sniper could be waiting to take a shot from across the street. Doesn't stop half the Wards from being deployed to minor gang scuffles." I counter.

"We can practice for that. We train for that. Funnily enough, strolling into an enemy base isn't something that you can safely train for. You're just looking at the fact that you haven't been killed yet, and assuming that means you must be so smart and so skilled that nobody can stop you." Sophia shakes her head. "And, like. I get it. I get it! It's me! I felt invincible too. Random girl one day. Trivially beating up a guy twice my size the next before I even knew how to fight. But, you can't let it get to your head. You need experience." I snort. "I'm serious. You're going to keep testing for your limits, and instead of finding them you're going to get slightly unlucky and end up dead. No retries."

If only she knew. "I appreciate the concern, but you're making this into a bigger deal than it needs to be." I come to a halt and cast my gaze around sternly for the benefit of anyone looking our way. Our act as guards wasn't exactly Oscar-winning, but it wasn't like the people we were imitating were professionals anyway. "I know what I'm doing here. I've spent-" Days. "-hours mapping this place out and seeing how they organise themselves. I'm more prepared for this than any other time you've seen me." I clear my throat. "And, sure - the original plan was to attack them as a three-man unit later on - but that doesn't mean that everything I know is useless now."

Now it's Sophia's turn to express disbelief. "Sure. You walked around licking the dirt off of Skidmark's boots for an hour or two, now you're qualified to star in a shitty spy movie about breaking into their little party - except instead of shit ratings, you just die. But don't let me talk you out of it, I'll say something nice at your funeral." She sends me a harsh look. "Look at it this way. I wouldn't do this. Why do you think its a good idea for you to do it, with a worse power and less experience?"

"Less experience? Do you have any idea how many times-" I cough. "I mean, come on. I'm pretty sure I have the edge on you there. It isn't like you ever get the chance to do anything relevant with your powers since joining the Wards."

"The fuck does that mean?" She hisses, voice low only as we pass by a smoking partygoer seeking a moment of solitude away from the crowd. I wait for us to gain some distance, the music in the distance providing an extra layer of soundproofing despite the open-air of our surroundings.

"Just that the PRT have taught you everything they know about being cautious, taking no risks and generally doing nothing that will get the Youth Guard breathing down their necks." I continue for her. "I won't say that you've gone soft-"

"Better fucking not." Sophia mumbles darkly.

I shrug. "-but you've been working with them for a while now. The PRT doesn't do infiltrations. They don't do sneaking around and ambushing people. They would never dream of sending you into a base of armed hostiles like this. And so, you don't practice for it. Instead, they teach you how to fight in a team, rescue people and stand up to villains in a fair fight. They've encouraged you to patch up your weaknesses rather than exploit your strengths, because all of your strengths are useless to them."

I direct her down to the side of the fence. A pair of guards had been lingering around the fence line here the last time I found a current-time WRLD modifier - I wanted us to be in the shadows on the approach, so I would see them first if they were there.

I continue. "And now you've let them gaslight you into thinking that something like this - too dangerous for a generic superhero to do - is something that you aren't capable of either. This is- this is you. This is your element. A base of oblivious hostiles, some VIPs to reach and take down somewhere in the middle of it all and no real help coming if you set off an alarm." I wave a hand at nothing. "Hell, we're actually making it harder than something you could do on your own. You could just shoot Skidmark once you find him, rather than dragging things out to teach him a lesson." I knew exactly what I wanted to do to Skidmark. But if I told her now, she would probably back out. "Every security measure in this place is designed around the fact that humans have to walk through certain checkpoints and entrances to get anywhere. Your power tramples all over that from the very first move, never mind what happens when we actually reach the building."

"All we did was phase through a wall." She dismisses my words. "Don't try and make it any more than it was."

Is she actively trying to miss the point? "It's not about that. Half of the Bay could get in here. It's everything else. It's about the stealth, mobility and options you have. Glory Girl could fly in here just the same, but she knows that her forcefield is unreliable once bullets start flying."

Sophia pauses for a half-step at that, then resumes walking. Did she not know she wasn't invincible? Or was she surprised that I knew?

As she doesn't voice a question, I elaborate on my point. "But you? I'm pretty sure you could get onto the roof of that building without me from this point, poke your head through the roof, plant a crossbow bolt through Skidmark's head and leave before anyone even realised you were here, let alone thought of looking for you in particular. There's not a single person here who could stop you from sprinting out of the centre of this camp and out into the city, even if everyone was chasing you. Stealth. Lethality. Dexterity. Mobility. It's an assassin build. You knew that when you named yourself. There's a reason you aren't called Shadow Brawler or something." I gaze towards the central building, noting the rotating lights periodically illuminating it - and at the far edge of the visible area, the shadows of two distant guards ambling towards their next destination.

"And that's where the theory ends and reality kicks in." She argues. "Yeah, if the fate of the world was at stake - maybe I would be pretty well suited for a mission like that. But day-to-day bullshit? I've only got one life. A guard rounds a corner a few minutes early when I'm not looking? Some electrician made a mess of the wiring in the wall and I go through it too fast? It's over. I got a sensor of sorts in my helmet after joining the Wards, that's the thing that would enable me to do something like this on my own if I wanted - unfortunately, it came with a collar attached." She shakes her head. "Not that - as a vigilante - I ever found a place where serious Capes were hiding anyway. Some warehouses, sure - but never anything where I knew, for certain, that there was someone inside worth risking my life to get at. The PRT gets info like that sometimes. But, again, the timing of it all - everything I need to be effective, and the promise of juvie if I dare to use any of it."

I consider that for a moment. "Suppose I can't really blame you for looking at it like that." I was used to Shadow Stalker's power being near all-powerful within the constraints of a building like this. The idea that Shadow Stalker wouldn't share the feeling of near-invincibility that I did with a dozen escape options available to me was a novel one. I suppose, without the benefits of my first few dozen deaths teaching me all the right and wrong ways to infiltrate any given building and where electrical cables should be expected, that this must seem a little insane. Still pretty safe, but it was a dice roll every time. Hitting a natural one was unlikely, but if you kept on rolling... "So does that mean you've never done something like this before?" I take her silence as a yes. "I'm sorry. If I'd known this was your first time, I'd have been more gent- ow!" I send her a wounded look as she kicks me in the shin, barely breaking her own stride.

"Don't go getting an ego, thinking that you're better than me with my own power. I've got months and months of experience over you-" Probably not true, actually. "-and the fact that you were stupid enough to risk losing your life in a random drug den to one misplaced power cable doesn't change that."

"You know, for once, I really wasn't trying to be mean there." I raise my hands as she sends me a disbelieving look. "I'm serious! I was joking around a little, but I respect the point. I mean, if I hadn't already scouted out this place thoroughly - and if I didn't have a host of other powers to fall back on if needed - I wouldn't have risked coming in here, Cape or not." I only ever needed to find one person with a challenge based on the area or with a WRLD modifier to know absolutely everything about a building. Which walls were safe to run through, where I could access the ceiling, or dive down into a basement level - not quite as effective as just being able to see electricity though. I needed to steal that design at some point, it was probably Armsmaster's - would I be able to interpret it with another Tinkers power, or did it lean on his speciality too much? "But I get the feeling that you'd have been more willing than me before the PRT came along."

She's silent for a moment. "Honestly speaking? Yeah. Maybe I would- could have done something before I got this leash on me." She grunts bitterly. "Too late to do anything meaningful now. I'm not going to juvie to get one loser off the streets." She shakes her head, adopting a wistful tone. "I used to have a list. Every villain in the Bay that would die to a crossbow bolt appearing in their skull. Used to imagine what the scene would look like if I could just do that in one night, pair up with some Thinker to point me in the right direction - eliminate most of the villain population overnight. Wouldn't even have to do the rest myself, the PRT would just sweep up the rest for me if they weren't outnumbered - right?"

"Love the faith in the PRT. Must have been early days." She snickers at that as we near the corner of the compound and turn to follow the fence line. Regardless of her own feelings on the matter, her plans wouldn't have changed much, at a guess. Most likely, the big gangs downsize their territories and the Teeth would have seen some prime real estate to move back into with their main rivals gone. They didn't seem to be loving their time in Boston, based on what I've seen in the news lately. "Not Lung. Not Alabaster. Fifty-fifty on the other Brutes. Not Krieg. Maybe not Cricket. Everyone else dies." I offer after a moment of thought.

"Something like that. Thought Krieg wouldn't be able to do anything to a fast enough bolt. I was thinking I could maybe handle Lung if I had a larger payload. Even tried timing some explosives and attaching chemicals to the bolts, which didn't really go that well. I'm not a Tinker. Or even particularly good with DIY. Obviously, it didn't work out - never even saw the guy. Probably for the best, after seeing the PRT's folder on him - he definitely would have shrugged it off." She clears her throat. "But, yeah - spent a lot of time thinking about how much I was going to achieve - do what nobody else seemed to be able to do. And then, the minor details in between started to become my problems. Sure, I can shoot Kaiser - how do I find him? Fine, Oni Lee dies if I catch him unawares - how do I do that? What patrol is good? Should I patrol? Is it good for people to see me, or does it just scare my targets away? Everyone knows the ABB is in the downtown area - but you could run for an hour and not even check the outer perimeter of an area as vague as that. Where do I go? How do I find them, so I can shoot them? That was the problem."

Sophia sighs loudly. I opt not to interject, sensing her desire to continue.

"I guess you're new to this, you got lucky with a partner who can search for trouble in such a wide area, and you only did a few patrols before you stumbled on Oni Lee by sheer luck - but... Brockton Bay is big." She makes an expressive motion with her hands. "And not everybody is a full-time Cape. You can go days, weeks of patrolling and just never meet another Cape. Even when you're really trying. Even if you cause some chaos deliberately, try to scare some low-ranking members to get their big guns to come after you - they usually won't bite. They can just give it up as a minor loss, hope that someone kills the nosy Cape with a lucky bullet. And then, one day, all of a sudden - they all bite at once. Ambush. Almost got myself killed trying that with the Empire. Not to mention how Armsmaster got me within a week once he started looking. Still don't know how he managed that when I change streets every patrol."

I nod in understanding. "It's a lot for one person. I get it." I really did. "You hear about a Cape fight just starting and by the time you get there, everyone's already gone home. I've got speedster powers now and I still have that issue."

"Yeah." She scowls. "If I'd known about a meetup like this back then - even just once - I could have done something. Done more in one night than I managed in weeks on my own. Now, the PRT has all the information I could ever ask for - and I can't do a fucking thing with it."

"Until I came along." I hum. "Plausible deniability is great, isn't it?" A ghost of a smile appears on her face. "And you were so annoyed when I showed that I had your powers the first time." The smile disappears as fast as it arrived.

"I'm still annoyed, don't get it twisted." She levels a scowl at me. "I had to go through real trauma for my powers. And some shut-in nerd gets them by manning up and talking to girls for once in his life? Anyone would be mad."

"I think you're being a bit uncharitable there. My power isn't quite that simple." Sure, I hadn't exactly explained the full details for obvious reasons - but it did grate a little bit to have people minimising my own efforts and struggles that went into acquiring new powers. There was nothing I could really do about it, being honest would be a complete disaster - but... still. Anyway. I probably shouldn't be trying to defend myself too hard here. Time to deflect. "We did way more than talk."

"Yeah? How many extra powers did you get in the few hours you were in there today?" She jerks her head towards the courtyard and buildings across the path behind us.

I pause. "Okay, I did get all three-" I concede. "-but that doesn't mean-"

"See? Absolute bullshit." Sophia crosses her arms for a moment as she walks. "You won the power lottery and you're complaining you have to walk to the desk to get your numbers checked."

"At least you're admitting I won the power lottery now." I grin. "Feels like only yesterday that you were praying for my downfall as a useless grab-bag Cape that could only hold a few useless powers at once."

"I'm still praying." She tells me shortly. "You'll run into a limit one of these days. Sooner, when Armsmaster drags you in for powertesting and a forced induction into the Wards after catching you jaywalking."

"I feel you might be a little biased." I tell her drily. "Time to face it. I'm going to be Triumvirate tier eventually. Beyond that, even." I wink. "Don't worry, I'm the humble sort. Never one to forget all the people who helped me along the way." I squeeze her ass as we continue along the patrol path. "I'll find a use for you, I'm sure."

"Keep dreaming." She looks a little mulish at my actions, but words can't entirely hide her body language. Try as she might... Sophia couldn't hide the fact that she liked it when I was arrogant and possessive. "Besides, you'll never make it to Triumvirate if you get shot in the face today because you don't realise that you're walking too fast." She tugs me back.

I click my tongue, following her gaze to note the shadowy figures in the distance - figures barely illuminated every few seconds by the rotating lights of the party. I hadn't noticed them in the lengthening shadow of the main building as nighttime descended on Brockton Bay. We would probably have passed without challenge at a distance... but getting too close might have caused a scene. "Thanks."

She shifts, almost not knowing what to say. "...just pay attention."

I give her a simple grunt of agreement. "Once we round that corner, it's a straight-shot up to the building that the main party is in. Guards are watching the back entrance and the lit-up areas of the path heading out, but naturally - there's nothing to stop someone from just lurking in the shadows around the edge of the building and slinking up to the roof. The hall that most of the guests are sitting in doesn't share the attic, so don't drop through in the wrong place. The back half of the building is no different from breaking in to your standard office." I pause at the lack of acknowledgement from Sophia. "I mean, you know those square-tile things that you can lift away from some ceilings? And the little runways you can walk or crawl on while you're up there? How do you think the aircon, pipes and electricity cables get around buildings like that? There's a whole mini-floor up there that you don't get to see, minus the headroom." She shrugs. "You need to get out more."

"Rich, coming from you." She snorts.

I adopt a smug expression. "I know you'd like to think that you're the real go-getter here, but you're the one looking like a complete novice at navigating a building like this. What were you even using your powers for, up until this point?"

"Beating up criminals. Saving innocent people. Training with the Wards." She rolls her eyes at me. "Not much time on the agenda to practice breaking in."

"It's called Urban Exploration, Sophia. We're not criminals." I chide her, resuming on the patrol path at a slower pace as the distant shadows start to move on.

"Is that what you call perving on the female showers at Winslow? It's not like you have any more reason to be using your powers around buildings than I did - especially without my mask to help out." She frowns as I stop dead. "What?"

"I never did that." I stare straight ahead.

"Sure-" She tugs my shirt and keeps walking, half-dragging me along as we go.

"No, really - like, never." She almost looks uncomfortable for the accusation after seeing my expression. "What was wrong with me?"

"Can't believe I was about to apologise." She snorts and increases her pace.

I race to catch up. "I mean, take me back a few months - that would be right at the top of my to-do list the second I got a power that could look through walls or floor like that. Go peek on the track team as they come in from their practice. Rows upon rows of soaking, naked girls enjoying a bit of skinship-"

"That absolutely does not happen." Sophia denies. "And nobody uses the open showers, the hot water doesn't last. Everyone uses the cubicles."

"Don't ruin this for me." I ignore her. "And that kind of thing, it's basically what your power is built for. The same kind of tier as invisibility, right? Ask any guy-"

"That is not what my power is built for." Sophia denies the truth. "Can we not have this conversation?"

"-and I was no different. Yet, the thought of peeping never occurred to me until now." I tilt my head to the side. "Has my perversion been robbed from me? Has my power taken that away, somehow?"

"I'm bringing a taser into the showers from now on." Sophia levels a glare at me. "And I cannot believe that you just tried to suggest that you aren't still a pervert. You're the most degenerate soul I know."

I return the look. "I'm not the one that gets off on violence and has a defeat fetish a mile wide." I dodge the kick at my shin this time.

"Not even going to dignify that with a response." Sophia states icily. "Focus. The guards are gone."

"Alright, alright. I'll stop." I grin. "Just making pleasant conversation. And you've stopped worrying about the guards running into us, at least."

"I was never worried about the guards." Sophia scowls. "Your plan only gets stupid once we get into the building and look for Skidmark. This bit was always simple and easy."

"That's not what you were saying a few minutes ago." I sing-song. "You didn't even want to go through the wall until you verified the route for yourself and saw the first few patrols go past in person."

She bristles. "That's because only a moron would trust your memory and sense of timing. You should be happy that at least one of us has the good sense to have a bit of caution when walking into enemy territory. Now we know the gaps between patrols, and we know you weren't entirely full of shit about their pathing. And all we lost is a few minutes of time that we had plenty of anyway."

"So little faith in me. I haven't been wrong yet, have I?" I guide her up an incline.

"Yet." She stresses. "There's still plenty that can go wrong here."

"There is." I admit. "But that's why we take it slow. Like I said, if we don't get the perfect opportunity... we leave as quietly as we came."

"I don't know about that." Sophia hums, hefting the gun in her hands and peering down the sights. "It's only a problem if we get noticed as Capes. If it looks like we can't get anything done, no reason why we can't just act like a lone Merchant took a shot and did a runner."

"We're not doing that." I shake my head. I didn't really have any personal compunctions about killing him, but the prize of eventually getting a more complete version of Skidmark's power was enough to tilt the balance in favour of keeping him alive. "And we're looking to hit the entire gang at some point, remember? If we don't get anything done, it isn't like we'll just be letting them off scot free. It's just... an opportunity to teach Skidmark a lesson without necessarily tying it to our Cape identities." I breathe out steadily then gesture at the path ahead. "Come on. Straight up the side of the building. You can turn pretty much weightless with your power, so you should be able to jump up to the roof from that corner-"

"You forget who you're talking to." Sophia sprints past me. I follow behind as quickly as I can. I frown as I find myself slightly outpaced anyway, the light wisps of smoke streaming behind her enough of an indication that she was doing... something, to run faster. Or perhaps, to ignore the uneven ground to an extent? Hard to tell in the poor lighting around here, not something I'd seen her do in any of her challenges. Perhaps another thing that she only learned after power testing with the PRT? If I thought she would tell me, I'd ask - but I doubted I'd get any use of it anyway. It was a minor gain in speed, far inferior to my speed state and I'd never sacrifice my precious shadow state charges just to run a little bit faster. Maybe I'd look into it once I was free of the limitations of the nerfed Shadow Stalker powerset - but by that time I'd probably have better movement powers anyway.

Shadow Stalker practically flies up the wall, a level of parkour that I could only hope to match in the weightless world of my speed-state - as it is, I expend a charge to land soundlessly on a discarded pallet, surging up in a glide with the next charge and then sinking the final one into, once again, landing without making a sound on the rooftop. I doubted anyone would notice a commotion with the music and general atmosphere of the party, but good habits die hard - or whatever it is that people say.
