I'm pretty sure she doesn't have any real input over where the Merchants go - and the lack of a phone or any other method of communication was pretty obvious as well. I could buy one, but I didn't have anything to hand - and honestly, at this challenge level, I wouldn't trust her to pick up the phone when it rang anyway. If she even kept it on at all.

I needed Squealer. The Merchants couldn't organise a thing without looping her in. She was the de-facto second-in-command. And she was a Tinker. No way she would have any trouble with modern communication or arranging a meetup.

...was it even worth attacking the Merchants at this point? Really, I could just back away - appear entirely uninvolved with this situation, and find a way to get eyes on Squealer just once more. If I could come to some kind of arrangement... maybe even 'leak' the fact that I had healing powers that might work on Skidmark to arrange a few 'healing' sessions. Clearly, showing my face properly was out - even if my actions had made it obvious, Mush hadn't taken long to connect my costumeless-but-healed face with the scarred visage of 'James' and even if Skidmark was an incoherent mess of a human being, I wouldn't bet on him being any slower to make that connection if we met face-to-face before the memory had a chance to fade.

But then again, why would Squealer trust me with that if they were otherwise in a good position? I was a hero, they were villains. They didn't have a reason to even entertain my offer, a twin lack of both desperation and trust. Was it worth leaving them alone, just in the hope of keeping an amicable relationship with people that I was mastering anyway? And what did I say to Taylor and Sophia, both jumping at the bit to strike a blow against the minor gang? What did I say to PHO, after telling the boards to just sit tight and wait for my next move after the relative silence since Oni Lee's capture?

...I don't know. Maybe it's a good idea to hit the Merchants here, get one last set of challenges attempted and call it a day - or maybe I was being an idiot. But I was here now. If I fucked it up, there were other fish to fry in the Bay. I wanted to kick the anthill here. If we lost or drew, we could just retreat and brag on PHO about starting a fight. If we won, we get to drag the Protectorate out of bed to arrest them - for however many days they'd manage to keep them under lock-and-key - and I'd get another set of challenges to try from whoever they sent to investigate. Plus, the PHO bragging rights again. The actual rank-and-file Merchants getting a taste of Arachne would work against Skidmark and his attempt to stoke enthusiasm towards turning them into a rival gang to the Empire and the ABB. I'd- we- would get our second big feather-in-our-caps as local heroes since Oni Lee.

I wanted to fight. Or, I wanted to win. To be seen to win, at the very least. To get a last round of challenges in against Squealer and Skidmark. Squealer first, naturally. It didn't really need to make a difference - sending the gang scattering into the wind with their tail between their legs was probably the most likely outcome, seeing how most of Squealer's 'fights' usually went. But that was good enough. I'd get an opportunity to shit on the PRT not doing anything about it, they'd most likely send someone to investigate even if we didn't truss anyone important up as long as enough noise was made in the process.

Yes. This was still a good idea. The absolute worst-case, ignoring any random, unexpected deaths - was that the Merchant Capes all got arrested. And that was still something I could work with and adapt to. They were all low-priority and bound for low-security prisons, someone would probably break them out in return for favours or cash. And if I was wrong and they didn't, great - they were all stuck in one place just waiting for me to come and visit one day. But it probably wouldn't come to that. They just didn't have the rap sheet that someone like Hookwolf or Oni Lee had. Mush might even just get recruited by the Protectorate given her lack of criminal history - and while that was slightly awkward after seeing our faces, I doubted she was the type to volunteer information.

Although she could absolutely ruin Sophia's day by describing the girl at my side. She might have gotten away with being guessed as Arachne at a glance, but Taylor's new suit didn't cover all of her skin - and she definitely wasn't black.

But that would be Sophia's problem. I never told her to blatantly announce herself, or even show up in person before I was done talking with Mush. Hiding her face only went so far when her abrasive personality was still on full display. I could easily have kept her out of sight if she'd been patient, made some kind of excuse about needing a container for my ash clone to travel in - but either she was a bit too trusting of my plan, or perhaps just had faith in Mush not to spill the beans.

Or, maybe something else was at play entirely. Sophia and Mush were both affected by my power - did that impact their approach towards each other as well? Did it matter?

Whatever. As I said. Sophia's problem. If things got that far, I'd leave it to her to work it out or coach Mush into saying the right things. If it didn't work out, I'd just fix the consequences when I take charge of the PRT.

Amazing how simple it all ends up being. Just keep fighting. Keep getting stronger. And all these silly questions about the optimal path and the concerns of other people just melt away. Who needs ethical conundrums and lasting consequences when you're strong enough to have the final word? And maybe that was still a way off, but I wouldn't knock my efforts today. I'd walked into a gang and walked back out with a copy of every single power on offer. If I could just repeat that with the Empire, or the Protectorate... game over.

Skidmark said he didn't want to see me anyway, so I might as well just stay away for as long as I can, right?"

I separate from Mush, almost tripping as I escape the confines of the lowered cockpit and get back on to solid ground. "This place is perfect. We'll make sure not to let anyone find us that easily. Wouldn't want to get our new friend into any trouble after all you've done for us. Right?" I eye Sophia as she sourly escapes from her trashcan, still making just a token effort to hide her face from Mush's view.

"Speak for yourself."" She mutters darkly. "Not my friend, I have stand- ouch!" She lashes her leg back out at me in response to me deliberately stepping on her toe. "Fuck you!" She narrowly sidesteps a falling trash bag, filled to the brim with drink bottles.

Mush settles back into her home of choice, taking a seated position once more as Sophia glowers up at her. "Sorry, this thing falls apart over time - I don't usually use my power in a shape like this." Mush is absolutely lying, but neither of us can prove it. Not that I want to. My girls being catty towards each other is kind of hot. I didn't even think Mush was capable of it. "It's my fault."

"Don't worry about it. And try not to pay too much attention to her, she's got certain expectations for how a Cape should be and she's built her entire personality around being a bitch. You're doing fine." She preens under my words. Compliments seemed effective before, so why stop? I wanted to be her pillar of support - to such an extent that when I'm not there, there's no way she couldn't notice the difference. I wanted her reliant on me. I wanted her to look forward to seeing me again. And I couldn't entirely trust that my current challenges would do all of the work for me at this level.

Maybe taking advantage of her attention-starved nature and obvious loneliness was a dick move, but if it's all in the name of getting her into the harem eventually - I was really just doing her a favour. Picture how much happier Taylor would have been if I'd pushed her a little harder at the start. I'd bet anything Taylor would have been a lot happier about my ideas if she had the confidence that I liked her and her body too - rather than me 'being seduced' by Emma before she could even work out her own feelings.

Damn, I really wanted to see how far I could push Mush. But not in front of Sophia. I didn't want to form too much of a pattern too fast. Leet was one thing, but doing the same with the very next villain she sees me with? Maybe she wouldn't care, or chalk it up to the natural response of some predator/prey bullshit - but equally, she might think it was strange. Maybe she'd start being suspicious about my confidence and 'luck' with women, or even if she didn't - maybe she would just make the wrong kind of comment about me towards someone more inclined to start investigating.

But I had to get over that hurdle eventually. Would this be a bad place to start? Mush latching on to me would be a lot easier to explain that Glory Girl dumping that one guy for me. I was aiming for the harem end here, at some point I needed the kind of reputation where someone saw a new Cape fawning over me - and instead of suspicion or consternation, they would just shake their fist at the heavens and scream 'He can't keep getting away with it!'.

It could work out. But, it also might not. That was the test, really. There were A-class threats that were too powerful to antagonise or hunt down. I knew my Cape lore well. The level of power where people wouldn't want to ask those questions - or, even, where they would already know the answer and choose not to do anything about it - I wasn't there yet. I wasn't even close. I needed to be... Lung. That was the level. Not just strong enough to beat him, but known to be strong enough that I would beat him. I couldn't undo a clash with the PRT if they started throwing accusations around.

So I do nothing, letting Mush nervously peek out across the street as if waiting for Skidmark to round a corner and start screaming at her for associating with us at any moment. A comical sight, considering it was done in a mech that could stand and be almost as tall as the building she was hiding behind.

Organised. Not something I would have expected from the Merchants. Did the other gangs do the same? Somehow, I found it hard to imagine Hookwolf clicking through slides on his laptop, trying to give a presentation to the younger Nazis. "...did he ever ask?"

Better hope I get a better version of her powers, or I'll spend the next month sulking that the best thing I can tinker up is a glorified push bike." She snorts at that. "Alright. Think that's enough stalling - the small fry have bigger problems now. Let's go."

Sophia goes right. I follow the twirling butterfly to the left, letting it rest on my hand as I dip into my speed state to cross the distance.

Things had been a bit more chaotic than I'd expected tonight. I'd... maybe gotten a little carried away. Got a little too petty and spiteful over things that I shouldn't. Took a few risks. Got a lot of rewards. But just because I'd won big, didn't mean I couldn't win more. Squealer was the prize - the target - that I was looking for. Our time together had been all-too-brief back in the compound. If I could have stalled for a few more minutes, I'd probably already have the current challenge completed.

But it wasn't just about challenges. It was about real life too. Getting her alone, away from Skidmark - and away from my own teammates - that was everything I could ask for.

And when I look across the street to see the wild movements of a towering behemoth of a vehicle, with armoured slats thicker than my fist and turrets bigger than my head? When I see the convoy of lesser vehicles skidding and sliding around in her wake? When I see the shuddering blasts of flame, water and electricity smashing away the swarm clones getting too close to the terrified batch of Merchants unfortunate enough to not be safely inside a vehicle?

I'd never seen someone so vulnerable. She might as well have wrapped herself up for me.

After a moment's thought, I grab my phone - flicking it on and resting it against a nearby wall, setting it to record in the process.

Nothing wrong with a bit of self-promotion for PHO. Solid footage meant a lot to those who were interested. People like me - or, how I used to be, at least.

I slowly walk towards the behemoth. To my left, my ash clone stirs to life - falling in lockstep with me. To my right, a hidden tentacle snakes past my foot from the ash clone - barely visible even under the streetlights. The knight that forms on my right side isn't as flawless as the one I made against the challenge version of Mush. There wasn't enough metal in the nearest dumpster. It's a humanoid mess of cardboard and plastic as much as it is wood and steel - but the details aren't important for Mush's power. It doesn't have the materials to properly appear to walk like my ash clone and I - but the rhythmic slumping is close enough.

"Cape!" FInally, one Merchant notices my approach. I brace myself for a hail of gunfire, ready to shift from the momentary protection of Glory Girl's forcefield into the shadow state - already selecting the target vehicle I intended to dash towards.

Perhaps, because the regular guns were in such poor shape - and the non-regular ones were somewhat busy with the swarm - no such assault comes. Instead, one Merchant makes my decision for me. He takes his truck, and slams his foot on the pedal in my direction.

Thirty feet. Twenty. Ten. Five. Shadow state. Glory Girl's forcefield to eat the sudden 'acceleration' from landing right in the driver's seat, right in the face of a horrified driver that hadn't thought this far ahead.

"Hi." I whisper. I wrench the steering wheel sharply to the side, without breaking eye contact. I'm already out of there with the shadow state by the time the car careens off the road, flipping onto its side as the driver tries and fails to regain control in time to avoid a crash.

I grin widely towards the remaining vehicles, more of which were now directing their attention at me as the car behind me ignites - a terrified Merchant clambering his way out of it and sprinting away - getting all of a dozen metres before being mobbed by yet another swarm. My ash clone - with Mush's power active - seems to have found a good spot to secure itself, using the 'knight' formed by Mush's power to literally rip the closest barricade to shreds to reinforce itself. The knight was invincible so long as the ash clone stayed alive, and I doubted any of these guys would ever discover that fact.

This is what life is about. This is power. I wasn't a top-tier yet. But all the challenges so far meant something. I didn't need to be afraid of petty gangsters. I could trust my survival instincts. Trust my powers. Trust Taylor, watching over me with a mastery of the battlefield few could match. Trust the fact that I had a version of Squealer's power, and the briefest glance with it active told me that I had little to fear from her 'construct' save for the slow-moving turrets at the top.

Five vehicles, plus the juggernaut and the tinker inside. A dwindling number of Merchants that had no reason to have made it this long into Taylor's onslaught, save to give Squealer a reason to stay in place to defend them. Guns, webbed up - not quite as non-functional as Taylor probably thinks - but spent and incapable of being reloaded at least. Let alone aimed, given Taylor's omnipresence.

I can do this. I will do this. And when every Merchant blocking the way between Squealer and I lies broken at my feet... it will be time to have a long overdue chat with the Tinker of the Merchants.

First things first. I make a beckoning gesture to the next closest car.

"Next."

#2,543
Everyone on PHO loved to talk about how fights were chaotic and unpredictable. And it was true - how many fights had I lost to trickery, or weapons and new aspects of powers being revealed for the first time? Unexpected obstacles interfering with my best laid plans, crossfire from a different fight - there were plenty of ways to lose that were no fault of any particular lack of preparation or skill.

But on a smaller scale, when all of the cards were down? Fights tended to be simple. Each side only had a few paths to victory. There was a reason I don't lose against normal people anymore - I was immune to grapples and headlocks of all descriptions ever since I first defeated Sophia, so the only way for a regular guy to beat me was with a lethal weapon, or one singular blow that I wasn't ready for. And these days? I just didn't leave the same openings for one lucky punch or elbow to knock me out. Those openings had been beaten out of me, quite literally. And that was before all of my subtle and not-so-subtle powers gave me a way to cheat. There was a good reason I liked keeping powers in reserve that would save me from surprise gunfire, because in challenges - that was the most likely way for me to lose.

My route to victory here was clear. Wipe out the remaining merchants on the ground, find a way to enter Squealer's vehicle without getting a nasty zap in my shadow state - and then meet the Tinker face to face. Considering all the factors putting me at an advantage against the beleaguered, unprepared Merchants - that shouldn't be too difficult to manage. At least, the first part. Getting inside Squealer's vehicle - not so easy. That thing was a tank by any stretch of the name, and the stray sparks and stray wiring trailing across it to each of the weapon platforms left me no illusions that a poorly-considered shadow state might be the end for me. I had options, of course - but I needed time to experiment with them. Time that was uninterrupted by either onlookers or the driver - so, really, the core of my first objective was just to reach the centre of the convoy, without Squealer noticing, and without it being extremely obvious to everyone else that I was targeting Squealer specifically. If she got a clue and just decided to drive off, my chance was probably just gone - especially if she made a beeline to rescue and evacuate Skidmark. Very plausible. Too plausible. Actually, more likely to happen than me simply losing this fight. Take that into consideration, Greg.

Fortunately, Taylor was doing a good job of selling the idea that Squealer was doing something valuable with every second she spent here - an impression I was keen to encourage. Presenting another 'Cape' for her to handle via my ash clone and the puppet only made more space in the battlefield for me to carve a path towards her through her blindspots. And then? Crack it open, enjoy the reward inside. A simple challenge and done. I don't expect her to pose much of a struggle on her own.

...but that kind of thinking had me losing challenges to Skidmark, of all people. For all that today had already been a great haul - it could have been better. Should have been better, maybe. Or, maybe not. Skidmark's current cooldown timer was maybe a bit too long for me to get in the repetitions I would need to overcome his preparation - even my moderate success at barging through the front door stripped away a few too many of the melee-focused powers that I needed to overcome his regular power and the backhand of death he had access to. It was hard to imagine that I would have had much more success with only another attempt or two.

But it would have felt better, at least. Getting in attempts against walls like Skidmark and Mush were worthwhile failures. It was the lazy, slow start - the failure to consider the worst possibility - that had earned me my first loss to Skidmark, and paused my efforts against Squealer's current challenge that I was absolutely sure that I could beat. It wasn't a lack of skill. Neither of those challenges were beyond my means. I didn't have a single reason not to immediately close the gap against Skidmark's first challenge - even if I thought he was a normie at the time, I didn't have any ranged attacks. Rushing in and overwhelming the target would always be the correct play. I hadn't respected the CONT modifier against Squealer, and what she might do after I had... not cheated, but perhaps, not joined her in a fair race.

I didn't have a redo in real life. No failure screen waiting for me here. I fuck up like that, I'll just die. And that had a way of sharpening the mind.

But, in the same way - this wasn't like the simulations. The world wasn't twisting itself to present an unfeasible challenge to me, presenting me with a unified, cool-headed and well-prepared enemy. Quite the opposite - this was weighted in my favour, because even if Taylor wasn't exactly looking - simply having her within range was a cheat code all on its own. Squealer's turrets and toys were distracted with repelling Taylor's swarm, the only effective repellent against a seemingly-endless wave of chittering, buzzing clones. The gun-wielding goons were more of a danger to each other than me with their weapons - for once - as useless in their hands as they usually would usually be in mine. The creeping darkness as bugs moved to cover every streetlight, headlight and hastily-pointed flashlight was an asset to me - concealing the dark colours of my ash clone in the shadows and enabling me to dash from one car to the next, bludgeoning the drivers and leaving before they even registered I was approaching.

I feel strong. Invincible. A heady feeling that I actively push down on, forcibly conjuring up memories of my more ignominious defeats - the sudden turns in fortune that a hidden weapon or surprise attack could invite - but this feeling of dancing through shadows around a confused and disoriented enemy... I feel like I understand Sophia a little better, like this.

Maybe that sounds like something I should be experiencing with her power constantly - but, no. Not only did I have a distraction and a serious threat in the ever-present swarms swelling up into humanoid figures in the street - but it was also dark. And for all that my challenges and patrols took place in a variety of environments and times, visibility was rarely bad. Whether it was indoors, or the sun had yet to fully set, or my foes and targets gathered themselves under some streetlight or glowing sign - I rarely had an opportunity like this, where a few quick sidesteps out of the headlights of the trucks would make me as invisible as any power until I entered the cone of the handheld flashlights or one of the trucks spun back around to face me to try and hit me again - or at least to try and direct gunfire my way.

But none of the drivers seemed that motivated anymore. Perhaps because now that I had already closed the distance there was no longer a reason for Taylor to favour distraction over takedowns - the humanoid swarms start to collapse in on themselves and simply surge forward as a chittering tide - but even that is still theatre, because she had insects in position around their feet before the first shot had even been fired. Two, three, four Merchants break ranks and split off from the convoy. A pair of trucks split away from Squealer's formation along with them, one veering off the road and slamming into a wall as the panicked drivers discover that their vehicles aren't anywhere near as airtight as Squealer's.

The next truck I phase into has a driver that almost looks grateful to be bludgeoned into unconsciousness rather than dealing with the mass of chitin creeping across his face and crawling underneath his collar. The second truck in line seems to have benefitted from having their windows shut, but a quick punch to shatter the window on the way past is enough to let the swarm in - just because I didn't want to use a shadow state charge until the next one came back up. I slip into the shadows again as the headlights wink out, considering the 'fight' as it continues. There's still a certain jankiness to the movements of the swarm. Not quite as coldly practiced as I'd faced in my challenges. One Merchant seems practically paralysed with fear in the passenger seat as his driver gets overran, with him being entirely untouched until an errant flier bumps into him - then the swarm promptly splits in two and jumps on him as well. An imperfect search pattern, imperfect area awareness - proving that it was still possible to avoid her if you had the fortune to simply not have any bugs on you.

Not that such a thing was easy, when a massive swarm was surging through the air like this.

But it was an indication that she couldn't see through her bugs yet. Yet. I knew it was possible - and that would eventually cause problems for my secret-keeping tendencies... but not today. I was still happy to see how adeptly she'd taken my 'ideas' and incorporated them so extensively into her fighting style - happy for all kinds of reasons. Happy that one of my 'team' was finding such success, which boosted my own threat and reputation. Happy for Taylor personally, with all of her confidence issues a showing like this was bound to help out. Happy for my own ego, knowing that Taylor would forevermore need to attribute her boost in Master rating - and her ability to be more than a flood of pesky bugs - to me and my influence. Happy that, when all was said and done, perhaps the strongest Master in the Bay was already mine - a key marker of progress in my quest to seize the reins of power in the Bay.

The only thing to be unhappy about was that I hadn't been able to steal anywhere near the level of that power that I would expect from the challenges I had cleared. Sure, most powers had restrictions - but I couldn't even send a small swarm at someone, let alone use anything like she did. Yes, the Administrator power was probably still more of a net benefit than simply widening the reach of the original, pathetic, bug control power - but I couldn't pretend that I wasn't a little bit irate at the difficulties I was having claiming the rest of Taylor's power for my own. I usually didn't think about it much, but maybe recent losses were making it sting a bit more. Maybe my ego just found it easier to appreciate other people having good powers when I could confidently say that I could replicate sixty-percent of what they could do already. Shadow Stalker, for example. Taylor? Not even close.

I half-trip over a fallen Merchant, his unconscious body practically hidden in the shadows I was hiding in - I send a mean-spirited kick to his face, just for good measure. Wasn't like I could make them any uglier, and I didn't really want to waste my attention on the small fry anymore. For me, it was always about moving through the edge of the convoy and getting closer to its beating heart. Let the bugs, my ash clone and the formidable knight of twisted metal it was controlling draw any remaining eyes - I just needed to be close enough to Squealer before she decided to cut her losses and run.

Most likely, that would be soon. Now that Taylor had stopped sandbagging, the impact of the Tinkertech weaponry was no longer as notable. The harder-hitting cannon wasn't doing much to the knight either - save for the fact that materiel was being blasted entirely clear of its grasp, forcing it into a continuous cycle of tearing up new armour from disabled trucks while bullets and more cannonfire ineffectually attempts to disable it fully. My ash clone itself had taken the executive decision to cower under a car to save itself from being dispersed by accidental crossfire - and the tendril of power linking the latter to the 'feet' of the former had gone unnoticed so far in the poor vision and chaos of the battlefield.

...there is an argument that I should show restraint with that 'trick'. Challenges were one thing. Real life was another. The moment someone on PHO realised that the 'invincible' clone-knight was controlled entirely by the fragile, one-hit wonder that the ash clone was - I'd have people looking for that trick every time. Even now, the only reason my ash clone was still surviving in its current position was because heat and shocks weren't really enough to dispel it unless they came with a significant physical component - but even one unlucky bullet bounce would dispel it now, and keep it gone for quite a while considering the length of time it had been active. If one person noticed and took a shot, the secret would be all over PHO in a week even if they were arrested - and I wasn't going to kill them in real life just to keep a lid on something so minor.

Of course, there was an equal argument that - given the nature of my powers - I'd find just as much luck protecting myself by drowning such weaknesses via sheer quantity - security through obscurity. Having so many powers, so many combinations, that people are just unable to adequately learn, guess and train against them all. I didn't need much from a challenge to completely transform that power relationship into something entirely different - if my administrator-gifted powers no longer scaled down in potency when I selected a bug, or if Blessing could target my own clones to grant durability, if I could create more than one ash clone, or stack a defensive power on top of the ash clone itself. A mover rating like the rest of Oni Lee's powerset, some other form of Master power that worked with Administrator just as well as this one - giving me yet another angle of approach that nobody expects. Enough strength on the tentacle to burrow it through the ground and hide the ash clone that way. There were so many ways that the most logical 'next-steps' from my power benefited me, it almost felt silly trying to long-term conceal the existence of such a flawed interaction with so much room to evolve. If someone saw this and developed a countermeasure, maybe that was even good - it probably wouldn't work by the time they get the chance to try it.

I hunker down next to a truck, the driver having long-since fled towards the defensive semi-circle that the remaining Merchants were cowering in. I could, easily, break that line myself - but that wasn't the ultimate aim. Now that I was within spitting distance of Squealer, I could leave that part to Taylor and my clones. I needed to get myself attached to Squealer and her vehicle before she decided to cut her losses.

I activate her Tinker power. Of course, there was nothing that I could really make with it here and now - but it was good for understanding schematics. Not a full breakdown, but glaring hard at the front section of her truck and setting the power to think of ideas - when you get three ideas back that all involve a hidden trapdoor leading into the heart of the giant vehicle, it's pretty easy to notice that there might be a running theme with the materials I was providing.

The huddle of Merchants behind me starts to break apart under the slow advance of my knight. Good distraction. Keep distracting. A little slower, maybe. Squealer was only here because she was still able to 'help' those Merchants. Winning too quickly was a problem all on its own.

I quietly take a step out of cover and towards the target vehicle, stepping in an arc away from her likely cone of vision - assuming she was firing the weapons directly. A few seconds later, my hand is touching the closest wheel of Squealer's vehicle - and I gain a new appreciation for the size of it all. PHO joked about a Monster Truck specialisation - and it was easy to see why. I could barely stretch to reach the top of the rim, let alone find a neat way to propel myself up into the heart of the vehicle without clambering up the side first. I pause for long enough to allow Squealer a moment to react - but despite a slight revving of the engine, not a single turret even blinks in my direction. Undetected. Just as I had hoped. She just wasn't that kind of Tinker. Not the type to trust in some fancy software doing things for her. She wants to rev the engine. She wants to control the wheel. And certainly, she wants to fire the guns. So if she doesn't notice me, I'm home free.

Now, phasing through the armour would be a mistake with all of those cables around. But the 'trapdoor' that I had noted earlier didn't seem electrical in nature. So, with the combination of a foothold from Clockblocker, Vista and a healthy glide from Shadow Stalker-

-I take my first step onto the roof of the vehicle for the first time. I wince as the material of the roof gives a little more than I had expected from how sturdy the construction looked, freezing for just a moment to see if Squealer noticed the sound.

She does. The engine starts screaming, and its all I can do to throw myself at the nearest turret to hold on for dear life as Squealer sets out to prove that bulk was no obstacle to acceleration. She ducks and weaves through the streets, drifting around a corner and setting herself into a wild spin - leaving the collection of despairing Merchants behind as she does her best to dislodge me from my perch.

Fuck. Gave the game away a little too early. I'd wanted the opportunity to slowly probe the 'entrance' I'd found first with the shadow state before needing to commit, and now I couldn't really do that. My handhold was poor, and it was only a matter of time before she either succeeded in knocking me off, or realised that she it was just as viable to take over the weapons and start trying to blast me off instead. That meant I either needed to get inside now, or stop the vehicle now. Throw myself down the entryway blind, or drag the car from a roaring pace to complete stillness in a fraction of a second by having it crash into a clockblocked object.

Without knowing the situation inside, that second option could kill her. Did she even have a seatbelt? Would this thing explode if disabled? Where was she even sitting within the vehicle? I'd guessed it was the bulging area near the front that seemed to be a natural position for a driver - but that was all guesswork. Nothing internal was visible from the outside.

Why didn't I use the second charge of my shadow state to muffle my landing? No, I knew why. I just wanted to conserve my defensive options. I would have done it in a challenge to maximise the odds of success, but the threat of real life was getting to me. Only, my caution had put me in a worse position now. The smartest decision was probably to back off, look for another chance the next time she stopped. But, what were the odds of that? We've long since tipped our hand at this point - even the Merchants would have to realise that the smartest thing to do was scatter. This is what they did best - PHO was full of Squealer's escape clips for this exact reason.

If I let her go, the evening was over. No more challenges tonight. The reward vault at the end of the dungeon left unopened. Worst case, the whole thing might fizzle out before they even get around to sending a hero to investigate the ruckus.

Not a chance. Not a chance.

Think about it. The worst-case scenario of throwing myself into the entrance blindly - I find myself surrounded by some sketchy generator and a few hundred cables, with a gun pointing at me. That's the absolute worst case. A scenario so unlucky, so rigged, that it could have been drafted up by my power directly.

Squealer still wouldn't kill me. Not in that scenario, where I was essentially a sitting duck. Skidmark might. Maybe. Especially if he realised the odds of two blond assholes opposing him in the span of thirty minutes were incredibly low - but Squealer wouldn't. Because this was real life. And in many ways, that made it more of a game than ever before. I didn't have the reputation for brutality and lethality in real life and none of the Merchants really knew me. I was a pesky do-gooder who got too nosy, and they're a background gang too unimportant for the other gangs to stamp down on - and if Squealer gets a choice, she'll want to keep it that way.

You don't get to stay under the radar if you get the blood of the blue team on your hands. And she wasn't the leader. Even if she was inclined to hurt me, it wasn't her decision to make.

And in every other scenario? All of the likely scenarios? That entrance is no different to phasing through the sunroof of a mobile home. I get inside, it's a wide-open room or some kind of seating area with a bunch of Tinkery-looking levers to pull. The exact kind of situation where I would hold all the advantages in a confrontation.

Come on, Greg. Tonight's your night.

I hurl myself into the hidden panel I'd identified earlier as the secret entrance. Maybe if this was more obvious, I'd be worried about some form of trap protecting it - but it had clearly been deliberately hidden in a design without any other inkling of subtlety to be found anywhere. I'd been picturing it for minutes now and I still couldn't fully grasp the exact motions and movements required to even make the latch visible to the naked eye - but I didn't need to see it to phase through it. Exactly like a manhole cover, no need for a special tool or unlock method - if it's there, I can simply phase into the hole just past it without any of the fuss.

"Hah! You thought I was driving from the front? You and every other idiot!" The shrill, mocking tone emanates from the back of the large open area I find myself in. "You have any idea the number of times every Blaster in the Bay tries to take out the part of the truck where the driver is 'obviously' sitting? Anyone would start taking precautions, the way people in the Bay seem to act like I have a Brute rating to work with." I turn to face the source of the voice. An extremely smug-looking Squealer, half-swiveled around in her chair - one hand holding an extended steering wheel, the right leg keeping a pedal pressed to the floor as the streets zip by outside the window behind her.

And between us, layers upon layers of glass-like walls, coupled with no shortage of weaponry.

"Finally." A warm, wet feeling emerges with my breathy exclamation. A slight choke in my voice.

Squealer pauses. "Uh, buddy? For a guy picking a fight with the Merchants out of nowhere, you really sound like you're about to start crying right now. Don't- don't make this weird. I just want to slam you into a few walls and leave you in a crater choking on my dust, it doesn't have to be anything more than that. If you're that scared about facing me, I guess you could- you could surrender? If you really have to?"

She doesn't recognise me at all. And she's surprisingly chill about facing an enemy Cape.

"I'm not crying. I'm just happy. Happy that I took a gamble, and things finally went my way for once." I grin. "When it seems like the world is rigged against you for so long, you kind of forget how life is for normal people. You win some, you lose some. You get lucky sometimes without doing anything to force it."

"..." She stares at me. "Motherfucker. You're looking down on me right now, aren't you?" She snaps. "And here I was, acting all nice for the new kids on the block that doesn't get how things work - but you really think you're such hot shit that you can start bragging and planning your victory speech just because you got to meet me face-to-face? You think the Tinker isn't going to be able to do a thing from this position? Bitch, I will destroy you-"

I chuckle softly to interrupt her. I couldn't say she was entirely wrong. I was extremely happy to be facing her right now. I did think I was greatly favoured in this confrontation. But, above all, I was happy because for all the defences installed in this thing sitting between me and her - not a single one of them actually blocked line of sight. There were almost no Capes in the Bay with powers that really worked with line of sight, save for Oni Lee - why would you need countermeasures for something like that? "Challenge." I whisper.

This time, I don't hesitate to run. Vista into Shadow Stalker into Velocity, a tried-and-tested combo that is quite simply my best 'get out of here now' option from any given position. It's even possible to start the transformation into the speed state mid-air, relying on the rapid bleed-off of my mass to protect me from any serious damage while 'skipping' a fair amount of the time usually spent paralysed while my body maintained momentum through the air.

Damn, now that I think about it - I could incorporate my version of Skidmark's power into the trick somewhere. The effect on myself at low-mass must be significant, maybe I could even completely avoid appearing frozen at all with that pushing me constantly. Although, if I just tried it without practice and preparation - I'd most likely just end up with his power grinding circles into the concrete with my face for a few seconds. That would have been overkill for this. Squealer hadn't been all that fast at charging through the wall, and while she was probably looking to cut out the small-talk this time - it was probably a safe bet that she didn't start the challenge inside her tank. She had to run in, turn it on, steer it towards my side of the building and then-

The ground shakes behind me as the speed-state kicks in and I leave the scene in a mad dash. That.

Admittedly, there is a part of me left with the feeling that approaching this challenge honestly might have been more enjoyable. An honest race, an honest Tinker-off against the vehicle Tinker? It sounds fun. I didn't regret my delays with Shadow Stalker - but I also had reasons for going into that arrangement. The easy access I had to Sophia every day, the inability to progress normally anyway, my lacking hand-to-hand skills - none of which applied here. Yes, I could probably get some good advice on Tinkering - but was I really willing to forego simply getting a better power, and a better connection to Squealer, for some slim potential like that? If things didn't go in the direction I hoped today, there were good odds that I didn't see Squealer again until I was the strongest Cape in the Bay doing a tour of victory to pick up the forgotten scraps. This wasn't the time to play it slow, or worry about the 'feelings' the simulations were emulating.

Now was the time to win. To get strong.

So, sorry Squealer. That fair challenge you were looking for, it's not happening today - not that you seemed in any kind of mood to believe me last time around.

But I know you'll be looking for my tricks from last round this time. So you'll be facing a Tinker now - just the way I'd intended to face you before you so rudely interrupted me before. I wasn't going to be able to make a vehicle that could match up, but I had faith in my one, good design: The Mecha-Blade from Leet.

No, that wasn't right. Leet didn't make this. I made this. Sure, I'd started with his - with her - design, but... it was a giant fuck-off sword with an unnatural edge and a mechanism to swing it hard. I was hardly stealing the most innovative of ideas in the first place - and after I'd changed it from a weapon attached to a mech into something closer to an exoframe with a blade attached? Yeah. Not Leet's design anymore. This was mine. Copyright holds no power here anyway.

Well. Maybe my power didn't entirely agree that it was different - because the failure chances of the original were still there, and now there was an additional chance to... I inspect the design in my mind's eye again. Right. Part of the support frame could come unhook from the arm after the weapon makes contact with a target. Very low chance, not actually that impactful in regular use. Something that could compound into problems in a potential future version, but I was pretty happy that I'd gotten lucky on the 'new' failure point for this version.

And it was just a failure chance. As much as I'd bolstered Leet's mood with the talk of 'critical hits' - the same didn't fully apply to me. Or, it did - but only if I was a real Tinker that put enough effort in. I hadn't done a good enough job with the design for that. In a perfect world with infinite time, Leet's tech should only ever have one flaw - the latest 'quirk' of the most recent version. Every 'quirk' before that should be accounted for by the modifications that went into the next prototype. The simple mechablade had the 'critical hit' where it rapidly reversed the direction of the attack at an absurd speed - in the larger mech, that threatened to rip the entire thing apart and Leet had changed it into a remotely-piloted thing for safety reasons. The flaw was still there, it was just a 'special move' now that it didn't kill the pilot. That modification to the wider mech created a new flaw, and the entire thing became a race of failure conditions and patch-jobs fighting over what gave up first.

Problem: My exoframe - and I felt like a bit of a fraud even calling the loose collection of supports designed to go over my upper body something as sci-fi sounding as that - wasn't really good enough to handle that initial flaw in the way Leet and I did in our brief 'collaboration'. If I could control the momentum somehow, or get the thing away from my body when it fires... well. There's a dozen different ideas that could probably fix it. But, no - none that I'd been able to incorporate so far within the limitations I already had. Materials. Time. Skill. The space of the box I could 'paste' the design into - a real liability when so much of it was occupied by a massive slab of absurdly-sharp metal, even if did fold down somewhat. I wasn't arrogant enough to compare myself to the Tinkering greats just because I could print a design fast when needed. Leet could do better. Armsmaster could have done better. Hell, Squealer could probably do it too.

But, dammit - I'd built something that worked, I think. In theory. Shrunken down for my needs, but admittedly, still with the old flaws - which were now more of a problem than before.

Essentially, I had the same issue as the original mech had, except instead of the mech being twisted in half by the forces involved in the 'special move' it would now be my spine. There were probably ways to fix it, but really, it's something that I'd want to fix together with the new flaw that I'd introduced by making a second version. That part of the frame unclipping itself wasn't a serious problem, I was pretty fortunate for that. It wouldn't kill me if it happened, just slow me down while I re-secured it if I needed to keep swinging at a certain point. Trying to puzzle out the intended positives of the new quirk was a more interesting exercise - perhaps some kind of deliberate detachment could be implemented in the next version? Throwing the weapon in some way? Whatever. Leet's tech got by with dozens of similar micro-issues that went unaddressed, I'd have to do the same here.

I wasn't all that bothered. The original issue was the only one of note. Leet's design was mostly hydraulic-based save for the control panel, so my plan for an unexpected failure was simply going to be to use the Shadow State before the upper half of my body is separated from the lower half. I'd drop the weapon in the process, but most likely anything in a large circle around me would be in ruins. And if Squealer's vehicle was gone? I was going to win.

Well. I was getting a little ahead of myself. Because the workshop with all of my materials in? That wasn't an option for me right now. I wasn't sure if Squealer was just going to stay there in the tank and ensure I didn't return, or if she'd just started to loot my side of materials, or maybe even just returned to Tinkering on her own vehicle as if nothing happened - whatever her choice, she hadn't burst through the side of the building trying to find or chase after me. Which was good, in a way. Also, bad now that I think of it. Having the opportunity to ambush her as she drove around and completely take her out of the race again would have been amazing for me, and I would be able to preserve the secret about the fact that I could actually pick a fight with her vehicle without tricking her into driving around a corner too fast or into time-locked razorwire.

Nothing for it. My workshop may be gone, but there's an entire city full of resources here. There may be no people, but that didn't mean that the interior of all these buildings would be empty. There were computers to rip apart, tools to repurpose, pipes to stack up - certainly easier if I had the power tools that were right there where I started... but that was life. My amateurish attempts at Tinkering with the design are actually a boon here - because all of the materials I opted for were commonplace. I'm sure a stronger Tinker would have pencilled in some obscure alloy to reinforce the joints and maximise power and durability and that would have screwed the required material before my design would let me 'paste', but my simpler work could be satisfied with just ripping apart junk.

I had an hour. That should be plenty.

But that wasn't even a simple task on its own, even ignoring the technical aspects - how could I transport a weapon like that, keep it to hand on patrol, actually use it on him without relying on the shadow state as that would drop it to the floor before I could reform?

No. I needed something simpler. Smaller. Easy to use, easy to conceal. The idea of making a gun flits through my mind briefly, as forbidden as it seemed to be in my challenges - would that restriction hold true out here in real life? Maybe, maybe not. But, even if I could probably make a pretty cool gun if I put the work in - I didn't think I could make a gun so cool that it would match a barrage from Purity on a Lung that had yet to even truly transform. If he could heal and thrive off of that, I doubted I could make anything that would help unless it literally decapitated him in his base form.

And then I wouldn't get his power. So even if I did manage to accomplish something that the majority of the superpowered population of the city had been trying to do for years, it would be a complete own-goal anyway.

So what did I want to do? If I couldn't one-shot him, any true offensive would be pointless. That left retreating, or stalling. Escape, or containment.

I could probably work something out, using Squealer's haul. Easier, if Leet got around to answering her DMs anytime soon. I wanted to arrange another meetup, and snag Uber while I was there - but she hasn't been online on PHO ever since our last interaction. Probably enjoying TInkering with a new understanding of her power, which was understandable - but I just wish she'd do that after telling me where to find her. Because the only Tinkers in the Bay that I'd trust to do anything about in the face of Lung were her and Armsmaster - and I doubted I was beating the absolute bullshit that were the modifiers on the latter anytime soon.

I pause. No, that wasn't quite true. I had a... semblance of an idea for Armsmaster. The makings of a plan. But, in the face of the CONT modifier, it needed to be perfect the first time I tried it - and, most annoyingly, it needed me to die at least once against him getting the information I needed for it to work. As his first challenge, that didn't actually amount to a huge cooldown - but seeing Armsmaster at all was not exactly a regular occurrence for me.

Something to help in a fight, but not to cause injury. No active electricity while I was carrying it around. Or, if I couldn't deal with that, I'd have to hand it off to Taylor and let her handle it. Think. Leet's power, activate! Except, no. No flash of brilliance - no insane idea that just might work, that might break open the world of Tinkering for me forever. I had ideas, sure - but ideas more in the line of 'this is better than a dedicated team of engineering students could build' than 'this is going to turn Lung into a frog with the wave of a hand'.

I cast a slightly sour glance at the discarded sack in the corner. My greatest Tinker invention, bar none, was built from basically stealing a tried-and-tested design from Leet and then bastardising it for my own use. Even with my power providing some shortcuts, my Tinker powers were clearly intended to work in concert with somebody else. I should probably accept that if I didn't want to spend weeks iterating and improving on a design - I needed to stick to my roots: Being a shameless leech.

The teleporter beacon, then. I fish it out of the bag, taking another few moments to find the paired device that comes with it. Beacon, target. Simple. Intended as an emergency escape tool, except for a glaring weakness where electrical energy disrupted the scanning and calibration steps, which then threw off the targeting system. Which was a great thing for my power to tell me, but actually fixing that was no easy feat - my power didn't make it easy for me to work out how to fix it, it just told me the nature of the problem and whether said problem was still there or not.

But it was fine. Because rather than doing the equivalent of taking over a senior coding developer's work - 10,000 lines in the making, no comments and a vague description of the bug at the top of the file - I could just work around it. Fine. It starts to fuck up if it tries to transport electricity, even organic things. No problem. How can I use that? The first idea - simply using it as an offensive weapon - goes out the window. Lung would melt the thing before he got close. And even if it did work, what if he died? What if he didn't and just came right back at me from the relatively-small range it would drop him off at?

I scratch my head, skimming through ideas as Squealer's power surges to the forefront of my mind. Too many ideas. Too many possibilities, that all ignored whether it was truly feasible for me or not. I couldn't afford to be a regular Tinker that could hide away for weeks on a project. I needed an idea that just worked. And, was also useful to me. That latter part was the biggest issue.

"It's not going on a monster truck, stop that." Just needed to finesse my way around her specialisation first. "Not a tank. Not an offroader." More and more ideas stream through my head. "Not a bike. Not a-" I pause. "Actually, hold that thought." I was never going to get the power to separate entirely from the idea of this thing attaching to a vehicle in some way, the trick was more about getting a great schematic that I could then rip out of the vehicle and attach to a person - even if I had to lean on Leet's power to do it. It was an awkward way to do things, the necessity of switching into different Tinkertech powers and iterating on the different designs and failures didn't play well with the lengthy cooldown on my paste-box - and I wanted to save that for any sudden meetup suggestions from Squealer or Leet anyway.

Good old Tinkering by hand. That was fine. I needed the practice, and I needed some way to pass the time anyway. I didn't have any real plans today, and the city was usually pretty quiet the day after a big fight like that happens. Neither Taylor or Sophia had raised the idea of another patrol this weekend, which made our next likely meetup Monday night.

That gave me most of the weekend, including the nights, to get this thing into functional shape.

Loads of time. Maybe I wasn't a true genius, but let's face it - I'm better off than most. My experience and knowledge, born from wading through pages and pages of threads discussing every change across every ArmsCycle version - would shine through here.

Resources? Not an issue. Probably. Squealer had offered up access to one of 'her' scrapyards during our 'negotiations'. I didn't really need much in raw materials, but if Squealer's power wasn't going to give me any ways to implement this design without having an oversized vehicle around it - then I may as well start with an actual vehicle.

I zip away from the garage in my speed state, scattered collection of tools and the oh-so-crucial teleport beacon from Squealer tucked under my arms. Small enough for my speed-state to register them as attached to me, fortunately - or this would be one awkward trip.

Ten seconds later, I zip back - and put on my mask. Not in a challenge right now Greg, pay attention.

Tinkering time.



---



It doesn't take long after I arrive at the unmarked, fenced-off location - which appeared to be something closer to an abandoned towing business - to realise that Squealer might have exaggerated the value of one of her 'premiere scrapyards' when negotiating for my assistance. Namely, that she'd already picked the place clean of all of the good stuff. There was hardly a vehicle in sight that hadn't been cored out for parts or general scrap, leaving behind hollow shells that barely helped with the designs in my head at all.

I couldn't be mad. I got everything I wanted out of that transaction anyway, and maybe it was a bit too much to expect a thriving scrapyard from a gang too weak to hold any territory worth holding at all. And, at the end of the day - it wasn't like she'd be able to hide her better scrapyards and resource stores from me once we were properly Tinkering together. I could be patient on that front. She'd come to me, I'm confident about that.

And the fact of the matter is, I could still use this place. It would just be a little more awkward. Nothing here was capable of being driven back to my 'workshop' - but I could build here just fine. Nobody seemed to be actively watching the place save for the stoned guard at the entrance that took one look at my mask and pointedly looked away to mind his own business, and it was tucked away enough from the main roads that I wasn't worried about any passers-by getting curious about any noise.

I take some time to peruse the small sea of dead vehicles. This was every bit as much about seeing something that could prompt Squealer's power to make the right kind of idea as it was about finding resources. It wasn't enough to just want to attach a teleportation feature onto an existing vehicle, I needed the feature to work in a certain way - to offer a certain level of utility or combat potential to me specifically. Sure, a car that could teleport to the other side of the road was generally useful, but it didn't change anything for me personally. I needed a game changer - and directing the flow of ideas was hard, it felt more along the lines of browsing through a photobook of half-related suggestions rather than specifying my needs to a mechanic.

Not a sports car. Not a monster truck. The half-hearted suggestions keep coming. Employing the teleportation beacon as a method of repeatedly building up speed on a straight line just wasn't that useful to me. Nor were the next half-a-dozen ideas that come as I roam through heaps of discarded, twisted metal. A 'digging machine' that simply transported the material in front of it away? Interesting, but still - useless.

Would I need to use Leet's power in the end after all? I didn't want to use it at this early stage. It added complexities and failure points that I didn't really have time to test against and mitigate. And as much as I loved the modified mechablade, there was little getting around the fact that it nearly killed me in the challenge - I didn't really want to test my luck in real life just because I had to lean on Leet's power to make not just the overall device, but the individual components. Not just one potential quirk, but dozens - even if the chances were low for now.

I eye up one gouged-out vehicle. A crane, of sorts - though not the type that would be found towering over the skyline. Smaller than that. Something to pick up heavy loads, swing them around and drop them somewhere - not too dissimilar to a forklift, except for the grabbing claws being clearly designed to pick up different loads from above rather than lifting from below. I'm about to dismiss the idea Squealer's power proposes again, until I pause in thought and consider it closer.

There was barely anything left of the vehicle. The inner workings that gave it any true lifting strength were long-gone - but that didn't matter. I had the vision. The spark of an idea as Squealer's power proposed the union of the Tinkertech in my hand, and the vehicle in front of me. I could see it. This vehicles cargo appearing directly within the clawed contraption, no need for any precision on the arm if you only ever needed to place materials down or drop them in place - for a moment, I can't help but be distracted by the idea of this becoming part of a larger manufacturing suite - but that's not what I'm looking for right now. The design was there. Not perfect, but a good enough start. I seize onto it. The way the teleportation beacon should be embedded within the arm itself, the extra power cable that would be required, affixing the destination-targeting markers onto the tips of each claw - and how to redesign the 'bracelets' to account for the new, non-human cargo.

Two problems. One, as expected, the design was too big for my paste-box. Not that I would have it back for another few hours still, but that was a problem. Two, even once I was done - everything would still be firmly attached to a vehicle that wouldn't move - and that I wouldn't want to use even if it would.

One thing at a time. That first part? Fine. I knew this was going to need some real Tinkering, and this wasn't going to be a one-man job anyway. My ash clone - and with it, the knight and the Brute rating that came with it - were the next best thing to powertools that I had without getting back to my workshop and the freshly-acquired collection inside. And, if I wanted, I could go and buy or find whatever I was missing while my ash clone took over the tinkering. The second part? Well. I could say the same thing about Leet's sword not being designed for anything other than a mech, and I managed to make that work - didn't I?

I could do that.

But of course, a vehicle like that didn't help me - but the actual utility might. Looking at what it actually does, ignoring what it is attached to? I could use it. Flip the script. Instead of transporting movable things away to a set beacon, transport fixed-in-place items towards me as I move around. I carry the beacon personally, slap target markers on whatever needed moving before my patrol and trigger it whenever I need it. I already have a few stashes of confiscated grenades lying around, the natural consequences of stumbling the hideouts of random gang members here and there - being able to teleport those, directly onto my location with no real warning, then phase out? That could be the 'oomph' that I was missing in my kit. Adding containment foam to the mix would be nice too, except - I didn't know where to get that.

Correction, I didn't know where to get that without being a thief. I knew exactly how to walk into the rig, and I'm confident at least some of the passwords I remember will work - it's just, it will be pretty obvious it was me once I use them - or just once they review the tape. Unlike my challenges, there were consequences here.

I'd have to work on that one. I couldn't exactly ask nicely to get containment foam. I don't think they even gave that to New Wave, and certainly wouldn't make them available to me - not while I was still skirting the line of vigilantism. Normal grenades for now. Just for Brutes, of course. I'd want some kind of mechanism to prime them before detonation - teleport a bundle at once for added effect. The range of the teleport beacon already scaled up as the objects got smaller, so with the right set-up I didn't need to limit myself to grenades. I could tag different items in advance, ensure I was never truly unarmed. Never truly that far away from my costume. Give myself access to tools, to first-aid kits, carry a phone without leaving it powered off all the time to carry it in the shadow state.

The more I think about it, the more I like it. It's not such a departure from the original purpose of the device that I was moving into uncharted territory. I was just making adjustments - moving the order of operations around a bit. Adding on minor features that didn't really affect the part of the device that was pure Tinkertech bullshit. I wouldn't need weeks of Tinkering and experimentation to complete it, all the hard work was already done.

And actually making it was simplicity itself. I couldn't skip straight to the final product, but I could build the working example on the vehicle frame as Squealer's power intended - and then strip it out and slim it down for personal use, in precisely the same way I did for the mechablade.

My ash clone stirs to life next to me, and a moment later, a stray tentacle ekes towards the nearest pile of broken metal and discarded nuts and bolts. The familiar image of my knight slowly forms as the tentacle folds over itself, increasingly coated in a rusty, metallic coating as more and more trash is gathered into itself.

I nod to myself as it starts to tear into the nearest car, Brute strength messily separating metal and plastic into different piles as it attempts to gather the resources I need to complete the design.

As for me... I'm going to need to see how many tools were left behind in my workshop from the previous owner, or maybe just buy some new ones. I might not need to get the complete design working, but this was certainly too big to leave in the hands of the paste-box.

But I could do it. And it would be amazing.

And everyone would be falling over themselves to see it first.

Step. Waddle. Step. I fumble for the door handle somewhere in front of me. Somewhere- there. Push open.

"Gooood afternoon Parian!" I cheer through the open doorway, not spotting her at the counter.

A dark shadow looms over me, I tilt my head over my shoulder to note the imposing figure of an oversized gorilla hanging over me. Not quite up to her usual work, but the vague shape was there. And, presumably, the power. I knew how these things tended to scale with size. The arms might look soft, but that thing was probably in the top 3 Brutes in the Bay right now.

"I like your bouncer! Very cool!" I call out, absently stepping through the doorframe. Not that I had much choice. My mobility was... somewhat impaired like this, turning around at this point wasn't an option.

A pair of gigantic teddy bears flank me on this side of the doorway as Parian finally enters the room and steps towards me - every graceful, deliberate step leaning into her doll-like costumes theme.

Good enough for me to work with. I wasn't just here to show off, after all - getting a glimpse of the rogue was all I needed, and honestly was 90% of the reason I even showed up here.

Enough getting sidetracked. I don't know how long I have before Parian kicks me out, so getting attempts in early might be important here and let me squeeze an extra in before I leave. "Challenge."

Plus, challenging her before someone started talking always made things easier. Keeping track of where I was in the conversation when challenging someone mid-speech is deceptively hard - going straight from an all-out brawl in the dirt straight into an innocent questioning look at my extended silence? I'd like to see someone else try, that's all I was going to say on the matter.

I shake my head. Refresher. Parian. Level two. If I remember rightly, similar to the first - near-invisible tripwires all across multiple floors of a hotel, touching any of them can 'aggro' her and cause her to start making her usual inflatable dolls to defend and attack with. I'd relied on stealth to get close for the first challenge, not understanding what I was even dealing with at the time - but appreciating that giving her less warning to build her larger, more powerful dolls was a good thing.

In this second challenge, the only real difference seemed to be that she was already moving - not actively fighting, but moving between different rooms and acquiring materials to work with. Making smaller dolls, even if she wasn't actively in combat mode yet. That meant that speed, not just stealth, was important here.

Would have been important. To another Greg. A weaker Greg - one who would have struggled with that requirement more. At that time, I would have only had a single shadow state slot with a sizable cooldown to work with. Being perfectly stealthy would have taken too long, left me fighting an oversized doll that I had no means of beating by the time I finally climbed up to the fourth floor where I'd found her before.

With the extra shadow state charges? With the second level of administrator unlocking so much extra versatility and intelligence out of my ash clone? With the knight? With the extra tricks I had now with her own power and clockblocking? I knew my limitations clearly now. The danger wasn't from her knowing I was coming, it was from not having a true answer to her largest creations. I only had to reach her fast enough to deny her the materials that she needed to reach that point, and rely on my experience and powers to carry the rest.

So it shouldn't be a surprise to anyone that I choose to simply surge up through the floors with no regard for subtlety, jumping off a nearby ledger to give me the height needed to reach the ceiling. First floor. Second floor. Third floor. I pause. Two seconds. One second. Zero. The first shadow state charge comes back off cooldown. Fourth floor. I brush my hand through the stream of ash as it starts forming the second I leave the shadow state. Mush's powerset slips away from me, the tentacle already racing towards a nearby, half-open door before the figure is even fully humanoid.

"Parian!" I roar my challenge out, not immediately seeing my opponent. The REAL modifier was to my benefit here. She had previously preferred to send dolls out to attack - aiming to stall rather than simply hide and hope I didn't find her.

Which meant that the moment two teddybears start bouncing and drifting around a corner to meet me, I know exactly which direction to find my target in. I couldn't entirely ignore the smaller dolls, they still possessed enough of a Brute rating to cripple a limb with a lucky hit - but there was a reason I only feared the larger constructs. These were pretty slow and predictable, especially so far from the guidance of the Master behind them.

I duck and weave past them, juking to the side and sprinting past before they can halt their momentum and come back after me. A stray thread pulls free from my clothes as I manipulate Parian's own power into a ready-to-use string. And then, Parian is right in front of me - ripped curtains already spinning through the air and forming into an uneven shape as I burst through the door. A moment later, my manipulated string settles into the doorway in a brutish criss-cross pattern. A brief touch clockblocks the entire thing, sealing us both in for the time-being - and momentarily blocking off the efforts of the two teddy-bears from catching up to me. Not that they could be deterred, but I wasn't alone here. My ash clone pulls one away and hurls it into the wall, backing away to dodge the swipe from the second even as the knight moves to intercept.

The knight is small and weak compared to usual. Not enough of the right materials - a body consisting of half-used perfume bottles and loose bathroom tiles just didn't suit the power well.

But I didn't need a powerhouse. I just needed her current minions to not interfere, either by themselves or by Parian merging them into a larger form that could simply break through the wall.

I could handle Parian. And her incomplete project. I might have tried to clockblock the material she was using first, but her larger dolls did get forcefields and I had to make a split-second decision between blocking out the currently-formed dolls to take the 1v1 or settling into a more chaotic 3v3 where she would grow stronger over time and any stray hit on my ash clone would leave me alone against her growing group.

And I liked my chances in the 1v1. Until that doll grew limbs and could direct its own power properly, it was little more than an oversized brick trying to knock me into a wall. She'd shown that she could make a pretty respectable missile out of those before, but as far as her power went she could do much worse than be a budget blaster. I step towards the oversized, unshaped blob as it hurtles towards me - wielding enough force to kill any normal person - but I was far from normal. With my shadow state charges back, I had nothing to worry about. I pass through it seamlessly, lunging into melee range before she even registers my use of Shadow Stalker's powerset.

If she'd had time to finish the puppet locked inside the room with me, this would still have been a painful position. She was in costume, and I'd already found that her outfit offered pretty good protection from simple fists - I probably wouldn't fare well in an extended 2v1, not when one of those two had a Brute rating that I couldn't match.

But a mess like that? A simple ball, a boulder of force? Something like that couldn't discriminate in what it attacked. The moment I start grappling on the floor with Parian, she realises that fact too - that any attack with the orb potent enough to threaten me would also be enough to kill her in the process. And on her own? Not much of a fighter. I wrench at a poorly-placed arm as she seeks to defend herself, receiving a satisfying snap for my efforts. I slam my forehead directly into the centre of the mask, getting a stunned grunt of pain in response. I go back to swinging my fists at her as she flails under the assault.

To her credit, she doesn't slow or hesitate in changing tactics.
