And, ultimately, it wasn't like it was a true brick wall. There were plenty of powers in the Bay that could grant me the offensive power I needed. I just needed to meet the right people.

"Forget anything?" Her voice pierces through the fog as I return to the real world.

I make a show of patting my pockets as I step outside the door, taking care to not bash the protruding arm of the work-in-progress teleport beacon against the doorframe when I turn back around to face her. "Don't think so, unless I left some part of my outfit on the floor somewhere."

"That wasn't a question." She raises one hand in the air. A moment later, a screwdriver flies into it. "I told you, someone will trip on this if you just leave it around."

I stare at the object as she hands it off to me. No strings attached. Just telekinesis. "That's not made out of cloth."

"Very astute." She sounds amused. "Good night, Mr Cowboy."

"Your PHO entry really is just completely wrong. Maybe one of the most inaccurate ones in the city." I add absently. "Wait, so what actually is the limitation on your power? If you can move this, could you move, like - a grenade? Or, even-"

"Good night, Mr Cowboy." She repeats firmly. The undercurrent of amusement is still there, even as she closes the door and audibly locks it.

I glare at the door in faux-outrage.

She did that just to fuck with me. She knew speculating about her power would drive me crazy - and she was right, for more reasons than she knew. Because if her power wasn't textile-based, but simply works better with textiles - then how come my power rewards specified textiles only? I wanted general telekinesis too!

Alas. Nothing for it.

Time to head back. I hadn't only come here to see Parian, but to test out my Tinkertech. My little testing session had given me some ideas for the next step of my device, mostly working on slimming it down and refining it into something I can actually wear on patrol - but the controller for it was also probably a bit too clunky and easily waylaid. Not something I could rely on in an ambush, or easily fix and replace if it was destroyed.

Ideally, I'd make it something that was part of the design itself - but the 'part of the design' was still thinking it should be sitting on a disused construction vehicle. I'd need to lean on Leet's power to get the job done. Which was reasonable, so long as I was absolutely certain that I could handle the quirk that came out of it - and that I wasn't planning on iterating on the design afterwards. And I don't know if either of those points were true right now. I still had things that I could do with Squealer's power, as well as regular human ingenuity.

Actually, first thing I'm doing is swapping out the metal arms for something a little lighter. Or, even just a lighter metal. It was too heavy. Too bulky. The arm was obnoxious, but I was pretty sure I could just fold it down somewhere with relatively little effort - the only reason I hadn't already was because it was currently directing the approximate direction that the incoming teleports arrived in, and messing with that system without planning in advance seemed like a potential way to end up with something fused into my foot - or worse.

But those were all simple, relatively minor changes. In some cases, it wasn't even Tinkering - it was just, engineering. Moving one Tinkertech thing to connect with another. Once I'd stripped it down to the essentials - then I'd have something that was more than just a proof of concept. A weapon. A utility. The first of many, hopefully - even if I'd 'acquired' the most Tinker-y part of it from someone else, it was still mine.

I retrieve the remote. Change the dial to eight. Trigger. My ash clone catches the phone that tumbles out of the air, turning it on before passing it to me. Functional. If I could refine the targeting to become a bit more consistent as well, that would be great - but even like this, it was useful. A few limitations on total package size to consider, and the batteries would run flat at some point soon - they weren't exactly fresh when they went in - but not bad for a lazy weekend on my own, that's what I think.

I sigh. Back to Tinkering then. No such thing as a truly lazy day any more, even with school tomorrow - I still had a solid twelve hours ahead of me where I just didn't need to sleep. May as well use it. It could make a difference. Especially because refining this could result in a permanent armoury of sorts when out on patrol. Always having access to the modified mechablade if I could find the time to recreate it... well. I know it wasn't the most mobile or adaptable, and melee fighters had their own struggles against him - but even Lung or Hookwolf would have to fear and respect the power it could generate. It was the only anti-Brute weapon that I had aside from clockblocked strings, and teleporting it right on top of me was probably the only way I could bring it with me on patrol.

Were all of my Tinkertech toys going to have portability issues? I hope not. I need some smaller ones. Some fancy death-ray-pistol like the one that exploded in Leet's hands in their challenge. Something I can just tuck into my belt and have ready, without looking like I'm going to war.

I pause on that thought. Tools like that didn't have to be limited to Tinkertech - and I just got another one. A flex of will causes part of the seam holding my hoodie together unravel, enabling my ash clone to simply reach over and tear it off. I bring the upgraded textile manipulation power to the front of my mind as I inspect it. This one was different. A little stronger, yes - but I really needed to see if I could access a bit more of Parian's power. The real meat of it. The dolls.

I narrow my eyes at it. I know what I wanted, but it just wouldn't- I reach out to touch it. There we go. The hood folds in on itself in my hand, threads separating and binding to the opposing ends instead, forming a slightly off-shape ball.

A ball that slowly seems to inflate in my grip. I remove my hand, and the inflation stops - but the sensation of control remains. Touch limited for this part. Fine. I touch it again to resume letting the power seep in to the sphere - until, eventually, I hit a limit. Or, rather, until it seems like the amount I'm pumping into it is equal to the amount leaking out. I throw it from one hand to the other experimentally, bouncy - lightweight. And, most importantly, under my control - the same sensation of controlled manipulation as I had for the earlier thread-based power, except this was moving faster despite the extra size and mass. I have it float for a moment, then hurl it out to a nearby wall as fast as I can. About as fast as a child would throw a ball, nothing special.

Except it notably doesn't bounce off the wall to return to me. Instead, it makes a harsh thud and falls to the ground. I summon it back to me, the movement more sluggish than before - the power that I had poured into it already cut down by a third of what it had left my hand with. A problem with the materials? Distance from me? Some holes in the original hood that I simply hadn't fully closed?

I could work that out. What was more important was that - in my hand - I had a flexible ball again, greedily soaking more power back up into itself and reaching its limit again in just a few seconds. Soft and bouncy to me, but not to the rest of the world? That's how it seemed. On a whim, I toss it up into the air and slam my fist into it like I was hitting a volleyball. I use my control over the ball not to move it directly, but to guide it in a direction - preserving momentum while directing it towards my target rather than crashing uselessly into the ground.

The harsh sound of the impact on my target - an abandoned dumpster in an alleyway - resonates throughout the street. My ball limply collapses next to it, and I take a step closer to inspect the result. I trace out the side of the dumpster with a finger, marvelling at the near-perfect spherical indentation in the solid metal side of the container. Not quite piercing through, but drastically warping the thick metal all the same.

That had potential.

I scurry from the scene before anyone comes to investigate the sound, thoughts buzzing at the latest addition to my powerset. That was enough to kill a person if it hit them right, even if it might be a little difficult to aim at a moving target with the limited input the controlling part of the power had at those speeds. And it was a ranged attack. Not quite the one I was expecting or hoping to get first, but ranged all the same - with a bit of set-up, I would no longer need to be the one always obliged to close the gap as soon as possible in every fight. I might still be better off up-close depending on the matchup, but it wasn't because I had no other option any more.

My phone buzzes in my hand before I can consider the list of challenges where I could benefit from my recent power acquisitions. A new notification arriving the moment it finally finishes booting up.

The Brockton Tribune

PRT ENE set to announce new Ward!

In response to recent inquiries from the Brockton Tribune, the PRT ENE have confirmed that a reveal event has been scheduled for Tuesday the 5th of April at City Hall to announce the latest roster addition to the Brockton Bay Wards. While little is confirmed about the new hero and their powerset, we do have a name in advance - Browbeat! A name that certainly seems to evoke the feeling of an up-close-and-personal fighter. You can be certain that our reporters will be at City Hall to get all the juicy details about the newest addition to Brockton Bay's Cape scene, and perhaps, if we're lucky - snag an autograph in the meet-and-greet afterwards...

Well now. Isn't that interesting?

And here I was worried I'd have nothing to do this week.

A crossbow bolt thuds into the target. A half-second later, mine slams into a knocked-down table strategically placed in front of it.

"You didn't even try with that one." Sophia tells me.

"You mean it didn't work with that one." I wave the crossbow in my hand. "I'm telling you, I don't have that level of control."

"You can take things into the shadow state when they are touching your costume. You can select which parts of yourself and the objects you're holding go into the shadow state with you." She crosses her arms. "You're not thinking about it the right way."

"Or my version of the power doesn't work like that." I counter.

"Until suddenly it does. You suddenly go from an absurdly lame version of my power to what you have now? Even if you're right, why don't you think that will happen again? And if you're wrong and it's just a matter of practice and getting to master something that came to me instinctually, are you really just going to sit there crying about how its impossible - and leave yourself without any anti-Brute tools at all?" She narrows her eyes at me. "Hookwolf just kills you in a fight right now, you know that right? Lung kills you. Kaiser kills you. Krieg kills you. Mush? Pretty sure she stomps you in a straight fight too. Everyone with armour, everyone with a Brute rating - they all just naturally beat you until you have a weapon that can hurt them."

"Believe me, I know that better than anyone." I adopt a pained expression. More than she would ever realise.

"Then shut up and reload already." She raises her weapon. "Actually, don't do that." She looks around for a moment, then whips her shirt off and over her head.

I leer at her, deliberately misunderstanding whatever she was doing. "That time already? I don't mind-" She tosses the shirt at my face. "I don't really have that kind of fetish but-"

"Shut it. Hold that out with your hand. Go into the shadow state. Drop it on the floor." She settles back to watch.

I give her a curious look, but oblige. Enter shadow state, then a second shadow state that excludes the shirt - mission complete.

She hooks the fallen shirt with her foot and flicks it up at me again. "One shadow state. Drop it while you are inside it."

"I can't drop it, we're not-" I wave my arms in the air. "-physical. I'm a... blob of smoke that gets to reform after a second has passed, there's no fingers for me to release anything with - because when I'm all smoky, the shirt isn't being held anymore it's just moving along the same kind of vectors that the rest of my body is moving on. I haven't stepped into some shadow realm where everything is the same but spookier, the things that I'm wearing or holding are just more smoke, until that one second mark comes up and I either change what I'm targeting or reform. I can't let go of it anymore than I can let go of my entire arm."

"The one-second mark isn't important. You can still do things with your body to move around in that state. You run. You jump. You move your arm into a position to attack - just because it isn't solid yet, doesn't mean you aren't moving." She claps her hands together. "So instead of moving your arms or legs, let go of the shirt and toss it away."

I shift into shadow, stretch out my arm and- "That doesn't work." -watch as the shirt flutters down from my outstretched hand as gravity reasserts its hold only after I become solid again.

"It does work. It's just not instinctual to you for some reason." She growls. "This is basic stuff. How about this - hold it in both hands in front of you. LIke you were stretching it or something, except don't actually stretch it or I'll kill you." I obey. "Now. Shadow state. Left arm stays holding it, right arm goes and points to your right."

One shadow state later, the shirt flops to hang down from my left arm.

"Oh look, my shirt didn't suddenly stretch to twice its size just so that you could still be holding both ends afterwards. I guess you can let go of things after all!" She throws her hands in the air. "What a miracle. Who could have seen that coming?"

"The team's only got room for one sarcastic know-it-all." I grouch. "I don't know. I see the point you're making, it just feels... well. It doesn't feel like anything. I guess that's the problem."

"Did you know which hand it was in?" Sophia prods.

I blink. "What?"

"Which hand was still holding it afterwards - did you know?" She repeats.

I stare down at my hand. "I guess so. I knew it was the left one, I think?" I repeat the task. "Yeah. I guess I have a- a feeling of some sort. Not like I'm literally holding it, but - I know its there. Or, will be there."

"So. We've established you can let go of things in the shadow state. Now. Do it again, but let go with both hands." She raises an annoyed finger into the air. "And don't give me the bullshit you were spouting earlier. You were trying to argue that everything you were holding was all just part of your wider smoke-body earlier, in which case you should be able to control how that appears when you reform just as well as any other part of your body. And if you can't do that because it's a separate object, then you have to be able to treat it like a separate object and let go of it. You can't have it both ways."

I repeat the task. Both arms to the side. A second later, the shirt is dangling from my right hand. "Told you."

"What do you mean, 'told me'?" Sophia looks like she wants to throw something at else at me. "You're holding it. You're literally holding it!" She grits her teeth. "Fine. Don't hold it. Put it between both hands, like you were about to clap and it got in the way - so you're stopping it from falling. Now. Go again."

"Waiting for the cooldown." Two. One. Zero. Shift. Both arms to the side. A second later, the shirt reappears - already on the ground.

"You see! You see now?" Sophia gestures wildly at the ground. "It isn't welded to you in the shadow state after all. You stopped holding it, and it fell down on its own. Now, you just do the same with your hand instead of your arms."

"Holding something and releasing it is different to something just... not falling down because I'm exerting pressure on it, and then taking that pressure away." I argue.

"You literally just described how everything works under gravity." She glowers at me. "Go on, Mr Physics guy. Why would this magically work for your arms, but not your fingers? It's the exact same thing, you're just not visualising what you need to do as easily."

"I didn't mean it like that. I just mean, my powers sometimes put in random restrictions like that - it can be pretty arbitrary at times. Like Clockblocker's doesn't let me do things that someone is wearing or goes around them. Like, freezing a rope around them? Banned. Freezing that same rope against their chest without looping around? Fine. Sometimes its just like that. My power isn't an exact copy of yours, we know that."

"It isn't like that here." Sophia denies. "This is a toddler that's worked out how to stand, trying to tell me that it's impossible to lift one foot and put it in front of the other. 'But I'm not exactly the same as that adult over there!'" She adopts a whiny voice.

"Why am I the toddler now? There's got to be cooler examples you can think of." I gripe. "Don't get me wrong. I get what you're saying, and it sounds logical, but it just doesn't really click. The feedback of my body, that kind of precise movement - I don't feel it. Clearly, you're getting way more control and sensation over this than I am - to me it's like, I go in with a certain momentum and an idea of where I want to end up, and I can definitely achieve that, especially when the time comes to reform. But doing things outside of that window right at the start and end of each shadow state? It's just... I don't know, like I'm controlling something shaped like me, rather than just me. Or, no - better way to describe it. Like it's actually my shadow. Of course I can move my shadow by doing big motions while the sun is behind me, but small and finicky details just aren't going to show up until the shadow state comes to an end."

"Always with a new excuse." Sophia groans. "You're overthinking it. If you can't do it on a small enough scale yet, fucking practice it on larger things and work down."

"Yeah, I get it. I'll work on it, believe me - I'd appreciate the extra versatility if nothing else. What was even the point of this exercise again? I'm trying to shoot holes in things, learning how to litter in the middle of my shadow state doesn't help with that." Not that this was completely useless. Despite my complaining, splitting things out from my shadow state had never been an area that I'd successfully explored before - something I didn't even think was possible without the final power upgrade from Sophia. The general principle of being able to place, throw or shoot things through a wall without going through or even getting close myself had a lot of potential - regardless of the fact that I clearly didn't get the same instant-mastery tutorial package that Sophia had gotten.

"Proving a point. And it's a basic step of being able to disassociate where you start and the bolt ends. If you can do that, then you can work on keeping the momentum of a moving object as you turn it into shadow." She mimes throwing a bolt like a dart, fading into smoke at the last moment of the throw - resulting in a noticeable puff of smoke exiting her form and coalescing back into the dart shortly afterwards.

We already knew that Sophia and I couldn't just turn anything we touched into smoke - as in, we couldn't touch a wall and the entire structure disappear or come crashing down around the missing support. But we could do it to our clothes. And weapons. And some things that we were holding, but not others. I'd already encountered the mass limit when using the mechablade, but Sophia seemed to have a better grasp on what her power decided was attached enough to her to count. My attempts to justify 'holding' the bolt via touching it before firing hadn't counted enough to work, but phasing the entire crossbow in my grip - loaded bolt and all - apparently was fine. Powers were arbitrary sometimes, I'd prefer a hard-and-fast rule that I could munchkin around rather than working based off of feelings - sometimes it felt more like I was trying to squeeze results past a referee selectively enforcing the rules on a whim than executing scientific theory.

She retrieves the fallen weapon. "If you can do that, rather than killing the momentum completely - then the hard part is done. Then all you need to be able to execute it is to be fast enough to do it the instant you release the firing mechanism. It needs to be complete second nature to get the timing right, and you need to be able to do it in the middle of a fight - not some cozy shooting range with me holding your hand the entire way."

Well. Separating myself from a held object was one thing, applying actual momentum from within the shadow state was the end goal - and Sophia's aim of simply keeping the already-existing momentum was a happy middle ground.

I retrieve the crossbow. Aim. Fire-and-shadow-state. The bolt limply flops to the ground a few inches in front of me as I turn physical again. "Think I might skip straight to this step. Less for me to think about, I've just got to... stop the bit of my power that's making the weapon cling to my movements, don't need to actually move myself at all."

"Do what you like." She sighs. "It's not like this is something I've ever had to teach anyone else, maybe it really is easier to learn that way - who knows. I'm guessing as much as you."

Reload. Aim. Fire. This time, the crossbow itself is carried a half-metre across the room before turning physical and dropping to the ground. "That's a good sign."

"It is?" She makes a show of peering at my discarded weapon. "You're right. Maybe your enemies will think you're surrendering when you throw your weapon at them, or they'll think you're so clumsy that they die laughing rather try to fight you."

"It shows that it works, I'm just not precise enough to do the bolt rather than the entire thing." I roll my shoulders as I retrieve my weapon of choice. "It's progress. I wasn't so egotistical as to think I'd get it first try."

"Yes you were." She replies instantly. "That's why you were so dead-set on the idea that your powers just didn't allow it. You never considered for even a second that it could be a- what do you always call it -a skill issue?" She smirks. "I actually did do it on my very first attempt though, if you were wondering."

"I wasn't, but good to know." I respond sourly. Couldn't entirely deny that. "And you shouldn't sound so proud of doing it for the first time when the first attempt was several months into your Cape career when Armsmaster told you to do it in power testing."

She scowls at me. "Yeah? And how would you even know what I worked out on my own and what came up in power testing?"

The fact that I know exactly what the vigilante-era Shadow Stalker was capable of with her back against the wall, for one. I know you didn't have that trick then. "The fact that you didn't deny it tells me everything. Don't tell me you're embarrassed that you didn't think about it yourself? That's cute."

"I was doing something pretty similar already, they just had a few extra ideas." Sophia dismisses. "And, so what? They've got guys paid to do nothing but sit around a table and think about possible power interactions all day - it's no surprise that they came up with something useful eventually. At least I could do it instantly when prompted, which is more than I can say for your dismal efforts." She drawls as my crossbow clatters to the floor again.

I hand the crossbow off to my ash clone as it stirs to life next to me. Assign it as an administrator, hand it the shadow state powerset and...

I click my tongue in annoyance as it fumbles, too. Damn. I was hoping that the administrator's usual competence with powers would be useful here, but it's actual skill was usually a mirror of mine - except for not having to worry about the downsides of being a living, breathing human and being able to multi-task and switch between orders much faster than me. I'd need to improve my own ability first before handing this task off to my favourite powerset.

Reload. Aim. Fire. Reload. Aim. Fire. Retrieve all the bolts scattered across the empty shooting range. Reload. Aim. Fire. A bolt flies a full six metres before lodging into the ground. Sophia perks up a bit in sync with me at that.

The issue was that there wasn't really enough separation for me to split the two objects apart in my head. When it turned to shadow with me, it was part of me - it stuck to me in the same way that my clothes did. I needed to identify and split that precise part off in the tiniest fraction of a second before the velocity of the bolt was completely arrested. Too early, and the bolt didn't fire correctly in the first place, too late and the bolt was no longer touching the mechanism and wasn't included in the effect of my power. I'd already proven that I could do it, but to actually shoot with full power I needed the equivalent of a frame-perfect input in a fighting game.

Or, I needed to stretch that 'perfect' timing window out. I focus for a moment, swapping to Vista's powerset. Stretch space out in a small, narrow 'tunnel' where the bolt should release from, line the crossbow perfectly into the air where that tunnel was made. Aim. Fire.

I'm denied the satisfying thunk of the crossbow hitting the target, but only because the target is too close. Not entirely on-target, admittedly, but if not for the fact that the one-second mark hadn't passed by the time the bolt struck home it would have been a perfect shot to prove that I could actually do it. I turn to grin at Sophia. "Not bad, right?"

A smile almost reaches Sophia's face before she smooths it into a scowl. "Still with the one-second limitation, I guess that's going to stay a problem if you're using anything with real power behind it." Sophia shakes her head. "It's going to mean you have a massive minimum range, and the level of timing required to shoot someone through a wall is probably going to be too much of a pain to make work." She sounds frustrated at that.

I shake my head. "Well, I'll probably get a less-restrictive version of your power at some point - but that doesn't mean that I can't use this now. I've got a workaround for timing." Doing that to bugs that I infused with the administrator powerset killed the bugs, and it seemed to damage the ash clone enough for it to lose its stability too. But more importantly, by ripping away the administrator power - I had the shadow state back. Not the ash clone. And not the bolt either. After passing through the table blocking the target, it re-materialises and slams home.

Thunk.

I grin at Sophia.

She rolls her eyes at me. "You still missed."

"Something to work on." I allow, pacing towards her. "But we still did it."

"You did it." She half-corrects, half-affirms. "May-mphh!" She flails angrily as my lips meet hers. "What- what was that for?"

"Am I not allowed to show my appreciation?" I'm too old to attempt puppy-dog eyes. I try anyway. "You took time out of your day to teach me something cool. I appreciate that. I appreciate you." I am going to kill so many people with this once I master it.

She looks away and makes a great show of picking up some nearby bolts to try and hide her darkened cheeks. "I barely did anything. And what I did do, I only did because seeing you use my power so badly was reflecting poorly on me." She insists. "It hardly makes sense to hold back something useful if it might make you more effective at cleaning up the city. And, you were pretty cool the other day - just think of it like a reward for walking the walk."

I grin. "Yes, yes. You're the cool badass that has never done anything for anyone else's sake, ever. I believe you."

She glares at me, but doesn't comment. "Pass my shirt back." My ash clone throws it to me, I throw it again. "Thanks." She pauses. "That was unlike you."

"Hm?" I tilt my head at her.

"Just giving it to me like that." She narrows her eyes at me. "Usually you'd do your best to keep it away, or try to get the rest of my clothes off somehow. At worst, some comments on how you prefer the view like this."

"I could still do that if you want?" I offer.

"No!" She pauses for a little too long. She clears her throat. "I just- I'm suspicious. Spill."

"Am I really that obvious?" I stroke my chin. "Well, it's coming up to school time - and I was hoping to keep in your good books for a while longer. Because what I've got planned is probably going to make you mad at me."

"I'm not doing anything in public." She snaps. "Those classrooms are bad enough, last week was too close-"

"Not that." I cut her off with a smile. "No, something that might legitimately upset you." I pause. "I'm, uh, planning to apologise to Taylor. About the whole argument we had - that whole situation."

"Huh." Sophia doesn't seem to have a strong reaction to that. "For real?"

"I mean, I'm still a little annoyed at her - feels like I trusted her, but she didn't trust me. But, yeah, I get how it looks to her. It only looks like a realistic thing for 'Greg' to do when you realise I've got powers now and that I'm a different guy than I was." I shake my head. "To her, I get it. It looks like her only friend is either deliberately leaving her for Emma, or is just an idiot getting tricked into thinking he's helping her by hitching up with Emma. That's totally something Emma would do to hurt her, so reaching that conclusion makes sense. I can't be mad at her for just not having the right context."

"Except she does, because you outed yourself like an idiot and only got saved by the fact that she ignores everything you send her by default." Sophia points out.

"She doesn't - didn't - ignore everything. She's just bad with technology, and including it in a video game invite was maybe a bit too far." I feel the urge to defend our old friendship. "We saw eye-to-eye on a lot of things, that just wasn't one of them. I understand it."

She raises an eyebrow.

"I didn't say I wasn't annoyed. I said that I understood." I half-concede the point. "I didn't even mean to out myself like that anyway. I was just kind of making it up as I went along, and realised it after the fact. The point is, regardless of the reason - she didn't know. She thought I was a regular guy that had never so much as kissed a girl before, and assumed that Emma was successfully plotting to steal away her only friend. "Exactly what we agreed to do." She attempts to shrug herself free from my grip. "Putting this bitch in her place after she started thinking she was better than you this morning. Thanks for finding her, we'll take it from here. Mads, Sophia - come on, look at her hiding already!"

Ah. So that's how it is.

"I see." I did see. She was going to put on an act in front of Taylor to try and make it seem like this was all part of my plan, joining the Trio in truth. "So the whole conversation we had before now was just, what. Performative? A big joke that I wasn't included on?"

"What are you talking about, stop being weird and let's just go already-" She attempts to push my arm away. I tighten my grip. "-let go, you're hurting me-"

"And when I was telling you the choices that you had. Explaining how things worked between us. You didn't really listen to any of that." I don't take my eyes off the struggling redhead. "When I made it clear that your choice was to either step aside while I had this talk, or bury the hatchet at the same time - you chose the third option. You weighed up me, our relationship for the last few weeks and everything we've done together - and decided that was worth less to you than getting to bully Taylor a little more."

"Don't do this in front of her." She hisses. "This is for your benefit-"

For a moment, I wish the completed challenge symbol by her head would wipe itself clean. Offer some kind of bonus stage. I think I needed that right now.

That is funny. That is very funny.

Four challenges completed. Four doses of what was essentially a master power. Weeks of quiet conversations, passionate fucking across the school, ideologies fully in-sync, slotting into her friend group and putting up with all of her bullshit so far.

"You were just leaving." It isn't a question.

Madison nods swiftly and turns on one heel, beating a quick retreat.

Taylor is oddly silent.

I'm pretty sure the feeling is mutual, so she might actually be a lifesaver here.

No. She's not good enough for me. I hadn't even considered this as a serious possibility that Emma would choose this... hobby, over me. It was insulting to even imagine. Sophia must have considered it as likely, but she didn't know about the Master aspect of my powers. That should have been enough.

Hell. After all of this, it should have been enough without any Mastering at all. Was there even a single 'real' relationship in the entire school that would have failed this small of a 'test'?

"Fuck. Off." I repeat. "I wasn't asking."

Hurt flashes on her face for a moment. Not too long ago, I'd have felt bad about that.

Look at yourself. Look at how much better things have gotten for you since I gave you a chance. Your social status, your attitude, your sex life - you didn't have any of them before I decided to give you a chance. I did that. I made you into what you are, and without me - you'll go right back to that life. But at least you'll have Taylor, right? Maybe, if you keep on humiliating yourself enough - she might deign to let you sit in the cuck chair while her Merchant friends run a train on her. And if you're really good-"

I wanted to beat someone into bloody submission until I was too spent to be angry.

I grab her arm and throw her towards the floor. She drags me down with her. We grapple for a moment, trading one punch after the other - neither truly seeking to win like in our usual fights, just to land some hits. For a moment, it looks like Emma might try and join the fray - but takes one look at the frenzied exchange between Sophia and I before backing off. She heads towards Taylor instead, juicebox raised like a weapon - only for Taylor to surge out of the cubicle instead and knock her to the ground. Surprising from Taylor. Maybe it shouldn't be. 'Arachne' wasn't exactly a pacifist, but for some reason, it felt strange seeing Taylor act anything like her. I couldn't make out much of the half-hissed, half-whispered conversation that was going on between those two as Taylor holds Emma in place, but Sophia was clearly looking to get away from me to separate them rather than continue trading blows with me.

Not just because she was losing. Sophia was skilled, of course. But of the two of us, she relied on her powers more to keep our fights close. Certainly, she was still better than most - and that meant something coming from me - but her instincts were all wrong. The momentary hesitation as she stops herself from phasing through an attack and countering, and that hesitation is all I need to press an advantage. Bigger. Stronger. Tougher. We'd already done this song and dance before. I'll admit, I'm taking a beating too. I'm actually enjoying the flashes of pain that come with every hit she lands, the violence is a pleasant, familiar distraction to keep my brain from lingering on what just happened.

Sophia bites down on my fist as I linger on a blow a moment too long. Then my grapple falters into nothing as my fingers slip through thin-air, a momentary shift of part of her body into the shadow state - just slight enough to ruin my hold without clearly exposing her power, just significant enough to give her leverage over me instead of the other way around - unless I was willing to repeat the trick in a game of chicken to see who can cheat the most without outing themselves.

I'm not playing that game. I let her kick away from me, bounding up before me to reach Emma and Taylor first - the latter of whom shoves away the former, squares up to Sophia as she pushes Emma behind her away from Taylor. Towards me.

Emma, crying and raging, simply tackles me instead of actually trying to fight. Bigger and stronger I might be, but shrugging off her full weight like its nothing isn't something I can do.

And as much as a dark part of me wants to, bludgeoning Emma into submission probably had more consequences than doing the same to Sophia. She can't take the hits, and I can't exactly offer my healing services later if things leave too much of a mark. Kicking away Emma is the best I can do, while this was all basically foreplay to Sophia, the wide-grin on her face as Taylor lunges for her is a testament to that.

I wince. Taylor's made some big strides in close combat lately. But take it from me, big strides aren't always enough when you start at the bottom.

I took close to a hundred attempts against Sophia - and other people across the same period - before I was content to say that I was her equal in hand-to-hand combat. I had the off-brand version of Victor's powerset active for half of that time, accelerating my own growth in skill.

Suffice to say, Taylor had a way to go. And Sophia immediately proves it. A three-point combo punishes an overextended fist, a textbook move that she's used against me countless times. Taylor attempts a jab at her kidneys. Punished again. Leg sweep. Denied. Taylor takes a kick to the torso and crashes backwards into the cubicle she just came out of.

"Nu' 'on ge'-" Emma tries to speak as I dislodge her, clutching a bloody nose and backing away to the exit. She gives up on whatever she was trying to say. "Sho-Sho'ia!" She calls out to her friend.

Sophia backs away from Taylor before I reach her. We eye each other for a moment, before Sophia flicks her eyes to the door, gives me and Taylor a slight nod in turn and then steps away - one hand massaging her jaw. As if she hadn't been trading blows just a few seconds earlier. Not that she was ever really the type to hold a grudge over a bit of violence. She was probably getting off on this. The fact that I'd provided an excuse for her by slapping Emma had probably made her day. "Later." There's an odd emphasis on the word as she looks at me.

Right.

Not a statement of farewell. An acknowledgement of our original agreement - to keep meeting up no matter what happened in school. I hadn't really expected things to come to this, but Sophia likely had. And she agreed anyway. "Later." I agree.

So she was willing to go behind her best friend's back for me, to keep our... thing, going.

...and I hadn't beaten all of her challenges yet. How did that make sense?

Or maybe, it made perfect sense. Because I'd taken things much slower with Sophia. Not always intentionally, but I had. I'd interacted more, grown the relationship more organically - as opposed to Emma, where I'd progressed from acquaintance, to having her suck me off in abandoned classrooms in the space of about two days. A few thin excuses about jealousy and her own psychology had been the only thing our relationship was built on initially. Maybe I hadn't really given it the time to breathe that it needed. Relied too much on my power doing the heavy lifting and only enjoying the rewards - something which might have still been fine, if I hadn't tested the end result too much, too fast. Taylor had been far, far more important to her than I'd expected.

...no. I'm not going down this route. I'm not blaming myself for this one. Emma's logic was psychotic, and with all thoughts of how hot she was mostly out of my mind thanks to the feeling of indignant rage flowing through my veins - it was easy to see that, even when the conversations we'd shared hadn't always been about Taylor, that motivation had never really been far from her thoughts at any point.

Fine. I glance at Taylor, pulling myself from my thoughts. Taylor is staring. Not at Emma, oddly enough. But at Sophia. Not a look of caution or fear, not the kind of look I would expect her to have sent one of her arch-enemies after taking a minor beatdown. Shock. An uncomprehending, blank expression.

Well. Perhaps she hadn't expected to lose that decisively after all the training she'd been doing? Perhaps now that she's a little more versed in combat, she can see for the first time how outmatched she still is? I don't know. I'm not a mind-reader. Either way, she doesn't say anything as they leave.

I note the smattering of bugs flitting down from the ceiling to settle on the pairs clothes as they leave. She was probably doing the same to me too, not that I really had a problem with that right now.

We look at each other for a moment. My anger is gone, lingering in the back of my mind for the next time I see that treacherous bitch - but not suitable for this conversation. I'll file that grudge away. Maybe there was a bit of hypocrisy there, that I'm the only one allowed to hold grudges like that - but life isn't fair. Deal with it.

And you know what? Actually? This is a good thing. Now I get to see what happens to my maxed-out 'victims' when we break up and become enemies. Perhaps, in a twist of fate, Emma will be the one crawling back for forgiveness. Maybe I'll have to deal with a yandere from now on. Maybe I'll have to deal with a 'bully' of my own with an overly-sexual tint to it. Or maybe she just hates me, and I can't fix it. Or she hates me, and its oddly easy for me to fix it. Any of those outcomes were possible. Any of them would provide some useful insights into my power.

Insights that would be useful for more important targets.

Like Taylor. Taylor, who looked like she didn't know what to say. Struggling with finding the right opening words.

"I-" "This-" We both start, then stop at the same time.

I make a gesture. Taylor starts speaking first. "This doesn't change anything. Everything I said, I meant it."

"And I meant everything I said too." I counter amicably.

She nods. Then she kicks the cubicle door, a frustrated snarl finding its way onto her face. "I told you so. I fucking told you, Greg! This is what she does! That's what she's like!"

"That's what the master manipulator looks like, is it?" I challenge. "That's how you expect her to act in this situation? Every word, every expression?"

"Yes! No." She hesitates. "Fine. Maybe she felt something for you, but that doesn't change who she is. And that doesn't change the choice you made!"

"And what did I choose?" I tilt my head.

"Her!" She shouts. "You chose her, and now you're-" She throws a hand out wildly. "-I don't even know. What are you doing? What are you even trying to achieve? She won't forget that, she won't forgive it - what were you even thinking?"

"And this was all a part of the grand plan of me choosing her, that's what it looked like to you?" I cross my arms. "You still think everything I said earlier is a lie?"

"No." Taylor looks deflated. "And, Emma was never a good actress either. I don't understand what you're doing, or why - but-" She breathes in slowly. "-if it really means that much to you, I'll believe that you thought you were helping." Her eyes flash. "You weren't! To be clear, it was stupid. The single worst move you could possibly have taken. In fact, knowing that you thought that was what I would want hurts even more - it makes me feel like you never even knew me in the first place!"

"And I'm sorry! Again." I spread my hands. "And, as your friend, I'll make it up to you."

"We can't go back, Greg." She insists. "We can't just pretend nothing was ever said or done. It happened. Things are different now."

"Then let's move forward." I press. "It happened, fine. But now that you've accepted I'm not doing some crazy scheme on Emma's behalf, is it really impossible for me to build that trust back?"

Taylor hesitates. "Just-just do what you want. I don't know. I want to go back. I really, really do. I wish this never happened in the first place, but it did - and now, that trust we had... I don't know."

"We can rebuild it. Even if we have to build up to it. We don't need to pretend it didn't happen." I channel some wisdom. "Some bad things came out of it, some good things came out of it. We learned some lessons. I learned to be more considerate about your feelings. You learned that you need to have a bit more faith in the kind of guy I am. I think we can forge an even stronger bond than before out of that."

"You're sounding corny." Taylor complains. "And what do you mean, the kind of guy you are, a complete horndog? Don't try and claim that the threesome- no, it's a foursome- was all for my benefit." Taylor snarks without heat.

"I confess, there were also ulterior motives. The curse of being a straight guy struck me at a bad time." I concede. "Repeatedly."

Wait, did I even mention that fully in our conversation? Taylor, you're exposing your nature as a voyeur through your bugs!

"Pervert." The perverted voyeur accuses me.

"Well, I joke a little - but I really did sense weakness. A way to approach them that could help - and also, coincidentally, get laid." She snorts. "It wasn't perfect. I'll admit. I saw an opportunity, and took it. With Emma, it didn't work out. Fine. Madison? It worked. Sophia? It worked. You can't deny that."

Taylor stops. "Greg. Sophia-" She swallows her words. "-she-" She stops again.

"What?" I tilt my head.

"...nothing." She says quickly. "Just, be careful of picking a fight with her."

"I'm tougher than I look, believe it or not." I wave her off.

Taylor looks doubtful. "No, I-" She trails off again. "-maybe its nothing. Forget it." A longer pause, then a red blush creeping across her face. "And, yeah. I guess if I have to accept that it wasn't entirely Emma manipulating you, then you did kind of do something with the other two - rather than them joining in for some scheme. It's just hard to picture it. I mean, I can picture Madison bending over for you - but S-Sophia too?" She shakes her head. "I can hardly wrap my head around that. And, at the same time?"

"What can I say, I'm quite the catch." I puff up my chest. "Why, jealous?"

Taylor takes the rhetorical question a bit too seriously. "I guess I was."

"Ah." Now I feel bad. Knowing what I know now, I could definitely have gotten together with Taylor at a much earlier stage - it only makes sense that some of those feelings were noted on her side too. "W-well. Now that we've established that we're all on the same side-" I step closer. "-I could fix that jealous feeling right now?"

She blinks up at me wetly. Wait. Tears? "Not too long ago, I would have been so happy to hear that suggestion." She takes a steadying breath. "But, no. I can't. It's too late. I was serious when I said I had someone-" It's me! How am I cucking myself again? "-and I love him. I really do. So, no. Sorry. Not that I'd jump into bed with you as easily as those three. What kind of girl do you think I am? And wasn't I just saying how that trust we had is broken? We can't continue right from where we left off."

"Well, the offer will stay open." I state lamely. "But, that's not important. The important thing is: We're best friends again now, right?" I offer a hand for fist-bumping.

"No." Taylor stares at my fist. "But, maybe we can work on it together." She meets my hand with her own.

Stop reading so many drama books, Taylor. Just say yes like a normal person.

Bah. Close enough. I'll take it.

#2,866
I wave as Taylor steps away to go and prepare for her next class, a complicated expression on her face - but not a hostile one. That was a victory. That was a crisis averted. A crisis that probably hadn't needed to happen if I'd approached Winslow differently... but a crisis all the same.

Now I just needed to find more time to talk with her, build that bond back up - and then ease her into the reveal of my actual identity and I'd have completely navigated The Taylor Problem without any major issues.

Apart from the Emma thing. My smile flickers at that thought, but Taylor isn't looking anymore - so I allow it to fall from my face entirely. Nevermind that. It wasn't worth thinking about.

As it turns out, trying not to think about it doesn't help. Not purely because of my own thoughts, but because Emma had no intention of just letting things go either. I catch a glimpse of her as I take a late lunch in the cafeteria. She doesn't make a move to approach, just eyeing my presence with an expression made of some strange blend of tears and rage, spite and grief, heartbreak and contempt. When it becomes clear I have no intention of approaching her, her expression darkens and she turns back to the group of friends surrounding her. Not the Trio, but some familiar faces all the same. A dozen girls and half-as-many boys that take turns shooting me with glares or frowns before returning their attention to the redhead as she speaks in a hushed tone.

I could imagine the kind of story she was weaving right now. Some of it might even be true. But this wasn't really a matter of gossip, this was Emma readying her weapon of choice against me. I suppose she was thinking that I could be bullied into compliance, that without the 'benefits' that came from being around her, I might come crawling back. She was probably thinking I would be little different to Taylor. An easy target to bully. Social isolation. A war of words against the raw numbers that her widespread social network could provide. A hostile environment that would back her up at every turn and stifle any resistance I made.

That was absolutely terrible news for me. Not because of Emma specifically - but because of what that meant. It meant that I couldn't rely on my power to keep people loyal to me. That maxing out challenges just wasn't enough for someone to place my interests over their own. In the grand scheme of things, Emma being unable to let go of her grudge against Taylor didn't mean much - but knowing that any heroes that I completed would probably side against me if everything was revealed... that was more of a blow. Knowing that the 'alliances' and 'friendships' I'd made couldn't be fully relied on is painful to think about. Objectively, it makes me no worse off than anyone else... but pretty much nobody else has to worry about the world signing off on a kill order on them if they don't balance public support and personal power well enough.

And it posed problems to future harem management. Which was also a key concern. Not the only one... but I had that on my mind too. I won't deny it.

A sample size of one wasn't everything, of course. The upside was that, at least initially, Emma's 'betrayal' had been framed as her doing something for my sake. Saving me from Taylor, bettering me as a person, keeping me untainted by her 'weakness' - even if that damaged our relationship. And I wasn't unconvinced that, if I did want to fix things at any cost - I could reconcile with Emma pretty easily by renouncing the whole Taylor thing. I wouldn't be doing that, so I could probably expect the spurned girl to continue attempting to try and cause issues for me.

I wasn't worried. Nothing at school posed a credible threat to me. This was like I'd come back to the starter zone at level thirty, and accidentally triggered a level three sidequest. If anyone tried bullying me, or causing issues with my schoolwork or even - and the idea was a little laughable - resorting to physical violence? I'd just clear a few of their challenges and have them sheepishly apologising for being rude before they'd gotten through their first sentence.

Which meant I could ignore Emma. Which was good. Because I didn't care. Maybe I did a short while ago. But no more. Maybe I had been flip-flopping over whether or not she was someone I would naturally leave behind as I moved to a bigger stage, or if she was someone I might take with me. That decision had been made for me. It doesn't matter anymore. I can find another hot, jealous redhead without even leaving Winslow. I'm fine. I am. The only thing I'm upset about is the pragmatic implications of today - it certainly wasn't that I'd gotten attached.

Definitely not.

If anything, it was just the unfamiliar feeling of 'losing' something in the real world - coupled with the annoyance at how easily I could have navigated around it with the benefit of hindsight. If it was anything like my everyday challenges, this whole issue would have been completely irrelevant already.

Emma's laugh carries across the room and the group unsubtly turns to look at me again. I grimace at nothing, tossing the remains of my sandwich towards the nearest trash can. Not hungry anymore. If anything, today had proven that anything in my civilian life was a waste of time - evidently, no amount of Mastering on the student body could erase the permanent stain of simply being Greg Veder. Trying to fix that was an exercise in futility. 'Greg' had exactly one purpose: To get on with his school and home life without generating a missing person report that would eventually end up with the PRT once the police realised what was likely happening. Anything more than the minimum was just wasted effort.

With that in mind, I skip my next class to find a quiet corner of the school to laze around in - instead shifting my focus to the ash clone halfway across the city. It was holding Squealer's Tinker power right now - struggling to slim down every aspect of the teleporter, even as the efficacy of the work plummets as her speciality falls away in relevance. It wasn't entirely optimal, but I didn't have the time to iterate through designs endlessly with my paste-box and I didn't have the resources and manufacturing capabilities to try and design a fully Leet-based product that could do everything I wanted. Squealer's power might be off her speciality by this point in the design, but doing it this way limited the areas that the project had problems in - namely, that it was too heavy and used too much energy. Both issues would be manageable if attached to a monster truck with appropriate levels of size and power, but for now I could engineer my way out of them by using better materials, stripping out unnecessary parts and covering the rest with Leet's power. That gave Leet's power just one or two things to make 'interesting' rather than twenty different components all with unique quirks that needed careful analysis to make them synergise together properly - or at least non-lethally.

Iterating on Squealer's Tinkertech, using that as the core, was letting me skip up the tech tree to get a more potent product early. It was proof that letting a Tinker do the weeks, months-long process of iterating, testing and building before yoinking the final product was the optimal way for me to Tinker. The 'next level' here wasn't trying to build up a Tinker base of my own, it was waiting for Leet to finally exit her Tinker fugue and answer her phone - or wait for Squealer to come to terms with the reality of her situation and reach out to me again. Or maybe, somehow, I could find a way to get my hands on Armsmaster's actual tech and slingshot my way into the Tinkering scene like that.

"There you are." I turn at the sound of the voice, raising an eyebrow at Sophia as she approaches.

"Looking for me?" I cross my arms over my chest. "Didn't know you cared."

"When I didn't find you there, I figured you were just too embarrassed after losing to me in our little scrap and felt you couldn't show your face in public anymore - and sure enough, here you are, crying at the shame of your defeat in the darkest corner of the school."

I seem to distinctly remember you sucker-punching me and still getting effortlessly handled within the span of a few seconds. Perhaps you hit your head too hard when I threw you to the ground, and now you have memory loss? You should check on that."

You should be thanking me for my intervention - and for telling Emma that a real predator wouldn't go running to get help just because a cornered rat fought back for the first time."

"I appreciate that." Wouldn't have been necessary if I'd entertained the idea that there was a third option for Emma that wasn't 'step aside' or 'fall in line'. It's basically foreplay to us anyway, you get to look good in front of Taylor, I get to look good in front of Emma - everything is great, apart from your broken heart - but, I can't really do much about that."

As the one with the Master power, pretty much everything here comes back to me and my choices in the end. I should have extracted the full story from Emma weeks ago and gone from there. I'd have known that it was apparently a super-big-deal to her rather than just a hobby, the whole thing with Taylor would probably have been pretty easy to fix... I just hadn't been that interested. It was too low-level. Too civilian for me. I'd just hoped that the petty issues would even themselves out as I progressed Taylor - and now I was paying for that lack of interest.

Well. I had even less reason to care now. Eventually, once I'd ingratiated myself into the Wards and the Protectorate - I'd likely be transferring to Arcadia. Dragging Taylor with me would probably be easy enough - and Emma could just sit and rot in the results of her own bad decision-making.

And mine too, except those were less clear-cut. Of course, I could point to certain highlights. Avoiding the initial argument with Taylor by talking with her earlier, actually digging into the depths of the issue that those two had with each other - but, ultimately, it all paled in the simple fact that after beating Emma's final challenge when sleeping over at her house, she should have been completely loyal. Every assumption that I'd made about my power and eventual conquest of the Bay - and beyond - hinged on that fact.

And she'd turned on me over what was little more than a hobby. A trauma-fuelled one, maybe - but it wasn't even anything serious. How would it even compare to getting outed as a power-stealing Master intent on becoming an S-Class threat and subverting the entire world to his whims? If four relationship boosts couldn't guarantee a schoolgirl taking my side, how would having even fewer for Capes keep them at my side for anything serious?

I pause.

My gaze slides to Sophia.

Wait. That was a good question.

Maybe... maybe I was looking at this wrong. Instead of looking at Emma and seeing where my power had failed, I should look at Sophia to see where it hadn't. Sophia still had challenges left. I'd gained fewer relationship boost rewards with her. And she was still here. Practically walking around behind her best friend's back like her new blood feud was nothing but a passing phase from a sulking toddler that was best ignored by the adults in the room.

Not just that. She hadn't sold me out to the PRT for knowing her identity. Went along with our patrols. Dedicated her time to working with us for nothing in return. Had enthusiastically joined in on a blatantly illegal raid on the Merchants that had ended with Skidmark getting mutilated. Had continued to hang around me despite knowing that I was essentially copying her powers wholesale the longer she spent around me.

If I was taking Emma as representative of everyone - Sophia should have flipped on me a long time ago. She hadn't. Not even when I had less challenges cleared than I do now.

Which meant that something was different.

"Hey, Sophia." I begin. "Why are you here?" She adopts an offended expression and I rush to continue. "No, I mean - Emma's your best friend, right? You've known me for way less time. Maybe you didn't know in advance that it would be this dramatic, but you were already making plans to say you'd stick around with me even before the fight. You never went to the PRT to tell them I knew your identity, when that would clearly benefit you. It would have been pretty understandable to drop me at some stage, or go to the PRT just to ensure your own protection - why didn't you?"

"Are you stupid?" She sends me a harsh look. "We've been through too much together for me to ditch you just because you and Emma disagree about one girl. You get me. I get you. We're-" She shifts uncomfortably for a moment. "-partners. Honestly, I trust you more than the PRT." She shakes her head. "You said it earlier, right? Why end a relationship over something so minor?

"And then Emma proceeded to do exactly that." I counter.

She waves a hand into the air. "Sure, but you and me? We're obviously closer than you and Emma were." There's a sheepish expression on her face. "You and Emma were just fucking. There were feelings there, sure - but, from what I saw, I'd say that it wasn't as developed as what you and I have. You just ticked Emma's boxes in the mindset that she wants in a guy, and she got to fuck over Taylor in the process. And, I mean, I can't say it was too different for me at first - but, we've moved past that. We're more than that. If you took that away now, I'd still-" She cuts herself off.

"Still-?" I prompt, failing to keep a wry grin off of my face at the expression she was making. "Go on, I get the feeling you were about to say something sweet just now."

Sophia flips me off, a darker complexion than usual visible on her cheeks. "Fuck off. This is getting sappy and embarrassing. I'm not doing this bullshit. I'm just saying, we're partners. We don't get to walk away from each other because of stupid crap. It's that simple."

That simple?

Maybe it was.

"Yeah." I send her a genuine smile. "I guess it is. Thanks, Sophia - it's good having you around." She opens her mouth to say something snarky, and I take the opportunity to pull her close and press my lips to hers. The sound of outrage she lets out isn't accompanied by any real struggle.

We break apart a moment later. Sophia looks ready to argue, or complain, or rage about something on pure principle - but in the end, simply huffs and steps out of my reach. "At least you're not moping anymore, I guess. But I'm not playing therapist for you, I've got better things to do. Go fish for compliments somewhere else, I'm not here to massage your bruised ego - or to massage anything else, for that matter." She mock-glares at me before I can even open my mouth. I click it shut. "I didn't come over here for fun. Just wanted to say that I'm on console duty today and tomorrow - so I won't see you after school or for any patrols until that's out of the way."

"Pretty sure you could have said that in a message." I tilt my head at her. "You may as well be honest about why you're really here."

She rolls her eyes. "Fine, I also wanted to check that you weren't going to throw yourself off the roof or something after getting rejected. You looked pretty upset about how things went down, figured I could remind you that between your pretty-cool powers and having me around - your life is pretty fucking amazing even without Emma." I pull a face and make a dismissive gesture at her words. It was appreciated, but her estimation of me was way off. She smirks. "Plus, it sounds like even without Emma - you're going to have Hebert choking on your dick soon instead. I'd still call it a bad trade, but somehow I can see her getting into it."

I shrug. "She says she has a boyfriend."

Sophia bursts out laughing.

And keeps laughing.

She doubles over, her laugh turning into a hysterical wheeze.

I wait it out.

I keep waiting.

Eventually, she recovers. "That was a good joke for once-" She pats me on the shoulder as she turns away, shoulders still shaking with mirth. "-keep that up, and people will actually think that you're funny. Remember what I said. Things are great. I'm still here. We're still an awesome team. All of that stuff." She saunters away, seeming pleased with herself.

I wasn't joking, but... admittedly, the reality of the situation would have been even more comedic to her. "I'll remember." I agree. And I would.

Because even if Emma was gone, Sophia was still here.

And as much as I appreciated that fact on its own, there was another layer to it.

Even if Emma, with every single challenge complete, was gone - Sophia, with two challenges still to go, was still here. And Sophia was arguably doing a lot more for me than I'd ever asked of Emma. Her earlier explanation for my 'dumb' question springs to mind - that she was still here because we had a better bond. In a way, it was too simplistic - she didn't know about the Master element that was involved.

And in another way? It just worked.

Because that explanation? It made sense. Fundamentally, my issue came down to two parts - one, that my power couldn't - or wouldn't - do everything for me. Two, this was real life. I could do things, achieve things, that weren't explicitly given to me as a reward. Just like I could theoretically have found a girlfriend without ever clearing a challenge in my life, just like I could make a move on Taylor and Emma before completing their challenges - despite the game-like interface my powers had chosen, this wasn't a game. These were real people.

I'd already known that. I just hadn't extrapolated what that meant up to this point, partly because I'd simply never had cause for a maxed-out 'victim' to have their loyalty and obedience tested.

It did change things though. I'd been counting on the fact that discreetly, quietly completing someone's challenges would simply make them just as loyal as anyone else whenever I showed myself. But under that logic of assuming that all challenge rewards were equal, it was impossible to explain Emma's actions in the same context as Sophia making a - by her standards - half-hearted attempt at keeping appearances for her friend while inarguably keeping her in the dark over the fact that she'd very much chosen me over her. And was already considering me over the Wards too. Sophia, still missing a few of her challenges, Emma, fully completed. If the reverse had happened, it would make sense - but this way around? Something was different. The first possibility was that it was just different for Capes, but that didn't click right - I could only conclude that there was an element involving the quality of the relationship at play.

I couldn't deny Sophia's words. My thing with Emma had always been fairly shallow. Something born mostly from her looking to spite Taylor, which had grown into a power-fuelled addiction to me that I had eagerly exploited and fanned into love - of sorts, anyway. A sexual relationship where I was more of a... living example of what she wanted out of the 'perfect guy' rather than a desire for Greg Veder in particular. I could say the same for Sophia, but there was a lot more depth there - we'd seen the truth of each other's natures, challenged it, worked together and explored our relationship to a far greater extent.

It wasn't that abusing that starting line to launch the relationship was bad - nor did I even think it was a problem to just use the challenge rewards as-given if all I wanted was a burst of approval, to get laid or even just to get my foot in the door for a wider relationship. But at the same time, in Emma's case? I hadn't really tried to make it into anything more - perhaps partly because I kept mentally flip-flopping on whether Emma was a soon-to-be-discarded fling or someone worth keeping by my side even after the Taylor hatesex threesome.

And, damn - if that idea wasn't a lot less attractive now that I was the one feeling hateful. I'd get over it, probably. Attractive women had a way of making me forgive them, but I was empathising with Taylor more than usual right now.

Getting back from that tangent - I'd already known that giving my power more to work with made it less likely to attempt wild, sweeping changes to justify anything it did. A previously-existing relationship was better than one sprung from nothing. I just hadn't extended that logic to the fact that my power would only do so much, only go so far. That I needed to put effort into cultivating what was given - at least, if I wanted to put it through the metaphorical trial by fire by doing something that was against their nature.

There was a reason Sophia was still around, with us mutually bonding over violence, our outlook on the Bay, thoughts on the gangs, Skidmark, illegal vigilantism and the unspoken fact that I was blatantly farming powers off the heroes despite her position in the Wards. She was still here despite the messy breakup with Emma. Even before I'd progressed Sophia that far, she'd never looked to seriously throw me to the Protectorate for knowing her identity. Because I'd taken it slow. Taken my time. Enjoyed the journey.

The gamer part of me hated that. The one that looked at Brockton Bay like a spreadsheet and a living mission-tree. The part of me that looked at my issues - like with not seeing the heroes on patrol - and reasoned that one distraction with Mush's power, one quick detonation with a grenade would have an entire response force rushing out into my line of sight in an instant. The part of me that said I knew the Protectorate base like the back of my hand through the WRLD modifier, and that repeating a challenge or two to get clues towards some exact names and addresses before looking to catch a stray glimpse of the heroes going home from work or school would be trivial.

That part of me resented the fact that repeating a few tricks like that in subtle silence had been 'nerfed', that the end-result was weaker - shakier - compared to a Greg that had established common ground first, or during, the process of challenging them - a Greg that had taken the effort to grow that bond himself. A Greg that took the time to present himself to the world as a Hero, rather than as a threat-report notice from a panicking pre-cog or Thinker that glanced my way during their coffee break.

And part of me liked it. The part of me that looked at my interactions with Sophia, with Taylor - and now knew that it wasn't a waste. That my efforts and interactions wouldn't be overwritten and ignored the moment I cleared the next challenge. If a relationship worked on a scale of 1-100 - and a boost was worth, say, twenty points - putting in the time and effort to grow it by thirty on my own would mean something. They'd probably still fuck me if I cleared all of their challenges and nothing else - but trying to improve upwards from a point of '60' was probably harder than from '25'. Not impossible. Not even worth it, for a lot of my targets - it was a big world after all. But for the people I did care about, that I did interact with heavily - that I was trusting and expecting trust in turn... under this logic - and I felt the certainty in my bones this time - they would follow me into hell if I did it right. If I dedicated my time. Treated it like- well. Like a relationship, rather than an achievement.

Looking at it through that lens? I was feeling okay about things. Still livid about Emma. But, there was a learning experience there. And, for all that I was annoyed... at least it was 'just' Emma. I could find another hot, jealous redhead without even leaving Winslow. There was a reason I'd prioritised fixing things with Taylor over her feelings, and that was because - bluntly - I cared about Taylor and Sophia more. If I'd ruined things with one of them beyond my ability to repair? That would have been devastating, with long-lasting consequences. And while Taylor would still probably be mad at me if everything about my identity came out today... I don't think it would have the same catastrophic consequences to our relationship that it would have yesterday. Maybe she'd need some time away to think about things, but I wouldn't expect her to just run off to become a crazed supervillain at the revelation anymore.

Which wasn't an entirely unfounded worry, given what some of her challenges involved.

I debate skipping the rest of my classes for the day as well, not wanting to skip too many times in a row, but not really burning with any desire to attend either. I doubted much would come of a few one-off skips like this. I'd already made it a habit to challenge every teacher, every staff member, every bus driver - I had never been bored enough to do it for the entire student body, but I figured that clearing two challenges from everyone in a position of authority - or anyone that might feel obliged to report anything suspicious - would give me some leeway for anything I did here. The benefit of the doubt, whether it was reluctance to get me in trouble as a civilian - or whether it was to look at me with suspicion that I was a Cape doing something suspicious at the school. As long as it wasn't long-term enough to flag on a system, missing out on class here and there was just a solid perk from covering my bases.

I smile at the gossiping students. Speaking of challenging the student body, here they come again. A stream of challenge boxes flows through the corridor. Four challenges, sometimes five, sometimes three - that seemed to be the general rule for a civilian. I tended to assume four, and that let me use the 'current challenge' as something to categorise them without bothering to remember names. Ones to Fours, the people who liked me the least, and the ones who were already mine.

Mine, but to no greater an extent than Emma had been.

I ignore that sour thought. Things are great. I settle in to watch people go past, occasionally nodding in greeting at those who glance my way.

Fours meet my eyes and wave, or blush and duck away with a giggle to their friends. Threes and twos send me smiles, or nod in passing if they catch sight of me leaning against the wall. Sometimes, I just get silence in response - not irritation, not friendliness. Just an impassive acknowledgement. Ones ignore me. Those I had never challenged, or perhaps had challenged - but it had been so early in my career that I hadn't beaten them. Maybe half of the students were still 'ones'. It wasn't a lack of ability on my part, but a lack of patience and concern over what it might look like to be the only guy in a newly-all-girls school - nevermind the occasional reminder from my power that too many different challenges in a day would cause it to hit the brakes on my body.

The gossip that was a little too loud to be normal, the co-ordinated movement of a group 'stumbling' across me - all with a comment about my looks, my history as a drug abuser or a violent thug, my gang allegiances, my relationship with Taylor, the fact that I'd been dumped by Emma-

There's no reason to lose.

Success. Success. Success. Well, it does show how different things could have been - there's more than one path that I could have taken with my power, even if I'd never run into Sophia and Taylor as my first Capes.

Vista? Doable. Assuming she repeats the same move as before, I just need to cross the distance quickly - and splitting her focus and attention with my ash clone would be a good idea as well. I'd seen too many videos of him getting his ass kicked - no special Tinker effects, no inertia dampeners, no forcefields - nothing to protect him from my balls. My doll-balls. Ball-dolls. I'm not calling them that. It's Parian's doll power, in a ball shape - there's got to be a cool name I can use for it when someone asks.

Magic Football. Cloth Missile. Fabric Rocket. Ball of Doom. I don't know. Strange, I don't usually struggle with amazing names - but for some reason, they all sound a little bit cringe for once.

Whatever. I'm going to turn Gallant's helmet into a soup container by slamming a telekinetically-accelerated, forcefield-coated mass into the back of his head at great speed. That's what's going to happen. As for the challenges after that... I'm not sure. It's easy to know that I'm likely to be in a more head-to-head conflict - but, honestly, I don't even know how to prepare. He's a shit Tinker. Sometimes shoots baby blasts at people that can make you sad. How do you prepare for that? I don't know. Distract, surround by comboing with my ash clone, lock him down with Clockblocked strings and then tear him to pieces. I don't need a new power for that, the losses are more likely to come from the nature of the scenario than anything he can do. He's essentially a worse version of Triumph.

Speaking of which. Triumph. I don't have a great plan here. His Brute rating wasn't widely discussed, but it existed - and any Brute rating sucked for me in a challenge like that - where the fight immediately happens with no prep time. But even if I had that, even if I could make the Mechablade - it was his ranged power that was the problem. Too strong. Too long-ranged. Too low-cooldown. Any win would have to be capitalising on a mistake, letting him get in close and then immediately claiming victory before he could kill me. One hit, one kill. If I could give my clone some cloth, Parian's power and enough time to work with... no. Too cumbersome. Too obvious. And the sheer impact of the shockwaves he released... it's more likely than not that my ash clone can't even survive being in the same room as that attack - even if it isn't the direct target. One of the downsides of being at 1hp all the time. In short, I wasn't beating him as I was now.

What power would help? Kaiser? Hookwolf? The Blaster powers of New Wave were a bit too weak for a Brute at the level I was likely to get them, and flight wouldn't protect me from his range. Miss Militia, but I'd already been burned once hoping for a weapon out of her power. Clockblocker's power, if it lost the Manton effect - or even just the restriction on worn items. Assault? I have no idea how the shockwaves would interact with his power, but being realistic - I would need the full-fledged power for this, not the simple version I'd likely get to start with. Brandish? I nod to myself. Brandish. Lightsaber to the face would do the trick. I'd have to get that aspect of the power, but at a guess - my power was way less likely to screw me over a melee weapon than a ranged one.

Armsmaster... well. I had an idea for that one. I doubted any conventional new power would help with the modifiers of the challenge giving him intel on whatever new power I earned and the prep-time to account for it. I had my one trick planned, and we'd see where that went - otherwise, back to the drawing board.

Miss Militia? Repetition. Scouting and a good route was arguably more important than any easy-to-find powers.

Velocity - annoyingly, I hadn't challenged his current challenge to see what I was up against apart from the modifiers. We'd only met briefly at Canberra - that had been around the time that I'd found that there was somewhat of a Thinker-headache-equivalent to spreading my power around different targets too much in a short time and attempting the second challenge hadn't been a priority with no promise of a power boost on the line.

And, critically, I didn't think I could win. A painful admission, because I really didn't like Velocity - as a Cape, not a person. The worst power in the Bay, save for maybe some of the Case-53s you hear rumours about.
