It was a sad, sad moment when I had become a better Cape than Velocity from the instant I'd gained the weak, half-hearted echo of his power - simply because I could actually do other things than flail ineffectually at villains, while also getting the ability to run away very fast.

Unfortunately, running away very fast was good in a challenge. I had no way of catching him unless he made a mistake, and eventually, the anti-stalling measures of my power would ensure that he could turn my body into a smoothie by just running at me if he survived long enough. Even if he didn't do that, he could just stay forever at the edge of my attack range and throw grenades at me hoping to get lucky - taze me from behind, pepper spray in the eyes, anything was possible when the requirement wasn't for him to win, but for him to not lose. He might not be able to beat me straight-up, but I couldn't kill him either - and my power wouldn't tolerate an extended draw for long if I wasn't making progress.

I wasn't even sure what it would take for me to claim the win. Completely blindsiding him with a lethal attack from my ash clone was about it, and even then, how perfect would the situation have to be for that to work out in just a few attempts? No, that one was probably too difficult right now - even the first level was a minor miracle from my power, giving a modifier that benefitted me more than him in the form of CAGE. But now, balance concerns had slipped in from the metaphorical referee that was my power. For good reason, if the next level of the power eliminated the 3-second paralysis on either side of the speed-state, I'd be unstoppable. Again, because I had other powers. And he didn't. Sucks to suck.

I hope Dauntless shows up. I want to see what that looks like through the lens of my power, useless or game-changing - each as likely as the other, but as one of the few powers that gets explicitly stronger over time, it would be nice to get it rolling before I was ruling the Bay. The actual 'how' on how to beat him? Beg on my knees for my power to give me a freebie where he didn't have any equipment to hand. That was it. He was too much of a complete package for me to handle in a real fight right now.

I'm just getting into wishful thinking territory here. The point of this train of thought wasn't about what would be nice to get. There was a practical side of it - things that I could get in preparation.

I needed to make the most out of tomorrow's event. A rare opportunity to meet with the heroes outside of a crisis, without my Cape identity being tracked and monitored - and without my civilian identity looking suspicious. There was nothing suspicious about Greg Veder going to sit in the crowd at an event centred around the reveal of a Ward - I've done it before, prior to gaining any powers, so I wasn't too concerned about attracting too much attention this time.

Still a little worried. In a healthily paranoid kind of way. Using my civilian identity as a point of 'attack' on the heroes - this was exactly the kind of thing that could cause problems for me with the PRT if it came out. But, I'd done something similar before at the Meet and Greet event - and nothing happening after that was proof that a sufficient smokescreen for my intentions was enough to keep me somewhat safe. Greg Veder stumbling across consecutive, supposedly-secret patrols? Appearing halfway across a city to hang around Arcadia, a school that has nothing to do with him? Suspicious. Attending two events around a topic he's always been interested in? Not so much. This was going to be the best moment to slingshot myself ahead of the curve without revealing my hand.

But it wouldn't be enough to just scout challenges out and follow up later. Even if I found a winning strategy that I couldn't execute during the event, I didn't have an easy way to just walk over to Arcadia nonchalantly and finish someone off. Even as a Cape, I didn't exactly have a Stranger power. I might have a mask on, but I wasn't subtle - PHO was already full of sightings of me zipping around in my speed-state, running across rooftops wasn't much better. I, of all people, wasn't going to underestimate what a bored PHO-poster could achieve with a map, time, effort and enough Cape sightings and police reports to work with.

No, I couldn't treat this like the passive exposure I had on Sophia and Taylor - a few persistent challenges to hone myself against without any great need to win immediately. This time, I needed to win outright. And that meant maximising the powers I had now, and the ones that I could easily go and grab. Of all of my possible destinations... the Dallon household was at the top of the list. The Pelhams might have been better for my needs, but it was too isolated - there was no hiding spot or neighbouring window to peer in on their house entrances without looking suspicious.

It wouldn't be my first time staking out the location, but after my initial success - I'd found it a relatively underwhelming 'trick' so far. An inconsistent schedule, the possibility of the family arriving via a separate entrance or even just flight, the fall of darkness highlighting the fact that I needed a certain level of visibility to 'highlight' my target with my power even if I knew they were there, the fact that they genuinely didn't leave or enter the house that much - and the comparatively minor issue that the neighbour's house I was spying on them from was... someone else's house. I didn't want to make it obvious that I was spying on the Dallons specifically instead of just staring dramatically out of the window while the civilian recovered from the puddle I'd fucked her into. And now I knew, even finishing that last challenge or two wouldn't assure her loyalty if my true intentions were revealed. Help, yes - guarantee, no.

Then there was the small issue of timing. Combining the usual time I left school with travel time, coupled with the necessity of 'Greg' heading in that direction rather than Void Cowboy - I tended to miss them arriving home after school or work. I had to return again before long just to keep up appearances at home too, Clara and Alice were pretty blase about my newfound 'enthusiasm' for the Brockton Bay nightlife but I couldn't stretch their wilful ignorance too far before breaking it.

At least all of that wouldn't be a problem if I left as early as this. Skipping classes constantly might be mildly problematic eventually, but a few one-off occurrences wouldn't be noteworthy at all. I scurry out of the school towards the bus bay. Couldn't exactly go running to the Dallon household in my speed state without raising a few eyebrows.

The day I get a Stranger or teleportation power that means I don't have to worry about 'Greg' and his ability to travel around the city, I'll be a happy guy indeed.



Fifty-two minutes. That's how long it takes to catch the bus, ride it across the city, walk the remaining distance to my destination and arrive at my destination.

Plus three minutes of waiting outside the door of Katarina's door, pressing the doorbell periodically.

Not home?

Somehow, I'm not annoyed about that despite the inconvenience. Maybe I'm just not in the mood for redhead civilians that I've realised I can't really trust right now. Maybe this was actually preferable. When she was around, yes - we got to fuck, but I also had to work around the fact that I was in her house - usually being watched by her, even if there wasn't a hint of suspicion there. I could only lurk around the window so much before she might start to think that I wasn't just trying to look cool and composed, but that I might actually be looking at something. Such as the driveway of her superhero neighbours.

If I reeled back on my indignation and fury about the whole Emma thing, I could at least acknowledge that for her, the entire Taylor situation was on the same level as vigilantism was for Sophia. I'd already known that I wasn't likely to completely flip morals like that in my challenges, I didn't expect people to be willing to murder for fun just because I said so. I'd just underestimated what Emma's priorities were. But that underestimation was easy to make. I wasn't a mindreader. What did Katarina think of her neighbours, of the law, of vigilantes, of schoolboys playing truant? Somewhere, there was an invisible line where - regardless of the number of challenges - she would ignore my personal wishes and talk to someone. Perhaps even with the best of intentions towards me.

And if I spent enough time, sure, I could probably fix that - build up that depth in our relationship to something I could count on. But I wasn't going to. I might have been conflicted about Emma and her place in my life, but I wasn't conflicted about Katarina. She was a tool. That didn't mean I needed to be cruel to her or anything, but one day - I would disappear from her life and never return, and not think anything of it. And, hopefully, she wouldn't think anything of me either other than some fond memories. And the purpose of that tool was just to give me line-of-sight into people walking through the front door of their next-door-neighbours house.

Which I could do perfectly fine without her. Entering via the shadow state in broad daylight might be a bit too brave, but the door was out-of-the-way enough that I wasn't too concerned about nosy neighbours wondering what I was up to. A shape forms on the opposite side of the door as my ash clone stirs to life, freshly back from its long cooldown after working for the first half of the school day. I puppet it directly for a moment. Keys on the coatrack. A few seconds later, I let myself in - letting my ash clone close and lock the door behind me. The house is dark, obviously - and I'd be wise to leave it that way. I dismiss the ash clone, vaulting the stairs with my movement powers and heading up to the master bedroom - checking each room as I go. Nothing and nobody home. Excellent.

Maybe it's overcautious for a civilian household, but assuming that the lights being off means that nobody is there is a lethal mistake. One that you only make a dozen or so times before the lesson sinks in.

With no audience watching me, I'm free to lurk at the window without worrying about what anyone else thinks. No distractions. No need to turn around and talk, or keep up appearances. A perfect stakeout.

A perfect stakeout that soon gets rewarded. I almost miss it, laser-focused as I am on the road. A faint shadow crossing the street, followed by Glory Girl descending to street-level right outside the front door of the house - carrying a relaxed Panacea tightly in her arms.

Good enough. I focus on Panacea first. "Challenge."

I've crossed paths a few times with Panacea on hospital visits before. It had been a good way to meet up and interact with her, simply visiting and poking people with healing powers until the PRT 'asked' her to verify that I wasn't doing anything crazy. But eventually, they'd stopped directing her towards me in response - or perhaps she'd grown tired of responding - and my hospital visits just became an occasional routine where unimpressed doctors would come and glare at me sans Cape support. But in that time? I'd established a rapport with the girl. As much as I could, anyway. To the extent that, even with my newly-reinforced caution towards going too fast through challenges - I was pretty confident that I'd developed my relationship with Amy enough that completing her next two challenges - for the power reward and relationship boost - would put me on the same kind of 'healthy' trajectory as Taylor and Sophia.

Two challenges in one night might sound ambitious, but I've had some time to kill on this third challenge of hers. A fair few attempts working out the limits of the challenge - and I've got a lot more information now than I had going in.

The challenge was deceptive. A GANG modifier, Panacea running through a hospital healing a bunch of Capes that then tried to kill me? It made sense that it was a race to kill her before I was overwhelmed, right? Yes, but also no. Maybe it could be a race if I had a ranged one-shot technique, but I wasn't landing my super-football on a moving target from this range. No, the challenge was actually about harassment. Not about stopping her from getting to the patients to 'activate' them, but about preventing her from healing them. Same thing, right? No.

The fact is, everyone in the hospital is already activated. If I simply rush at Amy right away, another one will leap up from the bed 'just in time' and kill me in short order. That happens if I take ten seconds or if I take twenty. Same thing. After a certain amount of time, Amy will move on - the target will start fighting as normal and that's that. But that isn't a quirk of my simulation, she's actually healing them. That's the trick - every single person in the hospital is injured, lethally so. If I rush Amy at the start, Glory Girl will jump out of bed to block me - yes. But without any attacks from me, she'll also just keel over and die about sixty seconds later, assuming Amy didn't get a chance to start work on her. The other people present in the building are little better. 'Preserved' while waiting on the beds to be healed, but doing the equivalent of ripping out the life support and spending their dying breaths to save the healer any time I got close.

In that sense, it was a puzzle. As the target of the challenge, Amy - and everyone else - would prioritise her own safety when threatened. She'd flee from any conflict I offered, essentially leaving her patient to eventually die unaided. I didn't need to stop her, I needed to harass her. Force her to move on from each and every near-death patient before she could patch them up completely, and every time I got close or forced her to move on - I'd have an increasingly-large number of pissed-off Capes following in my footsteps to protect her. Capes that would die quite quickly, but even a single minute was a long time when it came to trying to fend off Brandish in an enclosed space.

But that was still progress. And despite how difficult it was for a third-level challenge... it actually felt pretty fair. There were a lot of ways to approach it, a lot of ways that any number of new powers could be used to break it open - and a lot of ways to optimise my route. I could leave her healing people that I didn't care as much about for longer if it meant being able to lead away, or even manually 'activate' more problematic Capes. I'd gotten pretty good at this. I'd even dare to call it fun.

First of all. The first room. A dead sprint towards the figure across the corridor, coupled with using Vista's power to shrink space, has to be the opening move. The speed-state paralysis takes too long here. Glory Girl lunges at me before I get too close to Amy, who's already stepping away to the next patient from the moment the former started moving. Glory Girl dies in thirty seconds. My ash clone stirs to life ahead of me, behind Glory Girl - close to Amy. A brilliant blade pierces through it before Amy can even start on her second patient. Immediately, the healer scurries to the third as Brandish turns to me. Brandish, dead in just over twenty seconds. Two of the more problematic ones.

I duck. I dodge. I dip. I phase down through the floor just to buy a few seconds away from the human blender, Glory Girl slams a hole through it a moment later - the Dallon matriarch following behind her in ball-form. I run backwards into the next room, slow enough that they feel confident in following rather than staying close to Amy. I bound off a nearby desk and shift through the ceiling to the next floor, ignoring the warning scream of my shadow-state as I brush the edge of an electricity cable. I dash back into the room I left Amy in, Glory Girl pursuing me once again - while the hum of Brandish and her blades cuts out with a distant choked gasp barely audible over the noise of Glory Girl tearing a larger hole in the floor.

As expected, Amy moves on as I approach. I create an ash clone, reach out and pass across the speed state power and send it to follow her out of the room, orders given in advance this time. I turn my attention to Gallant. One of the ones I was happy to let Amy heal up, because he was pretty easy for me to just kill again. Why? He wasn't in costume. I tackle him before he even clears the hospital bed, burning through the shadow state and my Echo power to just repeatedly pummel him in melee - ignoring Glory Girl as she falls to the floor behind me. A lot of iterating had gone into this route, striking the perfect balance between the 'timers' of both Brandish and Glory Girl - while also not allowing Panacea to entirely finish on Gallant and therefore 'wake him up' to start blasting before I had reached him. As long as the timing is right, the deaths and the fighting responses all happen the same way at the same time.

I know what Gallant is going to do before he does. He doesn't have most of his usual armour on, just the gauntlets and legs. Sophia is better at this anyway. I've got a more advantageous position. I have melee-focused powers acting as a cheat-code. His hand movements telegraph his blasts and aren't suited to close-quarters combat.

I don't even feel an ounce of satisfaction or any sense of thrill as his eyes roll up into the back of his head. This was the bare minimum result I should expect when looking at the facts.

I chase after Panacea. Or rather, my ash clone. Another lesson that had cost me some attempts: Actually landing a hit on Panacea is the 'enrage' equivalent. Every patient jumps up from their bed and starts trying to kill me. That was useful in its own way, survive for maybe twenty seconds after that point and everyone aside from the target is dead. Except, that twenty seconds is more than enough. The Blasters of New Wave are all elsewhere in the building, and critically - Clockblocker is in the next room. He needs to die first, or he'll freeze Panacea and give everyone the pass to ignore collateral damage and wipe out me along with the entire rest of the building - people with more destructive powers that would have been pretty useless if I was close to Panacea suddenly would rank among my biggest threats.

Which meant I needed to clear out this second room. This one would be less practiced than the first, but I knew the opening move: The Ash Clone zips past Panacea, careful to not actually attack her - reaches the next room... and starts making threatening gestures as she approaches. Sure enough, Panacea gives up on the second room of patients - scurrying to the third instead.

The occupants of the second room all jump up to attack my ash clone. Vista, Clockblocker, Shielder and Manpower - activated patients that haven't been touched at all will reliably die within twenty seconds. They spend five chasing my ash clone before I feel my ash clone vanish. I've sprinted after Panacea far enough that they won't catch me in the next fifteen, even with Vista trying to speed things up.

Now. Uncharted territory, except I know the plan. I know who is coming the moment I lay hands on Panacea, I just haven't reached that point cleanly before. Haven't found quite the right approach. I pull level with her, comfortably faster than her even without any assistance from my powers. She tries to weave away from me without truly changing course, but there isn't anywhere else for her to run to. Five rooms total, all three of the remaining ones are in a straight line ahead of us. The next room is full of dangerous Capes, but in some ways - too dangerous. Without Clockblocker and Shielder, there isn't much that they can even do in the limited time they have without killing Panacea as well.

I sway away as she attempts to catch my hand with her own. None of that. I still don't strike her. I just wait for more of my powers to become available. The last area of pinched space from Vista to unravel, the cooldown of my recently-killed ash clone to finish, the final charge of my shadow state - minor advantages that could be the difference between life and death when the lasers start flying. Finally, my ash clone surges to life in front of us - blocking off the door ahead. I brush my hand against it to assign it as an administrator and hand off a new powerset. Parian's power vanishes and I feel a faint tug on my shirt. I don't have time to watch the clone work - I tap into Panacea's own power and slam my foot into her midsection as she tries to sidestep around me. Not the best power selection for a straight-up fight, but without this or Glory Girl's shield as my active powerset, I can be knocked out with a single touch. And I'm pretty sure that if anyone knows the weakness to that forcefield, it's going to be Panacea.

But at the same time, I'm not exactly worried about my powers being restricted in a fight against Panacea. She's not a combatant. Not trained for this kind of situation. One hit in and she already looks ready to curl up in the corner in a defensive position. An easy, easy win - all I had to do was take a step forward, and finish the job.

I take a step back instead. Reaching out to the doorway and grazing my hand against the spiderweb of fabric my ash clone has woven across the closed doorway. I clockblock it. Not a moment too soon. The doorway slams into the fabric and stops cold. Everyone is up now. Not just the room beyond, but the rooms way beyond that. The only fortunate thing was that by sheer travel time, obstacles and the existence of elevators - none of the other rooms were likely to feature in this battle, they'd all largely die before they could make a difference.

Eighteen seconds. My ash clone and I turn on Panacea. She backs away, then resists. We break an overextended arm together. Fifteen seconds. I deliver a half-dozen consecutive punches as she tries to shield her face. Twelve seconds. The door practically disintegrates behind me as I cast a wary glance backwards - the clockblocked fabric was still holding firm as the furious Capes push for a way through. One hand snakes through an opening in the web to point at me, and I swiftly circle around behind Panacea in response to deter the attack. A halberd starts to carve through the side of the wall, creating a second doorway to reach through.

Five seconds. I back away from Panacea as the attackers rush through - smaller blasts of power easily dispersing my ash clone. I still have all three charges of my shadow state, so I can just stall for time until the majority of them drop dead.

Three. Two.

A heavy *throom* sound is all the warning I get before an armoured chestplate fills my vision - a half-dozen other Capes scattered to the side in the wake of the new arrival surging past them. I reach for the shadow state and then barely stop myself from locking it in, raising Glory Girl's shield instead as Dauntless thrusts his arclance towards me - a dull boom echoing in my ears as every other sound vanishes, replaced with every nerve in my body screaming in agony as I realise that while the initial blow might have been neutralised - the raw force of the attack had still knocked be back, the impact of hitting the wall behind me just separated enough for my version of Glory Girl's power to fade.

I spit blood. Zero. It's not a precise count. Indeed, many of the figures had started collapsing already - or simply hadn't been able to rise when Dauntless had burst past them and knocked them to the ground. Some take a few extra steps forward over the bodies of their comrades, only to fall themselves. Twenty two, twenty three seconds - if any of the blasters had been in that group of late-survivors, let alone Dauntless, I'd have lost again.

But that isn't the case. No further attack comes. I try to rise from the shattered wall I'm half-embedded in. No good. But I'm not dead.

Yet. That thought sharpens the mind. I wasn't a Brute, and even if my pain tolerance was pretty absurd these days - I couldn't rely on the shadow state saving me from the level of internal bleeding I probably had. Speaking of which, I activate it three times. Every little helps.

Still no attack. Amy has risen from her corner, clutching her arm and advancing towards me - doubtless looking to finish me off personally now that there were no patients left.

Before she's halfway to me, my ash clone returns from its cooldown. I'm not sure that it would even lose to Panacea in a straight fight, even as a glass cannon - but it doesn't have to. The shattered rubble I'm sitting in is exactly the kind of loose material that couldn't be found in the sterile, artificial rooms elsewhere in the hospital. The exact kind of material that Mush's power loves to work with. My knight forms next to me, the tentacle coating itself with shattered stone where the arclance had left its mark on the corridor. As it grows in size and mass, it could even have started incorporating the previously-unusable stray objects found in the previous rooms... but that isn't needed here. The current knight isn't much of a brute. But it still is one. And, critically, it isn't organic.

Panacea doesn't stand a chance.

SUCCESS

Reward: Biological Manipulation (2)​

Nice. Already worthwhile coming this way. I try to shake my vision, looking to get eyes back on the pair before they finish unlocking the front door - the brief period of being unable to see while reality continues is a real annoyance here, it's something I've gotten used to for continuing conversations and maintaining a walking pace, but that was just keeping a movement going. I couldn't clear up the remnants of the simulation fogging up my eyes faster with any amount of practice, it just happened at its own pace.

I momentarily hesitate as my vision clears and they both start to step through the doorway. One more freebie. Glory Girl or Panacea? Neither of them was a power upgrade if the pattern of alternating rewards held true. I wanted flight and the Brute power more, but Glory Girl had a variety of aspects to her power that I could get a 'dud' upgrade from. If I could only win one... then I should ignore any considerations about power and look at the actual in-real-life effect I would get.

I'd never met, or interacted, with Glory Girl. I had no way of reliably doing it. Any boost that my power gave me would likely just improve her first impression of me whenever we did meet. I doubt I'll be able to leverage any advantage out of that anytime soon. On the other hand, I've met Amy a fair amount - I can catch her doing hospital visits if I time things well enough or catch the news of her doing the rounds on PHO quick enough. This would also be the second boost, and I felt pretty comfortable saying that I'd interacted enough with Amy that I wasn't rushing if I won here - this wasn't an Emma version 2.0. I'd probably be able to nudge the antisocial healer into some form of intimacy with four of her challenges down, and that would give me a potential reason to deliberately meet up with Amy in the future. Which, in turn, might let me interact with Glory Girl when she comes to taxi her around.

Of course, that was all assuming that I could actually win. Amy's last challenge had stalled me for a while. This next one was probably harder than Glory Girl's current challenge, even if I couldn't think of an exact counter to the Brute opting to stay at range throwing cars at me right now - there was just a general expectation that later challenges were harder when comparing between peers.

Amy Dallon

Candidate 4/7

(LUST) (REAL)​

Not a common set of modifiers. In fact, I'd have called them completely contradictory given what they both do to the mindset of the target - one to simulate the target near-perfectly, the other to push aside their personality in favour of a mere vessel for their power.

And wasn't the challenge title 'heroine' before? I'd seen titles change before, but it hadn't been common so far - although perhaps that was just that I hadn't progressed many Capes far enough into their challenges to see every variation. "Challenge." Doesn't matter.

I touch down in the middle of a road. A familiar one. The Dallon household is directly in front of me. For a moment, I find myself wondering if this is one of the 'moving' challenges - those few that have no true fixed location, and just move the setting of the challenge to whatever was around me when I challenged my opponent. Then I take another look around. A few too many torn-up sections of the road. Shattered windows in the cars. A suspicious hole in the wall of the Dallon household and signs of battle. A bit too 'different' to be one of those challenges.

Which is enough to make me feel pretty cautious. It would be one thing if the location was just based on the area around me, but with that possibility eliminated - the scenario considered Amy, likely somewhere inside that building, to be a 'harder' challenge than the one I'd fought just before. Sometimes the 'harder' rule didn't always apply. Some challenges were easier to cheese than others. Taylor riding around on a giant bug immediately after I'd gotten a bug-controlling power was still a funny one to me - but at least I could understand the idea there. She objectively was stronger... if I hadn't had the tool ready.

But this one was harder to reconcile. No GANG modifier this time. No reinforcements coming her way via TIME or even WRLD at a stretch. Just a glorified mentality adjustment. On the surface, it looks like an easy win. That doesn't sit right with me. My powers given me freebies sometimes, but it usually feels somewhat obvious about it - usually a straight-fight that is within my capabilities to win in a single round, or a completely vulnerable target, or someone I can beat in the exact same way as the previous round with no adjustments.

If I took it at face value, I could walk in there right now with my ash clone and knight, start a 3v1 against a lone Panacea and win as long as I didn't let her touch me when I didn't have her own power active. Did I think that was exactly how it would go down? No.

LUST. What would that do to Panacea? I already knew, to a certain extent, that her power wasn't simply healing. I could excuse my own variant of the power being different, but fighting her challenges had given me enough of an understanding that she was, in reality, aware and capable of using her power as a weapon - not just a tool to knock someone out with. The only issue I had was that I didn't really know what that looked like, my own version of the power was fairly weak. Was I looking at a power that was usually used to re-set bones instead being used to break them? If she could fix eyesight, could she blind with a single touch as well? Did it even really matter? Just because her power might have the ability to be used in more destructive ways than she had so far, the reality was that I'd already seen the worst thing she could do by touching me - knocking me out with a touch. Whether she could command my heart to shut down or if she had to go and find a sharp object to finish me off didn't really matter once I was defenceless.

No, that was still too much wishful thinking. Just like how Clockblocker never used the extremely-lethal aspects of his power before the LUST modifier, Panacea must have a reason for the modifier to be here. I don't think I'd had a single Cape with that modifier yet that hadn't had at least one major new trick that they pulled out because of it. It wasn't one of the modifiers that was just thrown around as background noise, like ZONE or WRLD - it's presence meant that I was missing something fundamental. Something that she'd been hiding.

She was still a Striker. I'm sure of that much. There'd be no reason to hide that. And that meant that her tricks could be avoided by simply not being in close quarters with her. Nothing changed there.

Unless it was the Manton limit that was different? That could be it. If I assumed that her power actually was a more advanced version of mine, then she might have deliberately concealed the fact that she wasn't Manton-limited to maintain her non-combatant status. And if even I, with my power, was able to reshape bone and skin with a touch - then why would she be so limited? Perhaps this Panacea would be closer to Aegis. Three hearts. Four brains.

No. If her defensive utility could be that subtle, that limited to invisible, internal changes - she would have used it by now. It had to be something that was obvious and offensive by nature. A fighting style. Could she grow extra arms for herself, perhaps? Or did it even need to be human at all? This train of thought was making sense now. I doubted New Wave would have appreciated the PR from their cute healer sprouting scythes from her arms and covering herself with scales to become a pseudo-Brute. A powerful, regenerating Brute with a mover rating and the equivalent of an insta-kill on touch - that would be a challenge worthy of escalating from the previous hospital bet.

Maybe I'm getting ahead of myself. LUST wasn't exclusive to Capes. Normies had it too, and it wasn't like I needed to reinvent the wheel looking for tricks there. Just needed to walk inside and see what I was looking at. I was only being reluctant because this might be the only shot I get of her tonight. I intended to linger long enough to try out Brandish too, but that was a bad matchup for the current me to try and handle in a single challenge. The father of the house was a stay-at-home bum and rarely showed himself during my stakeouts unless New Wave as a whole left on a patrol. In summary, this was probably my best shot for the day unless I got lucky.

Two ways to play this out. Scout, or prepare for battle. I could send my ash clone in and peer through its eyes, try and see if I was walking into a trap or if anything crazy was happening. Or, I could build my knight. That wasn't quiet or subtle, but with the street looking somewhat torn-up there was enough material around to build it to a respectable level, at which point it would be enough of a Brute to pulverise the street and nearby walls to build itself up even more. Panacea would obviously notice the commotion right away, but it was still one of the strongest tools I had given time.

Time that I didn't necessarily have to sit around waiting, I remind myself. REAL didn't start the fight in the same way as ALRT, but it did mean that whatever Amy was doing - she was moving. She was doing something. Usually that aspect of the modifier was a mild curiosity at most, but combined with LUST? It would probably be best to not leave her to her own devices. I had the advantage, no need to let anything she could potentially work on change that.

Knight it is. Overwhelming force with something that wasn't even biological in nature. Not even the tentacle underneath it, despite appearances. My ash clone rises next to me, wordlessly accepting my gift of Mush's power before lashing out at a nearby driveway full of pebbles, the first makings of the knight slowly taking shape as the tentacle doubles back on itself to form the start of a centralised body.

And me? I just wait. If my power dropped me in front of a house, it usually meant that the target was inside. The enemy had a death-touch power, there was no reason for me to walk in when in less than three minutes my knight would be able to, albeit very awkwardly, flop on top of the building and flatten it via pure bulk. The 'giant' version might be terrible at anything other than simply shambling forward and collapsing on command, but raw, uncontrolled mass had advantages that the flexible, powerful knight didn't have - and it wasn't like the giant had to hold onto all of that mass either. If I needed the knight, then my ash clone only had to manipulate the tentacle to drop its load, condense itself into a tighter form and be more selective with the materials before the smaller figure emerges. That wasn't possible to do so easily in reverse - it would have to find a giants-worth of material first, not such an easy task to do in a hurry.

The door opens. And there stands Panacea.

It's definitely her. Although the white robes have more red than usual - and the expression on her face is... off.

"Greg." She locks eyes with me across the street. I blink. Ah. REAL did have a tendency to have more coherent enemies, but they didn't usually speak unprompted. "There you are."

"Here I am." I agree. Talking was good. My knight was probably already strong enough to pulp her in one swing, but the extra time only made it stronger with each second of gathering material. "Uh, how's life treating you?"

"You have the nerve to ask that? Funny." The hatred in her voice is at odds with the beatific smile on her face. "But to answer the question, it's fine. Even after everything you did... I saved them all. It's a temporary solution, but everything is going to be okay. Once you're gone - I'll fix this. I'll fix everything. Everyone. Everything will be back how it should be again." She pats at her baggy robes for a moment, the smile disappearing as a murderous expression appears. "You just have to die first."

"O-kay..." I click my tongue against my teeth. Not the first time I've been inserted into a fictional scenario, but I was definitely missing context here. "Listen, I'm not sure what exactly I did - or rather, what the person who you think I am did before I replaced them - but I'm willing to talk this out." Only a partial lie. I was absolutely going to split her skull open with my knight before she got close, but I was willing to fish for information about the scenario first. It could help in the next one, or even give me some unrelated insights like Taylor's bank-challenge had on the Undersiders and Browbeat.

Panacea doesn't dignify that with a response. Instead, she just charges towards me. A full-on suicidal sprint. I'd expected that. Hoped for it, even. It meant that she intended to win by touching me. Unfortunately, while she was a good deal faster than the last time I'd seen her - she clearly wasn't sprouting wings or hooved legs or anything - so my theory on LUST indicating a lack of a Manton limit just looked stupid now. My knight steps forward to block her path - not enough material gathered to form a weapon in addition to the body, but instead it had simply bulked up one arm to a greater extent to turn it into an oversized club.

Amy doesn't slow her sprint, or even turn her head to acknowledge certain death stepping into her path.

I don't like that.

I pinch space behind me and retreat, mentally brushing over my defensive powers. Speed state... not at this distance. Dashing through an unknown wall in the shadow state could cost me the fight for no reason, but simply retreating to maintain my current distance as best I can would be smart. I can't truly give a reason but... there's a common argument about what 'bloodlust' means on powerscaling boards - it doesn't mean literal bloodthirst, it means an optimised user of their power willing to do whatever they need to do to win. Now, how that interacts with REAL remains a mystery - but it meant that I couldn't chalk her charge down as the move of a maddened, enraged animal with no thoughts other than violence in her head. She was thinking. Planning out a way to win. Part of this plan was a rabid charge towards me, despite the obvious Brute about to kill her before she made it halfway.

If she's confident in the face of that, I'm worried.

A worry that is soundly vindicated when my knight winds up for a hammer blow down on Amy's head as she tries to pass - at this mass, I've seen hits like that tear through cars like paper and shatter concrete. On a human skull? There should be nothing left to recognise.

But the attack bounces off.

Literally bounces. My knight nearly falls over from the recoil, that entire 'limb' shedding a full half of its mass before starting to salvage and reform even while the knight itself turns to chase after the healer. Too slow.

No, too fast. I realise that now. I'd chalked it up to better running form at first, but she wasn't just running faster than her previous challenge-self - she was running faster than me.

And I wasn't ready for that. I didn't have threads extracted ready for Clockblocking, and the downside of making the initial knight was that I couldn't destroy and resummon my ash clone without waiting out the cooldown. I'd blown Vista's power already, and I'd need to survive for the next thirty seconds before space untangled itself and I could use it again.

If all she can do is try to touch me... I should be able to win. I still have other powers. I still have the knight, as long as I can circle back around to it. Echo. Forcefield. Panacea's own power should save me from the one-shot while touching. If that was all Panacea had, I should still easily win.

But I may be stupid, but I'm not stupid - if that makes sense. I know what I just saw. That wasn't any enhanced durability of her body that deflected my knight's killing blow. That was Glory Girl's forcefield. And while I didn't know exactly what to make of that, or her little speech at the beginning... I could extrapolate just a little bit and reason that if the defensive aspect of the forcefield was in play, then the offensive part might be too. I didn't mind the idea of fisticuffs and grappling against weak little Panacea, but the maths changes if she is going to start bench-pressing trucks and punching hard enough to shatter stone.

No thanks. I bound upwards, blowing two charges of my shadow state to extend the glide. I scramble at the edge of the low rooftop, my glide taking me just short of a comfortable landing - but I'm not leaving myself defenceless.

Not when that last line of reasoning led to the possibility that she can fly right now.

Fortunately, she doesn't.

Unfortunately, my ash clone abruptly dies while I'm scrambling up onto the roof - taking my knight with it.

Unusual, it's usually good at keeping itself at a safe distance while the knight is out - but I suppose it isn't a mover in its own right, there's nothing that it can do to run away from something faster than I am. That means I can't just lead her on a loop to get back to the relative safety of my undying protector until I can respawn my ash clone. That's bad. I need to stall, but my best move to do that is to completely leave the area via the speed state. If I do that, I'd have all the time in the world to recreate my knight at its strongest, with the best materials... but Panacea would have no need to come and fight me. With the LUST modifier, she could just disappear into the city if it was apparent that my knight was too strong to face and I'd never find her again before the anti-stalling measures kicked in.

Too late to doubt myself. I launch a spinning fist through the air, storing it as an Echo. I know how Glory Girl's shield works. I also know that, for the real deal, her Brute powers largely stem from the forcefield being active. I'm very confident that I'm still a more skilled fighter than Panacea no matter what modifiers she has. Even if I can only engage her for a single exchange of blows before her forcefield returns, that's still a trade that should be in my favour.

In theory. I watch as Panacea floats up to the rooftop in a short burst. A little unsteady, a little erratic. That was interesting. Just as interesting as seeing that she had flight, but hadn't used it so far. Glory Girl at full speed would have been able to catch me at her initial distance before I even had the chance to activate speed state. The fact that she hadn't - or couldn't - use it like that was a good data point. A data point that still left me incredibly confused as to what is happening.

She charges straight at me again as I mentally eye my recovering powers. Workable. I time the Echo to shatter her forcefield, my fist slamming towards her stomach a moment later - her lacking defensive guard easily opening up the opportunity for a clean hit. The hit doesn't register like it should. I hit something under her robes, but not in the way I was expecting. I didn't hit her, but something she was concealing underneath her baggy clothes.

And I'm pretty sure I just broke my hand. That too. Brute power? Very much still active. In a burst of paranoia, I switch away from Panacea's power to Glory Girl's just in time to halt her counterattack. I'm not sure if that would have been the weak hit that I was initially expecting, or if the toughness I'd felt in my attack would have translated to a powerful offensive strike too - but with my options limited, I'd prefer to show caution for the sake of getting more information.

Amy doesn't slow down. Her hand transitioning from a fist into a palm, curled as if grasping something - right as a sizzling spear of golden light materialises in her grip. I immediately drop into the shadow state, willing myself down through the ceiling to get away from the weapons formed from Brandish's power. Somehow, I'm not surprised about that. Nor am I surprised as her other hand comes up to point at the ceiling I'm vanishing into - already aglow with light. I'm still in the shadow state when the blast comes out and wipes out the area - I land uninjured, idly noting that interaction for the future. Whichever one that was, the blasts are kinetic and not 'energy' - the shadow state handles them fine.

Glory Girl. Brandish. One of the blaster-inclined Pelhams. And I'm pretty sure that I could attribute the other Brute effect and enhanced movement to Manpower. I see the theme. I don't understand how or why, but I see it. All of New Wave packaged into one awkward, angry healer.

Should have ran away with the speed state after all. I have nothing else left but another charge of the shadow state. The spear in her hand pierces through me as I shift around it, and I immediately reform - screaming as I find myself impaled on it.

It's over. She seizes my hand in hers, and I reflexively shift back into holding her own power as my active one to stop her from knocking me out. She pauses for a moment, then my entire arm starts to pulse in warning, a creeping, growing sensation of wrongness that quickly translates into raw pain - a burning sensation spreading through my body from the point of contact. I grimace, choking back the instinctive scream. I knew this one. Holding her power just stopped her from getting full insight into my body and doing whatever she wanted instantly, turning the surgeon's scalpel into a clumsy hacksaw. That kept me safe in short exchanges, but it wasn't the same as her not being able to do anything when given time to work and a plain canvas to experiment on.

Begrudgingly, I drop her power before she can do worse. I'm not a masochist, I'm out of winning options - I'll take the easy way out this time. The instant I drop her power, darkness consumes my vision.

FAILURE​

I hear the distant noise of the two sisters closing the door behind them as I shake my vision clear.

"What the fuck was that." I whisper to myself. Maybe I was onto something with the fake Manton limit? Perhaps she was modifying her own brain to mimic the Corona Pollentia of other Capes? Was that even possible? No. If it was that simple, she'd be an active Cape - a budget Eidolon even with what little I'd seen just now. And her speech... I could draw all kinds of theories from that. In the scenario, something had happened to the rest of New Wave - Panacea had done... something. Borrowed their powers in some way. But that wasn't her power. A second trigger? That would be a first. Completing challenges had sometimes seemed to tweak the powers of those I beat, but I'd never fought someone with a completely different power expression yet.

Could I be looking at the effects of a second unknown Cape? A Tinker, perhaps? That would explain the unusual shape of what was under her robes, although it was hard to tell if I was hitting armour plating, solid metal from a Tinkertech device or just Manpower's power in action. Or even Shielder, if the defensive construct could be made that close to her body. It was hard to be sure, but I was confident that it didn't feel the same as Glory Girl's shield. Which meant that it wasn't impossible to overcome with raw power. I'd like to test one of my Parian-fuelled footballs against it, but timing that attack around Glory Girl's shield would be difficult to say the least. The mechablade or my knight could do it too, but a surprise attack with either of those was... unlikely.

I sit in place to wait some more. No point in speculating. I knew what to avoid now for next round. Rather than over-focusing on avoiding her Striker range, I should opt to stay somewhat close to her so that I couldn't be separated from my knight - that was my greatest tool against all of 'her' new powers. No amount of slashes, blasts or concussive force would destroy it unless she noticed the ash clone hiding nearby and realised the deception - with the knight around, I'd be in a permanent 2v1 situation and probably fare quite a bit better than I had in surviving alone. Nevermind how much easier it would be to reliably break through Glory Girl's shield with a second melee combatant fighting with me.

I tap my foot against the floor. Boring. And I'd already killed my ash clone back at my workshop to ensure the downtime wasn't too long, so I couldn't even distract myself with a bit of Tinkering. Sitting around doing nothing for the next hour or two might be optimal, but that didn't make it any easier to stay focused.

To my surprise, the next activity isn't the arrival of the Dallon matriarch. It's Panacea, an oversized hoodie raised over her head as she half-jogs down the path - then turns down the street past my current observation spot.

Interesting. And a potential opportunity. If I stayed in place, I'd likely catch Brandish when she eventually returned from work - and I may or may not catch Panacea getting back from wherever she was going before I had to leave, depending on how long she was out for.

Or, I could follow Panacea. Not literally stalking her, but wherever she was going - she hadn't taken Glory Girl with her as a taxi. And while I couldn't claim to have a complete understanding of her social life, I was pretty sure she was closer to Taylor than she was to Em- Madison. I couldn't completely ignore the possibility that she was just going on a quiet shopping trip somewhere, but the far more likely scenario was that I'd spotted her slipping out to go on a hospital visit. An affair that would take hours, probably end with a request for someone to pick her up and also provide me with plenty of exposure to actually talk and interact with her if I 'just happened' to visit the same hospital.

Plus, I'd get more chances to finish her current challenge and that would probably be enough to get laid with the ever-grumpy healer.

An easy decision, when I frame it like that.

It's the work of seconds to find a nearby bug, assign it as an administrator and ferry it through the window in my palm with my shadow state. I head back through the household, monitoring the movements of my new administrator as it doggedly chases down it's target. Vision wasn't exactly great through my bug of choice, but it wasn't exactly a busy street - and Panacea's 'discreet' outfit had plenty of places for an enterprising bug to nestle in and hide.

With the tracker bug in position, I quietly leave the house and exit the street in a completely different direction to the path she took. I need to find a good spot to change into my 'costume' - albeit it wasn't quite the real-deal that I'd be picking up at Parian's... tomorrow? Tomorrow. Void Cowboy shouldn't be seen coming directly at an angle from the Dallon household, people would make entirely correct assumptions as to why I'd been in the area once they knew the truth. I needed to get to a separate area of the city, change, enter the speed-state and get ahead of wherever Panacea was walking - so that rather than me 'following' her, she just coincidentally went somewhere that I happened to be at already.

But first, setting a brisk pace while checking maps of Brockton Bay on my phone. It would be pretty awkward to set up shop in the wrong hospital only to realise she'd walked right past to the clinic a few blocks down the road. Or that she was going to a friends house instead.

I pause at that. No. Impossible. Amy was cut from the same cloth as Taylor, I was pretty sure of that. Any friends she had were caused by pure osmosis from hanging around her hot sister.

That was a good thing. For me. I feel like the loner, anti-social types tended to latch onto me better.

...damn. Saying that makes me feel like I'm some kind of domestic abuser, talking about how it's better if my wife doesn't have any other friends she can go to for help. It's not like that! Actually, it's better if they have close friends because then I can get them in the same net!

No, that sounds worse. Maybe I should stop thinking about better ways to phrase my choice in target selection, and focus my inner monologue on heroic-sounding things. Like how I was going to become the pillar of love and support that arguably the most heroic, selfless figure in the Bay truly deserved.

And if I had to smash her skull open a few times to do that? That was life.


All that effort to monitor her location, predict her path, narrow down the possibilities far enough in advance that I could slip in long before she arrived... and she just goes straight to Brockton General. Makes me feel like the effort was completely wasted, picking the most boring answer possible.

But it did make things easier. This wasn't the first time I've been to Brockton General. This wasn't even the first time clambering over the back fences and phasing through a second-floor window of Brockton General. The lady at the front desk was bitchy the first time around, talking about licenses and liability - so I just skip that step every time. Who needs an expensive doctor scaring away the only-slightly-shifty guy offering free healthcare? The patients can make their own choices, that's what I say.

The doctors were begrudgingly aware of me and what I did, so when I let myself in through the window a nurse just blinks blandly at me before shrugging and leaving the room, doubtless to make my presence somebody else's problem.

That's right. Leave the healing to the heavy-hitters. Big Pharma has nothing on my ability to poke people.

Void Cowboy, modern-day saint. Isn't it crazy that I've never even been offered a medal for this?

"No. You're lucky they don't arrest you for trespassing." My patient whines.

I blink. "Did I say that out loud?"

"Yes." The teen nods. "You sounded like an idiot." He lies. "Ow!" The boy hisses at me as I shift my grip around his knee. "Ow! Ow! That hurts!"

"Stop whining." I tell him blandly. "Painkillers are for nerds. And people who know anything about dosages." I match his level gaze as he glares at me, momentarily forgetting his pain in favour of complaining about Saint Veder. "No, really. It's just a fracture, or something like that. It will be fixed before you know it." I'm pretty sure the medical term is something like that, but I'm not going to lose any sleep if the correct term is a 'fuluminous break of the lower tibial vertebrae' or some other nonsensical string of words put together. I was a real healer, not an overpaid nerd with a fetish for latin. Leg bad? Poke. Leg good.

It really is that simple. My version of Panacea's power doesn't need me to know. I'm just going off vibes, telling my power to vaguely push things back to how they should be and not thinking too hard about it - the power runs off to do everything it needs to do, one step at a time. At times, it feels like setting some kind of healing-puppy loose on the body, watching it chase from one area of interest to the next - the majority of its moves easy to understand, some few only becoming clear when I really specify what I want the power to do.

Interviews with Panacea had often gone into the in-depth biological sense that she gets when healing, the control she needs to exhibit - but I don't have anything that crazy. The upgraded version of Panacea's power gave me more of a... wireframe image in my head of what I was touching. A heatmap of 'wrongness', coupled with expanding my 'range' from just a few inches from the point I was touching to something that radiated out across most of the body - with my ability to enact change still at its best and most precise at the point of contact. The boy winces again as bones move on their own under my thumb. "Here, want to know a cool pain management trick from Void Cowboy himself?"

"Who?" I resist the urge to murder him a little bit for that in the name of attitude improvement.

I adopt a wise expression. "Pain is about perspective. Like, a little snot-nosed kid falls over onto the ground - it's one of the most painful things that's ever happened to him. Right at the top of his pain scale, so he starts crying. But as they get older, they get tougher, they learn that there's way more painful things in the world. They get kicked in the balls by some bitchy girls. He falls off a building and breaks his leg. He loses his hardcore survival run in CapeScape because the power went out. Then, they fall over again, they realise its not really that painful at all and they just get over it like a man." I nod firmly. "That's how pain works. So all you need is one really painful experience at the top of the scale, and you'll be basically invincible from that point on. You'll break your bones and keep soldiering on like nothing ever happened."

"That's not right. That's stupid." He tells me.

"You're stupid." I frown at him. "Here. First time I ever got stabbed - I was basically useless until-" I died. "-I got better. Had to run away like a bitch and totally lost the fight. But I get stabbed these days? I laugh, because now they think they've won - but I can trap the knife and beat the shit out of them. I've realised that a dinky little bit of pain like that isn't so high on the scale after all, and that a little blood loss doesn't really matter if you can still move. It's a willpower thing. So take it from me - you can man up and soldier through this. Here: I know this isn't that bad. How painful is this for you right now, a four? A five?"

"Ten." He hisses.

"Ten is high." I inform him helpfully.

"Ten." He insists.

"Wow." I blink. "You're kind of a little bitch, huh? You're acting like a little kid and you're barely younger than me."

"I'm a patient, you'll get in trouble talking to me like that." It's his turn to frown back at me.

"Yeah?" I lean forward. "What are you going to do about it, cry on me?"

That shut him up for a moment. Long enough for the bone to slip back into place as if nothing changed. "Done, why don't you-"

The door slams open. "You!" Panacea jabs her finger at me.

"Me?" I point at myself innocently.

"You!" She confirms. "You're, what do you even think you're doing-" She glances at my current patient then storms over, grabbing his hand and blankly staring into nothing for a moment. "You did it again!"

"What did he do?" He says, suddenly looking more nervous than he ever had since I entered the room.

"Using my power like that, you can't just do that!" She glares at me, looking closer to a particularly outraged gerbil than anything truly intimidating.

"You've lost me." I admit. "I fixed his leg. That's pretty normal, I've done that before. Actually, I'm pretty sure you've stood around to watch as I do it when the PRT was getting kind of nervous about whether or not what I was doing was safe. Why complain now?"

"It's not what you did, it's how you did it. You fixed his leg by borrowing material from elsewhere in his body. You're not just healing, not just pushing things back together - you're moving things around. Changing things." She stresses that last part as if it means something. "You said- you said your version of my power couldn't do anything that serious!"

"Oh, right. I've noticed my copied powers get stronger as I hang around the people I copied them from. Guess we've bumped into each other enough that we crossed a hurdle, because I got a pretty neat upgrade in functionality." I nod. "And about the leg, yeah, pretty sure I felt my power stealing from his other one to make it work, I guess the surgery meant not everything was still inside the body, and if my power just shunted everything together he'd be shorter on one side and walk funny for the rest of his life. Made him a little shorter in the process, but not by much-"

"I'm shorter now?"

"-so you decided to mess with his future growth to fix that. A tweak to grow a little bit taller to offset what you did now." She cuts in. Is that what I did? Neat. "Do you have any idea the long-term damage you could do if you were even slightly off with your calculations?"

"Calculation? Nothing like that. It's not really me doing the work at that level, I'm kind of the supervisor. The middle-manager. The power wanted to do it, and I trust that it knows the technical details better than me - so I just gave it directions and let it work out the minor details itself. Worked great, as you can see." I pause. "As you can hopefully see? I'd appreciate a second opinion, still testing a few things since this side of my power got upgraded. It's always worked pretty well on my intent so far, but I do respect your expertise on the matter."

"No, it's fine. It's right, but-" She lets out a snarl of frustration. "-but you can't just start doing that. If you start changing things on a whim, where does it stop?"

I give her a strange look. "Why does it need to stop? It worked, didn't it?"

She glowers at me, then at my patient - then back to me. "We'll talk about this outside. This conversation isn't over." She glances at the boy. "I'll let the staff know that you're fine. They'll handle things from here. I need to have a private talk with this idiot."

"Wait, wait, wait - you can make me grow more with your power?" The boy pipes up urgently. I nod. "You did that to my legs specifically? You can target it?"

I nod again, then pause. "No way dude. That's gay."

"No, no - this is a thing between men! I wouldn't tell a soul, and I'm not talking anything crazy here - just, you know, a little edge in the future." He makes a pinching gesture with his hand. "Like, an inch or two could go a long way and nobody would ever think anything of it."

Panacea looks confused.

"Super gay." I repeat.

"It's not! It would be article one of the bro code if people knew about it!" He adopts a pleading expression. "I'll take back every bad thing I ever said about you. I'll admit I was being a little bitch earlier just to be annoying. Just a tweak."

"Not in the habit of doing things like that." But... Panacea's reaction would probably be funny. "But, sure. Here." I poke his thigh, letting my power radiate out and directing it with a thought.

Panacea sends me a deeply suspicious look, then reaches out wordlessly to take the patient's hand again.

She kicks me in the shin. Hard. "Ow, what the fuck?" I gripe at the sudden assault.

"After everything I just said!" She growls at me. She attempts to kick me again. I dodge this time. "Stay still!"

"No!" I refuse. The next kick misses as I transfer into the shadow state.

"It's done?" The boy grins. "Brother, I will literally die for you. Don't worry, I'll never tell a soul - it's all natural! You won't regret this. I'm gonna buy all your merch. I'm gonna-"

"Don't encourage him!" She seizes hold of my ear and starts half-dragging me out of the room. Ow! What the fuck? "We're done here!"

As I allow myself to be hauled out of the room by the irate healer, my previous patient - now apparently transformed into my biggest fan - glances between the two of us, seems to come to an unspoken conclusion about what was happening, then sends me an exaggerated wink, a thumbs up and a whispered 'good luck'. The crude gesture with his hands afterwards is entirely unnecessary. I get the point.

But, thanks - brother. I'm actually kind of glad I didn't kill you a few times to get a more agreeable chick now.

Amy tries to drag me somewhere for a private chat. But I'd rather delay that chat for as long as possible. After all, this was clearly important - and now that she's calmed down, also something that she doesn't want to discuss in front of patients. Clearly, she wasn't going to part ways until she'd pinned me down for that chat. But she would be willing to leave if there were still patients in the building in need - couldn't heal everyone at once, not in a building this size.

So, to maximise my Amy time... I scurry into the next patient room despite her best efforts to pull me aside. And then the next. And then... "Challenge." Time for another round, now that the timer was down enough.

This time, I know the plan. The ash clone hides in a nearby building, stretching out the tentacle into the street before starting to form the knight. The final product would be a bit weaker, but that was nothing compared to the danger of losing the knight. From what I'd seen, the gain in speed and power wasn't worth the danger here - and the street wasn't torn-up enough to try anything tricky like hiding the ash clone in a ditch or a crater somewhere.

Amy emerges again. Faster than before, if only because I deployed the knight and started making noise earlier. The same opening speech, and the same lack of details coming my way. She's not interested in a real conversation. Kind of a shame, actually. The LUST modifier is probably screwing me a bit here, if talking is suboptimal then the modifier must be pushing her to avoid it - especially as my knight continually grows in size and strength.

More prepared this time, and more aware of what options she has - it's easier to think. Easier to notice. Easier to ask questions.

Question one: If she has, presumably multiple, Blaster powers - why does she run into melee range against my obviously-melee-focused knight and myself? Raw hatred? Not with the LUST modifier in play, even if REAL was playing a part somewhere - this had to be more than just a preference or a choice in fighting style. Somehow, blasting me continuously from afar was a suboptimal move for the girl in front of me. Why is that?

What follows her charge is a little more than fifty seconds of me briefly exchanging blows, burning a defensive power and then cowering behind my infinitely-recovering knight. She hadn't shown herself as able to notably tear away the mass that the knight had gathered - and simply applying concussive force or occasionally slicing it apart only served to make the material more and more suitable for Mush's power. She certainly had the strength to rip pieces off and throw them away, the tentacle itself wasn't that strong - immortal, yes, impossible to temporarily rip apart, no. But she either didn't recognise the power, or was content in just briefly neutralising it for a few seconds at a time while she focused on me - exactly what I'd been hoping for.

But the whole exchange highlighted the second question: Why wasn't I seeing Flashbang's power at all? It should be amazing in this exact scenario - exploding orbs scattered all around the knight, hitting me would be assured unless I burned through my limited stock of defensive powers. Why was she bothering to cycle through short-ranged-blasts and Brandish's power at all, when using Manpower for an extended period of time would catch me with comparative ease? I could excuse not knowing about the weakness of the shadow state, but she had enough pseudo-Mover powers that I shouldn't really be able to get away with ducking and running around my knight like this so easily.

The third question starts to form in my head a little over a minute after that. When she starts to dodge rather than take blows head-on, the almost-rabid pace of her attacks making way for a somewhat more measured approach - which ironically makes it easier for me, giving me more time to get my cooldown-based powers back between each engagement. The thought crystallises when I land in a clean hit on her face in exchange for a blade of surging light scoring a line of blood across the side of my torso. The question: Why did that hit? I hadn't taken down Glory Girl's shield yet.

Panacea bounds away, hands already rising to deliver a warning set of concussive blasts to create distance. I duck behind my knight again as it weathers the barrage largely unscathed - swaying like an oversized willow but ultimately reshaping itself again, the only loss being the material that had been blasted clear from the area at the point of impact.

Running out of juice for her powers? She wants to get away, which means I want to follow her. It means taking my ash clone and knight with me and potentially risking that trick being discovered as the clone leaves its hiding spot, but I don't have a choice. Even with her extra powers seeming to have some issues, I don't fancy my chances in a 1v1.

She's still faster than me outside of the speed state, almost seeming to glide across the ground at times - something that I can now recognise as the briefest bursts of the multiple flight powers she has access to right now. Another question, all of them leading me to the same answer - that she's rationing her power use. That it's a limited resource. And, presumably, she's backing off now in an attempt to replenish it.

It doesn't take long to verify that. Amy's hand snakes around the throat of a nearby NPC, who momentarily struggles before going limp - as I slow my approach and wait for my knight to catch up, letting it take a small detour to stockpile more resources for itself.

It's a testament to how completely used I am to the occasional NPC wandering the streets and not reacting to my fights that I'm more shocked about one actually being relevant than I am at whatever she's doing right now. The NPC practically erupts like a blood bag, coating the girl blood and viscera - the remains of the man still held loosely in one hand as she turns to me, spare hand raised to start firing blasts at me.

My knight quietly steps in front of me as I burn a shadow state charge and Glory Girl's shield to survive the barrage. The knight steps in front of me, a nearby car door wrenched in two to be used as a shield - I reach across and tap it to Clockblock it in place. The effects of the barrage immediately drop in potency, although Amy's enthusiasm for it doesn't diminish with it.

But I'm pretty sure I've solved this mystery now. Her power, the limitations of my version, the oddities I'd observed so far and now this... 'harvesting'? All I have to do is wait, and let my theory be proven.

I smile when the assault stops. Laserdream and Lady Photon would both have done a better job in a few seconds than Amy's imitation had done over the last few minutes. "Careful now, looks like you've drained your little battery there dry."

She spits on the ground as she slowly walks towards me, a manic look in her eyes. "I don't need them to kill you."

I grin wider. "But that's just it, isn't it? It's not about killing me. I'll admit, it took me a while to piece it together - I had a pretty set vision of what your power could and couldn't do, and just assumed that my power was the weird one. When I was thinking about what 'twist' on your powers the LUST modifier could do, I was thinking that your power wasn't healing - but just generally manipulating the human body into a desired shape. That the big secret was that you could just, turn everyone into Aegis if you wanted. Give them some extra features, make your own personal army. Then you showed off your, New Wave all-in-one trick and I thought - 'aha, it's the no-brains thing! She can tweak brains to copy other Capes powers!'. I really thought that I'd solved it."

She paces closer, utterly silent.

I shake my head. "But seeing you turn that guy into a husk like that, it really gave me a new perspective on the things you've been doing. The fact that you were covered in gore last time I got a clean look at you, and now you're looking almost normal again - another interesting datapoint. You're not manipulating bodies. You're manipulating biomass and repurposing it however you please. I wonder, do your parents know that baby Nilbog has been living under their roof this entire time?" I taunt the approaching healer.

"I don't want to hear that from you of all people, you fucking monster." She spits.

"That's not very Panacea-like of you." I tilt my head at her. "And, 'me, of all people'? I suppose that's fair, I understand the scenario now. I wondered why your title had changed to 'Candidate', but it's pretty obvious now. This entire scenario is a what-if event, showcasing your application into the Slaughterhouse Nine. And I'm Jack. Or, Greg, I suppose. Not a very villainous name, but I suppose people called Jack used to feel the same once upon a time."

"Application?" She scoffs. "I'm not like you. I'm nothing like you or any of your pathetic little group members. I'm going to kill you, and all of your friends. I'm a heroine, a proud member of New Wave - and nothing is going to change that."

I send her a mocking grin. "Poor Mr Bloodbag back there would probably disagree with some of that." A blast attempts to interrupt me. I burn a shadow state without moving. My ash clone discretely finds a spot to cower in nearby while I continue to draw her attention. Don't die, buddy - or I'll die with you. "But I am impressed with the self-delusion, that you can say all of that with a straight face. I'm a newcomer to this scenario, but even I have to admit that you're fitting right in with a prospective member right now. Filling out the vibe perfectly."

"Because one person had to die to take you down? That's a worthwhile trade for someone with a kill-count in the thousands. Countless heroes would make the same trade in a heartbeat." She counters bluntly, not yet making an aggressive move as my knight matches her every attempt to circle around it to face me directly.

I snort. "Amy, Amy, Amy. It's just the two of us. Even the big guy here can't really think. You don't need to lie. You don't need to pretend you're in the same group as those great heroes you're talking about. You're in this position for a reason. You were always going to be in this position. You're one of us." Before she can spit a denial out, I continue. "And if you want to say that I'm wrong, then just look me in the eye and say it - but, please, before you do... why don't you show me what you've got hidden under those robes of yours?"

She instantly surges forward to attack, a furious expression of hate on her face as a glowing broadsword materialises in her hands. My knight steps in and gets cleaved in two, but that isn't truly such an obstacle - it's rampant flailing as it starts to reconstitute itself clips Amy, and her forcefield drops for a moment in time for me to land a quick jab with the aid of Vista's power confusing the distance between us.

"Or rather-" I continue, weaving away from her assault. "-should I say, who?"

"It's your fault!" She screams. A trio of blasts race towards me and shatter the ground harmlessly-

-and my knight collapses. I blink. Then turn my head towards the ground she'd just hit. Ah. She accidentally severed the tentacle trailing from my hidden ash clone to the knight. Not 'lethal', but also not something that my ash clone would be able to fix in time to save me. I could buy... eight seconds or so of an enraged Amy on my own, including time spent kiting backwards away from the knight. At that point, I'd be dead even if the knight was made active again.

I make my decision. My ash clone dissolves into nothing as I forcibly retrieve Mush's power, activate it and plunge it directly into the knight at my side. I'd practiced a bit since my first use of this power, and while I was pretty sure my administrator would always be a more skilled user than me... it didn't take much finesse to fill what was already there and swing it all wildly to the side. Amy's forcefield drops again, her attack momentarily cancelled as she moves to defend herself from the next blow. I reach out to her again, already noting the sudden flex of hexagonal blocks appearing directly through her robes with a barely-noticable light. That was fine, I wasn't trying to hit her. I brush one finger against her robes before she can think to counter.

Skidmark's power. I'd barely used it since getting it. Just hadn't been able to find the right trick to use it in a fight. I could make a single-use missile of sorts with the current version with prep time - but in reality, anything that gave me prep time meant that I could either use my mechasword or my knight, both of which were superior to throwing a big rock very fast. But, as arrows appear on her robes along the line my finger traces - maybe I've found a minor use for it after all. A half-second passes, I activate the power and step back. A full half of Amy's costume shoots directly upwards, almost concealing her vision before she claws it out of her face with her hands, trying futilely to force it back down to obey gravity.

Sorry, doesn't work like that.

And, sorry - the jig is up now. I can see everything. And I'm not talking about the surprisingly-racy fashion choices.

A shivering sac of some kind hangs around her waist, pulsing, sickly-looking tubes emerge out of it - each one leading to one of seven dessicated-looking brains attached to her torso like limpets.

"There's New Wave. Your new pets to help on your quest to be a real hero, I presume?" I taunt. "Bonesaw would be proud of the little puppet-show you're pulling on. The end-result might look messy, but you're really pushing the field of medical science forward with this - how does it work, do you just push on the bits of the brain you need for the power? Or are they all in there, screaming in horror about what you've done to them?"

"Shut. Up." She seethes. "You caused this. I did this to save them, and I'll fix them all once you're dead and gone."

"Better hurry." I smile wryly. Playing the villain was fun, actually. "That's the trick, isn't it? If this was stable, this wouldn't be a fourth-level challenge. Eight combined Capes, that's an Eidolon-level fight. But, it's closer to babysitting than anything else. All of those brains constantly drying out, constantly needing to be squeezed by your power in order to activate theirs - there must be attrition along the way, burning energy, causing brain damage that not even you can fix - you can stave it off with easy-access to biomass, but without that, you're forced to slowly murder your family just to keep your pathetic life going for just another few seconds. Which is exactly what you proceed to do. You really do belong with us, don't you?"

Her response is an incoherent scream of rage that accompanies a powerful blast that sends the remains of the knight to scatter halfway across the street. Without the tentacle rooting it from the ground, it just doesn't disperse force as well.

She surges forward.
