Eight seconds. That was how long I had guessed I could last on my own from this range when she had the full range of 'her' powers.

Three minutes. That was around how long it would be before I could resummon my ash clone.

Surprisingly, I don't quite make it that long.

But I like to think that my mocking, congratulatory laughter as she tears me to pieces did a respectable amount of mental damage. I've got a role to play here, after all. Nobody truly liked Jack Slash... but you couldn't deny that he was committed to the bit. How could I let myself be outdone by him?

FAILURE​

Surprisingly, I don't really care about the failure.

Because I understood the challenge now. And it was something I could strategise around. A battle of attrition, pressing the advantage at moments of weakness - no different to hitting weak points on a video game boss during the intermission phases. Hit a brain with a clean, suitably powerful hit - and she loses a power. Forever. Keep chipping away... and it's back to just Amy. A slightly more psychotic Amy than I was used to, but I could handle that.

And actually, my newfound knowledge could be put to good use against the real, non-crazy Amy too. Because now I knew that her previous concern about 'how' I was healing people was less about the actual mechanics of what I was doing, but about how I was using her power and stepping over the rules she'd imposed on herself to not be like Bonesaw and Nilbog. It's almost enough to make me feel bad... but at the same time, that's no way to live.

"You don't understand what you're doing-" Amy insists, a hint of frustrated tears in her eyes as we leave yet another patients room.

"Actually, I think I understand perfectly." I raise a finger in the air, then correct myself. "At least, the overall picture of what I'm doing. The technical details under the hood... I guess you know better on that front. But don't worry. I understand this power better than I did. Your power. Not healing, right?"

Some frozen noise emerges from Amy's throat. Not a denial. That would be pointless after how far we'd come.

I show her some mercy. "Come on, let's take a walk somewhere quieter - we can come back for the other patients later. I'm guessing you'd rather have this chat away from anywhere you might get overheard - and I'd like to cycle Othala's power back to regeneration anyway."

She nods quietly, a stricken expression on her face. A part of me wonders why she looks so devastated - but looking at how she reacted to the scenario in her current challenge, how she reacted to my taunts... I could safely assume that the things that hit home then, are also things stewing at the forefront of her mind right now. Nilbog. Bonesaw. Recognising the things that she was easily capable of, and recoiling so hard that she became nothing but a healing outlet instead.

She follows me out of the hospital without a word. I say nothing as she hides most of her robes underneath her hoodie again as we pass through a quiet, isolated pathway, changing her appearance to looking like a mere, unfashinable normie than a superpowered individual out for a walk.

She stumbles in shock when I shrug and remove my mask and the outer outfit as well. "You already knew exactly what I looked like from the moment you touched me the first time, it's not exactly anything new to you is it?"

"It's not about that. What if someone else sees you?" She hisses.

"You were aiming for discretion, right? Or you wouldn't have covered up like that. Well, you won't draw any fewer looks walking next to an obvious Cape like me - but now? We just look like two young lovers out on a date, perfectly normal." I tap my head knowingly. "Now we can talk as much as we like, without worrying about drawing attention."

"We're not- this isn't-" Amy starts to protest, then gives up. "Whatever." She stews in silence for a moment as I narrow my eyes at her cooldown timer.

Her, unexpectedly short, cooldown. Fourth-level challenges were usually several hours of waiting between failed attempts. This one started that high, but flicks down a few minutes at a time whenever I'm not looking at it. By the time we find a park to walk through, a full half of the original cooldown is gone. For a moment, I'm reminded of Leet's challenges. That feeling of something else wanting me to keep going, to win, to push the power into being used the right way. The way I'd clicked into the zone with Leet so quickly - I was getting that same, heady feeling now. That sharpened awareness of who I was talking to and the way I should frame my approach.

Powers exist to be used. Amy's one was just the second-most obvious one about it yet. The way it practically jumped at the chance to enact any random whim, executing changes that I didn't have any real understanding of - but getting the general results I desired all the same. There was a drive there, some form of intelligence interpreting my will - it was eager to be used. And, in turn, I was eager to use it.

And I would bet my entire fortune that Amy would feel the same with just a little push.

Eventually, she speaks first. "When you said 'weak variant' of my powers, I'd really hoped it wouldn't get to this point."

"Why, because you're worried about what I might do?" I stretch my arms out. "Or, because you're worried about what it means for you?"

"Both. I wouldn't wish this power on my worst enemy. If people realise what you could do - might do - people can go to the Birdcage or get kill orders even before committing a real crime if they're dangerous enough. If people start to talk, start to realise that you don't have the limits that I said that I have - or that I lied about limits I said I have..."

I angle my head towards her. "What will happen, exactly? Eidolon could lock in a few Master powers and take over the country if he wanted. Is he too dangerous to live?"

A frustrated look appears on her face as I avoid her point. "No, because he's a hero. He can be trusted with all that power-"

"And you aren't? The way I see it, if everyone got to run around and vote to redistribute powers to people who can be trusted with them, I think you'd end up with the exact same one you have now. Maybe you were worried about what you could do with brains. Maybe you could have made a new invasive species that eats humans. Maybe you could have done something crazy with your powers at any time. But you didn't. You're still here, years later - you've never abused your powers. You've always used them to heal freely, without charging. Even in your own time, you go out on visits like this without anyone asking you to." I thump my chest with a closed fist. "Hell, if I didn't have your example to live up to, I probably wouldn't have bothered doing this kind of trip now and then myself. What are you even doubting yourself for? Does the person I'm describing sound like a bad person to you? The kind of person that other people should be terrified about going off the rails at any moment?"

"Only because people don't know what I do. They don't know what's going on in my head - how easy it would be to do something unspeakable. A flick of the switch, that's all it would take - one moment of weakness. And it wouldn't even need to be intentional, you said your power is the intermediary for you? It isn't like that with me. I've got a full understanding of everything I do, and full control as well. Any misstep, any slip up, any lapse in judgement could be the one that causes me to accidentally make a monster. To change a person's personality beyond recognition, or give them a worse health condition further down the line. A virus or disease that dwarfs anything anyone has ever seen before." She's talkative. Far more than she's ever been with me before. "It's all possible. I wish the rules that I made up were real. It would be a relief, knowing that the survival of the human race isn't reliant on me not having a mental breakdown."

Guess she's been bottling this up for a while. I'm fine with that. I can play the supportive therapist here, and then balance it all out by using every insecurity, secret and fear against her challenge self - which gives me more insight into the real Amy. A perfect cycle.

"I look at what Nilbog did, I look at news reports on what Bonesaw threatened to do this time - and my first thought isn't 'oh how terrible'. My first thought is how I could do it better. The simple tweaks I'd have to make on my next patient with a stray thought. Who thinks like that?" She shakes her head. "Nobody would agree to let me heal them in the first place if they realised I could rewrite them with a stray thought. You think I'm a hero for coming out here to heal people? I don't even like healing. I don't feel anything for the patients anymore. I just do it to feel better about myself."

"Same." I admit, earning a withering look of disbelief. "I mean, really. I get you! The healing isn't really my thing either, just doing my good deeds every now and then so that people stop calling me a do-nothing loser on PHO and they're forced to admit that there are some positives to me having powers. And thought crimes don't exist anyway. It's perfectly natural to compare abilities or situations like that - I used to do that even before I got powers. And the only difference is that now, instead of imagining how I'd do things better if I had their powers, I imagine how I'd do things better with my powers instead. Even if it's something a little grim, like a terror attack or a lethal Cape fight or something - putting yourself in their shoes and nodding that you would have done better, you'd have double-tapped the guy on the ground, you'd have blocked the exit, they struggled with this thing but your powers could do it better... that's just human nature. Or, maybe it's just the two of us are equally fucked in the head. I'm fine with either honestly."

She stares at me. "Was that supposed to sound encouraging, or make me feel better in anyway?"

"Eh." I make a face. "I mean, I'm not a real therapist anymore than I'm a real doctor. I'm just saying you're overthinking it. Everyone has weird thoughts. You haven't acted on them yet, you're worried about becoming a bad person. Sounds like you're doing a pretty good job of being a generally good person to me - no matter what your powers are. I'm pretty sure I wouldn't have done even a fraction as much good as you've done if I was in your position."

That's an understatement. If I had her full powers, I'd definitely be closer to Blasto than Panacea. I'd ride around on a fire-breathing T-Rex and it would take months or years before anyone learned I could heal humans too. Her sense of self-imposed duty at the cost of her happiness was something to admire, but not something that should be considered an objectively good thing. Which was why it was important that I took this moping, self-hating healer and injected some joy back into her life.

And, maybe it's just a hunch, but I think that change is going to have to come from changes in how she uses her powers just as much as any change caused by me clearing her challenges.

Speaking of which... that challenge box timer has been absolutely racing down since the conversation began - and now the multi-hour timer is back at zero. I can take a hint. "Challenge." I whisper.

I materialise outside of the Dallon household again.

But I've got better plans this time. I summon my ash clone. "You know what?" I murmur. "Let's go kill some people." I head left. My ash clone heads right, Mush's power held but not actively being used yet.

Got to be quiet - I'm not looking to start the festivities quite yet. With no ALRT modifier, I may as well take advantage.

The closest NPC's go down easily, not even suspecting any danger to themselves before I'm choking them out. That's not enough. I briefly experiment with Panacea's power, but for all of my newfound flexibility - it wasn't all-powerful yet. The biggest weakness was speed, but also that I couldn't direct every part of the power personally. I knew, objectively speaking, that the power could disconnect a single vein, sever a few nerves, move the spine in just a certain way or flick a switch in the brain - and any semblance of resistance would be over. The power didn't want to do that. Sometimes it refused entirely. Sometimes it was sluggish to execute the order, or took an over-engineered route to do something simple. Rather than exploding the heart in a second, it does... something in the blood closest to my finger that eventually cascades into a minor heart attack after a minute.

Unwilling to slice one important vein, but completely willing to practically flay the skin of an entire limb apart in a few seconds. Doesn't want to knock someone unconscious at a touch, happy to prod their brain until they're an incoherently raging maniac and a threat to everyone around them. Won't do a neat little slice on the spinal cord, happy to completely remove the ability to feel pain across the entire body.

More than usual, I was feeling the presence of artificial limits here. Combined with the obvious... partnership, that using this power involved - I'd have to describe it as a reluctance to kill. No, that wasn't quite right. Using it as a tool of execution on a downed target worked without issue. Killing was fine. A reluctance to end fights unceremoniously. That was it. Not too different to my primary powers apparent hatred for guns, now that I think about it.

I do an extra loop, taking my time to purge all the NPCs I can find and dispose of their bodies. If Amy needs these to keep those brains alive, then a concerted extermination effort in the vicinity might work well to my advantage. There's no ZONE modifier here, so I'll never be able to manage too large of an area without triggering the anti-stalling measures - but last time, she only ran looking for an NPC when some of her powers started playing up. The realisation that the occasional pedestrian in this area of the city had been quietly disposed of could simply come too late for her.

Plus, I get to experiment with Amy's power. It's good to know my limits - and lack of them. It was an opportunity to follow-up on some of the things that Amy is worried about. I quickly learn that my version of the power is not precise enough to do anything truly complicated with the brain other than pump chemicals and hormones around. I don't think I'm going to be making any super-plague or uber-predator either. I just didn't have the insight into genetics and biological functions like that, and my power remains inactive when I try and prod it into action - a sign that anything world-ending is probably reserved for future challenges. On the way back to the starting area, while waiting for my ash clone cooldown, I do manage to make a detached arm capable of moving itself around after a few minutes - but it's more a mess of randomly-firing nerves and muscles than any useful tool or combat-capable pet.

Vision. That was the hardest part. The wireframe-like look that my power gave me was a useful framework to express my desires on, but outside of simply 'fixing' things - I didn't truly know what I wanted, so my job as the 'director' of the power was lacking. It was fine when I was going in with the idea of 'fixing the leg to look like a normal leg', 'wake him up, 'make this guy's heart issues go away' or 'grow this eye back'. That was easy. A simple order to smooth out the wrongness that the power had already identified, or to restore to things to their default, natural shape. There were limitations on the power's side too, but I had to acknowledge the fact that I was the weaker link overall. But I can't dedicate myself to medicine and biology like Amy, until Victor's power can do enough work to make my own knowledge viable - I'll just have to wait for a Thinker power to better guide me on this one.

But that's fine. I'm used to waiting for later synergies by now. I never expected this to be an all-powerful world-destroying power at this level anyway. I'd gone into today hoping for an upgrade to my healing abilities and something that would help shred through flesh in the hopes that it would neutralise Browbeat's power when we meet tomorrow. The extra features? Unexpected, but interesting. I'll take them.

And, if Amy can hurry up and die already - I'll start working on the next one too.

Time for the next round to formally begin. I noisily form my knight again. Except, when Amy shows her face this time... I dismiss my ash clone. After all, as long as the material was gathered up - I'd just proven in the last round that a new application of Mush's power could re-occupy it relatively quickly if it was close enough. That potentially freed up my ash clone from permanent knight duty and lets me use it as a more dynamic fighter capable of being gifted other powers, as well as abusing its low respawn time when it gets killed early - as opposed to getting punished for the long respawn time when it survives for longer.

It wasn't a pure upgrade. Without the tentacle rooting it in place, any attacks on the abandoned 'knight' would send material far and wide - it wouldn't be as effective of a shield as before. But I was fine with that. Defence was important, but offence was the only way to claim the final victory.

After a brief exchange of words, she's charging at me again. I've got my Parian-fuelled football lined up this time. I raise my ash clone again as she gets close, ordering it forward and letting my foot fly at the same time. Melee was her only real shot at victory, but without her most-threatening weapon in Brandish, the enhanced physical stats or one of the active or passive shields I needed to penetrate to hit the brains again, I'd swiftly be able to dismantle the threat in front of me.

"You fucking monster-" She howls at me, blade already thrusting towards me - only to be interrupted by the first movement of my knight.

"I'm not the one using my family as shields. I only want you, Panacea. Your family can go free." She looks stricken, but doesn't let up her attack. "But you don't want that, do you? "You killed them! Not me!" She's crying. I should probably feel bad... but this isn't real. When REAL and CONT is involved, words are a weapon. And weapons exist to hurt people. "If it wasn't for you, Crystal-"

"Laserdream?" I tut. "One of the useless ones. Shame. You were terrible at using her power anyway, so she really died for no reason at all. That's just a tragedy, isn't it? What a waste. You should have labelled them, I'd have let her live."

A half-choked sob and an attempt to decapitate me is the only response I get. Maybe I'm enjoying this too much.

My ash clone is cut down and my knight stops moving once more. Frustrating. I'd really lost out on the lottery this time. Glory Girl would have been the jackpot, allowing me to win just by sniping her with high-powered moves like Parian's footballs or even Skidmark's missiles. Manpower and Brandish would have been great. Shielder would just be 'okay'. But Laserdream and Lady Photon were largely just clones of each other. Missing one limited how much she could lean on the power, but it didn't really change much. At least it wasn't Flashbang. That was the only real dud, going purely off of the fact that she'd never used that one. I could only guess that it was a lack of ability to aim or project the power without higher brain functions and real senses.

Eight seconds to survive. I try and repeat the trick with my ash clone spawning at my feet as I retreat under her assault, but she's looking for it now. She floats directly over it as it forms, leaning on her flight for the first time this challenge. Another wide-angle blast can't be dodged so easily. My last shadow state is spent, the next charge just a moment too far away to recover - and her Mover rating is still higher than mine. I can't back away fast enough, and a glowing dagger soon carves out a section of my chest.

We stare at each other for a moment, as she jerks her blade to the side and reaches out to touch me. Pointlessly, because I have Panacea's power active. Laserdream on the back. Brandish front-left. Good information. Good information. I try a last minute taunt at Panacea as my ash clone respawns - if I can get her to try and torture me instead of killing me, I might live long enough to be rescued by my knight as my shadow state returns. But I can't get the taunt out. Words are hard when your lungs are practically bisected. Who knew?

Even as Panacea's Brute-enhanced strength pulls my head clear from my spine - I'm happy with this session. I got a bit unlucky, but I was making some great progress on a tough challenge. This is the kind of challenge I would have had to run from in the past, but I feel like I've crested that hill now. I've got enough tools that a mere tough Cape or an unfair scenario isn't impossible anymore - there's a way for me to win, I just have to find it. Or to be more accurate, I've found it already - I just have to keep walking on that path until the success screen.

FAILURE​

Artificial limits that were too clean to be anything but deliberately crafted. Challenges that responded to my thoughts. Rewards that aligned with my will. The interactions with Leet. The feeling I sometimes got when I got deeply involved in my challenges, that feeling of standing in the shadow of a mountain that I can never see. I blink. Wasn't expecting that response. Not without clearing her next challenge, at least. Where did that come from? Why?

I start the dance with Amy again. This was good practice for fighting a high-tier all-rounder Cape. A tutorial mode, almost. Those times I'd saved someone as Void Cowboy and let them thank me properly? When I'd 'improved' some of the criminals I'd come up across on a whim and let them demonstrate their new skillset?

"It's hard to put a precise number on it." I brush the question off. "In my defence, the ones I was serious about - they all know that there's someone else in the picture, whether they know who any of those people are or not."

"Definitely your father's son." Was that a pout? "But, I suppose there was never much chance of it being otherwise - living here didn't exactly prepare you for monogamy, though I'm certain he didn't intend for us to get along as well as we did when he left you with us."

"Probably not." I agree blandly. "Too charming for my own good."

"And too humble and modest as well." She adds, a small smile tugging at her lips. "Just make sure you have a way to let all those girls down gently when the time comes to move on. That's where things fell apart for your father."

I turn my face towards her. "And you?"

She purses her lips. "The history is a bit complicated, but sure - by the end, bitterness and petty revenge kept us closer than love ever did. It was always more about hurting the other person than trying to move on. Not something I'm proud of, and I'm sure he felt the same at the end, but it worked out for the best eventually. I wouldn't have had Clara, and he wouldn't have come back with you."

"And what a terrible thing for the world that would be." I grin. "Feel like the moral of the story disappeared somewhere in the middle of that."

She can't deny that. "Just... try not to get any of them pregnant. It only takes one of them telling a white lie in the moment, and suddenly you've got a lifetime responsibility on your hands, maybe even with someone you didn't really intend to have any serious involvement with."

Maybe. But I'd been moderately careful early on in my Cape career - and at this point... it didn't really matter anymore. In nine months, I would be the strongest Cape in America, in the Birdcage or dead. My concerns weren't really the same as a regular horny teenager, even if our interests might overlap.

Not that I could say that. Explaining that I was a Cape might change her opinion, but I still didn't know what to expect after that reveal. I shouldn't risk that until I was ready to align myself with the heroes officially, which genuinely was on my to-do list at some point, but not something that was likely to happen soon. I didn't hate authority, I didn't hate the idea of working within that system - even working with the PR machine. I liked being popular, and getting visibly on the side of the angels in the eyes of the public was another layer of protection from people looking to 'stop' me and my power.

But I needed security as well. Safety. Whether that came from the relevant parts of that system being under my influence, having agreements with the top brass about my cooperation and what it would cost, or just being so absolutely untouchable that any opposition didn't matter.

I'm letting my thoughts drift again. Maybe it's a sign of nerves, knowing that today could be such a massive turning point for me. "I'll keep it in mind." I make a gesture at the screen. "I'll be out again later today too. Going to go see the new Ward get announced, probably won't be back until late, so don't worry too much about me."

She rolls her eyes. "I see you haven't changed too much, at least. But really, missing eating with us again? I'm starting to think it might be personal."

"It's nothing like that. It would just be a waste not to enjoy the full event if I'm making the trip, I'll eat the refreshments while I'm there - get at least a bit of the cost of the ticket back." I stretch my arms into the air as she feigns a pout. "How about this, I'm already here for the day - I'll help you cook before I leave. It's been a while, hasn't it?"

"A while might be underselling it. I don't think I've seen you near anything that isn't the oven or the toaster since you got here." She looks amused. "Where's all this confidence coming from, the fact that you don't need to be the one eating it when it goes wrong?"

"It won't go wrong, I'm better than you think." Victor's power - even nerfed as it was - ensured that. I hadn't noticed any notable drain on my acquired skills, just a soft cap based on the expertise of the people I was leeching from - so simply having it active in the cafeteria, the range just barely including the cooks in the back? That was enough.

"We'll see about that. Might be a fun activity to do together either way." She allows, stepping back through the entryway to my room. "I'll see you downstairs then, and I guess I'll let you off for skipping school this time."

I follow her down a few minutes later. I hadn't really planned on this on my schedule for today, but I didn't mind. Emma had shown that I'd taken my power for granted in some ways. Putting a bit of effort in on my end wasn't exactly the most arduous of tasks - and actually, it was kind of nice doing things that didn't involve killing or being killed on repeat now and then. And if a mildly pleasant side-quest happened to make my pseudo-family a little closer to me in the process, a little more likely to take my side when the chips finally fall? So much the better.

And even if things never reached the point where I needed that, it wasn't exactly a bad thing to act as a normal family for once.

I pause as I enter the kitchen, noting the presence of the apron on the sole occupier of the room and the distinct lack of anything else besides.

I amend my inner monologue as I saunter forward with a hum. Maybe not quite normal.

But being a complete normie was overrated anyway.


Things fall into place quickly. Alice drives me to City Hall, my ash clone takes Velocity's powerset and retrieves my completed costume from Parian. I dismiss the ash clone when it arrives nearby, discreetly resummon it directly below the car as I'm dropped off and leave it Shadow Stalker's power to retrieve and store the package safely. Naturally, I couldn't just take the costume in with me into the venue, any baggage would obviously be checked - but progressing her challenges had shown me that Shadow Stalker's power had a lot of ways to quietly store items in hollow walls that would never be stumbled upon by chance. City Hall and the surrounding area would obviously be busy tonight, but no patrolling officer was going to be so dedicated as to start knocking down holes or peering in drainpipes to ensure that there are no packages inside them.

Nor did they have any reason to. This wasn't some convoluted attack plan by me. I wasn't storing a bomb somewhere. This was just insurance. Ensuring I had a quick response option. Having the key parts of my costume to hand in case something did happen that warranted it. The costume made things official. I was a professional now - I couldn't just flip an old hoodie over my head or wrap a scarf around my face in a pinch, I needed to have standards. And until I trusted the teleporter enough to literally place my costume over my skin, having it nearby was going to be the best I could do.

And I did want it nearby. Anything could happen today. Yes, I could get caught by the Protectorate somehow, and that would be bad - but that wasn't actually my top concern. My concern was the gangs. Skidmark, reeling and furious from his recent humiliation. The Empire, despite a few of their members getting caught in the recent gang violence - they were just one big play away from being unopposed in the city save for wherever the Protectorate decided to patrol that day. Lung, the rumours were saying that he's been spotted around town - uncharacteristically silent since Oni Lee's capture. The mysterious benefactor that Leet had mentioned as hiring them to make a scene at a certain time for unknown reasons was still out there too.

With the full attention of the heroes and the media concentrated into a single place, tonight was a natural flashpoint for someone to cause a scene or get away with something while the heroes were stretched thin at an event that couldn't be allowed to go wrong - and any movement from one gang might trigger a response from the others too. I was fine with that. I was hoping for it, actually. But 'Greg' would look strange running towards a scrap between Kaiser and Dauntless if one broke out, and truthfully - I wanted that costume for my next real fight anyway. My power gave me a pretty good grasp of my own mortality, and while I'd been rightly confident against Skidmark and Squealer - I didn't want a repeat of the Oni Lee fight where I had survived the opening move only out of prior experience with his throat-slitting ways.

Not that I needed to worry about him specifically. He was still cooling his heels in jail and as dim as my expectations were that he would stay there long-term - Lung was just one guy. He could fight everyone, but he couldn't do that and extract a valuable target at the same time. He'd get bogged down, the target would be moved - and the Protectorate would eventually drive him back while the Empire carves swathes out of his territory.

But there were plenty of other killers in the bay and armour was underrated in this industry. There were Capes likely to be present at this very event that had only 'lived' in their challenges thanks to the protective features of their costumes. Gallant. Armsmaster. Clockblocker. Taylor wouldn't be around, but her too. When punches stopped meaning as much, when limbs failed to bend to breaking point because the armour simply refuses to yield that far, when the helmet is impossible to remove to make way for an eye-gouge, when I can't get the right kind of grip to grapple someone or snap their neck - those moments were always a lesson in the value of a good costume.

Maybe I was being overly dramatic. Maybe tonight would be uneventful, but this was going to be my new 'normal'. I wasn't going anywhere in my civilian identity without my costume close to hand. I'd need to duplicate it eventually, either asking Parian for more or leaning on Leet's power to 'reinterpret it', adding enough Tinker-ness to make it something I could paste into existence - something that was harder to do than I'd initially expected, my hopes of making a generic 'Tinker axe' or some convenient equivalent for regular challenges had been dashed so far by the lack of suitable designs. A basic weapon wasn't enough. It had to be Tinker-y, which added material requirements that were hard to reliably find in a challenge.

Something that wouldn't be an issue in real life. Maybe I was scamming Parian a bit by plotting to copy-paste her work with only minor modifications, but I was going to commission her again just to have an excuse to keep seeing her - so did it really matter? Piracy wasn't even a real crime in the first place.

"Ticket please." I fall into the short queue leading into the venue. I assume most people were already inside, the event was split into several stages - but I knew from experience that no heroes would show themselves until the main event, so I had no particular need to arrive too early. I breeze past security, every bit as uneventful as could be expected. I was Greg Veder, after all. Regular teenager, come to gawk at the newest Cape in the Bay. One guy in a sea of hundreds. The presence of the stern-faced armed guards scattered around the building, the protective screens, the metal detectors and random patdowns - those were deterrents for other threats. Not for me.

A year ago, I would probably have found this alarming - that someone like me could even make it this far into the venue undetected. I'd probably have said something about lazy Thinkers and precogs not caring about villain attacks because it gave them job security and better wages, or made a post about the Illuminati and how they were propping up the villain industry by giving them softball prison sentences, easy breakouts and weak security measures to contend with. Admittedly, I'd still stand by some of those takes - but I've come to accept that I have to face reality at some point. The Thinkers that I'm nervous over, the precogs that would be capable of seeing me take over the Bay in a few months... they just weren't looking for me. Maybe there were too few of them, maybe hero work just didn't pay the bills. They were busy elsewhere. Perhaps they were fighting A-class and S-class threats and schemes.

But until I made it into the big leagues, until I became more than a footnote at the bottom of Brockton Bay... they weren't coming for me specifically. That was step one of learning to relax in this kind of environment.

Step two was realising that, not only were they not looking for me specifically - but they weren't even looking to protect the Protectorate at all at events like this. I'd always used to think that there was a reason why human Masters didn't just 'win or die'. What was stopping Heartbreaker from being in this crowd with me, incognito? What about Valefor? The answer was nothing. Nothing was stopping them, save for the fact that after one immense victory, one catastrophe that sent the nation reeling - there would be a kill order put out, and they would die. That left them to keep largely to themselves, to carve out their little kingdoms in an area the local hero teams would begrudgingly forsake as a controlled loss. Too weak to withstand the reprisal of using their abilities openly and proudly.

I was better than them on every front. The flexibility of my powers, the ability to come and go as I pleased in my civilian identity, the relative subtlety of my powers effects, the fact that eventually I wouldn't need to worry about a sniper bullet through the skull taking me out when the heroes were fed up with me, the fact that the PRT still didn't fully understand what they were up against - and of course, the fact that I was morally better as well. That was objectively true, I wasn't exactly pure good - but, if Heartbreaker took his harem and attended Endbringer fights regularly and worked with the Protectorate against major threats, that would quantitatively be better than the current one. That was simple, undisputable logic. A hero with an ego, a dubiously acquired harem and questionable methods was better for the world than a literal villain.

"Keep moving, Sir." The guard ushers me onward to make room for the next person to be scanned. "Enjoy the event."

Enjoy? Unlikely. These events were usually boring and dry, with the only redeeming features tending to be the meet and greet sessions with the heroes afterwards and perhaps getting a demonstration of the new Cape's powers - especially if they hadn't been leaked already. I mean, I showed up to all of these on general principle, so I couldn't really talk - but it wasn't exactly primetime television material, I could at least say that much, even as a fan. Especially as a fan, if I'm biased towards a thing and say that it's trash - that's how you know my opinion is trustworthy.

I shimmy through the crowd as a speaker drones on about the valuable work of heroes in the city and the steps that our glorious leadership intended to take to tackle crime, as if anyone was really here to listen to him. Not even the press section of the seating area had more than half-a-dozen people sitting in it, a sure sign that they were backstage somewhere - a more private press-conference, exclusive interviews to get their articles out during the main event, catching the heroes and the main guest as they make their dramatic arrivals? Who knows. In this, I was as blind to the goings-on as any other member of the public.

If it was a challenge, I'd be clambering around the walls of the building right now. Scouting was something I was good at. But consequences were real here. Ideally, the PRT never even registered the idea that I might be here - and if they did, they never got any proof about the matter. Someone getting a lucky shot with their camera or looking up at the wrong moment was bound to attract questions and attention - and all for, what, half an hour of extra time to challenge people in? The odds were good that it wouldn't make a difference for the majority of Capes, challenge cooldowns had a tendency to go up fast - eventually I'd run into a wall that I can't get through, that also has a lengthy timer on it. I can be patient. I don't want to be patient, but I can.

I'm just twitchy. Not nervous, as such. Just... tense. I feel different to the last time I was at an event like this. Maybe it was the overexposure to violence, maybe it was the fact that people were more aware of me now or maybe 'ready to fight' was just my natural state now - a coiled spring ready to lash out with muscle memory honed by a thousand deaths.

There were no Capes around, but walking around like this went against every instinct I'd learned to safely handle civilians. Leaving my back exposed. Walking between a crowd that I didn't know or trust. Any of them could have a hidden weapon. A single bullet would kill me, I knew - truly, truly knew - that I wouldn't be able to react to a shot to the head before I was unconscious or dead, even if my shadow state or forcefield might have saved me if I'd been aware.

A uniformed man makes an apologetic smile as he weaves past me, a heavy-looking cable held over his shoulder as lights are moved out. I stir restlessly at my exposed position. Danger. My escape angle momentarily blocked off by the flow of electrical power, I'd never tested the floor below me to see if I could phase through it safely - or if there was even anything there at all. No walls to retreat to behind cover. I was in the centre of the room, I probably wouldn't make it to the edge of the room in my three seconds of shadow state and Vista's power was worthless in the crowd. A gunman would just kill me here. No ifs, no buts. My best bet would be Clockblocker's power, but there was nothing great to target it on - clothing would work, but there was no time. Idly, I wonder if dead people counted for that restriction - if a gunman killed someone, could I clockblock their shirt immediately and hide behind it? That would give me a way to survive from one angle, but I'd have to assume that any attacker would have friends mirroring their attack from the other side too-

-And then the danger passes. Because there was never anything to worry about. He's just a regular guy setting up the stage lights. Nobody here is trying to kill me. This is the real world, and as much as my challenges love to stack the deck against me - things don't really work like that in real life.

I knew that. The entire mental exercise was always a hypothetical. I wasn't literally a hair's breadth away from killing everyone around me or using them as a meatshield, waiting for the first excuse to do something psychotic. I was just... aware. An overly-violent evolution of a civilian imagining how they would save the day if a terrorist hijacked the plane right next to them - and just happened to have their backs turned in the right way. An evolution of watching a jacked guy come in and mentally categorising him, weight class, fighting style, concealed weapons, how easy would it be to beat him - that was probably natural for fighters. Soldiers. I was the same, just... more used to the absurd scenarios. The unfair surprises. The ones that overwhelmed my safety nets and ended in my usually painful death that felt all-too-real.

Which was a long-winded way of saying that my way of thinking was pretty normal, when you think about it. Thought crimes aren't real - I told Amy that, and it's true for me too.

I sidle over to the edge of the room, helping myself to the refreshments as I wait for the arrival of the heroes. Being away from the centre of the room didn't actually improve my mood, the multitude of switches, wires and wall sockets visible on the wall closest to me highlighted that phasing through it would be a risky, risky proposition indeed. I suppress the thought. These instincts were valuable, hard-learned lessons - but there was a time and a place for them.

Relax. I'm not being hunted here. I'm doing the hunting. The only one aware that there's even a hunt going on today.

Somehow, this was easier when I wasn't quite as aware of how easy it is to be killed. Ignorance is bliss. Nothing has truly changed, but the feeling of walking into a dangerous area or a PVP zone in a hardcore ironman run - that's what this felt like. Irrational, but my brain didn't care about rational or not. I don't even think it's an issue with my mindset, just an awareness of my own weakness. That my current defensive tools were insufficient to save me from the worst case scenario, especially now that I was unable to simply hold up Glory Girl's forcefield like I often do when walking the street - that kind of discrepancy when someone bumps into me might be noticed.

All it means is that I need more power. More powers, specifically. Something to give me my surety back, a Thinker power would do. A passive Brute effect. An extension to the shadow state long enough to just use it to sprint to safety. The speed state losing its wind-up time. There were so many minor tweaks to my current powerset that would put me at ease here, I just needed to keep pushing forward, keep winning, keep getting stronger.

And as discomforting as it felt right now, I was in exactly the right place to do that.

Up on the stage, a rat-faced bureaucrat backs away from the microphone - replaced by the more dynamic, exuberant-looking host. "And now, ladies and gentlemen - please put your hands together as we welcome Armsmaster to the stage, to introduce us all to the newest Ward gracing our fair city!"

I obediently join in the clapping, tension fading as Armsmaster's figure arrives on stage. A few minor changes to his suit since his last public outing, some winking lights on his shoulder that indicated some new feature or function that would probably only be revealed as a surprise trump-card three months down the line. His weapon remains holstered, folded down to something that casually rests on the waist of his power armour like a tradesman tucking a hammer into his belt.

If I could shrink the Mechablade down to a portable thing like that... well. I'm sure the weight is largely the same, I'd still need power-armour to manage it without the exoframe that came with it. There's more important things to focus on. Like the fact that Armsmaster is right in front of me.

"Challenge."

I'd avoided some opportunities to take this fight before. The modifiers were just too brutal, a Tinker getting PREP and CONT? Being almost immediately thrown into a fight against them? This being Armsmaster specifically? It was brutal. Too brutal for a first-tier challenge.

At least, at first glance. But I know more about my power now than I did then. Seen more examples of it in action, I understand how the cheat modifiers work better - and how the lack of them works too.

Advantage one: The order of operations mattered. PREP CONT was different to CONT PREP. For most? That didn't matter. Here? It was everything. PREP gives him a list of my powers and time to devise countermeasures, and then - only after that is done - does he load into the challenge with his previous memories of our fights.

Which meant, if he initially miscalculated a countermeasure or overlooked a power as harmless - he wouldn't have a dedicated counter ready, no matter how many repeats he went through. He'd just have to make do with what his original self had developed, unless I gained more powers that changed what he made with the PREP modifier. His combat loadout was always going to be identical unless I scared him so badly that he saw no option but to run away in the next repetition.

And that didn't sound like Armsmaster at all.

Advantage two: This was Armsmaster. And as much as the guy was cool, that didn't mean that he'd never lost a fight or that I was blind to his weaknesses. He was the swiss-army knife of Tinkers. The right tool for the occasion, every time. A scalpel of every size.

But when he's lost before, it's been to the hammer. When the one scalpel doesn't quite finish the job, and the rest of his suite isn't suited to the fight. When the miniaturisation specialty works against him, with all of those valuable, delicate components compressed so tightly together that one heavy hit takes out a half-dozen systems at once. When his regular power armour clashes directly with a strong Brute, the armour would usually break before the Brute did. Any damage to power systems, servos, hydraulics, batteries or sensors taking him from peak form to crippled with the wrong hit to the wrong place.

Oh, he was skilled. It's not that it was easy to make that kind of hit happen. PHO was almost completely sure that he had some kind of combat-Thinker emulator somewhere in his kit - but still, he had losses on his record. Fair, undisputed 1v1 defeats. Usually, they came from one powerful hit - something that dents the armour and hits something important underneath it, or simply overpowers the durability of the armour. Armsmaster's armour was a toolkit as much as it was real armour, other Tinkers tended to make themselves as Brute-like as possible with thick armour, overpowered strength and a few cool weapons attached - Armsmaster wanted to use that space to store his gadgets. It was a winning formula, but it wasn't all upsides. If I could get a clean hit with one of my anti-Brute tools - I'd probably just cleave right through him, armour and all.

Advantage three: He was expecting me to beat him by getting stronger than him. He was expecting me to grow in strength and overpower him as soon as I'd worked out every one of his counters. He was expecting me to continue facing him in a direct fight as I already had been for the last few attempts, scouting him out as much as he was scouting me. In turn, his path to maximising his long-term odds through the CONT modifier lay in not using every trick he had right out of the gate. He wouldn't be hitting me with unnecessary countermeasures until it was needed, not out of mercy - but so that I couldn't counter him in turn. He would expect me to only be able to win once I had so many powers that I just ran him over in a fair fight despite whatever he could build in his prep-time.

I would not be waiting for that time to come. Call it a mark of respect for his skills, but I intend to win with cunning, treachery and trickery.

Fourth and final advantage: He was overreliant on his halberd. It wasn't that he didn't have some tricks with his armour or the ArmsCycle - but it was a safe bet that the majority of his tricks were stored in his weapon, that was just how he worked.

In summary: His loadout would not notably change between attempts. A powerful anti-Brute attack could overcome his defences. He was expecting a straight fight, thinking my route-to-victory lay in either acquiring enough other powers that he couldn't counter them or successfully mapping out his entire loadout and every one of his tricks. And his best tricks were likely all stored in his weapon, and without it he'd be far, far weaker.

Which gave me a plan. A plan that would need a second attempt, and one where I probably wouldn't get a third thanks to the CONT modifier. He'd keep his distance if he knew, or even back off entirely and start re-tinkering with his loadout.

The ArmsCycle screams around the corner and bears down on me. I flee down a nearby alleyway. Not to get truly get away, I just wanted distance from the ArmsCycle. Armsmaster effortlessly dismounts and transitions into a pursuit immediately. A dart of some kind phases through my chest harmlessly with a wisp of smoke, and then his enhanced speed has him right on top of me. My knight, only half-formed, lunges at him to stall - but the man casually throws something towards the shadows where my ash clone was hiding. The knight collapses a moment later.

He turns back to me, accelerates again - and swings his halberd in a swift, deadly motion.

A clean, perfect execution. I'd tried something, and it hadn't worked - he'd overcome it effortlessly and I'd be back with a slightly different approach next time.

That's what it should look like to him. If I'd been too blatant about my real aims, he might have been suspicious, changed things up for next time.

I don't have eyes for Armsmaster as my torso parts ways with my legs - I just burn the sight in front of me into my mind. A failure screen, not yet the one for the challenge itself - but for a different power. A failed Paste, centred around his weapon. The schematic I'd tried to make? Unimportant, the biggest, most expensive box-like design that needed more of every resource than I could possibly find, could still make with Leet's speciality and have my power still consider it as Tinkertech. The design didn't even really do anything, it was just for this moment. Because if my design specified 3kg of carbon fibre, and I was looking at a screen saying I was missing 2.1kg? That my 1kg of graphene was 0.7kg short? That I had insufficient amounts of silicon, lithium, copper, gold - inverting those numbers gave me valuable information. Suddenly, I had a list of resources to work with - the elements and materials that made up the weapon in front of me.

And therefore, if I had a design that used those elements and had no shortages? Well. I wonder. How well would Armsmaster's halberd work if a few elements in their entirety were abruptly removed between one moment and the next? Naturally, it would stop working. Probably fall apart, if there was even anything of note left. My paste-box wasn't Manton limited, it didn't care if he was holding the weapon, only that he wasn't blocking the final product. I wouldn't be just stealing the screws, I could steal the entire thing into a weapon of my own - leave him with a handful of wires and confused sludge between one blink and the next.

And the only requirement was that I stayed within the pseudo-recipe that my 'error' had gifted to me.

There was one downside. my paste-box was too small for the entire halberd - especially with the requirement to keep the rest of Armsmaster from physically blocking the space my new creation would spawn in. I'd need to content myself with just the top half that I'd initially attempted to replace - but I'd wager that with a Tinker as good as Armsmaster, having half of his weapon literally disappear and be instantly repurposed would shut down a great deal of his attack plans even if he still had a few tricks left.

But that... was hardly a downside at all. It was a technical specification, nothing more.

FAILURE​

But it didn't feel like a failure at all.

I turn to the closest stranger. An ALRT based challenge. "Challenge."

An office building? Perfect. All I needed was a chair, some paper and something to write with.

The sound of snapping plastic and shattered wood fills the room for a short time. The target arrives, pauses at the sight of me, my ash clone and a solid mass of splinters, plastic and stray desk decorations - then runs back the way he came.

I wave a hand. "Don't kill them." My knight shambles after him, my ash clone racing behind.

All the time in the world to Tinker up the right design. And... for once, I didn't have to worry about the exotic, hard-to-find materials that Leet's tech often wanted. Armsmaster's halberd was a buffet of expensive materials waiting to be utilised, it had everything, albeit often in smaller quantities than I would like.

First, write down everything I could remember from the resource list and the quantities. Then... see what I could do. Not the Mechablade. Not this time. Something that, in my hands, would instantly be able to hit Armsmaster before he could react with enough force and penetration to get through his armour. From something I could just grasp in my hand, to an immediate, lethal attack. Not an actual explosion, Armsmaster was great at tanking those. Not a gun, my power would never let me have it. Leet's power makes a proposal with the parameters I give it. A spear, or something like it. Extendible, to ensure it worked within the paste box - then all I had to do was point and extend it with explosive force directly into the centre of his chest. Dead.

Nice idea.

Some problems with the initial design. It's aimed at cleaving through people, not metal plates, the design was focused on repeated puncturing attacks, not a single lethal blow - I didn't need to retrieve the weapon, I just needed it to work once. Durability, cost and practicality meant nothing compared to speed, precision and power for that initial surprise hit. Leet's power proposes a design. I veto it, the quirk is too problematic - my single shot needs to work without the slightest chance of luck ruining it. If it doesn't, the CONT modifier will ensure I never get a second try.

Another design. Unsuitable. Some materials that weren't on my list, the halberd might still have them - I could only confirm the presence of materials that my junk-cube design had contained, but I couldn't take the risk. I refine some more, discarding variant after variant, tweaking some around, swapping to Squealer's power for a bit to see if simple, solid engineering could bridge the gap to a usable weapon that I needed.

No. But it was fine. I had time. I had all the time. Resources and complexity were the real bottlenecks for my tinkering, the former a simple issue of my power requiring complex materials that usually had a complicated creation method or were difficult to extract from everyday items - and the latter simply a restriction of working with multiple low-level tinker powers rather than a single, maxed-out one.

But this relatively simple thing wasn't any of those things. An hour later, I have it - the design burns to cinders around my palm as it occupies my paste-slot. Then the challenge ends, to the distant sound of a person screaming as he's hurled from the roof to the ground below.

SUCCESS​

I brush away the notification. Irrelevant.
