I click my tongue against my teeth in annoyance as I extend that train of thought to the logical conclusion. Correction. He wouldn't get any new full info on my powers. With the previous challenge having the PREP modifier, he'd carry all of his memories of the powers I had then into this one. Anything I acquired from this point on, would be a surprise to him. Initially, at least.

Which meant that, once again, I was in the unenviable position of not wanting to fight him at all until victory was assured. And this time, he'd be respecting my paste-box a lot more than before - and I couldn't rely on the environment to limit his movements, form my knight or provide material for Tinkertech.

This has to be favouritism by my power, but I'll just deal with it. It's not like he's my only viable target. As soon as the other heroes show up, I'm hoping to get enough challenges in to have my power hitting the brakes on me - just like it did at Canberra. In that context, excluding Armsmaster from the rotation wasn't even a bad thing.

And, more importantly, the reason I had for waiting on defeating Browbeat was no longer valid. "Challenge."

I immediately erupt into a sprint away from my opponent once more. I'd have to be trickier with the string this time. Landing a precise hit, hoping that he tore open a wound in his heart was a bit of a longshot with how much he was moving and growing from one step to the next - but I wasn't really aiming to win like that. I just needed to lance him through, get enough curvature into the line that once he'd impaled himself on a solid metre or two of thread, he could barely find a way to back out before he was dead.

An idea occurs. Curves, or a slope? There was no way around the fact that the string had to be level with him at the point he was struck - but it didn't have to stay there. If I pinched the thin air below the string with Vista's power, as the power unwound - I'd introduce a near-vertical spike for him to navigate.

I think. Was that how it worked with Clockblocked objects and Vista's powerset? It made sense at a glance, but the physics always looked a little strange when edge-cases got involved. I think I was safe here though, I wasn't elongating the string itself, just bringing him slightly closer to the 'real' height of the string.

I was confusing myself now. Caveman Greg understands it. String starts high. Vista brings the string low. Browbeat go splat. Vista's power expires. Browbeat can't reverse through the 'high' string because he can't fly. Simple, as long as you don't think about how Vista's power works. I pu theory into practice. Shape the string with Parian, make an absurd knot at my end so he can't escape by continuing forward. Vista's power on the air in front of me, then back to Parian to re-establish the shape of my weapon before freezing it.

A messy plan, an awkward execution.

But functional. That's the important part. Browbeat lets out a roar of agonised pain as his own momentum impales him on the 'tracks' that I'd prepared for him - his body tumbling into the obstacle and opening his wound wider before he comes to a halt. If he didn't have regeneration, I could probably just have slipped into my speed-state and waited for him to bleed out from that. As it was, I didn't trust that it would be impossible for him to ease himself out over time - to say nothing of the fact that Clockblocker's power would eventually expire, and I couldn't reapply it because the Manton Limit would stop me now that he was touching it.

Just have to kill him before then, or I'll lose.

Suits me fine. I strip off, lining up my first Parian missile on the hulking target. Before I can kick the ball, I pause - noting that he's already brought his arms up into a defensive posture - not fully understanding the nature of the power, but clearly understanding that it was an attack. Sure, I could probably batter through the limbs - but that was probably the easiest thing for his power to repair. Plus, I'd need to break through the forcefield twice - once going through his arms, and again going through his face.

So I circle around first. As fast as I can, ignoring the agonised sounds he makes as he tries to keep me in sight. Shooting at his comparatively defenceless back, knowing I only need a good, clean hit on his head - or perhaps just his spine depending on how his power really worked - even I couldn't fuck it up from here.

That isn't to say I nail it the first time. The first missile is too slow, my aim is a little off and I need to correct the angle with Parian's power rather than driving it directly forward. The second, a slightly lopsided 'doll' constructed from my jeans, bounces off of the timelocked thread. I send my ash clone scurrying after them even as I continue to strip. No time to be self-conscious in the heat of combat, Clockblocker's power would expire at random. In three seconds or three minutes - couldn't afford to wait on the ideal missiles or my own sense of dignity.

My sock missile is the first to get a good hit in. Too small to obliterate his head, but his half-turned jaw is blasted clean off by the shot. My ash clone hurls my shirt back to me as it races to retrieve the next fallen item of clothing. Meanwhile Browbeat seems intent on redirecting the full force of his power into his shoulder muscles, bulking them up to such an extent that they might be able to shield his head as he continues to try - and fail - to free himself. My next shot hits his body, not piercing straight through - but the kinetic force it imparts does have the benefit of pressing his insides against the Clockblocked thread. A fresh cry of agony.

Not quite what I'm looking for. I don't think I have the firepower to completely blast through an area of his body where he's built up his muscles - especially if the words about the telekinetic field benefitting from his increased muscle mass is true. It only highlights the importance of hitting areas where he can't buff himself up - namely, his skull.

And even with my accuracy, his desperate attempts to blindly dodge and the obstacles in my way - I only have to get a clean hit once. The seventh kick yields the result I need. A hit bouncing off the top of his head, not quite resulting in the shower of gore I was hoping for - but the immediate slump of his body despite the agony it should have caused him tells the story. One head impact too far, completely unconscious. His muscles start to shrink as I line up my next shot. Presumably the telekinetic field is gone too now that his power was inactive - which means this shot should be the last.

One kick. One hit. His head fully detaches from his spine upon impact.

SUCCESS

Reward: Physical Amplification (1)​

That sounded like a Brute power if I've ever seen one. I don't want to expect too much from just the first level, but... finally. I've been waiting a long time for this.

I pick a random face out of the crowd to test. "Challenge."

I activate the power. A slight tingling sensation races across my body, not causing my muscles to warp or bulge like Browbeat - but the sensation of light pressure couldn't be denied. I summon my ash clone and have it hit me. The ashy fist slows as it reaches me, the impact distributed harmlessly across my upper body. There's the forcefield. Maybe just the forcefield? I certainly wasn't feeling capable of regenerating or expanding my muscles. I consider the power closer. Was it getting stronger? Not anymore, but it was certainly stronger now compared to when I had initially applied it. A few seconds to scale up to full power? I could work with that, I suppose. I drop the power to test the theory.

I blink at the sensation I'm still feeling. "Oho." I backhand my ash clone. My hand just barely not touching it, but my ash clone crumples to dust anyway.

The power was still active. Weakening, but active. A few seconds to charge up to 100%, but it was the same when I dropped it as an active power - a few seconds to fully lose the effect, slowly winding down. Which means I could still have the partial effect if I had to drop into my shadow state defensively. Or offensively, coming out of that state with a cheap shot backed by half of a Brute power would be devastating. And that said nothing about the defensive benefits. I might not have both sides of the Brute effect that Browbeat had, but the forcefield alone had been a powerful effect that had neutered all but the strongest variants of my most powerful non-Tinkertech attack even at it's weakest point.

I refill the amplification field back up to 100%. Quickfire test time. Echo? I head to a nearby door, line up an attack - then close the door, letting the field fade completely before releasing the echo. The door rocks, but remains fixed in place. No real change from my baseline hits there. I repeat the process again, this time releasing the echo when the field was halfway to being depleted.

My ash clone and I peer through the new hole in the doorway. "Nice." So the Echo wasn't copying any effects on my limbs at the time of the attack, but when it did unleash the attack - it was copying my limbs as they were right now, whether they had a forcefield on them or not. That was powerful, dampened only by the issue that timing would be difficult thanks to the requirement of holding the Echo as my active power to stop it from firing early.

I pass the power to my ash clone. It attempts to break a few objects largely ineffectually. I throw a stapler at it and it vanishes.

Interesting. I could probably take that to mean that the 'synergy' between body strength and forcefield power is still there. It's strong on me, but it does nothing to a frail body like my ash clone or a bug. Presumably, if I gained a further power that bolstered my physical stats - I might gain myself a stronger forcefield even without needing a direct upgrade. The lack of synergy with my ash clone wasn't a major loss, it could only hold one power at a time and Mush's power under its control was such an integral part of my kit now that I wouldn't want to swap it out anyway.

What I really wanted to know was how far I could take this power. I'd seen from Browbeat how well the forcefield scaled when it could distribute damage, the already-thin horizontal thread had been greatly weakened and only the single-point impaling trick had been able to fully power through it. I'd felt my ash clone's punch hit the forcefield and distribute it across my torso, not even feeling like much more than a half-hearted shove from a child. A bigger hit, one that hit me over a wider surface area, would naturally let my forcefield distribute the force across more and more of my body before yielding - that kind of distribution of force would make me invincible in a fist fight. I could stand in front of a car going at the speed limit and end up with a mild bruise after getting knocked aside.

But the kind of force was important. Just like Browbeat, concentrated force, piercing and less physical effects would still be a threat - but it was nice to know that in a situation of raw kinetic impacts, I had a trump card to meet them with. And hit back with - all with a power that didn't go on cooldown or deplete when used. Bullets? I wasn't too keen to try it, the more concentrated force would minimise how much of the forcefield would take the hit - but I should experiment, if I had a power that could convert a bullet hit to a level that would merely bruise then I'd hit the jackpot. I wouldn't have to waste the shadow state or Glory Girl's forcefield on the lesser threats unless I was truly caught off guard.

I glance around for my target, but I don't see him. Not going to bother to find him and win the challenge - just a civilian. I hurl myself out of the window.

FAILURE​

Good tests. A nice upgrade for me. And hopefully not the last one of the night. I had no intention of battling Armsmaster again today, but I could keep attempting Browbeat - and surely the other heroes would be appearing any second now to show their support in front of the cameras?

Browbeat
Brockton Bay Ward (2/4)
(ALRT) (HUNT) (TIME)​

Didn't really think much of it before, but the number of challenges is oddly low here. Was it simply that the power wasn't very interesting, or was it some other factor that decided it? Maybe it was just that it couldn't think of many ways to make the challenges different, it was already throwing three modifiers at me and I already knew that I would be one-shotting this one. It had only been difficult before because I didn't have my knight - unless he runs away, he's going to get squished after I stall for a minute or two. How could the challenge really escalate from there? The power just wasn't really suited to things that weren't a direct fight, and if it lost there... what else was there to cover that wouldn't end in the same way?

Not that it bothered me. The possibility of getting to the third challenge today and upgrading my Brute power again was all too real. "Challenge."

Office- no, this was the Wards HQ. The admin area on the third floor. Familiar territory. I didn't see Browbeat, but I could probably assume he had spawned in the living room. He'd take some time dropping down the flights of stairs to reach me, which made this a foregone conclusion. My ash clone walks around methodically shattering screens, tearing up plastic and emptying out drawers as my knight draws loose materials into its body. The heavy thuds in the distance indicate how fast Browbeat is crossing the three floors between our spawning locations - but this time, the terrain favours me. It might have been more troublesome in an open field, especially with the time modifier putting limits on how long I could take to defeat this presumably more-skilled version of Browbeat - but that hadn't happened.

When Browbeat finally emerges from the stairwell, he's met with an equal. My knight clashes with him directly, pinning him in place in a direct contest of strength and durability. To Browbeat's credit, he's putting his skills to work. My knight isn't a martial arts expert, it takes heavy, brute-enhanced hits to the body - trash and debris crumples and splits under the attacks, but the damage isn't real. In fact, it only refines the material to a smaller, looser form for the power to work with.

He doesn't realise that the power underneath it is invincible, guided by my hidden ash clone. He doesn't realise that the only way to weaken the knight is to tear the material clear from its body. And, most critically, he doesn't realise that the form of the 'knight' is merely an affectation. A suggestion to make mobility and movement easier. The true form of the power is flexible mass of tentacles, the original owner of the power had effortlessly made a spider to navigate a doorway on a whim - and while my version wasn't as flexible as that, it was fully capable of sacrificing it's appearance as a 'man' when needed.

Browbeat doesn't notice the creeping tendril of trash at his feet, he only notes that the knight is smaller and more sluggish than before. He doesn't glance behind him as a tendril emerges from the ground, the sharpest and sturdiest of materials pulled with it - the tendril surging in strength as the knight pumps more and more of its true form into it. The blade plunges into Browbeat's back just as the knight's body is torn in half, a roar of triumph cut short before he can turn his gaze onto me.

My ash clone is practical. The blade is withdrawn, and impales him again. Again. Again. If he's learned a good way to regenerate, it won't help him here. Again. Again. Ag-

SUCCESS

Reward: Browbeat+​

I'm on a roll. Can I make it four in a row? I eye the stage, momentarily stopping to appreciate that the heavily-built figure in the concealing, full-body costume that only served to outline muscles was gone - replaced by a grinning, amazon-like figure proudly displaying her muscled midriff for the world to see. She flexes and poses some more for the crowd, highlighting to me the vast differences between the two costumes. Far closer to the kind of shorts and sports-bra combination you might see at the gym than the skinsuit of before, proudly showing off well-defined thighs and biceps to the cheers and whoops from the crowd.

At that thought, I give a flat look to the suddenly very supportive crowd around me. The crowd that had been ready to leave just a few seconds ago, now cheering on her every move and pose. I hear someone distantly call out a confession, drawing the attention of a frowning security guard nearby.

As a guy, I'm offended. This says something about our society.

Also as a guy, I get it. Would.

No. That's not right. Will. I might have to keep my distance for now, but this girl would be mine for the taking before too long.

Browbeat
Hero (3/4)
(PREP) (CAGE) (ALRT)​

The challenge descriptors are changing fast on this one. It's almost weirding me out, I'm used to them staying roughly the same - but maybe it's more normal than I think, and I just haven't pushed most Capes far enough for it to be relevant. It shouldn't mean much in this case, just an approximation of the skill and experience of my opponent. The return of the CAGE modifier was painful, but I could try and repeat my previous trick - they might know about Parian and Clockblocker's power, but that didn't guarantee they would think about the threat of that particular combination. "Challenge."

I'd just have to tr- Close! I shift into my shadow state immediately, surging backwards and activating Vista's power to gain more space from the mountain of muscle that claps down on the space where my head just was. It surges forward, the distance seeming manageable for a moment, if not for the fact that Vista's power works the same for everyone. They cross the shrunken space in an instant, and I faintly realise that I genuinely don't have an escape tool that can help here. He- no, it's she now - is just faster than me by default. And she spawned way, way too close for me to make use of my previous strategies.

My third shadow state is depleted, my ash clone takes Parian's power and desperately starts to tug a thread free from my shirt to start working with as I try and use Browbeat's own power in defence. I'm fully grasped in a bear hug, my torso cracks as blood fills my mouth. I need-

FAILURE​

I take a moment to gather my breath.

Fuck that. That was bullshit. That was cheap. If they'd started out at a normal distance it would still have been fair. Or, as fair as it could be with the CAGE modifier denying my knight.

I let the bitterness fester for a moment before dismissing it. Fine. Whatever. It exposed a weakness, I suppose. There's still not much I can do about a Brute that's directly on top of me without warning. And there's a lesson to learn there about my version of Browbeat's power, immunity to brief hits is fine - but continuous pressure will get through the forcefield anyway, especially if the forcefield runs out of 'field' to distribute it to that isn't already under attack.

...I'm still a little bitter. That was a sneak attack. I don't think I have a good way to handle it anyway, but that's besides the point. My power is usually pretty fair with me about distances where enemies spawn in. What, should I expect to start the next fight with Hookwolf with me spooning the guy naked?

Bad image. Bad thought. Why did you even think that, Greg? At least wait until Hookwolf is a cute girl before having thoughts like that.

Ew. I shudder mentally, turning my gaze back onto the beaming girl on stage to cleanse the mental sin I just committed. She was finishing up her speech, should I be listening? I'm pretty sure the rest of the crowd isn't. I'd imagine it's something to do with the fact that, as part of the current power demonstration, her bulging muscles almost make it look like half her costume is ready to snap off and give everyone a show. I'm sure that's not the reality, it's probably some absurdly stretchy material that would survive Fenja wearing it to war - but that doesn't change the fact that the showcase has ended up being a little more engaging than she might initially have realised.

I make sure to shake my head at the crowd around me. Perverts, honestly. What is the world coming to? Unfortunately for them, the demonstration was coming to an end - her muscles shrinking back to their usual, still impressive, size.

Armsmaster returns to the front of the stage, signalling an end to the power showcase. "That is the end of this presentation. Thank you for your attention. The current team leader of the Brockton Bay Wards, Aegis, would like to say a few words now."

The Ward steps forward from behind the curtain.

Aegis
Brockton Bay Ward (1/6)
(TIME)​

I don't even bother to wait for the speech to start. "Challenge."

I spawn on the street. Relatively clean streets. Solid concrete all around. I'd have to destroy a few things to get my knight up to scratch. The TIME modifier is... three minutes? I softly swear at that. Five minutes is the most common one I see, but my power seems intent on not making things easy for me today - especially given that he hasn't even spawned in front of me or aggroed on me from the start.

But simply making enough noise should attract his attention. My knight, ash clone and myself set about breaking up the environment around us. Upturning soil, breaking up the pavement and hammering on walls, doors and windows to get my knight the material it needs. It's slow going, not a great area - but as my knight grows in strength, and I lean on Browbeat's power, we start to make faster work of it.

And then, naturally, we attract the attention of our foe. He drops on me from above, completely blindsiding me with a move that probably would have been lethal if Browbeat's power hadn't been in the active slot. Instead, it felt more like someone had used my head as a stepping stool out of nowhere.

God I loved having Brute powers.

Especially now that I knew that Aegis literally couldn't hurt me. He was a cockroach, but not really a very offensive one. Enhanced strength, but if that kind of kick from above couldn't help him - then nothing he could do would. I'd phase out of any grapples or containment foam, so this would be a one-sided affair.

If not for the timer. But I'd just have to make quick work of him. Which should be easy. He's fast in the air, but what can he really do? He comes at me directly again, and I simply take the hit directly - grab onto him and-

-and get carried directly upwards, away from the 3v1 I'd been hoping for.

Fair. I hadn't considered that as an option. I guess he could just fly away if he wanted, with me as a passenger or not. A one-on-one it is then. We grapple each other, and I swiftly realise that this is a doomed endeavour. I need to inflict a massive amount of damage to him in a short timeframe, Browbeat's power just wasn't enough - especially outside of the single-hits that it was so good at inflicting and mitigating. I'd seen Aegis shrug off a close-quarters struggle with Hookwolf just after his debut, he hadn't done much more than get to torn to shreds but at the end of the day - he just walked away from it. I couldn't exceed that with any single power unless he stood still for me. The only thing I can think of is trying to use Panacea's power destructively, but it's too slow - and I can see how effortlessly his own power is outpacing mine at adapting to the worst I can do.

Before long, the timer ticks over - and the rush of air in my ears changes course. A new timer begins, but I suspect that it won't be needed. Aegis slams me directly into the ground - the shadow state making his efforts useless, but it didn't matter. His reinforcements were here. A small stream of PRT troopers emerging from a line of trucks that appeared out of nowhere in the middle of the street. Everyone one of them armed, everyone of them aiming at the both of us.

And every one of them fires, seemingly uncaring of whether or not they hit Aegis too.

Which sucks, because he can take it. And I really can't. I get my answer on how Browbeat's power holds up to bullets. Acceptably for the first few bullets, incredibly poorly under a concentrated barrage.

FAILURE​

Well. That was decisive. I don't think I even have a solution there. Rooting myself to the ground somehow, perhaps Clockblocking some handles for myself - hiding indoors? But then, all he had to do was nothing - the pressure was on me to engage. If I took away his preferred strategy, he could just wait around for reinforcements. It wasn't even a matter of catching him and dragging him out of the air, he could pull upwards more than I could pull down - I didn't have a way to fix that.

All of this progress today, but Brutes are still my weakness. That's a bit frustrating.

"-to serve in the Wards program is one the highest callings-" Aegis drones on as I return to real life. I'm pretty sure I remember that line from Triumph's old speeches. Copying? Or, maybe I should give him the benefit of the doubt and call it a tribute.

No, fuck that. If he has an annoying challenge, he doesn't get the benefit of the doubt. Fuck him, speech-stealing bastard. I don't make the rules, just enforce them. Go easier on me next time if you want me be nicer with my mental accusations.

Boring. Three Capes on stage, three walls. I feel like I'm being taunted. Armsmaster seems as bored as me, because he steps up and interrupts Aegis's speech mid-sentence. "Due to suspected villainous activity in the nearby area, this event is cancelled. Please evacuate immediately in an orderly fashion through the exits at the rear and sides of the room." A momentary pause as the room stares at him. "This is not a drill. I repeat-"

Nobody moves, the hall falling into a momentary hubbub of confusion.

Then the front door implodes. I whirl around, catching the barest glimpse of a red-and-green painted truck with a rider hanging on top - throwing something into the air above the crowd-

Bomb? I activate Glory Girl's forcefield, but the package pauses in the air and hangs there. I scramble backwards anyway, as the crowd mostly stands transfixed - only a few people actually attempting to make an escape - only to be warded off by . "Good evening Brockton Bay." A crackly voice emanates from the floating device. "My name is Bakuda. The greatest and most intelligent Tinker that has ever graced this city. You are now all my hostages. This building is under my complete control and I could blow you all to smithereens on a whim. As proof of this, please direct your attention to the second-best Tinker on the stage."

The crowd shifts. Armsmaster doesn't move or react.

He continues to not move or react. Same with Aegis. Same with Browbeat. I dimly realise that he hadn't finished his speech, not because he'd been interrupted - but because he'd been stopped. Suspended in time.

Clockblocked? I surreptitiously pull my phone out as the closest members of the audience prod an invisible on the stage.

"I've taken the liberty of putting these so-called heroes in a timeout as proof of my capabilities. If you attempt to escape out of any of the doors or windows, I will simply blow you up-" A burst of flame erupts out of the front door, swiftly matched by a burst of icy wind that leaves icicles hanging off the walls nearby. "-so do be so kind as to stay well away so you aren't harmed by the fruits of my genius. However, please feel free to call the PRT and beg for them to save your miserable lives. I have no intention of stopping you as they are utterly incapable of matching me anyway."

I relax minutely. This lady had an ego on her, but a hostage situation was understandable territory. I think I was getting the gist of things now. This chick was a new trigger for the ABB, and she was making a scene that the heroes couldn't afford to ignore - and Lung was probably trying to break out Oni Lee right now. That was all understandable. Probably doomed, the heroes could split their focus two ways pretty comfortably unless this was coordinated with the other gangs - and the other gangs would be more than happy to watch the ABB lose here. Lung would be driven back, this chick would get tracked down pretty quickly and get captured - and everyone here would probably be safe.

Probably. I wouldn't be sticking around to find out. Not least because of the implication that she could blow everyone here up when she started losing. The hostage process would be long and arduous. And, quite frankly, I wanted to be out and about right now - Cape fights! Heroes! Villains! Plus, if I could find this Bakuda chick, a few challenges and I could probably sweet talk her down from this ill-conceived plan - and then move on to find Lung afterwards. All I needed to do was sneak off to the bathroom, and phase through walls until I was out. I doubted she cared about individual escapees anyway, so long as she had enough hostages to keep the Protectorate and PRT interested.

I make for the stairway as the spell on the crowd seems to break. Screams, some panic, some more running for the side doors only to be repelled. More reaching for phones to reach out to the PRT as first suggested, though I highly doubt they are unaware at this point. I duck into the bathroom, flip my clothes around and cover my face, then experimentally dip one hand into the back wall. No wires. I phase through. Again. Again. Last wall, I peer through to check for gunmen or arrogant-sounding Tinkers waiting on the other side - seeing none, I wait for two charges - then rush out, burning the second charge to handle the fall down to street-level. Bring up Glory Girl's forcefield.

No cries of alarm. No explosions. Safe.

First order of business. Retrieve costume. I'd just been at a public event. PHO detectives will out me if I show up in Cape footage with this as my disguise. Now I'm glad for my foresight. I wasn't really expecting the ABB, my money was on the Empire making a play - but this was exactly the kind of reason I kept it nearby. In the speed-state, I arrive at the stash in less than a minute - and I'm changed just two minutes after that. Ready. And, if I dare say so myself, looking awesome.

I make my way to the rooftop and-

-and that is a lot of ABB colours. A lot. And more streaming down the street. Blockades in the road to block the police at every junction, while members roam the surrounding streets in small groups firing guns into the air and generally making a nuisance of themselves.

Definitely looking to draw all the heroes in to restore order. The situation was a powder keg waiting to explode. The police wouldn't want to start a real shootout, they'd rather wait for the Cape business to resolve and pick up the stragglers afterwards. Law and order, the path of least bloodshed - you could always count on the authorities to be predictable around here.

What you couldn't count on, was the villains. Because I'm pretty sure the lightshow and flaming buildings three streets across is the result of Lung clashing with Dauntless - or perhaps New Wave. And if he's here, and the Tinker lady is presumably monitoring the hostages and distracting as many other heroes as she can - judging by the other periodic explosions I can see intermittently appear in the distance - then what happened to my prediction that this was all about Oni Lee? Was this just a blaze of glory from Lung? Overconfidence? That didn't seem like him.

But he was here. Not wherever Oni Lee was being stored. That was an inarguable fact.

...it didn't change anything. I am here. The villains are here. It's as simple as that. It's not the target that I'd been counting on today, but unless I'd misjudged the strength of this Bakuda outside of the admittedly-impressive trick of catching Armsmaster off-guard - and I'd wager that the entire building was compromised before he ever stepped foot in it - the ABB would all be in prison by the end of the day. Lung would be Birdcage-bound, and I would lose access to his power forever.

Can't have that now, can we? I've been looking forward to getting that one.

The hunt begins.

#3,165
The first order of business was deciding how I should approach things. This was a much more public affair than my usual outings. Should I be making a point to go out of my way to save civilians? Should I wipe out as many of the gangbangers on the way through as I could? Or was it better to just make my way directly to the Cape fight? Was this 'Bakuda' the optimal target, or Lung?

Did I even want to be at the Cape fight? Maybe it was paranoia from my challenges repeatedly fucking me over, but I didn't see this situation as 'Lung and Bakuda randomly start a fight downtown' that I happened to stumble across. Running into Oni Lee back then was just bad luck. This was a fight that had been chosen by the ABB. Everything, from the stage the heroes had been speaking from, to the blockades covering the streets, to the bombs surrounding the building, to the location that Lung had started making a scene in - had been planned.

And that last one was my problem. It stinks. It's absolutely clear and obvious to anyone with a brain that the purpose of this fight is to, somehow, free Oni Lee. Yet, Lung starts a fight in the middle of town - miles from any likely holding facility. He miraculously finds a second Cape, yet that Cape also seems to be involved - at least, judging by how well-timed and directed the explosions inside the building, and now out on the streets as well - seems to be. I couldn't entirely rule out remote control while Bakuda frees Oni Lee, but the speech seemed live to me and we were looking at direct supervision at least. Plus, Bakuda was a completely new face in the Bay, they wouldn't need to announce her presence as the opening move - she would already be raiding a containment facility by the time anyone realised that there was another Cape around.

It just didn't line up. Bakuda, somewhere around here. Lung, here. The vast concentration of heroes, also here. Oni Lee, locked away somewhere that was not here. Why? Why had they chosen this, deliberately, as their opening move?

Option A - and maybe I was being paranoid - was that this was exactly that: This was just the opening move. Draw the heroes in, and repeat the trick against Armsmaster to get just one or two more heavy hitters. The fact of the matter was that the heroes in the Bay were rather top-heavy in terms of power budgets. Triumph, Velocity, Assault, Battery, most of the Wards, most of New Wave - they had their moments to shine against other villains, but not Lung. Not against that level of force and durability. Few people had the firepower to put him down, most would just escalate the fight into causing more havoc to the city and the people nearby.

Against Lung, the hero-aligned options were far more limited. Armsmaster and Dauntless. I could add in my challenge-earned knowledge and concede that Miss Militia could be added to that list in a desperate situation, but would be unlikely to use the firepower needed. Kid Win's alternator cannon... maybe if he somehow landed a clean hit. That thing had hit hard in the bank challenge, but I'd count on Lung if I had to bet. Otherwise... what, praying for Clockblocker or Vista to safely use their powers to stall and isolate him? Outside of their top two or three fighters, all the Protectorate had were niche options and the nuclear-threat of running and crying to the Triumvirate if Lung caused too much trouble.

That was it. New Wave had tried and failed to handle him as an entire team before, so I'd count them out entirely. The Wards would be held back from a fight with Lung by default, likely redirected to crowd-control duty. The literal kind, redirecting civilians to safety and the like. Armsmaster was out of commission thanks to Bakuda. The fact was that the face of heroic resistance against whatever Lung wants to do today... was Dauntless, with potential support from the very-squishy Miss Militia. But really, just Dauntless.

So naturally, he'd be drawn to Lung's position like a fly to honey. I could already see the flash of lights in the distant flames that I was pretty sure was him. But did he even fully understand what had happened to Armsmaster yet? Did he realise that the street he was charging his opposition in, could be covered in all kinds of exotic bombs ready to take him out of the fight as well? I can well imagine how simple it must be to create a bomb that would take out Dauntless but that a ramped-up Lung would simply shrug off.

Or was I overthinking it? Because there was a second option. Option B: They did this not because they needed to wipe out the people who can stop them, but because simply forcing the heroes to respond is enough. They fulfil their role as distractions while the jailbreak happens elsewhere. A third Cape under Lung's control? Another trigger, on top of Bakuda? Could Lung really have gotten so lucky?

Did he even need luck? Faultline's crew had done jailbreaks for money before. Even Circus might be enough with the heroes drawn away. Oni Lee would be utterly trivial to break out, they wouldn't be keeping him sedated full time - he was likely restrained only by virtue of lacking the line-of-sight to get to an escape route. Opening even the slightest hole in his cell would enable him to leave any facility in seconds.

But then again, did I care? I was on the side of the heroes, but I wasn't exactly on the side of 'keep the villains locked away'. Aside from the teensy detail that Oni Lee probably still wants to kill me, it was better for me if he was out and about - I couldn't challenge him from whatever cell they were keeping him in - and even the first level of Oni Lee's power had become a core component of my fighting style. I owed so many victories and synergies to that abiility already, and there was so much potential for it to grow even further in future challenges.

What a pain. I'm torn between two trains of thought on all fronts. Let the ABB win so Oni Lee is a viable target again and the rest of the ABB Capes remain a challenge target? Help the PRT to get my challenges in now, secure my reputation and get away from the persistent threat of Lung jumping my ass in a back alley? My challenge-instincts say that this could be a trap and I should stay well clear of any fights, sniping glances at the major Capes to get my challenges in from positions of safety. My real-life side tells me that Lung doesn't do that, and that being seen around - but not helping - is going to hurt my reputation.

I'm not concerned about my own situation if Oni Lee is out and about, but it isn't just about me anymore. I could survive an ambush. Taylor can't. And if I want to go through with expanding the influence of the Merchants as I slowly take control of them, a weaker, sluggish ABB would help with that. Or should I just disregard that risk, knowing that it wouldn't take too many victories for the target on my back to disappear? I was a lot stronger now than the last time I fought Oni Lee, I might genuinely be able to solve the problem today.

A part of me is surprised I'm even bothering to think like this at all. I'm usually not so paranoid, but the sudden shift in the situation has thrown me off my game. Seeing Armsmaster - of all people! - so effortlessly taken out of the equation had me doubting what I could achieve myself. I had a better understanding than most about my strength relative to everyone else in the Bay, and seeing a local top-tier get taken out easily was enough to kill my usual sense of bravado. Cheap trick? Sure. But I had no idea how much preparation time the Tinker had in the lead-up to this moment. Was that one attack the peak of their craft, something that had taken weeks and months to make? Or was that a glimpse of a basic application of their speciality, and they actually had both the time and resources to easily cover the city with similar traps in preparation for this showdown with the Protectorate?

To say nothing of what might happen if Lung spotted me. He was undoubtedly already ramped up. I'd ran away from him before in Emma's challenges - and frankly, if he was already at a decent size and noticed me before I was in my speed-state, I was dead. My speed-state was just enough to get away and stay away when he started from his base state before growing during the chase. So even just getting close to get a glimpse wasn't completely safe, not when I already knew I was on his most-wanted list. I'd only want to be around him when I had plenty of backup next to me, because as good as Dauntless was at keeping himself out of the dragon-man's grasp - I had my doubts about his ability to save me nearly as effectively. And that was completely ignoring the possibility of being blindsided by the Tinker.

And on top of all of that, it didn't even need to be a Cape that did me in. I flick my eyes across the intervening space between my position and the distant battle several rows of streets away. Hundreds of buildings. Thousands of potential sniper spots. Unfamiliar territory to me, so I couldn't even leap sideways into a wall with confidence without the risk of hitting electricity.

Yes. My challenges were unfair. They generated bullshit, unreasonable scenarios constantly. Real life wasn't so weighted in my enemies favour. But it had drilled something into me. How not to die like a bitch. Because as much as I try and rationalise that I'm probably overthinking this, I can't give myself an honest reason why I shouldn't expect the worst from a scene so obviously intended to attract the attention of any and all heroes in the area. I knew the reason why my power didn't allow guns, and that was because most enemies just didn't have a Brute rating. Most of the heroes responding were alive because of luck, and a general aversion to escalating shared by the majority of their likely foes - but I wasn't really the type to assume mercy and luck would be on my side these days. Not when walking into enemy territory like this.

I flick my gaze downwards to the police cars lining up in a concave around the closest barricade. That? That was fine. The ABB couldn't have set things up here so easily. It would have been too hard to sneak regular people past the patrols and security checks. But over there? In the convenient area that had never had to stand up to the scrutiny of Armsmaster checking security? That never had security patrols and inspections for people even drawing close to the street? There could be anything over there.

Was I really thinking about walking away? Surely not. "Come on Greg, you can't chicken out with the grand prize right there." Lung and Dauntless, plus a capable mystery Tinker waiting around somewhere. A gold mine for me.

My attempt to psyche myself up fails. I remain rooted in place at the overhanging roof I'd landed on. Fear. That was my issue. Not the paralysing sort that leaves you unable to act in the moment, but the surge of paranoia and caution that comes from real life being no different to playing a game on ironman mode. No saves. No second life. Was the leap into the unknown really worth it? The treasure chest is right there in sight, as long as I don't roll the metaphorical one. But the game-over screen is right there too. Is this really the right course of action? Would a delay of another week really be that painful? The snowball was already rolling downhill, did I need to risk breaking it on a sharp rock when I could just weave to the side?

The safe play is to walk away. Take the guaranteed path to power. Lurk in the shadowy corners of the streets and take my challenges where I could snipe a glance at the fighters without being seen.

But to continue the ironman metaphor... the safe play was always to never leave the starting zone. Never take on a dangerous quest. Never take on that challenging raid. Just sit there, grinding mobs and digging up plants to level to 99 without any possibility of death. But that wasn't playing the game. Wasn't being true to the reason gamers opted into that kind of challenge in the first place.

My shoulders untense. Right. Video games truly did hold all the wisdom of the world. Why worry about what the villain of this act was plotting anyway? I'd already established that either outcome was something that I could adapt to and use to my advantage. The details would unfold when they needed to unfold. None of the other heroes would be beating themselves up over whether they should try and fight Lung or do what they were actually best at, so why should I? I'd fit right in the crowd by simply leaving Dauntless to it and prioritising everything else first. Hostages. ABB gang members. Bakuda. Maybe even saving Armsmaster for the ultimate street cred experience.

A grin spreads across my face. Yes. That was it. That was perfect. That was the shape of the level I was in right now. A challenge without being a challenge. Beat the mobs. Save the NPCs. Acquire reputation among my peers. Take out the miniboss. And then, and only then, would I consider the final boss and what kind of difference I could make there without getting unceremoniously taken out like Armsmaster or worse.

It was that simple. I was a hero. There were villains here. That was enough.

There was no need to limit my options for no reason, splitting this into a pure 'fight Lung 1v1' or 'hide like a coward' situation. Nobody else, aside from Dauntless and a few ranged Capes, was even considering that first one as a realistic option. I should just take a page out of Velocity's book. Show up. Be seen, and then run away to contribute to smaller-scale problems that are more my pay-grade. The fact is, even though I do have some tools that could be used against Lung - they can be a bit clunky. Hard to hit on a moving, resisting target. Something I was willing to try in a challenge, but not something I wanted to opt-into when my life was on the line.

So. Take out the small fry first. Easy enough to do. The ABB forces and the police were both seemingly content to have a standoff everywhere they met, at least as far as I could see from here. And I... could definitely do something about that. If I was worried about Lung and his Tinker - then all I had to do was free up more and more heroic resources to pressure him and draw more tricks out of them. It wasn't like I had to challenge them now or miss my chance forever, I could catch them on the retreat too - and if they got captured... people could hardly blame me for sneaking a parting shot at the defeated as they get secured in the van.

I drop off the last roof with a burst of decisiveness. I spin up my knight as I hit street-level, but don't reveal myself right away - waiting patiently for thirty seconds until it was large enough to be a threat all on its own. Then, I send out my minion - the thin tendril connecting it to my ash clone near-invisible in the fading evening light. I grin to myself at the sound of panicked yells from the ABB goons lazing around the street, bursts of gunfire, the sound of something detonating - and then finally some foreign-sounding expletives accompanying the screech of tires as one car after the other makes some distance, only to realise that they're stuck between my knight and the very unhappy police.

I consider the scene before stepping out. Two gangbangers on the ground. One car with a gaping hole in the side of it. Nicely done. One of the fallen men tosses a grenade at the knight. I frown at that. He's too close, that explosion could kill him. I mentally shift my focus back to my ash clone to indirectly-order the knight to shield the man before bringing Glory Girl's forcefield back onto myself.

A moment later, I realise I didn't need to bother. And that I need to mentally adjust my expectations for the threat level of the 'normies' of the ABB. Because the grenade doesn't explode. It activates. A solid, perfect sphere of flame engulfs my knight and then stays there - not an explosion, not a flame, just a shimmering orb of controlled fire that starts to melt and ignite parts of the nearby car out of pure proximity as both of the gang members backpedal away from the scene.

I mentally add another digit to my estimation of their Tinker. Not because of the effect, but because a complete nobody had been given it. The effect whimpers out after a few more seconds, my knight still standing despite the smoking, molten ruin that it was now encased in. Durability was never a question for it, and the gangbangers seem appropriately horrified that their very-lethal method of attack had been shrugged off by their opponent.

As they should be. That was lethal force, whether they realised what that grenade could do wasn't really important. Retaliation would have been very justified for a normal Cape. Alas, I'm not normal. Just too heroic and wholesome for my own good.

I quietly circle around their line-of-sight, Vista's power placing me next to them before they even realise they're under attack. Browbeat's power makes them easy to handle - I was more than capable of snapping limbs and breaking bones with just my base strength and a good angle. Browbeat's power made it into a joke. And to think, I didn't even have access to its full synergistic potential, this was just the forcefield generated by my... well. I didn't exactly have noodle arms these days, I was muscular and well-built across the board - but I wasn't a full adult. My body wasn't a steroid-abusing bodybuilder's dream and it certainly wasn't anything close to the absurdity of the self-modification that Browbeat had done to themselves in the challenge.

All of that, and I was still throwing around two full-grown men like they were toddlers. I don't blink at the screams of pain and agonising-sounding cracks and snaps, I can't trust them after throwing an attack like that out. I'm not even sure that my shadow state would survive a Tinker attack like that - so they can just consider their mistakes in the hospital.

The sound of tortured metal announces the failure of the would-be-escapees to dodge my knight. The occupants of the vehicle scramble away, racing towards the police lines with hands above their heads rather than entrust their fate to the seemingly-unstoppable, vengeful figure of my half-molten knight. They're quickly taken into custody.

I frown as nervous-looking police edge towards me, weapons and riot shields raised but not pointed directly at me. "I'm Void Cowboy. Hero. Don't mind me." I make a dismissive gesture. They seem to relax, but don't entirely lower their guard as I step away - Glory Girl's shield fully active just in case someone gets... twitchy.

"New costume? Looks good on you!" One policewoman walks up, less cautious than most. "Though I see you haven't made much of an improvement on subduing criminals peacefully." I note the floating '3/4' in her challenge box. Huh. What were the odds? I didn't recognise her, but must have been someone I've run into on my patrols.

Kind of cute. Shame she isn't alone.

And this isn't the time for that anyway.

I shake my head. "Don't want to take any risks in case they had more Tinkertech like that in their pockets." I gesture at the near-spherical hole in the street nearby, already cooling from its angry red glow. "I might be able to take it, maybe, but if they pretended to surrender and tossed that at one of you guys... well. Even if Panacea was standing right here, I don't think anyone would walk away from it."

The other police start to relax as the conversation continues. They fan out, a few inspecting the damaged cars, a few racing down the street past us and others returning to their own vehicles to relocate closer to the hostage-crisis.

"They're not all that bad. And I'm pretty sure most of these jokers don't have a clue what they're holding. Heard one guy accidentally dropped it, tried to kick it away - his entire leg turned into crystal. Unless it turns back, he's losing that leg." Another cop offers. "Still, should be grateful for their Tinker being such a weirdo. A real explosion would have killed him five-times-over from that range."

"Guess the special effects have their own limitations." I nod. "But I don't think anyone is keen on testing those when it comes to what the Tinker was showing off in the main building. Whatever she used to freeze Armsmaster, and the little system she's got blocking the doors and windows off to stop the hostages from leaving whenever - the only person I'd really trust to defuse it is... well. Armsmaster."

"Tough break. Chatter was that Kid Win was going to come down and give his opinion, but getting through to the venue has been difficult so far - and they obviously had their reasons to take the long route. This whole thing only gets worse if Lung gets his claws wrapped around a Ward as a hostage to keep the big guns away." A gruff-sounding man adds his thoughts as the groaning ABB members are led away.

I nod to myself. "Sounds like helping clear the path for him is the most productive thing I can do right now. Unless you know where the Tinker is hiding?" I add the last question in a hopeful tone.

"Not a clue." One gruff-looking man speaks up. "Even if we knew that, we wouldn't be able to spare anyone to go after them. We're stretched too thin as it is. WIth the Empire kicking off too, there isn't even enough Capes to go around for this mess."

"The Empire?" I tilt my head. "Oh, grabbing Victor and Krieg, I guess. I forgot about them." Mostly because I wasn't involved. Well. This was the exact reason I didn't pay much attention to news like that anyway. The PRT was playing softball with everyone right now. Aside from Lung and Hookwolf, prison security may as well not exist for all the effort that goes into stopping breakouts. Sure, you can't position Capes there permanently for an attack that could happen at literally any time - but it would be somewhat nice if the PRT put effort into keeping criminals secure even if they weren't Birdcage-bound.

No, that was a lie. That was what the old Greg used to think, obviously I have a different perspective now and PRT levelling up their game would be terrible for me now - but still. I understand not wanting to force the Empire into an all-or-nothing, blood-on-the-streets battle with the law over some street-level Capes... but things are never going to get better if you don't just... ask Strider to swing by and leave them on a deserted island for a month or two while the courts get everything in order. Throw them in a random cop car and drive them three hundred miles up-country. Why not? Was there a rule that criminals had to be kept somewhere so local and easy to break into? Maybe there was. That would explain it.

Or maybe, people were just happy to not rock the boat. I was a terminally-online Cape nerd, I pay attention to the state of the Bay. But most people didn't really know or care about the day-to-day happenings between the gangs or the balance of power in the city. They wouldn't ever see a Cape fight in person, or seriously note the effects of their presence in the Bay. A few dozen people in a city boasting hundreds of thousands of people. There was a legitimate argument that, given the choice of excising all the gangs from the Bay and fixing the rail network or clearing out the Boat Graveyard - picking the gangs would be the least effective choice for change in the Bay.

But infrastructure projects didn't shoot lasers or fly last time I checked, so fuck that. And the argument only held true as long as everyone agrees to keep the kid gloves on - and that wasn't the safest assumption to make when the gangs were fully prepared to kill each other or die trying.

"Right. Seems like every prison and holding facility across the city is getting hammered today. Not to mention all the random lowlifes kicking off. Heard some freak abducted the mayor's niece in broad daylight the moment they realised the police were all busy. Involving some kid for, what, a bit of ransom money to pay for drugs? I hate this city sometimes." A pair of cops nod to each in commiseration before joining the inspection of the nearest car and dragging away a selection of weaponry from inside. The crowd around me has thinned now, any concern about me being a threat long-since removed - just a trio of cops that have yet to split off to their own tasks.

Or, correction, one cop and two uniformed PRT officers. Same thing in my book, but I don't think they would agree in more peaceful times.

"I get it. All that effort, and they're out in the space of a few weeks." I shake my head. "I guess most Capes that can't do anything against Lung will be heading off the Empire. Where's Kid Win coming in from? If he's got any ideas on freeing Armsmaster, that's probably the best way to stop the ABB - and we can solve the hostage crisis at the same time."

The two PRT officers hesitate as one while their comrades continue to filter past them. "I don't know if that's the kind of information we should hand out-" One grimaces. "I know you're on our side, but we can't really hand out-"

I cut a hand through the air to stop their apologies. "I get it, I get it. Got to be even more careful when they're Wards, right? I respect that. I wouldn't want to force it out of you." I draw in a breath, then near-inaudibly release it again. "Challenge."

It doesn't take long. In fact, it takes no time at all for the steady stream of success notifications to speed through my view. These guys were only slightly more difficult than an average civilian because of their fitness and the fact that they were all armed in their challenges. But, factors like that didn't matter to me these days. The modifiers weren't strong enough. They would need a small army to even make me need to think about the difficulty of the challenge.

Oh, my power could do that. Sure it could. It didn't need the presence of Capes to make things hard. But equally...

Well. It was obvious that it wasn't trying to do that. In fact, these were possibly some of the easiest challenges that I've ever done with the way they rush at me without any attempt at their only real chance to win - an ambush.

But it makes sense. I like to think I've gotten a good grasp on my power's tendencies these days. The way it rewards some behaviours, punishes others. And while it was certainly possible that pure, dumb luck had resulted in these easy challenges being raced through with ease - I trust my gut feelings when it comes to my power.

"You don't want to waste any more time on these guys than I do, do you?" I ask nobody in particular as I pad through an unfamiliar police station.

"Die!" My target lunges around a corner, pistol barking rapidly.

Shadow State. Browbeat. Vista. Shadow State. Kick to the head. Dismiss success screen. Challenge again.

I hum to myself as the world reforms around me. "I mean, that wasn't any fun for anyone. No challenge to it. But, in real-life terms - it's valuable for me to keep doing these, right? Way more than I already am. But... these aren't exactly the big-ticket brawls you like stretching out." I continue. "This time, it's just a half-dozen fights for a bit of information. But... you don't want me doing this hundreds and hundreds of times, do you? Maybe before, when it was still a struggle - but that doesn't really apply anymore, does it?"

I get no response. I didn't expect one in the first place.

I burst through the next door in the shadow state. The victim has their back turned to me. Dead. Success. Goodbye.

A ghostly challenge box appears next to the newly-completed policewoman's head, overlaid over her personal challenge box.

Brockton Bay Security Forces

1/3

(GANG) (FOCS) (CTRL) (LUST) (PREP) (TIME)

NOT ENOUGH INFLUENCE​

Well. That wasn't there before. I parse it for a moment. An interesting title, actually. Security forces wasn't the title of a specific group, but I'd wager that it encompassed both the normie-PRT forces and the BBPD together. That made the challenge a little harder, but also a little more rewarding if I could claim victory.

Sure. That will do. Only trouble is that error stopping me from trying my luck right now. I've only seen that organisation-level challenge box for the Empire so far, and the message stopping me from actually challenging it then was still the same. I hadn't quite worked out if it indicated a need to beat more challenges among their members overall as I first assumed, or, like Leet, develop a sufficient level of reputation or closer bonds in real life first.

I was okay with either option. They went hand-in-hand at the end of the day. I wasn't bothered about the inability to attempt it right at this moment. It wasn't needed now anyway, and I wasn't going to pretend that I'd already largely suborned the entire police department to my will already and deserved to 'sweep' the rest of it already, or that my 'infiltration' had even gotten that deep into the overall structure. My power was just highlighting it as an option for the future, and it gives me an interesting tool to test out in the future when I can start sniping and interacting with more senior members of the police force. Might save me some time on the 'chore' of easy civilian challenges in the future.

And then I could find out what happened on a victory for that type of challenge. Would it create a new challenge 'floor' for all the members to act as a new baseline? Could a new power be on the cards? Or some kind of, organisation-wide trend or inefficiency when it came to following up on anything I did? There were a lot of possibilities, but this would be a lot easier to achieve than the one for the Empire - taking a day or three later on to find out could be a good move.

"Come on, it's not like he's with the ABB - and there's not much harm that he can even do with that information while they're playing safe anyway. If he can free them up, great." One of the trio interjects, newly enthusiastic about sharing information after completing her challenges.

"I suppose that's true." One wets her lips as her eyes trail down my new costume. "We need all the help we can get. Triumph was waiting outside the venue at the time of the attack, so he's been keeping the back half of the building clear of any thugs in the hope that the heroes can navigate past the doorway without alerting the Tinker if there's nobody around to let her know that people managed to get in."

"Only trouble is that the ABB aren't making it easy to move through the streets at all. I don't know if they're aware of what the Empire has been doing, but they must know that they'd be crushed out in the open like this if not for the hostages - so they're doing everything they can to stop us from getting too close to the building to work on freeing the hostages."

"And it's a new Tinker, so nobody knows if she's bluffing or crazy." I conclude.

A nod. "Anyway, last I heard they were coming along-" She takes out a phone and fiddles with it for a moment. "-here." I nod at the map. There's a mall nearby, I've been there a few times - not in real life though. "But they didn't want to just blow through and let the Tinker know who is approaching from where, so they're waiting for the police to clear a path."

"Very patient of them." Wasn't Shadow Stalker on console duty right now? She must be hopping and screaming in outrage right now. She'd definitely already be inside the building alone right now if she had the chance, hoping to find the Tinker in some hidden closet somewhere. But the rest of the Wards? They were all too happy to sit tight and wait for orders. The bank challenge highlighted that clearly enough, otherwise I'd never have pulled out the win. "I guess I'll go and knock some heads together in that direction. Will you be alright here?"

"Don't worry about us, we won't be doing much until we get reinforcements. Last thing we want to do is get ourselves surrounded by pushing faster than everyone else." One of them waves a hand down the street, where more cop cars were already fanning out in a new concave closer to the venue - another would-be-blockade from gangbangers that didn't seem to have much concern over whether they had a way out or not.

Faith in Lung, I suppose. If Lung continued his rampage, and offered the PRT a truce in exchange for the return of any of his gang - they would take it. The PRT weren't a gang in the truest sense. They couldn't just take the approach that hurt their rivals the most, that crippled their enemies the most - they were there to preserve lives. And if that meant being predictable against an overwhelming threat, then that's just what it meant.

"I'll get going then." I wave and shift into my speed-state, waiting out the paralysis before turning to leave.

"Hey, if you want to give me your number - I can let you know any updates that we get-" One voice is cut-off by the scandalised giggling of another - and I disappear down the street before I can hear any more.

I head back towards the venue first. I hadn't made a huge amount of distance during my escape from my perspective, just a few streets and rooftops to gain some distance - but it was easy to see how the ABB had effectively blocked off every intersection that normal people would take. I blitz past a few attempted blockades to return to the venue. Just outside the front entrance, armed ABB are swarming - half-a-dozen faces turn towards me in alarm as I approach, too slow to do anything but start to point weapons in my direction. But they aren't the interesting thing here. Above them, a circular drone hovers in the air - the slightly-feminine figure of who I could only assume was Bakuda outlined in a hologram projection above it.

"A hero?" The drone barks out, the voice distorted by the heightened perception of the speed-state as it attempts to race after me. "You won't-"

Moving up to the rooftops, it's easy to see places where the ABB had set-up originally and later abandoned as the police did their best to restore order. If it was the Empire, this would make a lot of sense - regular law enforcement wouldn't want to push without Cape support out of fear that any of the dozen-odd Capes in their employ would show up to face them - but here? They were getting pushed back across the board, save for a few streets that seemed to have new 'fixtures' - warped scenery and obviously parahuman effects, likely courtesy of more of that Tinker's work. Not too effective in a fight, but it did cut off the street as a viable approach path.

...but it still wasn't a winning strategy. And that isn't a comforting thought, because I've never considered Lung as stupid. To me, it means he's either utterly confident in winning his duel against Dauntless and any support from New Wave - leaving the normie-troops with nothing to do other than flee as he rescues his gang, or he's confident that Oni Lee will be joining him to give the ABB the mobility and force projection needed to stop the ABB from nearly dissolving overnight with how much he could stand to lose here.

Or both. The heroes of Brockton Bay didn't exactly have a good track record of stopping Lung on a rampage, so whatever he was planning - there was always going to be the plan C of just taking the fight into a populated neighbourhood until the PRT folded to his demands like wet paper. The advantage of being the strongest guy in the Bay right there, I'd be looking forward to that kind of privilege myself one day.

My target is obvious as I approach. Or rather, familiar. In other words, he would duck and run for hours rather than take a single fair fight against an unknown like me. I couldn't assume he'd stay away from the real ordinance he had access to through the WRLD modifier, but that was most likely what he had closest to hand. Probably lethal on its own if I leave him to bleed out.

I stare in confusion. What? Those two modifiers... how would they even go together? They both restricted space, how did they even interact? Surely one would overwrite the other? "Challenge." I had to see this.

I spawn in. I lock eyes with Clockblocker. Oh.

That makes sense. My left shoulder was already brushing against a wall. I could reach out and touch the wall on the right. I didn't want to turn around, but I'm pretty sure it's a mirror of what I see in front of me. A very close Clockblocker, and a wall behind him.

So. The ZONE modifier just further restricted the boundaries of the CAGE. Good to know. But more importantly, there was absolutely no way to avoid Clockblocker's touch in a cramped space like this. My ash clone stirs behind me as he rushes forward. Does Glory Girl's shield stop-

-it? Clockblocker teleports, a kick breaking on Glory Girl's forcefield before he-

-teleports again. Another hit breaking on Glory Girl's forcefield and then-

-teleports again, back to establish some more distance. At least, as much distance as this place allows - just a metre of breathing room, even with me positioned at the furthest distance possible.

Huh. Interesting. My powers that go on cooldown still tick down when I'm Clockblocked. That's... not very useful, actually - but it's cool. If only I could Clockblock myself, I'd be invincible - if immobile.

He couldn't win like this. But, he didn't need to either. Even if he wasn't deliberately playing towards it - either the CAGE modifier would generate something to break the deadlock, or the anti-stalling measures would turn him into a physical god that could snap me like a twig if he kept freezing me forever.

So, I needed to either put him in a situation where he doesn't want to freeze me, or where I will eventually kill him with the fractions of a second I get to move before he freezes me again. If I pin him against the wall, or grapple him in a certain way - even if I'm frozen, he won't be able to move anyway. Something like that.

Do I have a tool for that other than Browbeat's power? Raw Brute strength? I don't think so. Every other weapon uses kinetic force which was useless against him.

On the plus side, that made things simple. He couldn't really dodge. I just charge at him, do my best to lock him down - I either win in what feels like a few seconds, or he survives for however long it takes for the stalling measures to kick in when we're actively 'fighting'. Gotta be longer than if I was hiding, surely?

He still doesn't approach. Good. Gives me time to think. My ash clone was important here. I couldn't protect it other than blocking access to it with my body, but I could spawn it behind me and use it as support - support that could respond when he had frozen me in place.

In the absence of an offensive power that could work against him, the best support would stop him from slipping out of my grasp at all. With space this limited, that either meant Vista, or Clockblocker's own power.

Or, I give it Glory Girl's power - and that can be the blocker instead? But would that be as useful? Probably not. I'd still need to be the one in front to crush him physically with Browbeat's power, it wasn't enough to stall and survive.

Vista, Clockblocker, Vista, Clockblocker. Clockblocker. With some strings from my shirt so that it could stop him from slipping through any holes in my attempt to block him in.

Set. Ready. Charge. My ash clone and I move as one. Not wide enough to truly move side-by-side - but the important thing was the initial grab. I sieze his wrist- he flickers in place, his arm now free, but my ash clone now firmly wrapped around his legs - frozen in place. I slam my hand into the armoured plate covering his neck, seeking to pressure him into the wall- and lose him again immediately. Ash clone is gone. I shrug off a hit to the back of the head. Got behind me? It's fine. That won't do anything while Browbeat's power is up. I resummon my ash clone. Again.

Slower this time. I block two thirds of the tunnel with my body. My clone takes the remaining third, ready to lock down the string at any moment. No escape. Slow and steady. One step. Two. He isn't playing this right, it's actually better for him to come to me - to give himself more room to escape back into. But that suits me. And it's easy for me to criticise, from his perspective - this is a horror-movie set-up.

We step forward again. Again. His hand lashes out to tag me. I don't react.

He's still there a moment later, seeming a little more out of breath. Ash clone? Still alive. We step closer. He tags me again. Step. Shuffle closer. Shuffle. Another tag- and he teleports, but not to a position of safety, he's trapped in a web of strings - my ash clone frozen in place pressing down on his head as if trying to saw it off on the string his neck was resting on. -of-

-his-

-neck-

I resummon it, Clockblocker could hardly move effectively with my hands firmly locked around his neck like this.

And all I had to do was squeeze. Oh, certainly, he was Clockblocking me. But what did it matter? The advantage of doing that was in escaping, in setting up some trap around me that I couldn't evade - here, that wasn't possible. The armoured plate cracks as my fingers dig under it, the hands attempting to force mine away seeming to surge with strength as every second goes by. Seconds where I was sitting there unmoving for minutes on end.

But if I don't notice it, does it matter? I've been in this position many times, his neck is just waiting to be broken - from my perspective, it won't take long. These helmets were designed to break. To absorb impacts and break rather than risk the occupant inside. They weren't meant to be pressured like this, squeezed and bent. His visor was cracked too, a testament to the equally slow, steady movements of my ash clone picking its own target.

Crack. Crack. My hands find flesh and a hammering pulse as the costume gives way to Brute-enhanced strength. It was funny to think that this was still a fairly low-tier Brute power. But against what was essentially a normal person? It was a cheat code. People on PHO would laugh off someone showing off their Brute powers by bending a metal bar. But that was exactly what I was doing here. Slowly. Unstoppably. With nothing he can do but freeze me and delay the end for another few minutes.

Crack. Crack. Blood pours onto my hands. My ash clone did well, but I can't move now to take advantage. This only works because he's pinned, unable to free himself because his only weapon is to do the equivalent of locking the jail cell shut around him.

To his credit, it might almost have been enough. The insistent pressure of his arm pushing mine away gets stronger and stronger with every moment, a telltale sign that the anti-stalling measures are stacking against me as the hours, maybe days, wear on.

But it isn't enough. The fraction of a second I get to move every time before his reactions can respond is just too much.

Crack. He finally goes still. No teleports now.

SUCCESS

Reward: Temporal Stasis (2)​

I grin. And for a moment, I almost turn my gaze in real life right back to Clockblocker's challenge sheet.

No. Behave. I've barely even spoken to the guy aside from today. Take it slow. Build a rapport first. I know I won't want to restrain myself if I get into that challenge and find myself in a winning position, so I won't even look.

Maybe its overly cautious. Maybe Emma was just crazy and it meant nothing for anyone else. But it was probably the right thing to do anyway, the kind of thing that sounded obvious when I said it out loud even if I was trying to frame it as a novel insight.

I roll my shoulders. I feel... a little drained, actually. My own fault for doing so many challenges in a row. I wasn't at my limit, but I was getting there. Thankfully, that's everything for now. I can take a breather. At least, until I run into the ABB Capes. Not missing out on that, no matter how much my power protests.

And despite how much my body is protesting, I've barely done anything yet. As far as the Wards around me are concerned, I should be as fit as a fiddle and ready to roll. Maybe it's a good thing that I was babysitting the Wards for a bit. Even if these guys were pretty close to my age, it was still babysitting. Experience matters more.

Vista shrinks the crystals down to ankle-level, then covers them with earth. "Let's go already."

You could learn from him." I give her a thumbs-up and form an L-shape on my forehead aimed at Clockblocker - much to his faux-outrage. Well said Vista!

"I- I was just trying to see if there was an obvious place for an explosive device. The one she was threatening to take everyone out at once with. I know it's hard to make broad statements when dealing with Tinkertech, but assuming a uniform explosion, a device that isn't going to wipe out too much of the surrounding area and potentially cause friendly-fire, and the need to potentially avoid the obstacle on stage that you mentioned seemed to be frozen in time - and therefore, potentially an obstacle to the force of an explosion. There's only a few basement rooms that could serve as a viable location for the bomb-" He babbles continuously. "We might need to head down there anyway - if the effect trapping the heroes on stage is possible to stop or disrupt, rather than just needing to wait for it to expire, then it will be found either backstage or below it. Probably the latter, it makes sense to place it in an area that not many people would walk through - and I'd guess none of the stage events had any kind of special effects that they'd use a trap door for."

Too many unknowns here. I almost wish I'd had a look around before leaving, but exiting safely and getting my costume on was definitely the better call.

We move together, a tense silence covering us despite the hubbub filling the hall below. A few guests are hiding up here, but are swiftly silenced with a hushed whisper as they approach us.

Navigating the building without entering the main hall proves a minor challenge, relying on Kid Win's map of the area and his flashlight to guide us forward into dark areas - with Vista occasionally tearing open a hole in some of the thinner walls or floors as discretely as she could in order to get us closer to our destination.

"Drone!" I warn the others, head reforming from the shadow state after a peek through the next door.

"Suspicious place for one." Kid Win pipes up. "Got to be keeping an eye out for people getting close to something important. Got to be related to the stage. Too close to be anything else. I could fry it, I'm pretty sure."

"Back the way we came. We can't reach the basement levels from here." Kid Win mumbles.

As we pull back, all four of the Wards freeze at once. I frown. "Problem?"

"Lung's heading this way." The response comes.

I tilt my head. "Dauntless is still fighting?"

"I'd guess Lung got too big to be put down, but Dauntless is too fast to be caught so Lung's just decided to ignore him. Apparently New Wave got hit by something, they're pulling back." Clockblocker paces. "We should pull out ourselves. Even if everyone walks free out of this building, the situation won't change with Lung standing outside over them instead."
