If he's only decided to walk this way now, it means they have what they wanted and are looking to concentrate force in one place - even if only to ensure the gang doesn't lose half of its armed membership to rescue one Cape."

Some kind of complex about other Tinkers, it would make sense if she didn't leave the attack on Armsmaster to chance - and even more sense if she was in the crowd to bask in her success."

Naturally, I have my ways of scanning likely targets. First of all. Alice Choi was famous. The Cornell bomber had made the news, taken a bunch of hostages, flattened some historic buildings over a bad grade and then disappeared with the wind. Seeing her emerge here in Brockton Bay was a surprise, but one I was happy to see. With her already being outed, even if she'd shown up in civilian clothes - I'd spot her in a single glance.

I'd probably have spotted her anyway though. With how versatile she seemed, I doubted that she would a four-challenge blip like certain Wards were. Civilians didn't tend to go that high, making it even easier to parse through a crowd at a glance. Especially when we factor in the fact that I can exclude everyone who wasn't female, Asian, young and somewhat crazy.

I'd completely sort through this entire crowd in just a few minutes. A few quiet challenges and I wouldn't even have to confront her at all, she might just shut it all down and leave on her own merits after realising that the hostage game wasn't all it was cracked up to be. At that point, I could just admit that I was wrong - bask in the success of freeing everyone anyway, and go and watch everyone team up on Lung until one side or the other ran away. Brilliant plan.

"Found her." Foiled by an overachieving ass who I didn't even invite to come with me anyway. Gallant directs my attention up instead of down at the assembly below, a lone figure loosely leaning against the balcony of one of the private seating areas - seemingly looking at her phone.

Vaguely female, that's about all I can make out. "You sure?" I express doubt.

"Yes." He affirms flatly.

"...sure. Why not. Let's go say hello." I shrug.

I flex Vista's powerset, the recently-upgraded power effortlessly sloping the seating area on the floor above us down to our level - creating a steep but manageable climb.

I could get used to that. So much better than just manipulating air. Still not quite as impressive as the real deal, but a huge step up from what I had.

From there, finding the stairway up to the alcove - finding it locked, and phasing through much to Gallant's annoyance, was effortless.

The woman turns to face me as I step closer. No mask. But...

Alice Choi

Student 1/6

(EVNT)​

I suppose, just this once, I'll have to concede Gallant did well to spot her. I eye the drones on either side of her. Had he seen those from his angle? Or was it something else that had tipped him off? They probably practiced at playing detective in the Wards, that would make sense - and it wasn't like it was that much of a leap of logic anyway, looking down on everyone as she orchestrates the chaos from a hidden corner was entirely on-brand now that I think about it.

"Hello, Bakuda." I pause. "Or, do you prefer Alice, like this?"

"Either is fine. It isn't much of a secret anyway." She smirks. "Everyone knowing my name is better, actually - the more they learn of me, the less they'll confuse me with... lesser Tinkers."

Evil smirk. Murderous threats. Hostages. Rampaging ego. The very real possibility that I was about to get punked like Armsmaster. Why did I find this so attractive?

"Alice isn't the most intimidating name I've ever heard. I'd stick to Bakuda." I give her some much-needed honesty. The look of disdain! Perfection.

"I wasn't asking for your opinion." She sniffs. "No, the only reason I even allowed your little... intrusion to continue was simple boredom. The so-called defenders of the city, thinking that a few scattered heroes and some children would be enough to handle me? Me?" Her voice rises in challenge at the repetition.

Yep. A little crazy.

She continues. "I'll forgive this first time as ignorance. Confusion, perhaps. Given the evident lack of quality of most Tinkers in this city, your minders must have had certain expectations for how easily I might be handled." She's trying to smile. She's failing. "Actually, I have spent weeks and weeks preparing for my first showing. So many sleepless nights, outfitting even the lowliest grunt, preparing the most overwhelming, undeniable display of Tinkering mastery that this wretched city has ever seen. Your so-called greatest Tinker, beaten and helpless in a single move. A private army powerful enough to clash as equals with your strongest Brutes. Hundreds of hostages, helplessly trapped in a storm of impending fire and death - existing only at my mercy... and they send in a few Wards. The Wards. As if I was a rowdy drunk that needed guiding to a warm cell to sleep overnight."

Where are the actual heroes, lining up to test themselves against my genius?" Her eyes flash with fury. She didn't seem concerned at least. Whether that was because she didn't care about the hostage, or had no idea that Vista could and would put a hole in the building that a train could pass through in the space of a few seconds. Gallant emerges from the stairwell. "Gallant. Brockton Bay Wards."

A dead Ward or two after they so foolishly backed me into a corner would go a long way towards fixing that for next time."

Probably shouldn't be riling her up like that, but it really just came naturally to me.

"Does Lung approve of that plan?" I inch closer to Gallant. Can't let him die on me now. Still got no idea why he followed me here. Suicidal, maybe. Or just carrying a chip on his shoulder about the Tinker fraud coming to light.

"I'm a new face, I couldn't possibly be expected to know all the rules back to front. Making mistakes is natural, if he even cares at all." She retrieves a gas mask from the nearby table. "But, if my introduction to the ABB meant anything? You two aren't asian enough for him to care about you."

I emerge right where I left as the shockwave fades through the wall, the two closest drones reduced to broken husks after their suicide attacks - the stairwell mostly on fire. No corpse of Gallant, so he got my meaning pretty quickly and made himself scarce.

I grin wildly at Bakuda, who seems unbothered about her initial failure - but does attempt to back away as she pulls out what seems to be a grenade launcher. In some ways, no different to Vista. Struggles to handle things up-close and personal because she's squishy too. Any explosive that hurts me at this range, hurts her too. Maybe not her custom Tinker stock, but how much of that did she even have?

Not much, I'd guess. In fact, I'd bet that she wasn't even supposed to be here at all. Lung wouldn't have wanted to risk his Tinker like this. She was here on her own, and her earlier words about why Lung was coming - a 'prisoner swap' - didn't that indicate that a third party was coming here to exchange Oni Lee for someone that the ABB had in their possession? I'd arrived at the right answer of Bakuda being present by completely the wrong logic, Lung wasn't coming here for her - he was coming here because this was the agreed exchange point for his chief lieutenant once he was broken out by this other party.

That still put me on a timer. An angry Bakuda, an angry Lung and an angry Oni Lee all at once would be dangerous for me unless I could get into my speed-state and beeline away. But a happy Bakuda begrudgingly conceding that the handsome Void Cowboy wasn't so bad for sparing her, a pragmatic Lung realising I wasn't easy prey and an Oni Lee that was just following the orders of his master? That was a recipe for survival.

Step one? Tame the crazy, hot bitch in front of me. I was looking forward to it. Something about a wild, unchecked ego like that... just made me want to tear it down.

Couldn't be too hard.

"Challenge!"

#3,307

NO CASUALTIES

PROTECT THE FACILITIES​

I swipe away the rules of the EVNT modifier, then step to the side as a screaming crowd surges past me, racing through the corridor and halfway trampling me in the process. I spot a girl stumble, momentarily swallowed by the crush - and I wonder if this challenge is going to be as tedious as the bank challenge had been, herding lemmings around to ensure that the 'no deaths' condition is fulfilled. The girl is pulled to her feet a moment later, and I breathe a small sigh of relief.

Good. I could only assume that this was Cornell University and that I was taking the place of the responding heroes, which meant I'd likely have my hands full defusing the actual bombs and hostage situation without worrying about random people dying without Bakuda lifting a finger.

Honestly, I'd expected this from the moment I saw the EVNT modifier and the 'Student' as the description of the challenge - it didn't take a genius to figure out the most likely scenario for my power to conjure up in relation to the infamous figure. It worked from multiple angles, chronologically, thematically - but also in a meta-sense, this was the earliest expression of her power where she had the least resources and the least experience with her abilities. Starting here meant that the increasing difficulty of future challenges could be simulated by more recent appearances.

No extra modifiers to concern myself with, just a few basic scenario rules that could be summed up as 'Don't let her blow things up'. This should be simple. And in theory, if I lost here - it was quite possible that simply getting access to my phone and researching the original attack in more detail would yield valuable information. I'd never been all that interested in the specifics of the event aside from some casual discussion on PHO and the awareness that naturally comes in with trying to be on top of Cape-related news - but it was more than likely that there was a map of the bomb locations for this attack out there somewhere, testimonies from how the bombs had been stopped last time, where the hostages had been held and plenty more besides. It was more than likely that most of that information would hold up, save for those parts where another hero that was no longer here would have changed something.

Alas. I don't have access to the internet right now. In fact, the lack of information was assuredly the most difficult part of this challenge. I didn't know if I was on a timer before Bakuda set something off, or if the scenario would just wait to 'react' to my eventual attack. I didn't know the mechanism that the bombs were triggered by. Proximity? Timer? Manual triggers? Should I expect a civilian to try to be a hero at some point, or was this all dependent on my own actions? Was Bakuda willing to use the hostages as a weapon? Would she blow them up when she saw me, or would she discard her previous efforts in favour of the usual 'Kill Greg' priority that drove most of my challenges?

And, the most crucial question of them all, did any of the above matter to me right now? To the current Greg, with all the powers and experience I've gained so far? Because I was fairly certain that Bakuda wasn't a Brute. And while Tinkers were certainly dangerous in their own way, I would wager that actually overpowering Bakuda was going to be trivial. If any crazy Tinkertech effects had been shown off at the Cornell bombing, I would have been way more interested in it - as far as I know, at this stage of her career, she was stuck on 'things that go boom'. And while that was dangerous, so was a guy with a grenade launcher. I had ways to survive explosions. I'd be fine.

It was the hostages that wouldn't be. So I was going to have to be smart about this.

I move through the hallways of the university, empty now except for the detritus of a sudden evacuation. Papers, bags, shoes and more left behind in the rush. I try and orient myself within the building, taking note of the signs and maps as I pass them - committing the unfamiliar markers to memory. It was an unfortunate fact that, with the entire challenge literally hanging on a hair-trigger - I was pretty likely to have to try this one twice. No reason to just assume my failure though. This was as much about stealth as anything else. Free every hostage, defuse every bomb - all before Bakuda realised that something was up and that she needed to press the explode button.

It would be easier without the 'no casualties' rule. Because it didn't say 'no hostage casualties' - that meant taking her in alive. I couldn't just win by decapitating her before she can turn around. Like Sophia, she needed to lose. To be beaten. To have no other recourse but to surrender. Or, perhaps, just to escape. Not that I'd trust her to do that without trying to blow something else up, but there was no rule saying I even had to beat her - just to end the scenario with no deaths and no significant damage to the structures.

Which does somewhat leave the door open for a win by honest conversation. And if the situation wasn't what it was, that would be my first choice. I would have liked to have a conversation with Bakuda, to try and understand her mind and her motivations both inside and outside of the challenge - but I was in the middle of a fight and a better understanding of Bakuda's powers or a slight reluctance on her part to actually kill me could be the difference between life and death.

Besides, even if I could stall the fight out long enough to challenge her repeatedly before Lung arrives, every minor delay was dangerous to me. Even timing this specific challenge had concerned me - with the minor delay it inflicted on my actions in the real world, the multi-second blindness that occurred at the end... I didn't want to present Bakuda a potential opportunity to accidentally kill me when I had momentarily crippled myself. That meant waiting until she was either mid-speech, or until she had already wasted her opening attack. Not too arduous, but knowing that I was in 'enemy territory' - it was something to think about, given how fast an explosion could hit me out of nowhere.

Not that I needed to worry about that right now, better to focus on what was right in front of me. And, come to think of it, I should make the most out of this pseudo-stampede while it was still around. Because while I doubted any of the NPCs would be able to help me in any real way, they were loud. Loud enough that my ash clone and I could run around rooftops, break window panes and kick open doors everywhere we went, without fear that Bakuda would identify it as something we were doing and decide to aggro. So that's exactly what I do, opening up pathways throughout the facility in the general direction the crowd was fleeing from - placing myself up on the roof for the final approach towards the gymnasium that appeared to be at the centre of the crisis.

I peek my shadowy head through the roof.

"-sy of my genius, and only now are you realising that actions have consequences-" Yep. Found her.

Now. Take it slow. The ash clone can scout out the surrounding area with the shadow state. I can kill it remotely by taking away the administrator powerset if it looks like it will get caught in a bad spot, so there wasn't much risk of it getting noticed. I doubted Bakuda had any real surveillance system in place, what little I knew about Cornell made it sound very much like a single Tinker building a bunch of bombs and immediately placing them around campus with no other real plan behind her. Hacking into the surveillance system was definitely a Tinker-y thing to do, but not something I expected from Bakuda specifically.

Not this Bakuda, anyway. She wasn't exactly performing at her full ability here. Whatever her issues were, it was all obviously quite personal and that was getting in the way of her judgement. Which was to my benefit - it kept her nice and distracted while I made a mental map of the room.

Three groups of hostages. One large batch of students, another of what I would guess are staff members - and then two particular people that had picked out from the group and were the core focus of Bakuda's ramblings.

And the bombs? I could only assume that the blocky devices with the ominous red lights on them were the explosives I needed to worry about - blocking every doorway with the mere threat of detonation.

This would be a lot easier if Bakuda wasn't aggro'd in real life. If I knew I had multiple free attempts and a full day of stalking her, I would just see what her immediate response is to confrontation. Go down there, tank one of the doorway bombs with my knight, ash clone or shadow state - and see if she just blows everything up or settles into a 'real' fight. The hole in the entrance would let the hostages slip out while I kept her distracted and all I would have to worry about would be damaging the buildings too much to trigger the fail conditions of the EVNT modifier.

But, at the same time, that could just fail me instantly. If her first response was to detonate her bombs, I'd instantly lose with little information gained. Multiple approaches, some of them guaranteed to failure - I just didn't know which ones.

I wait while my ash clone finishes circling the area. It locates two additional bombs. One outside, a second inside an empty lecture hall. Which probably meant that there were more. Makes sense. The bomb threat was supposed to be something that could take out the entire university, not a few small bombs that were barely more than grenades individually. There would be others around, stronger and better hidden. Even if I tried defusing them, I was likely to miss a few on the first pass - and I couldn't ignore the possibility of failing to defuse them at all, or Bakuda getting some kind of feedback that somebody was tampering with her devices.

Again, potential to instantly lose - and get no further to clearing the challenge.

Flip the script. What would get me further to clearing this? Rather than toying with every minor facet of the fail conditions, how did I get closer to winning? Naturally, I needed to fight Bakuda. Actually, considering it was a hostage situation - there might be a bit of leeway for 'not' fighting Bakuda and instead giving her absolutely everything she asks for - or otherwise neutralising enough of her arsenal that she just tries to flee instead. And if I wasn't as strong as I am right now, I might consider that as the best angle - doing my best to negotiate and defuse the situation directly or indirectly,

depending on if the sight of me turned her into a bloodthirsty maniac or not. But I'm pretty strong, and Bakuda is pretty weak. I think it's better to stick to my strengths in this case. Plus, the negotiations broke down in real life so it's not like I have a success story to build my approach off of, even if it ended bloodlessly in the end.

Dropping in from above has to be my best bet. She's not looking up, she pauses semi-frequently in her lectures to her audience, she isn't wearing any serious armour save for a welding mask. One good connection, and the fight would be over. The only real issue was that I wasn't allowed to kill her by the rules of the challenge, so no using Browbeat's power to turn my ambush into a lethal oneshot. Instead, I'd have to just neutralise her - get her away from the device in her hands that I could only assume was some kind of controller for her explosives - and the challenge would end once she conceded she had no way of escaping my grasp.

Clean. Simple. Easy to iterate on if anything went wrong. Not playing whack-a-mole with every bomb on campus, just attacking the source directly - knowing that the right attack would neatly sidestep the various issues of the scenario.

I phase through the roof, balancing myself on a supporting beam that lightly creaks under my weight. I hold myself steady, not panicking - I must be hard to see next to the glare of the lights next to me, and if she glanced up, I'd be even harder to see in my shadow state for a few seconds. No reaction.

"At the end of the day, you had a choice - to judge my work by its own merits, a fair, respectable grade worthy of my intellect, or to succumb to your biases. To reduce my score so that your classroom pets wouldn't be outshone. It seems so simple, when I phrase it like that - doesn't it? And yet, you chose wrong. Were you just jealous, perhaps? Or was there a deeper cause? A spot of racism? Something against the idea of a woman taking the top spot in your class? Perhaps you were offended at the idea that I understand the subject matter better than you, a supposed expert in the field-"

"Alice-" One of the hostages murmurs. "-we can fix this if you just-"

A beep emerges from the ground as she waves the gauntlet-like remote in her hand to cut them off. "You don't get to say my name anymore, professor. I'm tired of not getting the respect I'm owed in this place. And... fix? Look." She waves the remote behind her again, a chorus of beeping sounds emerging as the other hostages squirm in terror. "I've already fixed it. Finally, people have the right attitude. They beg for mercy. They plead for my attention and grace. They speak to me with the respect I'm due. I don't think I've had a single rude comment or slur aimed at me today - isn't that nice? All it took was a quick demonstration of how inferior they really were. And just think, if you'd kept control of your class better, enforced the rules fairly and equally - it wouldn't have needed to come to this. I'm not sure if I should be grateful or not."

Definitely loopy. Was this all about a bad grade? Honestly, I found it hard to even picture staying mad about something like that once I had superpowers. It's not like you'd need to apply for an office job anymore, traditional grades no longer had a meaning from the moment she triggered. Maybe there were some pre-existing grudges and ego issues at play, and downplaying somebody's trigger event was probably pretty poor of me when I just messaged Cauldron one day and woke up with powers a few days later, trauma-free. I should probably try to be more of an empath in that respect.

I miss the whispered undertones of what one teacher says. I don't miss the response. "I will blow you the fuck up!" She loses her cool again. "I press this button, and every single one of you will die - some painlessly, some will have the misfortune of living and be able to spend the last few seconds of their lives trying to locate their missing limbs and organs out from the slurry that used to be their friends."

...Ok. That might be enough of being an empath. I get the need to continually threaten the reality of the situation on the hostages, but... it was difficult to present this as a reasonable or justified response in any way. That was fine. I could handle crazy. In fact, with how my powers worked - I actually felt better about 'working' on crazy people. I was doing them, the world and myself a favour. Plus, with her obvious ego and need to prove her superiority - I get to repeat the Sophia experience again. Finding someone who thinks they're the top dog, and putting them in their rightful place on their knees.

That was a nice image. I think. I mean, her costume in the real world wasn't exactly the most form-fitting in the world and she's got a full-face mask on both in and out of the challenge, but I trust my power's track record with things like this. She'll definitely be hot, if she isn't already. And I get the feeling that she already is. The Crazy/Hot graph is a straight line nine times out of ten.

She circles below me again. I refrain from jumping as she paces side-to-side, launching into another rant interspersed with suspicious glances at the doors. Difficult to predict, my landing needed to be perfect - isolate that device of hers before she can even realise someone else is nearby. An attack faster than her reaction speed - it meant attacking that arm first, rather than trying to land in the shadow state and then wrestling it away from her. I wouldn't beat her thumb like that. If I could land on the arm as it was extended, or when her arm was relaxed at her side, so I could carry my momentum into ripping it away from her - even if only to get it out of her grip so that Clockblocker's power wouldn't consider it as being held-

I pause. Actually, come to think of it - I've literally just upgraded Clockblocker's power. I shouldn't just assume that all the restrictions are the same. I could safely guess that anything giving me a guaranteed lockdown of the target - and therefore a guaranteed victory - would still be restricted in some way, but I could easily imagine held items being included in some of the new leeway I should have around now. Assuming I wasn't buffed in some other way, I didn't feel any extra charges on that power but I couldn't rule it out.

I mentally mull the idea over, picturing myself using the power on the detonator-remote clasped in her hand as I crash down to earth. Clockblocker's power seems to shiver in response, itching to be used. That's a good sign.

I fall forward as Bakuda stands in front of the pair of teachers again. For a moment, I feel like her NPC speech is looped but actually it just seems like she just really can't get over this issue with her grades. Either way, she's halfway into a passionate rant about her 'towering intellect being maligned by incompetent fools' when I land on her - Vista's power momentarily used to adjust the direction of my fall for an optimal landing. One hand grasps hers a split-second before my face would hit the ground, and a quick swap from Clockblocker into the shadow state completes my opening move.

I stand, ready to lunge into an offensive grapple as Bakuda painfully wrenches her hand free of the timelocked device. A high-pitched whine emerges from multiple directions around us before I'm even out of the shadow state. Raised voices and shrill screams start to emerge from the hostages as they attempt to scramble away to other parts of the room, but neither Bakuda or I pay them any mind. Because, despite being attacked - Bakuda wasn't paying any attention to me right now. Instead, she was desperately attempting to interact with the remote I'd just frozen. "Undo this!" She snaps at me.

The whining noises subtly increases in pitch, a slow beeping pattern emerging and speeding up as every second passes.

I breathe in through my teeth. "I think I get the issue, bombs are set to explode if they don't get a signal from that thing every now and then?"

"Obviously! I mentioned that very clearly in my initial speech, as if I wouldn't have insurance against some idiotic Cape just trying to take a shot at me! If my tech loses connection, or if I stop resetting the timer - I blow this place sky high." She ineffectually stabs at a few more buttons. "So now that you get it, undo this before every single one of us dies here!"

"Most of us. I'll live, I think." Probably. I couldn't be sure, knowing the more Tinker-y bombs she was capable of - but this was probably just a large explosion. I could handle that, probably. Find a wall to hide behind, don't let the roof fall on my head without the shadow state up. Browbeat's power may or may not tank it, but I'd rather not test it against shrapnel or shockwaves like that - I needed the surface area to diffuse hits. Blunt force was the speciality there. Doesn't matter either way, I definitely wouldn't be passing the challenge whether I lived or died.

"What?" She shakes her head. "You don't understand, if I don't enter the code within the next... fifty seconds, this place is going to become a smoking crater marking one of the greatest disasters in American history and it will be entirely your fault."

I raise my hands in the air. "Alright, I'll admit I was a bit reckless on this one - just jumping in like this. But I think the distribution of blame is still, 90-10 towards you. You're the terrorist here, I'm the good Samaritan. There's precedent for this. I gave it an honest try, an unknown Tinkertech interaction caused things to go sideways-"

"Shut your stupid mouth and turn your power off before we all blow up!" She half-screams at me.

Rude. I wave a hand at nothing. "I can't." I shrug. "It's stuck like that for... anywhere between twenty-seven seconds and five-minutes twenty." She stares at me. I shuffle uncomfortably for a moment. "I mean, if I'm being honest - those are just the highest and lowest numbers I've recorded. Actually, it clusters together in the two-three minute range for most tests, something like eighty percent of my tests ended around then - probably pretty reasonable to assume that it's got another... ninety seconds at least before it comes unstuck."

"We're all going to die here." She talks to the air numbly. "Killed by a monkey? Me?"

I ignore that last comment.

"You could have thought about that before all of-" I make an encompassing gesture. "-this. Feels like a pretty natural progression on from leaving a bunch of overpowered bombs around."

"Oh really? I think it was all going fine until some incompetent moron fucked it up for everyone!" She jabs a finger at me. "And you have the gall to sit there and look offended? You did this. You killed me. You killed yourself. You killed these idiots-" A vague gesture behind her.

"I get it, I get it! I just wanted to fight, was that so wrong?" I shake my head to cut off her response. "Okay. Hear me out." The beeping increases in intensity. "Fine, I lied. I actually can manipulate the device when it's like that, how do I defuse it?"

"Twist the thumb clockwise until it detaches, hold down the button - then use the keypad. 03270717."

"And that defuses all the bombs? Or just turns off the part where they explode on their own?"

"The former part, no. There's no need to defuse all of them, just the ones that will kill me - the blood of everyone outside this building will still be on your hands, but I can't do anything about that. The latter, obviously not. Why would I leave such an obvious weakness in my master plan? As if I'd allow myself to be defeated by a single hacked radio signal and a lucky Thinker. It will just signal them to fall back onto alternative triggers that I programmed ahead of time, just to make sure the job was completed properly no matter what. A defuse option... absolutely not. Letting a single Master defeat me? No." She shakes her head. "Not that it matters, you can at least have faith that I will survive - and I'll allow you to live by staying near me. Hurry up and do it before we all-"

"I actually lied. Can't do it." I confess. "Sorry, just fishing for information."

A beat of silence stretches between us. It doesn't last long.

"You absolute fucking-" I mentally tune out the torrent of abuse and insults that spills from her mouth the moment it starts.

A bit annoying, but maybe just a sign that Clockblocker's power wasn't enough to instantly win here. The code didn't seem too complex, but-

"-if I have to die, I'll at least have the pleasure of watching the person who killed me go straight to hell first!" That drags my attention back to the situation at hand. She's made some healthy distance from me, and is fixed in a triumphant posture partially ruined by some very deliberate twitches of different parts of her body. If I hadn't heard her previous sentence and deduced that she intended to kill me with this, I'd have asked if she was having a stroke of some kind.

Twitch. Twitch. Shuffle. Twitch.

I open my mouth. "I-"

FAILURE​

I blink. My newly incorporeal body remains exactly where I just was, an oversized scorch mark and some falling 'debris' are the only signs that my physical body was there in the first place.

Ouch. But also, fine. Three lessons learned in addition to the facts I knew about her gauntlet-remote: First, she has a backup control somewhere under her costume - not a single device or something easily manipulated in her mask, but something that requires the movement of certain limbs to control. Doubtless a way for her to ensure that she isn't neutralised by a single lucky attack.

Secondly, that took a long time for her to arm and detonate. Or, perhaps just to highlight and select the bomb she wanted to explode? Nobody else had detonated yet when she blew me up, so there were extra bombs that weren't using the same system as the bombs intended to destroy the campus. This was personal, targeted and didn't seem to be fired at me - I had already been standing on it. At a guess, a miniature minefield laid out explicitly for a confrontation with the heroes.

Three, I couldn't react with the shadow state. Aside from her overly-dramatic speech, there hadn't been any cue that I was about to die - no sound or sensation that I could use to time my shadow state defensively. The only thing I could do in response was either to shadow state early and hope she mistimed things or stay so close to her that she couldn't hit me without hitting herself.

Which was doable. I just had to reconcile it all with the fact that she might just be able to blow the entire place up even without her primary remote. I need a way to stop her from doing that. Or, to stop her from wanting to do that? I'll admit, diplomacy seemed a little more on the cards than I'd initially thought from her ranting. I'd expected her to delight in the fact that hundreds were going to die, but she'd actually seemed rather irate about her hand being 'forced' - not just the part where she was one of those hundreds. Was she, perhaps, just a poser? Crying out for attention from the closest dashing hero?

I could see it. She wouldn't admit it, naturally - so making sure that her first response couldn't be 'kill everyone' and making it to the stage where I get to start a dialogue with her would have to be my priority for round two.

But before then... my priority had to be making it to round two. With a gesture, space pinches together - my ash clone surging forward to face the well-armed Tinker. This shouldn't be a difficult fight. It was all the extra details that I had to worry about. As much as I didn't have to worry about consequences aside from the mission rules in my challenges, if I pushed her hard enough that she blew up the entire building and killed Armsmaster and half the Wards - my reputation would never recover and I would find that all of the leniency with the law that I'd earned up to this point would vanish. Prison or probation in the Wards, no other options. No winning too hard, no making any mistakes against bomb Tinker, don't kill her because a dead-mans-switch is the most obvious, cliche thing for her speciality to suggest - it's easy to see why approaching this would be difficult for the heroes.

I was actually the best-suited in the entire Bay to handle this woman. All I had to do was keep her in the back foot, keep her in my sight... and before long, she'd be putty in my hands no matter how real her threats were originally.

A pair of drones screech towards me. I dip through the floor in my shadow state before they reach my just as Bakuda disintegrates my ash clone, the series of simultaneous explosions momentarily concealing us both from each other's line of sight. By the time it clears, I've settled on the floor below her - snatching up a set of napkins from a nearby table. They aren't quite large enough for my preferred missiles, but at least the shape is well-suited for turning into a ball. I resummon my ash clone, hand it Parian's power and the 'ammunition' and leave it to help manage any more drones that come in my direction.

I spare a glance down at the hall. No Wards in sight. Was that a good thing, or a bad one? Armsmaster was still frozen, so they hadn't done everything they'd hoped for right away - but I didn't even know for sure if that was possible to free him, and if it was, then I expected the Tinkertech involved to be complex enough to require some serious analysis. It doesn't really matter all that much, keeping Bakuda busy aligns with both my personal goals and the 'heroic' goals that my persona should have.

A drone falls from the sky, a glancing blow from my clone's Parian-infused missile taking out one wing and sending it into a spiral towards the ground floor. As for me? I was heading back up. I'd initially just intended to wait for every single shadow state to come back before trying to jump up to the next floor - but I didn't even need a long glide thanks to Vista's upgrade. Since my last boost, it didn't only have the expanded versatility, but it also seemed to 'snap back' faster when I no longer needed it. The pinched space I'd used to help my clone attack just a few moments ago was already undone. I attempt to warp the entire looking area above me down to my level, noting an unusual sense of resistance as I do so - clearly the Manton limit at play, something I'd never encountered with the original version I owned purely because that version literally only worked on air. The entire space had to be empty, so it was never really an issue.

I pull down only one side instead, settling for a convenient, if overly steep, ramp up to the floor above. One shadow state, or one punch-through the stretched-out floor with Browbeat's powerset - that's all I would need for a straight route to Bakuda.

And for Bakuda to have a straight shot at me. As much as part of me wanted to test my reflexes and defensive options, as much as I had so, so much confidence in myself against what seemed to be just a fancy grenade launcher and some defensive drones... I've died, so, so many times in so many painful ways because I didn't think I needed every advantage available. Because I overestimated myself, or underestimated my enemy. Because I thought that my own skills and power were enough for the task at hand, and didn't give myself enough room to recover when something went wrong.

Right now, Bakuda was probably feeling pretty good. She knows I'm wary of her real Tinkertech explosives, she's deterred me from melee - she's in a nice, defensive position with limited approaches, more of her own drones undoubtedly coming in and the presumed arrival of Lung and Oni Lee was likely just a few minutes away in the worst case scenario. For someone who liked talking about the relative difference in IQ between her and everyone else, and all the talk about being a genius... I could see the train of thought as if I was a literal mind reader. It's a familiar one.

Because I get it. I know that confidence she has in herself and her abilities. The self-assurance that comes from knowing that you've thought about how to win, how everything is going according to plan and how all of these other Capes are just brute-forcing everything while flailing in the webs of your plan. I really, really get it. More than anyone else. The feeling that you only lose because you're unlucky, or that it's rigged - and when you win, it's because you were better. Smarter. More deserving. That attitude is understandable, but a weakness all the same. A sign that she hasn't failed often enough. Hasn't felt the consequences of a lack of respect for her opponent. Hasn't had the raw combat experience she needs to claw for every advantage. Hasn't had her own weaknesses and tendencies highlighted and abused repeatedly.

That's why using Vista's power like that wasn't about me going up the ramp. It was about about her having to monitor two potential paths that I could approach from, it was about her eyes-in-the-sky being momentarily blinded by my clone until she could pull more of her drones in. It was about the fact that it's simple human nature to see the sudden creation of a new path and think that's the direction the attack is coming from. Like the police breaking down your front door, you'd never expect the first cop to crawl out from under your bed. Similarly, I don't give Bakuda the chance to consider my 'known' powers and the way I could use them. I don't give her time to think about why or how I'd survived her explosions so far and what that might mean.

Maybe she was too arrogant to care about anything other than the heavy hitters with the flashy powers, because as my elongated jump expires - two charges of the shadow state burned to sustain my upwards-momentum through the floor - my fist is already buried in the side of her torso. Brute-enhanced strength earns me an audible crack as something in her costume buckles under the blow, with the Tinker finding herself knocked away like a bowling pin - rolling across the ground a few times as she scrapes to a halt in an indignant heap.

I let her get up. If this was a challenge, I could have tried choking her out from that position. Thrown her backwards off of the balcony. Settled into a comfortable grappling position. Broken a limb. Done pretty much anything except knock her away.

But, again. Winning too quickly and easily had complications here. Dragging the fight out was relatively normal for Cape battles, better for the 'hostage situation', helped distract her from anything the Wards were doing elsewhere in the building and - most importantly of all - let me keep line-of-sight on her for my challenges. If I got her into a position where she didn't believe escape was possible - or that rescue wasn't coming - who was to say that she wouldn't act on her previous threat and blow us all up at once?

No, playing it slow. Dragging it out, enjoying myself - that was the best action I could take right now.

"Cheap shot-" She growls, voice heavily filtered by the mask. "-you won't get a chance like that again."

I grin, spreading my arms out wide. "Don't go making a mistake now. That was just a little warning shot from me, after you brushed me off earlier as some random small fry. I almost got a little angry, seeing some baby Tinker in their first real Cape fight - thinking that they deserved to skip past me like I was a level one mook."

She scoffs. "You think I'm wrong? Look down there at your precious Armsmaster, stuck as a spectator. You might not like it, but I am the new best Tinker in the Bay. The world, even. And I'm being modest with that."

I can't help the laugh that escapes me. "That's funny."

"Laugh all you want, it doesn't change reality." Another of her drones tumbles out of the sky behind me, not mobile enough to dodge my ash clone's Parian-based anti-air fire. Very effective, but at some point I'd need it to relocate to get access to more fabric. Tablecloths, curtains, napkins - anything would do, there was plenty around. But there were plenty of drones too, and she was trying to be sneakier with them now.

"The reality that you hit Armsmaster at his weakest with a sneak attack, cowered up here to fight the heroes remotely and arm a few gang members to do all the real fighting for you?" I taunt. "Nobody is going to respect that. The fact that you're proud of it is a little embarrassing, honestly." I skip to the side with Vista's power as a projectile is fired in my direction from her gauntlet. Easy to dodge, but when dealing with explosives it was better to make more distance. "The ABB might as well have ordered some fresh supplies from the latest rookie to join Toybox and been just as well off!"

"Small fry to deal with small fry, what of it? Is it my fault that handing out a few unwanted failures from my collection turns a few ABB grunts into powerhouses strong enough to terrify the Protectorate?" She sneers. "And it's perfectly natural to reserve my talents for someone actually worthy of facing them. I'd hoped that might be Armsmaster, but in the battle between Tinkers - he failed at the first hurdle. A disappointment - but not a surprising one."

The smile partially falls from my face at that. I'm trying to be fair, anyone would be proud of sneaking anything by Armsmaster like she had... but I'm not sure I appreciated the takeaways she was trying to make here. If Newter poked Lung in his sleep and knocked him out, we wouldn't start calling him the new strongest in the Bay - and certainly wouldn't run around trying to reinvent history concerning Lung's personal strength. Why did we have to do that here? Sure, I'm biased - I'll admit that much. But that doesn't mean that I'm wrong. Armsmaster packs this chick up ten times out of ten if you take out the booby-trapped venue.

After a moment of realisation, she bounds away from it - looking incredibly relieved. "I- um." All three of us look over to Tattletale, Bitch and-

-and Bakuda, who is held not-so-gently inside Angelica's jaws.

I surreptitiously pinch space between us and them so I can hear the conversation better. "-isn't a Master like you'd know it, she actually just empowers them. And when she isn't around, like when she gets knocked out or you try your luck? The dogs stay empowered until it would have expired. And in the meantime? They do whatever they like. Whatever seems natural to them. Now, I've seen that dog in action - and she is vicious at heart-"

"No she isn't." Bitch interjects. The conversation stalls for a moment as both Tattletale and Bakuda turn to her. "She's a good girl." Bitch doesn't seem to care about the stares she gets from either of them.

"...Thank you, Bitch. I'll take the talking from here." Tattletale continues. "As I was saying, the dogs do whatever they want - and in this case, she's just itching to bite down on this wriggling thing in her mouth. The only reason she isn't, is because of Bitch here. If she wasn't here? Or if she gave the order? You never get your vengeance. You never get your name written down in the history books. You never get the respect you think you deserve. Why? Because all you'll be is the Cape that PHO makes dog-food jokes about when they remember that one Tinker who killed herself right on her debut. So. Next collar, if you would." She taps at her own. "How about-"

"Brutus and Judas next." Bitch adds in. "Take them off first."

Tattletale looks aggrieved, but reluctantly nods - then elaborates at Bakuda's confused expression. "The two dogs that were with us."

"As if I care about those disgusting mutts anyway." Bakuda hisses. "I-" Angelica growls in warning, and Bakuda falls silent again. "There, that should be it. Even if I can't see the little terrors right now."

A cracking noise at the entrance draws the attention of the entire room. A set of flaming claws peels away a section of the wall like wet paper, widening a new entrance more and more with every motion. Lung. Another shockwave momentarily knocks him away, Triumph's power in action - but he was just a distraction, and Lung knew it. If Dauntless really had been taken out, then the heroes reportedly delaying him outside were nothing but mosquitoes.

I slide my eyes to the stage. Kid Win, we could really use Armsmaster right now. If you could hurry up with that, that would be great.

Fuck it. Let's sneak the challenges in against those two, then think about the action plan here. This wasn't the low-stakes night out I'd been hoping for, the Undersiders alone I could be confident that things wouldn't go too badly wrong with my power not conspiring to turn every lost fight into a lethal defeat. The ABB? I couldn't say the same.

"Challenge." I whisper at Bakuda.

What haven't I tried yet here? "Attention Bakuda!" I call out at a distance. "I've been sent to negotiate, but I'm too afraid of your incredible Tinkertech to come inside uninvited! Can we talk?"

"This isn't a negotiation!" Bakuda returns. "This, is a demonstration. A statement. A declaration. Today, is the day of judgement. But, if you'd like to talk - you may come inside. But if you try anything at all, then the entire facility will look like this!"

My eyes widen. "Wait-"

Click.

Boom.

FAILURE​

I'm going to strangle this bitch. I glance at Tattletale. Both of them. Where do they get off having challenges that don't respond well to direct combat ability? That's the entire point of the power! That's what I do! "Challenge."

What did I even want to try against Tattletale? I gained some knowledge last time, but I wouldn't say I was particularly close to a win either. The issue was that standing up to any amount of scrutiny was a tough ask, and I didn't know exactly what inconsistency her power was initially picking up on to pick me out for a more advanced check.

How did I fix that? Keep trying disguises until I find the perfect one by blind luck? No. Hell no. I've got to push at the limits of the challenge. No combat? Don't get spotted? Fine. But what did that really mean?

My ash clone lands on the ground, in plain view of Tattletale. A few surrounding NPCs react curiously, and the girl herself is no different - a wary look appearing on her face- Reset.

She looked right at me. Awkward. Should find a better hiding spot. Or look through my ash clones eyes next time. Point proven though, I'm not forbidden to use powers at all. I didn't fail the moment she saw my clone, even though she started looking for me afterwards - that meant that I could do things. Affect the scenario in certain ways.

Let's experiment again, with me hidden properly this time. My ash clone walks in front of her, the girl sending it a wary look and crossing the street to avoid it. The clone follows. Tattletale reaches into her pocket and- Reset.

Another lesson learned. I think that was the 'combat' failure condition. I need to remember, it's not necessarily me starting a fight - but it could also be her realising that my clone is targeting her specifically, and realising she's in a fight. I should probably assume the same response will happen if I just 'coincidentally' walk the clone near her too many times. I could use it as a minor distraction, but it obviously stands out - she makes a concerted effort to avoid it and seems to be scanning the area around her with far more than her usual intensity. Looking for the Master, probably.

Third and final attempt... what can I do with this? An indirect attack? No, she'd realise she was being targeted and I'd fail that way. A distraction? Maybe. But it would need to be a hell of a distraction. Something that lasted a while, to give me the time I needed to fill the progress bar - otherwise, she'd note the distraction, identify it for what it was, and then leave the area and go somewhere safer where she could verify everyone around in-depth.

What if she couldn't do that? What if there wasn't anywhere safer? What if she simply couldn't verify that everyone around her was who they appeared to be? The aim wasn't to beat her power at it's best, but to overwhelm it. Give it too much to look at. Overstimulation. I could use the crowds. I could even attack them. Cut off certain streets, create some obstacles. Herding. Create some panic, condense people into a smaller space - and she wouldn't be able to check everyone. Hell, if I made enough of a crush - she wouldn't even be able to move to see everyone.

Perfect.

I send my ash clone off to form the knight. A larger one than usual. Step one would be destroying a few cars and creating a blockade at the main street. I'd need to trap everyone in, then slowly box them together.

It takes time, but the knight does good work. I have to make a few examples of the citizens that attempt to just scramble over the blockade of cars and debris, but everyone gets the point eventually. "Villain attack, everybody panic! Run that way!" I think the voice cues help. But maybe the knight crashing into another store half its size is the real reason people listen to my directions.

Now then. Second problem. I only had one administrator. That meant, one knight, or the ability to track one bug - and with it, Tattletale - no matter where it was.

Which was to say, I didn't know where Tattletale was right now. Oh, I had a vague idea of the area - but, being totally honest, she could have moved anywhere by now. I could have started the attack closer to her, but considering the entire operation revolving around her challenge-self not realising that she was the target - I didn't want to test how suspicious she would feel about a Cape attack happening almost right on top of her, to say nothing of the fact that I would instantly lose if she pulled a gun or knife on raw instinct.

For now, I just walk in the crowd - pushing past bodies, ignoring the screaming. 0%. 0%. 0%. Should be around here somewhere, if she kept to her original route...

1%. There. I was in range. Barely. 2%. 6%. 10%. The crowd keeps moving. Which direction? 19%. I maintain the same path, only to note the bar shrinking again. 11%. 4%. Back to 0%. That meant that she was somewhere behind me, perhaps off to either side. I turn and fight my way through the crowd surging past me- Reset.

FAILURE​

I glower at the screen. Then soften my expression. No, can't be mad. It was a good strategy. I proved that a lot of things worked there. At the end, she must have been looking at me somehow - I made myself stand out, the only guy trying to head towards the attack. Perhaps she had a good vantage point, or just heard the complaints of the crowd in my way and looked over - but either way, it did imply that at some point, I'd walked past her and she hadn't noticed. Good strategy. A winning strategy. All I was missing was the knowledge of her exact position. I've proven that, just like in real life right now, she can have too many things to look into to give them all the time they need.

Next time, with three more chances? I'll win. Easily.

And then, I'm pretty sure, I'm going to get hit with the same challenge but with some loopholes closed. I know what my power is like. I'm ready for it.

Anyway. Where was I? Right. Collars. I guess they're doing fine, I suppose I'll leave them to it? It really did grate that Tattletale had my motives pinned down that easily, but it was all just common sense at the end of the day. In fact, I'd argue that the best thing for the heroes to do here was allow the 'negotiation' to happen - then swoop in to take possession of both Bakuda and the Undersiders all at once. Armsmaster would be free in literally seconds if Kid Win could hurry up and finish doing his thing - and then it's just Lung, and presumably Oni Lee.

Oni Lee, who hasn't come in here ahead of Lung, to save Bakuda? Oni Lee, who hadn't just decided to finish off the Undersiders at the end of their 'employment'? Oni Lee, I had yet to actually see at all during all of this?

No, that didn't sound like him at all.

My eyes slide to Grue's cloud. Grue and Regent, hiding together. Neither of them had revealed themselves at the same time. Why? Regent didn't like fighting in the darkness in the bank challenge, why start now?

Because he had to. Because, if that darkness wasn't there - people would see the truth of what was going on. Looking at their team, both Regent and Grue could 'restrain' Oni Lee. But Grue's power was the only one that people knew could do that, Regent was still lowballing himself in public. So they were carrying around Oni Lee within the cloud rather than splitting up. Tattletale had implied that I'd have to defend them from Lung when he comes in, why? Because they completed the 'trade' for their teammate, then Regent had simply walked Oni Lee back into range of the cloud as a bargaining chip when the collars hadn't been removed right away.

This is a clusterfuck. I think I'd actually prefer it if the Undersiders were just straight-up on the ABB's side, but instead there's this nasty little web of threats, insurance policies and different motives. Think. Lung will come in here for both Bakuda and Oni Lee - the Undersiders are keeping Oni Lee as a threat or a trade to any party that might stop them from leaving. They don't even have to try and fight, if Lung reaches them, they hand over both Oni Lee and Bakuda without resistance and leave the heroes to handle the mess of a full-power ABB. Oni Lee and Lung, in open conflict with the Wards? I didn't like that idea. That sounded messy. Oni Lee had tried to slit my throat on sight the first time I met him, and Taylor had narrowly avoided eating a grenade that night too. I wouldn't bet on him being any nicer with the Wards, there were precious few combat videos between the Wards and the ABB and I'm pretty sure that was a deliberate choice by the PRT to keep them away.

And the only way I had to stop it was to either kill Oni Lee outright, or obediently stop Lung from reaching the Undersiders at all.

Which proved Tattletale right. Oh, there were some other alternatives as well, I could take down all of the Undersiders and keep Oni Lee down too - but that didn't help if Lung was going to rampage around in here anyway and potentially kill anyone who couldn't pull themselves out of harms way. Best case scenario, Lung limps away - Oni Lee back in prison with Bakuda, Undersiders captured. But that was the heroes best case. Mine? No. That sucked for me. Oni Lee would be in the Birdcage as an absolute guarantee after this mess, it was already a surprise they hadn't fast-tracked him. The Undersiders would get sent across the country and I wouldn't get any more of their powers, not to mention the enmity of Tattletale for going against her 'brilliant' plan.

No, Tattletale most certainly understood my motives here. Which meant that she'd spent a little time researching me already.

On the plus side, she at least seemed to think I'd be a significant speedbump against Lung if I factored into her plans here at all.

On the down side, she was a poor enough judge of such things that she'd gotten her entire group captured after presumably picking a fight with Lung deliberately rather than skipping town.

Well. Fuck. But, I'm not entirely unprepared for this. I've been expecting a Lung to jump through the nearest wall on every patrol I've been on for the last week, even with Taylor around - I've been on edge. I step forward as Lung fully enters the room and looks around. Brutus and Judas immediately abandon their fights and race towards Bitch. Bad experience there, I'd guess?

Browbeat hesitates for a moment as her opponent leaves, then races to grab the red clump of flesh that was once identifiable as her teammate. "Oh my god, Aegis - are you okay? No, what am I saying, of course you aren't okay. I-I know some first aid-"

"I'm fine." Something that is distinctly not a mouth voices his response. "Get away from Lung, he's not someone you can handle - I'll hold him off until more heroes arrive."

"Maybe say that when you've got four working limbs again." I call out drily, my eyes fixed on Lung. "Browbeat, go make sure Gallant hasn't been beaten to a pulp yet. Aegis, just back off for the moment and heal up until you can contribute. Vista, support me, but don't get too close."

"You can't fight Lung!" Aegis objects. Still with that gross pseudo-mouth of his. Creepy dude, stop. "We need to pull back-"

"It's fine. We've only got to hold out until Armsmaster is free, right? And, I'm pretty sure that Grue over there is hiding Oni Lee - so if we let Lung go past us, we're just going to be dealing with both of them instead of just one. And you can't exactly run and leave Clockblocker and Kid Win behind, can you?" To be honest, the reasoning doesn't matter at this point. Honestly, I wanted to fight. Without my power favouring the enemy, just how well did we match up? I wanted to try my luck. I wanted the fight. Spitfire caught me off guard, but I'd been annoyed at myself for taking a fight against someone with completely unknown capabilities without checking their challenge first. I'd assumed she was at roughly the same level as the relatively-weak Undersiders. But I wasn't mad about going for the fight.

This is what being a Cape is about. This is what being a hero is about.

I press a button on my costume. The sole item of Tinkertech in my costume pulses, then glows steadily. A moment later, my costume gets a bulky addition to it - my teleporter, folded down with the weight properly distributed compared to the last version. The targeting remote settles around my wrist with a click. I trigger it, number one - the selection right at the top, ready to be teleported in at a moment's notice. The Wards step away as a crate appears next to me. Materials. The perfect amount for one specific design.

Paste. I burn a single shadow state charge to get inside the exoframe faster, then stand - bringing my right hand up, the Mecha-sword rising with it. It was tough to manipulate before, it was designed to be wielded by a robot and an appropriate power source after all. But with Browbeat's power fully active and the exoframe assisting... it felt almost light in my hands.

I aim a tight grin at Lung as he leisurely paces forward, the ground shaking with every step as the dragon-man makes his presence known - a wall of unpleasant heat already threatening to scorch me through my costume. Game on.

Last steps. I apply Othala's power to Vista to mulligan reflexes for something more useful, then summon my ash clone - finally back from it's long cooldown. I assign it Mush's power, and have it start gathering the knight immediately. Shouldn't take long, with the building in this state already - it was a shame I couldn't start it earlier, Lung will reach me long before-

I blink as Lung's draconic visage doesn't seem to be approaching that quickly at all, despite motions that look somewhat hurried to me. He's covering too little ground with every step. I look at Vista, who's staring intently in that direction and biting her lip. "Thanks." I mutter. Her lips quirk upwards, but she doesn't look away.

Anything else that might help? I'd like to apply Skidmark's power to the sword to give myself extra thrust, but it fades away when it isn't my active power and I'd like to stick to cycling between Browbeat, Glory Girl, Echo and Vista in this fight. "Hey, Spitfire." She straightens at my callout. "Can you blast my knight over there with your power? Make it last as long as you can, if that's alright." I'm not testing my version in real life, and her one was undoubtedly more powerful anyway.

Spitfire hesitates, glancing over to her companions before nodding. "Sure?"

The burning figure settles into place a small distance away from me. Just what we needed, more heat. But I'd bet that it won't be pleasant to Lung either. I point the Mecha-blade at him as he draws closer. In return, he emits a repeating, rough barking sound that I eventually realise is something close to his laughter.

"Careful." I take another step forward, and my burning knight mirrors my action. "If you underestimate me too much-"

The Mecha-blade hums through the exoframe. With this iteration. Leet's quirk activation chance had increased. 4.8% chance of activating the reverse swing every time I make an assisted attack. 95.2% chance of normal function. The normal attacks alone would be a threat to Lung. The superpowered spin attack... well. I'd have to stick to angles that wouldn't direct something lethal to every other occupant of the room. As for Lung...

I finish my warning to the strongest Cape in the Bay.

"-you might just die."

--
