Interlude - Gallant:

Gallant was sure that some cosmic god was having a laugh at his expense today - one problem would crop up, he'd idly wish it to be resolved and he'd get his wish in a way worse than ever dreamed. Over and over and over.

It had all started innocently enough. Vicky threatening to drag him shopping for swimsuits? Any guy would think they would be lucky to go on such an adventure, but he knew it was a trap by now. That was one date that always ended badly, always ended up with the wrong thing said, the wrong assurance given, not enough compliments, too many compliments, dangerous questions asking him about his opinion on the models lining the shop walls, posters and magazines, expressing interest, not expressing interest - there weren't any right answers there either. He'd prayed for an excuse.

He'd gotten one. Speech duty for a press event, another friendly face in the Wards showing support to their newest teammate.

Fine. He could do that. Smile. Look pretty for the cameras. The usual. It wasn't really the excuse he was looking for, rather than spending an hour ogling Vicky, spending another hour apologising for whatever argument they'd had and the remaining time hanging around with his still-fuming girlfriend - his entire evening was now block-booked out by an event with absolutely no enjoyment to be found anywhere. It was worse. It was definitely worse. Alas, he'd accepted the request before asking about the full details of the event, and it was technically for the benefit of his new teammate anyway so it was hard to find another excuse... but, still. Was it so wrong to want a bit of excitement in his schedule?

Yes, yes it was wrong. But he'd gotten exactly what he'd asked for anyway. He'd been caught outside when the ABB attacked, not even in his costume yet - he hadn't been due to make an appearance until later in the evening anyway, he'd figured that he wouldn't be missed. Well. He hadn't been missed, except it might have been better if they had kept him closer to hand. Things weren't clear on how exactly things had gone down at the moment of the attack, but he can't rule out the possibility that an emotion-sensor and a Blaster could have done something to disrupt whatever attack had happened on stage to freeze Armsmaster and his two teammates in time.

Sitting outside, near-powerless to help, no costume - just scrambling to get away from the ABB roadblocks and panicking civilians so that he could get a clear line to the PRT - he'd felt useless enough then. Only to find out that the Empire was attacking halfway across the city, and his girlfriend was already there - recklessly wading into the violence like she always does. That only redoubled the frustration. Two places where he wanted to be, to make a difference - and he wasn't achieving a thing at either of them.

Even Shadow Stalker was doing more than he was, and she was just sitting on console duty. Absolutely livid that they weren't authorising her to leave and join the rest of the Wards on account of the danger travelling through the city - but she was still contributing as much as she could, biting commentary aside. He wanted to do something to help the heroes out too.

Again, he'd gotten his wish. The hostage situation, after some panic, was eventually deemed to be the work of one new Tinker and some accompanying goons. Lung was confirmed elsewhere, so the Wards were deployed on what should be a simple mission: Sneak into the building when the Tinker wasn't looking, break out all the hostages, leave. No combat, unless the Tinker was exposing themselves or looking vulnerable. As a bonus, his costume was in there - and unless the PRT could spare a van to do a supply run back to HQ, that was the only way he was going to get some real protection in this situation. His only concern was how to approach this heavily-fortified building that seemed to be covered in traps and patrolling drones, any reinforcements that the heroes could spare would be valuable here - though of course, he understands that the Empire and Lung are the main threats.

But the devil laughs, because his unspoken wish was heard once more. They do get reinforcements. Velocity was greatly appreciated, Triumph was in the area too. He was grateful for their presence. What he wasn't grateful for, was the other arrival. Void Cowboy.

Now, he didn't hate the vigilante. Not really. There was, admittedly, an instinctive dislike there - someone with a reputation for excessive violence, someone who hadn't run to join the heroes the moment they had powers and, of course, the fact that he was a power copier.

He's sure he isn't the only one to have all kinds of feelings about that last one, even if his feelings on it aren't quite the same as his teammates. They would be annoyed that their powers were being copied by someone who didn't go through their trigger event, but he was a bit different in that he didn't have a trigger event. But, he did have to live with the constant knowledge that his powers were bought - and that fact alone would be enough to upend his friendships if it came out at the wrong time. The fact that someone had the potential to just scoop up his power by pure proximity, looking to become an improved version of Gallant without a shred of the guilt, shame and anxiety that came from the origin of his powers? Sure. He had feelings about it too. He wasn't sure he really had the right to have those feelings, but he had them all the same.

But he's a professional. He can put mild distaste and discomfort aside and work with a neutral party against the villains. He's not that petty. He may have been more than happy to follow the advice of avoiding the vigilante and rerouting patrols away from areas where he'd been seen - just to mitigate the chance of having his powers copied - but none of that mattered now. This was important. Lives were at risk. This was a chance to see Void Cowboy's true nature for himself, overcome his instinctive bias and see what the truth of the vigilante was.

And once again, the monkey's paw had curled.

Because Void Cowboy wasn't a hero.

Maybe that was too dramatic, but he wouldn't say he was wrong. Void Cowboy wasn't a plucky young teenager too rebellious to bow to authority. He was just dangerous - it was obvious to him within moments of interacting with him for the first time. It had started out fine. The emotional aura around the younger teen when he was talking with Velocity had been chaotic, spiking from greed and excitement to cool contempt and anticipation as the hero discussed the situation. That alone wasn't a cause of alarm, wandering thoughts could do a lot to a mental state - Gallant knew that. The flicker of awe and enthusiasm at the sight of the Wards leaving the van and coming into his view was something more standard, and for a moment, Gallant had been content to relax at the additional help they'd received. Everything was standard here. The occasional flicker of other emotions was normal, not too different from his teammates own anxious-yet-excited state.

Until, in an innocuous part of an otherwise pleasant conversation - Void Cowboy had happened to glance at him, and everything changed. The jumpy, flickering emotions resolved into a tidal wave of bloodlust, a conflagration of something close to rage and decisiveness - that perfect combination that he'd relied on for years as the signal that somebody was about to attack. It had never failed him. The pseudo-precognition of knowing someone had mentally prepared themselves for violence, the murky colours of anticipation transforming into conviction, excitement and decisiveness... he trusted it with his life.

So, still not understanding exactly what had triggered the fight - Gallant had sprung into a defensive posture. As nothing happened.

Absolutely nothing. In fact, he hasn't even brought his arms fully up before the emotions that concerned him were just gone. Not fading away and replaced by others as a new train of thought dislodges them, but literally gone between one blink and the next as if abruptly deleted. Replaced entirely by what he would have to describe as 'smug triumph'.

And then, within seconds of that, it happens again - the bloodlust returns, except it doesn't vanish entirely this time. This time, the angry dark reds of sullen anger, the purple-green of disappointment plus the orange of spite were the dominant emotions - added to the thrumming pulse of murky red that indicated a desire for violence was still there underneath it all.

As he continues holding the conversation without so much as a tensed muscle or stutter in his speech. If not for the roller-coaster of emotions he was witnessing - there would be nothing to say that Void Cowboy was anything other than what he seemed, a helpful, if somewhat misguided hero looking to do his best for the city. He was the only one who could see underneath the mask. Who could see... whatever this was.

By the time he realises that, to everyone else, there isn't any reason to be alarmed - he's already made a bit of a scene. The lances of amusement and confusion lancing through his teammates auras were frustrating enough, presumably thinking that he had gotten jumpy over a movement in the shadows or a distant explosion. But he could live with that, he could explain things later. That isn't what annoys him. What annoys him is the real icing on the cake: The absolute tidal wave of derision and contempt from Void Cowboy as Gallant reluctantly settles back into a more neutral posture.

Gallant isn't going to challenge him on it. Not now. This part of his power is one of the best-kept secrets of the Wards, an edge he's reluctant to let go of - and right now, that kind of edge is what might be needed to unearth the mysteries of Void Cowboy.

At first, it's just a distraction - he assumes the boy must have a split personality, or that he's got a hyperactive imagination, or that his power just completely throws an error against his through some quirk in biology. But it soon becomes apparent that nothing along those lines is happening. His power is working just fine, it's just telling him that the 'real' Void Cowboy is hiding his real feelings.

Sometimes. The emotions match up with the words sometimes. When he gets pumped about the mission, when he gets excited about seeing other people flex their powers - and, annoyingly enough, when he absent-mindedly insults Gallant's powers. He'd half-heartedly not-quite apologised, but the exact same flood of contempt and derision had swept away any illusion that he was sorry. Right. He hates this guy. It's decided. He would have settled on that answer even if he wasn't constantly looking at his teammates like a serial killer assessing his victims. The bloodlust, the greed, the possessiveness, the lust - nobody should even dare to look at his teammates like that with those emotions with that level of determination in their aura.

He's still not entirely sure what's going on here, but he is sure that Void Cowboy knows. What he was seeing was real, and now that he knew what he was looking for - it was impossible to overlook that the bloodlust was always there, even underneath the more natural, pleasant emotions. This isn't a moment of inflamed passion or drunken rage, it's deeper and more intense than anything like that. It was calculated - both the aggression, and his ability to hide it. Masking his desire to fight, to kill, to dominate, to fuck - in no particular order either.

Needless to say, Void Cowboy was one fucked-up individual.

He knew that now. But, nobody else did. Nobody else could see what he saw. Everyone else saw an admirable hero. And he didn't have anything to change their minds on that. Just flashes of colours, and he knew what they would say to that - wondering thoughts, a mental disorder, a power interaction or just a 'user error' on his part. There have been mistakes and failures through his powers before, they won't take him at his word - nor had he done anything that inspired a reason to not trust him. And that was before considering that the PRT had special orders to soft-ball him to lure him into the team. He had nothing, no justification at all that would be listened to.

Which meant that there was nothing he could do but watch in horror as Velocity agrees to include the vigilante into the Wards mission, something that fills said vigilante with a fresh fountain of glee, smugness, bloodthirst and greed. And... more lust? Not just when looking at Vista or when the conversation turned to the new ABB Tinker, but when looking at Clockblocker or himself too. It was so odd and ill-timed to the conversation that he wasn't even sure he was reading it right. Needless to say, all of that combined was hardly the standard emotional profile that come with a chance to work with your heroes.

There was little he could do about the enthusiasm of his teammates towards the new arrival. And, again, some god out there was laughing at him. Not even a few weeks ago, he'd been praying for Vista to get over her feelings for him and find someone more appropriate. It was a constant source of discomfort for him, but also something that would be a huge breach of privacy and trust to even hint about. If his teammates understood the depths of the emotional spectrum he could comprehend, it could cause some issues. When Vista's feelings towards him had started to wither and dull just a few days ago, he'd been overjoyed.

Now, as much as he didn't want to admit it, he wished she was still chasing after him. Not because Gallant would ever reciprocate himself, but because at least he wasn't Void Cowboy. There was something uniquely terrifying at realising that the soft-pink tones in the air between those two were coming from Vista, even as the boy returned the look with renewed waves of dark-red bloodlust amid the lighter yellow of some probably-fucked-up form of affection, desire and protectiveness. Needless to say, the stronger emotion was overpowering every other aura in the vicinity.

Vista. No. Please find someone else.

Naturally, he'd done all he could to keep the two separate, hopeful that this would just be a temporary, quickly-forgotten moment. The twin bursts of sharp-green annoyance and derision coming from both in front and behind him when getting between them highlighted that it would take more work than that - while also highlighting that any lingering rapport he had from Vista's crush couldn't be relied on any longer. Unfortunate, but this time it doesn't matter - the tables have turned. He's the one doing a normal action, and neither Void Cowboy or Vista are willing to say the truth of what's on their minds. Crisis... not averted, but delayed.

And with that, the mission would begin. Two missions, in fact. Because there was the first one, to rescue the hostages and perhaps take out the Tinker if they could be found - and, if he was being fair, which he wasn't - he might even have admitted that Void Cowboy was an excellent addition to the team for that specific mission.

But then there was the second mission. His mission. His crusade. He couldn't contribute much to the team in the overall scenario, but he was the only one who knew something close to the truth about Void Cowboy's true self. He'd made it his self-appointed task, there and then, to not let Void Cowboy out of his sight. When the team had split up, he'd ensured that he was paired with the teenager and Vista was sent off to help the hostages - earning himself another frustrated pulse of anger from a fuming Vista that hadn't managed to think of a reason to stay together with the vigilante fast enough.

He could take her anger. This was important. This was how he had chosen to contribute. He was the only one that was ready for the mask to slip. It wasn't just about his team either, it was about the Tinker they were moving to confront. If he was left alone with her... they'd probably be left with nothing but a corpse. And that wouldn't just be bad for general heroic reasons, but also specifically because of the threat of a dead man's switch. He needed to be there to both protect and attack this potentially-vulnerable Tinker. If anyone was going to fall victim to the barely-restrained violent-tendencies that practically dripped off of the supposed hero, it was going to be him.

Things didn't quite go as expected. The Tinker was more prepared than any intelligence had led them to expect. Openly psychotic and violent. She had far more in reserve than anticipated, certainly not just a regular pushover once confronted in person. Void Cowboy had actually saved his life. Not out of kindness or comradery, but in a bland, near-emotionless way like he was ticking off an objective on his to-do list and feeling mildly annoyed at the effort expended to do something so minor - the omnipresent contempt that seemed to be there whenever he looked at Gallant never shifted for a second, even as he donated a speedster power to help him escape the ambush.

Gallant... wasn't sure how to take that. But, in this case, Void Cowboy's desire to engage the Tinker in combat was genuine - and helpful to everyone else in the building. He'd made a beeline to his costume, the hostages had been saved and he'd managed to score some hits on the drones flying around to help in the fight himself. He was feeling better about his utility. The Tinker was handled. Void Cowboy had beaten his low expectations and exercised considerable restraint - even if it was tainted by the naked disappointment and boredom emanating from his body after the rush of battle had ended. The bomb was stable under Clockblocker. Those frozen on the stage were already being freed. Things were looking up.

That summarises the situation up until now - this very moment.

The point where, naturally, things had all gone to shit. The entrance of the Undersiders, barely allowing even a few sentences of conversation before racing towards Bakuda - attacking anyone in their way. The frantic, agonised warnings from Triumph that Lung was already in hot pursuit of the lesser-known gang and nobody was in good enough shape to stop him - the begging for them to just step aside, reluctantly conveyed as a 'run away if you're a gutless coward' by Shadow Stalker. The slow realisation that they were in a completely unenviable position, to stand aside and let Lung through - spelling the death of the Undersiders, the complete victory of the ABB and placing themselves as the new 'hostages' of the scenario. Or, getting played like a fiddle and squaring off against Lung - hoping to buy just enough time for reinforcements to arrive, the Undersiders to leave and the rest of the ABB Capes to be secured away somewhere safe.

But the choice wasn't up to him. It was already made. The howling, swirling bloodlust and competitive spirit at his side tells the story for him before the first mocking taunt escapes from Void Cowboy's mouth - for a moment, he considers slamming the younger teen with a blast of some kind of calming emotion... but he isn't even sure that would work. After all, he seemed both capable and willing to dive into combat like it was just boring routine - and he certainly didn't want to give him the excuse he needed to direct his violence towards the Wards.

Nor did he expect to have much luck convincing his teammates, not with Kid Win giving frantic progress updates on how quickly Armsmaster would be freed, with Vista practically glowing with the desire to show off, with Aegis and Browbeat psyching themselves up for battle as if the suggestion to stand aside had never been uttered, with Shadow Stalker saying...

Ahem.

He's going to ignore Sophia's comments about the size of his genitalia and what she's going to do to him if he 'chickens out now' and lets Void Cowboy fight to the death alone. He probably shouldn't be surprised that she's a fan of his methods. Was Browbeat the only female Ward that actually had good taste in men? Maybe he was speaking too soon on that, but she seemed like a sensible girl. It would be fine.

Probably. Maybe it would still be a good idea to give her an introductory crash course on the sizable list of incidents and injuries directly caused by Void Cowboy on his 'friendly patrols', and maybe a few of his worst posts on PHO too. He might not be able to satisfactorily warn people about Void Cowboy via his power, save for a few quiet discussions with Armsmaster or Director Piggot - but helping people realise the truth of who he really was? That the friendly persona was just a mask, tossed aside whenever it didn't suit him? That was just common sense. The PRT might want to play things slow with him because his power might be useful, but Gallant will be damned before he lets anyone - anyone - look at his friends and colleagues like that and decide not to do anything about it.

Breathe in. Breathe out. He's getting distracted. Which was bad, because right now - the enemy right in front of him wasn't Void Cowboy. It was the man-turning-dragon that was racing across the room, alight with both the metaphorical flames of ego, wounded pride and fury - as well as the literal flames that blasted them with heat from across the room, only compounding with the building inferno the fire-breather had made parts of the building into already. Lung, the nigh-unstoppable force of nature that had stalemated the wider Protectorate for years now - and had clearly already knocked Dauntless and Triumph out of the fight to even reach this point.

"I have him." Vista's excited tone echoes in his ears through the comm-piece. "Stay back!"

The ground in front of the group buckles, then curves as if forming a bowl - the loping charge of the half-transformed Lung stumbling as the ground turns uneven, then into a near cliff-edge. Gallant peers over the edge and fires off a half-hearted string of blasts at the centre of the pit. A deep pit, one that had neatly merged itself with what seemed to be some form of basement or perhaps a maintenance tunnel. It's a good idea. After all, the best method of fighting Lung is simply not to fight him - forcibly settling him into a trap like that and waiting for him to lose steam would be an excellent idea.

But Lung isn't the type to just sit around and let someone do that to him. Void Cowboy obviously knows that. There's barely even a flicker of hope, surprise or jealousy at Vista seeming to win the fight in the first move - just a steady, patient anticipation as he works on his own preparations. Vista's bubbles of excitement and pride slowly bleed away into matching strings of nervousness, the slowed rate of her power closing the lid of the trap reflecting the fact that Lung was likely clambering closer and closer to the top - interfering with her power due to his pure proximity. "No good." She murmurs, hastily backstepping. "He's coming through!"

Gallant ducks to the side as the trap all but explodes outwards in an eruption of flame and molten debris, ducking lightly behind Void Cowboy's armoured minion - batting away a questing 'limb' that tries to wrap itself around his armour and weakly pull him closer. No thank you. He pulls away from it to stand with the rest of the Wards as the vigilante who had been most keen on starting this fight-

-struck a pose and pointed his sword at Lung? Could that thing even be called a sword? Where did that even come from? It unfolded to be taller than Gallant, and Gallant was pretty sure that he had a solid year or two of growth on the vigilante. The loosely-hanging exoframe covering his suit was clearly supposed to provide support to power it, but Gallant knew a thing or two about power armour and equivalents - and he could say with one-hundred-percent confidence that the frame wasn't even being used right now as the teen waves around the oversized block of metal one-handed.

Found a Brute rating somewhere. Great. Just when he was starting to think that he had a clear weakness. And a Tinker rating. Obviously. They'd already suspected that, but it was good to have proof. There was nothing natural about that weapon, nor the glowing purple orb awkwardly clipped to his chest. And the Master rating, because that thing off to his side had never stopped growing - the limbs had become distinct now, a figure that stood twice his height and loomed protectively over the Cape.

When Lung barks out a mocking laugh in the vigilante's face in response to something he hadn't quite managed to hear, the response is immediate. The black-costumed figure lunges forward, the frame surrounding him whirring and hissing to life as Lung matches his approach with enthusiasm. As the sword winds up for a telegraphed attack, a draconic limb is raised in response - already distinctly inhuman and coated in scales.

A half-second later, that same limb practically crumples as it fails to block the raw speed and power of the initial sword swing. The sword continues through, smashing into Lung's downturned lizard-like face - the collision generating an agonising screech of metal-on-metal.

And Gallant can do nothing but watch as Lung rockets backwards - skidding and tumbling across the room, a trail of muted flames left in his wake. He turns to stare at Void Cowboy, aglow with a feeling of smugness and self-satisfaction - albeit with the same omnipresent lust for battle that had underpinned his every emotion since their first conversation outside the building. Still ready for a fight. He knows that it wasn't enough. But he seems far too happy anyway. He mimes a few test swings, the exoframe around him once-again disengaged as he does so.

"Don't sit directly behind me, by the way." Gallant listens as he murmurs loud enough for the Wards to hear. "This thing's got a... critical hit function, of sorts? It's Leet-tech. Can't control when it hits, but, uh - yeah. It slams everything into reverse. Turns my hits into a circular AOE-" What was that supposed to mean? "-and the range is way longer than just the blade. Supercharges the power too. You'll die if you get hit, so just make sure you keep some distance or stay at an angle. Pure vertical, pure horizontal - that's all it can do with that effect, so you'll be fine if you're paying attention."

Gallant hadn't planned on getting anywhere close to the blade anyway, but he dutifully backs further away. Looking at Lung slowly regathering himself, the bloodied metallic 'faceplate' that his head had transformed into - he felt it was pretty obvious that nearly anyone in the Wards would die after getting a clean hit from that. And that wasn't the 'critical hit'? He didn't see any obvious sign of a cooldown period for the Tinkertech either, the sword looked just as capable now as it did when he first saw it.

A fact that is proven as Lung finishes his regeneration and lets out a roar of challenge, loping towards them again as the swordsman mirrors the charge. There's less fury from Lung this time, a sliver of enjoyment in the aura - a sense of pride in the test of strength that was ongoing. Lung could dodge, they likely both knew that. But some twisted sense of honour demanded that strength be met with strength. This time, Lung's limb doesn't snap entirely - some scales buckle and crack, but in the end, the dragon is the one that wins the clash. Void Cowboy ducks under the claw, swings yet again at Lung's comparatively fleshy body - biting deep into his torso before kicking away with the sword as the attack stalls, his chest flashing purple as something scatters around him before he ducks to the floor - resting the sword against the ground and activating the attack yet again to spring himself back to safety.

A second later, Lung practically seems to explode - a selection of grenades erupting from beneath his growing bulk in a flash of light and fury. Lung lets out a roar of pain in response, followed by a broken, unintelligible string of words that fails to leave his distinctly-inhuman mouth in an understandable form. But already, he seems ready for another round - shaking away fragments from the blast as they cling to the scales creeping across the rest of his body.

Gallant swallows drily. He's not happy to see the display of strength from either fighter. The sentiment was likely a common one when seeing Lung shrug off attacks, but it should at least have been good to find out more about Void Cowboy's capabilities - a few more tricks unearthed that he could be ready for later.

But it wasn't making Gallant feel any better, or any more prepared. If anything, he feels more useless than ever. What, exactly, was Gallant supposed to do if Void Cowboy had chosen to attack the Wards? He'd given himself the self-appointed task of keeping an eye on the obvious dangerous nutcase, assuming that, in the worst case scenario - a few solid hits from his stronger physique and his taser would take him down, the obvious underestimation and lack of respect the teen had for his powerset working to his advantage. And, since retrieving his power armour - that confidence in his ability to handle the Cape if his tenuous control over his emotions snapped at the wrong time had only grown. The electricity in the armour would neutralise Shadow Stalker's powerset if he tried to phase through, and it was very apparent that his assumed replica of Glory Girl's forcefield was simply a shadow of the original. He could have done it.

That's what he had thought. Looking at the situation now as Lung tries to trap the blade - taking a gouge to the eyes for the trouble - it was painfully obvious that there was never a chance of that working out. He was a liability here, unable to help even when he was perhaps the only person in the world with the knowledge of what was coming.

And the worst part was that, with every passing second, his ability to warn people was slipping away. He knew that this was just a battle of egos, that the reluctance to jump into the fight was feigned and that Void Cowboy's act as a hero was simply a paper-thin mask to cover up a level of deranged psychopathy that he hadn't even seen in seasoned serial killers.

But to everyone else? This looked like genuine heroics. The bold knight, refusing to allow the dragon to pass - not to his injured and vulnerable teammates, not even to his enemies. Not swayed by fear even in the face of the most unstoppable force in the city, getting up again and again to try another angle - just buy a little more time. Vista had split off to ward away some ABB footsoldiers that had tried creeping through the hole that Lung had made in the wall, but even from here he could see the giddy pulses of light-blue and pink in her aura as she looks back at the fight. Even Aegis, Browbeat and the select few Undersiders that were visible at the back of the room arguing with Bakuda had various shades of respect coating their otherwise-varied emotional auras when he noticed them glancing at the ongoing battle.

He can't blame them. Every now and then, the thought crosses his mind that it might be a mistake - a bad power interaction. That, somehow, those emotions aren't really his. But as strange as the spikes and fluctuations are, everything else is perfectly logical, happening at appropriate times and changing in predictable, understandable ways. Everything was normal, except for the parts that he was hiding - the times when there were consequences to acting out. That was when he held himself back.

It didn't escape him that, so far, he was blaming the Cape for a thought crime. Thoughts were not actions, no matter how worried he was about his intentions. But... at the same time, this didn't look like someone restraining intrusive thoughts. There was no flash of guilty recrimination, no self-loathing or horror, no panic at what they might have done - just a moment of indulgence before a flicker of some other emotion that was never quite enough to sate the ambition lurking underneath. There was something terribly, terribly wrong with his head.

It was a terrible thought, but the problem could solve itself soon. Most Protectorate engagements with Lung ended with both sides mutually agreeing to walk away - the actual danger to the Wards if they chose to back down was relatively minimal based on his established behaviours. But in a pitched battle like this? Lung wasn't the type to hold back - and Void Cowboy's powers were known to be cheap-copies, no matter the performance he was putting on combining them today. It was more than likely that, as Lung grew to a certain point - Void Cowboy just got in over his head and ended up at his limit, dead in one blow before he realised his powers had failed him.

Gallant grits his teeth. No. As a hero, he can't cheer for a result like that - not even if he's doing it out of fear of what might happen to his teammates if the potential serial-killer-in-the-making continues to thrive.

But at the same time, there's a reason he's on the sidelines right now. Because it isn't his decision anyway. The PRT tried his emotion blasts against Lung once before, hoping that a rage dragon without the rage would be easier to handle - and once it had been proven that Lung's emotional state didn't diminish his power, and in some cases only strengthened it, Gallant had never been pulled into a fight against the man again. Even the kinetic aspect of his powers didn't help here, not at this level - good enough to knock around baseline humans, but nothing to a Brute. Useless.

He was just a spectator here, stuck to vapid observations on how Lung was still transforming. Where Void Cowboy's sword had initially crushed a limb like cardboard and left a gaping wound in Lung's overly-armoured face, it had just found itself halted in an attempt to bisect Lung's torso. That he'd managed to escape that situation was impressive, but the previous wound he'd made was already healed - already gleaming with the glint of silvery scales that continued to race across his body. All the efforts from the Protectorate to disengage and force him to shrink down when he was waiting outside were being reversed by the damage he was taking now, the steady growth of his serpentine form highlighting that the slim chance of victory from the start of the fight had already slipped away.

It wasn't purely because of his physical strength and durability. It was the heat. The flames. Void Cowboy had already been limiting himself to brief clashes before creating distance once again, but the flames had only grown hotter since then - the scorch and singe marks on his seemingly-new costume told the tale of how even the limited exposure so far had established the limits of what he could take. It was obvious - his Brute rating didn't protect him from the heat. The same reason why Browbeat had gone from looking for an angle to close in and assist, to hanging back just like him - hovering protectively over Aegis as their leader literally pulls himself back together.

This was the problem with Lung. Most Capes just didn't have an answer to the complete package.

Except Void Cowboy, again. The Cape himself might be discovering the reason why Lung was still active all these years, but that metal knight by his side was still weathering Lung's assault without much issue. Not the flames, nor the increased physicality was making a notable difference. It wasn't winning, not at all. In fact, it was being readily torn apart every time it stepped forward to intercept the dragon-man - the ready sacrifice to ensure that Lung couldn't move freely. But it did two things well - first, it pulled itself together again just as easily as it was torn apart.

And secondly, the Manton limit clearly didn't apply to it. Vista lets out another gleeful warning as the ground buckles again, the ground around Lung crumbling while he takes a moment too long to rend the knight apart - yet another pit-trap having been formed under his feet, only revealed at the last moment. It might not have been possible in a short timeframe with multiple fighters dancing around getting in the way of her power, but with only a single 'real' person to account for whenever Void Cowboy retreats she seems to be having better luck manipulating the area.

It won't hold. It can't hold. Lung isn't even recognisably human anymore. He doesn't clamber up the walls this time, he slithers - the pit walls closest to him left glowing from his mere passing.

His eyes snap around to a flare of colour appearing in the corner of his eyes. Confusion. Concern. "Kid Win, I'm seeing Armsmaster reacting to the fight, but he's not moving."

"Still working on it." The distracted voice comes back. "I was hoping I could shrink the field down enough to keep him out without switching the entire thing off with him inside - but it's just not going to work. Turning it off is a delicate thing, it's set-up like a, like a vacuum, but for time. Well, that isn't exactly right-" Gallant clears his throat meaningfully to head off the Tinker talk. "-right. Uh. I mean, if we stick with the vacuum talk - I'm just bleeding off some of the differential in how time passes to ease the transition back to real time, make sure there's no sudden, uh, explosion."

"Just do your best, Kid Win. We could really use the help up here." Aegis speaks over the channel coolly. "Does that mean he's able to hear us?"

"Um. Sure? Well. No. He could, but he's not on this channel, he's got this cool alert system in his helmet but it's something he needs to actively switch to-"

"Shut it, morons. I'll swap channels and fill him in while he's stuck in place." Shadow Stalker's annoyed voice squawks over the comms. "Just keep sitting there, looking useless. You're doing great."

As much as he'd like to issue a retort, he can't. This isn't the Empire, where he could put up a respectable fight against most of the roster - Lung was... Lung. Aside from Vista and perhaps Aegis up to a point, the best the remainder of them could do was simply avoid becoming collateral damage or future hostages.

He casts an annoyed glance at the Undersiders. They still haven't left. He's sure they aren't stalling, the majority of them have lost their collars by now - but the process is taking too long. Probably deliberate on Bakuda's part, despite the 'encouragement' from her captors. If they were gone, this situation becomes so much easier - the Wards could just leave, take the entire reason Lung was even here away with them. The fight would just end. They could engage them right now, but starting a second fight when they didn't even have an advantage in the first seemed questionable - and the overall logic of the situation hadn't changed yet.

Yet.

He turns back to Lung as another purple flash illuminates the room for a split second, blinking as he's just in time to spot Void Cowboy throwing a containment foam grenade directly at Lung's head. Where the hell did he get that? Had he robbed the PRT at some point? Was it wrong for him to hope that he had, if only to have an actual crime to point to? Lung weaves his head away, not just strong - but fast as well.

But not the fastest. Half-a-dozen other hissing grenades explode a moment later, the blur of a slightly-scorched Velocity momentarily pausing to watch his handiwork is all he can catch before the Cape is gone again - likely to return to suppressing the rioting gangbangers outside.

On most Capes, that would be enough. On Lung, at this level of his transformation? It was only enough to slow him down. The foam resists heat well, but Gallant can already see it starting to smolder and turn black in places - and Lung is physically strong enough that he can rip the foam away with the rest of the wall and keep on moving. It has limited his movement, but the fight isn't necessarily any easier.

A point highlighted by Lung opening his mouth wide and, for the first time in the fight, blasting the room at large with his fire breath. Gallant hurls himself to the ground along with Aegis and Browbeat, Vista lets out a girly shriek and propels herself upwards and away on a pillar of rock. The Undersiders barely even react, the darkness-wielder - Grue? - shifts the cloud slightly to block the stray attack that reaches them, seeming to suppress it immediately on contact.

But they weren't really the primary target. Void Cowboy was. As slippery as he'd been so far, there was no way to dodge around the concentrated blast of heat.

He'd used his shadow state, and both the sword and the frame that held it had clattered to the ground around him. Lung doesn't give him a moment to recover it, racing forward at his fastest pace yet and bringing an entirely-draconic claw down on the Tinkertech - pulverising it into pieces in an instant as Void Cowboy can do nothing but beat a hasty retreat - diving into the ground with Sophia's power and reappearing at a safer distance a few seconds later. Annoyance coats his aura at that, but half-a-second later as a followup wide-angled firebreath blasts him harmlessly - Glory Girl's forcefield? - that transitions to alarm, for a reason that takes a few more seconds to become apparent to Gallant.

The metal knight had frozen, seeming to start collapsing in on itself between one step and the next as it chased after Lung. Not a hint of movement, or any sign of the immediate recovery it had shown off earlier. The exact specifics of the power and why it had suddenly deactivated weren't clear, but without his Tinkertech and without the knight - it was clear that there was nothing left. Once Lung closed the gap again, Void Cowboy would die - and he knew it.

It's over.

But nobody told the other Wards that. With their complete misunderstanding of Void Cowboy's motives, they're inspired - irrationally willing to put it all on the line for their fellow hero in his moment of vulnerability. Aegis crashes down on Lung's elongated neck from above, while Browbeat - muscles bulging as she swells to twice her usual height - comes in to echo the attack on the dragon as he is momentarily knocked down. Gallant starts firing too, naturally. Except, his contribution isn't in trying to win - it's trying to manage Lung's response. He knows that those attacks are near-meaningless at this stage. Being able to move the dragon or force him to the ground momentarily didn't mean that you had done any meaningful damage. Gallant had a clear role here - to dull the furious reprisal that's coming, dampen the murderous response to Lung's insulted pride that would have him focus his full attention on the weaker Brutes in front of him with lethal consequences. Instead, Lung is filled with feelings of dismissive contempt and superiority. Aegis is batted aside, getting up immediately and seeking another angle - Browbeat is met with a barrage of flames and inelegantly hurled into the nearest wall while she's blinded.

After a moment of pause, Lung prowls onwards - directly towards the Undersiders. The growl of the engine serving as an unspoken promise-

Wait. Engine? That wasn't Lung growling, certainly not. Gallant turns again, just in time to catch Armsmaster diving through the air far above him, linking up with the ArmsCycle as it slams through a cracked window to make its entrance. Then, together - man and machine descend upon the flaming lizard - adjusting mid-air to ensure the first strike connects despite Lung's attempt to dodge without even needing to look behind.

"I understand the situation. Wards, stand down - reinforcements are inbound." Armsmaster's gruff voice takes over their comms. "Engaging."

The confidence is earned, Gallant knows that much. And immediately, the difference in Tinkertech quality between Void Cowboy and Armsmaster becomes apparent. Void Cowboy had a powerful weapon, but that was all. Armsmaster had everything. A defence sufficient to ignore the flames, mobility that didn't need to sacrifice any other aspect of his kit, offensive power in the halberd that was every bit as potent as the blade - except wielded with far more dexterity and skill.

Not for the first time today, Lung finds himself harried in melee combat by an elusive opponent that seems to refuse to get hit - except, this one isn't forced away by the surges of heat or periodic flame blasts. It doesn't take Lung long to realise that brute force won't work - as flame jets and basic swipes of superstrength fall short, he turns to more unorthodox methods of attack. He collapses a nearby wall and flicks the flaming debris at his new opponent - a full-body tackle with his entire serpentine bulk, knowing that any damage inflicted can simply be regenerated. Some hits connect on both sides, halberd gouging into scales while Armsmaster's suit lights up in protest at being tested by the Brute's attacks.

"Hey, Browbeat! Aegis! Uh, I guess Gallant too. Help me out." Void Cowboy is back, seeming unaffected by his close shave with death. No sign of lasting panic, fear or giddiness - nothing that seems like it might eventually manifest as PTSD. If anything, he's enthusiastic - excited. A bit of awe? Perhaps it was just the presence of Armsmaster, he was supposed to be a fan - if Gallant remembers rightly. In other circumstances, it would be a good emotion to see. In this situation, it's just another sign that something is wrong with his head. "Maybe he took the first one out with a cheap shot, but what's he going to do about the second? He even left it all in one place for me."

Before anyone can ask what he means, he marches over to the ruins of his previous blade, extends a hand over it and-

"Bro! I need that!" Kid Win's drone squawks, peering over their shoulders. Not the Ward himself, had he opted to stay with Clockblocker to work on the bomb? "Can you do that whenever you want? What are the limitations? Can I borrow you for a project-"

"I get that reaction a lot." Void Cowboy chuckles, re-equipping his weapon. "And there's a few restrictions on it. It's a charge-based system, so I'm done for the day. Aside from that, I'm happy to rent it out at some point. I'll need the next few charges myself to get back into top condition, I think I ruined my teleporter in the heat - and I've promised a few uses of it to a friend already, but I'm definitely intending to let you guys get some mileage out of it too. We're all on the same team, right?"

"Of course."/"Naturally."/"Obviously."/"Sure!" His teammates agree enthusiastically.

"I'd like to hope so." Gallant reluctantly adds, his late answer drawing some looks. "I mean, he doesn't want to be in the Wards for a reason - right?"

"Shut it, Gallant! Don't ruin this for me! You have no idea what I just witnessed as a Tinker!" The drone does a spin. "He's a Ward in spirit and that's what counts, right - right?!"

"Right. And I really do intend on joining the heroes properly at some point, just not right now."

Behind his helmet, Gallant frowns in challenge. "Too much oversight?"

"Oh absolutely. I'd never get anything done. They'd definitely panic over people getting the wrong idea about my power. Better to wait until the cat's already out of the bag, right?" He probably shouldn't have aired his real thoughts, but Void Cowboy seems to have interpreted it in his own way. "Anyway, I had an idea for Lung but it's not something I can set up easily on my own - and my knight falls apart when it tries it, but with you here, we've got a real shot at taking him down."

"I hate to break it to you, but you weren't even making him bleed at the end there - your sword isn't going to cut it. Literally." Gallant interjects, earning himself a flash of annoyance and contempt for his entirely correct observation.

"The sword was blunt at that point, and I wasn't even trying to hit him normally - I was trying for the critical hit. If it got lucky, we'd be calling Amy to come and save his life right now." No. This had too much potential to go wrong. It was good that Void Cowboy was the one taking the risk.

A small, treacherous part of his mind was concerned that Void Cowboy could kill all three of them with a casual movement right now, it wouldn't even have to be deliberate - if the blade slipped and he applied just the slightest bit of acceleration it would come around so fast that none of them would have time to dodge. It's logical. He still hates it.

♦ Topic: Statement and Summary On Recent Gang Violence Outbreak - April 5th 2011

In: Boards ► Places ► America ► Brockton Bay

►PRTENE_OFFICIAL (Original Poster) (Verified Official)

Posted On April 5th 2011:

The Parahuman Response Team, working with the Protectorate and local law enforcement, is providing the following update on the series of parahuman incidents that took place across Brockton Bay today. Beginning around 17:30 this afternoon, multiple threats unfolded from several different criminal elements at once.

Firstly, the ABB launched an unprecedented and unprovoked assault on the charity event dedicated to the debut of our newest Ward, Browbeat. It immediately became apparent that this action was led by a dangerous and unhinged Tinker by the name of Bakuda, who specialises in explosive devices and is believed to be the Cape identity of the failed 'Cornell Bomber'. In her opening ambush, several heroes on stage were temporarily restrained - in contrast to public speculation, we can reassure all parties that all of the individuals caught up in the initial assault by the amateur villainous Tinker were swiftly freed by more experienced PRT-aligned Tinkers and remain in excellent condition. The Tinker issued several threats to the population within and without the building, stating her intention to take the hundreds, if not thousands of hostages for no clear purpose - and claimed to have a powerful bomb ready if opposed. We took these threats extremely seriously and issued an evacuation order and quarantine of the surrounding areas while considering our best response.

At the same time of this assault, Lung launched a vicious assault on secure PRT holding facilities elsewhere in the town. Protectorate heroes, led by Dauntless, went to combat the threat and drive the Cape away from his intended target. They were able to successfully prevent Lung from progressing further into the building, entering into a protracted battle to pin the Cape down and prevent him from reinforcing his new Tinker partner.

In addition to this, the Empire Eighty-Eight launched an assault on a prison transport to free several of their captured members. This drew an immediate response from Protectorate forces with the assistance of New Wave and an independent vigilante. This team prioritised the preservation of innocent life and successfully de-escalated the situation despite being significantly outnumbered, we thank all parties for their efforts in preventing the situation from getting out of hand in a time of crisis elsewhere in the city.

Finally, the previously small-time criminal team 'The Undersiders' assaulted a secure holding parahuman holding area and kidnapped the ABB-affiliated Cape 'Oni Lee' from detention. Due to the speed of the attack, the powers involved and the critical events requiring a response elsewhere in the city - manpower was not available to stop this attack at the time.

These events all occurred within an exceptionally narrow time-frame, indicating a combined, cross-gang effort to stretch and exhaust Protectorate and PRT resources across the city.

PRT leaders made the decision to activate the Wards to perform a limited, low-risk mission to end the hostage situation from the rookie ABB Tinker. With the aid of another independent hero, the team was able to successfully defeat Bakuda, free the hostages and their fellow heroes without issue. At this stage, both Lung and the previously-mentioned Undersiders approached the scene - resulting in a standoff and a brief confrontation. This concluded with the Undersiders and Wards escaping the building while Armsmaster engaged Lung alone. At this stage, the Undersiders released Oni Lee - who demonstrated an ability to replicate Bakuda's Tinkertech and use it to unleash a devastating bombing spree. Oni Lee's presence created immediate chaos, severely disrupted Armsmaster's capture of Lung and resulted in the release of Bakuda from custody. With that window of opportunity missed - leadership reassessed the situation and the best path forward from there.

With civilian lives suddenly at greater risk, PRT leadership ordered all hero teams to stand down and allow both the ABB and Undersiders to withdraw. This decision was made to prevent loss of life and limit additional damage. The PRT is proud and relieved to report that despite the scale of the fighting and the dangerous powers involved, no civilian deaths occurred. All injured individuals, whether hero, villain, or bystander, received prompt medical care. Property damage remained largely confined to the areas where combat took place. The PRT and Protectorate continue to prioritise the safety of Brockton Bay and its civilians. Full investigations into today's coordinated attacks, the circumstances surrounding the prison breakouts and the new parahuman Bakuda are already underway. We will provide further updates as they become available. Citizens are urged to report any suspicious activity through the PRT tip line and to stay clear of any areas still designated as active scenes until authorities declare them safe.
