"Fifth challenge my ass." I grumble. "Shouldn't this be the last one?" The fact that it wasn't must surely imply that, once I did reach Amy, I'd likely annihilate her in a fight. Otherwise the difficulty scaling was just broken.

I'm going to die to the TIME modifier soon. Barely a few seconds left until the first wave, and I'd barely even cleared the first street. I'm not particularly upset at that. The search area is too large for me to meaningfully cut it down at a normal pace. Best to just gather information as well as I can.

On that note... I sidle towards the closest building, reaching out to touch the nearest vines. They seemed connected to each other, so if this was connected directly to Panacea I might be able to glean something about her location from what her own power would tell me about it.

Immediately my senses expand, all across the wall and roof of the building the vines were spread across. Not just around the outside, but throughout the walls and floors as well - not a single room inside the house was missing crawling tendril. The stretch below me, clear to the naked eye - but the plant snaked through the concrete under my feet and into the pipes below just as easily as it went through the walls.

But that was it. I cast an annoyed glance at the next house, seeing and sensing the problem at the same time. It looked like a single, gigantic plant - but it wasn't. It was a series of individual ones, all connected together to form a network. I could sense the points where they linked into the next one along the chain, complex biological sequences conveying information onwards in some indecipherable plant-language. That too, was deliberate. In the same way that I couldn't touch one person, and scan someone else that they were holding hands with - I couldn't touch a single part of this network and get a map of its spread across the city, or any idea about where it's creator might be hiding.

Another deliberate design decision to work around the limitations of one of my powers. I'm not actually upset about this. Getting countered like this is what I should probably expect from other highly-flexible powersets and Tinkers. Not just in challenges, but in real life too - I wouldn't expect an enemy Tinker to ever challenge me without an answer to every one of my currently-documented defensive powers. Shadow Stalker's main weaknesses not being well-known was helping me for now, but even the weaker Tinkers of the Bay would find it trivial to add a few sparks into their creations if it meant fucking over my power of choice. Getting tested in a way where simple obscurity wouldn't help me had a certain appeal to it.

The TIME modifier in my head ticks to zero. Shorter than the usual five-minutes most of them offer before the first wave, but it doesn't bother me. I would have hit fast-forward on it if I could. I want to see what the first wave is, get a full understanding of what I'm up against for future runs.

I glance around. Nothing? Nothing. The timer was already racing towards the second wave, but I couldn't even hear anyone moving in the distance. I usually had cars screeching and sirens blaring as the first wave, powered or unpowered, rushed in my direction - but the streets were just as empty as ever.

Good? I grimace. No. I should assume that any deviations from the norm were bad for me. In that case, what did this achieve for her?

It hid information, for one. Not just on the foes I would be fighting and in what order, but also where and how they appeared. If knowing their initial location, even over the span of multiple attempts, might give some estimate of where Amy was hiding? Then holding them back and letting me wander, then ensuring that they were released into the city out of my sight was a generally smart idea.

And aside from the information game, she could also just be using them as a defensive force. Assuming that I was correct in considering Amy herself as the 'weak' point of this setup, she could realise that too - and direct new reinforcement waves into becoming her personal bodyguards. I could handle gunmen individually and deal with groups stealthily given time, preparation or enough chaos - but I didn't have a way to just kill someone through a hail of gunfire. Sending people out into the city to chase me wasn't necessary. I could only win by getting to her.

Fine. I'll just... search where I can while I wait. I don't expect to find anything, but a miracle might happen. I summon my ash clone, take control of the nearest bug with my administrator power and begin a three-pronged search. Room by room. House by house. Street by street. I wasn't necessarily looking to find Amy right away, I was looking to exclude possibilities. Even confirming simple things, like an overly dusty room indicating a lack of footfall, or a lack of secret tunnels, could exclude large swathes of the target area. Especially as my power usually starts my challenges with my body facing in the approximate direction of my enemy. I could tentatively say that the entire half of the city behind me was, at the very least, not where Amy had spawned in. She might have moved there, but she wasn't there at minute zero.

It's only after my mental timer announces the arrival of the third wave that I encounter my first enemy. A gun-toting individual who announces his presence by unleashing a storm of bullets through the walls of the house I was searching with uncanny accuracy and almost ending the challenge on the spot before I find cover.

Well. Hardly uncanny, actually. I glance with annoyance at the pointing, accusing vines stretching in my direction from all angles. A gigantic target marker, for those who knew how to look. I'd hoped that the reinforcements would struggle just as much as I had in this hostile environment, and had even held out a slim hope that the reason I hadn't seen the first waves was because they'd simply perished to the effects of the pollen.

As my ash clone strikes the man from behind and knocks him down, that hope is finally extinguished. The man is hardly even a man at all, the flowers have taken any identifying features from him - roots trail out of every orifice as he gasps in pain from each hit as my clone and I effortlessly tag-team to tear him apart. Wounds burst open as I smash his head and chest in, viscera and some kind of pus exploding outwards with each hit - his blood simply curdles on the spot, turning a sickly-yellow colour as it's exposed to the air. Worst of all, with his brain half-splattered across the street - he doesn't die. Long-established roots and branches manipulate his muscles and limbs directly, an intelligence - or perhaps just a very, very complex ingrained response - that I haven't quite been able to identify directs him to pick up his gun again and attempt to complete his task.

Panacea's power ends that in a flash. The parasitical plants have no resistance to the power, obviously - and fall to pieces in seconds. The man slumps and falls silent. I consider him cautiously. Well-dressed, for an obvious thug. Given the name-change and the designation given to this challenge, combined with what Tattletale had let spill during the bank challenge - was it safe to assume that this man was with Marquis? Was my power going for the alternate-history route here? Was Amy going to announce herself as the Marquess when I reached her? Or would it be Marchioness? What was the difference again? It probably wasn't important. What was important was the idea that I needed melee contact with Panacea's power to fully defeat every enemy in this challenge, I wasn't happy about that - another thing to overcome in the group combat that I was expecting this late into a TIME mission. I can't even hand that duty off to my ash clone because I'll just die without constantly cycling back to Panacea's power to cleanse myself.

Just one enemy. Could have been a problem in a more thorough ambush, but perhaps group tactics like that are a little bit beyond the capabilities of the parasites controlling my opponents this time. Maybe I could use that. There was definitely something here. Even two or three gunmen would have greatly improved the chance of killing me in this ambush, the fact that Amy hadn't opted for that... that was interesting. A limitation, somewhere. Would they fight each other if they were in combat and lured into each other? What if- I stumble, a flash of pain pulsing from my chest. Panacea's power identifying something for the barest flash of a moment before going worryingly silent.

I spit blood onto the ground, rolling over to consider my attacker.

My own ash clone.

Except, I could hardly call it that anymore. It was just an infestation surrounding the shell of my ash clone, a flopping, extended plant retracting from its arm - a needle-like protrusion dripping with some unidentified liquid. Likely what I'd just been injected with, going by the pain in my chest but the lack of a gaping hole that that usually signified. I dismiss my ash clone, watching as my attacker sags and falls over - a mass of plantlife attempting to push itself upright without any more leverage to do so. And nothing to sustain it's incredible growth with - it's already starting to turn in on itself for food. Not that the ash could have been that nutritious... perhaps it was the proximity to the attacker? The pollen must have set on the ash clone, then activated in response to touching the flesh of the man, or the fluid splatter as we were hitting him, or some type of pheromones or... something. I can't interpret it. My version of Amy's power likes to tell me what is happening, but not why - which makes the overly complex biological signals essentially impossible to interpret for me.

I wince. My body feels weak. Heart is racing, and my chest is screaming in agony with a sharp-painful squeeze. Heart attack, I guess. A new one for me - which actually seems a little surprising given the huge amount of times that I've died already. I didn't want to use the shadow state fully, but shifting parts of my body isn't an issue. Shift my torso, leaving the skin out of it - I expend every charge I have on it in a row, then settle back into my physical body in exactly the same state I left it in.

Well. Fuck you then. I sit back and wait for death, absently watching through my bug-administrators eyes to check one more building off of my search area. Every little helps. When I get my hands on you, Amy...

FAILURE​

I blink my eyes a few times as the real world filters back, Amy's concerned face appearing at the edge of my vision - but that softens into a more neutral expression as I focus on her.

A familiar soreness pulses from my arms and legs. There goes my power protesting at it's self-imposed limit on simulations again. Just as bad as after I fended off Oni Lee and Bakuda. No, worse than that - I was happy to move around after that, although maybe some adrenaline was helping. Now, I don't even want to do that. Glad I'm already lying down, I wouldn't want to get up anyway.

"Was it everything you dreamed?" I wink.

"I feel like I have more questions than answers." She answers. "You had me worried for a moment there, but you seem okay now - was that, did that feel normal? To you? You look- I can tell you're in pain. You should have said no if it was going to be this bad."

"Pretty average. Doesn't hurt that much, I've had way worse." I nod. The content of the simulations shouldn't affect me externally, apart from that one time with Newter - but that had a DNGR modifier. In reality, this should be just like any other single simulation.

She hums distractedly. "All of that elevated brain activity, the adrenaline spikes, the heart-rate, the traces of damaged muscles - it's already starting to look normal to me, like you've been in this state for hours. It's hard to believe that it looked like you were having a panic attack and a stroke at the same time just a few seconds ago."

"I told you, I get some aches and pains if I overdo it - and then it all fixes itself when I ease off the gas. Again, it's the equivalent of a Thinker headache except I'm too tough for a headache to stop me. You've probably seen one of those in action, right?" She shakes her head. Really? I feel like I consistently overestimate how much people experiment with different parts of their powers. "Well. Whatever. Are you going to stop worrying about me now?"

"No." She deadpans. "But I can at least say that the 'damage' it's doing when you do that isn't going to kill you. Directly. It isn't damaging your heart or anything similar in the same way that it's weakening your limbs. I guess, as you said, if you take it easy for a few days - you'll be back at 100%. I'd actually like to see if your power will stop reversing my changes after a certain point of recovery, but maybe we can test that out another day."

"Medical tests are boring. Sorry." I make a face. "Also, can't promise that - I'm staying down for a day, maybe a day and a half. But then I'm back in the fight."

She frowns at me. "I'm not saying you can't go on patrol, just avoid trying to copy powers for a bit."

I shake my head. "Can't do it. Sorry. It's too useful in the middle of a fight." I note her frustrated expression and tap my head. "I wouldn't insist if it wasn't serious. I'm needed out there. You see - part of that process is, I guess you could say, connecting to the powers? I get a bit of insight into what they can do. Well, I did that to Oni Lee and Bakuda-" Just Oni Lee, but semantics don't matter here. "-right at the end of this evening's events. So I can tell you with complete confidence - Bakuda's crappy bombs? Pale imitations of what they could be. Oni Lee's little bombing run tonight trapped a lot of people, but pretty much everyone lived - right? New Wave got most of their members trapped in crystal, but they weren't affected themselves. Manton limit. Problem is, that isn't an actual limitation of Bakuda's tech. She just didn't have the time or a push from Lung to work around it for her more interesting bombs. But she can. And she will. If I don't take the fight to her and beat some sense into her, she's going to give Oni Lee bombs that could let him fight the entire Protectorate ENE branch on even footing."

Honestly, if that was all - I might not have cared. A second Lung wasn't a problem. But my power hadn't shown me a Cape with that level of restraint. I'd seen civilian casualties on a scale I would have associated with the Slaughterhouse 9. Was my power exaggerating, making things worse than the actual likely reality - just to make the challenge harder? Maybe. But Bakuda didn't strike me as someone who wouldn't eagerly participate in the scenes that I saw. And Oni Lee is just following instructions, as ever. That scenario had seemed all too likely.

I was arguably a villain. But I wasn't that kind of villain. I wasn't going to allow that kind of scene to happen in my city. Not that level of civilian casualties, nor would I allow someone with that lack of restraint to display that kind of power against my girls. Taylor had already come close to death against Oni Lee the first time around, I didn't want to see the outcome of that fight if the grenades simply deleted space in an area five times the size of the old ones - or if they simply converted a building and every occupant in it into glass. As much as I liked to joke around, I did need to step in here.

"That sounds like something you should be telling the PRT." Amy leans forward. "And New Wave, for that matter. If she's that much of a danger, everyone needs to be involved."

"Even if I could explain my 'hunch', which I can't - you already know that nobody is going to pick a fight with Lung when he's arguably at the strongest he's ever been. Oni Lee is free, and he has a pet Tinker. Everyone knows the ABB is going to ram their fist right into the Empire's asshole to make up for all the territory they lost while Oni Lee was out of the picture. The Protectorate isn't strong enough to stop them and quietly wants that to happen anyway, two of their enemies fighting each other - and they just minimise damage and civilian casualties. A strong ABB against a strong Empire... everyone is hoping they just cripple each other and I can't even blame them for thinking that. New Wave just tried and failed to beat both Lung and then Oni Lee separately, they're smart enough to know that they can't just jump into an open fight like this. Nobody wants to pick a fight now, even if they knew that they were going to be more problematic in the future."

"The Protectorate and New Wave isn't strong enough, so you should fight them instead?" She scowls, one leg flipping over my body to allow her to stand up properly from her seated position on me. She gives the costume she's holding in her other hand a frustrated flick to straighten them out, as if they'd done something to personally offend her.

"I'm not looking for a fair fight. I don't even intend to show my face to Lung. I'm not part of a highly-public, flashy hero team like the Protectorate or New Wave. I'm allowed to be more practical and flexible in how I approach problems. If New Wave jumped Bakuda in front of the lights and cameras, she'd blow everyone up just so that nobody saw her lose." And I'd wager anything that the next deadman's switch won't have a Clockblocker-sized weakness in it. "If I jump her in the middle of the night, offering friendship and a temporary alliance against the Empire on one hand - so long as she stays within certain rules - and outright violence in the other, I think I can convince her to limit her destructive tendencies. Lung was able to threaten her into compliance without creating a spectacle, and I made some pretty good progress in my talks with her earlier. I just need to do the same - make it so that she doesn't even need to acknowledge a defeat publicly to change her plans and tech to something that suits everyone."

"That sounds like a stupid idea." At least she's honest. "Even if you did, somehow, find her and then also beat her and Oni Lee and Lung to have your 'conversation' - there's just no way that she would agree to limit her powers like that. Or that Lung would even let her."

She's right, but I'm right too. More right. Righter. The rightest. Because she was missing information, even after all I'd dumped on her tonight. Unfortunately, I couldn't really come out and say 'Actually, I have a really good chance of convincing her and Oni Lee not to carpet bomb the city because I'm a human Master and I'm going to master them just like I did you! Once I'm done with them, they'll be very wholesome Capes who don't turn people into glass statues for fun and coincidentally also love my dick'. I don't think that would go down well, even if it's actually a very reasonable and well-thought out plan.

"Everyone's a critic." I wave her off. "Fact of the matter is, this doesn't even need to be a fight. Just a reminder that all of us Capes play by the same rules. Even Lung knows not to act up too much. This is just a... welcome to the neighbourhood speech that got interrupted before I could finish tonight."

"You make it sound so easy." Amy rolls her eyes. "Well. When you get caught creeping in the middle of ABB territory and end up looking twice as crispy as you were today, I hope you'll actually ask me for healing then rather than trying to be tough about it." She sighs. "From what they were saying earlier, we were already planning on a show of force over the next few days to try and hammer home the fact that the gangs really can't get away with things like this. You'll probably see each us on your patrols no matter what you do - and I can hardly criticise you for wanting to find Bakuda on one of those patrols when my team wants to do exactly the same. At least you won't really be alone when you're trying to pull off your stupid plan. Best case scenario, you find them - we arrest them and we never need to worry about what she might have been able to build."

Patrol? Ah. Right. She thinks that I don't know where Bakuda is right now. She doesn't know that my administrator bug is currently cocooned safely in Bakuda's costume, halfway across the city. In a basement, going by the angle. I wouldn't be 'looking' for Bakuda - I'd be dropping in from the ceiling like the wrath of god. That was the reason for my time-limit too. That bug was going to die at some point, and then I'd lose my only way to track their location.

Maybe I shouldn't say that. It was nice to be able to say this much and be rewarded for that trust, no sign of her pulling an Emma, having a meltdown over each new revelation or running off to ruin my plans by trying to send New Wave on the warpath or anything of the sort. But I think she's only avoiding a panic by thinking that I'm not actually going to end up in a real fight. Telling her that actually this matchup was a guaranteed face-to-face battle rather than just an enthusiastic patrol-with-intent that would never get further than fighting some gangbangers and running away? Yeah. Maybe not. Gotta remember that this girl could poke me and lock me into her bedroom for my own safety if I pushed her too much at once.

"I wasn't going to be alone. I've got a team, you know? I haven't asked yet, but Arachne is always up for some gang-busting activity. Shadow Stalker isn't an official member, but I doubt she'll be happy with the PRT's likely plan to sit on their asses and watch - so she might be around too." I watch as Amy slips her costume back on. And that is the right word, with the way parts of it melts and wraps around her skin before adopting the approximate appearance and texture of regular cloth once more. I knew this was a good idea, I can practically sense her mood improving as she regards her reflection in a nearby mirror - and my own mood soars as I note that she's included my advice for 'accessibility' as half the costume folds away with a thought, then unfolds back out again.

She spots me staring and flushes, brushing imaginary dust off of herself and straightening up. Her expression turns back to a neutral one as she fully turns to face me, biting her lip as if mulling over a difficult question. "If-" She starts, hesitancy in her voice. "I could- I mean-" She trails off, gaze fully-focused on her sleeves - where her robes billow as if in an invisible wind, the only indication that something is different about it than usual. "No. Nevermind."

I guess the direction of her thoughts easily. "Thinking of lending a hand on the frontlines yourself?"

"What? No. Well. Maybe. Not now." She sighs. "It was a selfish thought. I'd be a liability, I wouldn't even know what to do in a fight. I'm good at healing. That's always useful. If I got myself injured because I got ideas about being able to do more, then couldn't heal someone when it was needed..."

"I think you would work it out pretty quickly, but the ABB probably aren't the best people to start learning to fight against." I concede. "That's no reason to give up on the idea entirely though. It would be a fun way to use your powers, and being able to defend yourself is always a good idea even if you did intend to stay as a healer forever. You should come and train with us sometime. Arachne gets beaten up by Shadow Stalker regularly to learn how to fight in hand-to-hand - there's no reason why we'd exclude you, if you wanted to try throwing some punches or test out your latest plant-armour thing."

"I'm part of New Wave. I'm not joining your team." She reminds me, leaning her hand over her shoulder to look back at me.

"You're currently part of New Wave." I correct. "Just as Shadow Stalker is currently part of the Wards. She still shows up. And you don't need to stay with them until you're ninety years old. They'll still be family, even if you did join another hero team. Plus, I can promise that Arachne isn't going to say anything about how weird it is that Panacea can grow tentacles out of her costume and Shadow Stalker wouldn't tell anyone just because she dislikes the PRT. If you're not ready to reveal more of your powers, but you still want to experiment... you'll have to get in touch."

"I'll- I'll think about it. Maybe it's a little fast for me. Things have already changed a lot in just a few weeks." She shakes her head, but her words seem more about convincing herself. "I should head back. I think I need to think about things properly. Work out what I really want to do."

"Take your time. We're not going anywhere." Honestly, it didn't matter if she joined my team or not. At the end of the day, by the time I was done - every team in the Bay would be 'my' team. I just had a preference for a team that was more obviously under my control, away from expectations and obligations that I didn't want anything to do with. Faultline's crew got away with things that New Wave would get the hammer dropped on them for - I wanted that same operational freedom and general hands-off approach from the authorities for my team.

"Thanks. I'll call Vicky. My excuse for being out this late is wearing pretty thin at this point." She starts to walk towards the door, then pauses at it - turning towards me wryly. "Care to let me out of the sex-dungeon? Or do I need to dust off a spot in the corner to sleep in?"

I mock-glare at her, ready to retort... except, it's difficult to do that given what we've been doing ever since arriving here. "Just wait until I get you and Vicky in a room at the same time. You'll see the difference."

"Won't ever be able to do that if you get blown up by the bomb lady."

"Don't worry." I state firmly.

I won't make a mistake in this. And I won't take chances on anyone that hasn't been affected by my power. Oni Lee's third and fourth challenges were enlightening, to say the least. And as much as I would like to handwave it off as the kind of alternate-history simulation that my power loves, it didn't need to take any creative liberties with personality or technologies at all to get the bombing spree that I'd seen. If I can't get all of the ABB Capes past their second challenge to at least blunt any of their more homicidal plans, or at least finish off Oni Lee's fourth challenge to hopefully put some kind of moral safeguard on the person that can do the most damage with those bombs... then I'll just kill Bakuda and Oni Lee and be done with it. It would be a shame to lose their future powers, but there's a limit to the risks I'm willing to take. Not for my sake - but for the girls around me.

"I won't lose."
